terms.d_en: The view that past, present, and future things all exist. Also called the block universe.
terms.d_zh: 主張過去、現在、未來的事物全都存在。也稱為「塊體宇宙」。

terms.zh: A 系列與 B 系列
terms.d_en: McTaggart’s names for the ordering of events as past, present, and future, and as earlier and later.
terms.d_zh: 麥塔加的命名：把事件排成「過去、現在、未來」，以及排成「早於、晚於」。

terms.d_en: The marking of an event as past, present, or future relative to the time of speaking.
terms.d_zh: 相對於說話的時刻，把事件標示為過去的、現在的或未來的。

terms.d_en: Newton’s view that time exists independently of events, and Leibniz’s view that it is only their order.
terms.d_zh: 牛頓的看法：時間獨立於事件而存在；萊布尼茲的看法：時間只是事件的次序。

terms.d_en: Happening at the same time. In relativity it depends on the observer’s state of motion.
terms.d_zh: 在同一時刻發生。在相對論裡，它取決於觀察者的運動狀態。

terms.d_en: The difference between the past and future directions of time.
terms.d_zh: 時間的「過去」與「未來」兩個方向之間的差別。

terms.d_en: Augustine’s description of time as the mind’s extension through memory, attention, and expectation.
terms.d_zh: 奧古斯丁對時間的描述：心靈藉由記憶、注意與期待而伸展開來。

vocab.eg: We handle time without difficulty.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們處理時間毫無困難。

vocab.eg: Part of the minute has already fled.
vocab.eg_zh: 這一分鐘有一部分已經逃走了。

vocab.eg: The present is a boundary with no extent.
vocab.eg_zh: 現在是一條沒有寬度的界線。

vocab.eg: I recite a psalm that I know by heart.
vocab.eg_zh: 我背誦一首熟記的詩篇。

vocab.eg: Expectation is used up and all of it is memory.
vocab.eg_zh: 期待用盡，全部成了記憶。

vocab.eg: Most philosophers have been unwilling to put time inside the mind.
vocab.eg_zh: 多數哲學家不願意把時間放進心靈裡。

vocab.eg: Absolute time flows equably without regard to anything external.
vocab.eg_zh: 絕對時間均勻地流逝，與任何外在的事物無關。

vocab.eg: All events are laid out along the dimension of time.
vocab.eg_zh: 所有事件沿著時間這個維度鋪開。

vocab.eg: There is no single “now” that spans the universe.
vocab.eg_zh: 並沒有一個橫跨全宇宙的、單一的「現在」。

vocab.eg: The pressing question was what the moment calls for.
vocab.eg_zh: 迫切的問題是：這個時刻要求什麼？

quiz.q: Why does Augustine conclude that the present “hath no space”?
options: Any stretch of time can be divided into a part that is past and a part that is future.
The present lasts exactly one second.
God exists outside time.
Clocks had not yet been invented.

quiz.q: Where, according to Augustine, do past and future exist?
options: In the soul, as memory and expectation.
In another world.
Nowhere at all, in any sense.
In the stars.

quiz.q: What is the difference between Newton’s and Leibniz’s views of time?
options: For Newton time exists independently of events; for Leibniz it is only their order.
Newton denied that time exists; Leibniz affirmed it.
Newton thought time was circular; Leibniz thought it was straight.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: What does eternalism claim?
options: Past, present, and future events are all equally real.
Only the present exists.
Time will never end.
The soul is immortal.

quiz.q: Why does relativity create a difficulty for presentism?
options: Observers in relative motion disagree about which distant events are simultaneous, so there is no universal “now.”
It proves that time runs backward.
It shows that clocks cannot be trusted.
It denies that anything happens.

write.en: Describe an hour that felt very long and an hour that felt very short. What does the difference suggest about what you were measuring?
write.zh: 描述一個感覺非常漫長的小時，以及一個感覺非常短的小時。這個差別，說明了你量的是什麼？

write.en: Which is harder to accept: that the people you have lost do not exist in any sense, or that your whole future is already there? Explain in about 150 words.
write.zh: 哪一個比較難接受：你失去的那些人在任何意義上都不存在，還是你的整個未來已經在那裡了？用大約 150 個英文字說明。

write.en: Mencius calls Confucius “the sage who was timely.” Describe a decision of your own in which the timing mattered as much as the choice.
write.zh: 孟子稱孔子為「聖之時者」。描述一個你自己的決定：在其中，時機跟選擇本身同樣重要。

paras.en: The debate between presentism and eternalism was conducted in India, in detail, some two thousand years before McTaggart. One early school took its very name from its answer. The Sarvāstivādins, “those who say that all exists,” held that past, present, and future things are all real (三世實有), and that a thing’s being present consists only in its exercising its activity. Their reason was a familiar one: if the past did not exist, past deeds could not bear fruit, and a memory would have nothing to be a memory of. Their opponents, the Sautrāntikas, replied that only the present moment exists, that the past is what has ceased and the future is what has not arisen, and that causal influence is passed along from moment to moment like a flame from lamp to lamp. The arguments on each side match the modern ones closely.
paras.zh: 現在論與永恆論之間的辯論，在印度被詳細地進行過，比麥塔加早了大約兩千年。有一個早期的部派，連名字都取自它的答案。說一切有部（Sarvāstivāda，「說一切存在者」）主張過去、現在、未來的事物全都是真實的（三世實有）；一樣東西之所以「現在」，只在於它正在發揮作用。他們的理由聽來很熟悉：如果過去不存在，過去的業就無法結果，而記憶也就沒有對象可記。他們的對手經量部回應說：只有現在這一剎那存在；過去是已經滅去的，未來是還沒生起的；因果的影響是一剎那一剎那地傳下去的，就像火焰從一盞燈傳到另一盞。雙方的論證，跟現代的論證非常吻合。

paras.en: Nāgārjuna rejected both. If present and future exist in dependence on the past, he argued, they would have to be in the past already; and if they do not depend on it, they cannot be established at all (若因過去時，有未來現在；未來及現在，應在過去時). The three times are defined by one another and none stands by itself, which is what he means by calling time empty. The practical teaching goes with this. A well-known verse says: “Let one not trace back the past, nor yearn for the future. What is past is left behind, and the future has not been reached” (Majjhima Nikāya 131). Augustine found that the mind is stretched painfully between memory and expectation, and he looked to eternity for rest. The Buddha, starting from the same observation, taught his followers to see each present state clearly as it arises, without being carried away by the other two (Dharma and the West, D16).
paras.zh: 龍樹兩邊都不接受。他論證：如果現在與未來是依待過去而有的，它們就得已經在過去之中；如果它們不依待過去，那它們根本無法成立（「若因過去時，有未來現在；未來及現在，應在過去時」）。三時是彼此界定的，沒有一個獨自站得住；這就是他說時間是「空」的意思。實踐上的教導與此相應。有一首著名的偈說：「不追憶過去，不期盼未來。過去已經捨離，未來還沒到來」（《中部》131）。奧古斯丁發現，心靈在記憶與期待之間被痛苦地拉扯，於是他望向永恆尋求安息。佛陀從同一個觀察出發，教導弟子在每一個當下的狀態生起時清楚地看見它，而不被另外兩者帶走（佛法與西方哲學 D16）。

terms: the doctrine that all three times exist

further.t: Augustine, Confessions, Book XI, translated by E. B. Pusey
further.n_en: Chapters 14 to 28 contain the whole argument.
further.n_zh: 第 14 到 28 章包含了整個論證。

further.t: Aristotle, Physics, Book IV, chapters 10–14
further.n_en: Time as the number of change.
further.n_zh: 時間作為變化之數。

further.t: J. M. E. McTaggart, “The Unreality of Time,” Mind (1908)
further.n_en: Eighteen pages that set the terms for a century. Public domain.
further.n_zh: 十八頁，定下了此後一個世紀的討論框架。公版。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Time”
Carlo Rovelli, The Order of Time (2018)
further.n_en: A physicist’s short and readable account of what is left of time.
further.n_zh: 一位物理學家寫的短而好讀的書，談時間還剩下什麼。

lessons.title: What Makes You You?
lessons.blurb_en: Soul, body, or memory: three accounts of what it takes to be the same person over time, a teleporter that breaks all of them, and the suggestion that identity may not be what matters.
lessons.blurb_zh: 靈魂、身體，還是記憶：關於「歷經時間仍是同一個人」需要什麼的三種說法；一台把三者全部弄壞的傳送機；以及這個提議——重要的也許根本不是同一性。
lessons.big_en: We care about our own future in a way we care about no one else’s. The puzzle of personal identity asks what that concern is tracking, and the unsettling answer is that there may be nothing there of the kind we assume.
lessons.big_zh: 我們在乎自己的未來，那種在乎是我們對任何別人都沒有的。人格同一的難題問的是：這份關切追蹤的到底是什麼？令人不安的答案是：那裡也許並沒有我們所以為的那種東西。

paras.en: Find a photograph of yourself at the age of five. You have no doubt that the child is you. Yet almost nothing connects the two of you that you could point to. The child was a third of your height, knew a fraction of what you know, wanted different things, and was made of other matter. You remember perhaps a dozen moments from that whole year. If a stranger differed from you in all these ways, it would not occur to you to say that the two of you were one person. So what is the fact that makes it true of the child? The last unit asked this about a ship. Asking it about ourselves is harder, because we have a strong sense that in our own case there must be a definite answer.
paras.zh: 找一張你五歲時的照片。你毫不懷疑那個孩子就是你。可是你們兩個之間，幾乎沒有什麼你指得出來的東西是相連的。那個孩子只有你身高的三分之一，知道的只是你所知的一小部分，想要的東西不同，構成的物質也不同。那一整年，你記得的也許只有十來個片刻。如果有一個陌生人在這些方面全都跟你不同，你根本不會想到要說你們兩個是同一個人。那麼，是什麼事實使「那個孩子是你」為真？上一個單元對一艘船問了這個問題。對我們自己問，比較難，因為我們有一種強烈的感覺：輪到自己的時候，一定有一個確定的答案。

paras.en: The oldest answer is that you are a soul, an immaterial thing that stays the same while body and mind change around it. Plato held this, and Descartes gave it its modern form: I am a thinking substance. The view has the advantage of giving a definite answer in every case. Its weakness was pointed out by Locke. A soul, as the theory describes it, has no features by which it could be recognized. If the soul in your body were replaced each night by another exactly like it, carrying the same memories, neither you nor anyone else would notice. A soul that makes no difference to anything we can observe cannot be what we mean when we say that this is the same person we met last year.
paras.zh: 最古老的答案是：你是一個靈魂，一個非物質的東西；身體與心智在它周圍變化，它自己保持不變。柏拉圖這樣主張，笛卡兒給了它現代的形式：我是一個思考的實體。這個看法的好處是，在每一個情況下都給出確定的答案。它的弱點是洛克指出的。照這個理論的描述，靈魂沒有任何可供辨認的特徵。假如你身體裡的靈魂每天夜裡都被另一個一模一樣、帶著同樣記憶的靈魂換掉，你不會察覺，別人也不會。一個對我們所能觀察的一切都毫無差別的靈魂，不可能是我們說「這是我們去年見過的同一個人」時所指的東西。

paras.en: A second answer is that you are a living human animal. You are the same person as the child because you are the same organism, which has grown and replaced its matter as organisms do. This view, now called animalism, fits what biology tells us, and it explains why we identify one another by faces and fingerprints. Locke’s objection to it has convinced most readers since. “Should the soul of a prince, carrying with it the consciousness of the prince’s past life, enter and inform the body of a cobbler,” everyone sees, he says, that the person who wakes in the cobbler’s bed is the prince. He remembers the palace and is “accountable only for the prince’s actions.” A modern version puts a brain in place of the soul. If your brain were transplanted into another body, most people judge that you would go where the brain goes. If so, we are not simply our bodies.
paras.zh: 第二個答案是：你是一個活著的人類動物。你跟那個孩子是同一個人，因為你們是同一個有機體；它像一切有機體那樣長大，並且更換了自己的物質。這個看法現在稱為「動物論」；它符合生物學告訴我們的事，也解釋了我們為什麼靠臉孔與指紋辨認彼此。洛克對它的反駁，說服了此後大多數的讀者。他說：「假如一位王子的靈魂，帶著對王子過去生活的意識，進入並主宰了一個鞋匠的身體」，那麼每個人都看得出來，在鞋匠床上醒來的那個「人」是王子。他記得宮殿，而且「只須為王子的行為負責」。現代的版本把靈魂換成了腦。如果你的腦被移植到另一個身體裡，多數人判斷：腦去哪裡，你就去哪裡。若是如此，我們就不單純是自己的身體。

paras.en: Locke’s own account was the first to locate identity in the mind’s contents. A person, he says, is “a thinking intelligent being, that has reason and reflection, and can consider itself as itself, the same thinking thing, in different times and places.” What makes a later person the same as an earlier one is consciousness reaching back: I am whoever I can remember being. The proposal was brilliant, and two objections were raised at once. Thomas Reid imagined a brave officer who remembers being flogged as a boy, and who later, as an old general, remembers his deeds as an officer and has forgotten the flogging. By Locke’s test the general is the officer and the officer is the boy, and the general is not the boy, which breaks the logic of identity. Bishop Butler added that memory cannot make me the same person, because it assumes that I am. To remember doing something, as opposed to merely seeming to, I must be the one who did it.
paras.zh: 洛克自己的說法，是第一個把同一性放在心靈內容裡的。他說，一個「人格者」是「一個會思考、有智能的存在者，有理性與反省，並且能夠在不同的時間與地點，把自己當作自己，當作同一個思考的東西」。使後來的人與先前的人同一的，是往回延伸的意識：我記得自己曾經是誰，我就是誰。這個提議很高明，而立刻就有人提出了兩個反駁。里德設想了一位勇敢的軍官：他記得自己小時候挨過鞭打；後來他成了老將軍，記得自己當軍官時的事蹟，卻忘了那次鞭打。照洛克的檢驗，將軍就是軍官，軍官就是那個男孩，而將軍卻不是那個男孩；這就破壞了同一性的邏輯。巴特勒主教補充說：記憶不可能使我成為同一個人，因為它預設了我是。要「記得」做過某件事，而不只是「好像記得」，我就必須是做了那件事的人。

paras.en: Later philosophers repaired the theory. They replaced direct memory with overlapping chains of memory, and added the other connections that make up a mental life: intentions carried out, beliefs and character that persist. On the repaired view you are the child because a continuous series of such links runs from the child to you. This is the psychological continuity theory, and for most of the twentieth century it was the leading account.
paras.zh: 後來的哲學家修補了這個理論。他們把「直接的記憶」換成「彼此重疊的記憶鏈」，並且加上構成一個心智生命的其他連結：被執行的意圖、持續下去的信念與性格。照修補後的看法，你是那個孩子，因為有一串連續的這類連結，從那個孩子一直通到你。這就是「心理連續論」；在二十世紀的大部分時間裡，它是領先的說法。

paras.en: In 1984 the Oxford philosopher Derek Parfit described a machine that puts the leading account under strain. You step into a booth on Earth. A scanner records the state of every cell in your body and, in doing so, destroys it. The information is sent to Mars, where a machine builds an exact replica out of local matter. The person who steps out on Mars has your memories, your character, and your plans, and believes that he has just made the journey. On the psychological theory this is you, and teleportation is a way of traveling.
paras.zh: 1984 年，牛津的哲學家帕菲特描述了一台機器，讓這個領先的說法吃緊。你走進地球上的一個小艙。掃描器記錄下你身體每一個細胞的狀態，並且在掃描的同時把它毀掉。資訊被傳到火星，那裡的機器用當地的物質造出一個一模一樣的複製體。在火星走出艙門的那個人，有你的記憶、你的性格、你的計畫，並且相信自己剛剛完成了這趟旅程。照心理連續論，這就是你，而傳送是一種旅行的方式。

paras.en: Now suppose the scanner is improved so that it no longer destroys the original. You step out of the booth on Earth, and a moment later you are speaking by video to someone on Mars who looks and thinks exactly as you do. Nobody believes that the two of you are one person. Yet the replica stands in exactly the same relation to you as before. Everything that made the first case a journey is still present. What is new is only that you have also survived in the ordinary way. If the replica is not you in the second case, it is hard to see how it was you in the first, and then the first case was a death. And if you decide that it was a death, you have to say why the copying of everything you value about yourself should count for nothing.
paras.zh: 現在假設掃描器改良了，不再毀掉原本的那個。你走出地球上的小艙，片刻之後，你正透過視訊跟火星上的某個人說話，他的長相與想法跟你一模一樣。沒有人相信你們兩個是同一個人。然而，那個複製體跟你的關係，跟先前完全一樣。使第一種情況成為「旅行」的一切，全都還在。新增的只有一點：你也以平常的方式存活了下來。如果在第二種情況裡複製體不是你，就很難看出在第一種情況裡它怎麼會是你；那麼第一種情況就是一次死亡。而如果你判定那是一次死亡，你就必須說明：你看重自己的一切都被複製過去了，為什麼這件事毫無分量？

paras.en: Parfit’s conclusion was radical. He argued that in these cases there is no further fact about whether the resulting person is me. We know everything there is to know once we know what happens to the body and how the mental states are connected. The question “But will it be me?” has no answer, and what is more surprising, it does not need one. What I have reason to care about is that there will be someone whose mental life continues mine, and that holds in the teleporter case whether or not we call it survival. Identity, he said, is not what matters. He reported that believing this changed his life. He had seemed to himself to be moving through a glass tunnel toward death, and afterward, he wrote, “the walls of my glass tunnel disappeared. I now live in the open air.”
paras.zh: 帕菲特的結論很激進。他論證，在這些情況裡，對於「結果出現的那個人是不是我」，並沒有進一步的事實。一旦我們知道身體發生了什麼、心理狀態之間怎麼連結，我們就知道了所有可知的事。「可是那會是我嗎？」這個問題沒有答案；而更令人意外的是，它並不需要答案。我有理由在乎的是：將來會有一個人，他的心智生命延續著我的；而在傳送機的情況裡，不管我們稱不稱之為「存活」，這一點都成立。他說：重要的不是同一性。他說，相信這一點改變了他的人生。他原本覺得自己像是在一條玻璃隧道裡走向死亡；後來，他寫道：「我那條玻璃隧道的牆消失了。我現在活在露天之中。」

paras.en: The Western debate assumes that the self is something inside one person, and asks what it is. Classical Confucian thought starts somewhere else. A person is first of all a son or daughter, a parent, a friend, a subject or a minister, and to be good is to be these things well: “let the ruler be a ruler, the minister a minister, the father a father, the son a son.” On this view what I am cannot be stated without mentioning other people, and a human being with no relationships would be missing most of what makes a person. Zhuangzi goes further in the other direction. One of his characters comes out of a trance and says, “Just now I lost myself” (今者吾喪我). The Chinese uses two different words for “I,” and commentators have long taken the sentence to distinguish the self that we construct and defend from whatever it is that is left when that construction is dropped.
paras.zh: 西方的辯論預設自我是一個人「裡面」的某個東西，然後問它是什麼。古典儒家思想從別的地方出發。一個人首先是兒子或女兒、父母、朋友、臣民或大臣；而做個好人，就是把這些身分做好：「君君，臣臣，父父，子子。」照這個看法，「我是什麼」不提到別人就說不出來；一個沒有任何關係的人，會缺少使人成為人的大部分東西。莊子往另一個方向走得更遠。他筆下的一個人物從出神的狀態回來，說：「今者吾喪我。」這句中文用了兩個不同的「我」字；歷來的註家認為，這句話區分了我們建構並捍衛的那個自我，以及把這個建構放下之後剩下的不管什麼東西。

essay.h_en: Why it is not an idle question

paras.en: These puzzles are sometimes dismissed as science fiction. Their consequences are practical. When a person with advanced dementia no longer remembers her own life, families ask whether the wishes she wrote down years ago still bind, and the answer depends on whether she is the same person who wrote them. When a crime comes to trial forty years late, we ask whether the old man in the dock should be punished for what the young man did. Every promise assumes that the one who keeps it will be the one who made it. And each of us is concerned about one death in particular. If Parfit is right, that concern attaches to something less sharp-edged than we suppose. If he is wrong, there is some further thing that makes you you, and after two and a half thousand years of looking nobody has yet said convincingly what it is.
paras.zh: 這些謎題有時被當成科幻小說打發掉。它們的後果是很實際的。當一位重度失智的人不再記得自己的一生，家屬會問：她多年前寫下的意願還有沒有約束力？而答案取決於她是不是寫下那些意願的同一個人。當一樁罪行遲了四十年才受審，我們會問：被告席上的老人，該不該為那個年輕人做的事受罰？每一個承諾都預設：履行承諾的人，將是許下承諾的人。而我們每一個人，都特別關切某一個人的死亡。如果帕菲特是對的，這份關切所附著的東西，沒有我們以為的那麼輪廓分明。如果他錯了，那麼就另有某個東西使你成為你；而找了兩千五百年，還沒有人令人信服地說出它是什麼。

lab.title_en: Try it: three trips to Mars
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：去火星三趟
lab.lead_en: Parfit’s thought experiment in three stages. Answer each question before reading on. At the end you will be shown what your answers commit you to.
lab.lead_zh: 帕菲特的思想實驗，分三個階段。每一題先回答，再往下讀。最後會讓你看到，你的答案讓你必須承擔什麼。

text.en: You step into the booth on Earth. The scanner destroys your body as it records it. On Mars, an exact replica is built from new matter. It has all your memories up to the moment you pressed the button.
text.zh: 你走進地球上的小艙。掃描器在記錄你身體的同時毀掉了它。在火星上，一個一模一樣的複製體用新的物質造了出來。它有你按下按鈕那一刻之前的全部記憶。

q.en: Is the person on Mars you?
q.zh: 火星上的那個人是你嗎？

t.en: Yes. I have traveled to Mars.
t.zh: 是。我旅行到了火星。

t.en: No. I died, and a copy is living my life.
t.zh: 不是。我死了，有個複製品在過我的人生。

text.en: The scanner has been improved and no longer destroys the original. You step out of the booth on Earth, unharmed. On Mars, the replica steps out too. Each of you is certain that he is the one who pressed the button.
text.zh: 掃描器改良了，不再毀掉原本的那個。你毫髮無傷地走出地球上的小艙。在火星上，複製體也走了出來。你們兩個都確信，自己就是按下按鈕的那個人。

q.en: Which of the two is you?
q.zh: 這兩個當中，哪一個是你？

t.en: The one on Earth
t.zh: 地球上的那個

t.en: The one on Mars
t.zh: 火星上的那個

t.en: Both
t.zh: 兩個都是

t.en: Neither
t.zh: 兩個都不是

text.en: A technician tells the one on Earth that the new scanner has damaged his heart. He will die within a few days. The replica on Mars is healthy, and has promised to finish his work, care for his family, and carry out every one of his plans.
text.zh: 技術人員告訴地球上的那個：新型掃描器損傷了他的心臟，他幾天之內就會死。火星上的複製體很健康，並且承諾會完成他的工作、照顧他的家人、實現他的每一個計畫。

q.en: How should the one on Earth regard what is about to happen?
q.zh: 地球上的那個，應該怎麼看待即將發生的事？

t.en: As his death. The replica is no consolation.
t.zh: 當作他的死亡。那個複製體算不上安慰。

t.en: As about as good as ordinary survival.
t.zh: 當作跟平常的存活差不多一樣好。

yes-earth.en: In trip 1 you said the replica was you. In trip 2 an identical replica exists, and you say it is not. The only difference is that the original was not destroyed. So on your view, whether the person on Mars is you depends on what happened to someone else on another planet. Philosophers call this the “no rival” condition, and many find it hard to believe that identity could work that way.
yes-earth.zh: 第一趟你說複製體是你。第二趟有一個一模一樣的複製體，你卻說它不是。唯一的差別是：原本的那個沒有被毀掉。所以照你的看法，火星上那個人是不是你，取決於另一個星球上的另一個人發生了什麼事。哲學家稱之為「沒有對手」條件；許多人覺得很難相信同一性會是這樣運作的。

yes-mars.en: You hold that you go where the replica goes, even when the original walks away unharmed. Then the man who stepped out of the booth on Earth, with your body, your brain, and an unbroken stream of consciousness, is not you. Almost no one can accept that.
yes-mars.zh: 你主張複製體去哪裡，你就去哪裡，即使原本的那個毫髮無傷地走開了。那麼，從地球小艙走出來的那個人，有你的身體、你的腦、沒有中斷過的意識之流，卻不是你。幾乎沒有人能接受這一點。

yes-both.en: You are being consistent about what matters and are in trouble with logic. One person cannot be two people who are in different places and will go on to lead different lives. Parfit’s conclusion is that the relation you care about, which holds between you and both of them, is therefore not identity. This is the heart of his view.
yes-both.zh: 你對「什麼才重要」很一致，卻跟邏輯起了衝突。一個人不可能是兩個位於不同地方、接下來會過不同人生的人。帕菲特的結論是：你在乎的那個關係——它在你與他們兩者之間都成立——因此不是同一性。這就是他的看法的核心。

yes-neither.en: You said that one replica is survival. Two successors, one of them made of your original matter, you count as the end of you. Parfit asks how a double success can be a failure. If having one continuer is as good as surviving, having two cannot be as bad as dying.
yes-neither.zh: 你說一個複製體算是存活。兩個後繼者，其中一個還是用你原本的物質構成的，你卻算作你的終結。帕菲特問：雙重的成功怎麼會是失敗？如果有一個延續者就跟存活一樣好，那麼有兩個不可能跟死亡一樣糟。

no-earth.en: Your answers are consistent. You are your body, or your brain, and a copy is a copy however perfect. The cost is this. The replica has everything you value in yourself: your memories, your loves, your unfinished work. You must hold that none of that is you, and that what you are is the particular lump of matter that happens to carry them, although its atoms are replaced over the years in any case.
no-earth.zh: 你的答案是一致的。你就是你的身體，或你的腦；複製品再完美也只是複製品。代價是這樣的：複製體擁有你看重自己的一切——你的記憶、你所愛的、你未完成的工作。你必須主張這些都不是你；而你所是的，是那一團碰巧承載著它們的特定物質，儘管它的原子多年下來反正都會被替換掉。

no-mars.en: In trip 1 you said the replica was a mere copy, and in trip 2 you say the replica is you while the unharmed original is not. These answers cannot both stand. It is worth asking which of them you would give up.
no-mars.zh: 第一趟你說複製體只是複製品；第二趟你卻說複製體是你，而毫髮無傷的原本那個不是。這兩個答案不可能同時成立。值得問問你自己：你會放棄哪一個？

no-both.en: In trip 1 you said the replica was not you, and in trip 2 you count it as you along with the original. Something in the second story has changed your mind. It may be that seeing the replica alive and talking made its claim more vivid, and if so your first answer may have been about the destruction and not about the replica.
no-both.zh: 第一趟你說複製體不是你；第二趟你卻把它連同原本的那個一起算作你。第二個故事裡有某個東西改變了你的想法。也許是看到複製體活著、說著話，讓它的主張變得更鮮明；若是如此，你的第一個答案談的可能是「毀滅」，而不是複製體。

no-neither.en: You hold that copying does not preserve you, and also that the unharmed man on Earth is not you. On that view an ordinary scan, which changes nothing in your body, ends your existence. You may want to reconsider the second answer.
no-neither.zh: 你主張複製並不能保存你，同時又主張地球上那個毫髮無傷的人不是你。照這個看法，一次普通的掃描——它對你的身體毫無改變——就終結了你的存在。你也許想重新考慮第二個答案。

death.en: This is the natural reaction, and Parfit thought it mistaken. Compare it with trip 1. There, too, the original body ceased and a replica went on, and if you called that travel, the only new element here is a delay of a few days. He argued that what we fear in death is the ending of this stream of experience with nothing to continue it, and that here something does continue it. He admitted that he could not always feel what he believed.
death.zh: 這是很自然的反應，而帕菲特認為它是錯的。把它跟第一趟比一比。在那裡，原本的身體同樣終止了，一個複製體繼續下去；如果你稱那為旅行，那麼這裡唯一新增的元素，是延遲了幾天。他論證：我們在死亡裡害怕的，是這道經驗之流終止了，而沒有任何東西接續它；而在這裡，確實有東西接續它。他承認，他相信的事，他自己並不總是感受得到。

fine.en: This is Parfit’s own answer. What matters, he held, is that someone will exist whose mental life continues yours, and the replica is such a person. Notice how far the view goes. It implies that ordinary death is less bad than we take it to be, to the extent that others carry on what we cared about, and that our concern for our own future selves differs only in degree from our concern for other people.
fine.zh: 這是帕菲特自己的答案。他主張，重要的是將來有一個人存在，他的心智生命延續著你的；而複製體就是這樣一個人。留意這個看法走得多遠。它蘊涵：只要別人接續了我們在乎的東西，平常的死亡就沒有我們以為的那麼糟；還有，我們對未來的自己的關切，跟我們對別人的關切，只有程度上的差別。

argument.lead_en: Parfit’s case that identity is not what matters is usually put in terms of division. The brain has two hemispheres, and people have survived the loss of one. Imagine that each half of your brain is transplanted into a new body. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 帕菲特主張「重要的不是同一性」，通常是用「分裂」來陳述的。腦有兩個半球，而有人失去其中一個之後活了下來。想像你的腦的兩半，各自被移植到一個新的身體裡。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: If only one half of my brain were successfully transplanted, the resulting person would have my memories and character, and I would have survived.
steps.zh: 如果我的腦只有一半移植成功，結果出現的那個人會有我的記憶與性格，而我就算是存活了下來。
steps.ob_en: Accepted by anyone who thinks we go where our psychology goes. Animalists deny it: on their view I am the organism that was left behind, and the operation moved an organ.
steps.ob_zh: 凡是認為「我們的心理去哪裡，我們就去哪裡」的人都接受。動物論者否認這一點：照他們的看法，我是被留下來的那個有機體，那場手術只是搬走了一個器官。

steps.en: If both halves are transplanted, there are two people, each related to me exactly as the single survivor was.
steps.zh: 如果兩半都移植了，就有兩個人，各自跟我的關係，恰恰就是那個單一存活者跟我的關係。
steps.ob_en: Follows from the description of the case.
steps.ob_zh: 由這個情況的描述推出。

steps.en: I cannot be identical with both, since they are two people, and there is no reason to say that I am one of them in preference to the other.
steps.zh: 我不可能與兩者都同一，因為他們是兩個人；而也沒有理由說我是其中一個、而不是另一個。
steps.ob_en: The four-dimensional view from the lesson on the ship resists this. It says that there were two people all along, sharing one body until the operation. Most find that a high price.
steps.ob_zh: 「船」那一課的四維看法抗拒這一步。它說：從頭到尾就有兩個人，在手術之前共用一個身體。多數人覺得這個代價太高。

steps.en: A double success cannot be worse than a single one. So division is not as bad as death.
steps.zh: 雙重的成功不可能比單一的成功更糟。所以分裂不像死亡那麼糟。
steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked. Critics reply that what I want is that I should continue, and a result in which nobody is me is a failure however many good copies exist. Whether one finds the premise obvious or outrageous tends to decide which side of the whole debate one takes.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步。批評者回答：我想要的是「我」繼續下去；一個「沒有任何人是我」的結果，不管存在多少個優良的複製體，都是失敗。一個人覺得這個前提是顯然的還是離譜的，往往就決定了他在整場辯論裡站哪一邊。

steps.en: Therefore what matters in survival is not identity. It is the continuation of my mental life, which can hold where identity does not.
steps.zh: 所以，在存活這件事上，重要的不是同一性。重要的是我的心智生命的延續；而這種延續，在同一性不成立的地方也可以成立。
steps.ob_en: If the conclusion is true, the question “Will that be me?” can lack an answer without anything important being left unknown. Parfit compared it to asking whether a club that has dissolved and re-formed is the same club.
steps.ob_zh: 如果這個結論是真的，「那會是我嗎？」這個問題可以沒有答案，而並沒有任何重要的事因此仍屬未知。帕菲特把它比作這樣的提問：一個解散之後又重組的社團，還是同一個社團嗎？

source.work: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, chapter 27 (added in 1694)
source.work_zh: 洛克《人類理解論》卷二第二十七章（1694 年增補）
source.tr: in the original English (public domain)
source.lead_en: The modern discussion begins with a chapter that Locke added to the second edition of the Essay at the suggestion of his friend William Molyneux.
source.lead_zh: 現代的討論，始於洛克在朋友莫利紐茲的建議下，為《人類理解論》第二版增補的一章。

passages.en: …we must consider what PERSON stands for;—which, I think, is a thinking intelligent being, that has reason and reflection, and can consider itself as itself, the same thinking thing, in different times and places; which it does only by that consciousness which is inseparable from thinking.
passages.zh: ……我們必須考慮「人格者」（PERSON）代表什麼；我認為，那是一個會思考、有智能的存在者，有理性與反省，並且能夠在不同的時間與地點，把自己當作自己，當作同一個思考的東西；而它之所以能這樣做，只是憑著那與思考分不開的意識。
passages.note_en: Locke’s first move is to separate three ideas that had been run together: the same substance, the same man, meaning the same living animal, and the same person. A person is defined by a capacity, that of considering oneself as oneself over time. The definition leaves it open whether a person must be human or made of any particular stuff, which is why the chapter is still cited in arguments about animals and machines.
passages.note_zh: 洛克的第一步，是把三個向來混在一起的觀念分開：同一個實體；同一個「人」（man），意思是同一個活的動物；以及同一個「人格者」（person）。人格者是由一種能力來界定的：歷經時間，把自己當作自己。這個定義並沒有規定人格者必須是人類，或必須由哪一種特定的材料構成；這就是為什麼在關於動物與機器的爭論裡，這一章至今仍被引用。

passages.en: For should the soul of a prince, carrying with it the consciousness of the prince’s past life, enter and inform the body of a cobbler, as soon as deserted by his own soul, every one sees he would be the same PERSON with the prince, accountable only for the prince’s actions: but who would say it was the same MAN?
passages.zh: 因為，假如一位王子的靈魂，帶著對王子過去生活的意識，在鞋匠的身體一被他自己的靈魂離棄之後，就進入並主宰了它，那麼每個人都看得出來，他與王子是同一個「人格者」，只須為王子的行為負責；可是誰會說那是同一個「人」呢？
passages.note_en: This is the first body-swap story told to make a philosophical point, and the method it introduced, testing a concept against an imagined case, is the one used in the exercise above. Notice the word “accountable.” Locke calls “person” a forensic term, one that belongs to law and morality. He wants to know who should be rewarded and punished, and his answer is the one who can be conscious of having done the deed. (“Inform” has its old sense, to give form or life to.)
passages.note_zh: 這是第一個為了提出哲學論點而講的「交換身體」的故事；而它引進的方法——拿一個想像的情況來檢驗一個概念——就是上面那個練習所用的方法。注意「負責」這個詞。洛克稱「人格者」是一個「法庭用語」，屬於法律與道德。他想知道的是誰該受賞、誰該受罰；而他的答案是：能夠意識到自己做過那件事的那一個。（inform 在這裡用的是舊義：賦予形式或生命。）

items.o_en: Thought experiments about teleporters prove nothing. Our concept of a person was formed for a world where such things do not happen, and it is no surprise that it gives no clear verdict when they do.
items.o_zh: 關於傳送機的思想實驗什麼也沒證明。我們的「人」這個概念，是為一個不會發生這種事的世界形成的；遇到這種事，它給不出明確的判決，一點也不奇怪。
items.r_en: The objection has force, and Parfit partly agreed: he thought the concept does break down in such cases. His point was that it should not break down if a person were a soul or any other all-or-nothing thing. That there are cases with no answer is itself the finding. And several of the cases are real in milder forms. Patients whose brain hemispheres have been surgically disconnected sometimes behave as though two centers of awareness were present.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁是有力的，而帕菲特部分同意：他認為這個概念在這類情況裡確實會崩潰。他的重點是：如果人是一個靈魂，或任何別的「全有或全無」的東西，它本來不該崩潰。有些情況沒有答案，這件事本身就是發現。而且，其中有幾種情況以比較溫和的形式真實存在。腦的兩個半球被手術切斷連結的病人，有時表現得好像有兩個覺知的中心同時在場。

items.o_en: Memory cannot be what makes me the same person, because the concept of memory already includes identity. I can only remember what I myself experienced.
items.o_zh: 記憶不可能是使我成為同一個人的東西，因為「記憶」這個概念本身就已經包含了同一性。我只能記得我自己經驗過的事。
items.r_en: This is Butler’s objection, and the standard reply defines a wider notion that does not assume identity. Call it quasi-memory: an apparent memory that was caused, in the right way, by someone’s actual experience. Ordinary memories are quasi-memories of one’s own experiences. The theory can then be stated in terms of quasi-memory without circularity. Whether a state can be “the right kind of cause” without our already knowing whose it is remains disputed.
items.r_zh: 這是巴特勒的反駁；標準的回應是界定一個更寬的、不預設同一性的概念，稱之為「準記憶」：一個表面上的記憶，而它是由某個人的實際經驗、以恰當的方式造成的。平常的記憶，就是對自己經驗的準記憶。這樣，理論就可以用準記憶來陳述，而不犯循環。至於一個狀態，在我們還不知道它是誰的之前，能不能就算是「恰當種類的原因」，仍有爭議。

items.o_en: If there is no deep fact about who I am, then nothing I do today is really done by the one who promised it yesterday, and morality collapses.
items.o_zh: 如果關於「我是誰」沒有深層的事實，那麼我今天做的任何事，都不真的是昨天許下承諾的那個人做的，道德就崩潰了。
items.r_en: Parfit drew the opposite moral. Responsibility and commitment rest on the connections between earlier and later stages of a life, and those connections are real and come in degrees. A promise binds me because I am closely continuous with the one who made it. The view does revise some judgments: a man who has utterly changed over forty years may deserve less punishment. It also weakens the boundary between my interests and other people’s, which Parfit thought an improvement.
items.r_zh: 帕菲特引出的是相反的教訓。責任與承諾，建立在一個人生較早與較晚的階段之間的連結上；而那些連結是真實的，並且有程度之分。一個承諾約束我，是因為我跟許下它的那個人緊密地連續著。這個看法確實會修正某些判斷：一個四十年來徹底改變了的人，也許該受的懲罰比較少。它也削弱了「我的利益」與「別人的利益」之間的界線；帕菲特認為這是一種改進。

said.claim: “Know thyself.” (Socrates)
said.claim_zh: 「認識你自己。」（蘇格拉底）
said.en: Socrates quotes the words in Plato’s dialogues, and he did not coin them. Gnōthi seauton was carved at the entrance to the temple of Apollo at Delphi, and the Greeks attributed it to one or another of the Seven Sages who lived two centuries before him. Its original sense was probably “know that you are a mortal and not a god.” Socrates turned it into a philosophical task. This lesson suggests that the task is harder than he knew, since it is unclear what the object of the knowledge is.
said.zh: 蘇格拉底在柏拉圖的對話錄裡引用過這句話，但它不是他造的。Gnōthi seauton 刻在德爾菲阿波羅神廟的入口；希臘人把它歸給比他早兩個世紀的「七賢」當中的某一位。它原本的意思大概是：「要知道你是凡人，不是神。」蘇格拉底把它變成了一項哲學的任務。這一課顯示，這項任務比他所知道的更難，因為這份「認識」的對象是什麼，並不清楚。

terms.d_en: What makes a person at one time the same person as a person at another time.
terms.d_zh: 使某一時刻的一個人，與另一時刻的一個人是同一個人的東西。

terms.d_en: In Locke, a being that can consider itself as itself over time. Distinguished from “human being,” which names an animal.
terms.d_zh: 在洛克，指能夠歷經時間把自己當作自己的存在者。與「人類」（指一種動物）有別。

terms.d_en: The holding of overlapping chains of memory, intention, belief, and character between earlier and later stages.
terms.d_zh: 較早與較晚的階段之間，有彼此重疊的記憶、意圖、信念與性格之鏈相連。

terms.d_en: The view that each of us is a human organism and persists as long as it does.
terms.d_zh: 主張我們每個人都是一個人類有機體，它存續多久，我們就存續多久。

terms.d_en: A case in which one person is continued by two.
terms.d_zh: 一個人被兩個人延續下去的情況。

terms.d_en: About persons: the view that a person’s existence consists in nothing more than a body and a series of connected mental events.
terms.d_zh: 就人而言：主張一個人的存在，不過就是一個身體加上一連串相連的心理事件。

terms.d_en: An apparent memory caused in the right way by someone’s experience, defined without assuming whose.
terms.d_zh: 由某人的經驗以恰當方式造成的表面記憶；界定時不預設那是誰的經驗。

terms.o: L. forum ‘the place of public business’
terms.zh: 法庭的、與責任歸屬有關的
terms.d_en: Belonging to law and the assignment of responsibility. Locke’s word for the concept of a person.
terms.d_zh: 屬於法律與責任歸屬的。洛克用這個詞形容「人格者」這個概念。

vocab.eg: It would not occur to you to say that the two of you were one person.
vocab.eg_zh: 你根本不會想到要說你們兩個是同一個人。

vocab.eg: A soul that makes no difference to anything we observe cannot be what we mean.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個對我們所能觀察的一切都毫無差別的靈魂，不可能是我們所指的東西。

vocab.eg: He is accountable only for the prince’s actions.
vocab.eg_zh: 他只須為王子的行為負責。

vocab.eg: Two objections were raised at once.
vocab.eg_zh: 立刻就有人提出了兩個反駁。

vocab.eg: To remember doing something, as opposed to merely seeming to.
vocab.eg_zh: 要「記得」做過某件事，而不只是「好像記得」。

vocab.eg: Parfit described a machine that puts the leading account under strain.
vocab.eg_zh: 帕菲特描述了一台讓這個領先說法吃緊的機器。

vocab.eg: You step out of the booth on Earth, unharmed.
vocab.eg_zh: 你毫髮無傷地走出地球上的小艙。

vocab.eg: Why should the copying of everything you value count for nothing?
vocab.eg_zh: 你看重的一切都被複製了，為什麼這件事毫無分量？

vocab.eg: The concern attaches to something less sharp-edged than we suppose.
vocab.eg_zh: 這份關切所附著的東西，沒有我們以為的那麼輪廓分明。

vocab.eg: Do the wishes she wrote down years ago still bind?
vocab.eg_zh: 她多年前寫下的意願，還有沒有約束力？

quiz.q: What is Locke’s objection to the view that personal identity consists in having the same soul?
options: A change of souls that left memory intact would be undetectable, so the soul cannot be what we track.
Souls do not exist.
Only animals have souls.
The soul is located in the brain.

quiz.q: What does the story of the prince and the cobbler show, according to Locke?
options: The same person can be found in a different human body.
Princes are superior to cobblers.
Memory is unreliable.
The body is the person.

quiz.q: What is Reid’s brave officer meant to show?
options: Direct memory gives results that violate the logic of identity.
Soldiers have poor memories.
Courage is a kind of knowledge.
Flogging should be abolished.

quiz.q: Why does the improved teleporter cause a problem?
options: The replica is related to you just as before, yet no one thinks you and it are one person.
It is too expensive to build.
Mars is too far away.
The replica has no memories.

quiz.q: What does Parfit mean by saying that identity is not what matters?
options: What we have reason to care about is the continuation of our mental life, whether or not it counts as identity.
People should not care about anyone.
Names are unimportant.
The soul is immortal.

write.en: Describe yourself at fifteen. In what respects are you the same person, and in what respects a different one? Which standard are you using when you say “same”?
write.zh: 描述十五歲的你。你在哪些方面是同一個人？在哪些方面是另一個人？你說「同一個」的時候，用的是哪一種標準？

write.en: Would you use the standard teleporter if it were safe, cheap, and used by everyone you know? Explain your answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 如果標準型的傳送機安全、便宜，而且你認識的人都在用，你會用嗎？用大約 150 個英文字說明你的答案。

write.en: A person with severe dementia no longer recognizes her family or remembers her past. Is she the same person who signed her will? What should her family honor?
write.zh: 一位重度失智的人，不再認得家人，也不記得自己的過去。她跟當年簽下遺囑的是同一個人嗎？她的家人應該尊重什麼？

paras.en: Everything in this lesson would have been familiar to a Buddhist philosopher of two thousand years ago. The claim that a person is a body and a connected series of mental events, with no further owner, is the doctrine of anattā, not-self. The claim that the stages are tied together by causal continuity and not by a persisting thing is the Buddhist account of how one life, and one life after another, hangs together. Parfit knew this. Near the end of Reasons and Persons he observes that the Buddha would have agreed with him, and he prints passages from Buddhist texts in an appendix.
paras.zh: 這一課裡的一切，兩千年前的佛教哲學家都會覺得熟悉。「人是一個身體加上一串相連的心理事件，此外沒有另一個擁有者」，這就是 anattā（無我）的教義。「各個階段是靠因果的連續、而不是靠一個持存的東西繫在一起的」，這就是佛教對於一期生命、以及一期接一期的生命如何相連的說明。帕菲特知道這一點。在《理與人》接近結尾處，他說佛陀會同意他，並且在附錄裡刊印了佛典的段落。

paras.en: The first lesson of a new shelf in this series takes up the comparison in detail: which Western view comes closest to not-self, where the resemblance stops, and what the Buddhist teaching adds. It is the companion to this page.
paras.zh: 這個系列新書架的第一課，會詳細處理這個比較：西方哪一種看法最接近無我？相似到哪裡為止？佛教的教導又多了什麼？它是這一頁的姊妹篇。

link.en: Read D2 · No-Self and the West
link.zh: 讀 D2・無我與西方哲學

further.t: John Locke, An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, Book II, chapter 27
further.n_en: Twenty pages; the source of the whole modern debate.
further.n_zh: 二十頁；整場現代辯論的源頭。

further.t: Derek Parfit, Reasons and Persons (1984), Part Three
further.n_en: Chapters 10 to 13. Demanding, clear, and for many readers life-changing.
further.n_zh: 第十到十三章。吃力、清楚，而且對許多讀者來說改變了人生。

further.t: John Perry, A Dialogue on Personal Identity and Immortality (1978)
further.n_en: Fifty pages in dialogue form; the best short introduction.
further.n_zh: 五十頁，對話體；最好的短篇入門。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Personal Identity”
Zhuangzi, chapter 2, opening
further.n_en: “Just now I lost myself.”
further.n_zh: 「今者吾喪我。」

lessons.title: Can You Know What Another Mind Feels?
lessons.title_zh: 你能知道別人的感受嗎？
lessons.blurb_en: You have never felt any pain but your own. Mill’s analogy, Nagel’s bat, a scientist raised without color, and two friends on a bridge arguing about whether the fish are happy.
lessons.blurb_zh: 你從來沒有感受過自己以外任何人的痛。彌爾的類比、內格爾的蝙蝠、一位在沒有顏色的房間裡長大的科學家，還有橋上兩個朋友，為了魚快不快樂爭論起來。
lessons.big_en: Everything we know about other minds comes through bodies, faces, and words. The question is whether that evidence can ever reach what it is evidence for, and the answer now decides how we treat animals, patients, and machines.
lessons.big_zh: 我們對別人的心所知道的一切，都是透過身體、臉孔與語言得來的。問題是：這些證據到底搆不搆得到它所要證明的東西？而這個答案，如今決定了我們怎麼對待動物、病人與機器。

essay.h_en: The pain you have never felt

paras.en: A friend catches her hand in a door. You see her face tighten, you hear the cry, and you wince. You are entirely sure that she is in pain. Yet you did not feel it. You have never felt anyone’s pain but your own, and you never will. What reached you was a sound and a movement, and from these you arrived at once, without any sense of reasoning, at a fact about an experience that is closed to you. Philosophers call the puzzle this raises the problem of other minds. It has two parts. The first asks how you know that other people have an inner life at all. The second assumes that they do and asks whether you can know what it is like.
paras.zh: 一位朋友的手被門夾到了。你看見她的臉一緊，聽見那聲叫喊，自己也跟著縮了一下。你完全確定她在痛。可是你並沒有感受到那個痛。除了自己的痛，你從來沒有感受過任何人的痛，以後也不會。傳到你這裡的只是一個聲音、一個動作；而你從這些東西，沒有任何「在推理」的感覺，一下子就到達了一個事實，那個事實關乎一個對你關閉的經驗。哲學家把由此而來的難題稱為「他心問題」。它有兩個部分。第一個問：你怎麼知道別人真的有內在生活？第二個假定他們有，然後問：你能不能知道那是什麼感覺？

paras.en: The classic answer to the first question was given by John Stuart Mill in 1865. I know in my own case, he said, that a burn is followed by pain and that the pain is followed by a cry. I observe that other people have bodies like mine, and that when they are burned they cry out as I do. I conclude that the middle link is present in them as well. This is the argument from analogy, and it describes fairly well what we would say if asked to defend our belief.
paras.zh: 對第一個問題的經典回答，是彌爾在 1865 年提出的。他說：就我自己而言，我知道燙傷之後會痛，痛之後會叫。我觀察到別人有跟我一樣的身體，被燙到的時候也像我一樣叫出聲來。我於是推斷：中間那一環，在他們身上也有。這就是「類比論證」；如果有人要我們為自己的信念辯護，我們會說的話，它描述得相當準確。

paras.en: Its weakness is that it is an induction from a single case. The lesson on induction showed how little we may infer from one observation. If I had opened one box and found a beetle in it, I would have poor grounds for claiming that every box in the world contains a beetle. And here the conclusion can never be checked, since I cannot open a second box. There is a further oddity. Nobody acquires the belief in this way. An infant responds to its mother’s smile long before it could notice any correlation between its own feelings and its own face, which it has never seen.
paras.zh: 它的弱點在於：這是從單一個案做的歸納。「歸納」那一課顯示過，從一次觀察能推出的東西有多麼少。假如我只打開過一個盒子，發現裡面有一隻甲蟲，我就沒有什麼根據宣稱世界上每一個盒子裡都有甲蟲。而且在這裡，結論永遠無法檢驗，因為我打不開第二個盒子。還有一點更奇怪：沒有人是這樣得到這個信念的。嬰兒對母親的微笑有反應的時候，還遠遠不可能注意到自己的感受與自己的臉之間有什麼關聯；它從來沒看過自己的臉。

paras.en: Descartes saw the gap clearly. Looking down from a window at people passing in the street, he remarks in the Meditations, what he strictly sees is hats and coats, which could conceal automata. He judges that they are men. In the Discourse on Method he asked how one could tell a perfect mechanical imitation of a human being from the real thing, and proposed “two most certain tests.” A machine could never arrange words “so as appositely to reply to what is said in its presence,” and it could never act sensibly across “all the occurrences of life,” because each of its skills would need its own special mechanism. Animals, he concluded, fail both tests and are machines without thought.
paras.zh: 笛卡兒把這道缺口看得很清楚。他在《沉思錄》裡說，從窗口往下看街上走過的人，嚴格說來他看見的是帽子與外套，底下藏的可能是自動機。是他「判斷」那些是人。在《方法論》裡，他問：一個模仿人類模仿得十全十美的機械，要怎麼跟真人分辨？他提出了「兩個最確定的檢驗」。機器永遠無法把字詞排列得「恰當地回應在它面前說的話」；它也永遠無法在「生活中的一切境遇」裡都做出合理的行動，因為它的每一項本事都需要一個專屬的機構。他的結論是：動物兩項檢驗都通不過，是沒有思想的機器。

paras.en: The passage is worth rereading today. Descartes was confident that no machine would ever pass his first test, and for more than three centuries he was right.
paras.zh: 這段話今天值得重讀。笛卡兒很有把握，沒有任何機器通得過他的第一項檢驗；而在三個多世紀裡，他是對的。

essay.h_en: What is it like to be a bat?
essay.h_zh: 當一隻蝙蝠是什麼感覺？

paras.en: Suppose the first question is settled and other creatures do have experience. In 1974 the American philosopher Thomas Nagel asked how far our knowledge of it can go. He chose bats because they are mammals, close enough to us that few doubt they feel something, and because they perceive the world chiefly by echolocation, a sense we lack. A bat sends out high-pitched cries and builds its picture of the space around it from the echoes. We can describe this process in complete physical detail. What we cannot do, Nagel argued, is know what it is like for the bat. If I imagine hanging upside down and hearing my way through the dark, I learn what it would be like for me to behave as a bat does. The bat’s own experience has a point of view built into it, and an objective description, which is written from no point of view in particular, leaves exactly that out.
paras.zh: 假設第一個問題解決了，別的生物確實有經驗。1974 年，美國哲學家內格爾問：我們對這種經驗的認識，能走多遠？他選了蝙蝠，因為牠們是哺乳類，跟我們夠近，很少有人懷疑牠們有某種感受；也因為牠們主要靠回聲定位來知覺世界，那是我們沒有的一種感官。蝙蝠發出高頻的叫聲，再從回聲建構出周圍空間的圖像。這個過程，我們可以用完整的物理細節來描述。內格爾論證，我們做不到的，是知道那對蝙蝠來說是什麼感覺。如果我想像自己倒掛著、在黑暗中靠聽覺找路，我得知的是：「我」表現得像蝙蝠會是什麼感覺。蝙蝠自己的經驗內建著一個觀點；而客觀的描述，是不從任何特定觀點寫成的，它漏掉的恰恰就是這個。

essay.h_en: The scientist who had never seen red
essay.h_zh: 從沒看過紅色的科學家

paras.en: Eight years later the Australian philosopher Frank Jackson made the point with a human being. Mary is a brilliant scientist who has lived all her life in a black-and-white room and learned about the world from black-and-white screens. Her field is color vision, and she has come to know every physical fact about it: the wavelengths, the cells of the retina, the pathways in the brain, the way people use the word “red.” One day the door is opened and she sees a ripe tomato. Does she learn anything? Most people answer that she does. She learns what it is like to see red. But she already knew all the physical facts. Jackson concluded that there are facts about experience that physics cannot state, and the argument has been disputed at every step ever since. You can try it below.
paras.zh: 八年後，澳洲哲學家傑克森用一個人說了同樣的道理。瑪麗是一位傑出的科學家，一輩子住在一個只有黑白的房間裡，透過黑白的螢幕認識世界。她的專長是色彩視覺，而她已經知道了關於它的每一個物理事實：波長、視網膜上的細胞、腦裡的路徑、人們怎麼使用「紅」這個字。有一天門打開了，她看見一顆熟透的番茄。她學到了什麼嗎？多數人回答：學到了。她學到看見紅色是什麼感覺。可是她原本就知道全部的物理事實了。傑克森的結論是：有一些關於經驗的事實，是物理學說不出來的；而這個論證，此後每一步都有人爭論。你可以在下面親自試一次。

paras.en: Wittgenstein thought the whole problem rested on a wrong picture. Imagine, he says, that everyone has a box with something in it that we call a “beetle.” No one can look into anyone else’s box, and each says that he knows what a beetle is only from his own. In that situation the thing in the box would play no part in the meaning of the word. The boxes could hold different things, or nothing. His point is that words such as “pain” cannot get their meaning from a private inner object that each speaker points to alone. We learn them in public, from people who comfort us when we fall. And in ordinary life we do not infer that someone is in pain. We see it in the face, as directly as we see that the face is pale. On this view the skeptic’s picture of minds sealed inside bodies is itself the mistake.
paras.zh: 維根斯坦認為，整個問題建立在一幅錯誤的圖像上。他說，想像每個人都有一個盒子，裡面裝著我們叫作「甲蟲」的東西。誰也看不到別人的盒子，每個人都說他只是從自己的那一隻知道甲蟲是什麼。在那種處境裡，盒子裡的東西對這個詞的意義毫無作用。各個盒子裝的可以是不同的東西，也可以什麼都沒有。他的重點是：「痛」這類的詞，不可能從每個說話者獨自指著的一個私有的內在對象得到意義。我們是在公共場合學會這些詞的，是從我們跌倒時安慰我們的人那裡學來的。而在日常生活裡，我們並不是「推論」出某人在痛。我們在臉上看見它，就像看見那張臉發白一樣直接。照這個看法，懷疑論者那幅「心靈密封在身體裡」的圖像，本身就是錯誤所在。

paras.en: The oldest statement of the problem is a conversation of about sixty words. Zhuangzi and his friend Huizi, a logician, were strolling on the bridge over the Hao River. Zhuangzi remarked that the minnows were swimming about freely, and that this was the happiness of fish. Huizi said: “You are not a fish. How do you know the happiness of fish?” Zhuangzi replied: “You are not I. How do you know that I do not know it?” Huizi pressed his advantage. “I am not you, so I do not know what you know. You are not a fish, so you do not know the happiness of fish. The case is complete.” Zhuangzi’s answer has been argued over for two thousand years. “Let us go back to the beginning. When you asked how I know, you already knew that I knew. I know it from up here on the Hao.”
paras.zh: 這個問題最古老的陳述，是一段大約六十個字的對話。莊子與他的朋友、名家的惠子，在濠水的橋上散步。莊子說，鯈魚游得從容自在，這就是魚的快樂。惠子說：「子非魚，安知魚之樂？」莊子答：「子非我，安知我不知魚之樂？」惠子乘勝追擊：「我不是你，所以不知道你知道什麼；你不是魚，所以你不知道魚的快樂。這就說完了。」莊子的回答，被爭論了兩千年：「請回到開頭。你問我『怎麼知道』的時候，就已經知道我知道了。我是在濠水上面知道的。」

paras.en: Huizi argues as Nagel’s reader might: knowledge of an experience requires being the one who has it. Zhuangzi first shows that the principle defeats itself, since Huizi relies on knowing something about Zhuangzi’s mind in order to state it. His last line turns on the Chinese word ān, which means both “how” and “from where.” He answers the second sense. He knows it from where he stands, on a bridge, on a fine day, watching them. The suggestion is that knowledge of another creature is had from within a shared situation, by a being that is itself alive and at ease, and that no proof conducted from outside is needed or possible. Mencius, his contemporary, made a similar observation about human beings. Anyone who suddenly sees a child about to fall into a well feels alarm and compassion, and feels it before any thought of reward. For Mencius that response is the root of all morality.
paras.zh: 惠子的論證方式，像是內格爾的一位讀者會用的：要知道一個經驗，就必須是擁有那個經驗的那一個。莊子先指出這條原則自己打敗自己，因為惠子要說出這條原則，就得靠著知道莊子心裡的某件事。他的最後一句，關鍵在「安」這個字，它既是「怎麼」，也是「在哪裡」。他回答的是第二個意思。他是從他站的地方知道的：在一座橋上，在一個好天氣裡，看著牠們。這裡的暗示是：對另一個生命的認識，是在一個共同的處境之內得到的，是由一個自己也活著、也自在的存在者得到的；從外面進行的證明，既不需要，也不可能。跟他同時代的孟子，對人類做過類似的觀察。任何人突然看見一個小孩快要掉進井裡，都會感到驚懼與不忍，而且是在想到任何好處之前就感到了。對孟子來說，那個反應是一切道德的根苗。

essay.h_en: Three places where the answer is needed

paras.en: The problem has left the seminar room. In 2012 a group of neuroscientists meeting at Cambridge signed a declaration that mammals, birds, and other creatures, octopuses among them, have the neural equipment for conscious states, and laws on animal welfare have begun to follow. In hospitals, some patients who show no response at all have been found, when placed in a scanner and asked to imagine playing tennis, to produce the same brain activity as healthy volunteers. And there are now machines that pass the first of Descartes’s tests with ease. They reply appositely to whatever is said to them, and when asked they will describe their feelings. Whether there is anything it is like to be such a system is a question on which serious researchers disagree, and no agreed method exists for settling it. In each of the three cases behavior has come apart from the usual signs, and we find that we have been relying on resemblance to ourselves without ever deciding which resemblances count.
paras.zh: 這個問題已經離開了研討室。2012 年，一群在劍橋開會的神經科學家簽署了一份宣言：哺乳類、鳥類與其他生物（章魚也在其中）具備產生意識狀態的神經構造；動物福利的法律也已經開始跟進。在醫院裡，有些完全沒有反應的病人，被放進掃描儀、並被要求想像自己在打網球的時候，產生了跟健康受試者相同的腦部活動。而現在也有了輕易就通過笛卡兒第一項檢驗的機器。不管對它們說什麼，它們都能恰當地回應；被問到的時候，還會描述自己的感受。「當這樣一個系統」有沒有任何感覺可言？認真的研究者在這個問題上意見分歧，也還沒有一個公認的方法可以解決它。在這三種情況裡，行為都跟通常的徵象脫了鉤；而我們發現，自己一直依賴的是「跟我們相似」，卻從來沒有決定過，哪些相似才算數。

lab.title_en: Try it: Mary’s room, then the ladder of minds
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：瑪麗的房間，然後是心靈的階梯
lab.lead_en: Two experiments. In the first you learn everything science can say about red, and then see it. In the second you say how sure you are that each of nine things has an inner life, and find out what rule you were using.
lab.lead_zh: 兩個實驗。第一個：你先學會科學對紅色能說的一切，然後看見它。第二個：對九樣東西，你各自說出你有多確定它有內在生活，然後看看你用的是哪一條規則。

intro.en: You are Mary. You have never seen any color. Read the four files on your screen. Together they stand for everything physical there is to know about red.
intro.zh: 你是瑪麗。你從來沒看過任何顏色。讀完螢幕上的四份檔案。它們合起來代表關於紅色所有可知的物理事實。

t.en: Red light has a wavelength of roughly 620 to 750 nanometers, the longest the human eye can detect.
t.zh: 紅光的波長大約是 620 到 750 奈米，是人眼能偵測到的最長波長。

t.en: It is absorbed most strongly by the L-cones of the retina. Color is computed from the ratio of signals from three cone types.
t.zh: 它主要被視網膜上的 L 型視錐細胞吸收。顏色是從三種視錐細胞訊號的比例計算出來的。

t.en: The signals pass through the optic nerve and the thalamus to the visual cortex, where particular groups of neurons respond.
t.zh: 訊號經過視神經與視丘，到達視覺皮質，在那裡有特定的神經元群起反應。

t.en: People call ripe tomatoes, blood, and stop signs “red.” They rate the color as warm, and it raises the heart rate slightly.
t.zh: 人們把熟番茄、血與停車標誌叫作「紅」。他們評定這個顏色是暖的；它會讓心跳稍微加快。

q.en: Did Mary learn anything new just now?
q.zh: 瑪麗剛才學到了任何新東西嗎？

t.en: Yes. A new fact: what red is like.
t.zh: 有。一個新的事實：紅色是什麼感覺。

v.en: This was Jackson’s conclusion. If she learned a fact, and she already knew every physical fact, then some facts are not physical, and the view that everything is physical is false. The price is high: these extra facts seem to do no causal work, since physics already explains every movement of Mary’s body, including her saying “So that is red!” Jackson himself later gave the argument up for this reason.
v.zh: 這是傑克森的結論。如果她學到了一個事實，而她原本就知道每一個物理事實，那麼有些事實就不是物理的；「一切都是物理的」這個看法就是錯的。代價很高：這些額外的事實似乎不起任何因果作用，因為物理學已經解釋了瑪麗身體的每一個動作，包括她說出「原來這就是紅！」。傑克森自己後來就為了這個理由放棄了這個論證。

t.en: Yes, but a skill and not a fact.
t.zh: 有，不過是一種本事，不是事實。

v.en: On this reply Mary gains know-how: she can now recognize red, imagine it, and remember it. Learning to ride a bicycle also gives you something no textbook could, and nobody concludes that there are non-physical facts about cycling. Critics answer that the abilities seem to rest on something she now knows, and that she could lose the abilities and still know it.
v.zh: 照這個回應，瑪麗得到的是「知道怎麼做」：她現在能認出紅色、想像它、記住它。學會騎腳踏車也給了你教科書給不了的東西，卻沒有人因此推斷有關於騎車的非物理事實。批評者回答：這些能力似乎是建立在她現在「知道」的某件事上；而且她可以失去這些能力，卻仍然知道那件事。

t.en: She learned an old fact in a new way.
t.zh: 她用新的方式認識了一個舊的事實。

v.en: This is the most popular reply among physicalists today. Someone who knows that water fills the lake may not know that H₂O does, though it is the same fact. Mary knew the fact about red under a scientific description. She now knows it under a concept that can only be acquired by having the experience. The difficulty is to explain why a mere new way of thinking should feel like such a discovery.
v.zh: 這是今天物理主義者最常用的回應。一個知道「湖裡都是水」的人，可能不知道「湖裡都是 H₂O」，儘管那是同一個事實。瑪麗原本是在科學的描述之下知道關於紅色的那個事實。她現在是在一個只有擁有過那個經驗才能取得的概念之下知道它。困難在於說明：僅僅是一種新的思考方式，為什麼感覺起來會像這麼大的一個發現。

t.en: No. If she really knew everything, she is not surprised.
t.zh: 沒有。如果她真的什麼都知道，她不會驚訝。

v.en: Dennett held that we misjudge the case because we cannot imagine knowing all the physical facts. We picture someone who has read a great deal. A Mary who truly knew everything would know exactly how her brain was about to react, and if you tried to fool her with a blue banana she would catch the trick at once. Most people find this hard to believe, and Dennett’s answer is that the difficulty of believing it is not evidence.
v.zh: 丹尼特主張，我們誤判了這個情況，因為我們想像不出「知道全部的物理事實」是什麼樣子。我們想到的是一個讀了很多書的人。一位真正什麼都知道的瑪麗，會確切知道自己的腦即將怎麼反應；如果你拿一根藍色的香蕉想騙她，她會立刻識破。多數人覺得這很難相信；丹尼特的回答是：難以相信，不算證據。

intro.en: Now the other question. For each of these, how sure are you that there is something it is like to be it? Move every slider, then press the button.
intro.zh: 現在是另一個問題。對下面每一樣，你有多確定「當它」是有某種感覺的？把每一條滑桿都拉過，再按按鈕。

n.en: A stranger on the other side of the world
n.zh: 地球另一端的一個陌生人

n.en: An AI system that says it is suffering
n.zh: 一個說自己在受苦的 AI 系統

go.zh: 讓我看看我預設了什麼

friend_sure.en: You are certain about your friend. Notice what that certainty is not based on: you have never observed your friend’s experience, and you never will. Whatever supports it, it is stronger than any argument that has been offered for it.
friend_sure.zh: 你對你的朋友是確定的。留意這份確定「不是」建立在什麼上面：你從來沒有觀察過你朋友的經驗，以後也不會。不管支撐它的是什麼，它比任何為它提出過的論證都更強。

friend_unsure.en: You left room for doubt even about your closest friend. That is the strict philosophical position, and almost no one can hold it outside the study.
friend_unsure.zh: 即使對你最好的朋友，你也留了懷疑的餘地。這是嚴格的哲學立場；而離開書房之後，幾乎沒有人守得住它。

drop.en: Your confidence falls most steeply between {a} and {b}. Ask what the second lacks that the first has. That is the criterion you are actually using for a mind.
drop.zh: 你的信心掉得最陡的地方，是在{a}與{b}之間。問問自己：後者缺了什麼是前者有的？那就是你實際上用來判定「有心」的標準。

flat.en: Your answers hardly vary. Either almost everything has an inner life or almost nothing can be known to. Both positions have defenders.
flat.zh: 你的答案幾乎沒有起伏。要嘛幾乎一切都有內在生活，要嘛幾乎什麼都無法得知。這兩種立場都有人辯護。

ai_over.en: You rate the AI system above the octopus. You are giving more weight to what a thing says and does than to what it is made of. This is the direction of Descartes’s first test and of functionalism. The octopus, which has neurons, an evolutionary history, and a body that avoids injury, can tell you nothing.
ai_over.zh: 你給 AI 系統的分數高過章魚。比起一樣東西是什麼做的，你更看重它說什麼、做什麼。這是笛卡兒第一項檢驗與功能論的方向。章魚有神經元、有演化史、有一個會避開傷害的身體，卻什麼也無法告訴你。

ai_under.en: You rate the octopus above the AI system. You are giving more weight to living tissue and shared ancestry than to anything that is said. Then testimony is not your evidence, and it is worth asking how much of your certainty about the stranger rests on biology and how much on words.
ai_under.zh: 你給章魚的分數高過 AI 系統。比起任何說出來的話，你更看重活的組織與共同的祖先。那麼「證詞」就不是你的證據；值得問一問：你對那位陌生人的確定，有多少是靠生物學，有多少是靠言語？

ai_same.en: You rate the octopus and the AI system about equally. The two cases are opposites: one has the biology without the words, the other has the words without the biology. Treating them alike suggests that you do not yet know which of the two matters.
ai_same.zh: 你給章魚與 AI 系統的分數差不多。這兩個情況正好相反：一個有生物構造而沒有言語，另一個有言語而沒有生物構造。把它們同等看待，表示你還不知道這兩者當中哪一個才重要。

t.en: You are none of these things. On what grounds do you claim to know about any of them? Put every slider in the middle.
t.zh: 這些東西你一樣也不是。你憑什麼宣稱知道其中任何一個？把每一條滑桿都放在中間吧。

t.en: You moved the sliders without difficulty, so you knew something. You knew it from where you stand, as a living thing among living things.
t.zh: 你毫不費力就拉動了滑桿，可見你知道些什麼。你是從你站的地方知道的：一個活著的東西，在活著的東西當中。

t.en: Ask two things. Can it reply appositely to whatever is said? Can it act sensibly in every circumstance? What fails is a machine. (He put the dog, the bat, and the octopus at zero.)
t.zh: 問兩件事。不管對它說什麼，它能恰當地回應嗎？它能在每一種境遇裡合理地行動嗎？通不過的就是機器。（他把狗、蝙蝠與章魚都放在零。）

t.en: The bat almost certainly has experience. What you cannot know is what that experience is like, and no amount of further fact about its brain will tell you.
t.zh: 蝙蝠幾乎可以確定有經驗。你無法知道的是：那個經驗是什麼感覺；再多關於牠的腦的事實，也不會告訴你。

argument.lead_en: Jackson’s knowledge argument in standard form. Each reply in the exercise above denies a particular step. Click a step to see which.
argument.lead_zh: 傑克森的「知識論證」，寫成標準形式。上面練習裡的每一種回應，各自否定某一步。點任何一步，看看是哪一種。

steps.en: Before she leaves the room, Mary knows every physical fact about color vision.
steps.zh: 在離開房間之前，瑪麗知道關於色彩視覺的每一個物理事實。
steps.ob_en: Dennett’s target. We grant this premise too easily, he says, without imagining what it would involve. A being who met it would be so unlike us that our intuitions about what she would say are worthless.
steps.ob_zh: 丹尼特攻擊的地方。他說，我們太輕易地承認這個前提，沒有去想像它牽涉到什麼。一個滿足這個前提的存在者，會跟我們差得太遠，以致於我們對「她會說什麼」的直覺毫無價值。

steps.en: When she leaves the room and sees red, she learns something: what it is like to see red.
steps.zh: 當她離開房間、看見紅色，她學到了某件事：看見紅色是什麼感覺。
steps.ob_en: Almost everyone accepts that something changes in Mary. The dispute is over how to describe it.
steps.ob_zh: 幾乎每個人都接受瑪麗身上有了某種改變。爭論在於怎麼描述它。

steps.en: What she learns is a fact.
steps.zh: 她學到的是一個事實。
steps.ob_en: The ability reply denies this: she gains a skill. The new-concept reply accepts that she comes to know a fact and denies that it is a new one. The whole argument turns on this step, which is usually left unstated.
steps.ob_zh: 「能力」回應否定這一步：她得到的是一種本事。「新概念」回應接受她認識了一個事實，卻否認那是一個新的事實。整個論證的關鍵就在這一步，而它通常沒有被明說出來。

steps.en: If she learns a new fact, then before leaving she did not know every fact.
steps.zh: 如果她學到了一個新的事實，那麼在離開之前，她並不知道每一個事實。
steps.ob_en: Follows from the meaning of “learn.”
steps.ob_zh: 由「學到」的意思推出。

steps.en: Therefore there are facts that are not physical facts, and physicalism is false.
steps.zh: 所以，有一些事實不是物理事實；物理主義是錯的。
steps.ob_en: If the conclusion is true, a complete science of the brain would still leave something out. If it is false, one of the premises is, and thirty years of argument have not produced agreement on which.
steps.ob_zh: 如果這個結論是真的，一門完整的腦科學仍然會漏掉某些東西。如果它是假的，就有一個前提是假的；而三十年的爭論，並沒有對「是哪一個」達成共識。

source.work: Zhuangzi, chapter 17, “Autumn Floods”
source.work_zh: 《莊子・秋水》
source.tr: translated for this series from the Chinese text
source.lead_en: The exchange closes one of the Outer Chapters, which were written by followers of Zhuangzi in the century or two after his death. The Chinese is given under each passage.
source.lead_zh: 這段對話是外篇其中一篇的結尾；外篇是莊子身後一兩個世紀裡，他的後學所寫的。每一段下面附上原文。

passages.ref: Zhuangzi 17, the debate on the Hao (first half)
passages.en: Zhuangzi and Huizi were strolling on the bridge over the Hao. Zhuangzi said, “The minnows swim out and about so freely. This is the happiness of fish.” Huizi said, “You are not a fish. How do you know the happiness of fish?” Zhuangzi said, “You are not I. How do you know that I do not know the happiness of fish?” Huizi said, “I am not you, so I certainly do not know you. You are certainly not a fish, so your not knowing the happiness of fish is complete.”
passages.zh: 莊子與惠子遊於濠梁之上。莊子曰：「鯈魚出游從容，是魚樂也。」惠子曰：「子非魚，安知魚之樂？」莊子曰：「子非我，安知我不知魚之樂？」惠子曰：「我非子，固不知子矣；子固非魚也，子之不知魚之樂，全矣！」
passages.note_en: Huizi’s reply is a neat piece of reasoning. He accepts Zhuangzi’s premise, that one being cannot know another’s mind, and shows that it yields his own conclusion. The word quán, “complete,” is a logician’s term: the proof is finished. Notice, though, what he has conceded on the way. To argue at all he had to understand what Zhuangzi meant, and he never doubts that Zhuangzi is in some state of mind about the fish.
passages.note_zh: 惠子的回答是一段俐落的推理。他接受了莊子的前提（一個存在者無法知道另一個的心），然後指出由它推得出自己的結論。「全」是名家的用語：證明完成了。不過請留意他一路上讓出了什麼。他要能夠論辯，就必須先懂得莊子的意思；而他從頭到尾都沒有懷疑，莊子對於那些魚是處在某種心理狀態裡的。

passages.ref: Zhuangzi 17, the debate on the Hao (second half)
passages.en: Zhuangzi said, “Let us go back to the root of this. When you said, ‘How do you know the happiness of fish?’ you asked me because you already knew that I knew it. I know it from above the Hao.”
passages.zh: 莊子曰：「請循其本。子曰『汝安知魚樂』云者，既已知吾知之而問我。我知之濠上也。」
passages.note_en: Readers have always divided over this ending. Some hold that Zhuangzi loses the argument and escapes with a pun on ān, which can mean “how” or “where.” Others hold that the pun is the point. Huizi asked for a proof, as though knowledge of another creature had to be reached by inference from outside. Zhuangzi names a place. His knowing happened there, in the company of the fish and of his friend, and it was already under way before the question of proof was raised. The passage gives no theory. It leaves two ways of standing on a bridge.
passages.note_zh: 對這個結尾，讀者向來分成兩派。有些人認為莊子輸了論證，靠著「安」字的雙關脫身；「安」可以是「怎麼」，也可以是「哪裡」。另一些人認為，那個雙關正是重點所在。惠子要的是證明，彷彿對另一個生命的認識，必須從外面靠推論才到得了。莊子說出了一個地方。他的「知」就發生在那裡，在魚與朋友的陪伴之中；而在「證明」這個問題被提出來之前，它就已經在進行了。這段文字沒有給出理論。它留下的是站在一座橋上的兩種方式。

items.o_en: This is not a real problem. Nobody doubts that other people have minds, and a doubt that no one can feel is not worth discussing.
items.o_zh: 這不是真的問題。沒有人懷疑別人有心；一個誰也感受不到的懷疑，不值得討論。
items.r_en: The question was never whether we believe it. It is what entitles us to, and the answer is needed wherever the belief runs out. We are certain about our friends and quite uncertain about fish, insects, the unresponsive patient, and the machine. A person who cannot say what grounds the easy cases has nothing to go on in the hard ones.
items.r_zh: 問題從來不在於我們相不相信。問題在於：是什麼讓我們有資格相信？而凡是這個信念用盡的地方，都需要這個答案。我們對朋友很確定，對魚、昆蟲、沒有反應的病人、機器卻相當不確定。一個說不出簡單情況的根據是什麼的人，在困難的情況裡就無所依憑。

items.o_en: Neuroscience will settle it. Once we know which brain processes go with consciousness, we can simply check whether a creature has them.
items.o_zh: 神經科學會解決這個問題。一旦我們知道哪些腦部過程與意識相伴，我們只要檢查某個生物有沒有那些過程就行了。
items.r_en: The method depends on the thing in question. We find out which brain processes go with experience by asking human subjects what they experience and trusting their reports. That gives us the signs of consciousness in creatures like us. Applying them to an octopus, whose nervous system is arranged on a different plan, or to a machine with no neurons, is once more an argument from analogy, and the question of how far the analogy holds is the original problem.
items.r_zh: 這個方法依賴的正是有待解決的東西。我們是靠著詢問人類受試者經驗到什麼、並且信任他們的報告，才找出哪些腦部過程與經驗相伴的。那給了我們「像我們這樣的生物」身上的意識徵象。把這些徵象用到章魚（牠的神經系統是照另一套藍圖安排的），或用到一台沒有神經元的機器上，就又是一個類比論證了；而類比能延伸多遠，正是原來的那個問題。

items.o_en: If something behaves in every respect as though it had feelings, there is nothing further to ask. To have a mind is to behave in those ways.
items.o_zh: 如果某個東西在每一方面都表現得好像有感受，就沒有什麼可以再問的了。有心，就是那樣表現。
items.r_en: This is behaviorism, and its attraction is that it makes other minds knowable. The standard reply is that it gets one’s own case wrong. When I am in pain, I am aware of more than a tendency to groan, and a trained actor can produce the behavior without the pain while a paralyzed patient has the pain without the behavior. The view survives in a subtler form, functionalism, which identifies a mental state with its whole causal role inside a system. Whether the right organization is enough, whatever it is made of, is the question now being asked about machines.
items.r_zh: 這是行為主義；它吸引人的地方，是讓他心變得可知。標準的回應是：它把一個人自己的情況弄錯了。我在痛的時候，我覺察到的不只是一種想呻吟的傾向；而一位受過訓練的演員可以做出那些行為卻沒有痛，一位癱瘓的病人有痛卻沒有那些行為。這個看法以一種更細緻的形式存活下來，就是功能論：它把一個心理狀態，等同於它在一個系統之內的整個因果角色。只要組織方式對了，不管是什麼材料做的，是否就夠了？這正是現在針對機器在問的問題。

said.claim: “Be kind, for everyone you meet is fighting a hard battle.” (Plato)
said.claim_zh: 「要仁慈，因為你遇見的每個人都在打一場艱苦的仗。」（柏拉圖）
said.verdict_zh: 一位蘇格蘭牧師，1890 年代
said.en: The sentence is found nowhere in Plato. Researchers have traced it to the Scottish minister and novelist John Watson, who wrote under the name Ian Maclaren, in the form “Be pitiful, for every man is fighting a hard battle.” It was credited to Plato and to Philo of Alexandria only in the later twentieth century. It belongs in this lesson all the same, since it states the practical conclusion many people draw from the problem of other minds: you cannot see what the person in front of you is carrying, so assume that it is heavy.
said.zh: 柏拉圖的著作裡找不到這句話。研究者把它追溯到蘇格蘭牧師兼小說家約翰・華森（筆名伊恩・麥克拉倫），原來的形式是：「要有憐憫，因為每個人都在打一場艱苦的仗。」直到二十世紀後期，它才被歸到柏拉圖與亞歷山卓的斐洛名下。儘管如此，它還是屬於這一課，因為它說出了許多人從他心問題得出的實際結論：你看不見眼前這個人背負著什麼，所以就當它很重吧。

terms.d_en: The problem of how one can know that others have experiences, and what those experiences are like.
terms.d_zh: 一個人如何能知道別人有經驗，以及那些經驗是什麼樣子的問題。

terms.d_en: The inference that others have minds because their bodies and behavior resemble mine.
terms.d_zh: 由於別人的身體與行為跟我的相似，而推論他們有心。

terms.o: L. qualis ‘of what kind’; singular quale
terms.d_en: The felt qualities of experience, such as the way red looks or pain feels.
terms.d_zh: 經驗被感受到的性質，例如紅色看起來的樣子、痛感覺起來的樣子。

terms.d_en: The view that everything that exists is physical, so that a complete physical description would leave nothing out.
terms.d_zh: 主張一切存在的東西都是物理的，因此一份完整的物理描述不會漏掉任何東西。

terms.d_en: Jackson’s argument that Mary learns a non-physical fact on first seeing color.
terms.d_zh: 傑克森的論證：瑪麗第一次看見顏色時，學到了一個非物理的事實。

terms.d_en: The view that only one’s own mind exists, or can be known to exist.
terms.d_zh: 主張只有自己的心存在，或只有自己的心能被知道存在。

terms.d_en: The view that to be in a mental state is to behave, or be disposed to behave, in certain ways.
terms.d_zh: 主張處於某種心理狀態，就是以某些方式行動，或傾向於那樣行動。

terms.d_en: The view that a mental state is defined by its causal role, whatever material carries it out.
terms.d_zh: 主張心理狀態是由它的因果角色界定的，不管由什麼材料來實現。

vocab.eg: You hear the cry, and you wince.
vocab.eg_zh: 你聽見那聲叫喊，自己也跟著縮了一下。

vocab.eg: A fact about an experience that is closed to you.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個關乎對你關閉的經驗的事實。

vocab.eg: They reply appositely to whatever is said to them.
vocab.eg_zh: 不管對它們說什麼，它們都能恰當地回應。

vocab.eg: Hats and coats, which could conceal automata.
vocab.eg_zh: 帽子與外套，底下藏的可能是自動機。

vocab.eg: An objective description leaves exactly that out.
vocab.eg_zh: 客觀的描述漏掉的恰恰就是這個。

vocab.eg: Huizi pressed his advantage.
vocab.eg_zh: 惠子乘勝追擊。

vocab.eg: His last line turns on the Chinese word ān.
vocab.eg_zh: 他的最後一句，關鍵在「安」這個字。

vocab.eg: A being that is itself alive and at ease.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個自己也活著、也自在的存在者。

vocab.eg: Behavior has come apart from the usual signs.
vocab.eg_zh: 行為跟通常的徵象脫了鉤。

vocab.eg: He has nothing to go on in the hard cases.
vocab.eg_zh: 在困難的情況裡，他就無所依憑。

quiz.q: What is the main weakness of the argument from analogy?
options: It generalizes from a single case, my own, and the conclusion can never be checked.
It assumes that bodies do not exist.
It applies only to animals.
It was invented too recently.

quiz.q: Why did Nagel choose bats?
options: They surely have experience, yet they perceive by a sense we lack.
They are the most intelligent animals.
They cannot feel pain.
They are easy to study in a laboratory.

quiz.q: What is Mary supposed to lack before she leaves the room?
options: Knowledge of what it is like to see red.
Knowledge of the wavelength of red light.
The ability to read.
A working visual system.

quiz.q: What is the point of Wittgenstein’s beetle in the box?
options: A private object that no one else can inspect could play no part in the meaning of a public word.
Insects have no feelings.
Everyone’s experience is exactly alike.
Boxes should be kept closed.

quiz.q: How does Zhuangzi first answer Huizi?
options: By showing that Huizi’s objection relies on knowing something about Zhuangzi’s mind.
By proving that fish have nervous systems.
By admitting that he does not know.
By changing the subject to politics.

write.en: Describe a time when you were sure what someone else was feeling and turned out to be wrong. What had you relied on?
write.zh: 描述一次你很確定別人的感受、結果卻弄錯了的經驗。你當時依據的是什麼？

write.en: Who wins the debate on the Hao, Zhuangzi or Huizi? Defend your answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 濠梁之辯，是莊子贏還是惠子贏？用大約 150 個英文字為你的答案辯護。

write.en: Suppose a machine tells you, consistently and in detail, that it is suffering. What evidence would persuade you that it is? What evidence would persuade you that it is not?
write.zh: 假設一台機器前後一致、而且很詳細地告訴你它在受苦。什麼樣的證據會說服你「它是」？什麼樣的證據會說服你「它不是」？

paras.en: The Buddha uses the argument from analogy, and he uses it for a different purpose. “All tremble at the rod, all fear death,” says the Dhammapada. “Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.” The Pali is attānaṃ upamaṃ katvā, literally “having made oneself the comparison.” In another discourse he teaches householders to reason in this way: I want to live and do not want to die, and others are the same; “the thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.” Mill offered the analogy as a proof that other minds exist, and as a proof it is weak. The Buddha offers it as a practice. He takes the existence of other beings’ suffering for granted and asks his hearers to keep turning their attention to it until it weighs with them as their own does. The later tradition calls the result the equality of self and other.
paras.zh: 佛陀也用類比論證，只是用在不同的目的上。《法句經》說：「一切皆懼刀杖，一切皆畏死。以己為喻，不殺、不教他殺。」巴利文是 attānaṃ upamaṃ katvā，字面是「以自己作為比喻」。在另一部經裡，他教在家人這樣推想：我想活、不想死，別人也一樣；「我所不喜歡的事，別人也不喜歡。」彌爾提出類比，是當作「他心存在」的證明；作為證明，它是弱的。佛陀提出它，是當作一種修習。他把其他眾生的苦當作既定的事實，然後要聽的人一再把注意力轉向它，直到它在他們心裡的分量，跟自己的苦一樣重。後來的傳統把這個結果稱為「自他平等」。

paras.en: Buddhist philosophers also met the skeptical problem head-on. The Yogācāra school held that what we experience is only mind, and its opponents replied that it must then deny that other minds exist. In the seventh century Dharmakīrti answered in a short treatise, the Proof of Other Mindstreams, and his proof is Mill’s: I observe that my own speech and action are preceded by intention, and I infer the same of speech and action that are not mine. Four centuries later Ratnakīrti argued that, on Yogācāra principles, the inference fails. The tradition also claims that the gap can be crossed directly. The early texts list knowledge of others’ minds among the powers that come with deep concentration, and compare it to seeing one’s face in a clean mirror. Whatever one makes of that claim, it shows that Buddhism never treated another mind as sealed in principle (Dharma and the West, D11 and D19).
paras.zh: 佛教哲學家也正面遇上了懷疑論的問題。瑜伽行派主張我們所經驗的唯是心識，反對者就回應：那麼它必須否認他心存在。七世紀，法稱在一篇短論《成他相續論》裡回答了；而他的證明就是彌爾的那一個：我觀察到自己的言語與行動之前有意圖，於是推論那些不屬於我的言語與行動也是如此。四個世紀之後，寶稱論證：照瑜伽行派的原則，這個推論不成立。這個傳統還主張，這道缺口可以直接跨過去。早期經典把「知他人心」列在深定所帶來的能力當中，並且把它比作在乾淨的鏡子裡看見自己的臉。不管我們怎麼看待這個主張，它顯示佛教從來沒有把另一個心當成原則上密封的（佛法與西方哲學 D11、D19）。

terms: the equality of self and other

further.t: Thomas Nagel, “What Is It Like to Be a Bat?” The Philosophical Review 83 (1974)
further.n_en: Sixteen pages; one of the most cited papers in the philosophy of mind.
further.n_zh: 十六頁；心靈哲學裡被引用最多的論文之一。

further.t: Frank Jackson, “Epiphenomenal Qualia,” The Philosophical Quarterly 32 (1982)
further.n_en: The source of Mary’s room.
further.n_zh: 瑪麗的房間的出處。

further.t: René Descartes, Discourse on the Method, Part V
further.n_en: The two tests for telling a machine from a human being.
further.n_zh: 分辨機器與人的兩項檢驗。

further.t: Zhuangzi, chapter 17, “Autumn Floods”
further.n_en: The debate on the Hao is its last paragraph.
further.n_zh: 濠梁之辯是這一篇的最後一段。

further.t: Peter Godfrey-Smith, Other Minds: The Octopus, the Sea, and the Deep Origins of Consciousness (2016)
further.n_en: A philosopher who dives with octopuses.
further.n_zh: 一位跟章魚一起潛水的哲學家。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Other Minds”

lessons.title: Can a Machine Think?
lessons.blurb_en: Turing’s imitation game, Leibniz’s mill, a mechanical performer at the court of King Mu, and a room in which you will hold a conversation in a language you cannot read.
lessons.blurb_zh: 圖靈的模仿遊戲、萊布尼茲的磨坊、周穆王宮廷裡的機關倡者，還有一個房間：你會在裡面用一種你看不懂的語言，跟人對話一場。
lessons.big_en: The question hides three others: whether a machine can do what thinkers do, whether it understands what it is doing, and whether it feels anything. They come apart, and most confusion about artificial intelligence comes from answering one of them and believing one has answered another.
lessons.big_zh: 這個問題底下藏著另外三個：機器能不能做到思考者做的事？它懂不懂自己在做什麼？它有沒有任何感受？這三者是分得開的；關於人工智慧的混亂，多半來自回答了其中一個，卻以為自己回答了另一個。

essay.h_en: The question Turing declined to answer

paras.en: In 1950 the English mathematician Alan Turing opened a paper with the sentence “I propose to consider the question, ‘Can machines think?’” He then declined to consider it. The words “machine” and “think,” he said, are too vague for the question to be settled by argument, and he replaced it with a test. An interrogator exchanges typed messages with two hidden parties, a human being and a machine, and must decide which is which. If the machine is taken for the human about as often as a human would be, it has passed. Turing called this the imitation game. He expected machines to play it well within fifty years, and he made a second prediction that has attracted less notice: “at the end of the century the use of words and general educated opinion will have altered so much that one will be able to speak of machines thinking without expecting to be contradicted.”
paras.zh: 1950 年，英國數學家圖靈用這樣一句話為一篇論文開頭：「我打算考慮這個問題：『機器能思考嗎？』」接著他就不肯考慮它了。他說，「機器」與「思考」這兩個詞太模糊，這個問題沒辦法靠論證解決；他用一個測驗取代了它。一位提問者用打字的訊息，跟兩個藏起來的對象交談，一個是人，一個是機器，然後必須判定誰是誰。如果機器被當成人的頻率，跟一個人被當成人的頻率差不多，它就通過了。圖靈稱之為「模仿遊戲」。他預期五十年內機器就能把這個遊戲玩得很好；他還做了第二個比較少人注意的預測：「到本世紀末，字詞的用法與一般受過教育者的意見將會改變到這個地步：人們談論機器在思考，而不必預期會遭到反駁。」

paras.en: The idea behind the test was three centuries old. “Reason,” wrote Thomas Hobbes in 1651, “is nothing but Reckoning (that is, Adding and Substracting)” of the consequences of names. If thinking is calculation, then anything that calculates thinks, and what it is made of is irrelevant. Leibniz, who built one of the first machines that could multiply, dreamed of a notation in which every dispute could be settled as accountants settle theirs: “Let us calculate.” The modern version of the idea is called functionalism. A mental state, it says, is defined by what it does, by its causes and effects within a system, in the way that a program is defined by its steps and can run on machines of quite different construction. On this view the mind stands to the brain as software stands to hardware, and a suitably programmed computer would not merely imitate thinking. It would think.
paras.zh: 這個測驗背後的想法，已經有三個世紀之久。霍布斯在 1651 年寫道：「理性不過就是計算（也就是加與減）」，計算的是名稱之間的推論。如果思考就是計算，那麼任何會計算的東西都在思考，而它是什麼材料做的並不相干。萊布尼茲造出了最早能做乘法的機器之一；他夢想有一套記號，讓每一場爭論都可以像會計師解決帳目那樣解決：「我們來算一算吧。」這個想法的現代版本叫作功能論。它說，一個心理狀態是由它「做什麼」來界定的，也就是由它在一個系統之內的原因與結果來界定；就像一個程式是由它的步驟界定的，可以在構造完全不同的機器上執行。照這個看法，心靈之於腦，就像軟體之於硬體；而一台程式寫得恰當的電腦，就不只是在模仿思考。它是在思考。

essay.h_en: The performer at King Mu’s court

paras.en: The opposite intuition is as old. The Daoist book Liezi tells how an artificer named Yan Shi presented King Mu of Zhou with a performer he had made. It walked, bowed, and looked about, “truly a human being.” When its chin was touched it sang in tune, and when its hand was lifted it danced in time. The king took it for a real person, until at the end of the show it winked at his concubines. He was furious and would have had the maker executed on the spot. Yan Shi at once took the figure apart, and it proved to be an assembly of leather, wood, glue, and lacquer, colored white, black, red, and blue. Every organ was there. The king removed the heart, and the mouth could not speak. He removed the liver, and the eyes could not see. Delighted, he asked: “Can human skill really equal the work of the Maker of things?” The story records the two reactions people still have. While the performance lasts we see a person, and when the case is opened we see parts.
paras.zh: 相反的直覺一樣古老。道家的《列子》記載，一位名叫偃師的工匠，把自己造的一個倡者獻給周穆王。它行走、俯仰、顧盼，「信人也」。碰它的下巴，它就合著音律唱歌；抬它的手，它就應著節拍起舞。穆王把它當成真人，直到表演快結束時，它對王的侍妾拋了個眼色。王大怒，當場就要殺掉偃師。偃師立刻把那個人形拆開；原來它是皮革、木頭、膠、漆拼合而成的，塗著白、黑、紅、青的顏色。每一個器官都齊全。王拿掉它的心，口就不能說話；拿掉它的肝，眼就不能看。王高興了，問道：「人之巧乃可與造化者同功乎？」這個故事記下了人們至今仍有的兩種反應。表演進行的時候，我們看見一個人；外殼打開的時候，我們看見零件。

paras.en: Leibniz gave the second reaction the form of an argument, and he gave it against his own machines. Suppose, he wrote in 1714, that there were a machine “so constructed as to think, feel, and have perception.” Imagine it enlarged until one could walk into it “as into a mill.” Inside “we should, on examining its interior, find only parts which work one upon another, and never anything by which to explain a perception.” A century later Ada Lovelace, describing the Analytical Engine that Charles Babbage had designed, added a different limit. The engine, she wrote, “has no pretensions whatever to originate anything. It can do whatever we know how to order it to perform.” Leibniz’s objection concerns experience and Lovelace’s concerns originality. They have been confused with each other ever since.
paras.zh: 萊布尼茲把第二種反應寫成了論證，而且他是對著自己造的機器提出的。他在 1714 年寫道：假設有一台機器，「被造得能夠思考、感受、擁有知覺」。想像它被放大，大到人可以走進去，「像走進一座磨坊」。在裡面，「我們檢視它的內部，只會發現一個推動一個的零件，永遠找不到任何可以用來解釋一個知覺的東西」。一個世紀之後，勒芙蕾絲在描述巴貝奇設計的分析機時，加上了另一種限制。她寫道，這台機器「絲毫沒有『創始』任何事物的自命。凡是我們知道怎麼命令它去做的事，它都能做」。萊布尼茲的反駁關乎經驗，勒芙蕾絲的反駁關乎原創。此後這兩者一直被混在一起。

paras.en: In 1980 the American philosopher John Searle turned the mill into a room and put himself inside it. He imagined a program that passes the Turing test in Chinese, a language of which he knew not a word. He is locked in a room with baskets of Chinese characters and a rule book in English. Slips of paper covered in characters are pushed under the door. He looks up their shapes in the book, which tells him which characters to push back. To the people outside, the replies are those of a fluent speaker. Searle has done everything the computer does: he has run the program. And he understands nothing. He does not know whether the slips are about the weather or about his mother. His conclusion is that carrying out a program, however good, is not sufficient for understanding. A program is defined by its syntax, the rules for moving symbols according to their shapes. Understanding requires semantics, knowing what the symbols mean, and no amount of shuffling will supply it.
paras.zh: 1980 年，美國哲學家瑟爾把那座磨坊變成了一個房間，並且把自己放了進去。他設想有一個程式，用中文通過了圖靈測驗；而中文他一個字也不懂。他被鎖在一個房間裡，裡面有一籃一籃的中文字，以及一本用英文寫的規則書。寫滿了字的紙條從門縫底下塞進來。他在書裡查那些字的形狀，書告訴他該把哪些字塞回去。對外面的人來說，那些回覆是一個流利的說話者寫的。瑟爾做了電腦所做的一切：他執行了那個程式。而他什麼也不懂。他不知道那些紙條談的是天氣，還是他的母親。他的結論是：執行一個程式，不管程式多好，並不足以構成理解。程式是由它的「語法」界定的，也就是依照符號的形狀搬動符號的規則。理解需要「語意」，也就是知道那些符號是什麼意思；而不管怎麼搬來搬去，都搬不出語意來。

paras.en: Searle chose Chinese because he could not read it. A reader who can should substitute a language that is closed to him, and the exercise below does so.
paras.zh: 瑟爾選中文，是因為他看不懂。看得懂中文的讀者，應該換成一種對自己關閉的語言；下面的練習就是這樣做的。

paras.en: The paper drew more replies than almost any other in the field. The systems reply grants that the man does not understand and says that he is only one component: the understanding belongs to the whole system of man, book, and baskets, as it belongs to a brain and to no single neuron.
