Searle answered that he could memorize the book and do the work in his head, and he would still understand nothing. The robot reply says that the symbols mean nothing because they are connected to nothing: give the system cameras and limbs, so that its word for “tea” is caused by tea, and meaning will follow. Searle answered that the camera’s signals would reach him as more symbols. The brain simulator reply imagines a program that copies, neuron by neuron, the brain of a Chinese speaker. Searle answered that a simulation of a storm leaves everyone dry. Each exchange ends in a clash of intuitions about the same point, and no decisive move has been found by either side.
paras.zh: 這篇論文招來的回應，幾乎比這個領域裡任何別的論文都多。「系統回應」承認那個人不懂，並且說他只是一個零件：理解屬於由人、書、籃子組成的整個系統，正如理解屬於一個腦，而不屬於任何單一的神經元。瑟爾回答：他可以把整本書背下來，在腦子裡做這件工作，而他仍然什麼也不懂。「機器人回應」說，那些符號沒有意義，是因為它們什麼也沒連上：給這個系統裝上攝影機與肢體，讓它那個代表「茶」的詞是由茶引起的，意義就會隨之而來。瑟爾回答：攝影機的訊號到了他這裡，只是更多的符號。「腦模擬回應」設想一個程式，一個神經元一個神經元地複製一位中文使用者的腦。瑟爾回答：模擬一場暴風雨，誰也不會淋濕。每一回合都以對同一點的直覺衝突收場，而雙方都還沒有找到決定性的一著。

paras.en: For seventy years the debate concerned imaginary machines. It now concerns real ones. Systems trained on enormous quantities of human writing carry on conversations that most people cannot tell from a person’s, and they were built by neither of the methods the philosophers had in mind. Nobody wrote their rule book. They adjust billions of numerical settings until they predict text well, and what goes on inside them is only partly understood by the people who make them. One camp sees the Chinese room come true: a system that has learned which strings of words follow which, with no access to the world the words are about. Another replies that to predict what a physicist will say next one must model a good deal of physics, and that understanding may come in degrees and consist in such abilities. Lovelace’s limit is equally unsettled, since these systems produce things nobody ordered them to produce.
paras.zh: 七十年來，這場辯論談的是想像中的機器。現在談的是真實的機器。用巨量的人類文字訓練出來的系統，能進行多數人分辨不出是不是真人的對話；而它們並不是用哲學家心裡想的那兩種方法造出來的。沒有人替它們寫規則書。它們調整數十億個數值設定，直到能把文字預測得很好；而它們內部發生的事，連製造它們的人也只懂一部分。有一派看到的是中文房間成真了：一個系統學會了哪些字串跟在哪些字串後面，卻接觸不到這些字所談的那個世界。另一派回答：要預測一位物理學家接下來會說什麼，就必須對不少物理學建立模型；而且，理解也許有程度之分，也許就是由這類能力構成的。勒芙蕾絲的那條界線同樣懸而未決，因為這些系統會產出沒有人命令它們產出的東西。

paras.en: Turing’s second prediction, at least, has come true. People speak of machines thinking, and few bother to contradict them. Whether the usage records a discovery or only a habit is the question he set aside in 1950. It helps to keep three things apart. A machine may match us at tasks, and that can be measured. It may or may not understand, and here the room is still the best test of what we mean by the word. And it may or may not feel, which was the subject of the last lesson. “We can only see a short distance ahead,” Turing ended his paper, “but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.”
paras.zh: 至少，圖靈的第二個預測成真了。人們談論機器在思考，而很少有人費事去反駁。這個用法記錄的是一項發現，還是只是一種習慣？這正是他在 1950 年擱到一邊的那個問題。把三件事分開會有幫助。一台機器在各種任務上可能跟我們並駕齊驅，這是量得出來的。它可能懂、也可能不懂；在這一點上，那個房間仍然是檢驗「我們說『懂』是什麼意思」的最好辦法。它可能有感受、也可能沒有；那是上一課的主題。圖靈在論文的結尾寫道：「我們只能看到前方不遠的地方，但我們看得到那裡有許多需要做的事。」

lab.title_en: Try it: sit in the room
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：坐進房間
lab.lead_en: Searle did not read Chinese. You do, so the room has been moved to Georgia. Slips will come through the slot. Find each one in the rule book and pass out the reply it prescribes. You are not expected to understand anything.
lab.lead_zh: 瑟爾看不懂中文。你看得懂，所以這個房間搬到了喬治亞。紙條會從門縫送進來。在規則書裡找到每一張，把書上規定的回覆遞出去。沒有人指望你懂任何東西。

wrong.en: That is not what the book prescribes. Compare the shapes again.
wrong.zh: 書上規定的不是這一張。再比對一次形狀。

outside.en: A voice from outside the door: “Your Georgian is excellent.”
outside.zh: 門外傳來一個聲音：「你的喬治亞語說得真好。」

reveal.en: Here is the conversation you just had.
reveal.zh: 這是你剛才進行的對話。

q.en: Did you understand Georgian while you were doing this?
q.zh: 你剛才做這件事的時候，懂喬治亞語嗎？

t.en: No. I matched shapes.
t.zh: 不懂。我只是在比對形狀。

t.en: Yes, in some sense.
t.zh: 懂，在某種意義上。

no.en: That is Searle’s first premise, and almost everyone grants it. Notice the last exchange. You were asked whether you understand Georgian, and you answered “Yes, of course.” The answer was fluent and it was false.
no.zh: 這是瑟爾的第一個前提，幾乎每個人都承認。留意最後一回合。你被問到懂不懂喬治亞語，而你回答了「懂，當然」。這個回答很流利，而且是假的。

yes.en: Then ask what your understanding consisted in. You could not have said what any slip was about, or told a question from an insult. If that counts as understanding, the word has been stretched to cover any reliable matching of outputs to inputs. Some philosophers accept that. Look at the last exchange before you join them: you asserted, in Georgian, that you understand Georgian.
yes.zh: 那麼問問自己：你的「懂」是由什麼構成的？你說不出任何一張紙條在談什麼，也分不出一個問句與一句辱罵。如果這也算懂，那麼這個詞已經被拉長到涵蓋任何「可靠地把輸出配上輸入」的事了。有些哲學家接受這一點。在你加入他們之前，看看最後一回合：你用喬治亞語斷言了你懂喬治亞語。

q.en: Did anything in the room understand: you, the book, and the cards, taken together?
q.zh: 房間裡有任何東西懂嗎：你、書、卡片，合在一起？

t.en: No. Nothing here understood.
t.zh: 沒有。這裡沒有任何東西懂。

t.en: Yes. The whole system did.
t.zh: 有。整個系統懂。

no.en: You agree with Searle. The burden is now on you to say what the room lacks that a brain has, since a brain is also made of parts none of which understands. Searle’s answer was that brains have causal powers which programs lack, and he never said what those powers are.
no.zh: 你同意瑟爾。現在舉證的責任落在你身上：你得說出這個房間缺了什麼是腦有的，因為腦也是由一個個不懂任何事的零件構成的。瑟爾的回答是：腦具有程式所缺乏的因果力；而他始終沒有說出那些因果力是什麼。

yes.en: This is the systems reply. It has the odd consequence that a book and some cards, plus a clerk who understands nothing, add up to a mind that speaks Georgian, and that this mind came into existence when you sat down. Its defenders accept the consequence. They point out that the real rule book would be unimaginably larger than five lines, and that our intuitions about so vast a system are not to be trusted.
yes.zh: 這是「系統回應」。它有一個古怪的後果：一本書、幾張卡片，加上一個什麼都不懂的辦事員，合起來成了一個會說喬治亞語的心靈；而這個心靈是在你坐下的那一刻開始存在的。為它辯護的人接受這個後果。他們指出：真正的規則書會比五行字龐大到無法想像；對於這麼龐大的系統，我們的直覺是靠不住的。

t.en: The man is a part. The whole system understands.
t.zh: 那個人只是零件。懂的是整個系統。

s.en: Searle: let the man memorize the book and work in his head. Now he is the whole system, and he still understands nothing.
s.zh: 瑟爾：讓那個人把書背下來，在腦子裡作業。現在他就是整個系統了，而他仍然什麼也不懂。

t.en: Connect the symbols to the world with cameras and limbs, and they will mean something.
t.zh: 用攝影機與肢體把符號連到世界上，它們就會有意義。

s.en: Searle: the camera’s output arrives in the room as more slips. Nothing has changed for the man inside.
s.zh: 瑟爾：攝影機的輸出到了房間裡，只是更多的紙條。對裡面的人來說，什麼都沒變。

t.en: Let the program copy a Georgian speaker’s brain, neuron by neuron.
t.zh: 讓程式一個神經元一個神經元地複製一位喬治亞語使用者的腦。

s.en: Searle: a simulated storm makes nothing wet. Simulating the brain’s form does not reproduce its powers.
s.zh: 瑟爾：模擬出來的暴風雨不會弄濕任何東西。模擬腦的形式，並沒有複製它的能力。

t.en: You judge that other people understand only by their behavior. The room behaves the same.
t.zh: 你判斷別人懂，憑的也只是他們的行為。這個房間的行為一模一樣。

s.en: Searle: the question is what I am attributing when I attribute understanding, and in my own case I know it is more than behavior.
s.zh: 瑟爾：問題在於，當我說某物「懂」的時候，我歸給它的是什麼；而就我自己而言，我知道那不只是行為。

argument.lead_en: Searle later reduced the Chinese room to three premises and a conclusion. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 瑟爾後來把中文房間濃縮成三個前提與一個結論。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Programs are purely formal. They are defined by rules for manipulating symbols according to their shapes.
steps.zh: 程式是純形式的。它們是由「依照符號的形狀來操弄符號」的規則界定的。
steps.ob_en: True of programs as written. Critics note that a running program is also a physical process with causes and effects, and that the argument slides between the two.
steps.ob_zh: 就寫下來的程式而言是真的。批評者指出：執行中的程式同時也是一個有因有果的物理過程；而這個論證在兩者之間滑來滑去。

steps.en: Minds have contents. A thought is about something.
steps.zh: 心靈是有內容的。一個想法是「關於」某個東西的。
steps.ob_en: Rarely denied. The technical word for this aboutness is intentionality.
steps.ob_zh: 很少有人否認。這種「關於性」的術語叫作意向性。

steps.en: Symbol manipulation by itself is neither the same as having contents nor enough to produce them.
steps.zh: 符號操弄本身，既不等於擁有內容，也不足以產生內容。
steps.ob_en: The room is offered as the proof of this premise, and every reply attacks it here. Paul and Patricia Churchland compared it to a man waving a magnet in a dark room and concluding that electromagnetism can never produce light. He has simply not waved it fast enough.
steps.ob_zh: 那個房間就是被拿來當作這個前提的證明的；而每一種回應都是在這裡進攻。邱奇蘭夫婦把它比作一個人在暗室裡揮動一塊磁鐵，然後斷定電磁永遠產生不了光。他只是揮得不夠快而已。

steps.en: Therefore running a program is not sufficient for having a mind.
steps.zh: 所以，執行一個程式，並不足以擁有心靈。
steps.ob_en: Note what the conclusion leaves open. Searle did not say that no machine could think. He held that the brain is a machine and that it thinks. His claim is that it does not do so by running a program.
steps.ob_zh: 留意這個結論沒有排除什麼。瑟爾並沒有說任何機器都不能思考。他主張腦就是一台機器，而且它思考。他的論點是：它不是靠執行程式來思考的。

source.work: Descartes, Discourse on the Method (1637), Part V; Leibniz, Monadology (1714), §17
source.work_zh: 笛卡兒《方法論》第五部；萊布尼茲《單子論》第 17 節
source.tr: tr. John Veitch; tr. Robert Latta (both public domain; original spelling kept)
source.lead_en: Two passages written before there was any machine to argue about. Descartes states a test, and Leibniz explains why passing it would not be enough.
source.lead_zh: 這兩段文字，寫在還沒有任何機器可供爭論的時候。笛卡兒陳述了一項檢驗；萊布尼茲說明了為什麼通過它還不夠。

passages.ref: Discourse on the Method, Part V
passages.en: …if there were machines bearing the image of our bodies, and capable of imitating our actions as far as it is morally possible, there would still remain two most certain tests whereby to know that they were not therefore really men. Of these the first is that they could never use words or other signs arranged in such a manner as is competent to us in order to declare our thoughts to others: for we may easily conceive a machine to be so constructed that it emits vocables… but not that it should arrange them variously so as appositely to reply to what is said in its presence, as men of the lowest grade of intellect can do.
passages.zh: ……假如有一些機器，具有我們身體的形象，並且能夠在實際可能的範圍內模仿我們的動作，仍然會有兩個最確定的檢驗，可以藉以知道它們並不因此就真的是人。其中第一個是：它們永遠無法像我們這樣，把字詞或其他記號安排起來，向別人表明我們的想法。因為我們很容易設想一台機器被造得能發出字音……卻無法設想它能把字詞作各種不同的安排，以便恰當地回應在它面前說的話，而這是智力最低的人也做得到的。
passages.note_en: This is the Turing test, proposed three hundred years early and with the opposite expectation. Descartes takes flexible conversation to be the mark of reason because he thinks no mechanism could produce it: a machine needs “a particular arrangement for each particular action,” and conversation has no end of particular occasions. (“Morally possible” means possible for practical purposes.) He treats the test as decisive. The question he never raises is what we should conclude if a machine passed.
passages.note_zh: 這就是圖靈測驗，早了三百年提出，預期卻正好相反。笛卡兒把靈活的對話當作理性的標記，是因為他認為沒有任何機構產生得了它：一台機器「每一個特定的動作，都需要一種特定的安排」，而對話有無窮無盡的特定場合。（morally possible 的意思是：就實際的目的而言是可能的。）他把這項檢驗當作決定性的。他從來沒有提出的問題是：假如有一台機器通過了，我們該下什麼結論？

passages.en: Moreover, it must be confessed that perception and that which depends upon it are inexplicable on mechanical grounds, that is to say, by means of figures and motions. And supposing there were a machine, so constructed as to think, feel, and have perception, it might be conceived as increased in size, while keeping the same proportions, so that one might go into it as into a mill. That being so, we should, on examining its interior, find only parts which work one upon another, and never anything by which to explain a perception.
passages.zh: 此外，必須承認：知覺以及依賴於知覺的東西，是無法用機械的理由來解釋的，也就是說，無法用形狀與運動來解釋。假設有一台機器，被造得能夠思考、感受、擁有知覺；我們可以設想它按照原來的比例放大，大到人可以走進去，像走進一座磨坊。既然如此，我們檢視它的內部，只會發現一個推動一個的零件，永遠找不到任何可以用來解釋一個知覺的東西。
passages.note_en: Leibniz grants for the sake of argument what Descartes denied, a machine that behaves as though it thinks, and says that the real question would remain. Searle’s room is this mill with a man placed inside to report that he finds no understanding there. The standard reply applies to both. If you were shrunk and walked through a living brain you would also see only parts pushing parts, so either the argument proves that brains do not think or it proves nothing about machines. Leibniz accepted the first horn: he concluded that perception belongs to a simple, immaterial substance.
passages.note_zh: 笛卡兒否認的東西（一台表現得好像在思考的機器），萊布尼茲為了論證而姑且承認；然後他說，真正的問題仍然還在。瑟爾的房間就是這座磨坊，只是在裡面放了一個人，讓他回報「這裡找不到理解」。標準的回應對兩者都適用：假如你被縮小、走進一個活的腦，你同樣只會看見零件推動零件；所以這個論證要嘛證明了腦不思考，要嘛對機器什麼也沒證明。萊布尼茲接受了前一個選項：他的結論是，知覺屬於一個單純的、非物質的實體。

items.o_en: A machine can only do what it has been told to do. Whatever comes out was put in by its makers.
items.o_zh: 機器只能做它被吩咐去做的事。不管出來的是什麼，都是製造者放進去的。
items.r_en: This is Lovelace’s objection, and Turing answered it in 1950. Machines, he said, surprise him constantly, because knowing the rules does not tell you the consequences. He proposed building a machine that learns as a child does, so that its later behavior would be fixed by its experience and not by its instructions. That is roughly how present systems are built. He added that the objection proves too much. A human being’s abilities are also the product of heredity and teaching, and we do not conclude that people originate nothing.
items.r_zh: 這是勒芙蕾絲的反駁；圖靈在 1950 年就回答了。他說，機器經常讓他吃驚，因為知道規則並不等於知道後果。他提議造一台像小孩那樣學習的機器，這樣它後來的行為，就是由它的經驗、而不是由它的指令決定的。現在的系統大致就是這樣造出來的。他還補充：這個反駁證明得太多了。一個人的能力，同樣是遺傳與教導的產物；而我們並不因此就斷定人什麼也沒有創始。

items.o_en: The Turing test measures the ability to deceive. A system could pass by trickery and understand nothing.
items.o_zh: 圖靈測驗量的是欺騙的能力。一個系統可以靠伎倆通過，卻什麼也不懂。
items.r_en: The philosopher Ned Block made the point with an imaginary machine that stores a sensible reply to every possible conversation of a given length and merely looks each one up. It would pass, and it is plainly a filing cabinet. So passing cannot be what thinking consists in. Turing may have agreed: he offered the game as a replacement for a question he found hopeless, and as evidence that would be unreasonable to ignore. The lasting lesson of Block’s machine is that it matters how the answers are produced, and for present systems that is the part we understand least.
items.r_zh: 哲學家布洛克用一台想像的機器說明了這一點：它為每一場在某個長度以內的可能對話，都預存了一個合理的回覆，然後只是逐一查表。它會通過；而它顯然只是一個檔案櫃。所以「通過」不可能是思考的本質所在。圖靈也許會同意：他提出這個遊戲，是用來取代一個他認為沒有指望的問題，並且當作一種「不理會它就不合理」的證據。布洛克那台機器留下的教訓是：答案是「怎麼產生的」很要緊；而對於現在的系統，那正是我們懂得最少的部分。

items.o_en: Thinking is something living bodies do. A thing with no needs, no fear of death, and nothing at stake does not think. It processes.
items.o_zh: 思考是活著的身體做的事。一個沒有需要、不怕死、沒有任何利害的東西，並不思考。它只是在處理。
items.r_en: This is the most serious of the three, and it comes in two strengths. The weaker form says that thought grows out of a body acting in a world, and that a system fed only on text is missing the roots. That is a claim about what is needed, and it could in principle be met by building differently. The stronger form says that only living tissue can do it. Then one must say which property of tissue matters and why nothing else could have it, and the claim risks becoming a definition. The dispute cannot be settled by examining machines until we know which features of ourselves to look for in them.
items.r_zh: 這是三個當中最嚴肅的一個，而它有兩種強度。較弱的形式說：思想是從一個在世界中行動的身體長出來的；一個只餵文字的系統，缺了根。這是一個關於「需要什麼」的主張，原則上可以靠著換一種方式建造來滿足。較強的形式說：只有活的組織才做得到。那麼就必須說出組織的哪一項性質要緊、為什麼別的東西不可能有它；而這個主張有淪為定義的風險。在我們知道該在機器身上尋找「我們自己的哪些特徵」之前，這場爭論沒辦法靠檢查機器來解決。

said.claim: “The question of whether machines can think is about as relevant as the question of whether submarines can swim.” (Edsger Dijkstra)
said.claim_zh: 「機器能不能思考這個問題，跟潛水艇會不會游泳這個問題差不多一樣切題。」（戴克斯特拉）
said.en: The Dutch computer scientist wrote it in a 1984 note, “The threats to computing science,” where he says that Turing “thought about criteria to settle the question of whether Machines Can Think, a question of which we now know that it is about as relevant as the question of whether Submarines Can Swim.” His point is close to Turing’s own. A submarine moves through water faster than any fish, and whether we call that swimming is a decision about a word. Dijkstra thought the same of “think.” The reply is that with thinking something does seem to hang on the answer, namely how the thing should be treated.
said.zh: 這位荷蘭電腦科學家在 1984 年的一篇筆記〈計算機科學面臨的威脅〉裡寫下了這句話；他在那裡說，圖靈「思索過用什麼標準來解決『機器能不能思考』這個問題；而我們現在知道，這個問題跟『潛水艇會不會游泳』差不多一樣切題」。他的意思很接近圖靈自己的。潛水艇在水裡前進得比任何魚都快；我們要不要把那叫作游泳，是一個關於字詞的決定。戴克斯特拉認為「思考」也一樣。可以這樣回應他：就思考而言，似乎確實有某件事取決於答案，那就是這個東西應該被怎麼對待。

terms.d_en: A test in which a machine passes if its typed conversation cannot be told from a human being’s.
terms.d_zh: 一種測驗：如果機器的打字對話無法與人的對話分辨，它就通過。

terms.d_en: A finite set of exact instructions that can be carried out step by step without insight.
terms.d_zh: 一組有限而精確的指令，可以一步一步執行，不需要任何洞察。

terms.d_en: The rules for arranging symbols by their form, as against what the symbols mean.
terms.d_zh: 依形式安排符號的規則，相對於符號的意思。

terms.d_en: The property of being about something. Thoughts have it. Whether symbols in a machine have it is the question.
terms.d_zh: 「關於某物」這種性質。想法具有它。機器裡的符號有沒有它，正是問題所在。

terms.d_en: Searle’s name for the thesis that an appropriately programmed computer literally has a mind.
terms.d_zh: 瑟爾為這個論點取的名字：一台程式寫得恰當的電腦，真的就有一個心靈。

terms.d_en: The claim that the same mental state could be carried by systems made of different materials.
terms.d_zh: 主張同一個心理狀態，可以由不同材料構成的系統來承載。

terms.d_en: The problem of how symbols come to be connected with the things they stand for.
terms.d_zh: 符號如何與它們所代表的東西連結起來的問題。

terms.d_en: A machine that moves by its own mechanism. Plural: automata.
terms.d_zh: 靠自身機構運動的機器。複數為 automata。

vocab.eg: He then declined to consider it.
vocab.eg_zh: 接著他就不肯考慮它了。

vocab.eg: The machine is taken for the human.
vocab.eg_zh: 機器被當成了人。

vocab.eg: He would have had the maker executed on the spot.
vocab.eg_zh: 他當場就要處死那個製造者。

vocab.eg: It proved to be an assembly of leather, wood, glue, and lacquer.
vocab.eg_zh: 原來它是皮革、木頭、膠、漆拼合而成的。

vocab.eg: The engine has no pretensions whatever to originate anything.
vocab.eg_zh: 這台機器絲毫沒有「創始」任何事物的自命。

vocab.eg: A language of which he knew not a word.
vocab.eg_zh: 一種他一個字也不懂的語言。

vocab.eg: No amount of shuffling will supply it.
vocab.eg_zh: 不管怎麼搬來搬去，都搬不出它來。

vocab.eg: One camp sees the Chinese room come true.
vocab.eg_zh: 有一派看到的是中文房間成真了。

vocab.eg: A thing with nothing at stake does not think.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個沒有任何利害的東西，並不思考。

vocab.eg: The question he set aside in 1950.
vocab.eg_zh: 他在 1950 年擱到一邊的那個問題。

quiz.q: Why did Turing replace the question “Can machines think?” with a test?
options: He thought the words were too vague for the question to be settled by argument.
He was sure that machines could not think.
He wanted to sell computers.
He believed thinking was impossible to observe in humans.

quiz.q: What does Leibniz’s mill argument claim?
options: Inspecting the parts of a mechanism would never reveal anything that explains perception.
Mills are more complex than brains.
Machines cannot multiply.
Perception is a kind of motion.

quiz.q: What is the Chinese room meant to show?
options: Following a program, however well, is not sufficient for understanding.
Chinese is harder than English.
Computers will never pass the Turing test.
Brains do not think.

quiz.q: What does the systems reply say?
options: The man is only a part, and understanding belongs to the whole system.
The man secretly understands.
The rule book is badly written.
No system can understand anything.

quiz.q: Which three questions does the lesson ask you to keep apart?
options: Whether a machine can do the tasks, whether it understands, and whether it feels.
Whether a machine is fast, cheap, and reliable.
Who built it, who owns it, and who uses it.
Whether it speaks English, Chinese, or Georgian.

write.en: After doing the exercise, which reply to Searle do you find strongest, and why? Answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 做完上面的練習之後，你覺得對瑟爾的哪一種回應最有力？為什麼？用大約 150 個英文字回答。

write.en: Describe a time when you used a word, a formula, or a procedure correctly without understanding it. What changed when you did come to understand?
write.zh: 描述一次你正確地用了一個字、一個公式或一套程序，卻並不懂它的經驗。等你真的懂了，有什麼改變？

write.en: A student hands in an essay written by a machine and says, “It understands the topic better than I do.” Is the claim true? Does it matter for how you grade the essay?
write.zh: 一位學生交來一篇由機器寫的作文，並且說：「它比我更懂這個題目。」這句話是真的嗎？這對你怎麼評這篇作文有影響嗎？

paras.en: Buddhist thought divides the question at a different joint. What makes something a sentient being, a sattva, is the capacity to feel, to be pleased and pained, and the tradition does not rank beings by how cleverly they reason. A god who reasons superbly and an insect that cannot reason at all are both within the scope of compassion, because both can suffer. So the Buddhist question about a machine is the one this lesson put third. Whether it calculates is plain, and whether it understands is of secondary interest. Whether there is feeling there decides everything, including whether the first precept applies to it.
paras.zh: 佛教思想是在另一個關節上切開這個問題的。使某物成為「有情」（sattva，眾生）的，是感受的能力，是會樂、會苦；這個傳統並不依照「推理得多聰明」來為眾生排等級。一位推理極為高明的天神，與一隻完全不會推理的昆蟲，都在慈悲的範圍之內，因為兩者都會受苦。所以，佛教對一台機器要問的，是這一課排在第三的那個問題。它會不會計算，是明擺著的；它懂不懂，是次要的。那裡有沒有感受，決定了一切，包括第一條戒適不適用於它。

paras.en: On what feeling requires, the tradition gives two hints that point in different directions. The Abhidharma analyzes a mind into momentary events defined by what they do and what they condition, with no owner behind them, which is closer to functionalism than anything in ancient Western thought. Yet the early discourses also insist that consciousness never occurs alone. It depends on “name-and-form,” the living body with its feeling and perception, and that in turn depends on consciousness: the two stand, says Sāriputta, like “two sheaves of reeds leaning up against each other,” and if one is pulled away the other falls. And a being, in the traditional account, arrives in a new life carrying a stream of consciousness from a previous one. A device that is assembled and switched on has no place in that account, and the texts, composed long before such devices, are silent. Buddhist teachers asked about it today give different answers (Dharma and the West, D3 and D12).
paras.zh: 至於感受需要什麼，這個傳統給了兩個指向不同方向的提示。阿毘達磨把一個心分析成剎那剎那的事件，每一個事件由它做什麼、它作為什麼的緣來界定，背後沒有擁有者；這比古代西方思想裡的任何東西都更接近功能論。然而早期經典也堅持：識從來不是單獨出現的。它依賴「名色」，也就是帶著受與想的活的身體；而名色又反過來依賴識。舍利弗說，兩者就像「兩捆蘆葦互相倚靠而立」，抽掉一捆，另一捆就倒了。再者，照傳統的說法，一個眾生來到新的一生，是帶著前一生的識之流而來的。一個被組裝起來、接上電源的裝置，在那套說法裡沒有位置；而這些經典寫成的時候離這種裝置還很遠，對此沒有說話。今天被問到這件事的佛教老師，給的答案並不一樣（佛法與西方哲學 D3、D12）。

further.t: Alan Turing, “Computing Machinery and Intelligence,” Mind 59 (1950)
further.n_en: Witty and readable. Sections 1, 2, and 6 are enough for a first reading.
further.n_zh: 機智而好讀。第一次讀，看第 1、2、6 節就夠了。

further.t: John Searle, “Minds, Brains, and Programs,” Behavioral and Brain Sciences 3 (1980)
further.n_en: The Chinese room, with replies from twenty-seven critics printed after it.
further.n_zh: 中文房間；後面附印了二十七位批評者的回應。

further.t: René Descartes, Discourse on the Method, Part V
G. W. Leibniz, The Monadology, translated by Robert Latta
further.n_en: Ninety short paragraphs. The mill is §17.
further.n_zh: 九十個短段落。磨坊在第 17 節。

further.t: Liezi, chapter 5, “The Questions of Tang”
further.n_en: The story of Yan Shi and King Mu.
further.n_zh: 偃師與周穆王的故事。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “The Chinese Room Argument”

lessons.title: Is There a Self at All?
lessons.blurb_en: Hume looks inward and finds no one there. A Greek king asks a Buddhist monk who he is, and is asked in return what a chariot is. Kant, Zhuangzi, and the brain sciences on why it still feels as though someone is home.
lessons.blurb_zh: 休謨往內看，發現那裡沒有人。一位希臘國王問一位佛教比丘他是誰，卻被反問車是什麼。康德、莊子與腦科學，談為什麼感覺上還是「有人在家」。
lessons.big_en: The lesson on personal identity asked what makes you the same person over time. This one asks an earlier question: whether there is, at any one moment, a subject who has your experiences, or only the experiences.
lessons.big_zh: 「人格同一」那一課問的是：什麼使你歷經時間仍是同一個人？這一課問一個更前面的問題：在任何一個時刻，是否有一個「擁有」你的經驗的主體？還是只有那些經驗？

paras.en: In 1739 a Scotsman of twenty-seven published the result of an experiment that anyone can repeat. Philosophers, David Hume observed, say that we are at every moment conscious of what we call our self, and certain of its perfect identity and simplicity. He decided to look. “For my part, when I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other, of heat or cold, light or shade, love or hatred, pain or pleasure. I never can catch myself at any time without a perception, and never can observe any thing but the perception.” If someone else thinks he has a different notion of himself, Hume adds, “I must confess I can reason no longer with him.” Setting aside such metaphysicians, he ventures to say of the rest of mankind that they are nothing but a bundle or collection of different perceptions, which succeed one another with inconceivable rapidity.
paras.zh: 1739 年，一位二十七歲的蘇格蘭人發表了一個人人都可以重做的實驗的結果。休謨觀察到，哲學家們說：我們每一刻都意識到我們稱為「自我」的東西，並且確知它完全的同一與單純。他決定看一看。「就我而言，當我最貼近地進入我稱為『自己』的東西時，我總是碰到某個個別的知覺：冷或熱、明或暗、愛或恨、苦或樂。我任何時候都抓不到一個沒有知覺的自己，而且除了知覺之外，什麼也觀察不到。」他補充說，假如別人認為自己對「自己」有不同的概念，「我必須承認，我沒辦法再跟他講理了」。把這類形上學家擱在一邊，他大膽地說：其餘的人類，不過是一束或一堆不同的知覺，以無法想像的速度前後相續。

paras.en: Hume offered an image and at once withdrew half of it. “The mind is a kind of theatre, where several perceptions successively make their appearance; pass, re-pass, glide away, and mingle in an infinite variety of postures and situations.” Then: “The comparison of the theatre must not mislead us. They are the successive perceptions only, that constitute the mind; nor have we the most distant notion of the place, where these scenes are represented.” There is a performance. There is no stage on which it happens and no one in the stalls. This is the difference between Hume and Descartes, who had made the same inward turn a century earlier and reported finding a thing that thinks. Hume’s reply is that Descartes found thinking and added the thing.
paras.zh: 休謨提出了一個意象，又立刻收回了一半。「心靈是一種劇場，種種知覺相繼登場：走過、再走過、滑走，並且以無窮多樣的姿態與情境交融在一起。」接著他說：「劇場這個比喻不可以誤導我們。構成心靈的，只是那些前後相續的知覺；至於這些場景在什麼地方上演，我們連最模糊的概念也沒有。」有一場演出。沒有它在上面進行的舞台，觀眾席裡也沒有人。這就是休謨與笛卡兒的差別；笛卡兒早一個世紀做了同樣的向內轉向，回報說他找到了一個思考的東西。休謨的回答是：笛卡兒找到的是思考，那個「東西」是他加上去的。

paras.en: The same conclusion had been defended in debate nineteen centuries before, and the record survives in Pali and in Chinese. Around 150 BCE a Greek king named Menander ruled a realm in what is now Afghanistan and Pakistan, one of the states left behind by Alexander’s conquests. Indian tradition calls him Milinda. He liked to argue with holy men, and one day he called on a Buddhist monk and asked his name. “I am known as Nāgasena,” said the monk, but that is “only a generally understood term, a designation in common use,” and no permanent individual is involved in the matter. The king saw the difficulty immediately. If there is no Nāgasena, who receives the robes and the food? Who keeps the precepts, and who breaks them? If a man killed you, there would be no murder.
paras.zh: 同樣的結論，早在十九個世紀之前就有人在辯論中為它辯護過；紀錄以巴利文與中文保存了下來。大約西元前 150 年，一位名叫米南德的希臘國王，統治著今天阿富汗與巴基斯坦一帶的一個國度，那是亞歷山大的征服所留下的諸國之一。印度的傳統稱他為彌蘭陀。他喜歡跟修行人辯論；有一天，他去拜訪一位佛教比丘，問他的名字。比丘說：「人們稱我為那先」，但那「只是一個通用的稱呼、一個日常使用的名稱」，這裡面並不涉及任何恆常的個體。國王立刻看出了困難。如果沒有那先，是誰接受衣服與飲食？是誰持戒？又是誰破戒？如果有人殺了你，那就沒有殺人這回事了。

paras.en: He then conducts Hume’s search aloud. Is the hair Nāgasena? The nails, the teeth, the skin, the heart, the brain? Is it the body, or the feelings, or the perceptions, or the impulses, or the consciousness? All of them together? Something apart from them? To each question the monk answers no. “Then thus, ask as I may, I can discover no Nāgasena. Nāgasena is a mere empty sound.” The monk asks how the king traveled there. In a chariot. Then what is the chariot? Is it the pole, the axle, the wheels, the frame, the yoke? All these together? Something apart from them? Now it is the king who must say no each time, and the monk who announces to the applauding crowd that there is no chariot and the king has told a lie. The king’s answer, and the point of the dialogue, are in the exercise below.
paras.zh: 接著，他把休謨的那場尋找，出聲進行了一遍。頭髮是那先嗎？指甲、牙齒、皮膚、心臟、腦呢？是身體嗎？是感受、認知、意志的衝動，還是識？是它們全部合起來嗎？是它們之外的某個東西嗎？每一問，比丘都答「不是」。「那麼，我不管怎麼問，都找不到那先。那先只是一個空洞的聲音。」比丘問國王是怎麼來的。坐車來的。那麼車是什麼？是轅嗎？軸嗎？輪子、車廂、軛嗎？是這些全部合起來嗎？是這些之外的某個東西嗎？現在輪到國王每一次都得說「不是」；而比丘向鼓掌的群眾宣布：根本沒有車，國王說了謊。國王怎麼回答，以及這場對話的要點，就在下面的練習裡。

essay.h_en: A hundred joints and no ruler

paras.en: Zhuangzi carries out the same inventory in three sentences. “The hundred joints, the nine openings, the six organs are all present and complete. Which of them should I feel closest to? Are you pleased with them all, or is there one you favor? Are they all servants? Then can servants not keep one another in order? Or do they take turns as ruler and subject?” He draws a conclusion that is more guarded than Hume’s. “It seems as though there were a true ruler, and yet we find no trace of him.” Something makes joy and anger arise, day and night, and “no one knows from where they sprout.” He does not deny that anything governs. He reports that the governor cannot be found, and he lets the matter rest there.
paras.zh: 莊子用三句話做完了同一份清點。「百骸、九竅、六藏，賅而存焉，吾誰與為親？汝皆說之乎？其有私焉？如是皆有為臣妾乎？其臣妾不足以相治乎？其遞相為君臣乎？」他引出的結論，比休謨的更有保留：「若有真宰，而特不得其朕。」有某個東西使喜怒日夜生起，而「莫知其所萌」。他並沒有否認有什麼在主宰。他回報的是：那個主宰找不到；然後他就讓事情停在那裡。

paras.en: The most serious reply to Hume came from Kant, who had been, he said, awakened by him. Hume describes himself as searching, stumbling on perceptions, failing to catch anything further. Who is this “I” that searches and fails? A heap of perceptions cannot look through itself and notice that something is missing. For there to be experience at all, Kant argued, the perceptions must be capable of being brought together as mine: “The ‘I think’ must accompany all my representations,” or they would be nothing to me. So the unity of the self is not one more item to be found on the stage. It is the condition of there being a stage. But Kant refused to give the old view its victory. From this unity, he said, nothing follows about what I am. It is a form that every experience must have, and it tells us no more about an underlying soul than the frame tells us about the painter.
paras.zh: 對休謨最嚴肅的回應來自康德；他說自己是被休謨喚醒的。休謨描述自己在尋找，碰到一個個知覺，卻抓不到更多的東西。這個尋找而失敗的「我」是誰？一堆知覺不可能把自己翻過一遍，然後察覺少了什麼。康德論證：要有經驗，這些知覺就必須能夠被匯集起來，成為「我的」：「『我思』必須能夠伴隨我的一切表象」，否則它們對我來說就什麼也不是。所以，自我的統一，並不是舞台上另一件有待尋找的東西。它是「有舞台」這件事的條件。但康德拒絕把勝利交給舊的看法。他說，從這個統一，推不出關於「我是什麼」的任何事。它是每一個經驗都必須具有的形式；它告訴我們的關於底下那個靈魂的事，並不比畫框告訴我們的關於畫家的事更多。

essay.h_en: Why it feels as though someone is home
essay.h_zh: 為什麼感覺上有人在家

paras.en: If Hume is right, a stubborn appearance needs explaining. The brain sciences have added three pieces. No place has been found in the brain where everything comes together for a single observer, and processing is spread over many regions working at once. Patients whose hemispheres have been surgically separated will act on an instruction shown only to the mute right half and then, when asked why, give a fluent explanation that the speaking half has invented on the spot. The talking part of us appears to be a commentator who takes itself for the author. And the sense of owning a body can be moved: in a well-known experiment, people who watch a rubber hand being stroked while their own hidden hand is stroked in time come to feel the touch in the rubber one.
paras.zh: 如果休謨是對的，就有一個頑固的表象需要解釋。腦科學補上了三塊拼圖。在腦裡，找不到一個「一切都匯集起來、呈給單一觀察者」的地方；處理的工作分散在許多同時運作的區域。兩個腦半球被手術分開的病人，會依照只給不能說話的右半邊看的指令行動；被問到為什麼的時候，卻能給出一個流利的解釋，那是會說話的那一半當場編出來的。我們身上那個會說話的部分，看來是一個把自己當成作者的評論員。而「擁有一個身體」的感覺是可以被搬動的：在一個著名的實驗裡，受試者看著一隻橡膠手被刷，自己那隻藏起來的手同時被同步地刷，後來就感覺那個觸感是在橡膠手上。

paras.en: Daniel Dennett proposed that the self is like a center of gravity. Every object has one, and engineers cannot do without it, yet nobody expects to find it by cutting the object open. It is an abstraction that lets us summarize how a complicated thing will behave. A self, on this view, is the center of the story a brain tells in order to hold a life together. The German philosopher Thomas Metzinger says that the brain builds a model of the organism and cannot recognize the model as a model, so that we look through it as through a window and take ourselves to be what it shows.
paras.zh: 丹尼特提議：自我就像重心。每一個物體都有重心，工程師少了它不行；可是沒有人指望把物體切開就能找到它。它是一個抽象，讓我們得以概括一個複雜的東西會怎麼表現。照這個看法，自我是一個腦為了把一段人生維繫在一起而講的那個故事的中心。德國哲學家梅辛格說：腦為這個有機體建造了一個模型，卻認不出這個模型是模型；於是我們像透過一扇窗那樣透過它往外看，並且把自己當成它所呈現的東西。

paras.en: Hume was the first to see that his account was incomplete. A year after the first volumes of the Treatise he added an appendix in which he reviews his section on the self and writes: “I find myself involved in such a labyrinth, that, I must confess, I neither know how to correct my former opinions, nor how to render them consistent.” If perceptions are distinct existences, something must explain why these ones belong together as one mind and are not scattered among many, and he could find nothing that does. He never returned to the subject. The puzzle he left has three parts, and every later theory is an attempt at one of them. Something makes experience unified at a moment. Something makes it seem owned. And something makes the thought “there is no self” so hard to feel, even for someone who is sure it is true.
paras.zh: 休謨是第一個看出自己的說明並不完整的人。《人性論》前兩卷出版一年後，他加了一篇附錄，回頭檢視談自我的那一節，寫道：「我發現自己陷在這樣一座迷宮裡；我必須承認，我既不知道怎麼修正先前的意見，也不知道怎麼使它們前後一致。」如果知覺是各自獨立的存在，就必須有某個東西說明：為什麼這些知覺同屬於一個心，而不是散落在許多個心當中？而他找不到任何這樣的東西。他此後再也沒有回到這個題目。他留下的難題有三個部分，而後來的每一種理論，都是在嘗試解決其中之一。有某個東西，使經驗在一個時刻是統一的。有某個東西，使它看起來是「被擁有的」。還有某個東西，使「沒有自我」這個想法這麼難以感受到，即使是對確信它為真的人也一樣。

paras.en: None of this abolishes the person who signs your letters. Nāgasena went on answering to his name. The claim is that the name refers to a great many things working together, and that our habit of picturing one small owner inside them is a picture and nothing more. What follows from the claim is taken up on another shelf.
paras.zh: 這一切並沒有取消那個在你的信上簽名的人。那先仍然繼續回應別人叫他的名字。這裡的主張是：那個名字指的是許許多多一起運作的東西；而我們習慣在它們裡面想像一個小小的擁有者，那只是一幅圖像，僅此而已。從這個主張會推出什麼，是另一個書架的題目。

lab.title_en: Try it: take the chariot apart, then look for yourself
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：把車拆開，然後找找你自己
lab.lead_en: Two searches. In the first you are King Milinda and Nāgasena is questioning you. In the second you repeat Hume’s experiment for thirty seconds and report what you found.
lab.lead_zh: 兩場尋找。第一場，你是彌蘭王，那先在盤問你。第二場，你花三十秒重做休謨的實驗，然後回報你找到了什麼。

ask.en: “You came in a chariot, Sire. Explain to me what that is. Point to it.”
ask.zh: 「大王，您是坐車來的。請向我說明車是什麼。指給我看。」

hint.en: Click any part of the chariot.
hint.zh: 點車上的任何一個部分。

tpl.en: “That is the {p}. Is the {p} the chariot?” — “Certainly not.” It is set aside.
tpl.zh: 「那是{p}。{p}是車嗎？」——「當然不是。」它被放到一邊。

empty.en: “Then is it all these parts lying here that are the chariot?” — “No, Sir.” “Is there anything outside them that is the chariot?” — “No.” Nāgasena turns to the crowd: “Then thus, ask as I may, I can discover no chariot. Chariot is a mere empty sound. It is a falsehood that your Majesty has spoken!”
empty.zh: 「那麼，擺在這裡的這些零件全部，是車嗎？」——「不是，尊者。」「在它們之外，有什麼東西是車嗎？」——「沒有。」那先轉向群眾：「那麼，我不管怎麼問，都找不到車。車只是一個空洞的聲音。大王說的是假話！」

q.en: You are the king. How do you answer?
q.zh: 你是國王。你怎麼回答？

t.en: You are right. There never was a chariot.
t.zh: 你說得對。從來就沒有車。

v.en: Then you walked here across the hot sand, and your feet say otherwise. This answer is called nihilism, and Nāgasena does not want it. Something carried you. The argument has shown that the chariot is not a part and not an extra thing. It has not shown that the word refers to nothing.
v.zh: 那麼你是踩著滾燙的沙子走來的，而你的腳說不是這樣。這個回答叫作虛無論，那先並不想要它。確實有東西載你來。這個論證顯示的是：車不是某一個零件，也不是額外的一樣東西。它並沒有顯示這個詞什麼也不指。

t.en: The chariot is something over and above its parts.
t.zh: 車是在零件之上、之外的某個東西。

v.en: Then it should be possible to remove every part and still have it, or to point to it beside them. You have just agreed that you cannot. This answer, applied to a person, is the soul. Its attraction is that it gives the word something single to stand for. Its cost is that the single thing can never be produced.
v.zh: 那麼，應該可以把每一個零件都拿掉而它還在，或者可以在零件旁邊把它指出來。你剛剛才同意你做不到。這個回答用在人身上，就是靈魂。它吸引人的地方，是給了這個詞一個單一的東西來代表。它的代價是：那個單一的東西永遠拿不出來。

t.en: It is because of all these parts that the word “chariot” is used.
t.zh: 正是因為有這些零件，才用得上「車」這個詞。

v.en: This is Milinda’s answer: “It is on account of its having all these things… that it comes under the generally understood term, the designation in common use, of ‘chariot.’” Nāgasena replies: “Very good! Your Majesty has rightly grasped the meaning of ‘chariot.’ And just even so it is on account of all those things you questioned me about… that I come under the generally understood term, the designation in common use, of ‘Nāgasena.’” The word is used correctly, and it does not name a further thing.
v.zh: 這就是彌蘭王的回答：「正是由於它具有這一切……它才歸在『車』這個通用的稱呼、日常使用的名稱之下。」那先回答：「很好！大王正確地掌握了『車』的意思。同樣地，正是由於您盤問我的那一切……我才歸在『那先』這個通用的稱呼、日常使用的名稱之下。」這個詞用得正確，而它並不指稱一樣額外的東西。

intro.en: Now Hume’s experiment. For thirty seconds, stop reading and attend to whatever is present in your experience. Look for the one who is having it. Then tick everything you found.
intro.zh: 現在是休謨的實驗。三十秒之內，停止閱讀，注意你的經驗裡出現的任何東西。找一找那個「正在擁有」它的人。然後把你找到的每一樣都勾起來。

skip.en: I have looked. Show the list

n.en: An urge to move or to stop
n.zh: 想動一下、或想停下來的衝動

n.en: A self, apart from all of the above
n.zh: 一個「我」，在以上這一切之外

count.en: You found {n} kinds of thing. Hume’s word for all of them is “perceptions.”
count.zh: 你找到了 {n} 類東西。休謨把它們統稱為「知覺」。

plain.en: You did not tick a self. This is Hume’s result: “I never can catch myself at any time without a perception, and never can observe any thing but the perception.” Notice, though, that you understood the instruction to look for the one having the experience. Kant’s question is what made that instruction intelligible.
plain.zh: 你沒有勾「我」。這就是休謨的結果：「我任何時候都抓不到一個沒有知覺的自己，而且除了知覺之外，什麼也觀察不到。」不過請留意：「找一找那個正在擁有經驗的人」這個指示，你是聽得懂的。康德的問題是：是什麼使這個指示聽得懂？

watcher.en: You ticked a sense of someone looking. Most people do, and most place it somewhere behind the eyes. William James examined that feeling in 1890 and reported that, as far as he could tell, it consisted mainly of small movements and tensions in the head and throat. If he is right, the watcher is one more item that is watched. Whether there is more to it than James found is something you can check again.
watcher.zh: 你勾了「有人在看」的感覺。多數人都會勾，而且多數人把它放在眼睛後面的某個地方。威廉・詹姆斯在 1890 年檢視過這種感覺；他回報說，就他所能分辨的，它主要是由頭部與喉嚨裡細小的動作與緊繃構成的。如果他是對的，那個觀看者就是又一樣被觀看的東西。它是否比詹姆斯所發現的更多，你可以再檢查一次。

self.en: You ticked a self apart from everything else. Hume says he cannot reason with you, which is not an argument. Three questions may help. Did it have a location? Did it have any quality by which you could tell it from the feeling of attending? And was it there as something you observed, or as the observing? If the last, you are closer to Kant, for whom the self is never an object found and always the finding. The Buddhist reply to Kant is that an observer who can never be observed is a supposition.
self.zh: 你勾了一個在其他一切之外的「我」。休謨說他沒辦法跟你講理，而這並不是一個論證。有三個問題也許有幫助。它有位置嗎？它有沒有任何性質，讓你能把它跟「正在注意」的感覺分開？還有，它在那裡，是作為你觀察到的某個東西，還是作為那個觀察本身？如果是後者，你比較接近康德；對他來說，自我從來不是一個被找到的對象，而始終是那個「找」。佛教對康德的回應是：一個永遠無法被觀察到的觀察者，是一個假設。

argument.lead_en: Hume’s reasoning in the Treatise, Book I, Part IV, section 6. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 休謨在《人性論》第一卷第四部分第六節的推理。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Every real idea is derived from some impression, that is, from something actually experienced.
steps.zh: 每一個真實的觀念，都來自某個印象，也就是來自某個實際經驗到的東西。
steps.ob_en: This is the empiricist principle that Hume applies everywhere. Kant denied it. Some concepts, he held, are conditions of having experience and so cannot be copied from it.
steps.ob_zh: 這是休謨到處運用的經驗主義原則。康德否認它。他主張，有些概念是「擁有經驗」的條件，因此不可能是從經驗複製來的。

steps.en: The self, as philosophers describe it, is one thing that remains the same through the whole of a life.
steps.zh: 照哲學家的描述，自我是一樣在整個一生當中保持不變的東西。
steps.ob_en: A critic may say that the target is too narrow. Perhaps a self is a changing thing, like a river, and Hume has refuted only the claim that it is unchanging. Hume would accept this and ask what, then, makes it one.
steps.ob_zh: 批評者可以說，這個靶子太窄了。也許自我是一個變動的東西，像一條河；休謨駁倒的只是「它不變」這個主張。休謨會接受這一點，然後問：那麼，是什麼使它成為「一個」？

steps.en: No impression is constant and unchanging. Pain and pleasure, grief and joy, succeed each other.
steps.zh: 沒有任何印象是恆常不變的。苦與樂、悲與喜，前後相續。
steps.ob_en: Rarely disputed as a report of what introspection finds.
steps.ob_zh: 作為「內省發現了什麼」的報告，很少有人爭論。

steps.en: So we have no idea of a self of that kind.
steps.zh: 所以，我們並沒有那一種自我的觀念。
steps.ob_en: Follows from the three premises.
steps.ob_zh: 由三個前提推出。

steps.en: What we call a mind is a bundle of perceptions in constant flux.
steps.zh: 我們稱為心靈的，是一束不斷流動的知覺。
steps.ob_en: This goes beyond C1, and Hume’s own appendix is the best objection to it. A bundle needs something to tie it. He could not say what makes these perceptions one mind, and he could not explain who it is that surveys the bundle and reports that nothing else is there.
steps.ob_zh: 這一步超出了 C1；而休謨自己的附錄，就是對它最好的反駁。一束東西需要有什麼把它綁起來。他說不出是什麼使這些知覺成為一個心；他也無法解釋，是誰在檢閱這一束、並且回報說那裡沒有別的東西。

source.work: The Questions of King Milinda (Milindapañha), Book II, chapter 1
source.work_zh: 《彌蘭王問經》；漢譯《那先比丘經》
source.tr: tr. T. W. Rhys Davids, 1890 (public domain)
source.lead_en: The text was composed in northwest India around the beginning of the common era and exists in a Pali version and two Chinese ones. The Chinese under each passage is a modern rendering of the English.
source.lead_zh: 這部經大約在西元紀年之初成於印度西北，現存一個巴利文本與兩個漢譯本。每一段下面的中文，是依英譯所作的白話翻譯。

passages.en: If, most reverend Nāgasena, there be no permanent individuality (no soul) involved in the matter, who is it, pray, who gives to you members of the Order your robes and food and lodging and necessaries for the sick? Who is it who enjoys such things when given? Who is it who lives a life of righteousness? Who is it who devotes himself to meditation? … If that be so there is neither merit nor demerit; there is neither doer nor causer of good or evil deeds.
passages.zh: 尊敬的那先，如果這裡面不涉及任何恆常的個體（沒有靈魂），那麼請問，是誰把衣服、飲食、住處與醫藥供養給你們僧團的成員？是誰在受用這些供養？是誰過著如法的生活？是誰致力於禪修？……若是如此，就沒有功德也沒有罪過；善惡之業沒有作者，也沒有使作者。
passages.note_en: The king is no fool. Before any metaphor is offered he states the strongest objection to the doctrine, and it is a moral one: responsibility seems to need someone to bear it. The lesson on personal identity met the same worry in Locke, who called “person” a forensic term. Notice that Nāgasena never answers by saying that there is, after all, a doer. He answers by explaining what kind of thing the word “Nāgasena” is.
passages.note_zh: 這位國王並不笨。在任何比喻被提出來之前，他就說出了對這個教義最強的反駁，而那是一個道德上的反駁：責任似乎需要有個人來承擔。「人格同一」那一課在洛克那裡遇過同樣的憂慮；洛克稱「人格者」為一個法庭用語。請留意：那先從頭到尾沒有用「畢竟還是有一個作者」來回答。他的回答，是說明「那先」這個詞是哪一種東西。

passages.en: ‘I have spoken no untruth, reverend Sir. It is on account of its having all these things—the pole, and the axle, the wheels, and the framework, the ropes, the yoke, the spokes, and the goad—that it comes under the generally understood term, the designation in common use, of “chariot.”’ ‘Very good! Your Majesty has rightly grasped the meaning of “chariot.” And just even so it is on account of all those things you questioned me about… that I come under the generally understood term, the designation in common use, of “Nāgasena.”’
passages.zh: 「尊者，我沒有說假話。正是由於它具有這一切：轅、軸、輪、車廂、繩、軛、輻、策，它才歸在『車』這個通用的稱呼、日常使用的名稱之下。」「很好！大王正確地掌握了『車』的意思。同樣地，正是由於您盤問我的那一切……我才歸在『那先』這個通用的稱呼、日常使用的名稱之下。」
passages.note_en: The king says “I have spoken no untruth,” and that is the hinge. It is true that he came in a chariot, and it is true that there is no chariot over and above the parts. Buddhist philosophers later named the two levels conventional and ultimate truth. The older Chinese translation puts the conclusion with great economy: 合聚是諸材木，用作車，因得車；人亦如是. “Bring these timbers together to make a chariot, and thereby there is a chariot. So it is with a person.” In the Chinese version the king, asked what the chariot is, “falls silent and does not speak” (王默然不語), and the monk supplies the answer himself.
passages.note_zh: 國王說「我沒有說假話」，這就是樞紐所在。他確實是坐車來的，這是真的；在零件之上、之外並沒有一輛車，這也是真的。後來的佛教哲學家把這兩個層次稱為世俗諦與勝義諦。較古的漢譯把結論說得極為精簡：「合聚是諸材木，用作車，因得車；人亦如是。」在漢譯本裡，國王被問到車是什麼的時候「默然不語」，答案是比丘自己說出來的。

items.o_en: The search is rigged. A self is the subject of experience and so cannot turn up among its objects, any more than an eye can appear in its own field of view.
items.o_zh: 這場尋找是被動過手腳的。自我是經驗的主體，所以不可能出現在經驗的對象當中，就像眼睛不可能出現在自己的視野裡。
items.r_en: This is the reply of Kant and, long before him, of the Upanishads. It concedes Hume’s finding and disputes what follows. The difficulty is to say anything more about this subject. If it has no observable features, we cannot know that it is one and the same from moment to moment, or that it is mine and not shared, or that it is a thing and not a feature of how experience is organized. Kant accepted all of this, which is why his “I think” is a form and no longer a soul.
items.r_zh: 這是康德的回應；而早在他之前，這也是奧義書的回應。它承認休謨的發現，爭的是由此能推出什麼。困難在於：對這個主體還能再說些什麼？如果它沒有任何可觀察的特徵，我們就無法知道它每一刻都是同一個，無法知道它是我的、而不是共有的，也無法知道它是一樣東西、而不是經驗組織方式的一個特徵。這一切康德都接受了；這就是為什麼他的「我思」是一個形式，不再是一個靈魂。

items.o_en: The denial defeats itself. To say “I find no self” is to use the word “I.” Someone must be doing the denying.
items.o_zh: 這個否定是自己打敗自己的。說「我找不到自我」，就用了「我」這個字。總得有人在否定。
items.r_en: The objection shows that English requires a subject for its verbs. Georg Lichtenberg, a contemporary of Kant, suggested that Descartes should have said “it thinks,” as we say “it rains,” where nobody supposes that an “it” is doing the raining. Nāgasena makes the same move with his name. He goes on saying “I” and answering to “Nāgasena,” and holds that the usage is correct and convenient and commits him to nothing beyond the parts working together.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁顯示的是：英文的動詞需要一個主詞。跟康德同時代的利希滕貝格提議，笛卡兒本來應該說「（它）在思考」，就像我們說「（天）在下雨」；沒有人認為有一個「它」在做下雨這件事。那先對自己的名字用的是同一招。他繼續說「我」，繼續回應「那先」這個名字；他主張這個用法是正確而方便的，並且沒有讓他承諾零件一起運作之外的任何東西。

items.o_en: If no one is there, no one deserves praise or blame, and no one is harmed by cruelty.
items.o_zh: 如果那裡沒有人，就沒有人值得讚美或責備，也沒有人會被殘忍所傷。
items.r_en: This is Milinda’s objection, and it mistakes the claim. Pain occurs whether or not it has an owner, and it is as bad as it ever was. What the view removes is the idea of an inner proprietor in addition to the pain. Responsibility likewise attaches to a continuous stream of intention and action, as it does in a court of law, where no one inquires about souls. Later in the same book Nāgasena says that the one who is reborn is neither the same as nor different from the one who died, as milk is neither the same as nor different from the curds it becomes.
items.r_zh: 這是彌蘭王的反駁，而它誤解了這個主張。不管痛有沒有主人，痛都在發生，而且跟向來一樣糟。這個看法拿掉的，是在痛之外另有一個內在業主的那個想法。責任也一樣，是附著在一道連續的意圖與行動之流上的；法庭上就是這樣，沒有人在那裡查問靈魂。在同一部經稍後的地方，那先說：再生的那一位，與死去的那一位，既不相同也不相異，就像牛奶與它變成的凝乳，既不相同也不相異。

said.claim: “You do not have a soul. You are a soul. You have a body.” (C. S. Lewis)
said.claim_zh: 「你並不是『有』一個靈魂。你『是』一個靈魂。你有的是一個身體。」（C. S. 路易斯）
said.en: The sentence is quoted everywhere under Lewis’s name and has not been found in anything he wrote. Versions of it were in circulation in Britain in the 1890s, before he was born, and it has been credited to the Scottish writer George MacDonald among others. Whoever said it, it is a clear statement of the view this lesson has been testing: that behind the body and the passing states of mind there is one thing that you are. It is Descartes’ view and Plato’s, and it remains what most people believe.
said.zh: 這句話到處被掛在路易斯名下引用，卻不曾在他寫的任何東西裡被找到。它的各種版本，在 1890 年代的英國就已經流傳了，那時他還沒出生；它曾被歸給蘇格蘭作家喬治・麥克唐納等人。不管是誰說的，它清楚地陳述了這一課一直在檢驗的那個看法：在身體與來來去去的心理狀態背後，有一樣東西，那就是你。這是笛卡兒的看法，也是柏拉圖的看法；而它仍然是多數人相信的。

terms.d_en: The view that a mind is a collection of perceptions with no owner in addition to them.
terms.d_zh: 主張心靈是一堆知覺的集合，在它們之外沒有另一個擁有者。

terms.d_en: Hume’s term for a vivid perception had in sensing or feeling, as against an idea, which is its fainter copy in thought.
terms.d_zh: 休謨的用語：在感覺或感受時所具有的鮮明知覺；相對於「觀念」，後者是它在思想中較淡的副本。

terms.d_en: Attending to one’s own mental states.
terms.d_zh: 注意自己的心理狀態。

terms.o: L. ad + percipere ‘to perceive in addition’
terms.d_en: Kant’s term for the fact that all my experiences can be thought of together as mine.
terms.d_zh: 康德的用語：我的一切經驗都能夠被一起想成「我的」這個事實。

terms.d_en: A thing that has properties and persists through changes in them. The soul was held to be one.
terms.d_zh: 擁有種種性質、並且歷經這些性質的變化而持續存在的東西。靈魂曾被認為是一個實體。

terms.d_en: A name used for convenience of many things together, with no single thing answering to it.
terms.d_zh: 為了方便而用來稱呼許多東西合在一起的名稱；並沒有單一的東西與它對應。

terms.d_en: The sincere production of a false explanation for one’s own behavior.
terms.d_zh: 真誠地為自己的行為編出一個不實的解釋。

terms.d_en: The self understood as the main character of the story a person tells about his or her life.
terms.d_zh: 把自我理解為一個人講述自己人生的那個故事裡的主角。

vocab.eg: I always stumble on some particular perception or other.
vocab.eg_zh: 我總是碰到某個個別的知覺。

vocab.eg: He ventures to say that they are nothing but a bundle of perceptions.
vocab.eg_zh: 他大膽地說，他們不過是一束知覺。

vocab.eg: Hume offered an image and at once withdrew half of it.
vocab.eg_zh: 休謨提出了一個意象，又立刻收回了一半。

vocab.eg: One day he called on a Buddhist monk.
vocab.eg_zh: 有一天，他去拜訪一位佛教比丘。

vocab.eg: Zhuangzi carries out the same inventory in three sentences.
vocab.eg_zh: 莊子用三句話做完了同一份清點。

vocab.eg: A conclusion more guarded than Hume’s.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個比休謨的更有保留的結論。

vocab.eg: He lets the matter rest there.
vocab.eg_zh: 他就讓事情停在那裡。

vocab.eg: An explanation that the speaking half has invented on the spot.
vocab.eg_zh: 會說話的那一半當場編出來的解釋。

vocab.eg: A commentator who takes itself for the author.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個把自己當成作者的評論員。

vocab.eg: Nāgasena went on answering to his name.
vocab.eg_zh: 那先仍然繼續回應別人叫他的名字。

quiz.q: What did Hume report finding when he looked for his self?
options: Particular perceptions, and nothing in addition to them.
A thinking substance.
Nothing at all, not even perceptions.
The soul of another person.

quiz.q: Why does Hume warn that the theater comparison must not mislead us?
options: There are only the successive perceptions, with no place where they are staged.
Theaters were immoral in his day.
The mind has many stages.
The audience is more important than the play.

quiz.q: What is King Milinda’s first objection to Nāgasena?
options: If there is no permanent individual, there seems to be no one who acts well or badly.
Monks should not use names.
Chariots are for kings only.
The body is the self.

quiz.q: What is Kant’s reply to Hume?
options: The unity of the self is a condition of having experience, not an item found within it.
The self is located in the brain.
Hume did not look carefully enough.
The soul can be seen in dreams.

quiz.q: What does Dennett mean by comparing the self to a center of gravity?
options: It is a useful abstraction that is not a part to be found inside the thing.
It is the heaviest part of the brain.
It pulls other selves toward it.
It is located in the middle of the body.

write.en: Repeat Hume’s experiment for two minutes and describe, in about 120 words, exactly what you found and what you did not find.
write.zh: 把休謨的實驗重做兩分鐘，然後用大約 120 個英文字，確切描述你找到了什麼、沒找到什麼。

write.en: Milinda asks: if there is no Nāgasena, who keeps the precepts and who breaks them? Write Nāgasena’s reply in your own words.
write.zh: 彌蘭王問：如果沒有那先，是誰持戒？是誰破戒？用你自己的話寫出那先的回答。

write.en: Is a school a thing over and above its buildings, teachers, students, and rules? Use your answer to explain what “designation” means.
write.zh: 一所學校，是在它的建築、老師、學生與規章之上、之外的一樣東西嗎？用你的答案來說明「假名」是什麼意思。

paras.en: This lesson has been half Buddhist already, since the chariot is the tradition’s own illustration. Two things may be added. Nāgasena’s list is not random. When the king has finished with hair and bones he asks about five things in turn: form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. These are the five aggregates, the scheme by which the Buddha sorted everything a person might take to be a self. Hume searched without a map and reported “some particular perception or other.” The Buddhist searcher is handed a map with five regions and told to examine each.
paras.zh: 這一課本來就有一半是佛教的了，因為車喻是這個傳統自己的例證。可以再補充兩點。那先的清單並不是隨意的。國王問完了頭髮與骨頭之後，依序問了五樣東西：色、受、想、行、識。這就是五蘊，佛陀用來把一個人可能當成「我」的一切加以歸類的架構。休謨是沒有地圖地在找，回報說找到「某個個別的知覺」。佛教的尋找者手上拿到的是一張分成五區的地圖，並且被告知要逐區檢視。

paras.en: The second point is the purpose. Hume found his result disturbing, shut the study door, and went to play backgammon. In the Buddhist texts the same result is the beginning of freedom, because the search is undertaken in order to stop clinging to what is found. A companion page takes up the map itself: what the five aggregates are, and which Western account of the mind comes closest to them.
paras.zh: 第二點是目的。休謨覺得自己的結果令人不安，關上書房的門，跑去下雙陸棋了。在佛教經典裡，同樣的結果卻是自由的開端，因為這場尋找本來就是為了不再執取所找到的東西而進行的。姊妹篇處理的是那張地圖本身：五蘊是什麼？西方對心靈的哪一種說明最接近它？

link.en: Read D3 · The Five Aggregates and the West
link.zh: 讀 D3・五蘊與西方哲學

further.t: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book I, Part IV, section 6, and the Appendix
further.n_en: Ten pages, and then the two pages in which he takes it back.
further.n_zh: 十頁；然後是他收回前言的那兩頁。

further.n_zh: 車喻的對話是第一問。

further.n_zh: 漢譯本，譯於四世紀或更早。

further.t: Daniel Dennett, “The Self as a Center of Narrative Gravity” (1992)
further.n_en: Twelve pages, and funny.
further.n_zh: 十二頁，而且好笑。

further.n_en: The hundred joints and the true ruler.
further.n_zh: 百骸與真宰。
