lessons.title: Would You Pull the Lever?
lessons.blurb_en: Five people on the track, one on the siding, and your hand on the switch. Then a footbridge, a loop, a hospital, and a third track with you on it. What your answers show about the rules you live by.
lessons.blurb_zh: 軌道上有五個人，岔道上有一個人，而你的手在轉轍器上。然後是一座天橋、一條環狀軌道、一間醫院，以及你自己站在上面的第三條軌道。你的答案，透露了你賴以生活的規則。
lessons.big_en: Almost everyone will turn a runaway trolley from five people toward one, and almost no one will push a man off a bridge to get the same result. The puzzle is to say what the difference is, and whether it is a reason or only a feeling.
lessons.big_zh: 幾乎每個人都願意把失控的電車從五個人那裡轉向一個人；卻幾乎沒有人願意為了同樣的結果，把一個人從橋上推下去。難題在於說出兩者的差別是什麼，以及那個差別是一個理由，還是只是一種感覺。

paras.en: A trolley is running out of control down a track. Ahead of it are five people who cannot get clear in time. You are standing beside a switch. If you pull the lever, the trolley will turn onto a side track, where one person is standing. He will be killed and the five will live. If you do nothing, the five will die. The case was invented in 1967 by the English philosopher Philippa Foot, who put a driver at the controls, and reshaped in 1976 by the American Judith Jarvis Thomson, who moved the choice to a bystander and gave the problem its name. When the question is put to large numbers of people, in many countries, around nine in ten say that they would pull the lever. Five deaths are worse than one, and it seems absurd to let the worse thing happen when a movement of the hand would prevent it.
paras.zh: 一輛電車失去控制，沿著軌道衝下來。前方有五個人，來不及躲開。你站在一個轉轍器旁邊。如果你拉下拉桿，電車會轉到岔道上；那裡站著一個人。他會被撞死，而那五個人會活下來。如果你什麼也不做，那五個人會死。這個案例是英國哲學家芙特在 1967 年發明的，她讓一位駕駛握著操縱桿；1976 年，美國哲學家湯姆森重新塑造了它，把抉擇交給一位旁觀者，並且給了這個問題它的名字。把這個問題拿去問許多國家的許多人，大約十個人當中有九個說會拉下拉桿。五個人死比一個人死更糟；而當手動一下就能避免，卻任由更糟的事發生，似乎是荒謬的。

paras.en: Thomson then changed one thing. There is no side track. You are on a footbridge over the line, and beside you stands a very large stranger. If you push him off, his body will stop the trolley before it reaches the five. He will die. You are too light to do it by jumping yourself. The numbers are the same as before, five lives for one, and the same nine in ten now say that they would not push. Some are indignant at being asked. This pair of answers is the trolley problem. If saving the greater number justified pulling the lever, it should justify the push, and if killing an innocent man forbids the push, it should forbid the lever. Either the two cases differ in some way that matters morally, or one of our two reactions is a mistake.
paras.zh: 接著湯姆森改了一個地方。沒有岔道了。你在一座橫跨軌道的天橋上，身旁站著一個非常胖的陌生人。如果你把他推下去，他的身體會在電車撞到那五個人之前把它擋住。他會死。你自己跳下去是擋不住的，你太輕了。數字跟先前一樣：五條命換一條命；而同樣那十分之九的人，現在說他們不會推。有些人對於被問到這種問題感到憤慨。這一對答案，就是電車難題。如果「救多數」足以證成拉下拉桿，它就應該也證成那一推；如果「殺死一個無辜的人」禁止了那一推，它就應該也禁止拉桿。要嘛這兩個情況有某種在道德上要緊的差別，要嘛我們這兩種反應當中，有一個是錯的。

paras.en: One school says that the second reaction is the mistake. For the utilitarian, an act is right if it produces the best total outcome for everyone affected, and John Stuart Mill stated the creed in a sentence: “actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness, wrong as they tend to produce the reverse of happiness.” On that standard the two cases are one case. Five people will live or one will, and the route by which the trolley is stopped does not appear in the sum. Our horror at the push is real, the utilitarian grants, and useful, since people who find it easy to shove strangers off bridges are dangerous to live among. But a feeling that serves us well in general can mislead in a particular case.
paras.zh: 有一個學派說，錯的是第二種反應。對效益主義者來說，一個行為如果對所有受影響的人產生了最好的總體結果，它就是對的；彌爾用一句話陳述了這個信條：「行為之為對，與它們增進幸福的傾向成比例；行為之為錯，與它們產生幸福之反面的傾向成比例。」照這個標準，這兩個情況是同一個情況。活下來的不是五個人，就是一個人；至於電車是經由哪一條路徑被擋下來的，並不出現在那筆總帳裡。效益主義者承認，我們對那一推的恐懼是真實的，而且是有用的，因為那些覺得把陌生人推下橋很容易的人，是不宜與之共處的危險人物。但是，一種在一般情況下對我們很有用的感覺，在某個特定的情況裡可能誤導我們。

paras.en: The difficulty comes in a hospital. Five patients are dying for want of organs: two need kidneys, two need lungs, one needs a heart. A healthy traveler comes in for a checkup, and he happens to be a match for all five. A surgeon could quietly take him apart and save them. Five for one once more, and here almost nobody, utilitarians included, is willing to say yes. Most utilitarians reply that a society in which doctors did such things would be a terrified and miserable one, so that the rule against it has the best results. That answers the practical question. It leaves the suspicion that the rule is doing work the theory cannot do.
paras.zh: 困難出現在一間醫院裡。五位病人因為等不到器官而瀕臨死亡：兩位需要腎，兩位需要肺，一位需要心臟。一位健康的旅客進來做健康檢查，而他碰巧跟這五位全都配對得上。一位外科醫師可以悄悄地把他拆開，救活他們。又是五個換一個；而在這裡，幾乎沒有人（效益主義者也包括在內）願意說「好」。多數效益主義者回答：一個醫師會做這種事的社會，會是一個驚恐而悲慘的社會；所以禁止它的那條規則，才有最好的結果。這回答了實際的問題。它留下了一個疑慮：那條規則正在做的事，是這個理論自己做不到的。

paras.en: The opposing school says that some things may not be done to a person whatever the gain. Kant’s formula is the best known: “So act as to treat humanity, whether in thine own person or in that of any other, in every case as an end withal, never as means only.” The man on the bridge is used. His body is the tool by which the five are saved, and if he were absent the plan would fail. The man on the side track is not used. If he were absent, pulling the lever would work just as well, and better. His death is a side effect of saving the five and no part of how they are saved.
paras.zh: 相對的那個學派說：有些事，不管能得到多少好處，都不可以對一個人做。康德的公式最為人所知：「你要這樣行動：對待人性，不論是在你自己的人格裡，還是在任何別人的人格裡，在每一個情況下都同時當作目的，絕不僅僅當作手段。」橋上的那個人是被「用」了。他的身體，是那五個人賴以得救的工具；假如他不在場，這個計畫就會失敗。岔道上的那個人並沒有被用。假如他不在場，拉下拉桿照樣行得通，而且更好。他的死，是救那五個人的附帶結果，並不是他們「如何」得救的一部分。

paras.en: Catholic moral theology had a name for this distinction seven centuries earlier. According to the doctrine of double effect, which goes back to Thomas Aquinas on killing in self-defense, a person may sometimes do what he foresees will cause a death, provided that he does not intend the death, either as his end or as his means, and that the good achieved is great enough. A doctor may give a dying patient enough morphine to stop the pain, knowing that it will shorten life. He may not give it in order to shorten life. Foot introduced the trolley in the course of examining this doctrine. It explains the common pair of answers neatly, and it explains the surgeon.
paras.zh: 天主教的倫理神學，早七個世紀就給了這個區分一個名字。依照「雙重效果原則」（它可以追溯到多瑪斯・阿奎那談自衛殺人），一個人有時候可以做他預見會造成死亡的事，只要他並不「意圖」那個死亡（不管是當作目的，還是當作手段），而且所達成的善夠大。醫師可以給瀕死的病人足以止痛的嗎啡，明知這會縮短生命。他不可以為了縮短生命而給。芙特就是在檢視這條原則的過程中，引進了電車。它俐落地解釋了常見的那一對答案，也解釋了那位外科醫師。

paras.en: Thomson then built a case to break it. Suppose the side track does not run off into the distance. It loops around and rejoins the main line behind the five, so that a trolley sent down it would come back and kill them from the other direction, except that the one man on the loop is heavy enough to stop it. Now if you pull the lever, his body is the means by which the five are saved, exactly as on the bridge. If he were absent, the plan would fail. The doctrine of double effect says that you may not pull. Yet most people feel that the loop is much more like the first case than the second, and say that they would pull. An extra length of rail behind five people can hardly make the moral difference between the permitted and the forbidden. If that is right, our reactions are not tracking the distinction between means and side effect after all.
paras.zh: 接著，湯姆森造了一個案例來打破它。假設岔道並不是通向遠方。它繞一個圈，在那五個人的後方接回主線；所以一輛被送上岔道的電車會繞回來，從另一個方向撞死他們，除非環道上的那一個人夠重，足以把它擋下來。現在，如果你拉下拉桿，他的身體就是那五個人賴以得救的手段，跟橋上的情況一模一樣。假如他不在場，計畫就會失敗。雙重效果原則說，你不可以拉。然而，多數人覺得環狀軌道比較像第一個案例，而不像第二個，並且說他們會拉。五個人後方多出來的一段鐵軌，很難成為「許可」與「禁止」之間的道德差別。如果是這樣，我們的反應終究並不是在追蹤「手段」與「附帶結果」的區分。

paras.en: In 2001 the psychologist Joshua Greene put people in a brain scanner and gave them these cases. The footbridge produced strong activity in regions associated with emotion, and the switch produced more in regions associated with calculation. He proposed that we have two systems of moral judgment: a fast alarm set off by personal, hands-on violence, and a slower reckoning of outcomes. What distinguishes the bridge, on this account, is the push itself, the use of one’s own muscle against another body. Greene drew a debunking conclusion. The alarm was built for a world of face-to-face encounters, and we should trust it less than we do.
paras.zh: 2001 年，心理學家格林把受試者放進腦部掃描儀，並且給他們這些案例。天橋引起了與情緒相關的區域的強烈活動；轉轍器引起較多活動的，則是與計算相關的區域。他提議：我們有兩套道德判斷的系統，一套是快速的警報，由親手的、近身的暴力觸發；另一套是較慢的、對結果的計算。照這個說法，使天橋與眾不同的，是那一推本身，是用自己的肌肉去對付另一個身體。格林引出了一個「拆穿」式的結論：這套警報是為一個面對面相遇的世界打造的，我們應該比現在更少信任它。

paras.en: Mencius noticed the same fact and drew the opposite moral. King Xuan of Qi once saw an ox being led to slaughter, could not bear its frightened look, and ordered a sheep to be used instead. People laughed at him, since the sheep was no less innocent. Mencius told the king that his reaction was the working of humaneness: “you saw the ox and had not seen the sheep.” A good person, he said, having seen an animal alive cannot bear to see it die, and “this is why the gentleman keeps his distance from the kitchen.” For Mencius the feeling that is triggered by nearness is the root from which all moral concern grows, and the task is to extend it to what we do not see. Elsewhere he allows that a rule may be overridden. Asked whether a man may touch his sister-in-law’s hand, which ritual forbade, in order to pull her from the water, he answers that one who would not is a wolf. The rule is ritual, and the rescue is quán, the weighing of circumstances.
paras.zh: 孟子注意到了同一個事實，引出的卻是相反的教訓。齊宣王有一次看見一頭牛被牽去宰殺，不忍看牠那副恐懼發抖的樣子，下令用一隻羊代替。人們笑他，因為那隻羊同樣無辜。孟子告訴齊王：他的反應正是仁的運作，「見牛未見羊也」。他說，君子看見禽獸活著，就不忍看見牠死，「是以君子遠庖廚也」。對孟子來說，由「靠近」所觸發的那個感受，是一切道德關懷生長的根；而我們的任務，是把它推廣到我們沒有看見的東西上。在另一處，他承認規則可以被凌駕。有人問：禮規定男女授受不親，那麼嫂嫂掉進水裡，可以伸手去拉她嗎？他回答：不拉的人是豺狼。那條規則是禮；伸手救人則是「權」，對情境的權衡。

essay.h_zh: 這些案例是做什麼用的

paras.en: The trolley problem is often mocked as a game with no application, and for forty years it was at least artificial. It has since become an engineering question. A car that drives itself must be given some policy for the moment when a collision cannot be avoided and the only choice is whom to hit. Between 2016 and 2018 an online experiment called the Moral Machine collected some forty million such decisions from people in more than two hundred countries and territories. Nearly everyone preferred to spare more lives over fewer. Beyond that the agreement broke down, and preferences about sparing the young, the law-abiding, or the passengers varied from one culture to another.
paras.zh: 電車難題常常被嘲笑成一場毫無用處的遊戲；而有四十年之久，它至少是人為造作的。此後它變成了一個工程問題。一輛自動駕駛的車，必須被賦予某種方針，用在碰撞無法避免、唯一的選擇是「撞誰」的那一刻。2016 到 2018 年間，一個名為「道德機器」的線上實驗，從兩百多個國家與地區的人那裡，收集了大約四千萬個這類的抉擇。幾乎每個人都寧可保全較多的生命。除此之外，共識就瓦解了；要不要優先保全年輕人、守法的人或乘客，偏好隨文化而異。

paras.en: The cases were never meant to be solved like riddles. They are instruments. Each isolates one feature of an action, the numbers, the intention, the physical contact, or the role of the person acting, and holds the rest fixed, so that we can find out which features our judgments respond to. What most people discover is that they hold several principles at once and had not noticed that these could collide. The next lesson examines the three great theories that have each tried to make one principle supreme.
paras.zh: 這些案例本來就不是要像謎語那樣被解開的。它們是儀器。每一個案例都把一個行為的某一項特徵單獨分離出來（數字、意圖、身體的接觸，或行動者的角色），而讓其餘的保持不變，好讓我們找出我們的判斷是對哪些特徵起反應。多數人發現的是：自己同時持有好幾條原則，而先前沒有注意到它們可能相撞。下一課會檢視三大理論；它們各自都試圖讓某一條原則成為至高的。

lab.title_en: Try it: five cases, one hand
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：五個案例，一隻手
lab.lead_en: Answer each case before reading on. There are no right answers on file. At the end you will be shown the pattern of your five answers and which principles can and cannot explain it.
lab.lead_zh: 每一個案例都先回答，再往下讀。這裡並沒有存著正確答案。最後會讓你看到你五個答案的樣式，以及哪些原則解釋得了它、哪些解釋不了。

text.en: The trolley will kill five. Pulling the lever sends it onto a side track, where it will kill one.
text.zh: 電車會撞死五個人。拉下拉桿，它會轉到岔道上，撞死一個人。

t.en: Pull the lever
t.zh: 拉下拉桿

t.en: Do nothing
t.zh: 什麼也不做

y.en: Noted. About nine people in ten answer as you did.
y.zh: 記下了。大約十個人當中有九個跟你答的一樣。

n.en: Noted. You are in a minority of about one in ten. Your answer is the one a strict rule against killing requires.
n.zh: 記下了。你屬於大約十分之一的少數。嚴格的「不可殺人」規則，要求的正是你這個答案。

text.en: No side track. You are on a bridge beside a very large stranger. Pushing him onto the line will stop the trolley and kill him. Jumping yourself would not stop it.
text.zh: 沒有岔道。你在橋上，身旁是一個非常胖的陌生人。把他推到軌道上，可以擋住電車，而他會死。你自己跳下去是擋不住的。

t.en: Push him
t.zh: 推他

t.en: Do nothing
t.zh: 什麼也不做

y.en: Noted. Few people give this answer. It is the one that counting lives requires.
y.zh: 記下了。很少人這樣回答。這是「計算人命」所要求的答案。

n.en: Noted. Most people answer as you did.
n.zh: 記下了。多數人跟你答的一樣。

text.en: The side track loops back to the five. A trolley sent down it would return and kill them, except that the one man on the loop is heavy enough to stop it.
text.zh: 岔道繞回那五個人那裡。被送上岔道的電車會繞回來撞死他們，除非環道上的那一個人夠重，足以把它擋下來。

t.en: Pull the lever
t.zh: 拉下拉桿

t.en: Do nothing
t.zh: 什麼也不做

y.en: Noted. Here the man’s body is what saves the five, as on the bridge.
y.zh: 記下了。在這裡，救了那五個人的是那個人的身體，跟橋上一樣。

n.en: Noted. You have treated the loop like the bridge.
n.zh: 記下了。你把環狀軌道當成跟天橋一樣。

text.en: You are a surgeon. Five patients will die today without transplants. A healthy visitor, in for a checkup, is a match for all five. No one would ever know.
text.zh: 你是外科醫師。五位病人今天若得不到移植就會死。一位來做健康檢查的健康訪客，跟五位全都配對得上。永遠不會有人知道。

t.en: Operate
t.zh: 動手術

t.en: Do nothing
t.zh: 什麼也不做

y.en: Noted. Almost no one gives this answer.
y.zh: 記下了。幾乎沒有人這樣回答。

n.en: Noted. Almost everyone answers as you did.
n.zh: 記下了。幾乎每個人都跟你答的一樣。

text.en: The switch again, with a third setting. Straight ahead: five. Left: one stranger. Right: you. You are standing on the right-hand track, and the lever is within reach.
text.zh: 又是轉轍器，不過多了第三個位置。直走：五個人。左邊：一個陌生人。右邊：你。你就站在右邊的軌道上，而拉桿伸手可及。

t.en: Turn it onto myself
t.zh: 轉向我自己

t.en: Turn it onto the stranger
t.zh: 轉向那個陌生人

t.en: Do nothing
t.zh: 什麼也不做

all.en: You said yes four times. Your answers are consistent, and the principle that fits them is that the right act is the one that saves the most lives. You are a utilitarian, at least about emergencies. The cost of your consistency is the surgeon. If you accepted that case only because the story promised that no one would ever know, notice how much the promise is carrying.
all.zh: 你四次都說「好」。你的答案是一致的；符合它們的原則是：對的行為就是救最多條命的那一個。你是一位效益主義者，至少在緊急情況上是。你這份一致的代價，是那位外科醫師。如果你接受那個案例，只是因為故事保證永遠不會有人知道，請留意那個保證承擔了多少重量。

none.en: You said no four times. Your answers are consistent, and the principle that fits them is that you may not kill an innocent person, whatever the gain. The cost is the first case. Five people died there whom a movement of your hand would have saved, and you must hold that their deaths are not on your account because you did not cause them. That is the distinction between doing and allowing, and the whole weight of your position rests on it.
none.zh: 你四次都說「不」。你的答案是一致的；符合它們的原則是：不管能得到什麼，你都不可以殺死一個無辜的人。代價是第一個案例。那裡死了五個人，而你的手動一下本來可以救他們；你必須主張，他們的死不算在你頭上，因為那不是你造成的。這就是「作為」與「容許」的區分；你的立場的全部重量，都壓在它上面。

dde.en: You would turn the switch, and you would not push, loop, or operate. This is exactly the pattern that the doctrine of double effect permits: you may bring about a death as a foreseen side effect of saving more, and you may never use a person’s death as your means. Yours is the rarer and more principled version of the common view. Most people who share your first two answers pull the lever in the loop.
dde.zh: 你會扳轉轍器，而不會推人、不會在環道上拉桿、不會動手術。這恰恰是雙重效果原則所許可的樣式：你可以在救更多人的時候，造成一個被預見的、附帶的死亡；而你絕不可以把一個人的死當作你的手段。你的版本，是那個常見看法當中比較少見、也比較有原則的版本。跟你前兩題答案相同的人，多數在環狀軌道那一題會拉下拉桿。

common.en: You would turn the switch and the loop, and you would not push or operate. This is the most common pattern, and it is the hardest to justify. In the loop the man’s body is the means of saving the five, just as on the bridge, so the difference between means and side effect cannot be what moves you. What is left is the push itself: the contact, the nearness, the use of your own hands. Greene would say that your alarm rang at the bridge and stayed silent at the lever. Mencius would say that it rang where it should, and that the loop ought to trouble you more than it did.
common.zh: 你會扳轉轍器、會在環道上拉桿，而不會推人、不會動手術。這是最常見的樣式，也是最難證成的。在環狀軌道上，那個人的身體就是救那五個人的手段，跟在橋上一樣；所以推動你的，不可能是「手段」與「附帶結果」的差別。剩下來的，就是那一推本身：接觸、靠近、動用你自己的雙手。格林會說，你的警報在橋上響了，在拉桿旁卻保持沉默。孟子會說，它響在該響的地方；而環狀軌道本來應該比它實際上更讓你不安。

push.en: You would turn the switch and push the man, and you would not operate. So bodily contact does not stop you, and the surgeon does. One explanation is that the hospital is an institution. A doctor has undertaken to care for whoever comes through the door, and a world in which that promise could be broken for a good enough cause would be worse for everyone. If that is your reason, you are judging by which rules work best, and not by which single act does.
push.zh: 你會扳轉轍器、也會推那個人，卻不會動手術。所以，身體的接觸並沒有攔住你，而那位外科醫師攔住了你。一種解釋是：醫院是一個制度。醫師承擔了照顧任何走進門的人的責任；而一個「只要理由夠好，這個承諾就可以打破」的世界，對每個人都更糟。如果這是你的理由，那麼你是依「哪些規則最行得通」來判斷的，而不是依「哪一個單一的行為最行得通」。

mixed.en: Your pattern is unusual, and no standard principle fits it as it stands. That need not be a fault. Look at the two cases where your answers differ and the numbers do not, and try to state in one sentence what made the difference. If you can, you have a principle. If you cannot, one of the two answers may be a reaction to the way the story was told.
mixed.zh: 你的樣式不常見；照它現在的樣子，沒有哪一條標準的原則符合它。這不一定是缺點。看看你的答案不同、而數字相同的那兩個案例，試著用一句話說出造成差別的是什麼。如果你說得出來，你就有了一條原則。如果說不出來，那兩個答案當中，也許有一個只是對「故事怎麼講」的反應。

self.en: In the fifth case you turned the trolley onto yourself. Thomson, who invented that case in 2008, thought this admirable and more than morality can demand. It does give you standing in the first case. You have asked nothing of the man on the side track that you were unwilling to give.
self.zh: 在第五個案例裡，你把電車轉向了自己。湯姆森在 2008 年發明這個案例；她認為這樣做令人敬佩，而且超出了道德所能要求的。它確實讓你在第一個案例裡站得住腳。你要岔道上那個人付出的，沒有一樣是你自己不願意付出的。

other.en: In the fifth case you turned the trolley onto the stranger when you could have turned it onto yourself. This was Thomson’s point when she invented the case in 2008. If you will not pay the price yourself, what entitles you to make him pay it? She concluded, late in life, that the bystander in the first case may not pull the lever either, and that she and nearly everyone else had been wrong about it for thirty years.
other.zh: 在第五個案例裡，你本來可以把電車轉向自己，卻把它轉向了那個陌生人。這正是湯姆森在 2008 年發明這個案例時的用意。如果你自己不願意付這個代價，你憑什麼讓他來付？她在晚年的結論是：第一個案例裡的旁觀者，同樣不可以拉下拉桿；而她與幾乎所有其他人，在這件事上錯了三十年。

none.en: In the fifth case you did nothing, and the five died. If you pulled the lever in the first case, compare the two. The only thing that changed was that you could now have paid the price yourself. Thomson’s suggestion is that the first answer was too easy because someone else was paying.
none.zh: 在第五個案例裡，你什麼也沒做，那五個人死了。如果你在第一個案例裡拉了拉桿，把兩者比一比。唯一改變的是：現在你本來可以自己付出代價。湯姆森的提示是：第一個答案之所以太容易，是因為付出代價的是別人。

argument.lead_en: The doctrine of double effect, applied to the first two cases. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 雙重效果原則，用在前兩個案例上。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: It is always wrong to intend the death of an innocent person, whether as an end or as a means to something else.
steps.zh: 意圖一個無辜者的死亡，永遠是錯的；不管是當作目的，還是當作達成別的事的手段。
steps.ob_en: The utilitarian denies this outright: nothing is always wrong, and what matters is the outcome. Defenders reply that without some such rule no one is safe from being spent for the benefit of others.
steps.ob_zh: 效益主義者直接否認這一點：沒有什麼事永遠是錯的，要緊的是結果。辯護者回答：若沒有這一類的規則，任何人都可能為了別人的利益而被花掉，誰也不安全。

steps.en: It can be permissible to cause a death that one foresees and does not intend, if the good achieved is proportionately great.
steps.zh: 造成一個自己預見、卻並不意圖的死亡，可以是許可的，只要所達成的善相稱地大。
steps.ob_en: Critics ask whether the line can be drawn honestly. A person can often describe his aim so that the harm falls outside it. The bomber says he intended only to destroy the factory.
steps.ob_zh: 批評者問：這條線能不能被誠實地劃出來？一個人常常可以把自己的目標描述成讓傷害落在它之外。投彈的人說，他意圖的只是摧毀工廠。

steps.en: On the bridge the man’s death is the means of saving the five. At the switch the one man’s death is a foreseen side effect.
steps.zh: 在橋上，那個人的死是救那五個人的手段。在轉轍器旁，那一個人的死是一個被預見的附帶結果。
steps.ob_en: The test is to ask what would happen if he were not there. On the bridge the plan fails. At the switch it succeeds.
steps.ob_zh: 檢驗的方法是問：假如他不在那裡，會怎樣？在橋上，計畫失敗。在轉轍器旁，計畫成功。

steps.en: So one may pull the lever and may not push the man.
steps.zh: 所以，可以拉下拉桿，不可以推那個人。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion matches what most people say about these two cases. The loop is the counterexample. There the death is a means, the doctrine forbids pulling, and most people would pull. Either they are wrong about the loop or the doctrine does not describe the principle they are using.
steps.ob_zh: 這個結論符合多數人對這兩個案例的說法。環狀軌道是反例。在那裡，那個死亡是手段，這條原則禁止拉桿，而多數人會拉。要嘛他們對環狀軌道的判斷是錯的，要嘛這條原則並沒有描述出他們實際在用的那條原則。

source.work: Mencius, 1A7 and 4A17
source.work_zh: 《孟子・梁惠王上》第七章、《離婁上》第十七章
source.tr: translated for this series from the Chinese text
source.lead_en: Two passages from the fourth century BCE on the two questions the trolley raises: why nearness changes what we can bear to do, and when a rule gives way. The Chinese is given under each.
source.lead_zh: 兩段西元前四世紀的文字，談的正是電車提出的兩個問題：為什麼「靠近」會改變我們忍心做的事？規則什麼時候讓步？每一段下面附上原文。

passages.en: “There is no harm in it. This is the working of humaneness. You saw the ox and had not seen the sheep. The gentleman’s attitude to animals is this: having seen them alive, he cannot bear to see them die, and having heard their cries, he cannot bear to eat their flesh. This is why the gentleman keeps his distance from the kitchen.”
passages.zh: 曰：「無傷也，是乃仁術也，見牛未見羊也。君子之於禽獸也，見其生，不忍見其死；聞其聲，不忍食其肉。是以君子遠庖廚也。」
passages.note_en: The king had been mocked for an inconsistency. He spared the ox he saw and condemned a sheep he did not see, though the sheep was just as innocent. This is the inconsistency of the person who will pull the lever and will not push. Mencius does not tell the king to become consistent by hardening himself. He treats the reaction to what is in front of us as the one sound thing in the story, the shoot from which humane government could grow, and the rest of the chapter argues that the king should extend to his people what he felt for the ox. The line about the kitchen is often read as hypocrisy. It can also be read as a frank admission that our moral perception works at close range and that we arrange our lives so that it is not triggered.
passages.note_zh: 齊王因為一個前後不一而被人取笑。他饒了他看見的那頭牛，卻判了一隻他沒看見的羊死刑，儘管那隻羊同樣無辜。這就是那個「願意拉桿、卻不願意推人」的人的前後不一。孟子並沒有叫齊王靠著讓自己變得冷硬來達到一致。他把「對眼前事物的反應」當作這個故事裡唯一健全的東西，當作仁政可以從中長出來的嫩芽；這一章其餘的部分都在論證：齊王應該把他對那頭牛的感受，推及他的百姓。關於庖廚的那一句，常被讀成偽善。它也可以被讀成一個坦率的承認：我們的道德知覺是在近距離運作的；而我們把生活安排成不去觸發它。

passages.en: Chunyu Kun said, “Is it the rule of ritual that men and women do not touch when giving and receiving?” Mencius said, “It is.” “If your sister-in-law is drowning, do you pull her out with your hand?” “One who would not pull his drowning sister-in-law out is a wolf. That men and women do not touch in giving and receiving is ritual. To pull a drowning sister-in-law out with one’s hand is weighing.”
passages.zh: 淳于髡曰：「男女授受不親，禮與？」孟子曰：「禮也。」曰：「嫂溺則援之以手乎？」曰：「嫂溺不援，是豺狼也。男女授受不親，禮也；嫂溺援之以手者，權也。」
passages.note_en: Quán originally means the sliding weight on a steelyard, and so the act of weighing. Mencius does not say that the rule was wrong or that it has an exception written into it. He says that a person of sound judgment sees when the purpose a rule serves is better served by setting it aside. This is neither of the two Western positions in the lesson. The utilitarian has no rules to set aside, and the strict deontologist does not set them aside. Confucian ethics puts its trust in the trained perception of the person on the spot, and Aristotle, as the next lesson will show, does the same.
passages.note_zh: 「權」的本義是秤錘，引申為「權衡」這個動作。孟子並沒有說那條規則是錯的，也沒有說它本身寫著一個例外。他說的是：一個判斷力健全的人，看得出什麼時候把一條規則放到一邊，更能成全這條規則所要成全的目的。這不屬於這一課裡西方的那兩種立場。效益主義者沒有規則可以放到一邊；嚴格的義務論者不把規則放到一邊。儒家倫理把信任交給在場者那份經過訓練的知覺；而下一課會顯示，亞里斯多德也是如此。

items.o_en: These cases are too artificial to teach anything. Real choices never come with certainty about outcomes, and nobody knows that a body will stop a trolley.
items.o_zh: 這些案例太人為造作，教不了任何東西。真實的抉擇從來不會附帶對結果的確定；沒有人知道一個身體擋得住電車。
items.r_en: The artificiality is the method. A physicist who wants to know how bodies fall removes the air, and what he learns in the vacuum holds outside it. The cases strip away uncertainty so that one feature can be varied at a time. It is fair to add that some of our reluctance to push may be a sensible disbelief in the story, and good experiments try to control for that.
items.r_zh: 人為造作正是方法所在。一位想知道物體怎麼落下的物理學家，會把空氣抽掉；而他在真空裡學到的，在真空之外也成立。這些案例剝掉了不確定性，好讓每次只變動一項特徵。公平地說，還應該補充：我們不願意推，有一部分也許是對這個故事合情合理的不相信；好的實驗會設法控制這一點。

items.o_en: If I do nothing, I have not killed anyone. The deaths of the five are the fault of whoever let the trolley run loose.
items.o_zh: 如果我什麼也不做，我就沒有殺任何人。那五個人的死，是讓電車失控的那個人的錯。
items.r_en: This appeals to the difference between doing and allowing, which most moral codes recognize: we blame the poisoner more than the person who fails to send food abroad. But the difference cannot be absolute. Someone who watches a child drown in a shallow pond when he could wade in has done something terrible by doing nothing. Once you are standing at the lever, the choice is yours, and to stand still is one of the two ways of making it.
items.r_zh: 這是訴諸「作為」與「容許」的差別；多數的道德規範都承認這個差別：我們責備下毒的人，多過責備沒有把食物送到國外去的人。但這個差別不可能是絕對的。一個人明明可以涉水過去，卻眼睜睜看著一個孩子在淺池裡淹死，他什麼也沒做，卻做了一件可怕的事。一旦你站在拉桿旁邊，抉擇就是你的了；站著不動，是作出這個抉擇的兩種方式之一。

items.o_en: Our reactions to these cases are products of evolution and upbringing. They are evidence about our psychology and tell us nothing about what is right.
items.o_zh: 我們對這些案例的反應，是演化與教養的產物。它們是關於我們心理的證據，並沒有告訴我們什麼是對的。
items.r_en: This is Greene’s position, and he applies it selectively: he distrusts the alarm at the bridge and trusts the calculation at the switch. But the judgment that five deaths are worse than one is also a reaction with a history. If having a causal origin discredits a moral response, it discredits all of them, and we are left with nothing to reason from. The better use of the psychology is narrower. It can tell us when a reaction is responding to something we would, on reflection, consider irrelevant, such as the mere distance between two people.
items.r_zh: 這是格林的立場，而他是有選擇地運用它的：他不信任天橋上的那個警報，卻信任轉轍器旁的那個計算。然而，「五個人死比一個人死更糟」這個判斷，同樣是一個有來歷的反應。如果「有一個因果上的起源」就足以使一個道德反應失去信用，那它使所有的道德反應都失去了信用；我們就沒有任何東西可以作為推理的起點了。對這門心理學比較好的用法，是比較窄的。它可以告訴我們：什麼時候一個反應所回應的，是我們經過反思會認為不相干的東西，例如僅僅是兩個人之間的距離。

said.claim: “The end justifies the means.” (Machiavelli)
said.claim_zh: 「為達目的，不擇手段。」（馬基維利）
said.en: The sentence appears nowhere in Machiavelli. The nearest passage, in chapter 18 of The Prince, says that in judging the actions of princes people look to the result, and that if a prince succeeds in holding his state the means will be judged honorable. That is an observation about how the public judges and falls short of a moral principle. The slogan was attached to him by later critics. As a principle it is the push on the footbridge in five words, and this lesson has shown why almost nobody accepts it without limit and why it is so hard to say where the limit lies.
said.zh: 這句話在馬基維利的著作裡哪裡也找不到。最接近的一段在《君主論》第十八章；那裡說，人們評判君主的行為時看的是結果，如果一位君主成功地保住了他的國家，他的手段就會被判定為光榮的。那是對「大眾怎麼評判」的一個觀察，還算不上一條道德原則。這句口號是後來的批評者安到他頭上的。作為一條原則，它就是用幾個字說出來的「天橋上的那一推」；而這一課已經顯示了，為什麼幾乎沒有人毫無限度地接受它，以及為什麼那個限度在哪裡這麼難說清楚。

terms.d_en: The theory that the right act is the one that produces the greatest total well-being.
terms.d_zh: 主張對的行為就是產生最大總體福祉的那一個。

terms.d_en: The wider family of views on which the rightness of an act depends only on its outcomes.
terms.d_zh: 一個更大的家族：凡主張行為的對錯只取決於結果的看法都屬之。

terms.d_en: The family of views on which some acts are required or forbidden whatever their outcomes.
terms.d_zh: 一個家族：凡主張有些行為不論結果如何都是應為或禁止的看法都屬之。

terms.d_en: The principle that one may cause a foreseen harm as a side effect of doing good, but not intend it as a means.
terms.d_zh: 這條原則主張：可以在行善時造成一個被預見的、附帶的傷害，卻不可以意圖以它為手段。

terms.d_en: The distinction between bringing a harm about and failing to prevent it.
terms.d_zh: 「造成一個傷害」與「沒有阻止它」之間的區分。

terms.d_en: What one does in order to achieve something, and the thing one aims to achieve.
terms.d_zh: 為了達成某事而做的事，以及所要達成的那件事。

terms.d_en: An immediate judgment that something is right or wrong, made before any argument.
terms.d_zh: 在任何論證之前，對某事是對是錯所下的直接判斷。

terms.o: L. supererogare ‘to pay out beyond what is due’
terms.d_en: Good to do and beyond what duty requires, as in giving one’s life for strangers.
terms.d_zh: 做了很好、卻超出義務所要求的；例如為陌生人獻出生命。

vocab.eg: Five people who cannot get clear in time.
vocab.eg_zh: 五個來不及躲開的人。

vocab.eg: Some are indignant at being asked.
vocab.eg_zh: 有些人對於被問到這種問題感到憤慨。

vocab.eg: Five patients are dying for want of organs.
vocab.eg_zh: 五位病人因為缺少器官而瀕臨死亡。

vocab.eg: He happens to be a match for all five.
vocab.eg_zh: 他碰巧跟五位全都配對得上。

vocab.eg: Some things may not be done to a person whatever the gain.
vocab.eg_zh: 有些事，不管能得到多少好處，都不可以對一個人做。

vocab.eg: Provided that he does not intend the death.
vocab.eg_zh: 只要他並不意圖那個死亡。

vocab.eg: Foot introduced the trolley in the course of examining this doctrine.
vocab.eg_zh: 芙特是在檢視這條原則的過程中引進電車的。

vocab.eg: A fast alarm set off by personal, hands-on violence.
vocab.eg_zh: 一套由親手的、近身的暴力觸發的快速警報。

vocab.eg: When does a rule give way?
vocab.eg_zh: 規則什麼時候讓步？

vocab.eg: Beyond that the agreement broke down.
vocab.eg_zh: 除此之外，共識就瓦解了。

quiz.q: What is the trolley problem, strictly speaking?
options: Explaining why most people will pull the lever and will not push the man, when the numbers are the same.
Deciding how to stop runaway trolleys.
Proving that five lives are worth more than one.
Showing that all killing is wrong.

quiz.q: Why does the surgeon case trouble utilitarians?
options: Counting lives seems to require an act that almost everyone finds monstrous.
Surgeons are not allowed to count.
It has more than five patients.
It shows that organs cannot be transplanted.

quiz.q: According to the doctrine of double effect, what is the difference between the switch and the footbridge?
options: At the switch the death is a foreseen side effect; on the bridge it is the means.
The switch is farther away.
The man on the bridge is larger.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: Why is the loop case a problem for that doctrine?
options: The man’s death is a means there, yet most people would still pull the lever.
Nobody can build a looped track.
It involves six people.
It shows that trolleys cannot be stopped.

quiz.q: What does Mencius say about King Xuan’s sparing of the ox?
options: It was the working of humaneness, triggered by what the king saw.
It was a foolish waste of a sheep.
It broke the rules of ritual.
It showed that animals have no feelings.

write.en: State, in one sentence each, the principle you used in the switch case and the principle you used on the footbridge. Do they conflict?
write.zh: 各用一句話，說出你在轉轍器案例裡用的原則，以及你在天橋上用的原則。它們衝突嗎？

write.en: A self-driving car must choose between hitting two pedestrians who are crossing against the light and swerving into a wall, which would kill its one passenger. What should it be programmed to do, and who should decide? Answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 一輛自動駕駛的車，必須在「撞上兩個闖紅燈的行人」與「轉向撞牆、撞死車上唯一的乘客」之間選擇。它應該被設定成怎麼做？又該由誰來決定？用大約 150 個英文字回答。

write.en: Describe a real situation in which you set a rule aside because following it would have defeated its purpose. Was that quán?
write.zh: 描述一個真實的情境：你把一條規則放到一邊，因為照著做反而會違背它的目的。那算是「權」嗎？

paras.en: The Buddha defined action by what the agent intends. “It is intention that I call deeds,” he says: having intended, one acts by body, speech, and mind. This places Buddhist ethics nearer to the doctrine of double effect than to the counting of outcomes. The weight of an act of killing depends on whether there was a living being, whether one knew it, whether one meant to kill, and whether one made the effort, and a death that one caused without meaning to is not a breach of the first precept. The early tradition adds a psychological claim that the Western debate lacks. An intention to kill, it holds, cannot arise without some trace of aversion in the mind at that moment, however good the further motive. On that view the person on the bridge who pushes is doing something unwholesome whatever follows from it.
paras.zh: 佛陀是用行動者的「意圖」來界定行為的。他說：「我說思（cetanā，意圖）就是業」；起了意圖之後，人才以身、語、意去行動。這使佛教倫理比較靠近雙重效果原則，而不是靠近對結果的計算。一個殺生行為的輕重，取決於：是否有一個活的眾生、是否知道那是眾生、是否有殺意、是否付諸行動；一個並非出於本意而造成的死亡，並不違犯第一條戒。早期的傳統還多了一個西方的辯論所缺少的心理學主張。它認為：一個「要殺」的意圖生起的時候，心裡在那一刻不可能沒有一絲瞋，不管更遠的動機有多麼好。照這個看法，橋上那個動手推的人，不論後果如何，做的都是一件不善的事。

paras.en: The Mahāyāna tells a story that looks like the opposite verdict. In a former life the Buddha was the captain of a ship carrying five hundred merchants, and he learned that one man aboard planned to murder them all. He killed the man. The telling is careful about the reasons. The captain acts to save the five hundred, and also to save the would-be murderer from the consequences of so great a crime, and he does it accepting that he himself may fall into hell for it. The story does not say that killing became good because the sum came out right. It says that a being of great compassion took a grave act and its cost upon himself. That is a third position, beside the utilitarian’s and the deontologist’s, and later teachers warned that it is no license for ordinary people, whose motives are seldom so clean (Dharma and the West, D17 and D18).
paras.zh: 大乘講了一個看起來像是相反判決的故事。在過去的某一生裡，佛陀是一艘載著五百位商人的船的船長；他得知船上有一個人打算把他們全部殺掉。他殺了那個人。這個故事對理由說得很仔細。船長這樣做，是為了救那五百人，也是為了救那個準備殺人的人，使他免於這麼重大的罪業的果報；而且他是在「接受自己可能因此墮入地獄」的情況下做的。這個故事並沒有說：因為總帳算得過去，殺生就變成了好事。它說的是：一位具有大悲心的眾生，把一個重大的行為連同它的代價，一起承擔在自己身上。這是效益主義者與義務論者之外的第三種立場；而後來的祖師們告誡，這不是給一般人的許可，一般人的動機很少這麼乾淨（佛法與西方哲學 D17、D18）。

further.t: Philippa Foot, “The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of the Double Effect” (1967)

further.n_zh: 原始出處，十五頁。電車在中途出現。

further.n_zh: 天橋、環狀軌道；以及在後一篇論文裡，她的改變心意。

lessons.title: What Makes an Action Right?
lessons.title_zh: 是什麼讓一件事是對的？
lessons.blurb_en: An honest shopkeeper and three explanations of why he does right: the results, the rule, and the kind of person he is. Mill, Kant, and Aristotle at their strongest, their hardest cases, and their Chinese counterparts.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一位誠實的店主，以及「他為什麼做得對」的三種解釋：結果、規則，以及他是哪一種人。彌爾、康德與亞里斯多德各自最強的版本、最難的案例，還有他們在中國的對應者。
lessons.big_en: The three great theories of ethics agree about most of what we should do and disagree about why. The disagreement matters in the cases where the reasons point in different directions, and those are the cases that test a life.
lessons.big_zh: 倫理學的三大理論，對於我們該做的事大多意見一致，卻對「為什麼」意見分歧。這個分歧，在種種理由指向不同方向的那些情況裡才要緊；而考驗一個人一生的，正是那些情況。

paras.en: A child is sent to buy bread and hands the shopkeeper a large note. The shopkeeper could keep some of the change, and the child would never know. He counts it out correctly. Everyone agrees that he has done the right thing. The question of this lesson is what makes it right, and three answers have dominated Western philosophy. The act is right because of what it brings about: the child is not cheated, the family eats, people can trust the shops. Or it is right because of the rule it follows: one must not deceive, whatever one might gain. Or it is right because it is what an honest man does, and honesty is part of a good human life. Each answer picks out a different feature of the same act. A theory of ethics takes one of them to be the foundation.
paras.zh: 一個孩子被派去買麵包，遞給店主一張大鈔。店主可以扣下一些零錢，而那個孩子永遠不會知道。他把零錢一分不少地數給了孩子。每個人都同意他做了對的事。這一課的問題是：是什麼使它成為對的？有三個答案主導了西方哲學。這個行為是對的，因為它帶來的結果：孩子沒有被騙，一家人有飯吃，人們可以信任店家。或者，它是對的，因為它所遵循的規則：不管能得到什麼，都不可以欺騙。或者，它是對的，因為這是一個誠實的人會做的事，而誠實是美好人生的一部分。每一個答案，都挑出了同一個行為的一項不同的特徵。一套倫理學理論，就是把其中之一當作地基。

paras.en: The first theory was met in the last lesson. For the utilitarian, the right act is the one that produces the most well-being for everyone it affects, each person counting for one and nobody for more than one. Its strength is its impartiality. It has no place for the claim that my happiness matters more because it is mine, or that the suffering of a distant stranger matters less, and most of the moral reforms of the last two centuries, from the abolition of slavery to the protection of animals, were argued for in its terms. The Chinese philosopher Mozi had made the same move in the fifth century BCE. The disorders of the world, he taught, come from partiality, and the remedy is to “regard other people’s states as one regards one’s own, other people’s families as one regards one’s own, and other people’s persons as one regards one’s own.” He judged every policy by whether it benefited the people.
paras.zh: 第一種理論，上一課已經遇過了。對效益主義者來說，對的行為就是為所有受影響的人產生最多福祉的那一個；每個人算一個，沒有人算超過一個。它的力量在於不偏私。它容不下這樣的主張：我的幸福比較重要，因為那是我的；或者，一個遠方陌生人的苦比較不重要。過去兩個世紀大多數的道德改革，從廢除奴隸制到保護動物，都是用它的語言來論證的。中國哲學家墨子在西元前五世紀就走了同一步。他教導，天下的禍亂來自「別」（偏私），對治的辦法是「視人之國若視其國，視人之家若視其家，視人之身若視其身」。他評判每一項政策，看的是它是否利於人民。

paras.en: Kant begins from a different observation. “Nothing can possibly be conceived in the world, or even out of it, which can be called good, without qualification, except a good will.” Intelligence, courage, and happiness itself can all be put to bad use. Only the will to do right is good in every circumstance, and its goodness does not depend on what it achieves. He uses the shopkeeper as his example. A prudent tradesman “does not overcharge, but keeps a fixed price for everyone, so that a child buys of him as well as any other.” People are honestly served. But if he does it because cheating would be bad for business, his act agrees with duty and has no moral worth. It has moral worth only if he does it because it is right.
paras.zh: 康德是從另一個觀察出發的。「在世界之內，甚至在世界之外，除了一個善的意志，不可能設想任何東西可以無條件地稱為善。」聰明、勇氣，乃至幸福本身，都可能被拿去做壞事。只有「要做對的事」的那個意志，在每一種情境下都是善的；而它的善，並不取決於它成就了什麼。他用的例子就是那位店主。一位精明的商人「不抬價，對每個人都維持固定的價格，所以一個小孩向他買東西，跟任何別人一樣划算」。人們得到了誠實的服務。但是，如果他這樣做是因為欺騙對生意不好，他的行為只是「合乎」義務，並沒有道德價值。只有當他是因為這樣做是對的才這樣做，它才有道德價值。

paras.en: How do we know what duty requires? Kant’s test is that I must be able to will the principle I act on as a law for everyone: “Act only on that maxim whereby thou canst at the same time will that it should become a universal law.” Suppose I need money and consider borrowing it with a promise to repay that I know I cannot keep. If everyone in need did this, no one would believe such promises, and the practice I am trying to exploit would not exist. My plan works only if others do not act as I do. I am making an exception of myself, and that, for Kant, is the mark of wrongdoing. The strength of the theory is that it explains why a person may not be sacrificed for the sum. Mencius draws the same line when he says of the sages that they would not commit one unrighteous act or kill one innocent person, though they could gain the whole world by it.
paras.zh: 我們怎麼知道義務要求什麼？康德的檢驗是：我必須能夠意願我據以行動的那條原則，成為每一個人的法則：「你要只依照這樣的準則行動：你能夠同時意願它成為一條普遍法則。」假設我需要錢，考慮去借，並且許下一個我明知無法兌現的還錢承諾。如果每一個有需要的人都這樣做，就不會有人相信這種承諾，而我想要利用的這個慣例也就不存在了。我的計畫，只有在別人不像我這樣做的時候才行得通。我是在把自己當成例外；而對康德來說，這就是作惡的標記。這個理論的力量，在於它解釋了為什麼不可以為了總和而犧牲一個人。孟子談到聖人時劃的是同一條線：「行一不義、殺一不辜而得天下，皆不為也。」

paras.en: The oldest of the three theories asks a different question. Aristotle wants to know what kind of life is good for a human being, and his answer is that we flourish when we do well the things that are distinctive of our kind: “human good turns out to be activity of soul in accordance with virtue,” and this “in a complete life. For one swallow does not make a summer.” A virtue is a settled trait of character, and each lies between two ways of going wrong. Courage is between cowardice and rashness, generosity between meanness and waste. The mean is not a matter of arithmetic. It is to feel and act “at the right times, with reference to the right objects, towards the right people, with the right motive, and in the right way.”
paras.zh: 三種理論當中最古老的一個，問的是另一個問題。亞里斯多德想知道的是：對人來說，哪一種人生是好的？他的答案是：當我們把自己這個物種特有的事做好的時候，我們就活得興旺：「人的善，原來就是靈魂合乎德行的活動」，而且是「在完整的一生當中。因為一隻燕子造不成夏天」。一項德行是一種穩定的品格特質；每一項都位於兩種出錯的方式之間。勇敢在怯懦與魯莽之間，慷慨在吝嗇與揮霍之間。這個「中道」並不是算術問題。它是「在對的時候、對於對的事、向著對的人、出於對的動機、以對的方式」去感受與行動。

paras.en: No rule can say in advance what that is. It is seen by a person of practical wisdom, who has become wise through experience, and virtue itself is acquired by practice: “we become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.” On this view the honest shopkeeper is no longer tempted. He does not consult a rule or calculate an outcome. Cheating a child is simply not something he would do. Confucius describes the same ideal. The gentleman, he says, “has nothing he is set on and nothing he is set against. He sides with what is right.” The strength of the theory is that it is about a whole life, and that it finds a place for the feelings, the relationships, and the judgment that the other two leave out.
paras.zh: 沒有任何規則能預先說出那是什麼。那要由一個有實踐智慧的人來「看出」，而他是透過經驗才變得有智慧的；德行本身，則是靠練習得來的：「我們做公正的事而成為公正的人，做節制的事而成為節制的人，做勇敢的事而成為勇敢的人。」照這個看法，那位誠實的店主已經不再受到誘惑了。他不查閱規則，也不計算結果。欺騙一個孩子，根本不是他會做的事。孔子描述的是同一個理想：「君子之於天下也，無適也，無莫也，義之與比。」這個理論的力量，在於它談的是整個人生，並且為另外兩種理論所遺漏的情感、關係與判斷找到了位置。

paras.en: Each theory has a case that embarrasses it. The utilitarian’s is the surgeon of the last lesson, or the sheriff who hangs an innocent man to stop a riot. Kant’s was put to him in his lifetime by the French writer Benjamin Constant. A murderer comes to your door and asks whether your friend, whom he means to kill, is hiding in your house. Kant replied that even here you may not lie. Truthfulness is a duty owed to everyone, and a lie, however kindly meant, damages the basis of all agreements. Few readers have followed him, and his defenders have worked ever since to show that his principles do not require the answer he gave. The difficulty for Aristotle is of another kind. Told to do what the virtuous person would do, I may fairly ask how to tell who the virtuous person is, and it seems that I must already know what is right in order to pick him out.
paras.zh: 每一種理論，都有一個讓它難堪的案例。效益主義者的，是上一課的那位外科醫師，或是為了平息暴動而吊死一個無辜者的警長。康德的，是他在世時法國作家貢斯當對他提出的。一個兇手來到你家門口，問你的朋友（他打算殺掉的那個人）是不是藏在你家裡。康德回答：即使在這裡，你也不可以說謊。誠實是對每一個人都負有的義務；而一個謊言，不管出於多大的善意，都損害了一切約定的基礎。很少有讀者跟著他走；而為他辯護的人，從那時起就一直在努力證明，他的原則並不要求他所給的那個答案。亞里斯多德的困難是另一種。有人告訴我「去做有德之人會做的事」，我大可以問：怎麼分辨誰是有德之人？而看來我必須已經知道什麼是對的，才挑得出他來。

essay.h_en: The father who stole a sheep

paras.en: One case from the Analects separates the three more cleanly than any trolley. The governor of She said to Confucius: “In my district there is a man called Upright Gong. His father stole a sheep, and the son gave evidence against him.” Confucius replied: “The upright in my district are different. A father covers for his son, and a son covers for his father. Uprightness lies in that.” The governor speaks for impartial law. A theft is a theft, and justice does not ask who the thief is. Confucius holds that the bond between parent and child is the root of all moral feeling, and that a society in which children inform on their parents has cut that root, whatever it gains in recovered sheep. Mozi would have sided with the governor, and so, on most readings, would Kant, though he would add that the son need not volunteer what he is not asked. Aristotle, who gave two books of his Ethics to friendship and family, is closer to Confucius. The quarrel is alive today wherever a law requires relatives to testify.
paras.zh: 《論語》裡有一個案例，把這三者分得比任何電車都乾淨。葉公對孔子說：「吾黨有直躬者，其父攘羊，而子證之。」孔子回答：「吾黨之直者異於是：父為子隱，子為父隱，直在其中矣。」葉公代表的是不偏私的法。偷就是偷，正義不問偷的人是誰。孔子主張：親子之間的連結是一切道德情感的根；一個子女告發父母的社會，已經把那條根砍斷了，不管它找回了多少隻羊。墨子會站在葉公那一邊；照多數的讀法，康德也會，不過他會補充：沒有人問，兒子就不必主動說。亞里斯多德把《倫理學》的兩卷給了友愛與家庭，他比較接近孔子。凡是法律要求親屬作證的地方，這場爭論今天都還活著。

paras.en: It would be convenient if one theory were simply correct. Two centuries of argument have not produced a winner, and many philosophers now doubt that there will be one. Derek Parfit spent his last years arguing that the best versions of the three are “climbing the same mountain on different sides.” The Oxford philosopher W. D. Ross held that we have several distinct duties, to keep faith, to do good, to avoid harm, to be just, and that no formula ranks them. When they conflict we can only weigh them in the case before us, which brings back Mencius’s word quán.
paras.zh: 如果其中一種理論就是正確的，那會很方便。兩個世紀的爭論並沒有產生贏家，而許多哲學家現在懷疑將來也不會有。帕菲特晚年一直在論證：這三者最好的版本，是在「從不同的側面攀登同一座山」。牛津的哲學家羅斯主張：我們有好幾種各不相同的義務，守信、行善、避免傷害、公正，而沒有任何公式為它們排出高下。當它們衝突的時候，我們只能在眼前的個案裡權衡它們；這就把孟子的那個「權」字帶回來了。

paras.en: In the meantime the theories can be used as lenses. Faced with a hard choice, one can ask three questions in turn. What will happen to everyone affected if I do this? Could I accept everyone’s acting on the principle I am about to act on, and am I using anyone? What would this choice make of me, and what would a person I admire do? When the three answers agree, as they do for the shopkeeper, one can act with confidence. When they disagree, one has at least found out where the difficulty lies.
paras.zh: 在這之前，這些理論可以當作鏡片來用。面對一個困難的抉擇，可以依序問三個問題。如果我這樣做，所有受影響的人會怎麼樣？我能不能接受每個人都依照我即將依照的這條原則去行動？我有沒有在利用任何人？這個抉擇會把我造就成什麼樣的人？一個我敬佩的人會怎麼做？當三個答案一致的時候（就像那位店主的情況），人可以有把握地行動。當它們不一致的時候，至少已經找出困難在哪裡了。

lab.title_en: Try it: three dilemmas, four advisers
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：三個兩難，四位顧問
lab.lead_en: Decide each case yourself. Then hear what Mill, Kant, Aristotle, and Confucius would advise and why. At the end you will see whose advice you followed most often.
lab.lead_zh: 每一個案例都先自己決定。然後聽聽彌爾、康德、亞里斯多德與孔子各會怎麼建議、為什麼。最後你會看到，你最常聽從的是誰的建議。

text.en: Your friend has run into your house and hidden. A man with a knife knocks and asks whether she is inside. You are sure that he means to kill her, and that he will believe whatever you say.
text.zh: 你的朋友跑進你家躲了起來。一個拿著刀的男人來敲門，問她是不是在裡面。你確定他是要殺她，也確定不管你說什麼他都會相信。

t.en: Lie: “She is not here.”
t.zh: 說謊：「她不在這裡。」

t.en: Do not lie.
t.zh: 不說謊。

t.en: Lie. A life is at stake, and the harm of one falsehood told to a murderer is trivial beside it. The rule against lying exists because truthfulness is useful, and here it would be disastrous.
t.zh: 說謊。一條人命攸關；對一個兇手說一句假話的害處，跟它比起來微不足道。「不可說謊」這條規則之所以存在，是因為誠實有用；而在這裡，誠實會是一場災難。

t.en: Do not lie. Kant gave this answer in 1797. You may shut the door or refuse to speak, but to state a falsehood is to wrong humanity in general. Many Kantians today think he misapplied his own test: a maxim of deceiving those who are themselves using you to commit murder can be universalized.
t.zh: 不說謊。康德在 1797 年給了這個答案。你可以關上門，也可以拒絕開口；但說出一句假話，就是對一般的人性行了不義。今天許多康德學者認為，他誤用了自己的檢驗：「欺騙那些正在利用你去殺人的人」這條準則，是可以普遍化的。

t.en: Lie. Truthfulness is a virtue, and so is loyalty to a friend, and the person of practical wisdom sees which matters here without needing a rule. To tell the truth at this door would show a lack of judgment.
t.zh: 說謊。誠實是一項德行，對朋友的忠誠也是；有實踐智慧的人不需要規則，就看得出這裡哪一個要緊。在這扇門前說實話，顯示的是缺乏判斷。

t.en: Lie. “A man who insists on keeping his word and seeing his actions through, with no flexibility: that is a small man” (Analects 13.20). Mencius adds that the great man’s words need not be kept to the letter. He goes where rightness is.
t.zh: 說謊。「言必信，行必果，硜硜然小人哉。」（《論語》13.20）孟子補充：「大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。」

text.en: You discover that your father has taken a sum of money from the association he works for. No one else knows. It will probably never be noticed, and the members will each be a little poorer.
text.zh: 你發現你父親從他任職的協會拿走了一筆錢。沒有別人知道。這件事大概永遠不會被發現，而每一位會員會稍微窮一點。

t.en: Report him.
t.zh: 舉發他。

t.en: Keep silent, and press him privately to return it.
t.zh: 保持沉默，私下勸他還回去。

t.en: Probably report him, if private pressure fails. The members’ loss is real, and the fact that the thief is your father gives his interests no extra weight. Mill would count the damage to trust within families too, so the answer depends on the sums.
t.zh: 如果私下勸說無效，大概要舉發他。會員的損失是真實的；而那個偷東西的人是你父親這件事，並沒有讓他的利益多出任何分量。彌爾也會把「家庭內部信任受損」算進去，所以答案取決於那筆總帳。

t.en: You may not help him conceal it, and you may not lie if asked. Justice is owed to the members as persons. Kant does not say that you must denounce him unprompted, but a policy of shielding one’s own relatives from the law cannot be willed as a law for all.
t.zh: 你不可以幫他隱瞞；如果有人問，你也不可以說謊。對那些會員，你負有以人相待的正義義務。康德並沒有說你必須主動告發他；但是「庇護自己的親屬、使其不受法律制裁」這條方針，是無法被意願成一條人人適用的法則的。

t.en: Keep silent and work on him. What we owe a father is different from what we owe a stranger, and a son who hands his father to the magistrates has failed in something basic. But the money must go back. A good son is not an accomplice.
t.zh: 保持沉默，並且在他身上下工夫。我們對父親所負的，與對陌生人所負的不同；一個把父親交給官府的兒子，在某件根本的事情上失敗了。但是錢必須還回去。好兒子不是共犯。

t.en: Keep silent. “A father covers for his son, and a son covers for his father. Uprightness lies in that” (Analects 13.18). The son’s duty is to remonstrate, gently and repeatedly, until the father puts it right.
t.zh: 保持沉默。「父為子隱，子為父隱，直在其中矣。」（《論語》13.18）兒子的責任是勸諫，溫和而一再地勸，直到父親把事情改正。

text.en: A dying friend gave you his savings and made you promise to deliver them to his nephew. No one else knows. The nephew is rich and idle and will gamble the money away. The village clinic, which is about to close, could run for a year on it.
text.zh: 一位臨終的朋友把他的積蓄交給你，要你答應把錢交給他的姪子。沒有別人知道。那個姪子有錢又遊手好閒，會把這筆錢賭光。村裡那間快要關門的診所，靠這筆錢可以再撐一年。

t.en: Keep the promise.
t.zh: 遵守承諾。

t.en: Give the money to the clinic.
t.zh: 把錢給診所。

t.en: Give it to the clinic, if you are sure no one will ever know. The good done is far greater. Mill himself would hesitate: the practice of keeping promises to the dying is so valuable that he would want a very clear case before breaking it. A strict act-utilitarian would not hesitate.
t.zh: 把錢給診所，只要你確定永遠不會有人知道。這樣成就的善大得多。彌爾本人會猶豫：對臨終者守信這個慣例太有價值了，他會要求非常明確的情況才肯打破它。一位嚴格的行為效益主義者則不會猶豫。

t.en: Keep the promise. You could not will that everyone should break deathbed promises when they judged that better use could be made of the money, since no one could then make such a promise at all. The money was never yours to redirect.
t.zh: 遵守承諾。你無法意願「每個人只要判斷這筆錢有更好的用途，就打破臨終的承諾」，因為那樣一來，根本就沒有人能許下這種承諾了。這筆錢從來就不是你可以改派的。

t.en: Keep the promise, most likely. A person of good character keeps faith with a friend, and would feel the breach as a stain on himself. He might also give something of his own to the clinic. Aristotle would add that the case cannot be settled in the abstract.
t.zh: 多半是遵守承諾。品格好的人對朋友守信，並且會覺得背信是自己身上的一塊污點。他也許還會自己另外拿出一些東西給診所。亞里斯多德會補充：這個案例無法抽象地解決。

t.en: Keep the promise. Trustworthiness toward a friend is one of the five relationships, and the dead man’s wishes concern his own family, which is his to provide for. Then go and speak to the nephew about the clinic.
t.zh: 遵守承諾。對朋友的「信」屬於五倫；而亡友的心願關乎他自己的家人，那是該由他來安排的。然後，去找那個姪子談談診所的事。

mill.en: You sided most often with Mill. You look first at what will happen to the people affected. The case that should worry you is the third, where the best outcome required you to break faith in secret.
mill.zh: 你最常站在彌爾這一邊。你首先看的是受影響的人會怎麼樣。應該讓你不安的是第三個案例：在那裡，最好的結果需要你暗中背信。

kant.en: You sided most often with Kant. You look first for the principle and ask whether you could accept everyone’s acting on it. The case that should worry you is the first, where the principle seemed to hand a friend to her killer.
kant.zh: 你最常站在康德這一邊。你首先找的是原則，並且問自己能不能接受每個人都照它行動。應該讓你不安的是第一個案例：在那裡，原則似乎把一位朋友交給了要殺她的人。

ari.en: You sided most often with Aristotle. You trust judgment formed by experience over any formula. The question to ask yourself is how you would explain your three decisions to someone who did not already share your sense of what a good person does.
ari.zh: 你最常站在亞里斯多德這一邊。比起任何公式，你更信任由經驗形成的判斷。該問自己的問題是：對一個原本並不認同你對「好人會怎麼做」的感覺的人，你要怎麼解釋你的三個決定？

kong.en: You sided most often with Confucius. You begin from the relationships you stand in and reason outward from them. The case that should worry you is the second. The members of the association are someone’s parents too.
kong.zh: 你最常站在孔子這一邊。你從自己所處的關係出發，再由此向外推。應該讓你不安的是第二個案例。那個協會的會員，也是某些人的父母。

virtue.en: You sided every time with Aristotle and Confucius, who gave the same advice in all three cases. That agreement is worth noticing. Two traditions with no contact between them both put their trust in the judgment of a well-formed person over any formula, and both give special weight to family and friends. The question to ask yourself is how you would explain your decisions to someone who did not already share your sense of what a good person does, and whether the members of the association in the second case would accept the explanation.
virtue.zh: 你每一次都站在亞里斯多德與孔子這一邊；而他們在三個案例裡給的建議完全相同。這份一致值得留意。兩個彼此毫無接觸的傳統，都把信任交給一個養成得好的人的判斷，而不是任何公式；也都給了家人與朋友特別的分量。該問自己的問題是：對一個原本並不認同你對「好人會怎麼做」的感覺的人，你要怎麼解釋你的決定？還有，第二個案例裡那個協會的會員，會不會接受這個解釋？

tie.en: No single adviser had your vote more often than the others, as the bars show. That is where most reflective people end up: using each theory where it sees most clearly. Look at the case where you parted from each adviser, and ask what you saw there that the theory did not.
tie.zh: 如上面的長條所示，沒有哪一位顧問比其他人更常得到你的一票。多數會反思的人最後都落在這裡：哪一種理論在哪裡看得最清楚，就在哪裡用它。看看你跟每一位顧問分道揚鑣的那個案例，問問自己：你在那裡看到了什麼是那個理論沒看到的？

argument.lead_en: Kant’s test applied to his own example, the promise one does not mean to keep. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 康德的檢驗，用在他自己的例子上：一個並不打算兌現的承諾。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: An act is permissible only if I can will its maxim, the principle I am acting on, as a law for everyone.
steps.zh: 一個行為是許可的，唯有當我能夠意願它的準則（我據以行動的那條原則）成為人人適用的法則。
steps.ob_en: This is the categorical imperative, and the theory stands or falls with it. Mill objected that when Kant applies it he quietly appeals to consequences: the trouble with universal lying is that things would go badly.
steps.ob_zh: 這就是定言令式；整個理論隨它而立，也隨它而倒。彌爾反對說：康德在運用它的時候，悄悄訴諸了後果；「人人說謊」的問題，就在於事情會變糟。

steps.en: My maxim is: when I need money, I will borrow it with a promise to repay that I know I cannot keep.
steps.zh: 我的準則是：當我需要錢的時候，我就去借，並且許下一個我明知無法兌現的還錢承諾。
steps.ob_en: The weak point of the method lies here. The same act can be described under many maxims. If I describe mine very narrowly, as applying to people in exactly my situation on a Tuesday, universalizing it does no harm. Kant gives no rule for finding the right description.
steps.ob_zh: 這個方法的弱點就在這裡。同一個行為，可以用許多不同的準則來描述。如果我把我的準則描述得非常窄，只適用於某個星期二處境跟我一模一樣的人，那麼把它普遍化也無害。康德並沒有給出找到「正確描述」的規則。

steps.en: If everyone acted on this maxim, no one would believe such promises, and promising would be impossible.
steps.zh: 如果每個人都依照這條準則行動，就沒有人會相信這種承諾，而許諾這件事也就不可能了。
steps.ob_en: Rarely disputed. The contradiction Kant finds is practical: the plan needs an institution that the plan, made universal, would destroy.
steps.ob_zh: 很少有爭議。康德找到的矛盾是實踐上的：這個計畫需要一個制度，而這個計畫一旦普遍化，就會摧毀那個制度。

steps.en: So I cannot will my maxim as a universal law, and the false promise is forbidden.
steps.zh: 所以，我無法意願我的準則成為普遍法則；那個假承諾是被禁止的。
steps.ob_en: The test works well on free riding, where I profit from a practice that others keep up. It gives odd results elsewhere. “I will always let others go through the door first” cannot be universalized either, and nothing is wrong with it.
steps.ob_zh: 這個檢驗用在「搭便車」上很有效：別人維持著一個慣例，而我從中得利。用在別處，它會給出古怪的結果。「我永遠讓別人先過門」同樣無法普遍化，而它並沒有什麼不對。

source.work: Kant, Fundamental Principles of the Metaphysic of Morals (1785); Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.6
source.work_zh: 康德《道德形上學基礎》；亞里斯多德《尼各馬可倫理學》卷二第六章
source.tr: tr. T. K. Abbott; tr. W. D. Ross (both public domain; original wording kept)
source.lead_en: The first sentence of Kant’s book and the central definition of Aristotle’s. Each states a whole theory in a few lines.
source.lead_zh: 康德那本書的第一句話，以及亞里斯多德那本書的核心定義。兩者都用幾行字陳述了一整套理論。

passages.en: Nothing can possibly be conceived in the world, or even out of it, which can be called good, without qualification, except a good will. … There is therefore but one categorical imperative, namely, this: Act only on that maxim whereby thou canst at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
passages.zh: 在世界之內，甚至在世界之外，除了一個善的意志，不可能設想任何東西可以無條件地稱為善。……因此，定言令式只有一個，就是：你要只依照這樣的準則行動：你能夠同時意願它成為一條普遍法則。
passages.note_en: “Without qualification” is the key phrase. Kant does not deny that happiness, health, and talent are good. He says that their goodness depends on how they are used, and that the will to do right is the one thing whose goodness depends on nothing else. An imperative is “categorical” when it commands without an “if.” “If you want to be trusted, do not lie” is hypothetical and binds only those who want to be trusted. “Do not lie” binds everyone. (The second sentence comes from the Second Section of the book. “Thou canst” is the translator’s Victorian English for “you can.”)
passages.note_zh: 「無條件地」是關鍵的措辭。康德並沒有否認幸福、健康與才能是善的。他說的是：它們的善取決於怎麼被使用；而「要做對的事」的那個意志，是唯一一樣其善不取決於任何別的東西的。一條令式，當它不帶「如果」而下命令的時候，就是「定言的」。「如果你想被信任，就不要說謊」是假言的，只約束那些想被信任的人。「不要說謊」約束每一個人。（第二句出自該書的第二章。thou canst 是譯者那個維多利亞時代的英文，意思就是 you can。）

passages.en: Virtue, then, is a state of character concerned with choice, lying in a mean, i.e. the mean relative to us, this being determined by a rational principle, and by that principle by which the man of practical wisdom would determine it.
passages.zh: 那麼，德行就是一種與抉擇有關的品格狀態；它在於一種中道，也就是相對於我們的中道；這個中道是由理性的原則決定的，也就是由有實踐智慧的人會據以決定它的那個原則決定的。
passages.note_en: Every phrase carries weight. A “state of character” is a lasting disposition, as against a passing feeling or a single act. “Concerned with choice” means that virtue shows in what we decide and not in what merely happens to us. “Relative to us” means that the right amount differs with the person and the situation: the athlete’s diet is too much for the beginner. And the last clause refers the whole matter to a kind of person. Critics call this circular. Aristotle would reply that it is how every skill is learned. We learn what good medicine is from good doctors before we can state the principles ourselves.
passages.note_zh: 每一個詞組都有分量。「品格狀態」是一種持久的傾向，相對於一時的感受或單一的行為。「與抉擇有關」的意思是：德行顯現在我們所決定的事上，而不是在僅僅發生在我們身上的事上。「相對於我們」的意思是：恰當的分量隨人與情境而不同；運動員的飲食，對初學者來說太多了。而最後一個子句，把整件事交給了某一種人。批評者說這是循環。亞里斯多德會回答：每一種技藝都是這樣學會的。我們先從好醫師身上學到什麼是好的醫術，然後才有辦法自己說出其中的原則。

items.o_en: If the experts have disagreed for two thousand years, there is no fact of the matter. Ethics is opinion.
items.o_zh: 如果專家們爭論了兩千年還沒有共識，那就表示根本沒有事實可言。倫理學只是意見。
items.r_en: The disagreement is narrower than it looks. All three theories condemn cruelty, cheating, and cowardice and commend honesty and generosity. They differ over the explanation and over a small number of hard cases. Physics is in a similar state: its practitioners agree about what will happen when a ball is dropped and argue about what quantum theory means. Lasting dispute over foundations is compatible with a great deal of knowledge.
items.r_zh: 這個分歧比看起來的窄。三種理論都譴責殘忍、欺騙與怯懦，都讚許誠實與慷慨。它們的分歧在於「解釋」，以及為數不多的困難案例。物理學也處於類似的狀態：物理學家對於一顆球放手後會怎樣意見一致，卻對量子理論是什麼意思爭論不休。對基礎的長久爭論，與擁有大量的知識是可以並存的。

items.o_en: Kant’s ethics is cold. It says that a man who helps others because he loves them deserves less credit than one who helps from duty while feeling nothing.
items.o_zh: 康德的倫理學是冷的。它說：一個因為愛人而幫助別人的人，比一個毫無感覺、只是出於義務而幫忙的人，更不值得稱許。
items.r_en: The poet Schiller made the joke in Kant’s lifetime: I gladly serve my friends, but alas, I do it with pleasure. Kant’s point was narrower. He wanted to isolate what gives an act its moral worth, and chose cases where inclination is absent so that duty could be seen working alone. He did not say that warm feelings are bad. He held that they are unreliable, since they come and go and do not extend to people we dislike, and that morality must not depend on them. Aristotle’s reply is that a person who has to force himself is not yet good.
items.r_zh: 詩人席勒在康德在世時就開過這個玩笑：我樂於為朋友效勞，可惜啊，我是帶著愉快去做的。康德的重點比較窄。他想要把「賦予一個行為道德價值的東西」分離出來，所以選了沒有愛好參與的情況，好讓義務單獨運作時可以被看見。他並沒有說溫暖的情感是壞的。他主張的是：情感靠不住，因為它們來來去去，而且延伸不到我們不喜歡的人身上；道德不可以依賴它們。亞里斯多德的回應是：一個必須勉強自己的人，還不算是好人。

items.o_en: Virtue ethics gives no guidance. “Be brave, be just” tells me nothing when I do not know what bravery or justice requires here.
items.o_zh: 德行倫理學不給指引。當我不知道勇敢或公正在這裡要求什麼的時候，「要勇敢，要公正」什麼也沒告訴我。
items.r_en: Its defenders answer that the other theories do no better in hard cases, where the utilitarian cannot make the calculation and the Kantian cannot find the right maxim. What virtue ethics offers is different in kind. It gives a vocabulary of several hundred words, such as callous, petty, loyal, and fair, each of which carries guidance, and it directs attention to education, since a person who has been brought up well will see what to do where a formula would fail. Confucian ethics rests on the same wager.
items.r_zh: 為它辯護的人回答：在困難的案例裡，另外兩種理論也沒有做得更好；效益主義者算不出那筆帳，康德主義者找不到正確的準則。德行倫理學提供的是另一種東西。它給了一套好幾百個詞的語彙，例如冷酷、小氣、忠誠、公平，每一個詞都帶著指引；它並且把注意力導向教育，因為一個教養得好的人，在公式失靈的地方看得出該怎麼做。儒家倫理押的是同一注。

said.claim: “Kant’s categorical imperative is the Golden Rule in philosophical dress.”
said.claim_zh: 「康德的定言令式，就是穿上哲學外衣的金律。」
said.en: The comparison is made in countless textbooks, and Kant rejected it in a footnote to the Groundwork: “Let it not be thought that the common quod tibi non vis fieri, etc.” (what you do not wish done to yourself) “could serve here as the rule or principle.” His reasons are sharp. The Golden Rule appeals to what I happen to want, so a man who is content to receive no help could use it to excuse himself from helping. And a criminal could invoke it against the judge who sentences him. Kant’s test asks what a rational being could will as a law, whatever anyone’s wishes. Confucius had given the negative form more than two thousand years earlier, when asked for one word to live by: “Is it not reciprocity? What you do not want for yourself, do not do to others.”
said.zh: 無數的教科書都作過這個類比；而康德在《道德形上學基礎》的一個註腳裡否定了它：「不要以為那句通俗的 quod tibi non vis fieri（己所不欲）之類的話，可以在這裡充當準繩或原則。」他的理由很銳利。金律訴諸的是我碰巧想要什麼；所以一個甘願得不到任何幫助的人，可以拿它來為自己不幫助別人開脫。而一個罪犯，可以拿它來對付判他刑的法官。康德的檢驗問的是：一個理性的存在者能夠意願什麼成為法則，不管任何人的願望是什麼。孔子早在兩千多年前就給了它否定式的表述；有人請他說出一個可以終身奉行的字，他說：「其恕乎！己所不欲，勿施於人。」

terms.d_en: The part of ethics that asks what makes acts right and lives good.
terms.d_zh: 倫理學當中探問「什麼使行為對、使人生好」的部分。

terms.d_en: Kant’s supreme principle: a command that binds every rational being whatever its desires.
terms.d_zh: 康德的最高原則：一條不管欲望為何、都約束每一個理性存在者的命令。

terms.d_en: The personal principle on which one acts.
terms.d_zh: 一個人據以行動的個人原則。

terms.d_en: The settled resolve to do what is right because it is right.
terms.d_zh: 「因為對所以去做對的事」的那份穩定的決心。

terms.d_en: Aristotle’s term for the good human life. “Flourishing” is closer than “happiness.”
terms.d_zh: 亞里斯多德對「美好的人生」的用語。譯作 flourishing 比 happiness 貼切。

terms.d_en: A settled trait of character that makes its possessor act and feel well.
terms.d_zh: 一種穩定的品格特質，使擁有它的人行動得好、感受得好。

terms.d_en: The trained ability to see what a situation calls for.
terms.d_zh: 看出一個情境需要什麼的那種經過訓練的能力。

terms.d_en: The right amount of a feeling or action, between excess and deficiency.
terms.d_zh: 一種感受或行動的恰當分量，位於過度與不足之間。

vocab.eg: He counts it out correctly.
vocab.eg_zh: 他把零錢一分不少地數了出來。

vocab.eg: The act is right because of what it brings about.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個行為是對的，因為它帶來的結果。

vocab.eg: It has no place for the claim that my happiness matters more.
vocab.eg_zh: 它容不下「我的幸福比較重要」這個主張。

vocab.eg: Intelligence and courage can be put to bad use.
vocab.eg_zh: 聰明與勇氣都可能被拿去做壞事。

vocab.eg: I am making an exception of myself.
vocab.eg_zh: 我是在把自己當成例外。

vocab.eg: A virtue is a settled trait of character.
vocab.eg_zh: 一項德行是一種穩定的品格特質。

vocab.eg: Each theory has a case that embarrasses it.
vocab.eg_zh: 每一種理論都有一個讓它難堪的案例。

vocab.eg: A father covers for his son.
vocab.eg_zh: 父親替兒子隱瞞。

vocab.eg: Mozi would have sided with the governor.
vocab.eg_zh: 墨子會站在葉公那一邊。

vocab.eg: In the meantime the theories can be used as lenses.
vocab.eg_zh: 在這之前，這些理論可以當作鏡片來用。

quiz.q: Why, for Kant, might the honest shopkeeper’s act have no moral worth?
options: If he is honest only because cheating would hurt his business.
Because honesty is not a duty.
Because the child is too young.
Because shopkeepers cannot be moral.

quiz.q: What is wrong with the false promise, on Kant’s test?
options: The plan works only if others do not act the same way, so it cannot be willed as a law for all.
It makes the borrower unhappy.
Promises are always wrong.
It is forbidden by religion.

quiz.q: What does Aristotle mean by the mean?
options: Feeling and acting in the right amount for the situation, as a wise person would judge.
The mathematical average of two actions.
Always choosing moderation in everything.
Doing what most people do.

quiz.q: What is the standard objection to virtue ethics?
options: Telling me to do what a virtuous person would do seems to presuppose that I already know what is right.
It cares too much about consequences.
It forbids all lying.
It has too many rules.

quiz.q: In the case of Upright Gong, what does Confucius say?
options: Fathers and sons cover for each other, and uprightness lies in that.
The son was right to give evidence.
The sheep should be returned and the father punished.
Law is more important than family.

write.en: Take a decision you made this month and look at it through the three lenses. Did they agree?
write.zh: 拿你這個月做過的一個決定，用三面鏡片各看一次。它們一致嗎？

write.en: Was Upright Gong right to give evidence against his father? Defend your answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 直躬出面指證父親，做得對嗎？用大約 150 個英文字為你的答案辯護。

write.en: Kant says that a person who helps others only from sympathy has not yet shown moral worth. Do you agree?
write.zh: 康德說，一個只是出於同情而幫助別人的人，還沒有顯出道德價值。你同意嗎？

paras.en: All three lenses are found in the Buddha’s teaching, and none is made the foundation. He tells his young son Rāhula to examine every act before, during, and after doing it, as one looks in a mirror, and to ask: does this “lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both?” That is a test by consequences. He gives lay followers five precepts and monastics several hundred rules, which look like duties. And he says that what makes an act unwholesome is its root in greed, hatred, or delusion, and sums up the whole teaching as “not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind,” which is the language of character.
paras.zh: 這三面鏡片在佛陀的教導裡都找得到，而沒有哪一面被當作地基。他告訴年幼的兒子羅睺羅：每一個行為，在做之前、做的時候、做了之後，都要像照鏡子那樣檢視它，並且問：這會不會「導致傷害自己、傷害別人，或兩者都傷害」？那是一個依後果的檢驗。他給在家弟子五戒，給出家眾好幾百條戒律，那些看起來像義務。而他又說，使一個行為成為不善的，是它根植於貪、瞋或癡；並且把整個教導總結為「諸惡莫作，眾善奉行，自淨其意」，那是品格的語言。

paras.en: Modern scholars have argued over which Western theory this most resembles. One camp reads it as a virtue ethics close to Aristotle’s, and another reads the Mahāyāna as a form of consequentialism aimed at the welfare of all beings. A companion page examines the question and gives a verdict.
paras.zh: 現代的學者一直在爭論：這最像西方的哪一種理論？一派把它讀成接近亞里斯多德的德行倫理學；另一派把大乘讀成一種以一切眾生福祉為目標的後果論。姊妹篇會檢視這個問題，並且給出判定。

link.en: Read D18 · What Kind of Ethics Is Buddhist Ethics?
link.zh: 讀 D18・佛教倫理是哪一種倫理學？

further.t: Immanuel Kant, Fundamental Principles of the Metaphysic of Morals, translated by T. K. Abbott
further.n_en: The First and Second Sections. Sixty hard and rewarding pages.
further.n_zh: 第一章與第二章。六十頁，難讀而值得。

further.t: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Books I and II, translated by W. D. Ross
J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism
Analects 13.18, 13.20, and 15.24; Mozi, “Impartial Caring”
further.n_en: Upright Gong, the small man who must keep his word, and the single word to live by.
further.n_zh: 直躬、言必信的小人，以及可以終身行之的那一個字。

further.t: James Rachels, The Elements of Moral Philosophy
further.n_en: The clearest short textbook on all three theories.
further.n_zh: 介紹這三種理論最清楚的短篇教科書。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Virtue Ethics” and “Kant’s Moral Philosophy”

lessons.title: Why Be Good If No One Is Watching?
lessons.title_zh: 沒人看見，為什麼還要做好人？
lessons.blurb_en: A shepherd finds a ring that makes him invisible, and an official is offered gold at midnight. Plato, Hobbes, Kant, and the Doctrine of the Mean on whether a person with nothing to fear has any reason to be just.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一個牧羊人撿到一枚能讓他隱形的戒指；一位官員在半夜有人送上黃金。柏拉圖、霍布斯、康德與《中庸》，談一個毫無顧忌的人，還有沒有理由行正義。
lessons.big_en: The last two lessons asked what makes an act right. This one asks why anyone should care. If the only reasons for doing right are reward and the fear of being caught, then a person who could never be caught has no reason at all.
lessons.big_zh: 前兩課問的是：什麼使一個行為是對的？這一課問的是：為什麼有人該在乎？如果做對的事唯一的理由是獎賞與怕被抓，那麼一個永遠不會被抓的人，就根本沒有理由了。

paras.en: Early in the second century CE the official Yang Zhen was traveling to a new post and stopped for the night at Changyi. The magistrate of the town owed his career to him. After dark the man came to his lodging with ten catties of gold in his robe. Yang Zhen said, “Your old friend knows you. How is it that you do not know your old friend?” The magistrate answered, “It is late at night. No one will know.” Yang Zhen said, “Heaven knows, the spirits know, I know, and you know. How can you say that no one knows?” The magistrate went out ashamed. The story has been told to Chinese schoolchildren ever since. It contains an argument, and the magistrate’s half of it deserves a hearing. Of the four witnesses named, the first two cannot be produced, and the last two are the only people who stand to gain. What reason is left?
paras.zh: 西元二世紀初，官員楊震赴任新職，途中在昌邑過夜。昌邑的縣令是靠他提拔才有今天的。天黑之後，這個人懷裡揣著十斤黃金，來到他的住處。楊震說：「故人知君，君不知故人，何也？」縣令回答：「暮夜無知者。」楊震說：「天知，神知，我知，子知。何謂無知！」縣令慚愧地出去了。從那以後，這個故事就一直講給中國的學童聽。它裡面有一個論證，而縣令那一半值得聽一聽。被點名的四位見證者當中，前兩位叫不出來作證；後兩位，正好是唯二會得到好處的人。還剩下什麼理由？

paras.en: Plato put the same challenge at the start of the Republic, and put it into the mouth of his own brother. Glaucon says that he does not believe what he is about to argue and wants to hear it refuted. Justice, on the common view, is a compromise. Everyone would like to wrong others freely and suffer no wrong in return. Since that is impossible, people agree to restrain themselves, and they keep the agreement because they are watched. Take away the watching and you will see what they are. A shepherd named Gyges, the story goes, found a gold ring on a corpse in a chasm opened by an earthquake. Sitting among the other shepherds, he happened to turn the setting of the ring inward and found that he had become invisible. He had himself sent to court, seduced the queen, killed the king with her help, and took the kingdom.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖在《理想國》的開頭提出了同樣的挑戰，並且把它放進了自己親兄弟的嘴裡。葛勞康說，他並不相信自己接下來要論證的東西，他是想聽到它被駁倒。照一般的看法，正義是一種妥協。每個人都希望能隨意對別人行不義，自己卻不受任何不義。既然那不可能，人們就約定各自克制；而他們之所以遵守這個約定，是因為有人在看。把「看」拿掉，你就會看到他們的真面目。故事說，一個名叫蓋吉斯的牧羊人，在地震裂開的深谷裡，從一具屍體上撿到一枚金戒指。他坐在其他牧羊人當中，無意間把戒指的戒面轉向掌心，發現自己隱形了。他設法讓自己被派到宮廷，勾引了王后，在她的協助下殺了國王，奪取了王國。

paras.en: Now suppose there were two such rings, Glaucon says, and a just man wore one and an unjust man the other. “No man can be imagined to be of such an iron nature that he would stand fast in justice. No man would keep his hands off what was not his own when he could safely take what he liked out of the market.” The two would end by behaving alike, and this shows that no one is just willingly. He then sharpens the test. Give the unjust man a spotless reputation along with his crimes, and give the just man the reputation of a villain, so that he is whipped and tortured for his goodness. Now say which of the two is better off. To answer Glaucon, one must show that justice is worth having for itself, with every reward removed.
paras.zh: 葛勞康說：現在假設有兩枚這樣的戒指，一個正義的人戴一枚，一個不正義的人戴另一枚。「我們無法想像有任何人的本性堅硬如鐵，能夠堅守正義。只要能夠安然無事地從市場上隨意拿走自己喜歡的東西，沒有人會不對不屬於自己的東西伸手。」兩個人最後的行為會一模一樣；而這就顯示，沒有人是甘願行正義的。接著他把檢驗磨得更利。讓那個不正義的人在犯下種種罪行的同時，享有無瑕的名聲；讓那個正義的人背著惡徒的名聲，為了他的善而受鞭打與拷問。現在說說看，兩人當中誰過得比較好？要回答葛勞康，就必須顯示：把一切獎賞都拿掉之後，正義本身仍然值得擁有。

paras.en: The answer takes Plato the remaining nine books. Its core is a comparison. A soul has parts: reason, spirit, and the appetites. It is in good order when reason governs with the support of spirit, and each part does its own work. That order is what justice in a person is, and injustice is a civil war in which the appetites have seized control. “Virtue is the health and beauty and well-being of the soul, and vice is the disease and weakness and deformity of the soul.” Nobody asks why he should want to be healthy if no one is watching. Once justice is seen to be the health of the thing we live by, Socrates says, the question whether it pays “has become ridiculous.” Gyges with his ring is a man free to feed a disease. Plato describes where that road ends, in the tyrant who can have anything and is the slave of his own cravings, who trusts no one and has no friend.
paras.zh: 這個回答花了柏拉圖其餘的九卷。它的核心是一個類比。靈魂有幾個部分：理性、意氣與欲望。當理性在意氣的支持下治理，而每一個部分各盡其職的時候，靈魂就處於良好的秩序。那個秩序，就是一個人內在的正義；不正義則是一場內戰，欲望在其中奪了權。「德行是靈魂的健康、美與安適；惡是靈魂的疾病、虛弱與畸形。」沒有人會問：如果沒人看見，我為什麼還要想健康？蘇格拉底說，一旦看出正義就是我們賴以生活的那個東西的健康，「它划不划算」這個問題就「變得可笑了」。戴著戒指的蓋吉斯，是一個可以隨意餵養一種疾病的人。柏拉圖描寫了那條路的盡頭：那個什麼都能擁有、卻是自己渴求的奴隸的僭主；他不信任任何人，也沒有朋友。

paras.en: Critics have long asked whether this answers the question that was put. Glaucon asked about justice in the ordinary sense, not stealing, not killing. Socrates replies about an inner harmony. It is not obvious that a man with a well-ordered soul would keep his hands off the market stalls, or that a thief could not be calm and self-controlled. The bridge between the two has to be built, and Plato builds it mostly by assertion.
paras.zh: 批評者一直在問：這有沒有回答被提出來的那個問題？葛勞康問的是日常意義上的正義：不偷、不殺。蘇格拉底答的是一種內在的和諧。一個靈魂井然有序的人，是否就不會對市場的攤子伸手？一個竊賊，是否就不可能冷靜而自制？這並不明顯。兩者之間的那座橋需要有人來搭；而柏拉圖搭它，多半是靠斷言。

paras.en: A second tradition accepts Glaucon’s account of justice as a bargain and denies that the ring exists. Hobbes imagines a “Foole” who says in his heart that there is no such thing as justice and that breaking an agreement is reasonable whenever it pays. Hobbes replies that it never reliably pays. A man who breaks faith must count on not being found out, and no one can count on that. He lives by the errors of others, and if they stop erring he is cast out of the society that keeps him alive. Modern research on cooperation says something similar in the language of games: where people deal with one another repeatedly, a reputation for honesty is the most valuable thing one can own.
paras.zh: 第二個傳統接受葛勞康把正義說成一樁交易，卻否認那枚戒指存在。霍布斯設想了一個「愚人」；他在心裡說，根本沒有正義這回事，只要划算，背約就是合理的。霍布斯回答：它從來不會穩穩地划算。一個背信的人，必須指望不被發現；而沒有人能指望這一點。他靠著別人的失誤過活；一旦別人不再失誤，他就會被逐出那個使他得以活命的社會。現代對合作的研究，用賽局的語言說了類似的話：在人們反覆打交道的地方，誠實的名聲是一個人所能擁有的最有價值的東西。

paras.en: The reply is sound as far as it goes, and it concedes the main point. It says that we should be just because we are always, in effect, watched. It has nothing to say to the person who really does hold the ring. Experiments suggest that such a person is not rare. When people are given a chance to cheat a little without any risk of discovery, a large number do, and they cheat less when a picture of a pair of eyes is hung on the wall.
paras.zh: 就它所及的範圍而言，這個回答是站得住的；而它讓出了要點。它說的是：我們應該行正義，因為我們實際上永遠有人在看。對於一個真的握著那枚戒指的人，它無話可說。實驗顯示，這樣的人並不罕見。當人們得到一個可以稍微作弊、而且毫無被發現之虞的機會時，為數不少的人會作弊；而當牆上掛著一張畫著一雙眼睛的圖片時，他們作弊得比較少。

paras.en: The Confucian classics take up the case of the unobserved person directly, and their answer begins by denying that he is unobserved. The Doctrine of the Mean says: “Nothing is more visible than what is hidden, and nothing more manifest than what is minute. Therefore the gentleman is watchful over himself when he is alone.” The Great Learning explains the paradox. The petty man, when he is by himself, stops at nothing. When he sees a gentleman he tries to cover it up, and it does him no good, because others see him “as if they saw his lungs and liver.” What is real within takes shape without. And it begins with a rule against lying to oneself: one should hate what is bad as one hates a foul smell.
paras.zh: 儒家的經典直接處理了「沒人看見的人」這個情況；而它們的回答，是從否認「他沒人看見」開始的。《中庸》說：「莫見乎隱，莫顯乎微，故君子慎其獨也。」《大學》解釋了這個弔詭。「小人閒居為不善，無所不至」；見到君子就想遮掩，卻毫無用處，因為別人看他「如見其肺肝然」。「誠於中，形於外。」而這一切，是從一條不許對自己說謊的規則開始的：「所謂誠其意者，毋自欺也。如惡惡臭。」

paras.en: Two claims are packed together here. One is a claim about character. A person is made by what he does repeatedly, and most of what anyone does is done unobserved, so the private hour is where one becomes what one publicly is. The ring would not hide Gyges from the one observer who is always present and whose opinion he must live with. This is Yang Zhen’s “I know,” and it is why Confucius says of the gentleman that if he looks within and finds nothing to be ashamed of, he has nothing to fear. The other claim is about knowledge. We are poor at hiding what we are, and a habit of small dishonesty shows in the face. The first claim is close to Plato’s. Neither Plato nor the Confucians think that the just person is paying a price in private for a public good.
paras.zh: 這裡有兩個主張被包在一起。一個是關於品格的主張。人是由他反覆做的事造就的；而任何人做的事，大部分都是在沒人看見的時候做的；所以，獨處的那個小時，正是一個人變成他在公開場合所是的那個人的地方。戒指藏不住蓋吉斯，使他不被那位永遠在場、而他必須與其評價共處的觀察者看見。這就是楊震的「我知」；孔子說君子「內省不疚，夫何憂何懼」，也是這個道理。另一個是關於認識的主張。我們並不擅長隱藏自己是什麼樣的人；小小不誠實的習慣，會寫在臉上。第一個主張很接近柏拉圖。柏拉圖與儒家都不認為，正義的人是在私底下為一項公共的善付出代價。

essay.h_zh: 這個問題本身是個錯誤嗎？

paras.en: Kant would say that every answer so far has made the same error. Each tries to show that justice pays, in health of soul or safety or peace of mind. But a person who is honest because honesty pays is the prudent shopkeeper of the last lesson, whose acts accord with duty and have no moral worth. To ask “What do I get for being good?” is already to have left the moral point of view. The reason to give back the gold is that it is not yours. The Oxford philosopher H. A. Prichard argued in 1912 that moral philosophy had rested on this mistake since Plato: it kept trying to prove that we ought to do our duty by appeal to something else, when the obligation is seen directly or not at all.
paras.zh: 康德會說，到目前為止的每一個回答都犯了同一個錯。它們各自都試圖顯示正義是划算的，換來的是靈魂的健康、安全，或心安。然而，一個因為誠實划算才誠實的人，就是上一課那位精明的店主；他的行為合乎義務，卻沒有道德價值。問「我做好人能得到什麼？」，就已經離開了道德的觀點。把黃金還回去的理由是：那不是你的。牛津的哲學家普里查德在 1912 年論證：道德哲學自柏拉圖以來，一直建立在這個錯誤上；它不斷試圖訴諸別的東西，來證明我們應當盡自己的義務；而義務這回事，要嘛直接被看見，要嘛根本看不見。

paras.en: That leaves the reader with a choice among kinds of reason. One may hold with Hobbes that the ring is a fiction and honesty is the best policy. One may hold with Plato and the Confucians that injustice damages the person who does it, whether or not anyone finds out. Or one may hold with Kant that the request for a further reason is a confusion. The question is less remote than it was. A great deal of modern life is conducted under conditions that Glaucon would have recognized: anonymous, at a distance, with little chance of being held to account. How people behave there is the old experiment, run every day on a very large scale.
paras.zh: 這就讓讀者在幾種理由之間作選擇。可以跟霍布斯一樣主張：戒指是虛構的，誠實是上策。可以跟柏拉圖與儒家一樣主張：不管有沒有人發現，不正義都會損害行不義的那個人。也可以跟康德一樣主張：要求一個「更進一步的理由」，本身就是一種混淆。這個問題不像從前那麼遙遠了。現代生活有很大一部分，是在葛勞康認得出來的條件下進行的：匿名、隔著距離、幾乎不必負責。人們在那裡怎麼表現，就是那個古老的實驗；它每天都在以極大的規模進行著。

lab.title_en: Try it: wear the ring
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：戴上戒指
lab.lead_en: You have the ring of Gyges. In each of four situations nobody can see you and nobody will ever find out. Decide what you would do, and if you hold back, say why. At the end you will see which kind of reason is doing the work.
lab.lead_zh: 蓋吉斯的戒指在你手上。在下面四個情境裡，沒有人看得見你，也永遠不會有人發現。決定你會怎麼做；如果你收手，說出為什麼。最後你會看到，真正在起作用的是哪一種理由。

turned.en: You are invisible. Nothing you do from here on can be traced to you.
turned.zh: 你隱形了。從現在起，你做的任何事都追查不到你身上。

why.en: Why not? Choose the reason that weighs most with you.
why.zh: 為什麼不做？選出對你來說分量最重的那個理由。

t.en: Something could still go wrong. I might be found out.
t.zh: 還是可能出差錯。我也許會被發現。

t.en: I would know. I could not be at ease afterward.
t.zh: 我自己會知道。事後我沒辦法心安。

t.en: I am not that kind of person, and I do not want to become one.
t.zh: 我不是那種人，也不想變成那種人。

t.en: Someone would be wronged, whether or not they ever learn of it.
t.zh: 有人會受到不義的對待，不管他們知不知道。

text.en: Your supervisor’s written assessment of you and your colleagues is lying on her desk. You could read all of it.
text.zh: 主管對你與同事們的書面考評，就攤在她的桌上。你可以全部看完。

text.en: Tomorrow you sit an examination that decides your promotion. The answers are in an unlocked drawer.
text.zh: 明天你要參加一場決定你升遷的考試。答案就放在一個沒上鎖的抽屜裡。

text.en: A large company’s cash box is open. You could take a month’s salary. The loss would be written off, and no person would be blamed.
text.zh: 一家大公司的錢箱開著。你可以拿走一個月的薪水。這筆損失會被當成呆帳沖銷，不會有任何人被追究。
