text.en: One other candidate stands between you and the post you have wanted for ten years. You could remove her application from the pile.
text.zh: 在你與那個你想了十年的職位之間，只隔著另一位候選人。你可以把她的申請書從那一疊裡抽掉。

did.en: You did most of these things. You are the man Glaucon describes, and you have at least been honest about it. Plato’s reply is addressed to you. He asks you to look ahead to what a person becomes who takes whatever he can safely take: someone whose wants grow with every success, who can trust no one because he knows what people do in the dark, and who has, in the end, no friend.
did.zh: 這些事你大部分都做了。你就是葛勞康所描述的那個人；而你至少對此是誠實的。柏拉圖的回答就是對你說的。他要你往前看：一個凡是能安然拿走的都拿走的人，會變成什麼樣子？他的欲求隨著每一次得手而增長；他無法信任任何人，因為他知道人在暗處會做什麼；而到最後，他沒有朋友。

fear.en: Your main reason was that you might be found out. Then you have not yet put on the ring. The case stipulates that you cannot be caught, and your answer shows how hard that is to imagine. It also means that Glaucon is right about you so far: remove the risk, and you have given no reason to hold back. Hobbes would approve. He thought the risk can never really be removed, and that this is reason enough.
fear.zh: 你主要的理由是可能被發現。那麼，你還沒有戴上戒指。這個案例規定了你不可能被抓；而你的回答顯示，這有多難想像。這也表示，到目前為止葛勞康說對了你：把風險拿掉，你就沒有給出任何收手的理由。霍布斯會贊成你。他認為風險永遠不可能真的被拿掉，而這個理由就夠了。

conscience.en: Your main reason was that you would know. This is Yang Zhen’s “I know,” and the Doctrine of the Mean’s watchfulness when alone: the ring does not hide you from the one observer who is always there. Glaucon has a reply. He would say that your unease is the voice of your parents and teachers, left behind in you, and that a clear-headed person would train it away. To answer him you must say why the inner witness deserves to be obeyed, which is the task Plato set himself.
conscience.zh: 你主要的理由是：你自己會知道。這就是楊震的「我知」，也是《中庸》的慎獨：戒指藏不住你，使你不被那位永遠在場的觀察者看見。葛勞康有話可回。他會說：你的不安，是你的父母與老師留在你裡面的聲音；一個頭腦清楚的人，會把它訓練掉。要回答他，你必須說出那位內在的見證者為什麼值得被服從；而那正是柏拉圖給自己的任務。

self.en: Your main reason was the kind of person you are and mean to be. This is Plato’s answer and the Confucian one. On this view injustice is a harm you do to yourself, as overeating is, and it needs no audience. The objection to weigh is whether this makes goodness too much about you. The candidate whose file you left in the pile is owed something, and it is not your character.
self.zh: 你主要的理由是：你是什麼樣的人、打算成為什麼樣的人。這是柏拉圖的回答，也是儒家的回答。照這個看法，不正義是你對自己造成的傷害，就像暴食一樣，不需要觀眾。值得掂量的反駁是：這會不會讓「善」變得太以你自己為中心？那位申請書被你留在那一疊裡的候選人，是被虧欠了某樣東西的；而那樣東西並不是你的品格。

others.en: Your main reason was that someone would be wronged. You did not ask what you would gain or lose. This is the answer Kant and Prichard would call the only moral one: the act is wrong, and that is the reason. Glaucon will say that you have not answered him, since he asked what good justice does the just person. Your reply must be that the question was the wrong one to ask.
others.zh: 你主要的理由是：有人會受到不義的對待。你並沒有問自己會得到或失去什麼。康德與普里查德會說，這是唯一算得上「道德的」回答：這個行為是錯的，而這就是理由。葛勞康會說你沒有回答他，因為他問的是：正義對行正義的人有什麼好處？你的回應必須是：那個問題問錯了。

mixed.en: Your reasons were spread evenly, and you gave different ones in different cases. That is common and may be the truth about most of us. Look at where you drew the line between what you would do and what you would not. Many people will read the file and will not touch the application, and the difference is usually that the last case has a face.
mixed.zh: 你的理由分布得很平均，在不同的情境裡給了不同的理由。這很常見，而這也許就是我們大多數人的真相。看看你在「會做的」與「不會做的」之間，把線劃在哪裡。許多人會看那份檔案，卻不會碰那份申請書；而差別通常在於：最後一個情境裡，有一張臉。

argument.lead_en: Glaucon’s challenge from Republic II. Each of the answers in the lesson denies a different step. Click a step to see which.
argument.lead_zh: 葛勞康在《理想國》卷二提出的挑戰。這一課裡的每一個回答，各自否定不同的一步。點任何一步，看看是哪一個。

steps.en: People value justice only for its rewards: reputation, safety, and the avoidance of punishment.
steps.zh: 人們看重正義，只是為了它的報酬：名聲、安全，以及免於懲罰。
steps.ob_en: Plato and the Confucians deny this. Justice is the good condition of the person, valued as health is. Kant denies it differently: to value justice for anything else is not to value justice.
steps.ob_zh: 柏拉圖與儒家否認這一點。正義是人的良好狀態，像健康一樣被看重。康德以另一種方式否認：為了任何別的東西而看重正義，就不是看重正義。

steps.en: A person who could never be detected would lose all of these rewards’ power over him.
steps.zh: 一個永遠不會被察覺的人，這些報酬對他就完全失去了支配力。
steps.ob_en: Hobbes denies that there is any such person. No one can be sure of never being found out, and a policy of injustice must be judged by its risks.
steps.ob_zh: 霍布斯否認有這樣的人。沒有人能確定自己永遠不被發現；而一種行不義的方針，必須依它的風險來評判。

steps.en: So such a person would have no reason to be just, and would act as the unjust do.
steps.zh: 所以，這樣的人就沒有理由行正義，而會像不正義的人那樣行動。
steps.ob_en: Follows from the first two. Glaucon adds that anyone who refrained would be thought a fool by those who praised him in public.
steps.ob_zh: 由前兩步推出。葛勞康還補充：任何一個收手的人，都會被那些在公開場合稱讚他的人當成傻瓜。

steps.en: Therefore no one is just willingly. Justice is a burden accepted for want of the power to do wrong.
steps.zh: 所以，沒有人是甘願行正義的。正義是因為沒有作惡的力量才接受的負擔。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion is a claim about what people are like, and it can be tested against cases. The exercise above is one such test. Those who would hand back the gold in the dark are counterexamples, unless Glaucon can show that they are deceiving themselves.
steps.ob_zh: 這個結論是一個關於「人是什麼樣子」的主張，可以拿案例來檢驗。上面的練習就是這樣的一個檢驗。那些在黑暗中會把黃金還回去的人，就是反例；除非葛勞康能顯示，他們是在自欺。

source.work: Plato, Republic, Book II (359d–360c) and Book IV (444d–e)
source.work_zh: 柏拉圖《理想國》卷二、卷四
source.tr: tr. Benjamin Jowett (public domain)
source.lead_en: The challenge and the answer, two books apart. Glaucon speaks in the first passage and Socrates in the second.
source.lead_zh: 挑戰與回答，相隔兩卷。第一段是葛勞康說的，第二段是蘇格拉底說的。

passages.en: Suppose now that there were two such magic rings, and the just put on one of them and the unjust the other; no man can be imagined to be of such an iron nature that he would stand fast in justice. No man would keep his hands off what was not his own when he could safely take what he liked out of the market, or go into houses and lie with any one at his pleasure, or kill or release from prison whom he would, and in all respects be like a God among men. Then the actions of the just would be as the actions of the unjust; they would both come at last to the same point.
passages.zh: 現在假設有兩枚這樣的魔戒，正義的人戴上一枚，不正義的人戴上另一枚；我們無法想像有任何人的本性堅硬如鐵，能夠堅守正義。只要能夠安然無事地從市場上隨意拿走自己喜歡的東西，或者走進別人家裡隨意與任何人同寢，或者隨意殺人、隨意把人從牢裡放出來，在一切方面都像人間的一位神，那麼沒有人會不對不屬於自己的東西伸手。這樣，正義者的行為就會跟不正義者的行為一樣；兩人最後會走到同一個地方。
passages.note_en: The list is carefully chosen: theft, adultery, murder, and the freeing of prisoners, which is the power over law itself. “Like a God among men” is the phrase to notice. The Greek gods did as they pleased and answered to no one, and Glaucon suggests that this is what every human being secretly wants to be. Plato wrote the speech with full force. He believed that an argument is refuted only when it has been stated at its strongest, and he gave this one to his brother.
passages.note_zh: 這份清單是精心挑選的：偷竊、通姦、殺人，以及釋放囚犯，那是凌駕法律本身的權力。「像人間的一位神」是值得留意的措辭。希臘的諸神隨心所欲，不必對任何人負責；而葛勞康暗示，這就是每一個人暗地裡想成為的樣子。柏拉圖把這段話寫得全力以赴。他相信，一個論證只有在被陳述到最強的時候才算被駁倒；而他把這一個交給了自己的兄弟。

passages.en: And virtue is the health and beauty and well-being of the soul, and vice is the disease and weakness and deformity of the soul. … Again the old question returns upon us: Is justice or injustice the more profitable? The question has become ridiculous.
passages.zh: 德行是靈魂的健康、美與安適；惡是靈魂的疾病、虛弱與畸形。……那個老問題又回到我們面前：正義與不正義，哪一個比較有利？這個問題已經變得可笑了。
passages.note_en: This is the hinge of the whole Republic. Everything depends on the comparison with health. A healthy body is one in which each organ does its proper work and none usurps another’s, and Plato has spent two books arguing that a soul has parts of which the same can be said. If the comparison holds, then asking whether injustice is profitable when undetected is like asking whether a secret illness is profitable. The comparison is also where the argument is most open to doubt, since we have an independent test of bodily health and no agreed test of the health of a soul.
passages.note_zh: 這是整部《理想國》的樞紐。一切都取決於這個與健康的類比。健康的身體，是每一個器官各盡其職、沒有哪一個僭越另一個的身體；而柏拉圖花了兩卷論證，靈魂也有可以這樣說的各個部分。如果這個類比成立，那麼問「不被察覺的不正義是否有利」，就像問「一種祕密的疾病是否有利」。這個類比，也是整個論證最容易受到質疑的地方；因為對身體的健康，我們有獨立的檢驗；對靈魂的健康，卻沒有公認的檢驗。

items.o_en: Plenty of unjust people sleep well and die rich. Plato’s claim that injustice makes a person miserable is simply false.
items.o_zh: 多的是不正義的人睡得安穩、死時富有。柏拉圖主張「不正義使人悲慘」，根本就是假的。
items.r_en: Plato must admit that they feel content. His claim is that they are badly off without knowing it, as a person can be seriously ill and feel fine. That move is legitimate only if there is a standard of a good human life that does not reduce to how the life feels from inside. Most of us accept one in some cases: we think that a contented addict, or a man happily deceived by everyone around him, is missing something. Whether the calm thief belongs on that list is the point in dispute.
items.r_zh: 柏拉圖必須承認，他們自己覺得滿足。他的主張是：他們過得很糟而不自知，就像一個人可以病得很重卻感覺良好。這一步要站得住，就必須有一個「美好人生」的標準，而它不化約為這個人生從裡面感覺起來如何。在某些情況下，我們多數人是接受這樣一個標準的：我們認為一個心滿意足的成癮者，或一個快樂地被身邊每個人欺騙的人，是缺了某樣東西的。至於那位冷靜的竊賊屬不屬於這份清單，正是爭議所在。

items.o_en: Conscience is only training. If I had been brought up differently I would feel no discomfort, so the discomfort is no reason.
items.o_zh: 良心只是訓練出來的。如果我是在不同的環境裡長大的，我就不會覺得不安；所以這份不安不算理由。
items.r_en: The origin of a capacity does not settle its worth. Our ability to do arithmetic is also the product of training, and nobody concludes that sums are arbitrary. What needs to be shown is that conscience tracks nothing, and the evidence points the other way: it responds to features of acts, such as harm and betrayal, that we can state and defend. A better-aimed version of the objection is that conscience can be mistrained, which is true and is a reason to examine it.
items.r_zh: 一種能力的來源，並不決定它的價值。我們做算術的能力同樣是訓練的產物，而沒有人因此推斷加減是任意的。需要被證明的是：良心什麼也沒有在追蹤；而證據指向相反的方向：它所回應的，是行為的種種特徵，例如傷害與背叛，而這些是我們說得出來、也辯護得了的。這個反駁瞄得比較準的版本是：良心可能被訓練錯；這是真的，而這是一個檢視它的理由。

items.o_en: If Kant is right that asking for a reason is a mistake, then there is nothing to say to someone who does not already care about doing right.
items.o_zh: 如果康德是對的，要求一個理由是個錯誤，那麼對於一個本來就不在乎做對的事的人，就沒有什麼話可說了。
items.r_en: That may be so, and it is less damaging than it sounds. There is also nothing to say to someone who does not care about evidence that will make him believe the earth is round, and this does not make its shape a matter of taste. What can be done for the person who does not care is what Aristotle and the Confucians recommended, which is to begin earlier. People are brought to care about doing right by upbringing and example, and argument comes afterward, to those who already care and want to understand why.
items.r_zh: 也許是這樣；而這沒有聽起來那麼有殺傷力。對於一個不在乎證據的人，同樣沒有什麼話可以讓他相信地球是圓的；而這並不使地球的形狀成為品味的問題。對於那個不在乎的人，能做的就是亞里斯多德與儒家所建議的：早一點開始。人是透過教養與榜樣才變得在乎做對的事的；論證是後來的事，是給那些已經在乎、並且想要明白為什麼的人的。

said.claim: 「天知，地知，你知，我知。」（楊震）
said.claim_zh: 「天知，地知，你知，我知。」（楊震）
said.verdict_en: Close. The original has “the spirits,” not “earth”
said.verdict_zh: 很接近；原文是「神知」，不是「地知」
said.en: The saying is quoted everywhere in this form, “Heaven knows, earth knows, you know, I know,” and it has given Yang Zhen’s descendants their ancestral hall name, the Hall of the Four Knows. The History of the Later Han, which is the source, has: “Heaven knows, the spirits know, I know, and you know.” “Earth” replaced “the spirits” in later retellings, probably because heaven and earth make a natural pair. The order matters a little. Yang Zhen names himself before his visitor.
said.zh: 這句話到處都以這個形式被引用，並且給了楊震的後人他們的堂號「四知堂」。作為出處的《後漢書》寫的是：「天知，神知，我知，子知。」在後來的轉述裡，「地」取代了「神」，大概是因為天與地是天然的一對。順序也有一點意思。楊震把自己排在來客之前。

terms.d_en: What is good in itself, and what is good for the sake of something else.
terms.d_zh: 本身就好的東西，以及為了別的東西才好的東西。

terms.d_en: The idea that justice arises from an agreement among people to restrain themselves for mutual benefit.
terms.d_zh: 主張正義出自人們為了互利而彼此克制的約定。

terms.d_en: The view that each person has reason to do only what serves his own interest.
terms.d_zh: 主張每個人只有理由去做符合自身利益的事。

terms.d_en: Sensible care for one’s own long-term interest.
terms.d_zh: 對自己長遠利益的明智顧慮。

terms.d_en: The awareness of the moral quality of one’s own acts.
terms.d_zh: 對自己行為的道德性質的覺察。

terms.d_en: Being the same person in private as in public.
terms.d_zh: 私底下與公開場合是同一個人。

terms.d_en: The Confucian discipline of guarding one’s thoughts and conduct when unobserved.
terms.d_zh: 儒家的工夫：在沒人看見的時候，守護自己的念頭與行為。

terms.d_en: Keeping oneself from knowing what one has reason to know.
terms.d_zh: 使自己不去知道自己有理由知道的事。

vocab.eg: The magistrate owed his career to him.
vocab.eg_zh: 那位縣令是靠他才有今天的。

vocab.eg: The magistrate’s half of the argument deserves a hearing.
vocab.eg_zh: 縣令那一半的論證值得聽一聽。

vocab.eg: The only people who stand to gain.
vocab.eg_zh: 唯二會得到好處的人。

vocab.eg: No man would stand fast in justice.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人會堅守正義。

vocab.eg: No man would keep his hands off what was not his own.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人會不對不屬於自己的東西伸手。

vocab.eg: He then sharpens the test.
vocab.eg_zh: 接著他把檢驗磨得更利。

vocab.eg: The reply is sound as far as it goes.
vocab.eg_zh: 就它所及的範圍而言，這個回答是站得住的。

vocab.eg: The petty man, when alone, stops at nothing.
vocab.eg_zh: 小人獨處的時候，無所不至。

vocab.eg: If you hold back, say why.
vocab.eg_zh: 如果你收手，說出為什麼。

vocab.eg: With little chance of being held to account.
vocab.eg_zh: 幾乎不必負責。

quiz.q: What is Glaucon trying to show with the story of the ring?
options: That people are just only because they are watched, and would not be if they could escape detection.
That magic rings exist.
That shepherds are dishonest.
That kings deserve to be overthrown.

quiz.q: What must a successful answer to Glaucon show?
options: That justice is worth having for itself, with all rewards and reputation removed.
That unjust people are always caught.
That the gods punish the wicked.
That justice makes a person rich.

quiz.q: What is Plato’s answer?
options: Justice is the health of the soul, so asking whether it pays is like asking whether health pays.
Justice is a useful agreement.
The ring does not exist.
No answer can be given.

quiz.q: Why does Hobbes’s reply concede the main point?
options: It says we should be just because we can never be sure of escaping detection.
It says justice is unimportant.
It denies that people make agreements.
It relies on the health of the soul.

quiz.q: What does the Doctrine of the Mean say about being alone?
options: Nothing is more visible than what is hidden, so the gentleman is watchful over himself when alone.
A gentleman should never be alone.
What is done alone does not matter.
Solitude is the reward of virtue.

write.en: You find a wallet with a large sum in it and a name inside. No one saw you pick it up. Write down honestly what goes through your mind, and then label each thought: fear, conscience, character, or concern for the owner.
write.zh: 你撿到一個皮夾，裡面有一大筆錢，還有失主的名字。沒有人看見你撿起它。誠實地寫下你腦中閃過的念頭；然後為每一個念頭貼上標籤：害怕、良心、品格，或對失主的關切。

write.en: Is Plato right that an unjust person who is never caught is still worse off? Defend your answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 柏拉圖說，一個永遠沒被抓到的不正義者，仍然過得比較糟。他說得對嗎？用大約 150 個英文字為你的答案辯護。

write.en: Explain the phrase 慎獨 to an English-speaking friend in four sentences.
write.zh: 用四個句子向一位說英文的朋友解釋「慎獨」。

paras.en: The Buddha names two qualities that he calls the guardians of the world: “These two bright things protect the world. What two? Conscience and prudence.” The Pali words are hiri and ottappa. Hiri is an inner sense of shame, the recoil of a person who respects himself from an act beneath him. Ottappa is a regard for consequences and for the judgment of the wise. Without the two, he says, people would live like animals. They correspond closely to two of the reasons in the exercise above, the reason from character and the reason from prudence, and the tradition holds that a sound moral life needs both.
paras.zh: 佛陀舉出兩種特質，稱之為世間的守護者：「這兩種白法守護世間。哪兩種？慚與愧。」巴利文是 hiri 與 ottappa。hiri（慚）是內在的羞恥感，是一個自重的人對有失身分的行為的退縮。ottappa（愧）是對後果、以及對智者評價的顧慮。他說，若沒有這兩者，人就會像禽獸一樣過活。它們與上面練習裡的兩種理由（來自品格的理由，與來自審慎的理由）對應得很緊；而這個傳統主張，健全的道德生活兩者都需要。

paras.en: On the ring itself the texts are blunt. “There’s no privacy in the world for someone who does bad deeds. You’ll know for yourself whether you’ve lied or told the truth.” That is Yang Zhen’s third witness. The teaching of karma then adds a claim that neither Plato nor the Confucians make in this form. An intentional act leaves a trace in the mind of the one who does it and bears fruit there, and this happens by a natural process that needs no observer and no judge. “Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft” is there a place to escape one’s deeds. Glaucon’s experiment assumes that an act unseen is an act without consequences for the agent. The Buddha’s reply is that the agent is where the consequences fall (Dharma and the West, D17).
paras.zh: 對於那枚戒指本身，經文說得很直接：「作惡的人，世間沒有隱密之處。你說了謊還是說了實話，你自己會知道。」那就是楊震的第三位見證者。接著，業的教導補上了一個柏拉圖與儒家都沒有以這種形式提出的主張。一個有意圖的行為，會在做它的人的心裡留下痕跡，並且在那裡結果；而這是藉由一個自然的過程發生的，不需要觀察者，也不需要法官。「不在空中，不在海中，也不在山洞裡」，沒有一處可以逃離自己的業。葛勞康的實驗預設：一個沒被看見的行為，對行為者是沒有後果的。佛陀的回答是：後果落下的地方，正是行為者自己（佛法與西方哲學 D17）。

further.t: Plato, Republic, Books II and IV, translated by Benjamin Jowett
further.n_en: The ring is at 359–360. The health of the soul is at 444–445.

further.t: 《中庸》第一章；《大學》「誠意」章
further.n_en: The two classical statements of watchfulness when alone.
further.n_zh: 慎獨的兩處經典陳述。

further.t: 《後漢書・楊震列傳》
further.n_en: The gold at midnight.
further.n_zh: 暮夜卻金。

further.t: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, chapter 15
further.n_en: The reply to the Fool.
further.n_zh: 對愚人的回答。

further.t: H. A. Prichard, “Does Moral Philosophy Rest on a Mistake?” Mind 21 (1912)
Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.9 and 3.40
further.n_en: The guardians of the world; no privacy for the doer of bad deeds.
further.n_zh: 護世二法；作惡者無隱密處。

lessons.title: Are People Born Good?
lessons.blurb_en: Mencius says that human nature tends toward good as water runs downhill. Xunzi says that it is crooked timber and must be steamed straight. Hobbes, Rousseau, and babies in a laboratory on the oldest quarrel in ethics.
lessons.blurb_zh: 孟子說，人性之向善，就像水往下流。荀子說，它是彎曲的木頭，必須蒸過才扳得直。霍布斯、盧梭，還有實驗室裡的嬰兒，談倫理學裡最古老的一場爭論。
lessons.big_en: How we raise children, punish criminals, and design governments depends on what we think people are like before anything has been done to them. The question is partly one of fact, and for the first time some of the facts can be tested.
lessons.big_zh: 我們怎麼養育孩子、怎麼懲罰罪犯、怎麼設計政府，都取決於我們認為人在「還沒有被動過任何手腳之前」是什麼樣子。這個問題有一部分是事實問題；而這些事實當中，有一些如今第一次可以被檢驗。

paras.en: Around 320 BCE two philosophers argued about human nature in images, and the record of it is the oldest sustained debate on the subject that we have. Gaozi said that human nature is like willow wood, and morality is like the cups and bowls a craftsman carves from it. Goodness is something made out of us. Mencius asked whether the craftsman follows the nature of the willow or does violence to it. If morality is a violence done to human beings, people will have every reason to hate it. Gaozi tried again. Human nature is like water whirling in a pool. Open a channel to the east and it flows east, open one to the west and it flows west. It has no preference between good and bad.
paras.zh: 大約西元前 320 年，兩位哲學家用意象爭論人性；這份紀錄，是我們手上關於這個題目最古老的一場持續的辯論。告子說：人性就像杞柳，仁義就像工匠從它雕出來的杯盤。善是從我們身上「做」出來的東西。孟子問：工匠是順著杞柳的本性呢，還是戕害它？如果仁義是對人的一種戕害，人們就大有理由憎恨它。告子換了一個說法。人性就像在水潭裡打轉的水。往東開一個口，它就往東流；往西開一個口，它就往西流。它在善與不善之間沒有偏好。

paras.en: Mencius accepted the image and turned it. “Water indeed has no preference between east and west. But has it no preference between up and down? Human nature is good as water flows downward. There is no person who is not good, and there is no water that does not flow down.” You can splash water over your head by striking it, and you can force it up a hill by damming it, but that is what circumstance does to it. When people are made to do wrong, something similar has been done to their nature.
paras.zh: 孟子接受了這個意象，然後把它轉了過來。「水信無分於東西，無分於上下乎？人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。」你拍打水，可以讓它濺過額頭；你築壩擋水，可以逼它上山；但那是形勢對它造成的。人被弄到去做不善的事，他們的本性也是遭到了類似的對待。

paras.en: Mencius did not mean that people are born virtuous. His claim was about tendencies. Anyone who suddenly sees a child about to fall into a well, he says, feels alarm and compassion, and feels it before any thought of gain or reputation. That feeling is a sprout. There are four of them, compassion, shame, deference, and the sense of right and wrong, and from them grow humaneness, rightness, propriety, and wisdom. “These are not welded onto me from outside. I have them from the start.” A sprout can be tended or trampled. His most famous image is Ox Mountain, which was once covered in trees. It stood near a great city, and axes cut it down. The stumps put out new shoots with the night air and the rain, and cattle and sheep grazed them off. People who see it bare suppose that it never had timber. “But is that the nature of the mountain?”
paras.zh: 孟子的意思並不是人生下來就有德行。他的主張是關於「傾向」的。他說，任何人突然看見一個小孩快要掉進井裡，都會感到驚懼與不忍，而且是在想到任何利益或名聲之前就感到了。那個感受是一個「端」，一株嫩芽。這樣的嫩芽有四個：惻隱、羞惡、恭敬、是非；從它們長出仁、義、禮、智。「仁義禮智，非由外鑠我也，我固有之也。」嫩芽可以被照料，也可以被踐踏。他最著名的意象是牛山；它曾經長滿了樹。它位在一座大城的郊外，斧頭把樹砍光了。殘留的樹樁靠著夜氣與雨露冒出新芽，牛羊又接著把它們啃掉。人們看它光禿禿的，就以為它從來沒有過木材。「此豈山之性也哉？」

paras.en: Two generations later Xunzi, the most systematic of the early Confucians, wrote a chapter that opens: “Human nature is bad. Its goodness is the product of deliberate effort.” People are born fond of profit, he observes, and if they follow that fondness there will be strife and no yielding. They are born with envy and hatred, and with desires of the ear and eye. To follow nature is to end in violence. “Crooked wood must be steamed and bent before it is straight, and dull metal must be ground before it is sharp.” Goodness comes from teachers, models, and ritual, which the sages invented because they saw what people are like without them. Xunzi was no pessimist about the result. He agreed with Mencius that the man in the street can become a sage. He located the capacity in intelligence and effort, where Mencius had located it in feeling. The practical difference is large. For Mencius education is gardening, and for Xunzi it is carpentry.
paras.zh: 兩代之後，早期儒者當中最有系統的荀子，寫了一篇這樣開頭的文章：「人之性惡，其善者偽也。」（「偽」是「人為」的意思。）他觀察到：人生而好利，順著這份喜好，就會有爭奪而沒有辭讓。人生而有嫉妒與憎惡，生而有耳目之欲。順著本性走，結局是暴亂。「枸木必將待檃栝、烝、矯然後直，鈍金必將待礱、厲然後利。」善來自師、法與禮義；聖人之所以創制它們，是因為看到了人沒有它們的時候是什麼樣子。荀子對結果並不悲觀。他同意孟子：路上的普通人也可以成為聖人，「塗之人可以為禹」。只是孟子把這份能力放在情感裡，他把它放在知性與努力裡。實際上的差別很大。對孟子來說，教育是園藝；對荀子來說，教育是木工。

paras.en: Europe had the argument nineteen centuries later, and its two great voices line up with the Chinese ones closely. Thomas Hobbes, writing during a civil war, asked what life would be like with no government to keep people in awe. His answer is that every man would be the enemy of every other, and there would be “no Arts; no Letters; no Society; and which is worst of all, continuall feare, and danger of violent death; And the life of man, solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short.” People are not wicked on his account. They are roughly equal, they want the same scarce things, and none can trust the rest. Order has to be imposed.
paras.zh: 歐洲在十九個世紀之後才有了這場爭論；而它的兩個最響亮的聲音，跟中國的那兩個對得很整齊。霍布斯在一場內戰期間寫作；他問：如果沒有政府使人們有所畏懼，生活會是什麼樣子？他的回答是：每個人都會是每個人的敵人；那裡將「沒有技藝，沒有文字，沒有社會；而最糟的是，持續不斷的恐懼，以及暴死的危險；人的生活孤獨、貧困、污穢、野蠻而短暫」。照他的說法，人並不邪惡。他們大致平等，想要同樣稀少的東西，而誰也信不過其餘的人。秩序必須被強加上去。

paras.en: Jean-Jacques Rousseau replied in 1755 that Hobbes had described people as society has made them and mistaken the portrait for nature. Natural man, he argued, is solitary, healthy, and peaceable, with two instincts, a care for his own survival and a pity that makes him unwilling to see another creature suffer. Corruption begins with property. “The first man, who, after enclosing a piece of ground, took it into his head to say, ‘This is mine,’ and found people simple enough to believe him, was the true founder of civil society,” and of all the crimes and wars that followed. His book on education opens with the sentence: “God makes all things good; man meddles with them and they become evil.” Ox Mountain could not be put more briefly.
paras.zh: 盧梭在 1755 年回應：霍布斯描述的，是被社會造就之後的人，卻把這幅畫像誤當成了本性。他論證：自然人是孤獨、健康而平和的，有兩種本能，一是對自己存活的關切，一是憐憫，使他不願看見另一個生命受苦。腐化始於財產。「第一個圈起一塊地、想到要說『這是我的』，並且找到一些頭腦簡單得肯相信他的人，就是文明社會真正的奠基者」，也是隨之而來的一切罪行與戰爭的奠基者。他談教育的那本書，第一句就是：「出自造物主之手的一切都是好的；一到了人的手裡，就全變壞了。」牛山的道理，沒辦法說得更簡短了。

paras.en: For most of history the question could be argued only from anecdote. In the last few decades psychologists have found ways to put it to infants, who have had little time to be taught. In experiments at Yale published in 2007, babies of six and ten months watched a puppet show in which one figure helped another up a hill and a third pushed it down. Offered the two afterward, most reached for the helper. In studies at Leipzig, toddlers of eighteen months who saw a stranger drop something and reach for it went and picked it up for him, unasked and unrewarded. These findings are Mencius’s child at the well, observed under controlled conditions.
paras.zh: 在歷史上大部分的時間裡，這個問題只能靠軼事來爭論。過去幾十年，心理學家找到了向嬰兒提出這個問題的方法；嬰兒還沒有多少時間被教導。在耶魯大學 2007 年發表的實驗裡，六個月與十個月大的嬰兒看了一場玩偶戲：一個角色幫另一個角色爬上山坡，第三個角色把它推下去。事後把那兩個角色拿給嬰兒選，多數嬰兒伸手去拿幫忙的那一個。在萊比錫的研究裡，十八個月大的幼兒看見一個陌生人掉了東西、伸手去搆，就走過去替他撿起來，沒有人要求，也沒有獎賞。這些發現，就是在受控條件下觀察到的「孺子將入於井」。

paras.en: The same researchers have found the other side. Infants prefer those who resemble them, and they like to see a puppet who chose a different food from theirs treated badly. Small children help freely and share grudgingly. And adults are easily led. In Stanley Milgram’s experiments of the 1960s about two-thirds of ordinary volunteers, told to do so by a man in a gray coat, went on pressing switches that they believed were giving severe electric shocks to a stranger. The prison experiment run at Stanford in 1971 is cited for the same lesson, though later study of the records has shown that the guards were coached, and it is now treated with caution.
paras.zh: 同一批研究者也發現了另一面。嬰兒偏好跟自己相像的對象；而且他們喜歡看到一個「選了跟他們不同食物」的玩偶被惡劣對待。幼兒幫忙很大方，分享卻很勉強。而成年人很容易被帶著走。在米爾格倫 1960 年代的實驗裡，大約三分之二的普通志願者，在一位穿灰色外套的人的指示下，持續按下他們相信正在對一個陌生人施加強烈電擊的開關。1971 年在史丹佛進行的監獄實驗也常被引來說明同一個教訓；不過後來對紀錄的研究顯示，那些「獄卒」是被指點過的，現在人們引用它時比較謹慎。

paras.en: The picture that emerges gives each ancient party something. Mencius was right that the beginnings of sympathy and of a sense of fairness are present before instruction, and Gaozi’s blank water is the view that has fared worst. Xunzi was right that we are also born with partiality, appetite, and readiness to follow, and that the first moral impulses are narrow: they extend to the helper, the kin, and the familiar face, and it takes training to carry them further. Both were right that everything depends on what is done next. They disagreed about which part of our equipment to call “nature,” and that is partly a dispute about a word. Mencius meant by nature what is distinctive of human beings and grows under good conditions. Xunzi meant what is present at birth without effort.
paras.zh: 浮現出來的圖像，給了古代的每一方一些東西。孟子說對了：同情與公平感的開端，在教導之前就已經存在；而告子那潭沒有方向的水，是處境最糟的一種看法。荀子也說對了：我們同樣生而具有偏私、欲望與隨從的傾向；而最初的道德衝動是狹窄的，它們只及於幫忙的人、親屬與熟悉的臉，需要訓練才能推得更遠。兩人都說對的是：一切取決於接下來怎麼做。他們的分歧在於：把我們天賦裡的哪一部分叫作「性」？而這有一部分是關於一個字的爭論。孟子所說的「性」，是人之所以為人的特點、在良好的條件下會生長的東西。荀子所說的「性」，是生下來就有、不必費力的東西。

paras.en: Something real is left when the word is set aside, and it is the choice between the gardener and the carpenter. A parent or a state that believes people are shoots to be tended will rely on example, trust, and room to grow. One that believes people are crooked timber will rely on rules, incentives, and supervision. Each policy tends to produce the evidence that supports it, since people who are trusted often become trustworthy and people who are watched often give cause for watching. That may be the most important fact about human nature: it responds to what is believed about it.
paras.zh: 把那個字擱在一邊之後，還剩下某個真實的東西，那就是「園丁」與「木匠」之間的選擇。一位相信人是有待照料的嫩芽的父母，或一個這樣相信的國家，會倚重榜樣、信任與成長的空間。相信人是枸木的，會倚重規則、誘因與監督。每一種方針，都傾向於製造出支持它的證據；因為被信任的人往往變得值得信任，被監視的人往往給出了該被監視的理由。這也許是關於人性最重要的一個事實：它會回應人們對它的看法。

lab.title_en: Try it: six pieces of evidence
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：六份證據
lab.lead_en: Set the slider where you stand now. Then read six pieces of evidence, one at a time, and move the slider after each if it changes your mind. At the end you will see the path you took and which piece moved you most.
lab.lead_zh: 先把滑桿放在你現在的立場上。然後一次讀一份證據，共六份；讀完每一份，如果它改變了你的想法，就移動滑桿。最後你會看到你走過的路徑，以及哪一份證據最推得動你。

start.en: Before any evidence: where do you stand?
start.zh: 在讀任何證據之前：你站在哪裡？

t.en: The child at the well
t.zh: 孺子入井

x.en: Anyone who suddenly sees a small child about to fall into a well feels alarm and compassion before any thought of reward.
x.zh: 任何人突然看見一個小孩快要掉進井裡，都會在想到任何好處之前，感到驚懼與不忍。

g.en: Mencius: this is the sprout of humaneness, and you did not learn it.
g.zh: 孟子：這就是仁之端；它不是你學來的。

b.en: Xunzi: a pang is not an act. Many who feel it walk on. What gets the child pulled out is training.
b.zh: 荀子：心頭一緊不等於行動。許多人有這個感覺，卻照樣走過去。真正把孩子拉上來的，是訓練。

t.en: A nursery without rules
t.zh: 沒有規矩的托兒所

x.en: Leave a group of two-year-olds alone with one attractive toy. They grab, hit, and bite. Sharing has to be taught, over years.
x.zh: 把一群兩歲的孩子跟一件吸引人的玩具單獨留在一起。他們會搶、會打、會咬。分享必須教，而且要教好幾年。

g.en: Mencius: the same children comfort one another when one cries. A sprout that has not yet grown is still a sprout.
g.zh: 孟子：同一群孩子，有人哭的時候也會彼此安慰。還沒長大的嫩芽，仍然是嫩芽。

b.en: Xunzi: this is nature before the steaming and bending. Fondness for gain comes first.
b.zh: 荀子：這就是蒸過、扳過之前的本性。好利在先。

t.en: The helper and the hinderer
t.zh: 幫忙的與搗亂的

x.en: Babies of six and ten months, after watching one puppet help another up a hill and a third push it down, mostly reach for the helper.
x.zh: 六個月與十個月大的嬰兒，看完一個玩偶幫另一個爬上山坡、第三個把它推下去之後，多數伸手去拿幫忙的那一個。

g.en: Mencius: a sense of right and wrong before speech.
g.zh: 孟子：在會說話之前，就有是非之心。

b.en: Xunzi: they prefer whoever would be useful to them. That is fondness for gain, wisely applied.
b.zh: 荀子：他們偏好的是對自己有用的人。那是好利，只是用得聰明。

t.en: The switch and the gray coat
t.zh: 開關與灰外套

x.en: About two-thirds of ordinary adults, instructed by an experimenter, went on giving what they believed were dangerous electric shocks to a protesting stranger.
x.zh: 大約三分之二的普通成年人，在實驗者的指示下，持續對一個不斷抗議的陌生人施加他們相信是危險的電擊。

g.en: Mencius: they sweated, trembled, and begged to stop. The sprout was there, and a bad situation overrode it, as a dam forces water uphill.
g.zh: 孟子：他們冒汗、發抖、懇求停止。嫩芽是在的；一個惡劣的情境壓過了它，就像築壩逼水上山。

b.en: Hobbes: people do what authority tells them. So make sure the authority is a good one.
b.zh: 霍布斯：人會照權威說的去做。所以要確保那個權威是好的。

t.en: Strangers after a disaster
t.zh: 災後的陌生人

x.en: After earthquakes and floods, studies of what people actually do find little of the panic and looting that officials expect. Most survivors share food and dig out their neighbors.
x.zh: 地震與洪水之後，對人們實際行為的研究發現，官員預期的那種恐慌與搶掠其實很少。多數倖存者分享食物，並且把鄰居從瓦礫裡挖出來。

g.en: Rousseau: remove the institutions for a week and pity reappears.
g.zh: 盧梭：把制度拿掉一個星期，憐憫就重新出現了。

b.en: Hobbes: for a week, among neighbors. Wait until the food runs out.
b.zh: 霍布斯：只有一個星期，而且是在鄰居之間。等糧食吃完再看。

t.en: Us and them
t.zh: 我們與他們

x.en: Divide strangers into two teams by the toss of a coin, and within minutes they favor their own side and think worse of the other.
x.zh: 用擲硬幣把一群陌生人分成兩隊；幾分鐘之內，他們就偏袒自己這一邊，並且把另一邊想得比較差。

g.en: Mencius: love begins with those nearest. The task is to extend it.
g.zh: 孟子：愛從最親近的人開始。任務是把它推出去。

b.en: Xunzi: partiality is inborn, and impartiality is an achievement of culture.
b.zh: 荀子：偏私是天生的；不偏私是文化的成就。

good.en: You end on the side of Mencius and Rousseau. You hold that the first impulses are sound and that wrongdoing has to be explained by what was done to the person. The cases you must account for are the nursery and the coin toss, where no one had yet done anything to anyone.
good.zh: 你最後站在孟子與盧梭這一邊。你主張最初的衝動是健全的，而作惡必須用「這個人遭遇了什麼」來解釋。你必須交代的是托兒所與擲硬幣那兩個案例；在那裡，還沒有任何人對任何人做過什麼。

bad.en: You end on the side of Xunzi and Hobbes. You hold that order and kindness are achievements, built against the grain. The cases you must account for are the infants and the earthquake, where help appeared with no teacher and no police.
bad.zh: 你最後站在荀子與霍布斯這一邊。你主張秩序與仁慈是成就，是逆著紋理建立起來的。你必須交代的是嬰兒與地震那兩個案例；在那裡，沒有老師、沒有警察，幫助卻出現了。

mid.en: You end near the middle, which is where most researchers now stand: we are born with sympathy and with partiality, and neither is the whole of us. This is close to Gaozi’s position with one correction. He thought nature indifferent. The evidence suggests that it pulls both ways at once, and that upbringing decides which pull is strengthened.
mid.zh: 你最後落在中間附近；多數研究者現在也站在那裡：我們生而具有同情，也生而具有偏私，而兩者都不是我們的全部。這很接近告子的立場，只需要修正一處。他認為本性是無所偏向的。證據顯示的是：它同時往兩邊拉；而教養決定了哪一股拉力被加強。

moved.en: The piece that moved you most was “{t}.” You shifted {n} points toward {d}.
moved.zh: 最推得動你的是「{t}」。你往{d}移了 {n} 分。

still.en: No piece of evidence moved you by more than a few points. Either you had weighed all this before, or you were reading each card through the view you began with. Xunzi and Mencius read the same cases and each found what he expected.
still.zh: 沒有任何一份證據讓你移動超過幾分。要嘛這些你以前都衡量過了，要嘛你是透過一開始的看法在讀每一張卡。荀子與孟子讀的是同樣的案例，而各自都找到了他預期的東西。

argument.lead_en: Mencius’s argument from the child at the well (2A6 and 6A6). Click a step to see what Xunzi would say against it.
argument.lead_zh: 孟子由「孺子將入於井」出發的論證（《公孫丑上》第六章、《告子上》第六章）。點任何一步，看看荀子會怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Everyone who suddenly sees a child about to fall into a well feels alarm and compassion.
steps.zh: 任何人突然看見一個小孩快要掉進井裡，都會感到驚懼與不忍。
steps.ob_en: A claim of fact, and “everyone” is strong. Mencius would treat a person who felt nothing as damaged, which protects the claim and also makes it harder to test.
steps.ob_zh: 這是一個事實主張，而「任何人」說得很強。孟子會把一個毫無感覺的人當成受了損傷的人；這保護了這個主張，卻也使它更難檢驗。

steps.en: The feeling does not come from a wish to please the parents, to win praise, or to avoid blame.
steps.zh: 這個感受，不是出於想討好孩子的父母、想博得稱讚，或想避免責備。
steps.ob_en: The word “suddenly” does the work: there has been no time to calculate. Xunzi could reply that a habit trained since infancy also acts without calculation.
steps.ob_zh: 起作用的是「乍」這個字：來不及盤算。荀子可以回答：一個從嬰兒時期就訓練出來的習慣，同樣不經盤算就起作用。

steps.en: What is felt by all, at once, and without ulterior motive belongs to human nature.
steps.zh: 人人都有、當下就有、而且沒有別的動機的感受，屬於人的本性。
steps.ob_en: By the same test, the toddler’s grab for the toy belongs to human nature too. The argument shows that a good impulse is innate. It does not show that only good impulses are.
steps.ob_zh: 照同一個檢驗，幼兒伸手去搶玩具，同樣屬於人的本性。這個論證顯示有一種善的衝動是天生的。它並沒有顯示「只有」善的衝動是天生的。

steps.en: So the beginning of humaneness is part of human nature, and a person who lacks it “is not human.”
steps.zh: 所以，仁的開端是人性的一部分；而缺少它的人，「非人也」。
steps.ob_en: Notice how modest the conclusion is. Mencius claims a beginning. Everything else depends on cultivation, and on that point he and Xunzi agree.
steps.ob_zh: 請留意這個結論多麼有節制。孟子主張的是一個「開端」。其餘的一切都取決於培養；而在這一點上，他與荀子是一致的。

source.work: Mencius 6A2; Xunzi, chapter 23, “Human Nature Is Bad”
source.work_zh: 《孟子・告子上》第二章；《荀子・性惡》
source.tr: translated for this series from the Chinese text
source.lead_en: The two passages every Chinese student once knew by heart. The Chinese is given under each.
source.lead_zh: 從前每一個中國學生都背得出來的兩段文字。每一段下面附上原文。

passages.en: Gaozi said, “Human nature is like whirling water. Open a passage for it to the east and it flows east. Open a passage to the west and it flows west. Human nature does not distinguish good from not good, as water does not distinguish east from west.” Mencius said, “Water indeed does not distinguish east from west. Does it not distinguish up from down? The goodness of human nature is like the downward flow of water. There is no person who is not good, and there is no water that does not flow down.”
passages.zh: 告子曰：「性，猶湍水也。決諸東方則東流，決諸西方則西流。人性之無分於善不善也，猶水之無分於東西也。」孟子曰：「水信無分於東西，無分於上下乎？人性之善也，猶水之就下也。人無有不善，水無有不下。」
passages.note_en: Mencius wins the exchange by accepting his opponent’s image and finding in it a feature the opponent had overlooked. That is skill in debate. It is fair to ask whether it is an argument. Water’s tendency to run downhill does not show that people tend to be good, and Gaozi could have answered with another image in which the pull was the other way. What the passage does is make a claim clear: nature is a tendency and not a fixed state, and a tendency can be overpowered without being absent.
passages.note_zh: 孟子贏下這一回合的方式，是接受對手的意象，並且在其中找出一個對手忽略了的特徵。那是辯論的本事。我們大可以問：這算不算一個論證？水往下流的傾向，並沒有顯示人傾向於善；而告子本來可以用另一個「拉力方向相反」的意象來回答。這段文字做到的，是把一個主張說清楚：本性是一種傾向，不是一個固定的狀態；而一種傾向可以被壓過，卻並非不存在。

passages.en: Human nature is bad. Its goodness is the product of deliberate effort. Now, the nature of man is such that he is born with a fondness for profit. If he follows this, strife and plunder arise and yielding disappears. … Thus crooked wood must await steaming and bending against the frame before it is straight, and dull metal must await grinding and whetting before it is sharp.
passages.zh: 人之性惡，其善者偽也。今人之性，生而有好利焉，順是，故爭奪生而辭讓亡焉。……故枸木必將待檃栝、烝、矯然後直，鈍金必將待礱、厲然後利。
passages.note_en: The key word is wěi, written with the signs for “person” and “to do.” In later Chinese it means “false,” and readers who took it that way thought Xunzi was calling goodness a sham, which helped ruin his reputation. He means “made by human effort,” as a pot is made. His point is that civilization is an artifact and a precious one. Notice also the shape of the argument. He reasons from what would happen if people followed their inborn desires without restraint, which is exactly how Hobbes reasons about the state of nature.
passages.note_zh: 關鍵的字是「偽」，由「人」與「為」組成。在後來的中文裡，它的意思是「虛假」；照這個意思去讀的人，以為荀子是在說善是假的，這對他名聲的敗壞出了一份力。他的意思是「由人的努力做成的」，就像一只陶器是做成的。他的重點是：文明是一件人造物，而且是一件珍貴的人造物。也請留意這個論證的形狀。他是從「如果人不受約束地順著天生的欲望走，會發生什麼」來推理的；霍布斯對自然狀態的推理，正是這個樣子。

items.o_en: The whole debate is confused. “Good” and “bad” are standards that societies apply. Nature is neither, as a river is neither just nor unjust.
items.o_zh: 整場辯論是混淆的。「善」與「惡」是社會所施加的標準。本性兩者都不是，就像一條河既不公正也不不公正。
items.r_en: This is Gaozi’s position, and it has a point: the words are evaluations. But the question can be restated without them. Do human beings, before instruction, tend toward the conduct that makes shared life possible, or away from it? That is a question about dispositions, and it has an answer whether or not we attach the words. Infants who prefer helpers are evidence about it.
items.r_zh: 這是告子的立場，而它有它的道理：這些詞是評價。但這個問題可以不用這些詞重新表述。人在受教導之前，是傾向於使共同生活成為可能的那種行為，還是背離它？這是一個關於傾向的問題；不管我們貼不貼上那些詞，它都有答案。偏好幫助者的嬰兒，就是關於它的證據。

items.o_en: If people are born good, there is no explaining how evil came into the world. Someone must have been the first to corrupt the rest.
items.o_zh: 如果人生而善，就無法解釋惡是怎麼來到世界上的。總得有人是第一個去腐化其他人的。
items.r_en: The objection hits Rousseau harder than Mencius. Rousseau must explain how good creatures invented bad institutions, and his story of the first fence is not much of an explanation. Mencius never said that we have good impulses only. He said that we also have a body with appetites, which he called the lesser part, and that a person goes wrong by letting the lesser part lead. His view needs no first corrupter. It needs only neglect.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁對盧梭的打擊，比對孟子的大。盧梭必須解釋：善良的生物，怎麼會發明出惡劣的制度？而他那個「第一道圍籬」的故事，算不上什麼解釋。孟子從來沒有說過我們「只有」善的衝動。他說我們還有一個帶著種種欲望的身體，他稱之為「小體」；一個人之所以走偏，是因為讓小體來帶頭。他的看法不需要一個「最初的腐化者」。它只需要疏於照料。

items.o_en: If people are born bad, the sages who invented morality could not have existed. Where did they get the goodness to see that it was needed?
items.o_zh: 如果人生而惡，那些創制道德的聖人就不可能存在。他們從哪裡得到那份善，看出道德是需要的？
items.r_en: This was pressed against Xunzi in his own day, and he answers it in the same chapter. The sages did not differ from other people in nature. They differed in the accumulation of thought and effort. A potter is not made of clay, and one need not be good by nature in order to work out, by intelligence, that a life without rules is miserable for everyone. The reply shows what Xunzi really believed in. He trusted human intelligence more than human feeling.
items.r_zh: 在荀子自己的時代，就有人拿這個來質問他；而他在同一篇裡回答了。聖人在本性上與別人並無不同。不同的是思慮與努力的積累。陶匠並不是陶土做的；一個人不必本性善良，也能憑著知性推想出：沒有規矩的生活對每個人都是悲慘的。這個回答顯示了荀子真正相信的是什麼。比起人的情感，他更信任人的知性。

said.claim: “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.” (Rousseau)
said.claim_zh: 「人生而自由，卻無處不在枷鎖之中。」（盧梭）
said.verdict_zh: 是真的，但談的不是純真
said.en: It is the first sentence of the first chapter of The Social Contract (1762), and it is usually quoted as a lament for lost natural freedom. The next sentences show a different purpose. Rousseau says that he does not know how the change came about and that his question is what can make it legitimate. The book defends a kind of chain: the laws that free people give themselves. The phrase people have in mind when they misuse this one, the “noble savage,” appears nowhere in Rousseau. It comes from a play by the English poet John Dryden, written forty years before Rousseau was born.
said.zh: 這是《社會契約論》（1762）第一章的第一句話；它通常被引來哀嘆失去的自然自由。接下來的幾句話顯示的是另一個目的。盧梭說，他不知道這個轉變是怎麼發生的；他要問的是：什麼能使它成為正當的？這本書辯護的是某一種枷鎖：自由的人為自己訂立的法律。人們誤用這句話時心裡想的那個詞，「高貴的野蠻人」，在盧梭的著作裡哪裡也沒有出現。它出自英國詩人德萊頓的一齣戲，寫於盧梭出生前四十年。

terms.d_en: What human beings are like prior to, or apart from, upbringing and culture.
terms.d_zh: 人在教養與文化之前、或之外的樣子。

terms.d_en: Mencius’s four inborn beginnings of virtue: compassion, shame, deference, and the sense of right and wrong.
terms.d_zh: 孟子所說的四種天生的德行開端：惻隱、羞惡、恭敬（辭讓）、是非。

terms.d_en: Xunzi’s term for what is achieved by conscious activity, as opposed to what is inborn.
terms.d_zh: 荀子的用語：由有意識的活動所成就的東西，相對於天生的東西。

terms.d_en: The condition of human beings without government, real or imagined.
terms.d_zh: 人在沒有政府的情況下的狀態；不論是真實的還是想像的。

terms.d_en: Present from birth and not acquired by experience.
terms.d_zh: 生來就有，而不是由經驗取得的。

terms.d_en: A standing tendency to act or feel in a certain way under certain conditions.
terms.d_zh: 在某些條件下以某種方式行動或感受的常態趨勢。

terms.d_en: The tendency to favor members of one’s own group.
terms.d_zh: 偏袒自己所屬群體成員的傾向。

terms.d_en: In Rousseau, a natural reluctance to see any feeling creature suffer.
terms.d_zh: 在盧梭，指不願看見任何有感覺的生命受苦的天然情感。

vocab.eg: Does the craftsman do violence to the willow?
vocab.eg_zh: 工匠是在戕害杞柳嗎？

vocab.eg: People will have every reason to hate it.
vocab.eg_zh: 人們就大有理由憎恨它。

vocab.eg: A sprout can be tended or trampled.
vocab.eg_zh: 嫩芽可以被照料，也可以被踐踏。

vocab.eg: The stumps put out new shoots with the rain.
vocab.eg_zh: 樹樁靠著雨露冒出新芽。

vocab.eg: Order and kindness are built against the grain.
vocab.eg_zh: 秩序與仁慈是逆著紋理建立起來的。

vocab.eg: Its two great voices line up with the Chinese ones.
vocab.eg_zh: 它的兩個聲音跟中國的那兩個對得上。

vocab.eg: No government to keep people in awe.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有政府使人們有所畏懼。

vocab.eg: Small children help freely and share grudgingly.
vocab.eg_zh: 幼兒幫忙很大方，分享卻很勉強。

vocab.eg: Gaozi’s view is the one that has fared worst.
vocab.eg_zh: 告子的看法，是處境最糟的一種。

vocab.eg: People who are watched often give cause for watching.
vocab.eg_zh: 被監視的人，往往給出了該被監視的理由。

quiz.q: What does Mencius mean by saying that human nature is good?
options: People are born with tendencies that grow into virtue if they are cultivated.
People are born already virtuous.
People never do wrong.
Only sages have a good nature.

quiz.q: What is the point of the story of Ox Mountain?
options: A bare mountain does not show that trees were never its nature; damage is not nature.
Mountains should not be near cities.
Cattle are harmful.
Trees grow best at night.

quiz.q: What does Xunzi mean by saying that goodness is wěi?
options: It is produced by deliberate human effort.
It is fake.
It is impossible.
It is a gift of Heaven.

quiz.q: On what point do Mencius and Xunzi agree?
options: Anyone can become a sage, and cultivation is essential.
Human nature is bad.
Ritual is unnecessary.
Feeling is more reliable than intelligence.

quiz.q: What do the infant experiments suggest?
options: Sympathy and a preference for helpers appear before teaching, and so does partiality.
Infants have no preferences.
Infants are purely selfish.
Morality is entirely learned from parents.

write.en: Are you raising your children, or teaching your students, as a gardener or as a carpenter? Give one example.
write.zh: 你養育孩子、或教導學生，是像園丁還是像木匠？舉一個例子。

write.en: Which of the six pieces of evidence do you find hardest to fit into your own view? Explain in about 120 words.
write.zh: 六份證據當中，哪一份你覺得最難放進你自己的看法裡？用大約 120 個英文字說明。

write.en: Translate 人之性惡，其善者偽也 into English in a way that avoids the word “false,” and say why that matters.
write.zh: 把「人之性惡，其善者偽也」譯成英文，不要用 false 這個字；並且說明為什麼這很要緊。

paras.en: The Buddha makes two statements that seem to belong to opposite camps. “This mind, mendicants, is radiant. But it’s corrupted by visiting corruptions.” The defilements are called visitors. They arrive and can be made to leave, and what they cover is bright. That is close to Ox Mountain. But when a monk suggested that an infant must be free of the fetters, since it has no concepts with which to form a wrong view, the Buddha corrected him. A baby has no notion of sensual pleasure or of other beings, “yet the underlying tendency to sensual desire still lies within them,” and the tendency to ill will too. That is close to Xunzi. The two statements are consistent. Latent tendencies toward greed, hatred, and delusion are present from the start, and none of them belongs to the mind’s nature, since all can be removed.
paras.zh: 佛陀說過兩句話，看起來分屬相反的陣營。「比丘們，這個心是光淨的，卻被客塵煩惱所染污。」煩惱被稱為「客」。它們是來訪的，也可以被請走；而它們所遮蓋的，是明亮的。這很接近牛山。然而，當一位比丘提出「嬰兒必定沒有結使，因為他沒有藉以形成邪見的概念」時，佛陀糾正了他。嬰兒沒有欲樂的概念，也沒有其他眾生的概念，「然而欲貪的隨眠仍然潛伏在他裡面」，瞋恚的隨眠也是。這很接近荀子。這兩句話是一致的。貪、瞋、癡的潛在傾向從一開始就在；而它們沒有一樣屬於心的本性，因為全都可以被去除。

paras.en: The Mahāyāna developed the first statement into the teaching of Buddha-nature: every sentient being has within it, covered by defilements, the nature of an awakened one. A companion page asks which Western and Chinese view of human nature this comes closest to, and where the comparison fails.
paras.zh: 大乘把第一句話發展成了佛性的教導：每一個有情眾生裡面，都有被煩惱覆蓋著的覺悟者的本性。姊妹篇要問的是：這最接近西方與中國的哪一種人性觀？這個比較又在哪裡行不通？

lessons.title: What Is Happiness?
lessons.blurb_en: A machine that could give you any experience you chose, for life. Whether you would plug in decides between three theories of what makes a life go well, with Epicurus, Aristotle, Zhuangzi, and Yan Hui in his alley.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一台機器，可以給你任何你選的經驗，給一輩子。你願不願意接上去，就在三種「什麼使人生過得好」的理論之間作了裁決；還有伊比鳩魯、亞里斯多德、莊子，以及陋巷裡的顏回。
lessons.big_en: Everyone wants to be happy and few can say what they are wanting. The word covers a feeling, a judgment about one’s life, and a way of living, and the three do not always go together.
lessons.big_zh: 人人都想要幸福，卻很少有人說得出自己想要的是什麼。這個詞涵蓋了一種感受、一個對自己人生的判斷，以及一種生活的方式；而這三者並不總是走在一起。

paras.en: In 1974 the Harvard philosopher Robert Nozick described a device that neuroscientists might one day build. You float in a tank with electrodes attached to your brain, and the machine gives you any experience you like. You could seem to write a great novel, win a friend, or climb a mountain, and it would feel from the inside exactly as the real thing feels. You may choose your experiences in advance from a large library, and once you are in you will not know that you are in. Your body is cared for. Others can plug in too, so there is no one you need stay outside to help. Would you plug in for the rest of your life?
paras.zh: 1974 年，哈佛的哲學家諾齊克描述了一種神經科學家有朝一日也許造得出來的裝置。你漂浮在一個水槽裡，腦上接著電極；這台機器可以給你任何你喜歡的經驗。你可以「好像」寫出了一部偉大的小說、交到了一位朋友、登上了一座山；而從裡面感覺起來，會跟真的一模一樣。你可以事先從一座龐大的資料庫裡挑選你要的經驗；一旦進去，你就不會知道自己在裡面。你的身體有人照料。別人也可以接上去，所以你不需要為了幫助誰而留在外面。你願意接上去，度過餘生嗎？

paras.en: Most people who are asked say no, and Nozick thought their refusal showed something. If all that mattered to us were how our lives feel from the inside, we would have no reason to hesitate. Since we do hesitate, something else must matter. He suggested three things. We want to do certain things, and not merely to have the experience of doing them. We want to be a certain kind of person, and someone floating in a tank is not brave or kind or anything at all. And we want to be in contact with reality, not confined to a world that human beings have made.
paras.zh: 被問到的人，多數說不；而諾齊克認為，他們的拒絕顯示了某件事。如果對我們來說要緊的，只是人生「從裡面感覺起來」如何，我們就沒有理由猶豫。既然我們確實猶豫，就必定還有別的東西要緊。他提出了三樣。我們想要「做」某些事，而不只是擁有「做了那些事」的經驗。我們想要「是」某一種人；而一個漂在水槽裡的人，既不勇敢也不仁慈，什麼也不是。還有，我們想要與「真實」接觸，而不是被關在一個由人造出來的世界裡。

paras.en: The machine sorts the answers that philosophers have given to the question of what makes a life go well for the person who lives it. The first is hedonism: a good life is one with the most pleasure and the least pain, and nothing else counts in itself. It is the simplest view and the one the machine was designed to embarrass, since a hedonist ought to plug in at once. The second is the desire theory: a life goes well to the extent that the person gets what he wants. It explains the refusal neatly. I want to write a novel, and in the tank I would only believe that I had. Its weakness is that people want things that do them no good, and can be pleased by the fulfillment of desires that were planted in them. The third view holds that some things are good for a person whether or not he wants them or enjoys them: knowledge, friendship, achievement, the exercise of his abilities. Philosophers call it the objective list theory, and its weakness is the question of who writes the list.
paras.zh: 關於「什麼使一個人生對過這個人生的人來說是好的」，哲學家給過種種答案；這台機器把它們分了類。第一種是享樂論：好的人生就是快樂最多、痛苦最少的人生，此外沒有任何東西本身算數。這是最簡單的看法，也是這台機器被設計來為難的看法，因為一位享樂論者應該立刻接上去。第二種是欲望論：一個人得到他想要的東西到什麼程度，他的人生就好到什麼程度。它俐落地解釋了那份拒絕。我想要的是寫出一部小說；在水槽裡，我只會「相信」自己寫了。它的弱點是：人會想要對自己毫無益處的東西，也可能因為被植入的欲望得到滿足而高興。第三種看法主張：有些東西對一個人是好的，不管他想不想要、享不享受：知識、友誼、成就、能力的發揮。哲學家稱之為「客觀清單論」；而它的弱點是這個問題：清單由誰來寫？

paras.en: Hedonism has had one great defender who was no friend of luxury. Epicurus taught in a garden outside Athens around 300 BCE, and his name has become a word for fine dining through a misunderstanding he tried to prevent. “When we say, then, that pleasure is the end and aim, we do not mean the pleasures of the prodigal or the pleasures of sensuality, as we are understood to do by some through ignorance, prejudice, or willful misrepresentation. By pleasure we mean the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the soul.” The pleasant life is produced by “sober reasoning,” which examines every desire and drives out the beliefs that disturb us. He sorted desires into three kinds. Some are natural and necessary, like the desire for food and shelter, and these are easily met. Some are natural and unnecessary, like the desire for fine food. Some are neither, like the desires for fame and power, and these can never be satisfied, since they have no limit. Happiness comes from wanting what is enough.
paras.zh: 享樂論有過一位偉大的辯護者，而他並不是奢華的朋友。伊比鳩魯在西元前 300 年前後，在雅典城外的一座花園裡教學；由於一個他曾經設法防止的誤解，他的名字後來成了「講究美食」的代名詞。「所以，當我們說快樂是目的與目標的時候，我們指的並不是揮霍者的快樂或聲色的快樂；有些人出於無知、偏見或故意的曲解，以為我們是這個意思。我們所說的快樂，是身體沒有痛苦、靈魂沒有擾動。」愉快的生活是由「清醒的推理」產生的；它檢視每一個欲望，並且趕走那些擾亂我們的信念。他把欲望分成三種。有些是自然而必要的，像對食物與遮蔽的欲望；這些很容易滿足。有些是自然卻不必要的，像對美食的欲望。有些兩者都不是，像對名聲與權力的欲望；這些永遠無法滿足，因為它們沒有限度。幸福來自「想要的是足夠的東西」。

paras.en: Aristotle would have refused the machine without hesitation, and his reason is the root of the third theory. Happiness, for him, is something we do. It is “activity of soul in accordance with virtue,” over a complete life, and a person asleep or inactive is no more happy than a harp that is never played is making music. The man in the tank does nothing. Aristotle also saw a consequence that gentler philosophers have tried to avoid. If happiness is a life of excellent activity, it needs equipment: health, some money, friends, a city at peace. A good person who suffers the fate of King Priam, who saw his sons killed and his city burned, cannot be called happy. So happiness is partly a matter of luck, and he discusses the old saying of Solon that we must “see the end” before calling anyone happy.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德會毫不猶豫地拒絕那台機器；而他的理由，就是第三種理論的根。對他來說，幸福是我們「做」的事。它是「靈魂合乎德行的活動」，而且要在完整的一生當中；一個睡著的人或無所作為的人並不幸福，就像一把從來沒有人彈的豎琴並沒有在演奏音樂。水槽裡的那個人什麼也沒做。亞里斯多德還看到了一個比較溫和的哲學家們設法迴避的後果。如果幸福是卓越活動的一生，它就需要配備：健康、一些錢、朋友、一座太平的城邦。一個好人，如果遭遇了普里阿摩斯王那樣的命運（眼看著兒子們被殺、城被焚毀），就不能被稱為幸福。所以，幸福有一部分是運氣的事；而他討論了梭倫那句古老的話：在說任何人幸福之前，我們必須「看到結局」。

essay.h_en: The alley and the highest joy

paras.en: The Chinese tradition has a famous case that tests Aristotle’s claim about equipment. Confucius said of his favorite student: “How admirable Hui is! A bamboo dish of rice, a gourd of water, a mean alley. Others could not bear the misery, and Hui does not let it change his joy.” Later Confucians made a standing question of it: what was it that Yan Hui delighted in? The answer could not be poverty, which no one enjoys. It was something that poverty could not reach, and they took it to be the delight of a person whose desires and whose sense of what is right had become one. This is a happiness that needs little luck.
paras.zh: 中國的傳統有一個著名的案例，檢驗了亞里斯多德關於「配備」的主張。孔子這樣說他最鍾愛的學生：「賢哉回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷，人不堪其憂，回也不改其樂。」後來的儒者把它變成了一個常設的問題：顏回樂的是什麼？答案不可能是貧窮；沒有人享受貧窮。那是貧窮搆不到的某樣東西；他們認為，那是一個人的欲望與他對「什麼是對的」的感知已經合而為一的時候，所擁有的那份悅樂。這是一種不太需要運氣的幸福。

paras.en: Zhuangzi goes further and doubts the pursuit itself. He looks at what the world calls happiness, wealth, rank, long life, good food, and at the people rushing after these things “as though they could not stop,” and says that he cannot tell whether their happiness is happiness or not. His own conclusion is a paradox: “The highest happiness is without happiness.” The joy that is sought and held is already anxious. What remains when the seeking stops has no name that the seekers would recognize. Mill discovered the same thing in his breakdown: “Ask yourself whether you are happy, and you cease to be so.”
paras.zh: 莊子走得更遠，懷疑起這份追求本身。他看著世人所謂的幸福（富、貴、壽、美食），看著那些追逐這些東西的人「誙誙然如將不得已」，說他分不出他們的樂到底是樂還是不樂。他自己的結論是一個弔詭：「至樂無樂。」被追求、被握住的那種樂，已經是焦慮的了。追求停下來之後剩下的東西，沒有一個追求者認得出來的名字。彌爾在他的崩潰裡發現了同一件事：「問問自己是否幸福，你就不再幸福了。」

paras.en: Psychologists now measure happiness by asking large numbers of people how they feel and how satisfied they are with their lives, and several findings bear on the old theories. People adapt. Those who win lotteries and those who suffer serious injuries both return, within a few years, much of the way to where they were, a pattern known as the hedonic treadmill. Epicurus would have expected it. Income raises reported happiness steeply among the poor and less and less above a moderate level. The two measures come apart: a parent of small children often reports less pleasure hour by hour and more satisfaction with life as a whole. And the longest study of adult lives, which has followed a group of Harvard graduates and Boston men since 1938, found that the best predictor of a healthy and contented old age was the quality of a person’s close relationships. No one in the study was in a tank.
paras.zh: 心理學家現在測量幸福的方式，是去問為數眾多的人：你感覺如何？你對自己的人生有多滿意？有幾項發現與古老的理論相關。人會適應。中了彩券的人與受了重傷的人，都會在幾年之內，回到離原來不遠的地方；這個樣式被稱為「享樂跑步機」。伊比鳩魯會預料到它。收入在窮人當中使自陳的幸福急遽上升；超過一個中等的水準之後，就越來越少。那兩種量度會脫鉤：幼兒的父母，往往每一個小時回報的快樂較少，對整個人生的滿意卻較多。而關於成人生活歷時最久的那項研究（從 1938 年起追蹤一群哈佛畢業生與波士頓的男性），發現健康而滿足的晚年最好的預測指標，是一個人親密關係的品質。研究裡沒有任何人待在水槽裡。

paras.en: The machine remains a good test because it separates what we feel from what is so. A reader who would refuse it has learned that he wants more from life than good feelings. A reader who would accept it holds a view with a long and honorable history. Either way it is worth doing the experiment slowly.
paras.zh: 那台機器仍然是一個好的檢驗，因為它把「我們感覺到的」與「實際如此的」分開了。一位會拒絕它的讀者，已經得知自己想從人生得到的不只是好的感覺。一位會接受它的讀者，持有的是一個歷史悠久而可敬的看法。不管是哪一種，這個實驗都值得慢慢地做。

lab.title_en: Try it: the experience machine
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：體驗機
lab.lead_en: First choose the life you would have inside. Then answer four questions. At the end you will see what, besides feeling good, your answers show that you care about.
lab.lead_zh: 先選出你在裡面要過的人生。然後回答四個問題。最後你會看到：除了感覺好之外，你的答案顯示你還在乎什麼。

pick.en: Program your life. Choose up to five experiences. They will feel completely real.
pick.zh: 為你的人生寫程式。最多選五種經驗。它們感覺起來會完全真實。

menu.en: Writing a book that is loved
menu.zh: 寫出一本受人喜愛的書
一段長久而幸福的婚姻

text.en: The technician is ready. Once you are in, you will not know it, and you will never come out. Everyone you love may plug in too.
text.zh: 技術人員準備好了。一旦進去，你不會知道自己在裡面，而且永遠不會出來。你所愛的每一個人也都可以接上去。

t.en: Plug in
t.zh: 接上去

t.en: Stay out
t.zh: 留在外面

text.en: A different offer. Two years in the machine, then you come out, remember it all, and decide again.
text.zh: 另一個提議。在機器裡待兩年，然後出來，全部都記得，再重新決定。

t.en: Take the two years
t.zh: 接受這兩年

t.en: Decline
t.zh: 婉拒

text.en: A voice interrupts you. You are told that your whole life so far has been inside the machine. Your real life is that of an ordinary person, healthy, with no memory of anyone you know here. You may wake up, or stay where you are and forget this conversation.
text.zh: 一個聲音打斷了你。有人告訴你：你到目前為止的整個人生，都是在機器裡面過的。你真實的人生，是一個普通人的人生；健康，卻不記得你在這裡認識的任何人。你可以醒來，也可以留在原地，並且忘掉這段對話。

t.en: Wake up
t.zh: 醒來

t.en: Stay
t.zh: 留下

text.en: Your newborn child can be placed in a machine that guarantees a lifetime of joy. She will never know. You must decide for her today.
text.zh: 你剛出生的孩子，可以被放進一台保證一輩子喜悅的機器裡。她永遠不會知道。你必須在今天替她決定。

t.en: Plug her in
t.zh: 讓她接上去

t.en: Do not
t.zh: 不要

hed.en: You plugged in, you would stay in, and you would give the same to your child. Your answers are consistent, and the theory that fits them is hedonism: what makes a life good is how it feels to the one living it. Epicurus and Bentham are with you. The question Nozick would put is whether you could say this to the child, grown up, if she ever found out.
hed.zh: 你接上去了，你會留在裡面，而且你會給你的孩子同樣的東西。你的答案是一致的；符合它們的理論是享樂論：使一個人生好的，是它對過這個人生的人來說感覺如何。伊比鳩魯與邊沁站在你這一邊。諾齊克會提出的問題是：假如那個孩子長大後終於發現了，你能不能當著她的面這樣說？

real.en: You stayed out, and when told that you were already in, you chose to wake. Your answers are consistent, and they show that you want your life to be real even at a cost in happiness: real achievements, real people, the truth about your situation. That is Nozick’s conclusion, and it supports the view that some things are good for us apart from how they feel. You owe an account of why truth is worth more than joy to someone who will never know the difference.
real.zh: 你留在外面；而當有人告訴你其實你已經在裡面的時候，你選擇了醒來。你的答案是一致的；它們顯示，你要你的人生是真的，即使要付出幸福作為代價：真的成就、真的人、關於自己處境的真相。這是諾齊克的結論；它支持這樣的看法：有些東西對我們是好的，與它們感覺起來如何無關。你欠一個說明：對一個永遠不會知道差別的人來說，真相為什麼比喜悅更有價值？

quo.en: You refused to enter the machine, and when told that you were already in one, you refused to leave. This is the most common pair of answers, and it undoes Nozick’s argument. If reality were what you valued, you would wake. What your two answers share is that you kept the life you have. The philosopher Felipe De Brigard, who ran this experiment in 2010, concluded that our reaction to the machine owes a good deal to attachment to the familiar, and that it tells us less about happiness than Nozick supposed.
quo.zh: 你拒絕進入那台機器；而當有人告訴你其實你已經在一台機器裡的時候，你拒絕離開。這是最常見的一組答案，而它拆掉了諾齊克的論證。如果你看重的是真實，你就會醒來。你這兩個答案的共同點是：你保住了你現有的人生。哲學家德布里加在 2010 年做了這個實驗；他的結論是：我們對那台機器的反應，有不少是出於對熟悉事物的依戀；它告訴我們的關於幸福的事，比諾齊克以為的少。

mixed.en: Your answers do not follow one rule, and you may have been weighing several things: pleasure, truth, the people you know, and plain caution about an irreversible step. Look at the question where you hesitated longest. The thing that made you hesitate is a candidate for what you think a good life needs besides good feelings.
mixed.zh: 你的答案並不遵循同一條規則；你也許是在掂量好幾樣東西：快樂、真相、你認識的人，以及對一個無法回頭的步驟單純的謹慎。看看你猶豫得最久的那一題。讓你猶豫的那樣東西，就是你認為美好人生在「好的感覺」之外還需要什麼的一個候選答案。

child_gap.en: Notice the fourth answer. You chose the machine for yourself and refused it for your child. Parents nearly always do. What we want for those we love is often a better guide to what we think is good than what we would settle for ourselves.
child_gap.zh: 留意第四個答案。你為自己選了機器，卻替你的孩子拒絕了它。做父母的幾乎都會這樣。我們為所愛的人想要的東西，往往比我們自己願意將就的東西，更能指出我們認為什麼是好的。

peace.en: You put peace of mind on your list. Epicurus would say that you had chosen the one item that makes the others unnecessary, and that it cannot be delivered by a machine, since it consists in having examined one’s desires.
peace.zh: 你把「內心的平靜」放進了清單。伊比鳩魯會說：你選中了使其他各項都變得不必要的那一項；而它是機器送不來的，因為它就在於已經檢視過自己的欲望。

argument.lead_en: Nozick’s argument against hedonism. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 諾齊克反對享樂論的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: If hedonism is true, the only thing that makes a life better for the person living it is the quality of its experiences.
steps.zh: 如果享樂論是真的，那麼使一個人生對過它的人來說更好的唯一東西，就是它的經驗的品質。
steps.ob_en: This is the definition of the view.
steps.ob_zh: 這是這個看法的定義。

steps.en: A life in the experience machine would have better experiences than any life outside it.
steps.zh: 在體驗機裡的人生，會比機器外的任何人生擁有更好的經驗。
steps.ob_en: Granted by the description of the case. Some people refuse because they do not believe the machine would work, and that is a doubt about the story and no evidence about happiness.
steps.ob_zh: 由這個案例的描述所保證。有些人拒絕，是因為不相信這台機器真的行得通；那是對這個故事的懷疑，並不是關於幸福的證據。

steps.en: Most people, on reflection, would not plug in, and they are not making a mistake.
steps.zh: 多數人經過反思之後不會接上去，而且他們並沒有弄錯。
steps.ob_en: The second half is where the argument can be resisted. The reverse case in the exercise suggests that much of the refusal comes from attachment to one’s present life and fear of change. A hedonist can say that the intuition is real and is a bias.
steps.ob_zh: 這個論證可以被抵擋的地方，在後半句。練習裡那個「反過來」的案例顯示：這份拒絕，有很大一部分來自對目前人生的依戀，以及對改變的恐懼。享樂論者可以說：這個直覺是真實的，而它是一種偏誤。

steps.en: So something other than the quality of experience matters to how well a life goes, and hedonism is false.
steps.zh: 所以，除了經驗的品質之外，還有別的東西關係到一個人生過得好不好；享樂論是錯的。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion is modest. It does not say what else matters, and the three candidates Nozick names, doing, being, and contact with reality, are suggestions.
steps.ob_zh: 這個結論是有節制的。它並沒有說還有什麼要緊；而諾齊克舉出的三個候選（作為、是什麼樣的人、與真實接觸），只是提議。

source.work: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus
source.work_zh: 伊比鳩魯《致美諾西斯書》
source.tr: tr. R. D. Hicks (public domain)
source.lead_en: One of three letters by Epicurus that survive, preserved by a biographer five centuries later. It is three pages long and contains his whole ethics.
source.lead_zh: 伊比鳩魯流傳下來的三封信之一，由五個世紀之後的一位傳記作者保存下來。它只有三頁長，卻包含了他整套的倫理學。

passages.en: Let no one be slow to seek wisdom when he is young nor weary in the search thereof when he is grown old. For no age is too early or too late for the health of the soul. And to say that the season for studying philosophy has not yet come, or that it is past and gone, is like saying that the season for happiness is not yet or that it is now no more.
passages.zh: 年輕的時候，誰也不要遲遲不去尋求智慧；年老的時候，誰也不要厭倦於尋求它。因為對靈魂的健康來說，沒有哪個年紀是太早或太晚的。說研習哲學的時節還沒到、或已經過了，就像在說幸福的時節還沒到、或已經不再有了。
passages.note_en: The letter opens by identifying philosophy with the pursuit of happiness, which tells us what Epicurus thought philosophy was for. It is medicine. “The health of the soul” is the same image Plato used for justice in the lesson on the ring, and Epicurus draws the practical conclusion: one does not postpone a cure. His school accepted women and slaves, which no other school in Athens did, on the ground that everyone has a soul that can be ill.
passages.note_zh: 這封信一開頭，就把哲學等同於對幸福的追求；這告訴了我們，伊比鳩魯認為哲學是做什麼用的。它是藥。「靈魂的健康」，就是「戒指」那一課裡柏拉圖用在正義上的同一個意象；而伊比鳩魯引出了實際的結論：治療是不拖延的。他的學園接納女性與奴隸，這是雅典任何別的學派都沒有做的；理由是：每個人都有一個可能生病的靈魂。

passages.en: When we say, then, that pleasure is the end and aim, we do not mean the pleasures of the prodigal or the pleasures of sensuality, as we are understood to do by some through ignorance, prejudice, or willful misrepresentation. By pleasure we mean the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the soul. It is not an unbroken succession of drinking-bouts and of merrymaking… which produce a pleasant life; it is sober reasoning, searching out the grounds of every choice and avoidance, and banishing those beliefs through which the greatest disturbances take possession of the soul.
passages.zh: 所以，當我們說快樂是目的與目標的時候，我們指的並不是揮霍者的快樂或聲色的快樂；有些人出於無知、偏見或故意的曲解，以為我們是這個意思。我們所說的快樂，是身體沒有痛苦、靈魂沒有擾動。產生愉快生活的，並不是接連不斷的飲宴與作樂……而是清醒的推理：它探究每一個取捨的根據，並且驅除那些使最大的擾動佔據靈魂的信念。
passages.note_en: Two Greek words lie behind the definition: aponia, freedom from bodily pain, and ataraxia, freedom from disturbance. Epicurus holds that when these are present nothing can be added, so that pleasure has a ceiling and the ceiling is easily reached. This is what makes his hedonism so unlike the popular kind. It is also where critics attack. Cicero objected that the absence of pain is a neutral state and that calling it the highest pleasure is a trick with words. The reader can test the claim on the experience machine, which offers something far more vivid than tranquility.
passages.note_zh: 這個定義背後是兩個希臘字：aponia，身體沒有痛苦；ataraxia，沒有擾動。伊比鳩魯主張：這兩者具足的時候，就沒有什麼可以再加上去了；所以快樂有一個上限，而這個上限很容易達到。這就是他的享樂論之所以這麼不像通俗的那一種的原因。這也是批評者進攻的地方。西塞羅反對說：沒有痛苦是一種中性的狀態；把它稱為最高的快樂，是在玩文字遊戲。讀者可以拿體驗機來檢驗這個主張；那台機器提供的東西，比寧靜要鮮明得多。

items.o_en: Happiness is subjective. If a person feels happy, he is happy, and no philosopher can tell him otherwise.
items.o_zh: 幸福是主觀的。一個人覺得幸福，他就是幸福的；沒有哪位哲學家可以說他不是。
items.r_en: This is true of the feeling and less clearly true of the thing we wish for our children. Consider a man whose wife and friends secretly despise him and who never finds out. He feels as happy as a man whose wife and friends love him. Most people judge that the second man’s life is going better, and would choose it for themselves. If so, how a life is going can differ from how it seems to the one living it.
items.r_zh: 就那個「感覺」而言，這是真的；就我們希望自己孩子擁有的那個東西而言，就沒有那麼清楚了。設想一個人，他的妻子與朋友暗地裡瞧不起他，而他始終沒有發現。他覺得自己跟一個被妻子與朋友所愛的人一樣幸福。多數人判斷後者的人生過得比較好，並且會為自己選擇那一個。若是如此，一個人生過得怎樣，就可能不同於它對過這個人生的人來說看起來怎樣。

items.o_en: The objective list is arrogance. Who is anyone to say that knowledge or friendship is good for a person who does not want it?
items.o_zh: 客觀清單是傲慢。誰有資格說，知識或友誼對一個不想要它的人是好的？
items.r_en: The worry is fair, and lists have been used to push people around. But the theory does not say that anything should be forced on anyone. It says that a person can be mistaken about what would be good for him, which everyone accepts about his own past. We all remember wanting things that would have harmed us. The list is a summary of what people who have tried many ways of living tend to report, and it can be revised as the reports come in.
items.r_zh: 這個憂慮是合理的；清單確實曾被用來擺布人。但這個理論並沒有說任何東西應該被強加在任何人身上。它說的是：一個人可能弄錯什麼對自己是好的；而對於自己的過去，每個人都接受這一點。我們都記得自己曾經想要過會傷害自己的東西。這份清單，是那些試過許多種生活方式的人往往會回報的東西的摘要；隨著回報陸續進來，它可以修訂。

items.o_en: Seeking happiness is selfish. A good person thinks about duty and about others, and lets happiness look after itself.
items.o_zh: 追求幸福是自私的。好人想的是義務、是別人，讓幸福自己照顧自己。
items.r_en: Kant held something like this, and Mill’s crisis taught him that happiness pursued directly escapes. Both points can be granted without giving up the subject. To ask what makes a life go well is necessary for anyone who cares about others, since we cannot benefit them without some idea of what a benefit is. And on the best ancient accounts, Aristotle’s and the Confucian, the happy life is the life of a person who is good to others. The two questions were asked together for most of history.
items.r_zh: 康德主張過類似的看法；而彌爾的危機教會了他：直接去追求的幸福會溜走。這兩點都可以承認，而不必放棄這個題目。對任何一個在乎別人的人來說，問「什麼使人生過得好」是必要的；因為如果對「什麼算是益處」毫無概念，我們就無法使別人受益。而照古代最好的說法（亞里斯多德的與儒家的），幸福的人生，就是一個善待他人的人的人生。在歷史上大部分的時間裡，這兩個問題是一起問的。

said.claim: “Eat, drink, and be merry, for tomorrow we die.” (Epicurus)
said.claim_zh: 「吃吧，喝吧，快活吧，因為明天我們就要死了。」（伊比鳩魯）
said.verdict_en: The Bible, quoting his opponents’ caricature
said.verdict_zh: 出自聖經，引的是他的對手對他的醜化
said.en: Epicurus said nothing of the kind, and the letter quoted above rejects “drinking-bouts and merrymaking” by name. The sentence is stitched together from two verses of the Bible. Ecclesiastes commends eating, drinking, and being merry, and Isaiah, repeated by Paul, has “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die,” as the motto of people without hope. It was attached to the Epicureans by ancient critics who found it easier to attack a party of gluttons than a community that lived on bread and water and counted a pot of cheese a feast.
said.zh: 伊比鳩魯沒有說過這種話；上面引的那封信，還指名拒絕了「飲宴與作樂」。這句話是由聖經的兩節經文拼接而成的。《傳道書》稱許吃、喝與快樂；《以賽亞書》（保羅引用過）則有「我們吃喝吧，因為明天要死了」，那是沒有盼望的人的座右銘。把它安到伊比鳩魯學派頭上的，是古代的批評者；他們發現，攻擊一群饕客，比攻擊一個靠麵包與水過活、把一罐乳酪當成盛宴的團體容易得多。

terms.d_en: How well a life is going for the person whose life it is.
terms.d_zh: 一個人生對過這個人生的人來說，過得有多好。

terms.d_en: The view that well-being consists in pleasure and the absence of pain.
terms.d_zh: 主張福祉就在於快樂與沒有痛苦。

terms.d_en: The view that well-being consists in getting what one wants.
terms.d_zh: 主張福祉就在於得到自己想要的。

terms.d_en: The view that certain things are good for a person whether or not he wants or enjoys them.
terms.d_zh: 主張有些東西對一個人是好的，不管他想不想要、享不享受。

terms.d_en: Freedom from mental disturbance, the Epicurean goal.
terms.d_zh: 心靈不受擾動；伊比鳩魯學派的目標。

terms.d_en: Aristotle’s term for a life of excellent activity. A way of living, not a feeling.
terms.d_zh: 亞里斯多德的用語：卓越活動的一生。它是一種生活方式，不是一種感受。

terms.d_en: The tendency to return toward a baseline level of happiness after good or bad events.
terms.d_zh: 在好事或壞事之後，回到幸福感基準線附近的傾向。

terms.o: L. status quo ‘the state in which’
terms.d_en: A preference for one’s present situation simply because it is present.
terms.d_zh: 偏好目前的處境，僅僅因為它是目前的。

vocab.eg: Would you plug in for the rest of your life?
vocab.eg_zh: 你願意接上去，度過餘生嗎？

vocab.eg: It would feel from the inside exactly as the real thing feels.
vocab.eg_zh: 從裡面感覺起來，會跟真的一模一樣。

vocab.eg: A defender of pleasure who was no friend of luxury.
vocab.eg_zh: 一位為快樂辯護、卻不贊成奢華的人。

vocab.eg: The pleasant life is produced by sober reasoning.
vocab.eg_zh: 愉快的生活是由清醒的推理產生的。

vocab.eg: A life goes well to the extent that the person gets what he wants.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個人得到他想要的到什麼程度，他的人生就好到什麼程度。

vocab.eg: Several findings bear on the old theories.
vocab.eg_zh: 有幾項發現與古老的理論相關。

vocab.eg: The two measures come apart.
vocab.eg_zh: 那兩種量度會脫鉤。

vocab.eg: What we would settle for ourselves.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們自己願意將就的東西。

vocab.eg: Let happiness look after itself.
vocab.eg_zh: 讓幸福自己照顧自己。

vocab.eg: A gourd of water, a mean alley.
vocab.eg_zh: 一瓢飲，在陋巷。

quiz.q: What is the experience machine meant to test?
options: Whether the quality of our experiences is the only thing that matters to how well our lives go.
Whether machines can think.
Whether virtual reality is possible.
Whether pleasure is bad.

quiz.q: What three things did Nozick say we want besides good experiences?
options: To do things, to be a certain kind of person, and to be in contact with reality.
Money, fame, and power.
Health, safety, and sleep.
Knowledge, travel, and food.

quiz.q: What did Epicurus mean by pleasure?
options: The absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the soul.
Feasting and luxury.
Fame and applause.
Constant excitement.

quiz.q: Why, for Aristotle, is happiness partly a matter of luck?
options: It is a life of excellent activity, which needs health, friends, and other external goods.
The gods distribute it at random.
It depends on one’s birthday.
It cannot be achieved by anyone.

quiz.q: What does the “reverse” experience machine suggest?
options: That much of our refusal to plug in may come from attachment to our present life.
That reality does not exist.
That everyone is a hedonist.
That machines are dangerous.

write.en: Write two lists: what gives you the most pleasure in a week, and what you would be proudest of at the end of your life. Where do the lists differ?
write.zh: 寫兩份清單：一個星期裡，什麼帶給你最多快樂？到了人生的終點，你會最引以為傲的是什麼？兩份清單在哪裡不同？

write.en: What did Yan Hui delight in? Answer in about 120 words.
write.zh: 顏回樂的是什麼？用大約 120 個英文字回答。

write.en: Sort five things you want this year into Epicurus’s three kinds of desire.
write.zh: 把你今年想要的五樣東西，分進伊比鳩魯的三種欲望裡。

paras.en: The Buddha ranks kinds of happiness in an ascending order, and the order is the reverse of what the machine offers. Lowest is the pleasure of the senses, which is real, brief, and bound up with the fear of losing it. Above it is the happiness of a mind that has given up such pleasures and become collected in meditation, which the texts describe as a joy that drenches the body as water soaks a ball of bath powder. Above that is the peace of a mind that no longer clings. The machine supplies the first kind without limit and cannot supply the others, since they are states of the person and not contents of experience. Epicurus, who placed tranquility above excitement, is the Western philosopher who saw this most clearly.
paras.zh: 佛陀把各種樂排成一個上升的次第；而這個次第，與那台機器所提供的正好相反。最低的是感官之樂；它是真實的、短暫的，並且與「怕失去它」的恐懼綁在一起。在它之上，是捨離了這類快樂、在禪定中收攝起來的心的樂；經典形容那種喜悅浸潤全身，就像水浸透一團澡粉。再往上，是一顆不再執取的心的安穩。那台機器可以無限量地供應第一種，卻供應不了其餘的；因為它們是「人」的狀態，而不是經驗的內容。伊比鳩魯把寧靜放在刺激之上；他是把這一點看得最清楚的西方哲學家。

paras.en: The tradition then makes a claim that goes beyond him. Sāriputta once declared, “Extinguishment is bliss!” A monk objected: “What’s blissful about it, since nothing is felt?” He answered: “The fact that nothing is felt is precisely what’s blissful about it.” Every feeling, however pleasant, is something that has arisen and will pass, and to depend on it is to be exposed. The Dhammapada puts the ranking in a line: contentment is the greatest wealth, and nibbāna “the ultimate happiness.” Whether a happiness that is not a feeling can be called happiness at all is the point at which Zhuangzi’s paradox, “the highest happiness is without happiness,” and the Buddha’s meet (Dharma and the West, D6 and D22).
paras.zh: 接著，這個傳統提出了一個超出他的主張。舍利弗有一次宣告：「涅槃是樂！」一位比丘提出異議：「既然那裡沒有任何感受，有什麼樂可言？」他回答：「正是沒有任何感受，才是其中的樂。」每一個感受，不管多麼愉悅，都是已生起、將消逝的東西；依賴它，就是暴露在危險之中。《法句經》用一句話說出了這個排序：知足是最大的財富，涅槃是「最上的樂」。一種「不是感受」的樂，到底還能不能叫作樂？莊子的弔詭「至樂無樂」與佛陀的說法，就在這一點上相會（佛法與西方哲學 D6、D22）。

further.t: Robert Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974), pages 42–45
further.n_en: The machine takes up three pages.
further.n_zh: 那台機器只佔了三頁。

further.t: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus and Principal Doctrines, translated by R. D. Hicks
further.n_en: Three pages and forty sayings.
further.n_zh: 三頁，加上四十條格言。

further.t: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book I, chapters 7–10
Zhuangzi, chapter 18, “Perfect Happiness”; Analects 6.11
Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011), Part V
further.n_en: The experiencing self and the remembering self.
further.n_zh: 經驗的自我與記憶的自我。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Well-Being”

lessons.title: What Can You Control?
lessons.blurb_en: A slave in Rome divided everything into what is up to us and what is not, and built a whole way of life on the line. The Stoic method, a pilot who tested it in a prison camp, its Chinese counterpart in Mencius, and where the line may be wrongly drawn.
lessons.blurb_zh: 羅馬的一個奴隸，把一切分成「在我們」與「不在我們」的兩類，並且在那條線上建起了一整套生活方式。斯多噶的方法、一位在戰俘營裡檢驗過它的飛行員、它在孟子那裡的對應，以及那條線可能劃錯的地方。
lessons.big_en: Most distress comes from wanting what is not in our power and neglecting what is. The Stoics claimed that a person who got this one distinction right could not be made unhappy by anything that happened to him.
lessons.big_zh: 大部分的苦惱，來自想要不在我們能力範圍內的東西，卻疏忽了在我們能力範圍內的東西。斯多噶學派宣稱：一個把這一個區分弄對了的人，不可能因為任何發生在他身上的事而變得不幸。

paras.en: Around the year 125 a student named Arrian wrote down a short summary of what he had heard from his teacher, a freed slave who ran a school in a provincial Greek town. The handbook begins: “There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power. Within our power are opinion, aim, desire, aversion, and, in one word, whatever affairs are our own. Beyond our power are body, property, reputation, office, and, in one word, whatever are not properly our own affairs.” The teacher was Epictetus, and the rest of his philosophy follows from the division. What is up to us is free and cannot be hindered. What is not up to us belongs to others, and whoever sets his heart on it “will lament” and “find fault both with gods and men.”
paras.zh: 大約在西元 125 年，一位名叫阿里安的學生，把他從老師那裡聽來的東西寫成了一份簡短的摘要；他的老師是一個獲釋的奴隸，在希臘一座外省小城裡辦了一所學校。這本手冊這樣開頭：「有些事物在我們的能力之內，有些事物在我們的能力之外。在我們能力之內的是：意見、志向、欲求、厭避，一言以蔽之，凡是屬於我們自己的事。在我們能力之外的是：身體、財產、名聲、職位，一言以蔽之，凡是不真正屬於我們自己的事。」那位老師是愛比克泰德；他其餘的哲學，都從這個劃分推出。在我們的，是自由的，無法被阻礙。不在我們的，屬於別人；誰把心放在它上面，誰就「將會悲嘆」，並且「怨天尤人」。

paras.en: Notice what is on the second list. The body is there. A man can train and eat well and still fall ill. Reputation is there, since it lives in other people’s minds. Even one’s own life is there. What remains on the first list is small and of a single kind: our judgments, and the wants and choices that follow from them.
paras.zh: 請留意第二份清單上有什麼。身體在上面。一個人可以鍛鍊、可以吃得好，仍然會生病。名聲在上面，因為它活在別人的心裡。甚至自己的性命也在上面。留在第一份清單上的東西很少，而且只有一種：我們的判斷，以及隨之而來的欲求與抉擇。

paras.en: The second step is a claim about where suffering comes from. “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.” Death is not terrible in itself, Epictetus argues, or it would have seemed so to Socrates. The terror lies in our opinion that it is terrible. When someone insults you, what hurts is your own view that you have been harmed. Between the event and the distress there is always a judgment, and the judgment is ours to make. Stoic training consists in catching that judgment before it has been made. An impression arrives: I have been wronged. The student learns to say to it, You are only an appearance, and to examine it before agreeing.
paras.zh: 第二步，是一個關於「苦從哪裡來」的主張。「擾亂人的不是事物，而是人對事物所抱的看法。」愛比克泰德論證：死亡本身並不可怕，否則蘇格拉底也會覺得它可怕。可怕的，是我們認為它可怕的那個意見。有人侮辱你的時候，傷人的是你自己「我受到了傷害」的那個看法。在事件與苦惱之間，永遠有一個判斷；而那個判斷是由我們來下的。斯多噶的訓練，就在於趁那個判斷還沒有下的時候把它攔住。一個印象到來：我被冤枉了。學生學著對它說「你只是一個表象」，並且在同意它之前先檢視它。

paras.en: The emperor Marcus Aurelius, who read Epictetus and kept a notebook of exercises for his own use, put it this way: “If thou art pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgement about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgement now.” He began his days by reminding himself that he would meet with ingratitude, arrogance, and deceit, so that none of it would come as a surprise.
paras.zh: 皇帝馬可・奧理略讀過愛比克泰德，並且為自己留了一本操練用的筆記；他是這樣說的：「如果你因為任何外在的事物而痛苦，擾亂你的並不是那件事物，而是你自己對它的判斷。而你有能力現在就把這個判斷抹去。」他每天一開始，就提醒自己今天會遇到忘恩負義、傲慢與欺詐的人，這樣就沒有一樣會讓他意外。

paras.en: What should one want, then? Epictetus answers with an instruction that sounds like surrender: “Demand not that events should happen as you wish; but wish them to happen as they do happen, and you will go on well.” His image is the theater. “Remember that you are an actor in a drama of such sort as the Author chooses. If it be his pleasure that you should enact a poor man, or a cripple, or a ruler, or a private citizen, see that you act it well. For this is your business—to act well the given part, but to choose it belongs to another.” He was himself lame, and had been a slave. The Stoics believed that the universe is governed by a rational providence, so that whatever happens is part of a good order. To want things otherwise is to quarrel with the nature of things. The teaching is not passivity. The actor works hard at the part. An archer does everything to aim well and then lets the arrow go, and whether it hits is no longer his affair.
paras.zh: 那麼，人應該想要什麼？愛比克泰德用一個聽起來像投降的指示來回答：「不要要求事情照你希望的那樣發生；要希望它們照實際發生的那樣發生，你就會過得順遂。」他用的意象是劇場。「記住：你是一齣戲裡的演員，這齣戲是什麼樣子，由作者決定。如果他樂意讓你演一個窮人、一個跛子、一位統治者或一個平民，你就要把它演好。因為這才是你的事：把分派給你的角色演好；至於選角色，那是另一位的事。」他自己就是跛的，並且當過奴隸。斯多噶學派相信，宇宙是由一個理性的天意治理的；所以，凡是發生的事，都是一個良好秩序的一部分。希望事情是別的樣子，就是跟事物的本性爭吵。這個教導並不是消極。演員會在角色上下苦功。弓箭手盡一切力量瞄準，然後放箭；至於中不中，就不再是他的事了。

paras.en: Mencius drew the same line four centuries before Epictetus, in two sentences. “‘Seek and you will get it, let go and you will lose it’: here seeking helps the getting, because what is sought lies within myself. ‘There is a way to seek it, and getting it depends on fate’: here seeking does not help the getting, because what is sought lies outside.” What lies within, for Mencius, is the cultivation of one’s own character, and what lies outside is wealth, rank, and length of life. Confucius described his own attitude in six characters: “I do not resent Heaven, and I do not blame men.” The Confucians gave the outside a name, mìng, what is decreed, and they taught that a person does everything that is his to do and then awaits the decree.
