paras.zh: 孟子比愛比克泰德早四個世紀，用兩句話劃出了同一條線。「『求則得之，舍則失之』，是求有益於得也，求在我者也。『求之有道，得之有命』，是求無益於得也，求在外者也。」對孟子來說，「在我者」是自己品格的修養；「在外者」是富、貴與壽命。孔子用六個字描述自己的態度：「不怨天，不尤人。」儒者給了「外」一個名字：「命」；並且教導，人要把分內該做的都做了，然後等待那個命。

paras.en: Zhuangzi states the conclusion in its most extreme form: “To know what cannot be helped and to rest in it as in fate is the perfection of virtue.” The resemblance to the Stoics is close, and the two traditions arose with no contact. The similarity of their situations may explain it. Both were philosophies for people living under powers they could not influence, an emperor in one case and the warring kings in the other.
paras.zh: 莊子把這個結論說到了最極端的形式：「知其不可奈何而安之若命，德之至也。」這跟斯多噶學派非常相像，而兩個傳統是在毫無接觸的情況下各自出現的。處境的相似，也許可以解釋這一點。兩者都是給「活在自己影響不了的權力之下」的人的哲學：一邊是皇帝，另一邊是爭戰中的諸王。

paras.en: In September 1965 the American pilot James Stockdale was shot down over North Vietnam. He had studied philosophy at Stanford a few years earlier, and a professor had given him the handbook of Epictetus. As he drifted down under his parachute, he later wrote, he said to himself that he was leaving the world of technology and entering the world of Epictetus. He was a prisoner for seven and a half years, four of them in solitary confinement, and was tortured repeatedly. He credited his survival to the first sentence of the handbook. His captors controlled his body, his food, and his news of home. They did not control what he would agree to, and he organized the other prisoners around that fact. He noticed that the men who broke were often the optimists, who told themselves they would be home by Christmas, and were crushed when Christmas passed.
paras.zh: 1965 年 9 月，美國飛行員斯托克戴爾在北越上空被擊落。幾年前他在史丹佛讀過哲學，有位教授送了他愛比克泰德的《手冊》。他後來寫道：當他吊在降落傘下往下飄的時候，他對自己說，他正在離開科技的世界，進入愛比克泰德的世界。他當了七年半的戰俘，其中四年被單獨囚禁，並且一再遭受酷刑。他把自己能活下來，歸功於《手冊》的第一句話。俘虜他的人控制了他的身體、他的食物、他與家鄉的音訊。他們控制不了他同意什麼；而他就圍繞著這個事實，把其他的戰俘組織起來。他注意到：崩潰的人往往是樂觀的人；他們告訴自己聖誕節前就能回家，而聖誕節過去的時候，他們就被壓垮了。

paras.en: The method has also been tested in clinics. The psychologists who founded cognitive behavioral therapy in the 1950s and 1960s, Albert Ellis and Aaron Beck, both cited Epictetus as a source, and the therapy’s central technique is his: identify the judgment that stands between an event and the distress, and examine whether it is true. It is among the best-supported treatments for anxiety and depression.
paras.zh: 這個方法也在診間裡被檢驗過。在 1950、1960 年代創立認知行為治療的心理學家艾里斯與貝克，都把愛比克泰德列為思想來源；而這種治療的核心技術就是他的：找出站在事件與苦惱之間的那個判斷，檢視它是否為真。它是對焦慮與憂鬱最有實證支持的療法之一。

essay.h_en: Where the line may be wrong
essay.h_zh: 那條線可能劃錯的地方

paras.en: Three doubts are worth carrying into the exercise. The first is whether the division is too sharp. Epictetus has two lists, and most of life seems to fall between them. My health, my child’s character, and whether I win the match are things I influence and do not determine. A modern Stoic, William Irvine, proposes a third category for these and a rule for handling them: set your goal in terms of what is yours. Aim to play your best game, since winning is not up to you. The second doubt is whether the first list is as secure as Epictetus thought. Our judgments are shaped by mood, fatigue, upbringing, and illness, and a person in a deep depression cannot simply wipe one out.
paras.zh: 有三個疑問，值得帶進下面的練習。第一：這個劃分是不是太截然了？愛比克泰德只有兩份清單，而人生的大部分似乎落在兩者之間。我的健康、我的孩子的品格、我能不能贏下這場比賽，都是我影響得了、卻決定不了的事。一位當代的斯多噶學者厄文，提議為這些事設立第三個類別，並且給了一條處理它們的規則：用「屬於你的東西」來設定目標。目標定為「打出自己最好的一場球」，因為贏不贏不由你。第二個疑問：第一份清單，真的像愛比克泰德以為的那麼牢靠嗎？我們的判斷受到情緒、疲勞、教養與疾病的塑造；一個陷在重度憂鬱裡的人，沒辦法說抹去就抹去一個判斷。

paras.en: The third doubt is moral. A philosophy that teaches people to change their desires and not their circumstances suits the powerless, and it also suits those who would like the powerless to stay quiet. Epictetus tells a man to remind himself, when he kisses his child, that he is kissing a mortal, so that he will not be shattered if the child dies. Many readers feel that something has gone wrong when grief is treated as an error of judgment. The Stoic reply is that one can love fully and still know what one loves. Whether that is wisdom or a refusal to be fully in one’s life is the question the school has always had to face.
paras.zh: 第三個疑問是道德上的。一套教人「改變自己的欲望、而不是改變處境」的哲學，適合無權無勢的人；它也適合那些希望無權無勢者保持安靜的人。愛比克泰德要一個人在親吻自己孩子的時候提醒自己：他親吻的是一個會死的人；這樣，孩子若是死了，他就不至於崩潰。當悲傷被當成一種判斷上的錯誤時，許多讀者覺得有什麼地方不對了。斯多噶的回答是：人可以全心去愛，同時仍然知道自己愛的是什麼。那是智慧，還是拒絕完全活在自己的人生裡？這是這個學派一直必須面對的問題。

lab.title_en: Try it: twelve things, three baskets
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：十二件事，三個籃子
lab.lead_en: Sort each item by how far it is in your power. Then compare your baskets with those of Epictetus, who allowed only two, and with a modern Stoic who allows three.
lab.lead_zh: 把每一項依「它在你的能力範圍內到什麼程度」分類。然後把你的籃子，跟愛比克泰德的（他只准有兩個）與一位當代斯多噶學者的（他准三個）比一比。

t.en: Up to me
t.zh: 在我

t.en: Partly up to me
t.zh: 部分在我

t.en: Not up to me
t.zh: 不在我

t.en: What I say next
t.zh: 我接下來要說的話

t.en: What other people think of me
t.zh: 別人怎麼看我

t.en: Whether I win the match
t.zh: 我能不能贏下這場比賽

t.en: How hard I train
t.zh: 我訓練得多努力

t.en: Tomorrow’s weather
t.zh: 明天的天氣

t.en: My health
t.zh: 我的健康

t.en: My opinion of a colleague
t.zh: 我對一位同事的看法

t.en: Whether I am promoted
t.zh: 我會不會升遷

t.en: Whether I take an insult as an injury
t.zh: 我要不要把一句侮辱當成傷害

t.en: What happened last year
t.zh: 去年發生的事

t.en: Whether my child grows up happy
t.zh: 我的孩子長大後幸不幸福

t.en: What I give my attention to
t.zh: 我把注意力放在哪裡

strict.en: You used the middle basket once or not at all. You sort as Epictetus does. His view is that “partly” is a confusion: every such case contains something that is wholly yours, the effort and the aim, and something that is not yours at all, the result. The cost of his view shows in the rows for health and for your child, where he tells you that the outcome is none of your concern.
strict.zh: 中間那個籃子，你只用了一次，或完全沒用。你的分法跟愛比克泰德一樣。他的看法是：「部分」是一種混淆；每一個這樣的情況裡，都有某樣完全屬於你的東西（努力與志向），以及某樣根本不屬於你的東西（結果）。他這個看法的代價，顯現在「健康」與「你的孩子」那兩列：在那裡，他告訴你結果不關你的事。

three.en: You used the middle basket often. You sort as Irvine does, and as common sense does. The Stoic advice for everything in that basket is to move your goal inward. You cannot make your child happy. You can be a patient parent today, and that goal is entirely in your hands. Look at each item you placed in the middle and find the part of it that could go in the first basket.
three.zh: 中間那個籃子，你用得很多。你的分法跟厄文一樣，也跟常識一樣。對那個籃子裡的每一樣東西，斯多噶的建議都是：把你的目標往內移。你沒辦法「使」你的孩子幸福。你可以在今天當一位有耐心的父母；而這個目標完全在你手上。看看你放在中間的每一項，找出其中可以放進第一個籃子的那個部分。

wide.en: You put several things in the first basket that the Stoics would take out of it, such as your health, your promotion, or what others think. This is the mistake Epictetus built his school to correct. He would say that you have staked your peace on things that can be taken from you, and that you will “lament and find fault with gods and men.” He may be too severe. But notice which of these items has cost you sleep.
wide.zh: 你把好幾樣斯多噶學派會拿出去的東西，放進了第一個籃子，例如你的健康、你的升遷，或別人的看法。愛比克泰德辦學，就是要糾正這個錯誤。他會說：你把自己的安寧押在了可以從你手上被拿走的東西上，而你將會「悲嘆，並且怨天尤人」。他也許太嚴厲了。不過請留意：這些項目當中，哪一樣曾經讓你睡不著？

narrow.en: You took out of the first basket some things the Stoics leave in it, such as your opinions, your attention, or whether you take an insult as an injury. You may be right. Judgments are less obedient than Epictetus assumed, and anyone who has tried to stop a worry by deciding to stop knows it. The Stoic reply is that these are skills. They are in your power in the way that playing the piano is, after long practice and not before.
narrow.zh: 你把一些斯多噶學派留在第一個籃子裡的東西拿了出去，例如你的意見、你的注意力，或你要不要把一句侮辱當成傷害。你也許是對的。判斷並不像愛比克泰德預設的那麼聽話；任何試過「決定不再擔心」來停止擔心的人都知道。斯多噶的回答是：這些是技能。它們在你的能力之內，是像彈鋼琴那樣的「在」：在長久練習之後，而不是之前。

argument.lead_en: The Stoic argument that a wise person cannot be made unhappy by events. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 斯多噶的論證：有智慧的人，不可能因為事件而變得不幸。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Distress is caused by the judgment that something bad has happened to me, and never by the event alone.
steps.zh: 苦惱是由「有壞事發生在我身上」這個判斷造成的，而絕不是單由事件造成的。
steps.ob_en: True of much distress, and the basis of cognitive therapy. Less clearly true of physical pain, of the terror of a small child, or of grief, which seem to come before any judgment.
steps.ob_zh: 對許多苦惱來說是真的，並且是認知治療的基礎。對身體的疼痛、幼兒的驚恐或悲傷來說，就沒有那麼清楚了；這些似乎先於任何判斷而來。

steps.en: Our judgments are entirely up to us.
steps.zh: 我們的判斷完全在我們。
steps.ob_en: The weakest step. Judgments depend on a brain that can be tired, drugged, or ill, and on habits laid down before we could choose. The Stoics themselves said that the first flinch is involuntary and that only the assent is ours, which already concedes something.
steps.ob_zh: 最弱的一步。判斷依賴一個可能疲倦、被下藥或生病的腦，也依賴在我們能夠選擇之前就已經養成的習慣。斯多噶學派自己就說過：最初的那一下退縮是不由自主的，只有「同意」才是我們的；這已經讓出了一些東西。

steps.en: Nothing outside our own character is really good or bad for us. Health, wealth, and reputation are “indifferent.”
steps.zh: 在我們自己的品格之外，沒有任何東西對我們來說真的是好或壞。健康、財富與名聲是「無關善惡的」。
steps.ob_en: This is the hardest Stoic doctrine to accept, and Aristotle rejects it: a good person on the rack is not happy. Without it the argument fails, since a true judgment that I have lost something good would be a reason for distress.
steps.ob_zh: 這是斯多噶最難接受的教義，而亞里斯多德拒絕它：一個在刑架上的好人並不幸福。少了它，這個論證就不成立；因為如果「我失去了某樣好東西」是一個真的判斷，它就是苦惱的理由。

steps.en: So a person who judges correctly will never be distressed, whatever happens.
steps.zh: 所以，一個判斷正確的人，不管發生什麼事，都不會苦惱。
steps.ob_en: Even those who reject the conclusion can keep the method. One need not believe that nothing external matters in order to benefit from asking, of each worry, which part of it is mine to do something about.
steps.ob_zh: 即使是拒絕這個結論的人，也可以保留這個方法。不必相信「外在的東西全都無關緊要」，也能從這樣的提問中得益：對每一個煩惱，問一問其中哪一部分是我可以著手的？

source.work: Epictetus, The Enchiridion (Handbook), chapters 1, 5, and 43
source.work_zh: 愛比克泰德《手冊》第一、五、四十三章
source.tr: tr. T. W. Higginson (public domain)
source.lead_en: The handbook has fifty-three short chapters and can be read in an hour. Arrian compiled it from his notes of the lectures so that a student could carry the teaching about with him. The Greek title means “something held in the hand,” and the word was also used for a dagger.
source.lead_zh: 《手冊》有五十三個短章，一個小時就能讀完。阿里安從他的聽講筆記編成了它，好讓學生可以把這個教導帶在身上。希臘文的書名意思是「握在手裡的東西」；這個詞也被用來指匕首。

passages.en: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things. Thus death is nothing terrible, else it would have appeared so to Socrates. But the terror consists in our notion of death, that it is terrible. When, therefore, we are hindered or disturbed, or grieved, let us never impute it to others, but to ourselves—that is, to our own views.
passages.zh: 擾亂人的不是事物，而是人對事物所抱的看法。所以死亡並沒有什麼可怕；否則蘇格拉底也會覺得它可怕了。可怕的，在於我們對死亡的那個看法：認為它是可怕的。因此，當我們受到阻礙、擾亂或感到悲傷的時候，絕不要歸咎於別人，要歸咎於自己，也就是歸咎於我們自己的看法。
passages.note_en: The argument about Socrates is a neat one. If death were terrible in itself, everyone who faced it would be terrified, and one calm man is enough to show that the terror is added by us. The last sentence states the practical rule. It is easy to misread as self-blame. Epictetus means it as good news: if the cause of my distress is a view I hold, the remedy is within my reach. He goes on to say that the beginner blames others, the student blames himself, and the fully trained person blames no one.
passages.note_zh: 關於蘇格拉底的那個論證很俐落。如果死亡本身就可怕，每一個面對它的人都會驚恐；而只要有一個平靜的人，就足以顯示那份驚恐是我們加上去的。最後一句陳述了實際的準則。它很容易被誤讀成自責。愛比克泰德是把它當作好消息說的：如果我的苦惱的原因是我所抱持的一個看法，那麼解藥就在我搆得到的地方。他接著說：初學者責怪別人，學生責怪自己，受過完整訓練的人誰也不責怪。

passages.en: Everything has two handles: one by which it may be borne, another by which it cannot. If your brother acts unjustly, do not lay hold on the affair by the handle of his injustice, for by that it cannot be borne, but rather by the opposite—that he is your brother, that he was brought up with you; and thus you will lay hold on it as it is to be borne.
passages.zh: 每一樣東西都有兩個把手：一個可以提得起它，另一個提不起它。如果你的兄弟行事不義，不要抓住「他的不義」這個把手，因為抓那一個是提不起來的；要抓相反的那一個：他是你的兄弟，他是跟你一起長大的。這樣，你抓住的就是這件事提得起來的地方。
passages.note_en: This is the gentlest chapter in the book and the best answer to the charge that Stoicism is cold. Epictetus does not ask the reader to deny that the brother acted unjustly. Both descriptions are true. He asks which true description one will take hold of, since that is a choice, and one of them makes it possible to go on living with the brother. Modern therapists call the move reframing.
passages.note_zh: 這是全書最溫和的一章，也是對「斯多噶是冷的」這項指控最好的回答。愛比克泰德並沒有要求讀者否認那位兄弟行了不義。兩種描述都是真的。他問的是：你要抓住哪一個「真的描述」？因為那是一個選擇；而其中一個，使你有可能繼續跟這位兄弟相處下去。現代的治療師把這一招叫作「重新框架」。

items.o_en: This is a philosophy for slaves. It teaches people to accept what they ought to fight.
items.o_zh: 這是給奴隸的哲學。它教人接受自己本來應該起而抗爭的東西。
items.r_en: The charge was made by Nietzsche and has some truth in it. Epictetus never called for the abolition of slavery. But the Stoics did not teach inaction. They held that each person has duties that go with his roles, as parent, citizen, or soldier, and Marcus Aurelius spent his reign at war on the frontier. What they taught was to act without making one’s peace depend on the result. Reformers who have had to work for decades without success have often found that useful.
items.r_zh: 這項指控是尼采提出的，其中有幾分是真的。愛比克泰德從來沒有呼籲廢除奴隸制。但斯多噶學派並沒有教人不行動。他們主張，每個人都有伴隨他的角色（父母、公民或士兵）而來的責任；而馬可・奧理略的在位期間，是在邊境的戰事中度過的。他們教的是：去行動，而不讓自己的安寧取決於結果。那些必須努力幾十年而不見成功的改革者，往往發現這一點很有用。

items.o_en: A person who feels no grief when his child dies is not wise. He is damaged.
items.o_zh: 一個孩子死了卻不感到悲傷的人，不是有智慧。他是受了損傷。
items.r_en: The later Stoics agreed more than their slogans suggest. Seneca wrote that the wise man will weep, and that tears come of themselves. What they opposed was the second movement, in which grief is fed by the judgment that the loss is unbearable and that life is now ruined. Critics reply that deep love makes one vulnerable by its nature, and that to remove the vulnerability is to love less. Aristotle is on the critics’ side, and so, in a different way, is Confucius, who wept without restraint when Yan Hui died.
items.r_zh: 後期的斯多噶學派，同意的程度比他們的口號所顯示的更多。塞內卡寫過：有智慧的人會流淚，而眼淚是自己流下來的。他們反對的是第二步：在那一步裡，悲傷被「這個損失無法承受、人生就此毀了」的判斷所餵養。批評者回答：深的愛，本性上就使人容易受傷；而去除這份脆弱，就是愛得少一點。亞里斯多德站在批評者那一邊；孔子也是，只是方式不同：顏回死的時候，他哭得毫無節制。

items.o_en: If everything that happens is part of a rational plan, then cruelty is too, and nothing can be called bad.
items.o_zh: 如果發生的每一件事都是一個理性計畫的一部分，那麼殘忍也是；就沒有什麼可以被稱為壞的了。
items.r_en: The objection strikes at Stoic theology, and most modern readers set that part aside. One can hold that the universe has no plan at all and still find the division of control useful, as a piece of practical psychology. The Stoics themselves distinguished between what happens and what a person chooses. The first is fate. The second, including the choice to be cruel, is the one thing they held us fully responsible for.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁打中的是斯多噶的神學；而多數現代的讀者把那一部分擱在一邊。一個人可以主張宇宙根本沒有計畫，同時仍然覺得「控制的劃分」有用，把它當作一則實用的心理學。斯多噶學派自己就區分了「發生的事」與「一個人所選擇的事」。前者是命運。後者（包括選擇殘忍）是他們認為我們要負完全責任的唯一一樣東西。

said.claim: “You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength.” (Marcus Aurelius)
said.claim_zh: 「你能支配的是自己的心，不是外在的事件。明白這一點，你就會找到力量。」（馬可・奧理略）
said.en: The sentence is one of the most shared quotations of the emperor and does not occur in the Meditations in that form. It is a loose modern summary of passages such as the one quoted in this lesson: “it is not this thing that disturbs thee, but thy own judgement about it. And it is in thy power to wipe out this judgement now.” The paraphrase is fair to his meaning. It is worth knowing that the book he actually wrote is rougher and sadder than the posters suggest. It is a private notebook, in Greek, that he never meant anyone to read, and much of it is a tired man reminding himself to get out of bed and do his work.
said.zh: 這句話是這位皇帝被轉貼最多的語錄之一，卻不以這個形式出現在《沉思錄》裡。它是對某些段落的一個鬆散的現代摘要；例如這一課引過的那一段：「擾亂你的並不是那件事物，而是你自己對它的判斷。而你有能力現在就把這個判斷抹去。」這個改寫並沒有違背他的意思。值得知道的是：他實際寫的那本書，比海報所顯示的更粗糙、也更悲傷。它是一本私人筆記，用希臘文寫成，他從來沒有打算讓任何人讀；其中很大一部分，是一個疲倦的人在提醒自己起床、把工作做完。

terms.o: Gk. stoa ‘porch,’ where its founder taught
terms.d_en: The school founded by Zeno of Citium in Athens around 300 BCE, which taught that virtue is the only good.
terms.d_zh: 季蒂昂的芝諾在西元前 300 年前後創立於雅典的學派；它教導德行是唯一的善。

terms.d_en: The division of all things into those that are up to us and those that are not.
terms.d_zh: 把一切事物分成「在我們」與「不在我們」兩類。

terms.d_en: What appears to the mind, and the mind’s act of accepting it as true.
terms.d_zh: 對心顯現的東西，以及心把它接受為真的那個行動。

terms.d_en: Things such as health and wealth, which the Stoics held to be neither good nor bad in themselves.
terms.d_zh: 健康、財富這類東西；斯多噶學派主張它們本身既不善也不惡。

terms.d_en: Freedom from the passions that arise from false judgments. Not “apathy” in the modern sense.
terms.d_zh: 不受由錯誤判斷所生的激情支配。不是現代意義上的「冷漠」。

terms.d_en: The rational ordering of the universe, which the Stoics identified with God and with nature.
terms.d_zh: 宇宙的理性安排；斯多噶學派把它等同於神，也等同於自然。

terms.d_en: In Confucian thought, what is decreed and lies beyond a person’s effort.
terms.d_zh: 在儒家思想裡，被決定而在個人努力之外的東西。

terms.d_en: Choosing a different true description of a situation in order to change one’s response to it.
terms.d_zh: 為了改變自己對某個處境的反應，而選擇另一個同樣為真的描述。

vocab.eg: Whoever sets his heart on it will lament.
vocab.eg_zh: 誰把心放在它上面，誰就將會悲嘆。

vocab.eg: You will find fault both with gods and men.
vocab.eg_zh: 你將會怨天尤人。

vocab.eg: In one word, whatever affairs are our own.
vocab.eg_zh: 一言以蔽之，凡是屬於我們自己的事。

vocab.eg: None of it would come as a surprise.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有一樣會讓他意外。

vocab.eg: Lay hold on it as it is to be borne.
vocab.eg_zh: 抓住它提得起來的地方。

vocab.eg: He credited his survival to the first sentence of the handbook.
vocab.eg_zh: 他把自己能活下來，歸功於《手冊》的第一句話。

vocab.eg: They were crushed when Christmas passed.
vocab.eg_zh: 聖誕節過去的時候，他們就被壓垮了。

vocab.eg: You have staked your peace on things that can be taken from you.
vocab.eg_zh: 你把自己的安寧押在了可以被拿走的東西上。

vocab.eg: The outcome is none of your concern.
vocab.eg_zh: 結果不關你的事。

vocab.eg: Tears come of themselves.
vocab.eg_zh: 眼淚是自己流下來的。

quiz.q: According to Epictetus, which of these is within our power?
options: Our opinions and desires.
Our bodies.
Our reputation.
Our property.

quiz.q: What does “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things” mean?
options: Between an event and our distress there is a judgment, and the judgment is ours.
Nothing bad ever happens.
People should avoid looking at things.
Events are illusions.

quiz.q: How does the Stoic archer illustrate the teaching?
options: He does everything to aim well, and treats whether the arrow hits as no longer his affair.
He refuses to shoot.
He always hits the target.
He blames the wind.

quiz.q: What did Mencius mean by “what is sought lies within myself”?
options: The cultivation of one’s character, where seeking helps the getting.
Wealth and rank.
Long life.
The favor of the king.

quiz.q: What is Irvine’s amendment to Epictetus?
options: A third category of things partly in our control, handled by setting internal goals.
That nothing is in our control.
That everything is in our control.
That the Stoics were Buddhists.

write.en: Take one thing you are worried about this week. Write two lists under it: what is yours to do, and what is not.
write.zh: 拿一件你這個星期正在擔心的事。在它底下寫兩份清單：哪些是你分內可以做的？哪些不是？

write.en: Is grief an error of judgment? Answer in about 150 words, with an example.
write.zh: 悲傷是一種判斷上的錯誤嗎？用大約 150 個英文字回答，並舉一個例子。

write.en: Rewrite a goal you have, such as passing an examination or being liked by a class, so that it is entirely up to you.
write.zh: 把你的一個目標（例如通過一場考試，或被一班學生喜歡）改寫成完全在你自己手上的樣子。

paras.en: The Buddha makes the Stoic point with an image. When an untrained person is touched by a painful feeling, he grieves and laments. “It’s like a person who is struck with an arrow, only to be struck with a second arrow.” The first arrow is the pain. The second is the mind’s reaction to it, the resistance and the story of how unbearable it is. A trained person feels the first arrow and is not struck by the second. This is Epictetus’s distinction between the thing and the view, located where the Stoics also located it, in the moment between feeling and reaction. The Buddha likewise lists the conditions that toss people about: “gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.” They are called the eight worldly winds, and every item belongs on Epictetus’s second list.
paras.zh: 佛陀用一個意象說出了斯多噶的那個要點。未受訓練的人被苦受觸及時，會憂愁、悲嘆。「這就像一個人被一支箭射中，接著又被第二支箭射中。」第一支箭是那個痛。第二支，是心對它的反應：抗拒，以及「這有多麼無法忍受」的那個故事。受過訓練的人感受到第一支箭，卻不被第二支射中。這就是愛比克泰德對「事物」與「看法」的區分；而它被放的位置，也是斯多噶學派放的位置：在感受與反應之間的那一刻。佛陀同樣列出了把人拋來拋去的那些條件：「利與衰、譽與毀、譏與稱、樂與苦。」它們被稱為「八風」；其中每一項，都屬於愛比克泰德的第二份清單。

paras.en: The two part company on what does the controlling. For Epictetus the faculty of judgment and choice is the true self, a fragment of divine reason, and the whole of ethics is to keep it free. The Buddha finds no such commander. Judgments and intentions are themselves conditioned events, and a person gains freedom by seeing them clearly and by long training of attention, with no inner citadel to defend. They differ also in what calm is for. Stoic calm rests on the belief that the world is governed for the best. Buddhist equanimity makes no such claim about the world, and it is listed beside loving-kindness and compassion as one of four states to be cultivated together, so that it does not harden into indifference (Dharma and the West, D20 and D22).
paras.zh: 兩者在「是什麼在控制」這一點上分道揚鑣。對愛比克泰德來說，判斷與抉擇的那個能力就是真正的自我，是神聖理性的一個片段；而倫理學的全部，就是讓它保持自由。佛陀找不到這樣一位指揮官。判斷與意圖本身，就是受條件制約的事件；人得到自由，靠的是把它們看清楚、靠的是對注意力的長期訓練，並沒有一座內在的堡壘要守。他們對「平靜是為了什麼」的看法也不同。斯多噶的平靜，建立在「世界是為了最好的結果而被治理的」這個信念上。佛教的「捨」對世界並不作這樣的主張；而且它是與慈、悲並列，作為要一起修習的四種心境之一，使它不至於硬化成冷漠（佛法與西方哲學 D20、D22）。

further.t: Epictetus, The Enchiridion, translated by T. W. Higginson
further.n_en: An hour’s reading.
further.n_zh: 一個小時讀完。

further.t: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, translated by George Long
further.n_en: Begin with Books II and IV.
further.n_zh: 從卷二與卷四讀起。

further.t: James B. Stockdale, “Courage Under Fire: Testing Epictetus’s Doctrines in a Laboratory of Human Behavior” (1993)
further.n_en: His own account, twenty pages.
further.n_zh: 他自己的敘述，二十頁。

further.t: Mencius 7A3; Zhuangzi, chapter 4; Analects 14.35
further.n_en: What lies within and what lies outside.
further.n_zh: 在我者與在外者。

further.t: William B. Irvine, A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy (2009)
further.n_en: The modern version, with the three categories.
further.n_zh: 現代的版本，含三分法。

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.6, The Arrow

lessons.title: What Is a Friend?
lessons.blurb_en: Aristotle’s three kinds of friendship, Montaigne’s one friend, a zither player who broke his instrument, and the man who said that his parents gave him life but Bao understood him.
lessons.blurb_zh: 亞里斯多德的三種友誼、蒙田唯一的那位朋友、一位摔碎了琴的琴師，以及那個說「生我者父母，知我者鮑子也」的人。
lessons.big_en: We use one word for the person we do business with, the person we laugh with, and the person who knows us. Philosophers have asked whether these are the same relation in different strengths or different relations altogether, and why a life without the last kind seems not worth living.
lessons.big_zh: 跟我們有生意往來的人、跟我們一起笑的人、了解我們的人，我們都用同一個詞稱呼。哲學家問過：這些是同一種關係的不同強度，還是根本不同的關係？還有，為什麼少了最後那一種，人生似乎就不值得過？

essay.h_en: The thing no one would live without

paras.en: Aristotle gave two of the ten books of his Ethics to friendship, more than to any other single subject, and he opens with a sentence that states its importance flatly: “without friends no one would choose to live, though he had all other goods.” The rich need friends in order to have someone to benefit, the poor need them as a refuge, the young to keep them from error, and the old to care for them. Modern moral philosophy has had much less to say. Its main theories are about what we owe to everyone, and a friend is someone to whom we give what we do not owe and from whom we expect what we could not demand. The ancient writers, Greek and Chinese, treated the subject as central, and the best way into it is still Aristotle’s question: what is it that we like when we like a person?
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德把他的《倫理學》十卷當中的兩卷給了友誼，比給任何別的單一主題的都多；而他用來開頭的那句話，直截了當地說出了它的重要：「沒有朋友，誰也不會選擇活下去，即使他擁有其他一切的善。」富人需要朋友，才有人可以施惠；窮人需要朋友作為避難所；年輕人需要朋友使他們不犯錯；老人需要朋友照顧他們。現代的道德哲學對此說得少得多。它的主要理論談的是我們「欠每一個人」什麼；而朋友，是我們給他並不欠他的東西、並且從他那裡期待我們無法要求的東西的那個人。古代的作者，不論希臘的還是中國的，都把這個題目當作核心；而進入它最好的路，仍然是亞里斯多德的那個問題：當我們喜歡一個人的時候，我們喜歡的是什麼？

paras.en: There are three things, he says, for which we can love anything: because it is useful, because it is pleasant, or because it is good. “There are therefore three kinds of friendship.” In the first, each party values the other for some advantage. Business partners are friends in this way, and so are many neighbors and colleagues. In the second, each enjoys the other’s company: the people we drink, travel, or play with. Aristotle does not despise these. He observes two things about them. In both, the other person is loved for something he supplies, and so they last only as long as the supply. “Those who love each other for their utility do not love each other for themselves but in virtue of some good which they get from each other.” When the usefulness ends or tastes change, the friendship dissolves, and no one is to blame.
paras.zh: 他說，我們之所以能愛任何東西，原因有三：因為它有用，因為它令人愉快，或因為它是善的。「所以友誼有三種。」在第一種裡，雙方各自因為某種好處而看重對方。生意上的夥伴就是這樣的朋友；許多鄰居與同事也是。在第二種裡，雙方各自享受對方的陪伴：跟我們一起喝酒、旅行或玩樂的人。亞里斯多德並不輕視這些。他對它們觀察到兩點。在這兩種裡，對方之所以被愛，都是因為他所提供的某樣東西；所以它們只能維持到那個提供停止為止。「因為有用而彼此相愛的人，並不是因為對方本身而愛對方，而是因為從對方得到的某種好處。」用處沒了，或者口味變了，友誼就消散了，而這不能怪誰。

paras.en: The third kind is different. “Perfect friendship is the friendship of men who are good, and alike in virtue,” and such friends “wish well to their friends for their sake.” Here the person himself is what is loved, his character and not his services. This friendship includes the other two, since good people are both useful and pleasant to each other, and it lasts, because character is the most durable thing about a person. It is also rare. It needs time and shared life, “for men cannot know each other till they have eaten salt together,” and nobody can have it with many people, any more than one can be in love with many at once. Aristotle adds a phrase that has been repeated ever since: a friend of this kind is “another self.”
paras.zh: 第三種不一樣。「完美的友誼，是善良而在德行上相似的人之間的友誼」；這樣的朋友「為了朋友本身的緣故而願他好」。在這裡，被愛的是這個人本身，是他的品格，而不是他的效勞。這種友誼包含了另外兩種，因為好人彼此既有用又令人愉快；而且它持久，因為品格是一個人身上最經久的東西。它也很罕見。它需要時間，需要共同的生活；「人若沒有一起吃過鹽，就無法彼此了解」。而且沒有人能跟很多人擁有它，就像一個人不可能同時愛上很多人。亞里斯多德還加了一個從此被一再重複的說法：這一種朋友，是「另一個自己」。

paras.en: Aristotle’s account makes friendship reasonable: we love the good because it is good. The French essayist Michel de Montaigne, who had one such friend and lost him, thought that this leaves out the center of the experience. He met Étienne de La Boétie at a crowded feast in Bordeaux when both were young magistrates, and from that first meeting, he says, nothing was so near to either as the other. La Boétie died a few years later, at thirty-two. Montaigne wrote the essay on friendship some ten years afterward. In such a friendship, he says, two souls “mix and work themselves into one piece, with so universal a mixture, that there is no more sign of the seam by which they were first conjoined.” Asked for the reason, he can give none. “If a man should importune me to give a reason why I loved him, I find it could no otherwise be expressed, than by making answer: because it was he, because it was I.”
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德的說明，使友誼成為合理的：我們愛善，因為它是善的。法國的隨筆作家蒙田有過一位這樣的朋友，又失去了他；他認為，這個說明漏掉了這種經驗的核心。他是在波爾多一場擁擠的宴會上遇見拉波埃西的，當時兩人都是年輕的法官；他說，從那第一次見面起，對兩人來說就沒有什麼比對方更親近的了。幾年後，拉波埃西去世，三十二歲。大約十年之後，蒙田寫下了那篇論友誼的隨筆。他說，在這樣的友誼裡，兩個靈魂「混合、交融成一體，融合得那麼徹底，以致於當初把它們縫合起來的那道接縫，再也看不出痕跡」。問他理由，他給不出來。「如果有人逼我說出我為什麼愛他，我覺得除了這樣回答之外，沒有別的說法：因為是他，因為是我。」

paras.en: The disagreement is real. For Aristotle a friend is loved for qualities, and anyone with the same qualities would in principle do as well. For Montaigne the friend cannot be replaced, and a list of his virtues would explain nothing. Both seem to be describing something true. We do admire our closest friends, and we would be dismayed to learn that they were cruel. Yet we would not exchange them for someone more admirable.
paras.zh: 這個分歧是真實的。對亞里斯多德來說，朋友是因為種種特質而被愛的；而任何具有同樣特質的人，原則上都一樣可以。對蒙田來說，那位朋友無可取代；把他的德行列成清單，什麼也解釋不了。兩人描述的似乎都是真的。我們確實欽佩自己最親近的朋友；如果得知他們是殘忍的人，我們會大為沮喪。然而，我們也不會拿他們去換一個更值得欽佩的人。

essay.h_en: The one who knows the tune

paras.en: The Chinese tradition has its own word for Montaigne’s kind of friend, and it comes from a story. Bo Ya was a master of the zither, and Zhong Ziqi was good at listening. When Bo Ya played with his mind on high mountains, Zhong Ziqi said, “Splendid! Lofty as Mount Tai!” When his mind was on flowing water, Zhong Ziqi said, “Splendid! Broad as the great rivers!” Whatever Bo Ya had in mind, Zhong Ziqi never failed to grasp it. When Zhong Ziqi died, another version adds, Bo Ya broke the zither and cut its strings and never played again, judging that there was no one left in the world worth playing for. The phrase zhīyīn, “one who knows the tone,” has meant a true friend ever since. What the story picks out is being understood. Zhong Ziqi did nothing for Bo Ya and gave him no pleasure that a paying audience could not have given. He heard what was meant.
paras.zh: 中國的傳統，對蒙田那一種朋友有它自己的詞；而這個詞來自一個故事。伯牙善於彈琴，鍾子期善於聽。伯牙彈琴，心裡想著高山，鍾子期說：「善哉！峩峩兮若泰山！」心裡想著流水，鍾子期說：「善哉！洋洋兮若江河！」伯牙心裡想的是什麼，鍾子期必定聽得出來。另一個版本接著說：鍾子期死了，伯牙「破琴絕弦，終身不復鼓琴，以為世無足復為鼓琴者」。從此以後，「知音」（懂得那個音的人）就是真朋友的意思。這個故事挑出來的，是「被了解」。鍾子期沒有為伯牙做任何事，他給伯牙的快樂，也沒有哪一樣是付錢的聽眾給不了的。他聽出了伯牙的意思。

paras.en: The historian Sima Qian preserves a second example in the words of the statesman Guan Zhong. When he was poor and took the larger share of their profits, his friend Bao Shuya did not think him greedy, knowing that he was poor. When he fled three times in battle, Bao did not think him a coward, knowing that he had an old mother. “It was my parents who gave me life,” Guan Zhong said, “and it is Bao who knows me.” To be known in this way is to be seen at one’s worst and read correctly. It asks more of a friend than Aristotle’s likeness in virtue.
paras.zh: 史家司馬遷用政治家管仲自己的話，保存了第二個例子。他窮的時候，跟鮑叔牙合夥做生意，分錢時自己多拿，鮑叔不認為他貪，知道他窮。他打仗時三次臨陣脫逃，鮑叔不認為他膽小，知道他家有老母。管仲說：「生我者父母，知我者鮑子也。」以這種方式被了解，就是在自己最糟的時候被看見，並且被正確地解讀。這對朋友的要求，比亞里斯多德的「德行相似」更多。

essay.h_en: Three that help and three that harm

paras.en: Confucius approaches the matter as a teacher would, by asking what a friend does to you. “Three kinds of friends are a gain and three are a loss. To have friends who are upright, friends who are true to their word, and friends who have heard much is a gain. To have friends who are smooth, friends who are soft and pleasing, and friends who are glib is a loss.” The helpful friend tells you the truth, can be relied on, and knows things you do not. The harmful ones are, in Aristotle’s terms, friends of pleasure. They agree with you. His student Zengzi states the purpose in a line: the gentleman “uses his friends to support his humaneness.” A friend is a partner in becoming a better person, and friendship is the one relationship among the five Confucian bonds that is chosen and that holds between equals.
paras.zh: 孔子是像一位老師那樣切入這件事的：他問的是朋友對你「做了什麼」。「益者三友，損者三友：友直，友諒，友多聞，益矣；友便辟，友善柔，友便佞，損矣。」有益的朋友對你說實話、靠得住，並且知道你不知道的事。有害的那幾種，用亞里斯多德的話說，就是快樂的朋友。他們順著你。他的學生曾子用一句話說出了目的：君子「以友輔仁」。朋友是「成為更好的人」這件事上的夥伴；而在儒家的五倫當中，朋友是唯一出於選擇、而且存在於平等者之間的一倫。

paras.en: Zhuangzi offers a caution about warmth. “The friendship of the gentleman is plain as water. The friendship of the small man is sweet as rich wine. The gentleman’s plainness brings closeness. The small man’s sweetness ends in a break.” A relation that needs constant sweetness is being held together by something other than the two people.
paras.zh: 莊子對「熱絡」提出了一個警告。「君子之交淡若水，小人之交甘若醴；君子淡以親，小人甘以絕。」一段需要不斷加糖的關係，把它維繫在一起的，是這兩個人之外的別的東西。

paras.en: The word has recently been stretched. A person may now have a thousand “friends” on a screen, most of whom he has not eaten salt with. The anthropologist Robin Dunbar has argued, from the size of primate brains and from counts of human groups, that a person can keep up stable relationships with about a hundred and fifty people, of whom about fifteen are close and about five are intimate. The numbers have held up fairly well in studies of telephone records and of online networks. They are Aristotle’s point in figures: the highest kind of friendship needs shared time, and time is limited.
paras.zh: 這個詞近來被拉長了。一個人現在可以在螢幕上有一千個「朋友」，其中大多數他沒有跟對方一起吃過鹽。人類學家鄧巴根據靈長類腦的大小與對人類群體的計數，論證一個人能夠維持穩定關係的對象大約是一百五十人，其中大約十五人算親近，大約五人算親密。在對電話紀錄與線上網絡的研究裡，這些數字相當站得住。它們就是用數字說出來的亞里斯多德的論點：最高的那一種友誼需要共度的時間，而時間是有限的。

paras.en: That leaves a question the exercise below is meant to raise. Most of the people we call friends are friends of use or of pleasure, and there is nothing wrong with that. The difficulty comes from not knowing which is which. We are hurt when a friendship of convenience ends with the convenience, and we neglect, because it is plain as water, the one that would have lasted.
paras.zh: 這就留下了一個問題，下面的練習就是要把它提出來。我們稱為朋友的人，大多數是有用的朋友或快樂的朋友，而這並沒有什麼不對。困難來自分不清哪一個是哪一種。一段因方便而起的友誼，隨著方便的結束而結束時，我們感到受傷；而那段本來可以長久的友誼，因為它淡若水，我們卻疏忽了。

lab.title_en: Try it: three friends
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：三位朋友
lab.lead_en: Think of a particular friend and keep that person in mind. Answer six questions about the friendship. Nothing is recorded and no name is asked. You may repeat it for a second and a third friend, and then compare.
lab.lead_zh: 想一位特定的朋友，把這個人放在心裡。回答六個關於這段友誼的問題。不會留下任何紀錄，也不問名字。你可以為第二位、第三位朋友各做一次，然後比較。

t.en: If neither of you could ever again do the other a favor or be of any use, would the friendship go on?
t.zh: 如果你們兩個從此再也幫不上對方任何忙、對彼此毫無用處，這段友誼還會繼續嗎？

t.en: If you could no longer do the enjoyable things you do together, would it go on?
t.zh: 如果你們再也不能一起做那些愉快的事，它還會繼續嗎？

t.en: Would this friend tell you a truth you did not want to hear?
t.zh: 這位朋友會對你說一句你不想聽的實話嗎？

t.en: Has this friend stood by you, or kept faith with you, when it cost something?
t.zh: 這位朋友曾經在要付出代價的時候，仍然站在你這一邊、或對你守信嗎？

t.en: Have you learned something from this friend that changed how you think or live?
t.zh: 你曾經從這位朋友身上學到某樣改變了你的想法或生活的東西嗎？

t.en: When this friend succeeds at something you care about, are you simply glad?
t.zh: 這位朋友在一件你也在乎的事情上成功了，你是單純地為他高興嗎？

t.en: By your own answer, this friendship rests on what each of you can do for the other. Aristotle counts it a real friendship and an honest one, so long as both know what it is. It will last as long as the usefulness does. If it ends then, no one has been betrayed.
t.zh: 照你自己的回答，這段友誼建立在你們各自能為對方做的事上。亞里斯多德認為它是真正的友誼，而且是正當的，只要雙方都知道它是什麼。用處維持多久，它就維持多久。如果它在那時結束，並沒有誰被背叛。

t.en: This friendship would survive the loss of advantage and would not survive the loss of the things you enjoy together. Aristotle thinks it better than the first kind, since it is at least the person’s company that is liked. It is the usual friendship of the young, he says, who change their friends as their pleasures change.
t.zh: 這段友誼熬得過「好處」的消失，卻熬不過你們共同享受的那些事的消失。亞里斯多德認為它比第一種好，因為被喜歡的至少是這個人的陪伴。他說，這是年輕人通常的友誼；他們的樂趣變了，朋友也跟著換。

t.en: This friendship would outlast use and pleasure, and it bears the marks that Aristotle and Confucius both look for: honesty, loyalty that has been tested, and goodwill without envy. Aristotle says that a person can have very few of these, and that they need time above all. It is worth asking when you last gave this one any.
t.zh: 這段友誼比用處與快樂更長久，並且帶著亞里斯多德與孔子都在找的那些標記：誠實、經過考驗的忠信，以及沒有嫉妒的善意。亞里斯多德說，一個人能擁有的這種友誼非常少，而它們最需要的是時間。值得問一問：你上一次給這一段友誼時間，是什麼時候？

t.en: This friendship does not depend on use or on shared pleasures, which already sets it apart. It lacks one or more of the marks of the complete kind. Look at the questions you answered with a no. A friend who would not tell you an unwelcome truth is, in the Analects, one of the three that harm. And if the no was yours, in the last question, the thing to work on is in you.
t.zh: 這段友誼不依賴用處，也不依賴共同的樂趣，這已經使它與眾不同了。它缺了完整的那一種的一個或幾個標記。看看你答「不」的那幾題。一位不肯對你說逆耳實話的朋友，在《論語》裡屬於損者三友。而如果那個「不」是你自己的（在最後一題），那麼需要下工夫的地方在你身上。

liang.en: true to his word 友諒

end.en: Aristotle would not be surprised by this table. He says that friendships of the complete kind are few, “for such men are rare,” and that the other two kinds are the ordinary fabric of social life. The point of sorting is to stop asking of one kind what only another can give, and to know which friends you would break the zither for.
end.zh: 亞里斯多德不會對這張表感到意外。他說，完整的那一種友誼很少，「因為這樣的人很罕見」；而另外兩種，是社會生活平常的質地。分類的用意，是不再向某一種友誼要求只有另一種才給得了的東西；並且知道，哪幾位朋友是你會為他破琴絕弦的。

argument.lead_en: Aristotle’s argument that only friendship based on character is friendship in the full sense. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 亞里斯多德的論證：只有建立在品格上的友誼，才是完整意義上的友誼。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: To be a friend to someone is to wish him well for his own sake.
steps.zh: 作某人的朋友，就是為了他本身的緣故而願他好。
steps.ob_en: Widely accepted as a mark of friendship. It distinguishes a friend from a customer.
steps.ob_zh: 作為友誼的一個標記，這一點廣被接受。它把朋友與顧客區分開來。

steps.en: In friendships of use and of pleasure, each loves the other for what he provides and not for what he is.
steps.zh: 在有用的友誼與快樂的友誼裡，每一方愛對方，是為了他所提供的東西，而不是為了他之所是。
steps.ob_en: This may be too harsh. Two colleagues who began by being useful to each other often come to care about each other. Aristotle allows that the lower kinds can grow into the higher.
steps.ob_zh: 這也許太苛刻了。兩位起初只是彼此有用的同事，往往後來變得在乎對方。亞里斯多德承認，較低的那幾種可以長成較高的那一種。

steps.en: What a person is, most of all, is his character.
steps.zh: 一個人之所是，最主要的就是他的品格。
steps.ob_en: Montaigne’s objection belongs here. If I love my friend for his character, I love a set of qualities that someone else could have. What I love is this person, and “because it was he” is the only reason there is.
steps.ob_zh: 蒙田的反駁屬於這裡。如果我是為了朋友的品格而愛他，我愛的就是一組別人也可能具有的特質。我愛的是「這個人」；而「因為是他」，是唯一有的理由。

steps.en: So only those who love each other for their character are friends without qualification. The others are friends by resemblance.
steps.zh: 所以，只有因品格而彼此相愛的人，才是無條件意義上的朋友。其餘的，是因為與之相似才被稱為朋友。
steps.ob_en: A consequence Aristotle accepts is that bad people cannot be true friends, and that if a friend becomes incurably bad the friendship should end. Many readers find the first too strict and the second too cold.
steps.ob_zh: 亞里斯多德接受的一個後果是：壞人不可能成為真朋友；而如果一位朋友變得無可救藥地壞，友誼就應該結束。許多讀者覺得前者太嚴，後者太冷。

source.work: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics VIII.3; Montaigne, Essays I.27, “Of Friendship”
source.work_zh: 亞里斯多德《尼各馬可倫理學》卷八第三章；蒙田《隨筆集》卷一〈論友誼〉
source.tr: tr. W. D. Ross; tr. Charles Cotton (both public domain)
source.lead_en: The philosopher’s definition and the essayist’s refusal to give one, nineteen centuries apart.
source.lead_zh: 哲學家的定義，與隨筆作家對下定義的拒絕；兩者相隔十九個世紀。

passages.en: Perfect friendship is the friendship of men who are good, and alike in virtue; for these wish well alike to each other qua good, and they are good themselves. Now those who wish well to their friends for their sake are most truly friends; for they do this by reason of own nature and not incidentally; therefore their friendship lasts as long as they are good—and goodness is an enduring thing.
passages.zh: 完美的友誼，是善良而在德行上相似的人之間的友誼；因為這些人是就對方之為善而同樣地願對方好，而他們自己也是善的。那些為了朋友本身的緣故而願朋友好的人，才是最真實的朋友；因為他們這樣做是出於自己的本性，而不是出於偶然。所以，只要他們是善的，他們的友誼就持續下去；而善是一樣經久的東西。
passages.note_en: “Qua good” means “in so far as they are good.” The phrase “for their sake” is the heart of the passage. Aristotle is contrasting it with wishing a friend well for one’s own sake, as a man wishes his wine to keep so that he may drink it. The last clause gives the reason such friendships last, and it shows what the argument depends on: that character is stable. A modern reader may doubt this. People change, and the friendships that survive are often those in which each has gone on loving the other through the change.
passages.note_zh: qua good 的意思是「就他們是善的這一點而言」。「為了朋友本身的緣故」是這段話的核心。亞里斯多德是把它跟「為了自己的緣故而願朋友好」作對比；後者就像一個人希望自己的酒不要壞，好讓自己可以喝它。最後一個子句給出了這種友誼之所以持久的理由，也顯示了這個論證依賴的是什麼：品格是穩定的。現代的讀者也許會懷疑這一點。人會變；而熬下來的友誼，往往是雙方在變化之中仍然繼續愛著對方的那些。

passages.en: …in the friendship I speak of, they mix and work themselves into one piece, with so universal a mixture, that there is no more sign of the seam by which they were first conjoined. If a man should importune me to give a reason why I loved him, I find it could no otherwise be expressed, than by making answer: because it was he, because it was I.
passages.zh: ……在我所說的那種友誼裡，它們混合、交融成一體，融合得那麼徹底，以致於當初把它們縫合起來的那道接縫，再也看不出痕跡。如果有人逼我說出我為什麼愛他，我覺得除了這樣回答之外，沒有別的說法：因為是他，因為是我。
passages.note_en: The most famous sentence Montaigne wrote was an afterthought. In the first edition of 1580 the passage ended by saying that the reason could not be expressed. He wrote “because it was he” in the margin of his own copy some years later, and “because it was I” later still, in different ink. The two halves matter equally. He is saying that the friendship is explained by nothing general on either side, neither by the friend’s merits nor by his own needs. “They” at the start refers to the two souls. The image of the seam comes from tailoring: two pieces of cloth so well joined that the join has vanished.
passages.note_zh: 蒙田寫過的最著名的一句話，是事後補上的。在 1580 年的初版裡，這段話的結尾說的是：理由無法表達。幾年之後，他在自己那一本的頁邊寫下了「因為是他」；又過了一些時候，用不同的墨水寫下了「因為是我」。這兩半同樣重要。他是在說：這段友誼，不由任何一方的任何「一般性的東西」來解釋；既不是由朋友的優點，也不是由他自己的需要。開頭的「它們」指的是那兩個靈魂。接縫的意象來自裁縫：兩塊布接合得太好，連接合處都消失了。

items.o_en: Friendship is unfair. Morality tells us to treat everyone equally, and a friend is someone we favor.
items.o_zh: 友誼是不公平的。道德要我們平等對待每一個人；而朋友，是我們偏袒的人。
items.r_en: The tension is real, and Mozi and the utilitarians have pressed it. Two replies are available. One is that a world without special attachments would contain far less care in total, since care for everyone in general is thin, so that even an impartial judge would approve of friendship. The other is that this defense gets the matter backward. A man who visits his friend in the hospital because friendship maximizes welfare has, as one philosopher put it, one thought too many. On this second view friendship is among the things that make a human life worth having, and a morality with no room for it has left something out.
items.r_zh: 這個張力是真實的；墨子與效益主義者都曾緊追不放。有兩種回應可用。一種是：一個沒有特殊情誼的世界，總體上的關懷會少得多，因為對「一般的每一個人」的關懷是稀薄的；所以，即使是一位不偏私的裁判，也會贊成友誼。另一種是：這個辯護把事情弄顛倒了。一個人到醫院探望朋友，是因為「友誼能使福祉極大化」；用一位哲學家的話說，他「多想了一層」。照第二種看法，友誼屬於使人生值得擁有的那些東西；一套容不下它的道德，是漏掉了什麼。

items.o_en: Aristotle says we should not befriend those worse than ourselves, and Confucius says the same. If everyone followed that advice, the better person in each pair would refuse, and no one would have a friend.
items.o_zh: 亞里斯多德說，我們不該跟不如自己的人交朋友；孔子也這麼說。如果每個人都聽從這個建議，每一對當中比較好的那一個就會拒絕，而誰也不會有朋友了。
items.r_en: The puzzle about the Analects line “have no friend who is not your equal” is old, and commentators have long read it otherwise: do not take as your model of friendship someone who is unlike you in aims, or more simply, look for what in each friend is better than you. Confucius also says that among any three people walking he will find a teacher. Friends are seldom better or worse across the board. One is braver and the other more patient, and each can be the other’s superior in something.
items.r_zh: 《論語》那句「無友不如己者」的難題由來已久；而歷來的註家有別的讀法：不要拿志向與你不同的人作為交友的榜樣；或者更簡單地說，去找每一位朋友身上比你好的地方。孔子也說過：「三人行，必有我師焉。」朋友很少是全面地比你好或比你差。一個比較勇敢，另一個比較有耐心；每一方都可以在某件事上勝過對方。

items.o_en: “Another self” is the wrong ideal. If my friend is another me, I have learned nothing and loved no one but myself.
items.o_zh: 「另一個自己」是錯誤的理想。如果我的朋友是另一個我，那我什麼也沒學到，而且除了自己之外誰也沒愛。
items.r_en: The objection takes the phrase too literally. Aristotle means that I stand to my friend as I stand to myself: I want his good as directly as I want my own, and his joys and griefs are mine. He does not mean that the friend resembles me in every respect, and elsewhere he says that we know ourselves best by looking at a friend, as we see our own face only in a mirror. That needs someone who is other. The Chinese stories make the same point by contrast. Zhong Ziqi could not play. What he gave Bo Ya was an ear.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁把那個說法看得太字面了。亞里斯多德的意思是：我對朋友的關係，就像我對自己的關係；我直接地想要他好，就像想要自己好一樣；他的喜與悲就是我的。他的意思並不是朋友在每一方面都像我。他在別處還說過：我們最能認識自己的方式，是看著一位朋友；就像我們只有在鏡子裡才看得見自己的臉。那需要一個「他者」。中國的故事用對比說出了同一點。鍾子期不會彈琴。他給伯牙的，是一隻耳朵。

said.claim: “A friend is one soul dwelling in two bodies.” (Aristotle)
said.claim_zh: 「朋友是住在兩個身體裡的一個靈魂。」（亞里斯多德）
said.en: The saying is not in any surviving work of Aristotle. It comes from Diogenes Laertius, who wrote about 230 CE and records it among anecdotes of things Aristotle was said to have answered when asked. Montaigne, in the essay quoted above, uses it and calls it “that very proper definition of Aristotle.” What Aristotle wrote in the Ethics is cooler: a friend is “another self.” The two phrases point in different directions. One soul in two bodies is Montaigne’s fusion, with the seam gone. Another self keeps two people, each of whom regards the other as he regards himself.
said.zh: 這句話不見於亞里斯多德現存的任何著作。它出自第歐根尼・拉爾修；他大約在西元 230 年寫作，把它記在一批「據說亞里斯多德被問到時這樣回答」的軼事當中。蒙田在上面引的那篇隨筆裡用了它，並且稱之為「亞里斯多德那個非常恰當的定義」。亞里斯多德在《倫理學》裡寫的比較冷靜：朋友是「另一個自己」。這兩個說法指向不同的方向。「兩個身體裡的一個靈魂」是蒙田式的融合，接縫消失了。「另一個自己」保留了兩個人，各自像看待自己那樣看待對方。

terms.d_en: In Aristotle, any relation of mutual and recognized goodwill, wider than the English word.
terms.d_zh: 在亞里斯多德，指任何彼此而且相互知曉的善意關係；範圍比英文的 friendship 廣。

terms.d_en: Usefulness. The basis of the first kind of friendship.
terms.d_zh: 有用。第一種友誼的基礎。

terms.d_en: Wishing another person well. It becomes friendship when it is mutual and known.
terms.d_zh: 願另一個人好。當它是相互的、而且彼此知道的時候，就成為友誼。

terms.o: Gk. allos autos; L. alter ego
terms.d_en: Aristotle’s phrase for a friend, toward whom one stands as toward oneself.
terms.d_zh: 亞里斯多德對朋友的稱呼：一個人對他的關係，就像對自己的關係。

terms.d_en: A friend who understands one fully, from the story of Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi.
terms.d_zh: 完全了解自己的朋友；出自伯牙與鍾子期的故事。

terms.d_en: Giving special weight to particular people, as against impartiality.
terms.d_zh: 給特定的人特別的分量；相對於不偏私。

terms.d_en: Mutual exchange. A friendship of use rests on it, and a friendship of character does not keep accounts.
terms.d_zh: 相互的交換。有用的友誼建立在它上面；品格的友誼則不記帳。

terms.d_en: The proposed limit, about 150, to the number of stable relationships a person can maintain.
terms.d_zh: 一個人能夠維持的穩定關係數目的上限；據提議大約是 150。

vocab.eg: A sentence that states its importance flatly.
vocab.eg_zh: 一句直截了當說出它有多重要的話。

vocab.eg: The poor need friends as a refuge.
vocab.eg_zh: 窮人需要朋友作為避難所。

vocab.eg: In virtue of some good which they get from each other.
vocab.eg_zh: 由於從對方得到的某種好處。

vocab.eg: When the usefulness ends, the friendship dissolves.
vocab.eg_zh: 用處沒了，友誼就消散了。

vocab.eg: If a man should importune me to give a reason.
vocab.eg_zh: 如果有人逼我說出理由。

vocab.eg: No more sign of the seam by which they were joined.
vocab.eg_zh: 那道接縫再也看不出痕跡。

vocab.eg: We would be dismayed to learn that they were cruel.
vocab.eg_zh: 如果得知他們是殘忍的人，我們會大為沮喪。

vocab.eg: Friends who are glib are a loss.
vocab.eg_zh: 友便佞，損矣。

vocab.eg: The numbers have held up fairly well.
vocab.eg_zh: 這些數字相當站得住。

vocab.eg: Has this friend stood by you when it cost something?
vocab.eg_zh: 這位朋友曾經在要付出代價的時候站在你這一邊嗎？

quiz.q: What are Aristotle’s three kinds of friendship based on?
options: Usefulness, pleasure, and goodness of character.
Family, school, and work.
Youth, middle age, and old age.
Love, fear, and habit.

quiz.q: Why do the first two kinds tend to end?
options: The other person is loved for something he provides, and they last only as long as it is provided.
They are immoral.
Aristotle forbade them.
They involve too many people.

quiz.q: What does Montaigne’s “because it was he, because it was I” deny?
options: That the friendship can be explained by general qualities on either side.
That he loved his friend.
That friendship exists.
That La Boétie was a good man.

quiz.q: In the Analects, which friends are a gain?
options: The upright, the trustworthy, and those who have heard much.
The smooth, the pleasing, and the glib.
The rich, the powerful, and the famous.
Those who always agree.

quiz.q: What does the story of Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi single out as the mark of a true friend?
options: Being understood.
Being useful.
Sharing wealth.
Living nearby.

write.en: Describe a friendship of yours that ended. Which of Aristotle’s three kinds was it, and does that explain the ending?
write.zh: 描述一段你已經結束的友誼。它是亞里斯多德三種當中的哪一種？那能解釋它的結束嗎？

write.en: Aristotle or Montaigne: do we love a friend for his qualities, or for no reason that can be given? Answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 亞里斯多德還是蒙田：我們愛一位朋友，是為了他的特質，還是沒有任何說得出的理由？用大約 150 個英文字回答。

write.en: Explain the phrase 知音 to an English-speaking friend by telling the story in five sentences.
write.zh: 用五個句子講那個故事，向一位說英文的朋友解釋「知音」這個詞。

paras.en: The Buddha’s attendant Ānanda once remarked that good friendship is half of the spiritual life. “Not so, Ānanda! Not so, Ānanda! Good friends, companions, and associates are the whole of the spiritual life.” A person with good friends can be expected to develop the path, and the Buddha describes himself as the good friend by relying on whom beings are freed. The Pali term is kalyāṇamitta, the beautiful or admirable friend. It is close to Aristotle’s friendship of character, with the goal moved: the friend is the one who helps you toward liberation, where Aristotle’s helps you toward a flourishing life in the city.
paras.zh: 佛陀的侍者阿難有一次說：善友是梵行的一半。「不是這樣，阿難！不是這樣，阿難！善友、善伴、善交遊，是梵行的全部。」有善友的人，可以期待他修習八正道；而佛陀把自己描述為那位善友：眾生依靠他而得解脫。巴利文的用語是 kalyāṇamitta，美善的、可敬的朋友。這很接近亞里斯多德的品格之友，只是目標移動了：這位朋友，是幫助你走向解脫的人；亞里斯多德的那一位，是幫助你在城邦裡活出興旺人生的人。

paras.en: For lay life the Buddha gave advice that reads like a longer version of the Analects passage. He tells the young householder Sigālaka to recognize four enemies disguised as friends, among them the one who only takes and the flatterer, and four good-hearted friends: “the helper, the friend in good times and bad, the counselor, and the one who’s sympathetic.” The counselor is described in words Confucius could have used: “They keep you from doing bad. They support you in doing good. They teach you what you do not know.” The tradition adds one thing the philosophers lack. Loving-kindness, mettā, comes from the same root as mitta, friend. It is friendliness trained until it no longer depends on who the other person is, and it is to be extended in the end to strangers and enemies. Aristotle says that we can be friends in the full sense with very few. The Buddha agrees about friendship and holds that the goodwill at its center can be made boundless.
paras.zh: 對在家的生活，佛陀給過一段建議，讀起來像是《論語》那一章的加長版。他告訴年輕的居士善生：要認出四種偽裝成朋友的敵人，其中有只知道拿的人與諂媚的人；也要認出四種善心的朋友：「能幫助的、苦樂與共的、能勸導的、有同情心的。」對「能勸導的」那一種的描述，用的是孔子也可能用的話：「他們使你遠離惡，支持你行善，教你所不知道的事。」這個傳統還多了一樣哲學家們所沒有的東西。慈（mettā）與朋友（mitta）出自同一個字根。它是被訓練到「不再取決於對方是誰」的友善，而最終要推及陌生人與敵人。亞里斯多德說，完整意義上的朋友，我們只能有非常少的幾位。佛陀對「友誼」同意這一點，卻主張友誼核心的那份善意，可以被修到沒有邊界。

further.t: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Books VIII and IX, translated by W. D. Ross
further.n_en: Chapters 1 to 4 of Book VIII give the whole theory.
further.n_zh: 卷八第一到四章，就是整套理論。

further.t: Michel de Montaigne, “Of Friendship,” translated by Charles Cotton
further.n_en: Book I, chapter 27 in this edition.
further.n_zh: 在這個版本裡是卷一第二十七章。

further.t: Analects 16.4 and 12.24
further.n_en: The three that help and the three that harm.
further.n_zh: 益者三友，損者三友。

further.t: 《列子・湯問》；《呂氏春秋・本味》；《史記・管晏列傳》
further.n_en: Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi; Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya.
further.n_zh: 伯牙與鍾子期；管仲與鮑叔牙。

further.t: Dīgha Nikāya 31, Advice to Sigālaka; Saṃyutta Nikāya 45.2
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Friendship”

lessons.title: What Do We Owe Strangers?
lessons.blurb_en: A child drowning in a shallow pond, a man who would lose a hundred million strangers more calmly than his little finger, and the Chinese philosopher who taught that we should regard other people’s families as our own.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一個在淺池塘裡溺水的孩子；一個失去一億個陌生人、會比失去自己的小指頭更平靜的人；以及那位教導「視人之家若視其家」的中國哲學家。
lessons.big_en: The last lesson was about the few people we love. This one is about everyone else. Nearly all of us believe that we must help a stranger in front of us at small cost, and nearly all of us live as though the same stranger, farther off, had no claim on us at all.
lessons.big_zh: 上一課談的是我們所愛的少數人。這一課談的是其餘的每一個人。我們幾乎都相信：眼前的陌生人，只要代價很小，就必須幫；而我們也幾乎都過著這樣的生活：彷彿同一個陌生人，只要離得遠一點，就對我們毫無要求。

paras.en: In 1971 a young Australian philosopher at Oxford, Peter Singer, wrote an article in response to a famine in East Bengal. Its argument begins with a story. On your way to work you pass a shallow pond and see that a small child has fallen in and is about to drown. You can wade in and pull the child out. You will ruin your shoes and be late. Should you do it? Everyone answers yes, and thinks worse of anyone who would hesitate. Singer then asks what principle lies behind the answer. It seems to be this: if we can prevent something very bad from happening at a cost to ourselves that is small by comparison, we ought to do it.
paras.zh: 1971 年，一位在牛津的年輕澳洲哲學家辛格，為了回應東孟加拉的一場饑荒，寫了一篇文章。它的論證從一個故事開始。你在上班的路上經過一個淺池塘，看見一個小孩掉了進去，眼看就要淹死。你可以涉水過去，把孩子拉上來。你會毀掉一雙鞋，而且會遲到。你應該這樣做嗎？每個人都回答「應該」，並且瞧不起任何一個會猶豫的人。接著辛格問：這個回答背後是什麼原則？看來是這一條：如果我們能夠阻止某件非常壞的事發生，而自己付出的代價相較之下很小，我們就應該去做。

paras.en: Now the principle says nothing about distance. A child dying of a preventable disease in another country is as real as the child in the pond, and for the price of the shoes an aid organization can do something to prevent the death. The principle also says nothing about whether other people could help and do not. If others were standing around the pond doing nothing, you would still have to go in. So the conclusion appears to follow that spending money on things we do not need, while children die whom the money could save, is the moral equivalent of walking past the pond. Giving to relieve great suffering, which we have always called charity and praised as generous, is on this argument a plain duty, and failing to give is wrong.
paras.zh: 而這條原則，對「距離」隻字未提。另一個國家裡一個死於可預防疾病的孩子，跟池塘裡的那個孩子一樣真實；而用那雙鞋的價錢，一個援助組織就能做點什麼來阻止那個死亡。這條原則也沒有提到「別人是否也幫得上忙卻沒有幫」。就算池塘邊站著別人、什麼也不做，你仍然必須下水。所以，結論看來是推得出來的：當有孩子正在死去、而錢救得了他們的時候，把錢花在我們並不需要的東西上，在道德上就等同於從池塘邊走過去。為了解除巨大的苦難而捐助，我們向來稱之為「慈善」，並且讚美它是慷慨；照這個論證，它是一項明明白白的義務，而不捐是錯的。

paras.en: The Chinese philosopher Mozi had reached the same position by another road in the fifth century BCE. He asks where the disorders of the world come from, and answers that they come from people not loving one another. A son loves himself and not his father, and so injures his father for his own gain. The lord of a state loves his state and not his neighbor’s, and so attacks it. The remedy is to replace partiality with impartial care: “regard other people’s states as one regards one’s own, other people’s families as one regards one’s own, and other people’s persons as one regards one’s own.” His critics said that the idea was fine and could never be put into practice. He replied with a test. Suppose you must go to war or on a long embassy, he says, and do not know whether you will return. You have to leave your parents, wife, and children in someone’s care. Would you entrust them to a man who holds that he should care for his friend’s family as his own, or to a man who holds that this is impossible? Even those who argue against impartial care, he observes, would choose the impartial man.
paras.zh: 中國哲學家墨子，在西元前五世紀就從另一條路走到了同樣的立場。他問：天下的禍亂是從哪裡來的？他的回答是：「起不相愛。」兒子愛自己而不愛父親，所以損害父親來利自己。一國之君愛自己的國而不愛鄰國，所以去攻打它。對治的辦法是用「兼」取代「別」：「視人之國若視其國，視人之家若視其家，視人之身若視其身。」批評他的人說：這個想法很好，卻永遠無法實行。他用一個檢驗來回答。他說，假設你必須上戰場，或者出使遠方，不知道自己能不能回來。你得把父母、妻子、兒女託付給某個人照顧。你會把他們託付給一個主張「應該照顧朋友的家人如同自己的家人」的人呢，還是託付給一個主張「這不可能」的人？他觀察到：就連那些反對兼愛的人，也會選擇那位主張兼愛的人。

paras.en: Against Singer and Mozi stands a fact about human beings that Adam Smith described in 1759. Suppose that the great empire of China, with all its inhabitants, were swallowed by an earthquake, and consider how a humane man in Europe would take the news. He would express his sorrow and reflect on the precariousness of life. Then he would go about his business. “If he was to lose his little finger to-morrow, he would not sleep to-night; but provided he never saw them, he will snore with the most profound security over the ruin of a hundred millions of his brethren.” Smith did not approve of this. He asks at once whether the same man would sacrifice those hundred million to save his finger, and answers that human nature recoils from the thought. Something in us, which he calls conscience or the impartial spectator, knows that we are one of the multitude and no more important than any other. But the feeling does not keep pace with the knowledge.
paras.zh: 擋在辛格與墨子面前的，是亞當・斯密在 1759 年描述過的一個關於人的事實。假設偉大的中華帝國連同它所有的居民，被一場地震吞沒了；再想想歐洲一位有人情味的人，會怎麼接受這個消息。他會表達哀傷，並且感慨生命的無常。然後他就去忙自己的事了。「假如他明天就要失去自己的小指頭，他今晚就睡不著；但只要他從來沒有見過他們，即使他的一億同胞毀滅了，他也會在最深沉的安穩之中打鼾。」斯密並不贊成這樣。他緊接著問：同一個人，會不會為了保住自己的指頭而犧牲那一億人？他回答：人的本性一想到這個就退縮了。我們裡面有某個東西（他稱之為良心，或「不偏私的旁觀者」）知道我們只是眾人當中的一個，並不比任何別人更重要。然而，感受跟不上這份知道。

paras.en: Psychologists have since measured the gap. People give more to save one named child with a photograph than to save eight children described in numbers, and their willingness to help falls as the number of victims rises. The effect has been called psychic numbing. A remark often credited to Stalin puts it brutally: one death is a tragedy, and a million deaths are a statistic.
paras.zh: 心理學家後來測量了這道落差。人們捐給「一個有名字、有照片的孩子」的錢，比捐給「用數字描述的八個孩子」的更多；而受害者的人數越多，人們幫助的意願就越低。這個效應被稱為「精神麻木」。一句常被歸給史達林的話，把它說得很殘酷：一個人的死是悲劇，一百萬人的死是統計數字。

paras.en: Mencius attacked Mozi in the strongest terms he ever used. “Mozi’s impartial care amounts to having no father. To have no father and no ruler is to be a beast.” Behind the abuse is an argument. Moral concern, for the Confucians, has a source, and the source is the family. A child learns to love by loving the people who feed and hold him, and the feeling is then extended outward: “Treat your own elders as elders should be treated, and extend it to the elders of others.” The order is “affection for kin, humaneness toward the people, and care for creatures.” A person who claimed to feel the same for his neighbor’s father as for his own would not have reached a higher love. He would have cut the root from which any love grows. When a Mohist named Yi Zhi buried his own parents with great expense, against his school’s teaching, Mencius took it as proof that even Mohists cannot live by the doctrine.
paras.zh: 孟子攻擊墨子，用了他平生最重的話。「墨氏兼愛，是無父也。無父無君，是禽獸也。」在這句謾罵背後，有一個論證。對儒家來說，道德關懷有一個源頭，而那個源頭是家。一個孩子，是靠著愛那些餵他、抱他的人而學會愛的；然後這份感情被往外推：「老吾老，以及人之老。」次序是「親親而仁民，仁民而愛物」。一個宣稱自己對鄰居的父親與對自己的父親感情相同的人，並沒有達到一種更高的愛。他是把一切愛賴以生長的那條根砍斷了。有一位名叫夷之的墨者，違反自己學派的教導，厚葬了自己的父母；孟子把這件事當作證明：就連墨者自己，也沒辦法照著這個教義過日子。

paras.en: The Confucian position is not that strangers have no claim. The king who would not extend his kindness to the people was told that he was leading beasts to devour men. It is that obligations come in degrees and that the degrees are right. Western philosophers have defended the same view under the name of special obligations. A parent who let his own child drown in order to save two strangers’ children would have done something wrong, however the numbers come out.
paras.zh: 儒家的立場並不是陌生人毫無要求。那位不肯把恩惠推及百姓的國君，被告知他是在率獸食人。儒家的立場是：義務有等差，而這些等差是對的。西方的哲學家用「特殊義務」這個名稱，為同樣的看法辯護過。一位為了救兩個陌生人的孩子、而任由自己的孩子淹死的父母，不管數字怎麼算，都做錯了某件事。

paras.en: Suppose one accepts that distant strangers have some claim. The hard question is where it stops. Singer’s principle has no natural stopping point. After I have given the price of the shoes there is another child, and after that another, and the argument applies each time with the same force. Followed strictly, it requires giving until one has reduced oneself to near the level of those one is helping. Singer accepts this as the truth about what morality asks, and suggests a public standard of giving a tenth or so as something people might actually do. Critics call the view too demanding. A morality that leaves no room for a person’s own projects, friendships, and family, they say, has misunderstood what a human life is.
paras.zh: 假設我們接受遠方的陌生人有某些要求。困難的問題是：它到哪裡為止？辛格的原則沒有天然的停止點。我捐出了那雙鞋的價錢之後，還有另一個孩子；那之後，還有另一個；而這個論證每一次都以同樣的力道適用。嚴格地照著它走，它要求人一直捐，直到把自己降到接近受助者的水準。辛格接受這就是「道德要求什麼」的真相；他並且提議，以捐出十分之一左右作為一個公開的標準，那是人們實際上可能做到的。批評者說這個看法太苛求了。他們說：一套不給個人自己的計畫、友誼與家庭留下任何空間的道德，是誤解了人的生活是什麼。

paras.en: Kant offers a middle position. Helping others in need, he holds, is a duty, since a person who willed a world in which no one helped anyone would be willing away the help he will himself one day need. But it is an imperfect duty. It commands us to make the well-being of others one of our ends and leaves to our judgment how much to do, for whom, and when. One may not do nothing. One is not required to do everything. In the last twenty years a movement called effective altruism has added a further question to Singer’s: given that one is going to give, where does a dollar do the most good? Its researchers have estimated that the best charities can save a life for a few thousand dollars. The movement has been criticized for its confidence in such calculations, and it has made the pond harder to walk past.
paras.zh: 康德提供了一個中間的立場。他主張，幫助有需要的人是一項義務；因為一個人如果意願一個「誰也不幫誰」的世界，就是把自己有朝一日也會需要的幫助一併意願掉了。但它是一項「不完全義務」。它命令我們把別人的福祉當作自己的目的之一，而把「做多少、為誰做、什麼時候做」留給我們的判斷。人不可以什麼都不做。人也沒有被要求什麼都做。過去二十年，一個名為「有效利他主義」的運動，在辛格的問題之外又加了一個問題：既然要捐，一塊錢花在哪裡能成就最多的善？它的研究者估計，最好的慈善機構用幾千美元就能救一條命。這個運動因為對這類計算太有把握而受到批評；而它也使那個池塘變得更難視而不見地走過去。

paras.en: The debate can be read as a warning against two errors. One is to care only for one’s own. Mozi saw that this is the root of war and of the indifference that lets the distant starve, and Adam Smith’s sleeper is its portrait. The other is to care for humanity and for no one in particular, which Mencius thought monstrous and which often turns out, in practice, to be care for nobody. A parable from the Gospel of Luke holds the two together. A lawyer asks Jesus who counts as the neighbor he is commanded to love. Jesus tells of a traveler beaten and left by the road, passed by a priest and a Levite and helped by a Samaritan, a foreigner of a despised people. He then turns the question round. The lawyer asked whom he must treat as a neighbor. Jesus asks which of the three proved to be one. The stranger in the story is a particular man in a particular ditch, and what was owed to him was owed by whoever came near.
paras.zh: 這場辯論可以讀成對兩種錯誤的警告。一種是只關心自己人。墨子看出，這是戰爭的根源，也是任由遠方的人餓死的那種冷漠的根源；亞當・斯密筆下那位酣睡的人，就是它的畫像。另一種是關心「人類」，卻不特別關心任何一個人；孟子認為那是可怕的，而它在實踐上往往變成誰也不關心。《路加福音》裡的一個比喻，把這兩者握在一起。一位律法師問耶穌：他被命令要去愛的「鄰舍」，誰才算？耶穌講了一個旅人的故事：他被打傷，丟在路邊；一位祭司與一位利未人從旁邊走過去；救他的是一個撒瑪利亞人，一個受人鄙視的外族人。然後他把問題轉了過來。律法師問的是：我必須把誰當作鄰舍？耶穌問的是：這三個人當中，哪一個成了鄰舍？故事裡的那個陌生人，是某一條溝裡的某一個人；而他被虧欠的東西，是任何一個走近的人都欠他的。

lab.title_en: Try it: six ponds
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：六個池塘
lab.lead_en: The case is changed one step at a time, and each step adds a single feature of the real world. At each step say whether you are obliged to help. You will be shown where you stopped and which feature stopped you.
lab.lead_zh: 這個案例一步一步地改變，每一步只加上真實世界的一項特徵。在每一步，說出你是否有義務去幫。最後會讓你看到你停在哪裡，以及是哪一項特徵讓你停下來的。

t.en: A child is drowning in a shallow pond in front of you. Saving her will ruin your shoes.
t.zh: 一個孩子在你面前的淺池塘裡溺水。救她會毀掉你的鞋。

t.en: The child is in another country. For the price of the shoes, sent today, she will certainly be saved.
t.zh: 那個孩子在另一個國家。今天寄出那雙鞋的價錢，她就確定會得救。

t.en: A million other people could each send the same sum. Almost none of them will.
t.zh: 另外還有一百萬人，每個人都拿得出同樣的金額。他們幾乎沒有一個會寄。

t.en: She is one of ten thousand children in the same danger. Your money will save one and leave the rest as they are.
t.zh: 她是處於同樣危險的一萬個孩子當中的一個。你的錢會救一個，其餘的維持原狀。

t.en: You cannot see the result. The best evidence is that money given this way saves a life about four times in five.
t.zh: 你看不到結果。最好的證據顯示，這樣捐出去的錢，大約五次有四次救得了一條命。

t.en: You gave last month. The same request arrives this month, and it will arrive every month for the rest of your life.
t.zh: 你上個月捐了。同樣的請求這個月又來了，而且在你的餘生裡，每個月都會來。

base.en: You stopped at the first pond. Very few people do. If the answer was sincere, you hold that no one is ever required to help a stranger, and the rest of the ladder does not concern you. It is worth asking whether you would say the same if the child were yours and the passerby were someone else.
base.zh: 你在第一個池塘就停了。很少有人這樣。如果這個回答是認真的，你主張的是：任何人在任何時候都沒有義務幫助陌生人；而這道階梯的其餘部分就與你無關了。值得問一問：如果那個孩子是你的，而路過的是別人，你還會這樣說嗎？

distance.en: Distance stopped you. This is the most common place to stop and the hardest to defend, since nothing about the child changed when she moved. Singer says that nearness is morally irrelevant. Mencius would take your side in a qualified way. He holds that care properly begins with what is near and is extended outward, and he would add that the king who saw the ox and spared it was told to extend the feeling, not to keep it where it was.
distance.zh: 讓你停下來的是距離。這是最常見的停止點，也是最難辯護的；因為那個孩子搬遠了，她身上卻什麼也沒變。辛格說，遠近在道德上不相干。孟子會有條件地站在你這一邊。他主張關懷本來就是從近處開始、再往外推的；而他會補充：那位看見牛、饒了牛的國君，被告知的是要把這份感受推出去，而不是讓它留在原地。

others.en: The presence of others who could help stopped you. Psychologists call this the diffusion of responsibility, and it is the reason a crowd will watch what a single passerby would prevent. Singer’s reply is the pond with bystanders: their failure does not lift the child out. A fairer version of your thought is that you owe your share and no more. That gives a duty and a limit, and many philosophers think it is the right answer.
others.zh: 讓你停下來的是「還有別人幫得上忙」。心理學家稱之為責任分散；這就是為什麼一群人會眼睜睜看著一件單獨一位路人會出手阻止的事。辛格的回答是「有旁觀者的池塘」：他們不作為，並不會把那個孩子撈上來。你的想法有一個比較公道的版本：你欠的是你的那一份，不多不少。這既給了一項義務，也給了一個限度；許多哲學家認為這才是對的答案。

numbers.en: The size of the problem stopped you. The thought is that a drop in the ocean is not worth giving. Notice that nothing has changed for the one child your money would save. She is as fully rescued as the child in the pond. What has changed is your feeling of having dealt with the matter. Mozi’s whole philosophy is aimed at this reaction, and the measured tendency to help less as the numbers grow is one of the best-established findings about moral psychology.
numbers.zh: 讓你停下來的是問題的規模。這個想法是：滄海一粟，不值得捐。請留意：對你的錢會救的那一個孩子來說，什麼都沒變。她得救的程度，跟池塘裡的那個孩子完全一樣。改變的，是你那份「把事情處理掉了」的感覺。墨子的整套哲學，就是瞄準這種反應的；而「人數越多、幫得越少」這個量得出來的傾向，是道德心理學裡最確立的發現之一。

doubt.en: Uncertainty stopped you. This is the most respectable place to stop, and the effective altruists agree that it matters: much aid has failed, and a gift that does nothing is no rescue. But four chances in five is far better than most of the bets we make with our money. If the pond were so murky that you could not be sure of reaching the child, you would still wade in. The real effect of doubt is to create a second duty, to find out where help works.
doubt.zh: 讓你停下來的是不確定。這是最體面的停止點；有效利他主義者也同意它要緊：許多援助失敗了，而一筆毫無作用的捐款算不上救援。但五分之四的機會，遠比我們拿錢去下的大多數賭注要好。假如池塘渾濁到你沒有把握搆得到那個孩子，你還是會下水。疑慮真正的作用，是產生了第二項義務：去弄清楚幫助在哪裡有效。

again.en: Repetition stopped you. You accept every step of Singer’s argument and resist its conclusion, that the demand never ends. This is Kant’s position. Beneficence is a duty that leaves the amount to your judgment, because a person is more than an instrument for relieving need. Singer would ask why the child who happens to come last should lose her claim. The honest reply may be that she does not lose it, and that a human being can carry only so much.
again.zh: 讓你停下來的是「一再重複」。你接受辛格論證的每一步，卻抗拒它的結論：這項要求永無止境。這是康德的立場。行善是一項把「多少」留給你自己判斷的義務，因為人不只是一件用來解除匱乏的工具。辛格會問：碰巧排在最後的那個孩子，憑什麼就失去了她的要求？誠實的回答也許是：她並沒有失去；只是一個人能扛的就這麼多。

all.en: You said yes six times. You have followed Singer and Mozi to the end, and by your own account you are obliged to give, month after month, as long as there are children to save and you have more than you need. Few people who say this live by it, and Mencius would predict that you cannot. The question to put to yourself is which you will now revise, your answers or your spending.
all.zh: 你六次都說「有」。你跟著辛格與墨子走到了底；照你自己的說法，只要還有孩子可救、而你擁有的超過你需要的，你就有義務一個月又一個月地捐下去。這樣說的人，很少照著過日子；而孟子會預言你做不到。該問自己的問題是：現在你要修改的是哪一樣，是你的答案，還是你的開銷？

t.en: None of the six changes makes a moral difference. Stop only when giving more would cost you something as important as a life.
t.zh: 這六項改變，沒有一項造成道德上的差別。只有當再多捐會讓你失去跟一條命同樣重要的東西時，才停下來。

t.en: Regard other people’s children as your own. Would you stop at any of these steps if she were yours?
t.zh: 視人之子若視其子。如果她是你的孩子，你會在這些步驟當中的任何一步停下來嗎？

t.en: Begin with your own and extend it. The duty to the far child is real and is weaker than the duty to your parents, and that is as it should be.
t.zh: 從自己人開始，再推出去。對遠方那個孩子的義務是真實的，卻比對你父母的義務弱；而這本來就該如此。

t.en: You must make the needs of others your concern. How much you give, and to whom, is left to your judgment. Nothing at all is not permitted.
t.zh: 你必須把別人的需要當作自己關切的事。捐多少、捐給誰，留給你自己判斷。什麼都不做，是不被許可的。

argument.lead_en: Singer’s argument from “Famine, Affluence, and Morality.” Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 辛格在〈饑荒、富裕與道德〉裡的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Suffering and death from lack of food, shelter, and medical care are bad.
steps.zh: 因為缺乏食物、住所與醫療而受苦、死亡，是壞的。
steps.ob_en: Not seriously disputed.
steps.ob_zh: 沒有人認真爭論這一點。

steps.en: If it is in our power to prevent something bad from happening, without giving up anything of comparable moral importance, we ought to do it.
steps.zh: 如果我們有能力阻止某件壞事發生，而不必因此放棄任何道德上同等重要的東西，我們就應該去做。
steps.ob_en: The whole argument rests here. The pond makes the principle seem obvious, and critics say that the pond is a special case: one victim, one rescuer, an emergency that ends. Generalized to a permanent condition of the world, the principle would make every hour and every dollar a person has answerable to strangers. Singer also offers a weaker version, on which we need only give up what is morally insignificant, and even that would change how most of us live.
steps.ob_zh: 整個論證就壓在這裡。池塘使這條原則看起來顯而易見；而批評者說，池塘是一個特例：一位受害者、一位施救者、一場會結束的緊急狀況。把它推廣到世界的一種恆常狀態，這條原則就會使一個人擁有的每一個小時、每一塊錢，都得向陌生人交代。辛格也提供了一個較弱的版本：我們只需要放棄道德上無足輕重的東西；而即使是那個版本，也會改變我們大多數人的生活方式。

steps.en: By giving to effective aid we can prevent such suffering without giving up anything of comparable importance.
steps.zh: 藉著捐給有效的援助，我們可以阻止這樣的苦難，而不必放棄任何同等重要的東西。
steps.ob_en: A claim of fact, and it has been challenged. Some economists argue that aid often fails or does harm. The reply is that this is a reason to give carefully, and the evidence for certain health programs is strong.
steps.ob_zh: 這是一個事實主張，而它受到過質疑。有些經濟學家論證，援助往往失敗，甚至有害。回應是：這是「謹慎地捐」的理由；而某些衛生計畫的證據是強的。

steps.en: Therefore we ought to give, and to go on giving, far more than is now thought normal or generous.
steps.zh: 所以，我們應該捐，並且繼續捐，遠遠超過現在被認為正常或慷慨的程度。
steps.ob_en: If the conclusion is true, most comfortable people are doing something seriously wrong every day. Some readers take that as a reason to doubt a premise. Singer takes it as a discovery.
steps.ob_zh: 如果這個結論是真的，大多數生活舒適的人每天都在做一件嚴重錯誤的事。有些讀者把這當作懷疑某個前提的理由。辛格把它當作一項發現。

source.work: Mozi, “Impartial Care,” Part II; Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759), III.3
source.work_zh: 《墨子・兼愛中》；亞當・斯密《道德情操論》第三卷第三章
source.tr: Mozi translated for this series from the Chinese text; Smith in the original English (public domain)
source.lead_en: The demand, and the fact about us that stands in its way.
source.lead_zh: 那項要求，以及擋在它前面的那個關於我們的事實。

passages.en: Master Mozi said: “Regard other people’s states as one regards one’s own state. Regard other people’s families as one regards one’s own family. Regard other people’s persons as one regards one’s own person. Then the lords of states will care for one another and will not go to war. The heads of families will care for one another and will not usurp. Person and person will care for one another and will not injure.”
passages.zh: 子墨子言：「視人之國若視其國，視人之家若視其家，視人之身若視其身。是故諸侯相愛，則不野戰；家主相愛，則不相篡；人與人相愛，則不相賊。」
passages.note_en: The word translated “care,” ài, is usually rendered “love,” and the usual English name for the doctrine is “universal love.” That is misleading. Mozi is not asking for a warm feeling toward all mankind. He is asking for a policy: in deciding what to do, give the interests of others the same weight as your own. The passage shows his method. He names a harm, traces it to partiality, and proposes the opposite. The argument is addressed to rulers, and its first aim is to stop wars. He was the first philosopher anywhere to make the benefit of all the test of right action.
passages.note_zh: 譯作 care 的那個字是「愛」；這個學說通常的英文名稱是 universal love。那是有誤導性的。墨子要的並不是對全人類的一種溫暖感情。他要的是一項方針：在決定怎麼做的時候，給別人的利益與自己的利益同樣的分量。這段文字顯示了他的方法。他點出一種禍害，把它追溯到「別」（偏私），然後提出相反的東西。這個論證是對統治者說的；它的第一個目標是止戰。在任何地方，他都是第一位把「利天下」當作行為對錯之檢驗的哲學家。

passages.ref: The Theory of Moral Sentiments III.3.4
passages.en: If he was to lose his little finger to-morrow, he would not sleep to-night; but provided he never saw them, he will snore with the most profound security over the ruin of a hundred millions of his brethren, and the destruction of that immense multitude seems plainly an object less interesting to him, than this paultry misfortune of his own.
passages.zh: 假如他明天就要失去自己的小指頭，他今晚就睡不著；但只要他從來沒有見過他們，即使他的一億同胞毀滅了，他也會在最深沉的安穩之中打鼾；而那無數人的毀滅，對他來說顯然還不如他自己這件微不足道的不幸來得要緊。
passages.note_en: Smith is known as the founder of economics, and he was first a moral philosopher. The passage is often quoted as cynicism, which reverses his meaning. He states the fact about our feelings in order to ask what corrects it. His answer is that we learn to see ourselves as an impartial onlooker would, and that from that standpoint each of us “is but one of the multitude in no respect better than any other in it.” The phrase “provided he never saw them” is the hinge. It is Mencius’s observation about the ox and the sheep. (“Interesting” has its old sense, affecting one’s interests. The spelling is Smith’s.)
passages.note_zh: 斯密以經濟學的奠基者聞名；而他首先是一位道德哲學家。這段話常被當成憤世嫉俗的話來引用，那是把他的意思弄反了。他陳述這個關於我們感受的事實，是為了問：是什麼糾正了它？他的回答是：我們學著像一位不偏私的旁觀者那樣看自己；而從那個立足點看，「我們不過是眾人當中的一個，在任何方面都不比其中任何別人更好」。「只要他從來沒有見過他們」這個條件句是樞紐所在。那就是孟子對牛與羊的觀察。（interesting 在這裡用的是舊義：與自己的利害相關。拼字是斯密的原樣。）

items.o_en: Charity begins at home. My duties are to my family and my community, and what I give beyond that is a gift.
items.o_zh: 行善從家裡開始。我的義務是對我的家人與我的社群；超出這個範圍所給的，是贈與。
items.r_en: The first half is Mencius’s view and has much to be said for it. The second half does not follow. Mencius did not say that care ends at home. He said that it begins there and must be extended, and he thought a ruler who kept his kindness within the palace had failed. The serious version of the objection is about priority. Family comes first when the claims conflict. Most of the time they do not, and the choice is between a stranger’s need and a luxury.
items.r_zh: 前半句是孟子的看法，而它很有道理。後半句卻推不出來。孟子並沒有說關懷到家為止。他說的是：它從那裡開始，並且必須推出去；而他認為，一位把恩惠關在宮裡的君主是失敗的。這個反駁認真的版本，談的是優先順序。當兩邊的要求衝突時，家人優先。而多數時候它們並不衝突；選擇是在一個陌生人的需要與一件奢侈品之間。

items.o_en: The causes of poverty are political. Giving money treats symptoms and can prop up the governments that cause the harm.
items.o_zh: 貧窮的原因是政治的。捐錢只是治標，而且可能撐住造成禍害的那些政府。
items.r_en: This objection grants the duty and disputes the means, and Mozi would agree with it. His own remedies were political: he tried to stop wars and to make rulers govern for the people’s benefit. If changing institutions does more good than sending money, then the argument tells us to work at changing institutions. It gives no support to doing neither.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁承認了那項義務，爭的是手段；而墨子會同意它。他自己的對治就是政治上的：他設法止戰，設法讓統治者為了人民的利益而治理。如果改變制度比寄錢成就更多的善，那麼這個論證就是叫我們去致力於改變制度。它並不支持兩樣都不做。

items.o_en: A morality that almost nobody follows cannot be the true one. Ought implies can.
items.o_zh: 一套幾乎沒有人遵守的道德，不可能是真的。「應該」蘊涵「做得到」。
items.r_en: “Can” is ambiguous. It is possible for almost any reader of this page to give more than he does, so the conclusion is not impossible to follow. It is hard, and unusual, and those are different things. Slavery was once universal, and those who called it wrong were told that their standard was unlivable. Still, the objection has a point for anyone trying to change conduct. A demand set so high that people give up is less useful than one they will meet. Singer has said as much, and so did Mencius about Mozi.
items.r_zh: 「做得到」是有歧義的。這一頁的幾乎任何一位讀者，都有可能捐得比現在多；所以那個結論並不是無法遵行的。它是難的、少見的；而那是不同的事。奴隸制曾經到處都是；那些說它錯的人，被告知他們的標準沒辦法過日子。不過，對任何想要改變行為的人來說，這個反駁有它的道理。一項定得太高、以致人們乾脆放棄的要求，不如一項他們會去達到的要求有用。辛格說過這樣的話；孟子談墨子時，說的也是這個。

said.claim: “One death is a tragedy. A million deaths is a statistic.” (Stalin)
said.claim_zh: 「一個人的死是悲劇。一百萬人的死是統計數字。」（史達林）
said.verdict_en: No record that he said it
said.verdict_zh: 沒有他說過這句話的紀錄
said.en: No Soviet document or reliable witness records Stalin saying this, and it was first attached to him in the American press after the Second World War. The thought is older. In 1925 the German satirist Kurt Tucholsky put nearly the same words into the mouth of a French diplomat in a comic sketch: the death of one man is a catastrophe, and a hundred thousand dead are a statistic. Whoever coined it was describing the reaction Adam Smith had noticed. The line owes its long life to being attributed to a man who caused deaths by the million and seems to have slept well.
said.zh: 沒有任何蘇聯的文件或可靠的證人，記錄過史達林說這句話；它是在第二次世界大戰之後的美國報刊上，才第一次被掛到他名下的。這個想法更早就有了。1925 年，德國的諷刺作家圖霍爾斯基在一篇諧謔短文裡，把幾乎相同的話放進了一位法國外交官的嘴裡：一個人的死是一場災難，十萬個死者是一個統計數字。不管是誰造了這句話，他描述的就是亞當・斯密注意到的那種反應。這句話之所以流傳得這麼久，是因為它被歸給了一個造成數以百萬計的死亡、而且看來睡得很好的人。

terms.d_en: Mozi’s doctrine that the interests of all should count equally in deciding what to do.
terms.d_zh: 墨子的學說：決定怎麼做的時候，所有人的利益應當同等地算進去。

terms.d_en: The Confucian view that care is rightly stronger toward those nearer to us.
terms.d_zh: 儒家的看法：對較親近的人，關懷理當較強。

terms.d_en: Duties owed to particular people, such as family, because of our relation to them.
terms.d_zh: 由於我們與特定的人（例如家人）的關係，而對他們負有的義務。

terms.d_en: Doing good to others. Distinguished from benevolence, which is wishing it.
terms.d_zh: 對別人做好事。與 benevolence（願別人好）有別。

terms.d_en: In Kant, a duty that must be fulfilled but leaves open how, when, and how much.
terms.d_zh: 在康德，指必須履行、卻沒有規定怎麼做、何時做、做多少的義務。

terms.d_en: Doing more good than duty requires. Singer’s argument shrinks this category.
terms.d_zh: 做得比義務所要求的更多。辛格的論證壓縮了這個範疇。

terms.d_en: The objection that a moral theory asks more of people than morality can reasonably ask.
terms.d_zh: 反對某個道德理論對人的要求，超過了道德所能合理要求的。

terms.d_en: A movement that uses evidence to find where resources do the most good.
terms.d_zh: 一個運用證據找出資源在哪裡能成就最多善的運動。

vocab.eg: You can wade in and pull the child out.
vocab.eg_zh: 你可以涉水過去，把孩子拉上來。

vocab.eg: Everyone thinks worse of anyone who would hesitate.
vocab.eg_zh: 每個人都瞧不起會猶豫的人。

vocab.eg: A cost that is small by comparison.
vocab.eg_zh: 相較之下很小的代價。

vocab.eg: As though the stranger had no claim on us at all.
vocab.eg_zh: 彷彿那個陌生人對我們毫無要求。

vocab.eg: Would you entrust them to a man who holds this view?
vocab.eg_zh: 你會把他們託付給一個抱持這種看法的人嗎？

vocab.eg: Then he would go about his business.
vocab.eg_zh: 然後他就去忙自己的事了。

vocab.eg: The feeling does not keep pace with the knowledge.
vocab.eg_zh: 感受跟不上這份知道。

vocab.eg: Mencius attacked Mozi in the strongest terms he ever used.
vocab.eg_zh: 孟子攻擊墨子，用了他平生最重的話。

vocab.eg: Aid can prop up the governments that cause the harm.
vocab.eg_zh: 援助可能撐住造成禍害的那些政府。

vocab.eg: He then turns the question round.
vocab.eg_zh: 然後他把問題轉了過來。

quiz.q: What principle does Singer draw from the pond?
options: If we can prevent something very bad at a comparatively small cost to ourselves, we ought to do it.
We should help only people we can see.
Children should not play near water.
Charity is always optional.

quiz.q: What is Mozi’s test for those who say impartial care cannot be practiced?
options: Ask whom they would trust with their own family when going to war.
Ask them to count their money.
Ask them to recite the Odes.
Ask them to give up their parents.

quiz.q: What is Adam Smith’s point about the little finger?
options: Our feelings for distant strangers are far weaker than our judgment says they should be.
Fingers are more valuable than people.
Earthquakes are common in China.
Europeans should not trade with Asia.

quiz.q: Why does Mencius reject impartial care?
options: Moral concern grows from family affection, and to deny its degrees is to cut the root.
He thinks strangers do not matter.
He believes war is necessary.
He holds that only rulers have duties.
