quiz.q: What does Kant mean by calling beneficence an imperfect duty?
options: We must help, but how much, when, and whom is left to our judgment.
It is not really a duty.
It applies only to the rich.
It can never be fulfilled.

write.en: At which of the six ponds did you stop? State your reason in one sentence, and then write the strongest reply to it you can.
write.zh: 你停在六個池塘當中的哪一個？用一句話說出你的理由；然後寫出你所能想到的、對它最強的回應。

write.en: Mozi or Mencius: should we care for all people equally, or more for those who are near? Answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 墨子還是孟子：我們應該同等地關懷所有人，還是多關懷親近的人？用大約 150 個英文字回答。

write.en: Retell the parable of the Good Samaritan in five English sentences, and say what question it answers.
write.zh: 用五個英文句子重述「好撒瑪利亞人」的比喻，並且說明它回答的是什麼問題。

paras.en: The Buddha states Mozi’s conclusion and reaches it by Mencius’s route. The Discourse on Love says: “Even as a mother would protect with her life her child, her only child, so too for all creatures unfold a boundless heart,” toward beings “seen or unseen, living far or near.” The scope is everyone, with no degrees. The image, though, is the most partial love there is, and the practice that goes with it begins with what is near. In the standard method one first wishes oneself well, then a person one loves, then someone neutral, then an enemy, and only then all beings without limit. The feeling is trained outward by stages until the stages disappear.
paras.zh: 佛陀說出的是墨子的結論，走的卻是孟子的路。〈慈經〉說：「就像一位母親用生命保護她的孩子、她唯一的孩子，對一切眾生也要這樣展開無量的心」；對象是「看得見或看不見的、住在遠處或近處的」眾生。範圍是每一個，沒有等差。然而，那個意象卻是世上最偏私的一種愛；而與它配套的修習，是從近處開始的。在標準的方法裡，修的人先願自己安樂，再願一位自己所愛的人，再願一位無親無怨的人，再願一位怨敵，然後才是無量無邊的一切眾生。這份感情被一階一階地往外訓練，直到那些階消失為止。

paras.en: This suggests that the quarrel between Mozi and Mencius is partly about the difference between a starting point and a goal. Mencius is right about how care grows. Mozi is right about where it should arrive. The Mahāyāna ideal of the bodhisattva takes the goal as far as it can go, to a vow to work for the liberation of all beings however long it takes. A companion page examines that ideal and asks which Western account of compassion comes nearest to it.
paras.zh: 這暗示了：墨子與孟子之間的爭執，有一部分是「起點」與「目標」的差別。關於關懷怎麼生長，孟子是對的。關於它應該抵達哪裡，墨子是對的。大乘的菩薩理想，把這個目標推到了盡頭：發願為一切眾生的解脫而努力，不管要多久。姊妹篇會檢視這個理想，並且問：西方對「悲」的哪一種說明最接近它？

link.zh: 讀 D19・慈悲與菩薩道

further.n_zh: 那段攻擊、與夷之的辯論，以及親親仁民愛物的次序。

further.t: Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments, Part III, chapter 3
The Gospel of Luke 10:25–37

further.n_zh: 好撒瑪利亞人。

further.n_zh: 一群試著照辛格的結論過日子的人的群像。

lessons.title: Why Do We Need Rules?
lessons.blurb_en: Imagine people with no government, no law, and no one to enforce a promise. Hobbes, Locke, Xunzi, and Mozi on what would go wrong, a game in which you can watch it go wrong, and the villages that manage without a sovereign.
lessons.blurb_zh: 想像一群人：沒有政府、沒有法律，也沒有人強制執行任何承諾。霍布斯、洛克、荀子與墨子，談會出什麼差錯；一個讓你親眼看著它出差錯的遊戲；以及那些沒有主權者也管得好的村莊。
lessons.big_en: Every rule limits someone, and most of us obey thousands of them without being asked. Political philosophy begins by asking what we would lose if they were gone, since the answer tells us what rules are for and when one has ceased to deserve obedience.
lessons.big_zh: 每一條規則都限制了某個人；而我們大多數人，沒有人要求就遵守著成千上萬條規則。政治哲學是從這個問題開始的：如果它們不見了，我們會失去什麼？因為答案告訴了我們，規則是做什麼用的，以及一條規則什麼時候已經不再值得服從。

paras.en: Philosophers have a method for finding out what a thing is for. They imagine the world without it. Applied to government, the method gives the thought experiment known as the state of nature: human beings as they are, with their needs, fears, and abilities, and no authority over them. There are no police, courts, or laws, and no one is in a position to make anyone keep his word. The question is what life would be like, and the answers have differed so widely that they define the main positions in political thought. The purpose is to understand the present. No one who uses the method supposes that people could return to such a state.
paras.zh: 哲學家有一個方法，用來找出一樣東西是做什麼用的。他們想像沒有它的世界。把這個方法用在政府上，就得出了那個稱為「自然狀態」的思想實驗：人就是現在這個樣子，有他們的需要、恐懼與能力，而沒有任何權威在他們之上。沒有警察、法庭或法律；也沒有任何人有辦法讓任何人守信。問題是：生活會是什麼樣子？而答案的分歧之大，界定了政治思想裡的幾個主要立場。這樣做的目的是理解當下。用這個方法的人，沒有一個認為人們可以回到那樣的狀態。

essay.h_en: Hobbes: war of all against all
essay.h_zh: 霍布斯：一切人對一切人的戰爭

paras.en: Thomas Hobbes published Leviathan in 1651, two years after the English had beheaded their king, and his account is the darkest. He starts from three facts. People are roughly equal, in that the weakest can kill the strongest by stealth or in company. They want many of the same scarce things. And none can be sure of the others’ intentions. It follows that each has reason to strike first, even if he wishes only to be safe, and each knows that the others have the same reason. “During the time men live without a common Power to keep them all in awe, they are in that condition which is called Warre; and such a warre, as is of every man, against every man.” War in his sense need not be fighting. It is the known readiness to fight, as bad weather is a tendency to rain. In that condition there is no farming, trade, building, or learning, since no one can count on keeping what he makes.
paras.zh: 霍布斯在 1651 年出版了《利維坦》，那是英國人把自己的國王斬首之後兩年；而他的說明是最陰暗的。他從三個事實出發。人大致上是平等的，因為最弱的人靠著偷襲或結夥，也殺得了最強的人。他們想要許多同樣稀少的東西。而誰也無法確定別人的意圖。由此推出：每個人都有理由先下手，即使他只是想求安全；而每個人也都知道，別人有同樣的理由。「在人們沒有一個共同的權力使大家都有所畏懼的時候，他們就處在那種稱為戰爭的狀況裡；而這種戰爭，是每一個人對每一個人的戰爭。」他所說的戰爭，不一定是在打仗。它是「眾所周知的隨時準備打」，就像壞天氣是一種「會下雨的傾向」。在那種狀況下，沒有農耕、貿易、建築或學問，因為誰也無法指望保得住自己做出來的東西。

paras.en: The way out is an agreement. Each person gives up his right to do whatever he judges necessary, on condition that the others do the same. But an agreement of that kind is worth nothing if anyone can break it when it suits him. “Covenants, without the Sword, are but Words, and of no strength to secure a man at all.” So the parties must also set up a power strong enough to punish any of them, a sovereign whom Hobbes calls the Leviathan and “that Mortall God.” His conclusion is that almost any government is better than none, and that to resist the sovereign is to risk the return of the war.
paras.zh: 出路是一個約定。每個人都放棄「凡是自己判斷為必要的事都可以去做」的權利，條件是別人也這樣做。然而，如果任何人只要覺得划算就可以背約，那樣的約定就一文不值。「沒有劍的信約，不過是空話，根本沒有力量保障一個人。」所以，立約的各方還必須設立一個強大到足以懲罰他們當中任何一個人的權力：一位主權者；霍布斯稱之為利維坦，稱之為「那位會死的神」。他的結論是：幾乎任何政府都比沒有政府好；而反抗主權者，就是冒著讓那場戰爭回來的風險。

paras.en: John Locke, writing forty years later, thought Hobbes had described the state of nature at its worst and called it the whole. Even without government, he argued, people are bound by a moral law that reason can discover. The state of nature is “a state of liberty, yet it is not a state of licence.” No one may destroy another’s life, health, liberty, or possessions, and most people know it. What is missing is a way of settling disputes. Each person must be judge in his own case, and people are partial to themselves and carried too far by anger when they punish. “Want of a common judge with authority, puts all men in a state of nature.” Government is set up to supply the judge. Its purpose is to protect rights that people already had, and Locke draws the consequence that Hobbes refused. A government that attacks the rights it was made to protect has broken the agreement, and the people may replace it.
paras.zh: 四十年後寫作的洛克認為，霍布斯描述的是自然狀態最糟的樣子，卻把它說成了全部。他論證：即使沒有政府，人也受到一條理性可以發現的道德法則約束。自然狀態「是一種自由的狀態，卻不是一種放縱的狀態」。誰也不可以毀壞別人的生命、健康、自由或財產；而多數人知道這一點。缺少的，是一種解決爭端的辦法。每個人都得在自己的案子裡當裁判；而人對自己是偏私的，懲罰別人時又會被怒氣帶得太遠。「沒有一位具有權威的共同裁判，就使所有人處於自然狀態。」設立政府，是為了提供那位裁判。它的目的，是保護人們本來就有的權利；而洛克引出了霍布斯所拒絕的那個後果。一個攻擊「它被設立來保護的那些權利」的政府，已經破壞了約定；人民可以把它換掉。

essay.h_en: Xunzi and Mozi: desire and disagreement
essay.h_zh: 荀子與墨子：欲望與分歧

paras.en: Chinese philosophers reasoned about the origin of order in the same way nearly two thousand years earlier. Xunzi asks where ritual and rules come from, and answers in a sentence that could be Hobbes’s: “People are born with desires. When they desire and do not get, they cannot but seek. When they seek without measure or limit, they cannot but contend. Contention brings disorder, and disorder brings exhaustion. The former kings hated this disorder, and so they established ritual and rightness to make divisions.” His account of what rules achieve is more generous than Hobbes’s. Rules exist, he says, to nourish desires and to see that goods and wants keep pace with each other. He also explains what rules make possible. A human being is weaker than an ox and slower than a horse, and yet oxen and horses work for us. “Why? Because people can form groups and they cannot.” Groups are possible because of divisions, and divisions because of a shared sense of what is right.
paras.zh: 中國的哲學家，早了將近兩千年就用同樣的方式推論秩序的起源。荀子問：禮與規則是從哪裡來的？他用一句可以出自霍布斯之口的話回答：「人生而有欲，欲而不得，則不能無求。求而無度量分界，則不能不爭；爭則亂，亂則窮。先王惡其亂也，故制禮義以分之。」他對「規則成就了什麼」的說明，比霍布斯的更寬厚。他說，規則的存在，是為了「養人之欲」，並且使物與欲「兩者相持而長」。他還說明了規則使什麼成為可能。人的力氣不如牛，跑得不如馬，而牛馬卻為我們所用。「何也？曰：人能群，彼不能群也。」人之所以能群，靠的是「分」；而「分」之所以行得通，靠的是共有的「義」。

paras.en: Mozi locates the trouble somewhere else. In the beginning, before there were rulers, he says, “each person had his own view of what is right. One person, one view. Two people, two views. Ten people, ten views.” Each approved his own and condemned the others’, families broke apart, and the world was in chaos like that of birds and beasts. The cause of disorder, on his account, is that people sincerely disagree about what ought to be done and have no way of settling it. His remedy is a ruler chosen for his worth, whose judgment unifies the standards of all. Locke’s missing judge is here already, and so is the danger that Mozi did not see, that the one who unifies the standards may be wrong.
paras.zh: 墨子把毛病放在另一個地方。他說，起初還沒有統治者的時候，「人異義。是以一人則一義，二人則二義，十人則十義」。每個人都肯定自己的、否定別人的；家人離散，天下大亂，「若禽獸然」。照他的說法，禍亂的原因是：人們真心地對「該怎麼做」意見分歧，卻沒有辦法解決它。他的對治，是一位因賢能而被選出的統治者，由他的判斷來統一所有人的標準（尚同）。洛克那位缺席的裁判，在這裡已經出現了；墨子沒有看到的那個危險也已經在了：那位統一標準的人，可能是錯的。

paras.en: In the twentieth century the argument was given a precise form. Two suspects are questioned separately. If both stay silent, each serves one year. If one informs and the other does not, the informer goes free and the other serves ten. If both inform, each serves five. Whatever the other does, each does better by informing, and so both inform and serve five years when they could have served one. This is the prisoner’s dilemma. Its lesson is that people who each choose sensibly can arrive together at a result that none of them wants. Herdsmen who each add one more animal to a shared pasture destroy it. Nations that each catch a few more fish empty the sea. The ecologist Garrett Hardin called this the tragedy of the commons and wrote, “Freedom in a commons brings ruin to all.”
paras.zh: 到了二十世紀，這個論證得到了一個精確的形式。兩名嫌犯被分開審訊。如果兩人都保持沉默，各關一年。如果一人告密、另一人不告，告密的獲釋，另一個關十年。如果兩人都告密，各關五年。不管對方怎麼做，每個人自己告密都比較划算；於是兩人都告了密，各關五年，而他們本來可以各關一年。這就是「囚徒困境」。它的教訓是：每個人各自作出合理的選擇，卻可能一起走到一個誰也不想要的結果。在共用的牧場上，每一位牧人各自多放一頭牲口，牧場就毀了。每一個國家各自多捕幾條魚，海就空了。生態學家哈丁把這稱為「公地悲劇」，並且寫道：「公地上的自由，給所有人帶來毀滅。」

paras.en: This is why Hobbes insisted on the sword. A rule that everyone would benefit from will still be broken if each person gains by breaking it while the others comply. Rules need enforcement, and the game below lets you watch that happen.
paras.zh: 這就是為什麼霍布斯堅持要有那把劍。一條人人都會從中受益的規則，如果每個人在別人遵守的時候自己違反能得到好處，它仍然會被打破。規則需要執行；下面的遊戲讓你親眼看著這件事發生。

paras.en: Hobbes concluded that only a single overwhelming power can end the trap, and here the evidence has gone against him. The political scientist Elinor Ostrom spent her career studying communities that share a resource: Swiss villages with common alpine meadows, Japanese mountain forests, Spanish irrigation canals, lobster fisheries in Maine. Many of them have managed without ruin for centuries, and they have done it with rules that the users made themselves, watched over by one another, with small penalties that grow for repeated offenses. She received the Nobel Prize in economics in 2009. Experiments tell the same story. In laboratory games, cooperation among strangers decays when free riding goes unpunished and recovers as soon as players are allowed to fine one another, which many will do even at a cost to themselves.
paras.zh: 霍布斯的結論是：只有單一而壓倒性的權力，才能終結那個陷阱；而在這一點上，證據對他不利。政治學家歐斯壯窮畢生之力，研究共用某項資源的社群：擁有共同高山草場的瑞士村莊、日本的山林、西班牙的灌溉水渠、緬因州的龍蝦漁場。其中許多已經管理了好幾個世紀而沒有毀掉；它們靠的是使用者自己訂的規則，彼此監督，罰則輕微，而屢犯者加重。她在 2009 年獲得了諾貝爾經濟學獎。實驗說的是同一個故事。在實驗室的遊戲裡，當搭便車的人不受懲罰時，陌生人之間的合作就衰退；而一旦允許玩家彼此罰款，合作就恢復了。許多人即使自己要付出代價，也願意去罰。

paras.en: So the old question has a more exact answer than it had. We need rules because sincere and reasonable people, left to themselves, fall into contests and disagreements that leave all of them worse off. We need the rules to be enforced, because a good rule can be undone by a few who ignore it. And we have some choice about who does the enforcing, which is where the next three lessons begin. A philosopher of the Legalist school, Han Fei, drew the harshest conclusion from the same facts. “The people submit to power, and few can be moved by rightness,” he wrote, and he advised rulers to rely on rewards and punishments alone. The state that followed his advice unified China and lasted fifteen years.
paras.zh: 所以，那個老問題有了一個比從前更精確的答案。我們需要規則，是因為真誠而講理的人，放任不管，會落入使所有人都更糟的爭奪與分歧。我們需要規則被「執行」，因為一條好規則可以被少數無視它的人毀掉。而由誰來執行，我們是有某些選擇的；接下來的三課就從這裡開始。法家的哲學家韓非，從同樣的事實引出了最嚴酷的結論。他寫道：「民者固服於勢，寡能懷於義」；他建議統治者只倚靠賞與罰。聽從了他的建議的那個國家統一了中國，維持了十五年。

lab.title_en: Try it: the common pot
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：公共的鍋
lab.lead_en: You and three computer players each get ten tokens a round. Whatever is put into the common pot is multiplied by 1.6 and shared equally among all four, whether they contributed or not. Play five rounds with no rules, and then five in which players may fine one another.
lab.lead_zh: 你與三位電腦玩家，每一輪各拿到十枚代幣。投進公共鍋裡的代幣會乘以 1.6，再平分給四個人，不管他有沒有投。先玩五輪沒有規則的，再玩五輪玩家可以彼此罰款的。

phase.zh: 第一到五輪・沒有規則
第六到十輪・可以罰款

ask.en: How many of your ten tokens will you put in the pot?
ask.zh: 你的十枚代幣，要投幾枚進鍋裡？

fineNote.en: A fine costs you 1 token and costs the other player 3.
fineNote.zh: 罰一次，你付 1 枚，對方扣 3 枚。

mid.en: Five rounds are over. Look at what happened to the pot. Now the rule changes: after each round, any player may pay to fine another. Ada and Ben will fine anyone who gives much less than the group.
mid.zh: 五輪結束了。看看那口鍋變成什麼樣子。現在規則變了：每一輪結束後，任何玩家都可以付錢去罰另一位玩家。阿達與阿本會罰任何一個投得比大家少很多的人。

pattern.en: Average contribution per player: {a} of 10 in the rounds without rules, and {b} of 10 once fines were allowed. This is the usual result in laboratories around the world. Without enforcement, those who give generously see others take advantage and give less each round. With it, contributions climb back.
pattern.zh: 每位玩家平均投入：沒有規則的那幾輪是 10 枚當中的 {a} 枚；允許罰款之後是 {b} 枚。這是世界各地實驗室裡常見的結果。沒有執行的機制時，大方投入的人看到別人佔便宜，就一輪比一輪投得少。有了它，投入又爬回來。

pattern_flat.en: Average contribution per player: {a} of 10 in the rounds without rules, and {b} of 10 once fines were allowed. In your game the fines did not raise the average, which is unusual. In most laboratories contributions decay without enforcement and climb back with it. Play again and watch what the other three do when you hold your own contribution steady.
pattern_flat.zh: 每位玩家平均投入：沒有規則的那幾輪是 10 枚當中的 {a} 枚；允許罰款之後是 {b} 枚。在你這一局裡，罰款並沒有把平均拉高，這並不常見。在多數實驗室裡，沒有執行的機制時投入會衰退，有了它又爬回來。再玩一次，把自己的投入固定住，看看另外三個人怎麼做。

you_free.en: You gave less than the others on average. In the first five rounds that paid, and it is exactly what Hobbes predicts a sensible person will do when no one can be made to keep faith. Notice what the fines did to that strategy.
you_free.zh: 你平均投得比別人少。在前五輪，這樣做是划算的；而這正是霍布斯所預言的：在沒有人能被迫守信的時候，一個明智的人就會這樣做。留意那些罰款把這個策略怎麼了。

you_gave.en: You gave more than the others on average, and in the first five rounds you paid for it: the free rider earned more than you did from your generosity. Mencius would be pleased with you and Hobbes would call you prey. Under fines your policy stopped being costly.
you_gave.zh: 你平均投得比別人多；而在前五輪，你為此付出了代價：那位搭便車的人，從你的大方當中賺得比你還多。孟子會對你很滿意；霍布斯會說你是獵物。有了罰款之後，你的方針就不再吃虧了。

you_mid.en: You gave about what the others gave, which is what most people do. Researchers call this conditional cooperation: willing to do one’s share as long as others do theirs. It explains both halves of the result, the decay and the recovery.
you_mid.zh: 你投的跟別人差不多；多數人都這樣。研究者稱之為「有條件的合作」：只要別人盡他們的那一份，我就願意盡我的。它解釋了結果的兩半：衰退，與恢復。

fined.en: You paid to fine another player {n} times. Punishing cost you tokens and gained you nothing directly. People do it anyway, in every culture where the game has been played, and it is this readiness that lets groups govern themselves without a sovereign. Ostrom’s villages run on it.
fined.zh: 你付錢罰了別的玩家 {n} 次。懲罰讓你損失代幣，而沒有直接帶給你任何好處。人們照樣這樣做，凡是玩過這個遊戲的文化都一樣；而正是這份意願，使群體沒有主權者也能自治。歐斯壯研究的那些村莊，靠的就是它。

nofine.en: You never fined anyone, and left the punishing to Ada and Ben. You benefited from an order that others paid to keep. Economists call that second-order free riding, and it is the reason Hobbes thought enforcement had to be someone’s job.
nofine.zh: 你從來沒有罰過任何人，把懲罰的事留給了阿達與阿本。你從一個別人付錢維持的秩序裡得了好處。經濟學家稱之為「二階搭便車」；而這就是霍布斯認為「執行」必須是某個人的職責的原因。

q.en: Last question. Would you rather the four of you go on fining one another, or pay a tax to a fifth party who does all the fining?
q.zh: 最後一個問題。你寧可四個人繼續彼此罰下去，還是繳一筆稅給第五個人，由他負責所有的罰款？

t.en: Keep it among ourselves
t.zh: 留在我們自己之間

v.en: This is Ostrom’s answer and, in spirit, Locke’s. It works where the group is small enough for everyone to see what everyone does, and where people expect to deal with one another again. Its weakness is that fines among equals can turn into feuds, and that it scales badly. Four people can watch a pot. Forty million cannot.
v.zh: 這是歐斯壯的答案；就精神而言，也是洛克的。它在這樣的地方行得通：群體小到每個人都看得見每個人做了什麼，而且人們預期彼此還會再打交道。它的弱點是：平輩之間的罰款可能變成世仇；而且它很難放大。四個人看得住一口鍋。四千萬人看不住。

t.en: Hand it to a fifth party
t.zh: 交給第五個人

v.en: This is Hobbes’s answer, and Mozi’s. A single enforcer ends the quarrels over who fined whom and spares everyone the cost of policing. The question Locke asked at once is who will fine the fifth party. You have solved the problem of the pot by creating someone who holds a sword and has nothing to fear from the rest of you.
v.zh: 這是霍布斯的答案，也是墨子的。單一的執行者，終結了「誰罰了誰」的爭吵，也讓每個人省下了維持治安的成本。洛克立刻就問的問題是：誰來罰那第五個人？你解決了那口鍋的問題，辦法是造出了一個握著劍、而且對你們其餘的人毫無所懼的人。

argument.lead_en: Hobbes’s argument from Leviathan, chapters 13 to 17. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 霍布斯在《利維坦》第十三到十七章的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: People are roughly equal in power, compete for scarce goods, and cannot be sure of one another’s intentions.
steps.zh: 人在力量上大致平等，爭奪稀少的資源，而且無法確定彼此的意圖。
steps.ob_en: Rousseau objected that Hobbes had described people formed by society, with its envy and ambition, and read them back into nature. Locke objected that most people recognize moral limits without being forced.
steps.ob_zh: 盧梭反對說：霍布斯描述的是被社會塑造過的人，連同社會帶來的嫉妒與野心，然後把他們讀回了自然裡。洛克反對說：多數人不必被強迫，也認得道德的界限。

steps.en: So without a power over them, each has reason to strike first, and life is a war of all against all.
steps.zh: 所以，若沒有一個在他們之上的權力，每個人都有理由先下手；而生活是一切人對一切人的戰爭。
steps.ob_en: The step from insecurity to war is where the prisoner’s dilemma does its work. It is strongest for strangers who meet once. People who expect to meet again have a reason to cooperate that Hobbes underrated.
steps.ob_zh: 從「不安全」跨到「戰爭」的這一步，正是囚徒困境起作用的地方。對只見一次面的陌生人來說，它最有力。預期還會再見面的人，有一個霍布斯低估了的合作理由。

steps.en: Agreements to keep the peace are worthless unless there is a power able to punish those who break them.
steps.zh: 維持和平的約定毫無價值，除非有一個能夠懲罰背約者的權力。
steps.ob_en: Accepted in some form by nearly everyone. The dispute is over the next step.
steps.ob_zh: 幾乎每個人都以某種形式接受這一點。爭議在下一步。

steps.en: Only a single sovereign with unlimited authority can be such a power.
steps.zh: 只有一位擁有無限權威的單一主權者，才能成為這樣的權力。
steps.ob_en: The weakest step. Locke replied that to escape foxes by handing oneself to a lion is no bargain, and that power can be divided and held to account. Ostrom showed that groups enforce their own rules. Hobbes feared that any limit on the sovereign reopens the question of who decides, and the question is real, but history has not borne out his answer.
steps.ob_zh: 最弱的一步。洛克回答：為了躲狐狸而把自己交給獅子，算不上划算的交易；而權力是可以被分割、被追究責任的。歐斯壯顯示，群體會執行自己的規則。霍布斯擔心的是：對主權者的任何限制，都會重新打開「由誰決定」的問題；這個問題是真實的，但歷史並沒有印證他的答案。

steps.en: Therefore reason requires us to set up such a sovereign and to obey it.
steps.zh: 所以，理性要求我們設立這樣一位主權者，並且服從它。
steps.ob_en: Hobbes allowed one exception. A subject need not submit to being killed, since self-preservation was the whole point of the agreement.
steps.ob_zh: 霍布斯容許一個例外。臣民不必乖乖被殺，因為自我保存正是這個約定的全部用意。

source.work: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan (1651), chapter 13; Xunzi, chapter 19, “Discourse on Ritual”
source.work_zh: 霍布斯《利維坦》第十三章；《荀子・禮論》
source.tr: Hobbes in the original English and spelling (public domain); Xunzi translated for this series, with the Chinese text
source.lead_en: Two accounts of why order had to be invented, written at opposite ends of Eurasia and nineteen centuries apart.
source.lead_zh: 兩段關於「秩序為什麼必須被發明出來」的說明；寫於歐亞大陸的兩端，相隔十九個世紀。

passages.en: Hereby it is manifest, that during the time men live without a common Power to keep them all in awe, they are in that condition which is called Warre; and such a warre, as is of every man, against every man. For WARRE, consisteth not in Battell onely, or the act of fighting; but in a tract of time, wherein the Will to contend by Battell is sufficiently known.
passages.zh: 由此可見：在人們沒有一個共同的權力使大家都有所畏懼的時候，他們就處在那種稱為戰爭的狀況裡；而這種戰爭，是每一個人對每一個人的戰爭。因為戰爭並不只在於交戰，或打鬥的行為；而在於一段時間，在這段時間裡，以交戰來爭奪的意願是充分為人所知的。
passages.note_en: The second sentence is the important one and is often left out when the first is quoted. Hobbes does not claim that people without government would fight all the time. He claims that they would live under a standing threat, and that the threat is enough to ruin everything worth having, since no one invests where nothing is secure. On this definition two armed states facing each other across a border are in a state of nature toward each other, and he says so. The capital letters and spellings are his.
passages.note_zh: 第二句才是重要的一句；而人們引用第一句的時候，常常把它漏掉。霍布斯並沒有主張，沒有政府的人會一天到晚打鬥。他主張的是：他們會活在一個長期存在的威脅之下；而光是這個威脅，就足以毀掉一切值得擁有的東西，因為在什麼都沒有保障的地方，沒有人肯投入。照這個定義，隔著邊界對峙的兩個武裝國家，彼此之間就處於自然狀態；而他自己就是這麼說的。大寫字母與拼法都是他的原樣。

passages.en: From what does ritual arise? I say: people are born with desires. When they desire and do not get, they cannot but seek. When they seek without measure or limit, they cannot but contend. Contention brings disorder, and disorder brings exhaustion. The former kings hated this disorder, and so they established ritual and rightness to make divisions, in order to nourish people’s desires and to supply what they seek.
passages.zh: 禮起於何也？曰：人生而有欲，欲而不得，則不能無求。求而無度量分界，則不能不爭；爭則亂，亂則窮。先王惡其亂也，故制禮義以分之，以養人之欲，給人之求。
passages.note_en: The chain of reasoning has four links, desire, seeking, contention, disorder, and each is joined to the next by “cannot but.” It is as tight as anything in Hobbes. The difference comes in the last clause. For Hobbes rules restrain. For Xunzi they nourish: the word is yǎng, used of feeding and raising. Ritual assigns each person a share and a place, and by doing so makes it possible for desires to be met at all. He goes on to say that fine food nourishes the mouth and music the ear, and that ritual is what lets everyone have some of each. His rules are closer to the rules of a kitchen than to those of a prison.
passages.note_zh: 這條推理的鏈子有四環：欲、求、爭、亂；每一環都用「不能不」扣到下一環。它跟霍布斯書裡的任何一段同樣緊。差別出現在最後一個子句。對霍布斯來說，規則是約束。對荀子來說，規則是滋養：用的字是「養」，餵養、養育的養。禮給每個人分派了一份、一個位置；而正因為這樣，欲望才有可能得到滿足。他接著說，美食養口，音樂養耳；而禮，是讓每個人都能各得一些的東西。他的規則，比較像廚房的規矩，而不像監獄的規矩。

items.o_en: There never was a state of nature and no one ever signed a contract. The whole argument is a fiction.
items.o_zh: 從來就沒有什麼自然狀態，也沒有人簽過什麼契約。整個論證是虛構的。
items.r_en: David Hume made this objection in 1748. Nearly all governments, he observed, were founded on conquest or usurpation, and to tell a poor peasant that he has consented by staying is like telling a man carried aboard a ship asleep that he consents to the captain by not jumping into the sea. The better defenders of the method agree that it is a device. It asks what rational people would agree to, and uses the answer to test the arrangements we have. A rule that no one could reasonably have accepted is suspect whether or not anyone was asked.
items.r_zh: 休謨在 1748 年提出了這個反駁。他觀察到，幾乎所有的政府都是建立在征服或篡奪之上的；而對一個貧窮的農民說「你留下來就表示同意了」，就像對一個在睡夢中被抬上船的人說：你沒有跳海，就表示你同意聽船長的。為這個方法辯護得比較好的人，同意它是一個「裝置」。它問的是：理性的人會同意什麼？然後用這個答案來檢驗我們現有的安排。一條沒有任何人可能合理地接受的規則，不管有沒有人被問過，都是可疑的。

items.o_en: People are naturally cooperative. Rules and rulers are what make them selfish and violent.
items.o_zh: 人天生就是合作的。使他們變得自私而暴力的，正是規則與統治者。
items.r_en: This is the anarchist’s reply, and it has support in the studies of infants and of small communities. But the same evidence shows cooperation breaking down as groups grow and as free riders appear. The communities Ostrom studied did not lack rules. They had made their own and enforced them. The finding that people can govern themselves is a finding about how rules may be made. It gives no reason to think that a large society could do without them.
items.r_zh: 這是無政府主義者的回答；而它在嬰兒研究與小型社群的研究裡，是有支持的。然而，同樣的證據也顯示：隨著群體變大、隨著搭便車的人出現，合作就瓦解了。歐斯壯研究的那些社群並不是沒有規則。它們訂了自己的規則，並且加以執行。「人能夠自治」這個發現，是一個關於「規則可以怎麼訂」的發現。它並沒有給出理由讓人認為，一個大型社會可以不要規則。

items.o_en: If rules exist for our benefit, then I may break any rule whenever breaking it benefits me and harms no one.
items.o_zh: 如果規則是為了我們的利益而存在的，那麼，只要違反某條規則對我有利、又不傷害任何人，我就可以違反它。
items.r_en: The reasoning is the free rider’s, and the game shows where it leads when everyone uses it. There is a narrower point in it that is sound. A rule that has lost its purpose, or that serves only those who made it, has lost its claim, and Locke built a theory of resistance on that. The test is whether you could accept everyone’s breaking the rule in cases like yours. The person who runs a red light on an empty road at night can perhaps pass it. The person who evades a tax cannot.
items.r_zh: 這是搭便車者的推理；而那個遊戲顯示了，人人都這樣推理的時候它通向哪裡。其中有一個比較窄的論點是站得住的。一條已經失去目的、或只為訂立它的人服務的規則，已經失去了它的資格；洛克就是在這一點上建立了一套反抗的理論。檢驗的方法是：在像你這樣的情況裡，你能不能接受每個人都違反這條規則？深夜在空無一人的路上闖紅燈的人，也許過得了這一關。逃稅的人過不了。

said.claim: “The life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short.” (Hobbes, on human nature)
said.claim_zh: 「人的生活孤獨、貧困、污穢、野蠻而短暫。」（霍布斯論人性）
said.verdict_zh: 是他的話，但談的是一種處境
said.en: The phrase is authentic, from chapter 13 of Leviathan, and it is regularly quoted as Hobbes’s verdict on human life or human nature. It is neither. The sentence describes life in one situation, where there is no power to keep the peace, and its point is how much we gain by leaving that situation. Hobbes did not think people wicked. He says in the same chapter that the desires and passions of man are in themselves no sin, and that in the state of nature nothing can be unjust, since there is no law to break. The trouble, on his account, lies in the situation. He was by all reports a cheerful man who played tennis at seventy-five and lived to ninety-one.
said.zh: 這句話是真的，出自《利維坦》第十三章；而它經常被引用，當作霍布斯對人生或人性的判決。兩者都不是。這個句子描述的是「某一種處境」下的生活：沒有權力維持和平的時候；而它的重點是，離開那種處境讓我們得到了多少。霍布斯並不認為人是邪惡的。他在同一章裡說：人的欲望與激情本身並不是罪；而在自然狀態裡，沒有什麼事可以算不正義，因為沒有法律可以違反。照他的說法，毛病出在處境上。據各方記載，他是個開朗的人，七十五歲還在打網球，活到了九十一歲。

terms.d_en: The condition of people living without any political authority, used as a thought experiment.
terms.d_zh: 人們在沒有任何政治權威之下生活的狀況；用作思想實驗。

terms.d_en: The agreement, real or hypothetical, by which people set up a government.
terms.d_zh: 人們藉以設立政府的約定；不論是真實的還是假設的。

terms.d_en: The person or body holding supreme authority in a state.
terms.d_zh: 在一個國家裡握有最高權威的人或機構。

terms.d_en: A binding agreement, especially one whose performance lies in the future.
terms.d_zh: 有約束力的約定；尤指履行在未來的那一種。

terms.d_en: A situation in which each party does best by defecting, yet all do worse if all defect.
terms.d_zh: 一種處境：每一方自己背叛最划算，但如果人人背叛，人人都更糟。

terms.d_en: One who enjoys a benefit that others pay to provide.
terms.d_zh: 享受別人付出代價才提供的好處的人。

terms.d_en: A resource open to a whole group, such as a pasture, a fishery, or the atmosphere.
terms.d_zh: 對整個群體開放的資源，例如牧場、漁場或大氣。

terms.d_en: Xunzi’s term for the system of roles and rules that the sages devised to end contention.
terms.d_zh: 荀子的用語：聖人為了止爭而制定的那一套角色與規則。

vocab.eg: No one is in a position to make anyone keep his word.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有任何人有辦法讓任何人守信。

vocab.eg: The weakest can kill the strongest by stealth.
vocab.eg_zh: 最弱的人靠著偷襲，也殺得了最強的人。

vocab.eg: Each has reason to strike first.
vocab.eg_zh: 每個人都有理由先下手。

vocab.eg: No one can count on keeping what he makes.
vocab.eg_zh: 誰也無法指望保得住自己做出來的東西。

vocab.eg: Anyone can break it when it suits him.
vocab.eg_zh: 任何人只要覺得划算就可以背約。

vocab.eg: People are partial to themselves.
vocab.eg_zh: 人對自己是偏私的。

vocab.eg: Goods and wants keep pace with each other.
vocab.eg_zh: 物與欲兩者相持而長。

vocab.eg: Cooperation decays when free riding goes unpunished.
vocab.eg_zh: 搭便車的人不受懲罰時，合作就衰退。

vocab.eg: Power can be divided and held to account.
vocab.eg_zh: 權力可以被分割、被追究責任。

vocab.eg: History has not borne out his answer.
vocab.eg_zh: 歷史並沒有印證他的答案。

quiz.q: What is the state of nature?
options: A thought experiment: people as they are, with no political authority over them.
A period of history before farming.
A national park.
Life after death.

quiz.q: Why, for Hobbes, does equality lead to war?
options: Roughly equal people competing for scarce goods cannot trust one another, so each has reason to strike first.
Equal people are wicked.
Equality makes people lazy.
Kings forbid equality.

quiz.q: What does Locke think is missing in the state of nature?
options: A common judge with authority to settle disputes.
Any moral law at all.
Food and shelter.
Religion.

quiz.q: According to Xunzi, what are ritual and rules for?
options: To make divisions that end contention and so nourish people’s desires.
To please the spirits.
To keep the common people poor.
To make everyone identical.

quiz.q: What did Ostrom’s research show?
options: Communities can manage shared resources for centuries with rules they make and enforce themselves.
Only a central state can prevent the ruin of a commons.
Shared resources are always destroyed.
People never punish free riders.

write.en: Describe a rule at your school or workplace that everyone benefits from and that each person is tempted to break. Who enforces it, and how?
write.zh: 描述你的學校或工作場所裡的一條規則：人人都從中受益，而每個人也都有違反它的誘惑。誰在執行它？怎麼執行？

write.en: Hobbes or Locke: is the worst thing a government can do to fail to keep order, or to abuse its power? Answer in about 150 words.
write.zh: 霍布斯還是洛克：一個政府所能做的最糟的事，是維持不了秩序，還是濫用權力？用大約 150 個英文字回答。

write.en: Translate 人能群，彼不能群也 and explain in two English sentences what Xunzi thinks makes grouping possible.
write.zh: 翻譯「人能群，彼不能群也」，並且用兩個英文句子說明：荀子認為是什麼使「群」成為可能？

paras.en: The Buddhist canon contains a state-of-nature story of its own, told as a myth and with some humor. In the beginning, it says, beings lived on food that grew by itself. Then some began to hoard. So they said, “We’d better divide up the rice and lay down boundaries.” With boundaries came theft, then accusation, lying, and blows. The beings gathered and said: “Why don’t we elect one being who would rightly accuse those who deserve it, blame those who deserve it, and expel those who deserve it?” In return they would give him a share of rice. He was called Mahāsammata, which the discourse explains as “elected by the populace.” The story has greed leading to property, property to conflict, and conflict to a ruler chosen by agreement and paid for a service. It places the origin of kingship in a contract and gives it no divine sanction, which was a radical thing to say in ancient India.
paras.zh: 佛教的經藏裡，有它自己的一個自然狀態的故事；它是以神話的方式講的，還帶著幾分幽默。故事說，起初眾生靠著自己生長出來的食物過活。後來有些眾生開始囤積。於是他們說：「我們最好把稻米分一分，劃定界線。」有了界線，就有了偷盜；接著是指責、說謊與毆打。眾生聚集起來說：「我們何不推選一位眾生，由他對該指責的加以指責、該訶責的加以訶責、該驅逐的加以驅逐？」作為回報，他們會給他一份稻米。他被稱為 Mahāsammata；這部經解釋說，意思就是「大眾所推選的」。這個故事說：貪導致私產，私產導致衝突，衝突導致一位由約定選出、因提供服務而受供養的統治者。它把王權的起源放在一個契約裡，沒有給它任何神聖的授權；在古代印度，這是很激進的說法。

paras.en: The Buddha’s own community was governed in a way that Ostrom would have recognized. The monastic rules were laid down one at a time, each in response to a particular problem, and the texts record the occasion for every one. The community met regularly, decided matters by agreement of all present, and had graded penalties ending in expulsion. There was no head with power over the rest. The Buddha declined to appoint a successor and told the monks that the teaching and the discipline would be their teacher (Dharma and the West, D18).
paras.zh: 佛陀自己的僧團，治理的方式是歐斯壯認得出來的。戒律是一條一條制定的，每一條都是回應一個具體的問題；而律典記錄了每一條的緣起。僧團定期集會，以全體在場者的同意來決定事務，並且有分等級的處分，最重的是擯出。沒有一位握有支配其他人的權力的首領。佛陀拒絕指定繼承人；他告訴比丘們，法與律就是他們的老師（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms: the one elected by the people
a formal act of the community

further.t: Thomas Hobbes, Leviathan, chapters 13, 14, and 17
further.n_en: Twenty pages that founded modern political philosophy.
further.n_zh: 二十頁，奠定了近代政治哲學。

further.t: John Locke, Second Treatise of Government, chapters 2, 3, and 9
《荀子・禮論》《荀子・王制》；《墨子・尚同上》
further.n_en: Desire and division; why people can form groups; one person, one view.
further.n_zh: 欲與分；人何以能群；一人則一義。

further.t: Elinor Ostrom, Governing the Commons (1990)
further.n_en: Chapter 3 has the long-lived cases.
further.n_zh: 第三章是那些長壽的案例。

further.t: Dīgha Nikāya 27, What Came First (Aggañña)
further.n_en: The Buddhist origin story.
further.n_zh: 佛教的起源故事。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Hobbes’s Moral and Political Philosophy”

lessons.title: What Is Fair?
lessons.blurb_en: Everyone wants a fair share and no one agrees on what it is. Aristotle’s proportion, Rawls’s veil of ignorance, Nozick’s basketball player, and a society you must design before you know which place in it will be yours.
lessons.blurb_zh: 人人都要公平的一份，而沒有人對「那是多少」有共識。亞里斯多德的比例、羅爾斯的無知之幕、諾齊克的籃球員；以及一個你必須在知道自己會落在哪個位置之前，就先設計好的社會。
lessons.big_en: The last lesson asked why we need rules at all. This one asks how the rules should divide what a society produces. People who agree that shares should be fair turn out to mean at least four different things, and the choice among them decides who pays for schools and hospitals, and who is owed what.
lessons.big_zh: 上一課問的是：我們到底為什麼需要規則。這一課問的是：規則應該怎麼分配一個社會所生產的東西。大家都同意每個人的那一份應該公平；結果他們指的至少是四件不同的事。而在這四者之間怎麼選，決定了誰為學校與醫院付錢，以及誰被欠了什麼。

paras.en: The sense of unfairness is older than philosophy and probably older than our species. In a well-known experiment, two capuchin monkeys in neighboring cages were paid for the same small task. Both were content to receive a slice of cucumber until one of them was given a grape. The other then threw her cucumber back at the experimenter. Children of three behave in much the same way. What takes longer to develop is the ability to state a rule that both sides can accept.
paras.zh: 不公平的感覺比哲學古老，大概也比我們這個物種古老。在一個著名的實驗裡，兩隻住在相鄰籠子裡的捲尾猴，做同一件小事而得到報酬。兩隻本來都滿足於拿到一片小黃瓜，直到其中一隻拿到了一顆葡萄。另一隻於是把她的小黃瓜朝實驗者丟了回去。三歲的孩子，行為也差不多是這樣。需要比較久才發展出來的，是說出一條雙方都能接受的規則的能力。

paras.en: Parents know one such rule. Two children are to share a cake, so one cuts and the other chooses. The child with the knife does not know which piece will be hers, and so she cuts as evenly as she can. No one has to trust anyone’s good will. The fairness comes from a procedure in which a person decides before she knows where she will end up. The most influential theory of justice of the last hundred years is that kitchen rule applied to a whole society.
paras.zh: 做父母的知道一條這樣的規則。兩個孩子要分一塊蛋糕；那就一個切，另一個選。拿刀的孩子不知道哪一塊會是她的，所以她盡可能切得一樣大。誰也不必信任誰的善意。公平來自一個程序：一個人在知道自己最後會落在哪裡之前，就先做了決定。過去一百年裡最有影響力的正義理論，就是把這條廚房裡的規則，用在一整個社會上。

paras.en: Aristotle gave the first careful account. Justice in distribution, he said, is a kind of proportion. Quarrels arise “when either equals have and are awarded unequal shares, or unequals equal shares.” If two people worked on a job and one worked twice as long, equal pay would be unfair. He then identified the real difficulty. Everyone agrees that shares should follow merit, and they do not agree about what merit is. Democrats say it is being a free citizen, oligarchs say wealth, and aristocrats say excellence.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德給出了第一個仔細的說明。他說，分配上的正義是一種比例。爭吵的起因是：「相等的人擁有或得到了不相等的份，或者不相等的人得到了相等的份。」如果兩個人做同一件工作，而其中一人做了兩倍的時間，那麼同酬就是不公平的。接著他指出了真正的困難。人人都同意，份額應該依照「配得」；而他們對「配得」是什麼，意見並不一致。民主派說是自由公民的身分；寡頭派說是財富；貴族派說是卓越。

paras.en: The argument has not changed much since. One side holds that shares should follow contribution, another that they should follow need, and a third that they should simply be equal. Chinese thinkers divided along the same lines. Mencius, arguing against a reformer who wanted goods of the same size sold at the same price whatever their quality, replied that “it is the nature of things to be unequal,” and that to treat them alike would throw the world into confusion. The Daodejing took the other side: the way of Heaven takes from what has too much and gives to what has too little, while the way of men takes from those who have too little to offer to those who have too much.
paras.zh: 從那以後，這場爭論並沒有改變多少。一方主張份額應該跟著貢獻走；另一方說跟著需要走；第三方說就該相等。中國的思想家也沿著同樣的線分開。有一位改革者主張，大小相同的貨物不論品質都賣同一個價錢；孟子反駁他說：「夫物之不齊，物之情也」，把它們一律看待，是把天下搞亂。《道德經》站在另一邊：「天之道，損有餘而補不足。人之道則不然，損不足以奉有餘。」

paras.en: In 1971 the American philosopher John Rawls proposed a way to settle the matter without first agreeing on merit. Imagine that the members of a society meet to choose the principles that will govern it. They know the general facts about economics and human psychology. They do not know anything about themselves: whether they will be rich or poor, clever or slow, healthy or sick, male or female, of which race or which religion. Rawls called this condition the veil of ignorance. Since no one can design rules to favor his own case, whatever is chosen there is fair, for the same reason the cake is fairly cut.
paras.zh: 1971 年，美國哲學家約翰・羅爾斯提出了一個辦法：不必先對「配得」有共識，就能把這件事定下來。想像一個社會的成員聚在一起，要選出將來治理這個社會的原則。他們知道關於經濟與人類心理的一般事實。他們對自己一無所知：自己會是富是窮、聰明還是遲鈍、健康還是多病、是男是女、屬於哪個種族或哪個宗教。羅爾斯把這種狀況稱為「無知之幕」。既然沒有人能設計出偏袒自己那種情況的規則，那麼在那裡選出來的不管是什麼，都是公平的；理由跟蛋糕切得公平是同一個。

paras.en: Rawls argued that people in that position would choose two principles. The first gives everyone the same basic liberties, such as freedom of speech and conscience and the vote. The second allows inequalities of wealth and position on two conditions: the positions must be open to all under fair equality of opportunity, and the inequalities must work to the greatest benefit of the least advantaged. He called this last condition the difference principle. A surgeon may earn more than a porter if paying surgeons more makes the porter better off than he would be under any other arrangement. The reasoning is that of someone who may turn out to be the porter.
paras.zh: 羅爾斯主張，處在那個位置的人會選出兩條原則。第一條給每個人同樣的基本自由，例如言論與良心的自由、投票權。第二條容許財富與地位的不平等，但有兩個條件：那些職位必須在公平的機會平等之下對所有人開放；而那些不平等必須對處境最不利的人最有好處。他把最後這個條件稱為「差異原則」。外科醫師可以賺得比搬運工多，如果付給外科醫師更多錢，會讓搬運工過得比在任何別的安排之下都好。這是一個「最後可能發現自己就是搬運工」的人的推理。

paras.en: Behind the veil lies a claim about luck. Nobody chooses his parents, his native talents, or the country and century of his birth. “No one deserves his greater natural capacity,” Rawls wrote, “nor merits a more favorable starting place in society.” If so, the fortunate may keep the fruits of their gifts only on terms that the unlucky could accept.
paras.zh: 幕的後面，有一個關於運氣的主張。沒有人選擇自己的父母、天生的才能，或是出生的國家與世紀。羅爾斯寫道：「沒有人應得他那較高的天生能力，也沒有人配得一個在社會裡較有利的起點。」如果是這樣，那麼幸運的人要保有他們天賦的果實，就只能依照不幸的人也能接受的條件。

paras.en: Three years later Robert Nozick, a younger colleague of Rawls in the Harvard philosophy department, published the best-known reply. Begin, he said, with whatever distribution you think is just. Call it D1. Now suppose that the basketball star Wilt Chamberlain signs a contract under which twenty-five cents from every ticket goes to him. In the course of a season a million people gladly drop their quarters in a box, and Chamberlain ends up with $250,000, far more than anyone else. The new distribution, D2, no longer fits your pattern. Yet everyone began with a just share and moved to D2 by free choices, so it is hard to see what could make D2 unjust.
paras.zh: 三年後，羅伯特・諾齊克發表了最有名的回應；他是羅爾斯在哈佛哲學系裡較年輕的同事。他說：從任何一個你認為正義的分配開始。叫它 D1。現在假設籃球明星張伯倫簽了一份合約：每張門票有二十五分錢歸他。一個球季下來，有一百萬人高高興興地把他們的二十五分錢丟進一個箱子裡；張伯倫最後有了二十五萬美元，遠比任何人都多。新的分配 D2，不再符合你的模式了。然而每個人都是從正義的一份開始，並且經由自由的選擇走到 D2；那就很難看出，是什麼能讓 D2 不正義。

paras.en: Nozick concluded that justice depends on how holdings came about and that no particular shape of distribution is required. What a person acquired fairly and received by free exchange or gift is his. To preserve any pattern, a government would have to interfere with people’s choices without end. Hume had made the same point in 1751: “Render possessions ever so equal, men’s different degrees of art, care, and industry will immediately break that equality.” Nozick drew a sharper conclusion than Hume did. Taxing earnings, he wrote, is “on a par with forced labor.”
paras.zh: 諾齊克的結論是：正義取決於持有物是怎麼來的；它並不要求任何特定形狀的分配。一個人公平地取得的、以及經由自由交換或餽贈得到的東西，就是他的。要維持任何一種模式，政府就得沒完沒了地干涉人們的選擇。休謨在 1751 年已經說過同樣的話：「就算把財產分得再怎麼平等，人們在技藝、用心與勤勉上的不同程度，也會立刻打破那個平等。」諾齊克得出的結論比休謨更尖銳。他寫道：對勞動所得課稅，「與強迫勞動無異」。

paras.en: Rawls’s reply was that his principles govern the basic structure of society, meaning its tax system, its schools, and its law of property and inheritance. They do not govern each transaction. Within fair background rules, people may trade as they like. Without such rules, Chamberlain’s children start the next game with an advantage they did nothing to earn, and their children with a greater one.
paras.zh: 羅爾斯的回應是：他的原則管的是社會的「基本結構」，也就是它的稅制、學校、財產法與繼承法。它們不管每一筆交易。在公平的背景規則之內，人們愛怎麼交易就怎麼交易。沒有這樣的規則，張伯倫的孩子在下一場比賽開始時，就帶著一份他們什麼都沒做而得來的優勢；而他們的孩子，帶著更大的一份。

paras.en: A second objection accepts the veil and disputes what would be chosen behind it. The economist John Harsanyi had used a similar device some years before Rawls, and he drew the opposite conclusion. A rational person who has an equal chance of being anyone would choose the society with the highest average, and that is the utilitarian answer. To insist on the best possible worst case is to reason like someone who never crosses a street. Rawls answered that the stake here is one’s whole life, with no second draw, and that no one could honestly ask the losers to accept their lot for the sake of a higher average.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁接受了那道幕，而對「幕後會選出什麼」提出異議。經濟學家約翰・海薩尼比羅爾斯早幾年就用過一個類似的設計，而他得出了相反的結論。一個理性的人，如果有同等的機會成為任何一個人，就會選擇平均最高的那個社會；而那是功利主義的答案。堅持「最壞的情況要盡可能地好」，就像一個從來不過馬路的人的推理。羅爾斯回答說：這裡的賭注是一個人的整個人生，沒有第二次抽籤；而沒有人能誠實地要求輸的人，為了一個較高的平均而接受他們的命運。

paras.en: In the 1980s two political scientists, Norman Frohlich and Joe Oppenheimer, tried the experiment on real people. Groups of students were asked to agree on a rule for dividing income before they knew what their own income would be. Almost none chose Rawls’s difference principle, and few chose the highest average. Most groups, in several countries, settled on a mixed rule: guarantee a floor below which no one may fall, and above it let the total grow as large as it can.
paras.zh: 1980 年代，兩位政治學家諾曼・弗羅利希與喬・歐本海默，在真人身上做了這個實驗。他們請一組一組的學生，在知道自己的收入會是多少之前，先對一條分配收入的規則達成共識。幾乎沒有一組選擇羅爾斯的差異原則；選擇最高平均的也很少。在好幾個國家，多數的小組都落在一條混合的規則上：保證一個誰都不會跌破的底線；在那之上，讓總量能長多大就長多大。

paras.en: None of this has ended the argument. What Rawls gave to both sides is a test for our own opinions. Most views about fairness fit the interests of those who hold them. The well-paid tend to believe in desert, and the badly paid in need. The veil asks one question: would you still favor this rule if you did not know which side of it you would be on? It is the question the child with the knife has to answer. A rule that passes may still be mistaken, but it is not merely self-serving.
paras.zh: 這一切都沒有終結這場爭論。羅爾斯給了雙方的，是一個檢驗自己意見的方法。大多數關於公平的看法，都很合乎持有這些看法的人的利益。高薪的人傾向於相信「應得」；低薪的人傾向於相信「需要」。這道幕只問一個問題：如果你不知道自己會落在這條規則的哪一邊，你還會贊成它嗎？這就是拿刀的那個孩子必須回答的問題。通過了的規則仍然可能是錯的；但它不只是為自己打算。

lab.title_en: Try it: choose before you know
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：在知道之前先選
lab.lead_en: A society has five equal groups, from the lowest paid fifth to the highest. Here are four ways it could be arranged. The bars show what a member of each group receives. You will choose three times: once knowing that you are at the top, once knowing that you are at the bottom, and once from behind the veil.
lab.lead_zh: 一個社會有五個人數相等的群體，從收入最低的五分之一到最高的五分之一。這裡有四種安排它的方式。長條顯示每一個群體的成員得到多少。你要選三次：一次知道自己在頂層，一次知道自己在底層，一次在幕的後面。

d.en: Everyone receives the same. The total is the smallest of the four.
d.zh: 每個人得到的一樣多。總量是四個當中最小的。

d.en: Unequal, but the bottom group does better here than in any other plan.
d.zh: 不平等；但最底層的群體在這裡過得比任何別的方案都好。

d.en: A guaranteed minimum, lower than the one above, and a larger total.
d.zh: 有保證的最低收入，比上一個方案低；總量比較大。

d.en: The highest average of the four and the lowest bottom.
d.zh: 四個當中平均最高，底層也最低。

tag.en: Choice 1 of 3 · You are in the top fifth
tag.zh: 第一次選擇 · 你在最高的五分之一

q.en: You know that you are among the highest paid. Which arrangement do you want your society to adopt?
q.zh: 你知道自己屬於收入最高的那一群。你希望你的社會採用哪一種安排？

tag.en: Choice 2 of 3 · You are in the bottom fifth
tag.zh: 第二次選擇 · 你在最低的五分之一

q.en: Now you know that you are among the lowest paid. Which arrangement do you want?
q.zh: 現在你知道自己屬於收入最低的那一群。你要哪一種安排？

tag.zh: 第三次選擇 · 在幕的後面

q.en: Now you do not know. You will be placed in one of the five groups after you choose, and you will live there for the rest of your life. Which arrangement do you want?
q.zh: 現在你不知道。選完之後，你會被放進五個群體當中的一個，並且在那裡過完一輩子。你要哪一種安排？

rowlab.en: Knowing you were at the top
Knowing you were at the bottom

moved.en: Your choice changed with your position. That is the ordinary human case, and it is what Rawls built the veil to remove. Of your three answers only the third was given without knowing whom it would benefit, and so it is the only one that he would count as a judgment about justice.
moved.zh: 你的選擇跟著你的位置變了。這是人之常情；而羅爾斯造那道幕，要拿掉的就是它。你的三個答案當中，只有第三個是在不知道它會對誰有利的情況下給出的；所以只有它，是羅爾斯會算作「關於正義的判斷」的。

same.en: You chose the same arrangement all three times. Either your view of fairness does not depend on where you stand, which is rare, or you were already reasoning from behind the veil in the first two rounds.
same.zh: 你三次都選了同一種安排。要嘛你對公平的看法不取決於你站在哪裡，這很少見；要嘛你在前兩輪就已經從幕的後面推理了。

equal.en: Behind the veil you chose equal shares. Notice that everyone, the bottom group included, would have had more under “Highest floor.” Rawls thought that to refuse a gain for all because others gain more is envy. The philosopher G. A. Cohen defended your choice: a society in which the talented must be paid extra before they will help the rest, he argued, has already given up something that matters.
equal.zh: 在幕的後面，你選了人人相等。請留意：在「底層最高」之下，每個人（包括最底層）本來都會有更多。羅爾斯認為：因為別人得到的更多，就拒絕一個人人都有的好處，那是嫉妒。哲學家柯亨為你的選擇辯護：他主張，一個社會裡有才能的人非得多拿錢才肯幫助其他人，這個社會就已經放棄了某樣要緊的東西。

maximin.en: Behind the veil you chose the highest floor. This is Rawls’s difference principle: inequalities are allowed as far as they raise the position of the worst off, and no further. You reasoned as he said a person would when the stake is a whole life and there is one draw. Harsanyi would say that you gave up a good deal of expected income to insure against one outcome in five.
maximin.zh: 在幕的後面，你選了底層最高。這就是羅爾斯的差異原則：不平等可以容許到它能提高最不利者的位置為止，不能再多。你的推理，正是他說一個人在「賭注是一輩子、而且只抽一次」的時候會有的推理。海薩尼會說：你為了替五分之一的機率買保險，放棄了相當多的預期收入。

floor.en: Behind the veil you chose a floor and then growth. This is what most groups chose when Frohlich and Oppenheimer ran the experiment: protect everyone from the worst, then let the total rise. It is roughly the principle of the modern welfare state. Rawls would ask how you decided where to set the floor, since the person standing on it would have had more under his principle.
floor.zh: 在幕的後面，你選了保底然後成長。弗羅利希與歐本海默做這個實驗時，多數小組選的就是這個：保護每個人不落入最壞的情況，然後讓總量上升。這大致就是現代福利國家的原則。羅爾斯會問你：那條底線放在哪裡，你是怎麼決定的？因為站在底線上的那個人，在他的原則之下本來會有更多。

total.en: Behind the veil you chose the largest total. This is Harsanyi’s answer and the utilitarian one: with an equal chance of each position, this plan gives you the highest expected income. You accepted a one-in-five chance of the lowest place in any of the four plans. Rawls would ask whether you could explain your choice to the person who ends up there.
total.zh: 在幕的後面，你選了總量最大。這是海薩尼的答案，也是功利主義的答案：在每個位置機會相等的情況下，這個方案給你的預期收入最高。你接受了五分之一的機率，落到四個方案當中最低的那個位置。羅爾斯會問：你能不能向最後落在那裡的那個人，解釋你的選擇？

lift.en: The veil lifts. You are in the {pos}. Under the arrangement you chose, you receive {x} thousand a year. Had you chosen “Highest floor,” it would have been {m}. Had you chosen “Largest total,” it would have been {t}.
lift.zh: 幕掀開了。你在{pos}。在你選的安排之下，你一年得到 {x} 千元。如果你選的是「底層最高」，會是 {m}。如果你選的是「總量最大」，會是 {t}。

nozick.en: Nozick would have refused to play. All four plans, he would say, treat income as a pie that someone hands out, when in fact it arrives already belonging to the people who earned it. He would want to know how each person came by what he has, and the bars leave that out.
nozick.zh: 諾齊克會拒絕玩這個遊戲。他會說，這四個方案都把收入當成一塊由某個人來分的餅；而事實上，它來的時候就已經屬於賺到它的人了。他要問的是：每個人手上的東西是怎麼來的？而那些長條並沒有畫出這一點。

argument.lead_en: Rawls’s argument from the original position, in A Theory of Justice. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 羅爾斯在《正義論》裡從「原初立場」出發的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Principles of justice are fair if they would be agreed to in a fair situation of choice.
steps.zh: 正義的原則如果會在一個公平的選擇情境裡被同意，那它們就是公平的。
steps.ob_en: Ronald Dworkin objected that a hypothetical agreement is no agreement at all. That I would have agreed to sell you my painting yesterday for a low price, before I learned its value, gives you no claim on it today.
steps.ob_zh: 德沃金反對說：假設的同意根本不是同意。我昨天在還不知道那幅畫的價值時，本來會同意低價賣給你；這並不讓你今天對它有任何權利。

steps.en: A situation of choice is fair when no one knows the facts that would let him tailor the principles to his own advantage.
steps.zh: 當沒有人知道那些能讓他把原則裁剪得對自己有利的事實時，一個選擇情境就是公平的。
steps.ob_en: Michael Sandel objected that a chooser stripped of family, faith, and community is not a recognizable person, and that what such a being would choose tells us little about what we owe one another.
steps.ob_zh: 桑德爾反對說：一個被剝掉了家庭、信仰與社群的選擇者，不是一個我們認得出來的人；而這樣的一個存在會選什麼，並沒有告訴我們多少「我們彼此欠什麼」。

steps.en: In such a situation, with one’s whole life at stake and no knowledge of the odds, it is rational to make the worst outcome as good as possible.
steps.zh: 在這樣的情境裡，賭上的是一輩子，又不知道機率；這時候理性的做法，是讓最壞的結果盡可能地好。
steps.ob_en: Harsanyi’s objection. With an equal chance of every position, the rational choice is the highest average. The rule Rawls recommends would have us give up large gains for many to secure a small gain for a few.
steps.ob_zh: 這是海薩尼的反駁。在每個位置機會相等的情況下，理性的選擇是最高的平均。羅爾斯建議的那條規則，會要我們為了確保少數人的一點小好處，放棄多數人的大好處。

steps.en: The principles that do this are equal basic liberties for all, fair equality of opportunity, and the difference principle.
steps.zh: 做到這一點的原則是：人人享有平等的基本自由、公平的機會平等，以及差異原則。
steps.ob_en: Amartya Sen asked what exactly is to be equalized. The same income does much less for a person with a disability than for one without. He proposed comparing what people are actually able to do and to be.
steps.ob_zh: 沈恩問：到底要讓什麼相等？同樣的收入，對一位身心障礙者的用處，比對沒有障礙的人小得多。他提議比較的是：人們實際上能夠做什麼、能夠成為什麼。

steps.en: So these are the principles of justice.
steps.zh: 所以，這些就是正義的原則。
steps.ob_en: Nozick rejects the whole form of the argument. Justice concerns how holdings arose. A distribution reached from a just start by just steps is just, whatever its shape.
steps.ob_zh: 諾齊克拒絕這整個論證的形式。正義關乎持有物是怎麼產生的。從一個正義的起點、經由正義的步驟而達到的分配就是正義的，不管它是什麼形狀。

source.work: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book V, chapter 3 (1131a); David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals (1751), Section III, Part II
source.work_zh: 亞里斯多德《尼各馬可倫理學》卷五第三章；休謨《道德原則研究》第三節第二部分
source.tr: Aristotle translated by W. D. Ross (public domain); Hume in the original English and spelling
source.lead_en: The oldest statement of what fairness in distribution is, and the classic warning about trying to enforce equal shares. Rawls’s and Nozick’s books are still in copyright and are quoted only briefly in the essay.
source.lead_zh: 關於「分配上的公平是什麼」最古老的陳述；以及關於「試圖強制執行均分」的經典警告。羅爾斯與諾齊克的書仍在版權期內，只在課文裡簡短引用。

passages.en: If they are not equal, they will not have what is equal, but this is the origin of quarrels and complaints—when either equals have and are awarded unequal shares, or unequals equal shares. Further, this is plain from the fact that awards should be ‘according to merit’; for all men agree that what is just in distribution must be according to merit in some sense, though they do not all specify the same sort of merit, but democrats identify it with the status of freeman, supporters of oligarchy with wealth (or with noble birth), and supporters of aristocracy with excellence. The just, then, is a species of the proportionate.
passages.zh: 如果人是不相等的，他們就不會擁有相等的東西；而這正是爭吵與抱怨的來源：要嘛是相等的人擁有並且得到了不相等的份，要嘛是不相等的人得到了相等的份。再者，從「獎賞應當『依照配得』」這個事實，這一點也很清楚；因為所有的人都同意，分配上的正義必須在某種意義上依照配得，雖然他們指的並不都是同一種配得：民主派把它等同於自由人的身分，寡頭制的支持者把它等同於財富（或高貴的出身），貴族制的支持者把它等同於卓越。那麼，正義就是合乎比例的東西的一種。
passages.note_en: Aristotle is speaking of the distribution of honors and offices in a city as much as of money. His formula is still the one everyone uses: treat like cases alike and different cases differently. The dispute is over which differences count.
passages.note_zh: 亞里斯多德談的，是一個城邦裡榮譽與職位的分配，不只是金錢。他的公式至今仍然是人人在用的那一個：相同的情況相同對待，不同的情況不同對待。爭議在於：哪些差異算數。

passages.ref: An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, III.ii
passages.en: Render possessions ever so equal, men’s different degrees of art, care, and industry will immediately break that equality. Or if you check these virtues, you reduce society to the most extreme indigence; and instead of preventing want and beggary in a few, render it unavoidable to the whole community. The most rigorous inquisition too is requisite to watch every inequality on its first appearance; and the most severe jurisdiction, to punish and redress it.
passages.zh: 就算把財產分得再怎麼平等，人們在技藝、用心與勤勉上的不同程度，也會立刻打破那個平等。或者，如果你壓抑這些美德，你就把社會降到最極端的貧困；你並沒有防止少數人的匱乏與行乞，反而使它成為整個社群無可避免的事。此外，還需要最嚴密的審查，來監視每一個剛剛出現的不平等；以及最嚴厲的司法權，來懲罰並矯正它。
passages.note_en: Hume grants a few lines earlier that a rule of equality would be highly useful if it could be kept. His objection is practical. Nozick’s Chamberlain argument is this paragraph turned into a story, with a claim about rights added.
passages.note_zh: 休謨在前面幾行承認：平等的規則如果守得住，會非常有用。他的反對是實務上的。諾齊克的張伯倫論證，就是把這一段變成一個故事，再加上一個關於權利的主張。

items.o_en: People deserve what they earn by hard work. The veil hides exactly the facts that justify unequal rewards.
items.o_zh: 人應得他們靠努力工作賺來的東西。那道幕遮住的，恰恰是讓不平等的報酬有正當理由的事實。
items.r_en: Rawls replied that the capacity for effort is itself shaped by a fortunate family and upbringing, so that desert cannot be the foundation. Many readers find this his least convincing step, since it seems to leave nothing that a person can take credit for. A moderate position is open: effort deserves reward, and the size of the reward that a given effort commands in the market is largely luck.
items.r_zh: 羅爾斯回答說：努力的能力本身，就是由幸運的家庭與教養塑造的；所以「應得」不能當作基礎。許多讀者覺得這是他最沒有說服力的一步，因為它似乎沒有留下任何一個人可以居功的東西。有一個溫和的立場可以採取：努力值得回報；而某一份努力在市場上換得到多大的回報，大體上是運氣。

items.o_en: If taxing earnings is forced labor, as Nozick says, then every modern state is a slave owner. That cannot be right.
items.o_zh: 如果像諾齊克說的，對所得課稅就是強迫勞動，那麼每一個現代國家都是奴隸主。這不可能對。
items.r_en: Critics answer that a worker who is taxed may choose his occupation, his hours, and whether to work at all, which a forced laborer may not. They add that Nozick’s theory requires holdings to have been justly acquired in the first place, and that almost no actual holding has a clean history. Nozick admitted that past injustice might call for large corrections, and he later wrote that the libertarian position he had defended was seriously inadequate.
items.r_zh: 批評者回答：一個被課稅的工作者，可以選擇自己的職業、工時，以及到底要不要工作；被強迫勞動的人不能。他們還補充：諾齊克的理論要求持有物一開始就是正義地取得的；而現實中幾乎沒有哪一份持有物有乾淨的歷史。諾齊克承認，過去的不正義也許需要大幅的矯正；他後來還寫道，他辯護過的那個自由至上主義立場有嚴重的不足。

items.o_en: Fairness is about how we treat one another. A society could satisfy Rawls’s principles and still be full of contempt for those at the bottom.
items.o_zh: 公平關乎我們怎麼對待彼此。一個社會可以滿足羅爾斯的原則，而仍然對底層的人充滿輕蔑。
items.r_en: Elizabeth Anderson, who studied under Rawls, pressed this point. The aim of equality, she argued, is that people stand as equals, with no one made to bow. Compensating the unlucky for their bad luck is a different thing. A check that comes with pity may worsen the insult. Rawls would largely agree. He listed the social bases of self-respect among the goods to be distributed, and called it perhaps the most important of them.
items.r_zh: 曾是羅爾斯學生的伊莉莎白・安德森，力主這一點。她主張：平等的目標，是人們以平等者的身分站在一起，沒有人被迫低頭。為不幸的人的壞運氣提供補償，是另一回事。一張帶著憐憫而來的支票，可能使羞辱更深。羅爾斯大體上會同意。他把「自尊的社會基礎」列在要分配的那些善當中，並且說它也許是其中最重要的一項。

said.claim: 「不患寡而患不均」 (Confucius: do not worry that there is little, worry that it is unequally shared)
said.claim_zh: 「不患寡而患不均」（孔子：不怕少，只怕分得不平均）
said.verdict_en: His words; the usual reading is doubtful
said.verdict_zh: 是他的話；通行的讀法有疑問
said.en: The line is in the Analects (16.1) and is often quoted as a call for equal shares. The context is a planned attack by the powerful Ji family on a small dependent state, and Confucius is rebuking two disciples who serve the family. The full sentence reads: “不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安.” Zhu Xi’s standard commentary glosses 寡 as “few people” and 均 as “each receiving his proper portion,” which is proportion in Aristotle’s sense. It does not mean equal shares. The Han scholar Dong Zhongshu quotes the saying in a different form, “不患貧而患不均,” and draws a conclusion that sounds like Rawls: let the rich have enough to show their rank without becoming arrogant, and the poor enough to sustain life without falling into distress.
said.zh: 這句話在《論語》裡（〈季氏〉第一章），常被引用來主張均分。它的脈絡是：有權勢的季氏打算攻打一個附庸小國顓臾；孔子是在責備兩個為季氏做事的弟子。完整的句子是：「不患寡而患不均，不患貧而患不安。」朱熹的《集注》把「寡」解作「民少」，把「均」解作「各得其分」；那是亞里斯多德意義下的比例。它的意思不是均分。漢代的董仲舒引這句話時，是另一個樣子：「不患貧而患不均」；而他由此得出的結論，聽起來很像羅爾斯：「使富者足以示貴而不至於驕，貧者足以養生而不至於憂。」

terms.d_en: Justice in the division of benefits and burdens among the members of a society.
terms.d_zh: 在一個社會的成員之間，分配利益與負擔時的正義。

terms.d_en: Rawls’s imagined situation in which people choose principles of justice without knowing their own place in society.
terms.d_zh: 羅爾斯所設想的情境：人們在不知道自己在社會裡的位置的情況下，選擇正義的原則。

terms.d_en: The condition of not knowing one’s own class, talents, sex, race, or beliefs when choosing principles.
terms.d_zh: 在選擇原則時，不知道自己的階級、才能、性別、種族或信念的那種狀況。

terms.d_en: Inequalities are just only if they work to the greatest benefit of the least advantaged.
terms.d_zh: 不平等只有在對處境最不利者最有好處的時候，才是正義的。

terms.d_en: The rule of choosing the option whose worst outcome is better than the worst outcome of any other.
terms.d_zh: 一條選擇的規則：選那個「最壞結果」比其他任何選項的最壞結果都好的選項。

terms.d_en: What a person deserves on account of what he has done or what he is like. Pronounced like dessert.
terms.d_zh: 一個人因為他做過的事或他的為人而應當得到的東西。發音跟 dessert（甜點）一樣。

terms.d_en: Nozick’s view that a holding is just if it was justly acquired and justly transferred.
terms.d_zh: 諾齊克的看法：一份持有物如果是正義地取得、正義地轉讓的，它就是正義的。

terms.d_en: In the Analects, a fitting distribution. The word later came to mean equal.
terms.d_zh: 在《論語》裡，指合宜的分配。這個字後來才有了「相等」的意思。

vocab.eg: She decides before she knows where she will end up.
vocab.eg_zh: 她在知道自己最後會落在哪裡之前，就先做了決定。

vocab.zh: 把事情定下來、解決爭議
vocab.eg: Rawls proposed a way to settle the matter without first agreeing on merit.
vocab.eg_zh: 羅爾斯提出了一個辦法：不必先對「配得」有共識，就能把這件事定下來。

vocab.eg: No one can tailor the principles to his own advantage.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人能把原則裁剪得對自己有利。

vocab.eg: Nozick thought taxing earnings was on a par with forced labor.
vocab.eg_zh: 諾齊克認為，對所得課稅與強迫勞動無異。

vocab.eg: He would want to know how each person came by what he has.
vocab.eg_zh: 他要問的是：每個人手上的東西是怎麼來的。

vocab.eg: One’s whole life is at stake, and there is no second draw.
vocab.eg_zh: 賭上的是一輩子，而且沒有第二次抽籤。

vocab.eg: No one could honestly ask the losers to accept their lot.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人能誠實地要求輸的人接受他們的命運。

vocab.eg: A rule that passes the test is not merely self-serving.
vocab.eg_zh: 通過檢驗的規則，不只是為自己打算。

vocab.zh: 居功、把…算作自己的功勞
vocab.eg: The argument seems to leave nothing that a person can take credit for.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個論證似乎沒有留下任何一個人可以居功的東西。

vocab.zh: 力主某個論點、緊追不放
vocab.eg: Anderson pressed this point against her own teacher.
vocab.eg_zh: 安德森對自己的老師力主這一點。

quiz.q: Why does “one cuts, the other chooses” produce a fair division?
options: The cutter does not know which piece she will get, so she has reason to cut evenly.
The chooser is always the younger child.
A parent checks the pieces afterward.
Both children are naturally generous.

quiz.q: What, according to Aristotle, do people disagree about in distribution?
options: Which kind of merit should count.
Whether shares should follow merit at all.
Whether justice matters.
How to do arithmetic with ratios.

quiz.q: What does the difference principle permit?
options: Inequalities that work to the greatest benefit of the least advantaged.
Any inequality that arises from free exchange.
No inequality of any kind.
Inequalities that raise the average.

quiz.q: What is the Wilt Chamberlain example meant to show?
options: That free choices will upset any pattern of distribution, so a pattern can be kept only by constant interference.
That athletes are paid too much.
That ticket prices should be regulated.
That people behind the veil would choose equality.

quiz.q: What did most groups choose in Frohlich and Oppenheimer’s experiments?
options: A guaranteed floor, with the total as large as possible above it.
The difference principle.
Strictly equal incomes.
The highest average with no floor.

write.en: Think of a rule you support, at work, in your school, or in national politics. Apply the veil: would you still support it if you did not know which side of it you would be on? Write 150 words.
write.zh: 想一條你支持的規則：在工作上、在你的學校裡，或是在國家的政治裡。用那道幕檢驗它：如果你不知道自己會落在它的哪一邊，你還會支持它嗎？寫 150 個字。

write.en: A teacher has one scholarship to give. One student has the highest marks, one has worked the hardest, and one comes from the poorest family. Who should receive it? Defend your answer against the two you rejected.
write.zh: 一位老師有一份獎學金可以給。一個學生成績最高，一個最用功，一個來自最窮的家庭。應該給誰？為你的答案辯護，回應你沒有選的那兩個。

write.en: Rawls says that no one deserves his natural talents. Does it follow that no one deserves what he makes with them? Argue for or against in 200 words.
write.zh: 羅爾斯說，沒有人應得自己天生的才能。由此能不能推出：沒有人應得他用這些才能做出來的東西？用 200 個字論證贊成或反對。

paras.en: The Buddha gave no theory of distribution, but one discourse reads like a parable about the floor. A king is told the duties of a just ruler, one of which is: “Provide money to the penniless in the realm.” He keeps order and neglects this one duty. Poverty spreads, and a man steals. Brought before the king, he says, “Your Majesty, I can’t survive.” The king gives him money. Others hear of it and steal as well, so the king turns to executions, and people arm themselves. The discourse sums up: “From not providing money to the penniless, poverty became widespread. When poverty was widespread, theft became widespread. When theft was widespread, swords became widespread.” The text does not say that everyone must have the same. It says that a society which lets some fall below what is needed to live will pay for it in violence, and that relief after the theft comes too late.
paras.zh: 佛陀沒有給出分配的理論；但有一部經，讀起來像一則關於「底線」的寓言。有人告訴一位國王，正直的統治者有哪些職責；其中一條是：「國內有貧窮的人，要給他們資財。」他維持了秩序，卻忽略了這一條。貧窮蔓延開來，有一個人偷了東西。他被帶到國王面前時說：「大王，我活不下去。」國王給了他錢。其他人聽說了，也去偷；於是國王改用處決，而人們開始武裝自己。這部經總結說：「因為不把資財給貧窮的人，貧窮就蔓延了。貧窮蔓延，偷盜就蔓延。偷盜蔓延，刀劍就蔓延。」經文並沒有說每個人擁有的必須一樣多。它說的是：一個社會如果任由一些人跌到維持生活所需的水準之下，就會以暴力來償付；而等到偷了才救濟，就太遲了。

paras.en: Within the monastic community the rule was closer to equality. Among the six qualities that hold a community together, the Buddha lists this: a monk “shares without reservation any material things they have gained by legitimate means, even the food placed in the alms-bowl.” Chinese Buddhism calls this 利和同均, harmony in the equal sharing of gains. The Buddha also rejected the oldest criterion of desert in India, which was birth: “You’re not a lowlife by birth, nor by birth are you a brahmin.” On one point, though, the tradition differs sharply from Rawls. For Rawls the circumstances of birth are a lottery and no one deserves his place. On the Buddhist account they are connected with past action. That teaching was never meant to excuse the fortunate. The king’s duty in the story does not depend on how the poor came to be poor (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18, D19).
paras.zh: 在僧團內部，規則更接近平等。在使一個團體和合的六種特質當中，佛陀列了這一條：比丘對於如法得來的任何物品，「乃至缽中所得的食物」，都毫無保留地與同修共用。漢傳佛教稱之為「利和同均」。佛陀也拒絕了印度最古老的那個「配得」的標準，也就是出身：「不因出身而成為賤民，不因出身而成為婆羅門。」不過在一點上，這個傳統與羅爾斯有鮮明的不同。對羅爾斯來說，出生的境遇是一場抽籤，沒有人應得他的位置。照佛教的說法，它們與過去的行為有關。這個教導從來就不是要為幸運的人開脫。在那個故事裡，國王的職責並不取決於窮人是怎麼變窮的（佛法與西方哲學 D18、D19）。

terms: harmony in the equal sharing of gains

further.t: Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics, Book V
further.n_en: Chapters 1 to 5 are the source of nearly every later distinction about justice.
further.n_zh: 第一到第五章，是後來幾乎每一個關於正義的區分的源頭。

further.t: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Morals, Section III
further.n_en: “Of Justice.” Short, and readable in one sitting.
further.n_zh: 〈論正義〉。短，一次就讀得完。

further.t: John Rawls, A Theory of Justice (1971), sections 1–4, 11–13, and 24
further.n_en: About fifty pages give the whole argument. The rest of the book defends it.
further.n_zh: 大約五十頁就給出了整個論證。書的其餘部分是在為它辯護。

further.t: Robert Nozick, Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974), chapter 7
further.n_en: The Chamberlain argument is on pages 160 to 164. The link is to an overview.
further.n_zh: 張伯倫論證在第 160 到 164 頁。連結是一篇概述。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Original Position”
further.n_en: A careful account of the veil and of the debate with Harsanyi.
further.n_zh: 對那道幕、以及與海薩尼的爭論的仔細說明。

further.t: 《論語・季氏》第一章；董仲舒《春秋繁露・度制》
further.n_en: The saying about 均 in its setting, and the earliest reading of it.
further.n_zh: 關於「均」的那句話的脈絡，以及對它最早的解讀。

lessons.title: How Free Should We Be?
lessons.blurb_en: Seat belts, drugs, hateful pamphlets, and a contract to sell yourself. Mill’s one very simple principle, the cases that strain it, Berlin’s two kinds of freedom, and Laozi’s ruler who governs by leaving people alone.
lessons.blurb_zh: 安全帶、毒品、充滿仇恨的小冊子，還有一份把自己賣掉的契約。彌爾那條「非常簡單的原則」、讓它吃力的那些案例、柏林的兩種自由，以及老子那位「不去管人民」的統治者。
lessons.big_en: The last two lessons gave reasons for having rules and for sharing things fairly. Both give other people power over us. This lesson asks where that power must stop: which parts of a life are nobody’s business but one’s own, and why.
lessons.big_zh: 前兩課給出了要有規則、要公平分配的理由。兩者都讓別人有了支配我們的權力。這一課問的是：那個權力必須在哪裡停下來？一個人的生活裡，哪些部分除了他自己，誰也管不著？為什麼？

paras.en: A government that can stop a thief can also stop a reader, a drinker, or a preacher. Every society therefore has to decide which of the things people do it will leave alone. The decisions are familiar ones. May the law require a motorcyclist to wear a helmet? May it forbid an adult to take a drug that harms only himself, or a newspaper to print what most people find disgusting? For most of history the answer was that rulers may forbid whatever is bad for the people or offensive to the gods. In 1859 John Stuart Mill argued, in a short book called On Liberty, that this answer is wrong.
paras.zh: 一個能攔住小偷的政府，也能攔住一個讀書的人、喝酒的人或傳道的人。所以每一個社會都得決定：人們做的事情當中，哪些它不去管。這些決定都是我們熟悉的。法律可以規定騎機車的人戴安全帽嗎？可以禁止一個成年人服用只傷害他自己的藥物嗎？可以禁止報紙刊登多數人覺得噁心的東西嗎？在歷史上大部分的時間裡，答案是：凡是對人民不好的、或冒犯神明的，統治者都可以禁止。1859 年，約翰・史都華・彌爾在一本叫做《論自由》的小書裡主張：這個答案是錯的。

paras.en: Mill proposed what he called “one very simple principle.” It reads: “the only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over any member of a civilised community, against his will, is to prevent harm to others. His own good, either physical or moral, is not a sufficient warrant.” We may argue with a man who is ruining his health, plead with him, or avoid his company. We may not force him. “Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.”
paras.zh: 彌爾提出了他所謂的「一條非常簡單的原則」。它是這樣寫的：「對一個文明社群的任何成員，可以違反他的意願而正當地行使權力的唯一目的，是防止對他人的傷害。他自己的好處，不論是身體上的還是道德上的，都不是充分的理由。」對一個正在毀掉自己健康的人，我們可以跟他爭論、懇求他，或是避開他。我們不可以強迫他。「對於他自己，對於他自己的身體與心靈，個人是最高的主權者。」

paras.en: Two features of the principle are easy to miss. It applies to social pressure as well as to law. Mill feared what he called the tyranny of the majority, by which he meant the power of neighbors and employers to make an unusual person’s life impossible, and he thought it reached further than any police. And the principle gives a necessary condition for interference. Harm to others makes interference permissible, but whether to interfere remains a further question. Competition harms the losing shopkeeper, and no one proposes to forbid it.
paras.zh: 這條原則有兩個特點很容易漏看。它既適用於法律，也適用於社會壓力。彌爾害怕他所謂的「多數的暴政」；他指的是鄰居與雇主讓一個不尋常的人活不下去的那種力量，而他認為那比任何警察都管得更深。此外，這條原則給的是干涉的必要條件。對他人的傷害，使干涉成為可以容許的；至於要不要干涉，仍然是進一步的問題。競爭傷害了輸掉的那位店主，而沒有人提議禁止競爭。

paras.en: Mill was a utilitarian, and he does not appeal to natural rights. He argues that liberty makes human life go better. The case is clearest for speech. If we silence an opinion, it may be true, and we lose the chance of “exchanging error for truth.” No one who silences is infallible. If the opinion is false, we still lose, because a truth that is never challenged comes to be held “as a dead dogma, not a living truth.” People repeat it without knowing why it is so. “He who knows only his own side of the case, knows little of that.” And most opinions in dispute are partly true, so that each side needs the other to correct it. Hence his most quoted sentence: “If all mankind minus one, were of one opinion, and only one person were of the contrary opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person, than he, if he had the power, would be justified in silencing mankind.”
paras.zh: 彌爾是功利主義者，他並不訴諸自然權利。他論證的是：自由使人的生活過得更好。這個論證在言論上最清楚。如果我們壓制一個意見，它可能是真的；那我們就失去了「以真理換掉錯誤」的機會。沒有哪一個壓制別人的人是不會錯的。如果那個意見是假的，我們還是有損失；因為一個從來不受挑戰的真理，會被人當作「死的教條，而不是活的真理」來持有。人們複述它，而不知道它為什麼是這樣。「只知道自己這一邊的理由的人，對這一邊也所知甚少。」而大多數有爭議的意見，都有一部分是真的；所以每一邊都需要另一邊來糾正它。於是有了他最常被引用的那個句子：「假如全人類除了一個人之外，都持同一個意見，而只有那一個人持相反的意見；那麼人類要那一個人沉默，並不比那一個人（假如他有權力的話）要全人類沉默更為正當。」

paras.en: The same reasoning covers ways of living. No one knows in advance what kind of life is best for human beings, so there should be “different experiments of living.” A person who lets custom choose for him needs no faculty, Mill says, but “the ape-like one of imitation.” Choosing for oneself is how judgment and character are exercised, and a people that is not allowed to choose will stop improving.
paras.zh: 同樣的推理也涵蓋生活的方式。沒有人事先知道哪一種生活對人最好；所以應該有「不同的生活實驗」。彌爾說，一個讓習俗替他選擇的人，除了「像猿猴那樣的模仿能力」之外，不需要任何別的能力。自己做選擇，判斷力與品格才得到鍛鍊；而一個不被允許選擇的民族，會停止進步。

paras.en: The principle is simple to state and hard to apply, and Mill knew it. He distinguished an opinion from an incitement. The view that corn dealers starve the poor may be printed freely, but it may be punished “when delivered orally to an excited mob assembled before the house of a corn-dealer.” He allowed one case of protecting a person from himself. A man who sees another about to step onto an unsafe bridge may seize him, since he “does not desire to fall into the river.” And he held that the law should refuse to enforce a contract by which a person sells himself into slavery: “The principle of freedom cannot require that he should be free not to be free.”
paras.zh: 這條原則說起來簡單，用起來困難；彌爾自己知道。他把「意見」與「煽動」分開。「糧商害窮人挨餓」這個看法可以自由刊印；但是「當它被口頭傳達給一群聚集在某位糧商門前的激動群眾時」，就可以懲罰。他容許一種「保護一個人免於傷害自己」的情況。看見別人正要踏上一座不安全的橋，可以把他一把抓住；因為他「並不想要掉進河裡」。他還主張，法律應該拒絕執行一份把自己賣為奴隸的契約：「自由的原則，不能要求他有『不自由』的自由。」

paras.en: Critics have pressed two points. The first is that almost nothing harms only oneself. The drinker has a family and the injured rider needs a hospital bed. Mill answered that we should punish the neglect of a definite duty, such as failing to support one’s children, and leave the drinking alone. The second is that the word harm is asked to do too much work. Should deep offense count as harm? Mill said no for opinions, but he accepted laws against public indecency. In the 1950s the English judge Patrick Devlin argued that a society may defend its shared morality as it defends itself against treason. The legal philosopher H. L. A. Hart replied, in Mill’s spirit, that disgust is no proof of harm.
paras.zh: 批評者緊追兩點。第一：幾乎沒有什麼事是只傷害自己的。喝酒的人有家人；受傷的騎士需要一張病床。彌爾回答說：我們應該懲罰的是對某個明確義務的疏忽，例如不扶養自己的孩子；至於喝酒，就別去管它。第二：「傷害」這個詞被要求做太多的事了。深深的冒犯算不算傷害？就意見而言，彌爾說不算；但他接受禁止公然猥褻的法律。1950 年代，英國法官派屈克・德富林主張：一個社會可以捍衛它共有的道德，就像它防衛叛國一樣。法哲學家哈特以彌爾的精神回應說：厭惡並不是傷害的證明。

paras.en: In 1958 Isaiah Berlin pointed out that Mill’s question is only one of two that go by the name of freedom. Negative liberty is the absence of interference: how many doors are open to me. Positive liberty is self-mastery: who is in control. An addict whom no one stops has the first and lacks the second. Berlin thought the positive idea the more dangerous in politics. Once a ruler claims to know what my true self wants, he can coerce me and call it liberation, and Rousseau had spoken of forcing a man to be free. Others replied that negative liberty alone is a thin thing to someone too poor or too ignorant to walk through any of the open doors.
paras.zh: 1958 年，以撒・柏林指出：頂著「自由」這個名字的問題有兩個，彌爾的問題只是其中之一。消極自由是沒有干涉：有多少扇門對我開著。積極自由是自我主宰：誰在掌控。一個沒有人攔阻的成癮者，有第一種而沒有第二種。柏林認為，在政治上，積極的那個觀念比較危險。一旦統治者宣稱他知道我「真正的自我」要什麼，他就可以強制我，而把這叫做解放；盧梭就說過要「強迫一個人自由」。其他人則回應：對一個太窮或太無知、以致走不進任何一扇敞開的門的人來說，只有消極自由，是很單薄的東西。

paras.en: China has an older tradition of governing by leaving alone. The Daodejing says that the more prohibitions there are, the poorer the people become, and that the more laws are published, the more thieves there are. Its sage says: “I do nothing, and the people transform themselves.” Yet Laozi is no Mill. The same book advises the ruler to empty the people’s minds and fill their bellies, and praises the ancients who kept the people simple and did not enlighten them. Laozi wanted a government that did not meddle and a people that did not argue. Mill wanted the argument above all. The Legalist Han Fei drew the opposite conclusion from both: in the state of an enlightened ruler there are no books, and “the law is the teaching.” The disagreement among the three is one that every government still has to settle.
paras.zh: 中國有一個更古老的「以不管來治理」的傳統。《道德經》說：「天下多忌諱，而民彌貧」；「法令滋彰，盜賊多有」。它的聖人說：「我無為而民自化。」然而老子並不是彌爾。同一本書勸統治者「虛其心，實其腹」，並且稱讚古人「非以明民，將以愚之」。老子要的，是一個不多事的政府，與一群不爭辯的人民。彌爾最想要的，偏偏是爭辯。法家的韓非則從兩人那裡得出相反的結論：「明主之國，無書簡之文，以法為教。」這三個人之間的分歧，是每一個政府到今天都還得做出決定的。

lab.title_en: Try it: you are the lawmaker
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：你來立法
lab.lead_en: Nine cases. For each, decide whether the law should forbid it or leave it alone. After each answer you will see how Mill decided and why. At the end you will see which principles you were using.
lab.lead_zh: 九個案例。每一個，請決定法律應該禁止它，還是不去管它。每次作答之後，你會看到彌爾怎麼判、為什麼。最後你會看到你自己實際上在用哪些原則。

t.en: An adult rides a motorcycle without a helmet.
t.zh: 一個成年人騎機車不戴安全帽。

why.en: Mill would leave it alone. The risk falls on the rider, and his own good “is not a sufficient warrant.” We may warn him and argue with him. Nearly every modern state disagrees with Mill here.
why.zh: 彌爾會不去管。風險落在騎士自己身上；而他自己的好處「不是充分的理由」。我們可以警告他、跟他爭論。在這一點上，幾乎每一個現代國家都不同意彌爾。

t.en: A newspaper prints an article arguing that a certain minority is a danger to the country. It does not call for violence.
t.zh: 一家報紙刊登一篇文章，主張某個少數族群對國家是個危險。它沒有號召暴力。

why.en: Mill would leave it alone. This is the opinion about corn dealers “simply circulated through the press.” A false and hateful opinion should be answered, and answering it keeps the truth alive. Many democracies now have laws against hate speech, on the ground that such writing harms the standing of its targets.
why.zh: 彌爾會不去管。這就是那個關於糧商的意見，「僅僅經由報刊流傳」。一個錯誤而充滿仇恨的意見，應該被回應；而回應它，使真理保持活力。現在許多民主國家有禁止仇恨言論的法律，理由是這樣的文字傷害了它所針對的人的地位。

t.en: The same writer shouts the same words to an angry crowd gathered outside a family’s home.
t.zh: 同一位作者，對著聚集在某戶人家門外的憤怒群眾，喊出同樣的話。

why.en: Mill would forbid it. The words are the same and the act is different: “even opinions lose their immunity” when the circumstances make them “a positive instigation to some mischievous act.”
why.zh: 彌爾會禁止。話是一樣的，行為卻不同：當情境使意見成為「對某個害人行為的積極煽動」時，「就連意見也失去了它的豁免」。

t.en: An adult uses a dangerous drug alone, at home.
t.zh: 一個成年人獨自在家裡使用一種危險的藥物。

why.en: Mill would leave it alone, and would require that the drug be sold with a clear label. If the user neglects his children, he should be punished for the neglect.
why.zh: 彌爾會不去管，並且會要求這種藥物販售時要有清楚的標示。如果使用者疏於照顧他的孩子，他應該因為那個疏忽而受罰。

t.en: A factory saves money by pouring its waste into the river that a town drinks from.
t.zh: 一家工廠為了省錢，把廢料倒進一條全鎮飲用的河裡。

why.en: Mill would forbid it. This is the plain case of harm to others, and no one’s liberty includes it.
why.zh: 彌爾會禁止。這是「傷害他人」最明白的情況；沒有誰的自由包括這個。

t.en: Two adults live together, by their own free choice, in a way that most of their neighbors think immoral. No one else is affected.
t.zh: 兩個成年人出於自己的自由選擇，以一種多數鄰居認為不道德的方式共同生活。沒有任何別人受到影響。

why.en: Mill would leave it alone. That others find a way of life wrong is, for him, no harm to them. This is the point on which Hart defended Mill against Devlin.
why.zh: 彌爾會不去管。別人覺得某種生活方式是錯的，對彌爾來說，並不是對他們的傷害。哈特就是在這一點上，為彌爾對抗德富林。

t.en: A man walks naked down a busy shopping street.
t.zh: 一個男人赤身裸體，走在一條熱鬧的商店街上。

why.en: Mill, perhaps surprisingly, would allow the law to forbid it. Acts done in public that violate good manners come, he says, “within the category of offences against others.” Critics think this hard to square with what he says about offensive opinions.
why.zh: 也許出人意料：彌爾會容許法律禁止它。他說，在公共場合做的、違反禮儀的行為，屬於「對他人的侵犯」這一類。批評者認為，這跟他對「冒犯人的意見」的說法很難一致。

t.en: An adult, fully informed and under no pressure, signs a contract to become another person’s slave for life.
t.zh: 一個成年人，在資訊充分、沒有壓力的情況下，簽了一份契約，要終身做另一個人的奴隸。

why.en: Mill would have the law refuse to enforce it: “The principle of freedom cannot require that he should be free not to be free.” Nozick, more consistent or less wise, thought a free society would allow it.
why.zh: 彌爾會讓法律拒絕執行它：「自由的原則，不能要求他有『不自由』的自由。」諾齊克比較一貫，或者說比較不明智；他認為一個自由的社會會容許它。

t.en: A father decides that his ten-year-old daughter will not go to school or be taught at home.
t.zh: 一位父親決定，他十歲的女兒不上學，也不在家裡受教育。

why.en: Mill would forbid it. He calls it almost self-evident that the state “should require and compel the education” of every child. A child is another person, and the father’s liberty covers only his own life.
why.zh: 彌爾會禁止。他說，國家「應當要求並強制」每一個孩子受教育，這幾乎是不證自明的。孩子是另一個人；父親的自由只涵蓋他自己的生活。

score.en: You decided {n} of the 9 cases as Mill did.
score.zh: 九個案例當中，你有 {n} 個判得跟彌爾一樣。

pat.en: You forbade something for the person’s own good. This is paternalism, and it is the thing Mill’s principle was written to exclude. You have the law of most countries on your side. The question Mill would put to you is where it stops: if helmets, why not diet, and if diet, why not opinions that are bad for us?
pat.zh: 你為了當事人自己的好處而禁止了某件事。這叫做家長主義；彌爾的原則，就是為了排除它而寫的。大多數國家的法律站在你這一邊。彌爾會問你的問題是：它在哪裡停下來？如果可以管安全帽，為什麼不管飲食？如果可以管飲食，為什麼不管那些對我們不好的意見？

off.en: You forbade speech that calls for no violence because of what it says. You are using an offense principle, or a wider idea of harm than Mill’s. Jeremy Waldron has defended this: hate speech tells its targets that they are not safe as equal members of society. Mill would ask who you trust to decide which opinions are too hateful to be heard.
off.zh: 你因為一段言論的內容而禁止了它，雖然它沒有號召暴力。你用的是一條「冒犯原則」，或者是一個比彌爾更寬的「傷害」概念。傑瑞米・沃德倫為這個立場辯護過：仇恨言論告訴它所針對的人，他們作為社會平等的一員並不安全。彌爾會問：你信任誰來決定，哪些意見因為太充滿仇恨而不該被聽見？

mor.en: You forbade a private way of life because it is thought immoral. This is legal moralism, Devlin’s position. Its difficulty is the historical record: the list of things once punished on this ground includes most of what we now call freedom of religion.
mor.zh: 你因為一種私人的生活方式被認為不道德，而禁止了它。這是法律道德主義，也就是德富林的立場。它的困難在歷史紀錄：曾經以這個理由被懲罰的事情，列出來，包括了我們今天稱為「宗教自由」的大部分內容。

lib.en: You left alone something that Mill would forbid. Where the case was the slavery contract, you are more of a libertarian than Mill. Where it was the crowd, the river, or the child, you have allowed one person’s freedom to cover harm to another, which no theory of liberty defends.
