lib.zh: 你放過了一件彌爾會禁止的事。如果那是賣身契，那麼你比彌爾更接近自由至上主義。如果那是群眾、河流或孩子的案例，那麼你讓一個人的自由涵蓋了對另一個人的傷害；沒有任何一種自由理論為這一點辯護。

mill.en: You drew every line where Mill drew it. Before you conclude that you agree with him, look again at the two cases where he forbids: the naked man and the slavery contract. Neither follows easily from “harm to others,” and they are where his critics start.
mill.zh: 你每一條線都劃在彌爾劃的地方。在你斷定自己同意他之前，請再看一次他主張禁止的那兩個案例：裸體的人與賣身契。這兩者都不容易從「對他人的傷害」推出來；而他的批評者就是從這裡下手的。

close.en: Mill’s principle is best used as a question that anyone who proposes to forbid something must answer: whom does this harm, apart from the person doing it? Laws that cannot answer it have a bad record.
close.zh: 彌爾的原則，最好的用法是把它當作一個問題；凡是提議禁止某件事的人，都必須回答它：除了做這件事的人自己，這傷害了誰？答不出這個問題的法律，紀錄並不好。

argument.lead_en: Mill’s argument for freedom of opinion, from chapter 2 of On Liberty. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 彌爾在《論自由》第二章為意見自由所做的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Any opinion we suppress is true, false, or partly true.
steps.zh: 我們所壓制的任何一個意見，要嘛是真的，要嘛是假的，要嘛部分是真的。
steps.ob_en: Few dispute this. The objections concern what follows in each case.
steps.ob_zh: 很少有人對這一步有異議。反駁在於每一種情況接下來會如何。

steps.en: If it is true, suppressing it deprives us of a truth, and we can never be certain that it is false.
steps.zh: 如果它是真的，壓制它就使我們失去了一個真理；而我們永遠無法確定它是假的。
steps.ob_en: We act on uncertain beliefs all the time. A government that cannot be certain may still be confident enough to ban an advertisement for a useless medicine. Mill replies that the confidence is earned only where the belief has been open to challenge.
steps.ob_zh: 我們隨時都在依據不確定的信念行動。一個無法確定的政府，仍然可以有足夠的把握，去禁止一則無效藥品的廣告。彌爾回答：只有在信念一直開放給人挑戰的地方，那份把握才是賺來的。

steps.en: If it is false, suppressing it lets the truth go unchallenged, and an unchallenged truth becomes a dead dogma.
steps.zh: 如果它是假的，壓制它就讓真理不受挑戰；而不受挑戰的真理會變成死的教條。
steps.ob_en: This assumes that truth gains from the contest. Where falsehood is cheaper to produce and more pleasant to believe, repetition can beat correction. Mill himself called it a “pleasant falsehood” that truth always triumphs over persecution.
steps.ob_zh: 這假定了真理會從這場較量中得益。在謊言製造起來比較便宜、相信起來比較愉快的地方，重複可以勝過更正。彌爾自己就說過，「真理總是戰勝迫害」是一個「令人愉快的謊言」。

steps.en: If it is partly true, only free discussion can separate the true part from the false.
steps.zh: 如果它部分是真的，那麼只有自由的討論，才能把真的部分與假的部分分開。
steps.ob_en: The step imagines discussion as a seminar. Critics note that some speech aims to drive others out of the discussion, and that protecting it may leave fewer voices heard.
steps.ob_zh: 這一步把討論想像成一場研討會。批評者指出：有些言論的目的，就是要把別人趕出討論；而保護它，可能使被聽見的聲音更少。

steps.en: So opinions should never be suppressed for what they say.
steps.zh: 所以，絕不應該因為意見的內容而壓制它。
steps.ob_en: The argument is about consequences, so it holds only as far as the consequences do. A defender of liberty who wants it to hold in all cases needs a right, and Mill gave up that ground at the start.
steps.ob_zh: 這個論證談的是後果；所以後果走到哪裡，它才成立到哪裡。一位希望它在所有情況下都成立的自由捍衛者，需要的是一項權利；而彌爾從一開始就放棄了那塊地。

source.work: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty (1859), chapter 1; Daodejing, chapter 57
source.work_zh: 彌爾《論自由》第一章；《道德經》第五十七章
source.tr: Mill in the original English and spelling (public domain); the Daodejing translated for this series from the Wang Bi text
source.lead_en: The paragraph that states the harm principle, and the chapter in which Laozi’s sage explains why he does nothing.
source.lead_zh: 陳述傷害原則的那一段；以及老子的聖人解釋自己為什麼「無為」的那一章。

passages.en: That principle is, that the sole end for which mankind are warranted, individually or collectively, in interfering with the liberty of action of any of their number, is self-protection. That the only purpose for which power can be rightfully exercised over any member of a civilised community, against his will, is to prevent harm to others. His own good, either physical or moral, is not a sufficient warrant. He cannot rightfully be compelled to do or forbear because it will be better for him to do so, because it will make him happier, because, in the opinions of others, to do so would be wise, or even right. […] In the part which merely concerns himself, his independence is, of right, absolute. Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign.
passages.zh: 那條原則就是：人類不論是個別地還是集體地，有理由干涉他們當中任何一個人的行動自由，唯一的目的是自我防衛。對一個文明社群的任何成員，可以違反他的意願而正當地行使權力的唯一目的，是防止對他人的傷害。他自己的好處，不論是身體上的還是道德上的，都不是充分的理由。不能因為這樣做對他比較好、因為這會使他更幸福、因為在別人看來這樣做是明智的甚至是對的，就正當地強迫他去做或不做某件事。……在只關乎他自己的那一部分，他的獨立性在權利上是絕對的。對於他自己，對於他自己的身體與心靈，個人是最高的主權者。
passages.note_en: The next sentences, which are quoted less often, exclude children and what Mill calls “backward states of society,” for which he thought despotism legitimate. He worked for thirty-five years for the East India Company. Readers must decide whether the exception is a flaw in the principle or only in the man.
passages.note_zh: 接下來的幾句比較少被引用：它們把孩子排除在外，也把彌爾所謂「落後的社會狀態」排除在外；他認為對後者，專制是正當的。他在東印度公司工作了三十五年。讀者必須判斷：這個例外是原則的瑕疵，還是只是這個人的瑕疵。

passages.en: The more prohibitions there are in the world, the poorer the people become. The more sharp tools the people have, the more disordered the state. The more skills men acquire, the more strange things appear. The more laws and orders are made known, the more thieves and robbers there are. Therefore the sage says: I do nothing, and the people transform themselves. I love stillness, and the people set themselves right. I undertake nothing, and the people grow rich of themselves. I have no desires, and the people return of themselves to simplicity.
passages.zh: 天下多忌諱，而民彌貧；民多利器，國家滋昏；人多伎巧，奇物滋起；法令滋彰，盜賊多有。故聖人云：「我無為而民自化，我好靜而民自正，我無事而民自富，我無欲而民自樸。」
passages.note_en: The four results the sage hopes for are order, uprightness, wealth, and simplicity. Diversity of opinion is not among them. Laozi’s case against interference is that it makes things worse. Mill’s is that a person has a claim to run his own life even when he runs it badly.
passages.note_zh: 聖人期望的四個結果是：化、正、富、樸。意見的多樣並不在其中。老子反對干涉的理由是：它使事情更糟。彌爾的理由是：一個人有資格經營自己的人生，就算他經營得不好。

items.o_en: People do not choose as Mill imagines. They are hasty, ill-informed, and weak-willed, and they regret their choices. A state that knows this and does nothing is negligent.
items.o_zh: 人並不像彌爾想像的那樣做選擇。他們倉促、資訊不足、意志薄弱，而且為自己的選擇後悔。一個明知如此卻什麼也不做的國家，是怠忽職守。
items.r_en: This is the modern case for paternalism, and psychology supports its premise. Mill’s bridge example already allows interference where a person lacks information and there is no time to warn him. What he resists is the step from “people make mistakes” to “officials should choose for them,” since officials are people too, with less knowledge of the life in question and less interest in it. A middle course keeps the choice and changes the setting: warnings, waiting periods, and defaults that can be refused.
items.r_zh: 這是現代為家長主義提出的理由；心理學支持它的前提。彌爾的那個橋的例子，已經容許在「一個人缺乏資訊、又來不及警告他」的時候加以干涉。他所抗拒的，是從「人會犯錯」跨到「官員應該替他們選」的那一步；因為官員也是人，而且對那個人的生活知道得更少、在乎得也更少。有一條中間路線：保留選擇，改變情境——警語、等待期，以及可以拒絕的預設選項。

items.o_en: The harm principle protects the strong. A worker “freely” accepts a dangerous job because the alternative is hunger. Leaving people alone means leaving them to whoever has power over them.
items.o_zh: 傷害原則保護的是強者。一個工人「自由地」接受一份危險的工作，因為另一個選項是挨餓。不去管人，就是把他們留給任何一個對他們握有權力的人。
items.r_en: This is the objection from positive liberty, and Mill half accepted it. He supported laws limiting working hours and requiring education, and in later life called himself a socialist of a kind. The honest reply is that On Liberty answers one question, when the majority may coerce an individual. It does not address the question of what a person needs in order to be able to use his freedom. A complete view has to answer both.
items.r_zh: 這是從積極自由而來的反駁；彌爾接受了一半。他支持限制工時與強制教育的法律，晚年還自稱是某一種社會主義者。誠實的回應是：《論自由》回答的是一個問題，也就是多數人什麼時候可以強制一個個人。它沒有處理另一個問題：一個人需要什麼，才有能力使用他的自由？一個完整的看法，兩個都得回答。

items.o_en: Mill’s ideal of the independent individual who questions everything is one way of life among others. A society that prizes harmony and respect for elders is not thereby less civilized.
items.o_zh: 彌爾的理想——凡事都質疑的獨立個人——只是許多種生活方式當中的一種。一個重視和諧與敬老的社會，並不因此就比較不文明。
items.r_en: The objection has force, and it has been made from Confucian and from religious standpoints. Mill can concede much of it. The harm principle does not require anyone to be an individualist. It forbids making people conform by force. A person may live by tradition, and in a free society his doing so is a choice he could have refused. Whether a tradition remains the same thing once it is one option among many is a real question, and Mill, who wanted every custom tested, would not have minded the answer.
items.r_zh: 這個反駁有力量；儒家的與宗教的立場都提出過它。彌爾可以承認其中的大部分。傷害原則並不要求任何人做個人主義者。它禁止的是用強制力使人順從。一個人可以依循傳統而活；在一個自由的社會裡，他這樣做，是一個他本來可以拒絕的選擇。一個傳統一旦成為眾多選項之一，是否還是原來那個東西，是個真問題；而希望每一種習俗都受到檢驗的彌爾，不會介意那個答案。

said.claim: “You can’t shout fire in a crowded theater.” (the limit of free speech in law)
said.claim_zh: 「你不能在擁擠的戲院裡大喊失火。」（法律上言論自由的界限）
said.verdict_zh: 引錯了，而且從來不是法律
said.en: The line comes from Justice Oliver Wendell Holmes in Schenck v. United States (1919). What he wrote was: “The most stringent protection of free speech would not protect a man in falsely shouting fire in a theatre and causing a panic.” The word “crowded” is not there, and the two conditions that are there, “falsely” and “causing a panic,” are usually dropped. The sentence was an illustration. It was not the ruling. The ruling upheld the imprisonment of a man who had distributed leaflets against military conscription, which is exactly the kind of political opinion Mill wanted protected. The United States Supreme Court replaced the Schenck standard in 1969 with a narrower one much closer to Mill’s corn dealer: speech may be punished only where it is directed to inciting imminent lawless action and is likely to produce it.
said.zh: 這句話出自大法官奧利佛・溫德爾・霍姆斯，在「申克訴合眾國案」（1919）裡。他寫的是：「對言論自由最嚴格的保護，也不會保護一個在戲院裡謊稱失火、並造成恐慌的人。」原文沒有「擁擠」這個詞；而原文有的兩個條件，「謊稱」與「造成恐慌」，通常被拿掉了。這個句子是一個比方。它並不是判決。那個判決維持了對一個人的監禁；他散發的是反對徵兵的傳單，而這恰恰是彌爾想要保護的那一種政治意見。美國最高法院在 1969 年以一個較窄的標準取代了申克案的標準，那個標準更接近彌爾的糧商：只有在言論旨在煽動「立即的不法行為」、而且很可能產生它的時候，才可以懲罰。

terms.d_en: Power may be used over a person against his will only to prevent harm to others.
terms.d_zh: 只有為了防止對他人的傷害，才可以違反一個人的意願而對他行使權力。

terms.d_en: Interfering with a person’s choices for his own good.
terms.d_zh: 為了一個人自己的好處，而干涉他的選擇。

terms.d_en: The view that the law may forbid conduct because it is immoral, whether or not it harms anyone.
terms.d_zh: 一種看法：法律可以因為某種行為不道德而禁止它，不管它有沒有傷害任何人。

terms.d_en: The oppression of individuals by prevailing opinion, through law or through social pressure.
terms.d_zh: 主流意見經由法律或社會壓力，對個人的壓迫。

terms.d_en: Freedom as the absence of interference by others.
terms.d_zh: 把自由理解為：沒有他人的干涉。

terms.d_en: Freedom as self-mastery: being in control of one’s own life.
terms.d_zh: 把自由理解為自我主宰：掌控自己的人生。

terms.d_en: Urging others to an unlawful act in circumstances where they are likely to do it.
terms.d_zh: 在別人很可能照做的情境下，慫恿他們去做不法的事。

terms.d_en: Laozi’s term for acting without forcing, and for governing without meddling.
terms.d_zh: 老子的用語：不強求地行動，不多事地治理。

vocab.eg: Every society has to decide what it will leave alone.
vocab.eg_zh: 每一個社會都得決定，哪些事它不去管。

vocab.eg: Which parts of a life are nobody’s business but one’s own?
vocab.eg_zh: 一個人的生活裡，哪些部分除了他自己誰也管不著？

vocab.eg: We may plead with him. We may not force him.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們可以懇求他。我們不可以強迫他。

vocab.eg: Two questions go by the name of freedom.
vocab.eg_zh: 頂著「自由」這個名字的問題有兩個。

vocab.eg: Laozi wanted a government that did not meddle.
vocab.eg_zh: 老子要的是一個不多事的政府。

vocab.eg: This is hard to square with what he says about offensive opinions.
vocab.eg_zh: 這跟他對「冒犯人的意見」的說法很難一致。

vocab.eg: Critics have pressed two points.
vocab.eg_zh: 批評者緊追兩點。

vocab.eg: You drew every line where Mill drew it.
vocab.eg_zh: 你每一條線都劃在彌爾劃的地方。

vocab.eg: Such laws are defended on the ground that hate speech harms its targets.
vocab.eg_zh: 這類法律的辯護理由是：仇恨言論傷害了它所針對的人。

vocab.eg: Laws that cannot answer the question have a bad record.
vocab.eg_zh: 答不出這個問題的法律，紀錄並不好。

quiz.q: According to the harm principle, when may power be used over a person against his will?
options: Only to prevent harm to others.
Whenever it is for his own good.
Whenever the majority disapproves of his conduct.
Never.

quiz.q: Why does Mill think a false opinion should not be silenced?
options: Because a truth that is never challenged becomes a dead dogma.
Because no opinion is really false.
Because false opinions are harmless.
Because the speaker has a natural right to be heard.

quiz.q: What does the corn dealer example distinguish?
options: Publishing an opinion from using it to incite a mob.
Rich traders from poor ones.
Spoken words from written ones.
Harm to oneself from harm to others.

quiz.q: What is the difference between negative and positive liberty?
options: Negative liberty is not being interfered with. Positive liberty is being in control of one’s own life.
Negative liberty is harmful and positive liberty is good.
Negative liberty belongs to individuals and positive liberty to nations.
They are two names for the same thing.

quiz.q: How does Laozi’s case for leaving people alone differ from Mill’s?
options: Laozi argues that interference makes things worse and does not value open debate. Mill values the debate itself.
Laozi wants more laws and Mill wants fewer.
Laozi defends free speech and Mill does not.
There is no difference.

write.en: Choose one law in your country that protects adults from themselves, such as a helmet or seat belt law. Defend it against Mill, or defend Mill against it, in 150 words.
write.zh: 選一條你們國家裡保護成年人免於傷害自己的法律，例如安全帽或安全帶的規定。為它辯護以對抗彌爾，或者為彌爾辯護以對抗它。寫 150 個字。

write.en: Mill thought social pressure a greater threat to liberty than law. Describe a case you have seen in which opinion, with no law involved, kept someone from living as he or she wished. Was the pressure justified?
write.zh: 彌爾認為，社會壓力對自由的威脅比法律還大。描述一個你見過的情況：沒有任何法律介入，輿論卻使某個人無法照自己的意願生活。那個壓力有正當理由嗎？

write.en: “The principle of freedom cannot require that he should be free not to be free.” Explain what Mill means, and say whether the same reasoning would justify forbidding addictive drugs.
write.zh: 「自由的原則，不能要求他有『不自由』的自由。」解釋彌爾的意思；並且說明，同樣的推理能不能為「禁止會上癮的藥物」提供理由。

paras.en: On Mill’s question the Buddha is close to Mill. He founded no state and gave laypeople no laws. The five precepts are undertaken by choice and are not enforced by anyone. He told the Kālāmas not to go by tradition or scripture or by the thought “The ascetic is our respected teacher,” and to accept a teaching only “when you know for yourselves” what it leads to. He held that no one can be made good from outside: “You yourselves must do the work, the Realized Ones just show the way.” And again: “Purity and impurity are personal matters, no one can purify another.” A Buddhist argument for the harm principle would rest on this last point. Virtue that is forced on a person has no value as virtue.
paras.zh: 在彌爾的那個問題上，佛陀很接近彌爾。他沒有建立國家，也沒有給在家人立法。五戒是自願受持的，沒有任何人來強制執行。他告訴卡拉瑪人：不要因為傳統、經典，或因為想到「這位沙門是我們尊敬的老師」就接受；只有「當你們自己知道」一個教導會導向什麼的時候，才接受它。他主張沒有人能從外面被弄成善的：「你們必須自己努力；如來只是指路的人。」又說：「清淨與不清淨都在於自己；沒有人能使另一個人清淨。」佛教為傷害原則提出的論證，會以最後這一點為根據。被強加在一個人身上的德行，作為德行沒有任何價值。

paras.en: On Berlin’s second question the Buddha goes much further than Mill. Mill calls a person free when no one stops him from doing what he desires. The Buddha asks whether the desire is free. One discourse puts it this way: “The world is wanting, insatiable, the slave of craving.” A person driven by craving, anger, and confusion has no outside master and is still unfree. The word for the goal of the path, vimutti, means release. This is positive liberty in its strongest form, and it avoids the danger Berlin saw in the idea. No one can be forced into it, since the release is something a person has to see for himself. A verse of the Dhammapada says, “One is indeed the lord of oneself, for who else would be one’s lord?” (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18).
paras.zh: 在柏林的第二個問題上，佛陀走得比彌爾遠得多。彌爾說，沒有人攔著一個人去做他想要的事，這個人就是自由的。佛陀問的是：那個「想要」是自由的嗎？有一部經這樣說：「世間不足，不知滿足，是渴愛的奴隸。」一個被貪、瞋、癡驅使的人，外面沒有主人，卻仍然不自由。這條道路的目標叫做 vimutti，意思是解脫。這是最強形式的積極自由；而它避開了柏林在這個觀念裡看到的危險。沒有人能被強迫進入它，因為解脫是一個人必須自己看見的東西。《法句經》有一首偈說：「自己才是自己的依怙，還有誰能做自己的依怙？」（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

further.t: John Stuart Mill, On Liberty (1859)
further.n_en: Five chapters. Read 1 and 2 first, then the hard cases in 5.
further.n_zh: 五章。先讀第一、二章，再讀第五章的難題。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Positive and Negative Liberty”
further.n_en: Berlin’s distinction and the debate that followed.
further.n_zh: 柏林的區分，以及隨後的爭論。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Paternalism”
further.n_en: The modern argument about protecting people from themselves.
further.n_zh: 關於「保護人免於傷害自己」的現代論辯。

further.t: Schenck v. United States, 249 U.S. 47 (1919)
further.n_en: Holmes’s opinion, four pages long, with the sentence about the theater.
further.n_zh: 霍姆斯的意見書，四頁長，有關於戲院的那個句子。

further.t: 《道德經》第三、十七、五十七、六十五、八十章
further.n_en: The political chapters, including the two that sit badly with a liberal reading.
further.n_zh: 談政治的幾章，包括跟自由主義式的解讀很不相容的那兩章。

further.t: Kesamutti Sutta (To the Kālāmas), AN 3.65
further.n_en: The Buddha on what to accept and why.
further.n_zh: 佛陀談該接受什麼、為什麼。

lessons.title: Who Should Rule?
lessons.blurb_en: Plato’s ship with a deaf captain and a mutinous crew, Mencius on the people and the tyrant, Han Fei’s system built for ordinary rulers, and a jury you can run to see when many heads are better than one.
lessons.blurb_zh: 柏拉圖那艘船：耳背的船長與叛變的水手；孟子談人民與暴君；韓非為平庸的君主打造的制度；以及一個你可以自己操作的陪審團，看看「人多」什麼時候勝過「一個人」。
lessons.big_en: Rules have to be made and enforced by someone. The oldest question in political philosophy is who that should be: the wisest, the best born, the strongest, or everyone. This lesson follows the answers, and then looks at a suggestion that the question itself was badly put.
lessons.big_zh: 規則總得由某個人來訂、來執行。政治哲學最古老的問題是：那該是誰？最有智慧的、出身最好的、最強的，還是每一個人？這一課跟著那些答案走一遍，然後看一個提議：這個問題本身，也許就問錯了。

essay.h_en: A ship with a deaf captain

paras.en: Plato grew up in a democracy and watched it put his teacher to death by a majority vote. In the Republic he describes what he saw as a ship. The captain, who stands for the people, is bigger and stronger than anyone on board, but he is a little deaf, does not see well, and knows little of navigation. The sailors quarrel over the helm. Each thinks he has a right to steer, though none has learned how, and they are ready to cut to pieces anyone who says that steering can be taught. They flatter the captain, drug him, and take over the ship, eating and drinking the stores. The one person on board who has studied the seasons, the sky, the stars, and the winds they call a stargazer and a good-for-nothing.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖在一個民主政體裡長大，並且看著它以多數決處死了他的老師。在《理想國》裡，他把他所見到的描述成一艘船。船長代表人民：他比船上任何人都高大強壯，但是有點耳背，眼力不好，對航海所知不多。水手們為了舵而爭吵。每個人都認為自己有權掌舵，雖然沒有一個人學過；而且誰要是說掌舵是可以教的，他們就準備把誰砍成碎片。他們奉承船長，給他下藥，接管了船，吃喝著船上的存糧。船上唯一研究過季節、天空、星辰與風的那個人，被他們叫做看星星的人、沒用的東西。

paras.en: The parable carries an argument. Ruling is a skill, like navigation or medicine. No one chooses a ship’s pilot by a show of hands. So political power should go to those who know, and Plato draws the conclusion that made him notorious: “Until philosophers are kings, or the kings and princes of this world have the spirit and power of philosophy … cities will never have rest from their evils.” His rulers are to be trained for decades, and they are to own no property and have no families of their own, so that nothing can tempt them from the common good.
paras.zh: 這個比喻帶著一個論證。治理是一門技藝，就像航海或醫術。沒有人用舉手表決來選領航員。所以政治權力應該交給有知識的人；而柏拉圖得出了那個使他聲名狼藉的結論：「除非哲學家成為國王，或者這個世界上的國王與君主擁有哲學的精神與力量……否則城邦永遠不能擺脫它們的禍患。」他的統治者要受幾十年的訓練；他們不得擁有財產，也不得有自己的家庭，這樣就沒有什麼能引誘他們離開公共的善。

paras.en: Aristotle, Plato’s student, found two weaknesses. A pilot knows how to reach a port, but the passengers decide where the ship is going, and political disputes are mostly about destinations. And he doubted that the few are always better judges than the many. “The many, of whom each individual is but an ordinary person, when they meet together may very likely be better than the few good … just as a feast to which many contribute is better than a dinner provided out of a single purse.” Each brings a share of good sense, and together they become like one man with many hands and many senses.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖的學生亞里斯多德，找到了兩個弱點。領航員知道怎麼到達一個港口；但是船要開往哪裡，是由乘客決定的；而政治上的爭論，大多是關於目的地的。此外，他懷疑少數人是否總是比多數人更好的判斷者。「眾人當中，每一個個別的人都只是普通人；但是當他們聚在一起的時候，很可能比那少數的優秀者更好……正如一場由許多人湊成的宴席，勝過由一個人的荷包辦出來的一頓飯。」每個人帶來一份見識；合在一起，他們就像一個有許多隻手、許多感官的人。

paras.en: Aristotle also changed the question. He sorted governments by two tests: how many rule, and for whose benefit. Rule by one, by a few, or by many can each be sound when it aims at the common good, and each has a corrupt twin that serves the rulers alone. Monarchy decays into tyranny and aristocracy into oligarchy. On this view the number of rulers matters less than whose interest they serve, and the best safeguard is that the law should govern, with officials as its servants.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德也改變了這個問題。他用兩個標準來分類政體：有多少人統治？為了誰的利益？一人統治、少數人統治、多數人統治，只要以公共的善為目標，各自都可以是健全的；而各自都有一個只為統治者自己服務的腐化的孿生兄弟。君主制敗壞成僭主制；貴族制敗壞成寡頭制。照這個看法，統治者的人數，沒有「他們為誰的利益服務」那麼要緊；而最好的保障是由法律來統治，官員則是法律的僕人。

essay.h_en: The people are the most important

paras.en: Chinese thinkers did not debate democracy, since no one had seen one. They debated what makes a ruler legitimate, and Mencius gave the boldest answer: “The people are the most important, the altars of the state come next, and the ruler is the least.” A king asked him whether it was true that a minister had once killed his sovereign, the tyrant Zhou. Mencius replied that a man who destroys humaneness and rightness is a mere fellow. “I have heard of the execution of a fellow named Zhou. I have not heard of the killing of a sovereign.” A ruler who abuses the people has lost the mandate and is no longer a ruler.
paras.zh: 中國的思想家並沒有辯論過民主，因為沒有人見過。他們辯論的是：什麼使一位統治者具有正當性？而孟子給了最大膽的答案：「民為貴，社稷次之，君為輕。」齊宣王問他：臣子殺了自己的君主（暴君紂），有這回事嗎？孟子回答：「賊仁者謂之賊，賊義者謂之殘。殘賊之人謂之一夫。聞誅一夫紂矣，未聞弒君也。」一位虐待人民的統治者，已經失去了天命，不再是統治者。

paras.en: Mencius even describes consultation. Before promoting or executing a man, the ruler should not listen to his courtiers or his ministers alone. Only “when the people of the state all say” so should he look into the matter himself, and then act. The people are to be heard, and it is still the ruler who decides. Two thousand years later Huang Zongxi pressed the idea further: in antiquity the world was the host and the ruler the guest, and now the ruler is the host and the world the guest, so that “the one who does the greatest harm to the world is the ruler.”
paras.zh: 孟子甚至描述了徵詢。在提拔或處決一個人之前，君主不該只聽左右或大夫的話。「國人皆曰賢，然後察之；見賢焉，然後用之。」人民要被聽見；而做決定的仍然是君主。兩千年後，黃宗羲把這個觀念推得更遠：「古者以天下為主，君為客……今也以君為主，天下為客」；所以「為天下之大害者，君而已矣」。

essay.h_en: Do not wait for a sage

paras.en: Han Fei attacked both Plato’s hope and Mencius’s from another side. Sage kings like Yao and Shun, he observed, appear once in a thousand generations, and so do monsters like Jie and Zhou. Most rulers are in between. A theory of government that depends on a sage will give a thousand generations of disorder for one of order. What is needed is a system that an average man can operate: published laws, fixed rewards and punishments, and the authority of the throne. “Holding to the law and occupying the position of power, he governs well.” To long for the ancient kings is to be like the farmer of Song who saw a rabbit break its neck on a tree stump, put down his plow, and waited by the stump for another.
paras.zh: 韓非從另一邊，同時攻擊了柏拉圖的希望與孟子的希望。他觀察到：像堯、舜那樣的聖王，一千世才出一個；像桀、紂那樣的怪物也是。大多數的君主在兩者之間。一個依賴聖人的治國理論，會給出一千世的亂，換一世的治。需要的是一個普通人就能操作的制度：公布的法律、固定的賞罰，以及君位的權威。「抱法處勢則治。」嚮往古代的聖王，就像那個宋國的農夫：他看見一隻兔子在樹樁上撞斷了脖子，就放下犁，守在樹樁旁邊等下一隻。

paras.en: The idea of designing for ordinary officeholders is a modern one, and it is the starting point of every written constitution. But Han Fei’s system binds everyone except the man at the top. The law “does not favor the noble,” and yet it is the ruler’s instrument, so that nothing in it protects the people from him.
paras.zh: 「為普通的在位者設計制度」是一個很現代的觀念；每一部成文憲法都從這裡出發。但是韓非的制度約束了每一個人，只除了最上面的那一位。法「不阿貴」，然而它是君主的工具；所以其中沒有任何東西保護人民不受他的侵害。

paras.en: In 1945 Karl Popper argued that the whole debate had asked the wrong question. “Who should rule?” invites the answer “the best,” and then every faction claims to be the best. He proposed to ask this in its place: “How can we so organize political institutions that bad or incompetent rulers can be prevented from doing too much damage?” On this view the value of democracy is that it lets a government be removed without bloodshed. It makes no claim that the people are wise. Popper’s question takes over Han Fei’s premise that rulers will usually be mediocre and reaches the opposite conclusion.
paras.zh: 1945 年，卡爾・波普主張：整場辯論都問錯了問題。「該由誰來治理？」招來的答案是「最好的人」；然後每一個派別都宣稱自己就是最好的。他提議改問：「我們怎樣組織政治制度，才能防止壞的或無能的統治者造成太大的損害？」照這個看法，民主的價值在於：它讓一個政府可以不流血地被換掉。它並沒有宣稱人民是有智慧的。波普的問題接收了韓非的前提，也就是統治者通常是平庸的；而得出了相反的結論。

paras.en: There is also a positive argument for the many, and it is mathematical. In 1785 the Marquis de Condorcet proved that if each voter is even slightly more likely than not to be right on a question, and they judge independently, then the majority becomes almost certain to be right as the number of voters grows. The same proof shows that if each is slightly more likely to be wrong, a large majority is almost certain to be wrong. Aristotle’s feast, in other words, depends on what the guests bring, and on their not all copying the same dish. The interactive below lets you try it.
paras.zh: 也有一個支持「多數人」的正面論證，而它是數學的。1785 年，孔多塞侯爵證明了：如果每一位投票者在一個問題上答對的機率，哪怕只比一半高一點點，而且他們各自獨立判斷；那麼隨著投票人數增加，多數決幾乎必然是對的。同一個證明也顯示：如果每個人答錯的機率比一半高一點點，那麼龐大的多數幾乎必然是錯的。換句話說，亞里斯多德的那場宴席，取決於客人帶來了什麼，也取決於他們不是全都抄同一道菜。下面的互動讓你自己試試看。

lab.title_en: Try it: Condorcet’s jury
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：孔多塞的陪審團
lab.lead_en: A question has a right answer. Each voter has some chance of getting it right. Set that chance, set the number of voters, and see how often the majority is right. Then let the voters copy one another.
lab.lead_zh: 一個問題有正確答案。每一位投票者有某個機率答對。設定那個機率，設定投票人數，看看多數決有多常是對的。然後，讓投票者互相抄。

lp.zh: 每位投票者答對的機率

lc.en: Voters who copy one loud voice
lc.zh: 跟著同一個大嗓門走的投票者

res_ok.en: This vote: {r} right, {w} wrong. The majority got it right.
res_ok.zh: 這一次：{r} 人對，{w} 人錯。多數決答對了。

res_no.en: This vote: {r} right, {w} wrong. The majority got it wrong.
res_no.zh: 這一次：{r} 人對，{w} 人錯。多數決答錯了。

t.en: Make each voter slightly better than a coin, and add voters.
t.zh: 讓每位投票者比丟銅板好一點點，然後增加人數。

v.en: Found. With each voter only a little better than chance and enough of them, the majority is right nearly every time. No expert is this reliable. This is Aristotle’s feast with a proof attached, and it is the strongest argument for deciding by vote.
v.zh: 找到了。每位投票者只比碰運氣好一點點，而人數夠多的時候，多數決幾乎每次都對。沒有哪位專家這麼可靠。這就是附上了證明的亞里斯多德的宴席，也是「用投票來決定」最強的論證。

t.en: Make each voter slightly worse than a coin, and add voters.
t.zh: 讓每位投票者比丟銅板差一點點，然後增加人數。

v.en: Found. The same arithmetic now runs the other way. If people are a little more likely to be wrong, because the question is technical or because they have been misled, a large electorate is almost certain to be wrong, and a single random person would do better. Plato’s sailors are this case.
v.zh: 找到了。同樣的算術，現在往反方向跑。如果人們答錯的機率高一點點（因為問題很專門，或者因為他們被誤導了），那麼龐大的選民幾乎必然是錯的；隨便挑一個人還比較好。柏拉圖的水手就是這種情況。

t.en: Give the voters a good chance of being right, add many of them, and then make most of them copy.
t.zh: 給投票者不錯的答對機率，增加到很多人，然後讓其中大多數人用抄的。

v.en: Found. When most voters follow one voice, the crowd is only as good as that voice, however many they are. A thousand people who copy make one judgment. Condorcet’s theorem needs independence, and this is why Mill’s argument for dissent and a free press belongs to the case for democracy.
v.zh: 找到了。當大多數投票者跟著同一個聲音走的時候，不管人有多少，這群人只跟那個聲音一樣好。一千個用抄的人，做出的是一個判斷。孔多塞的定理需要獨立性；這就是為什麼彌爾為異議與新聞自由所做的論證，屬於支持民主的理由的一部分。

q.en: All three found. What does the theorem show?
q.zh: 三件事都找到了。這個定理說明了什麼？

t.en: That the many should decide
t.zh: 應該由多數人決定

v.en: It shows this on two conditions: that voters are more often right than wrong on the question, and that they think for themselves. A democrat who relies on the theorem has taken on a duty to care about schools, honest information, and disagreement. The theorem also applies only where there is a right answer. Much of politics is about what people want, and there the case for voting is a different one, namely that each person’s interests should count.
v.zh: 它在兩個條件之下說明了這一點：投票者在這個問題上對的時候比錯的時候多；而且他們自己思考。一位倚賴這個定理的民主派，就承擔了一份責任：要關心學校、誠實的資訊，以及不同的意見。這個定理也只適用於有正確答案的地方。政治有很大一部分是關於人們「想要什麼」；在那裡，支持投票的理由是另一個，也就是每個人的利益都應該算數。

t.en: That those who know should decide
t.zh: 應該由懂的人決定

v.en: It shows that on a question where most people are likely to be wrong, counting heads is a bad method. That much Plato had right. It does not show who the knowers are or what will keep them honest. Experts copy one another too, and a small group has less protection against a shared error than a large one. Popper’s question remains: if they turn out to be wrong, how do we remove them?
v.zh: 它說明了：在一個多數人很可能答錯的問題上，數人頭是個壞方法。這一點柏拉圖說對了。它並沒有說明懂的人是誰，或者是什麼讓他們保持誠實。專家也互相抄；而一個小團體對「共同的錯誤」的防護，比一個大團體少。波普的問題還在：如果他們結果是錯的，我們怎麼換掉他們？

argument.lead_en: Plato’s argument for rule by those who know, from Republic V–VI. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 柏拉圖在《理想國》卷五、卷六為「由有知識的人統治」所做的論證。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Ruling well is a skill that requires knowledge of what is good for the city.
steps.zh: 治理得好是一門技藝；它需要「什麼對城邦是好的」的知識。
steps.ob_en: A navigator knows how to reach a port that others have chosen. In politics the dispute is about the port. There may be no expert knowledge of ends in the way there is of means.
steps.ob_zh: 領航員知道怎麼到達一個別人選定的港口。在政治上，爭議的就是那個港口。關於目的，也許並沒有像關於手段那樣的專家知識。

steps.en: In every other skill we give authority to those who have the knowledge.
steps.zh: 在其他每一門技藝上，我們都把權威交給有那門知識的人。
steps.ob_en: We consult the doctor, and it is still the patient who decides whether to have the operation. Knowing more does not by itself give anyone the right to command. David Estlund calls the mistaken step the “expert/boss fallacy.”
steps.ob_zh: 我們諮詢醫生；而要不要動手術，仍然是病人決定。知道得比較多，本身並不給任何人發號施令的權利。大衛・艾斯特倫把這錯誤的一步稱為「專家／老闆謬誤」。

steps.en: Most people lack this knowledge. A few, after long training, can acquire it.
steps.zh: 大多數人缺乏這種知識。少數人經過長期的訓練，可以獲得它。
steps.ob_en: Even if such people exist, the rest of us have no reliable way to pick them out, and everyone who wants power will claim to be one. Aristotle adds that “the guest will judge better of a feast than the cook.”
steps.ob_zh: 就算這樣的人存在，我們其餘的人也沒有可靠的方法把他們挑出來；而每一個想要權力的人，都會宣稱自己是其中之一。亞里斯多德還補充：「一場宴席好不好，客人判斷得比廚子好。」

steps.en: Those who have it will rule for the common good if they are denied property and family.
steps.zh: 擁有這種知識的人，只要不讓他們有財產與家庭，就會為公共的善而統治。
steps.ob_en: This is the step that history has treated worst. Power changes those who hold it, and no arrangement of their private lives has been found that prevents this. Hence the old question: who will guard the guardians?
steps.ob_zh: 這是歷史對待得最不客氣的一步。權力會改變握有它的人；而至今沒有找到任何一種對他們私生活的安排，能防止這一點。於是有了那個古老的問題：誰來看守那些看守者？

steps.en: So philosophers should be kings.
steps.zh: 所以，哲學家應該當國王。
steps.ob_en: Popper’s reply is that the argument answers the wrong question. Whoever rules, the institution must work when the ruler is bad, and one built on the hope of a good one has no remedy when the hope fails.
steps.ob_zh: 波普的回應是：這個論證回答的是錯的問題。不管誰統治，制度必須在統治者很壞的時候也能運作；而一個建立在「盼望有個好統治者」之上的制度，在盼望落空的時候沒有補救的辦法。

source.work: Plato, Republic, Book VI, 488a–489a; Han Feizi, chapter 40, “A Critique of the Doctrine of Position”
source.work_zh: 柏拉圖《理想國》卷六 488a–489a；《韓非子・難勢》
source.tr: Plato translated by Benjamin Jowett (public domain, original spelling); Han Fei translated for this series
source.lead_en: The case against trusting the many, and the case against waiting for the wise, written within about a century of each other at opposite ends of Eurasia.
source.lead_zh: 反對「信任眾人」的理由，與反對「等待智者」的理由；寫於歐亞大陸的兩端，相隔大約一個世紀。

passages.en: Imagine then a fleet or a ship in which there is a captain who is taller and stronger than any of the crew, but he is a little deaf and has a similar infirmity in sight, and his knowledge of navigation is not much better. The sailors are quarrelling with one another about the steering—every one is of opinion that he has a right to steer, though he has never learned the art of navigation and cannot tell who taught him or when he learned, and will further assert that it cannot be taught, and they are ready to cut in pieces any one who says the contrary.
passages.zh: 那麼請想像一支船隊，或者一艘船。船上有一位船長，比任何一個船員都高大強壯；但是他有點耳背，眼力也有類似的毛病，而他的航海知識也好不到哪裡去。水手們為了掌舵的事彼此爭吵：每一個人都認為自己有權掌舵，雖然他從來沒有學過航海術，說不出是誰教他的、什麼時候學的；而且他還會進一步斷言這門技術是教不來的；誰要是說相反的話，他們就準備把誰砍成碎片。
passages.note_en: The captain is the people, strong and easily managed. The sailors are the politicians who compete to manage him. Plato’s charge against democracy is that it rewards the skill of winning the captain’s favor, which is a different skill from navigation.
passages.note_zh: 船長是人民：強壯，而且容易被擺布。水手是爭著擺布他的政客。柏拉圖對民主的指控是：它獎賞的是「贏得船長歡心」的技術；而那跟航海是不同的技術。

passages.en: Yao and Shun, Jie and Zhou, appear once in a thousand generations. The rulers of the world come without a break from the middle sort, and it is for the middle sort that I speak of the position of power. The middle sort do not reach as high as Yao and Shun, and do not sink as low as Jie and Zhou. Holding to the law and occupying the position of power, they govern well. Turning their backs on the law and abandoning the position of power, they bring disorder. Now to set aside position and turn against law and wait for a Yao or a Shun, so that there is order when Yao or Shun arrives, is to have a thousand generations of disorder for one of order.
passages.zh: 且夫堯、舜、桀、紂千世而一出……世之治者不絕於中，吾所以為言勢者，中也。中者，上不及堯、舜，而下亦不為桀、紂。抱法處勢則治，背法去勢則亂。今廢勢背法而待堯、舜，堯、舜至乃治，是千世亂而一治也。
passages.note_en: Yao and Shun are the model sage kings, and Jie and Zhou the model tyrants. Han Fei’s point is statistical: a constitution should be judged by how it performs under the rulers it is actually likely to get.
passages.note_zh: 堯、舜是聖王的典型；桀、紂是暴君的典型。韓非的論點是統計上的：評判一個制度，要看它在「實際上很可能得到的那種統治者」之下表現如何。

items.o_en: Voters are badly informed, and they know that one vote changes nothing, so they have no reason to become better informed. The crew really is as Plato describes.
items.o_zh: 選民的資訊很差；而且他們知道一張票什麼也改變不了，所以沒有理由去增進了解。那群水手真的就像柏拉圖描述的那樣。
items.r_en: The evidence for voter ignorance is strong, and Jason Brennan has used it to argue for giving more weight to the votes of the informed. The usual replies are two. Any test of political knowledge would be written by someone with interests of his own, and in practice such tests have been used to exclude the poor and minorities. And the informed have interests too. A government answerable only to the educated will serve the educated.
items.r_zh: 選民無知的證據很強；傑森・布倫南用它來主張，應該給了解情況的人的票更大的權重。通常的回應有兩個。任何一份政治知識的測驗，都會由某個有自己利益的人來出題；而在實際上，這樣的測驗曾被用來排除窮人與少數族群。再者，了解情況的人也有利益。一個只對受過教育的人負責的政府，就會為受過教育的人服務。

items.o_en: Elections reward the short term. No voter is harmed today by a debt or a damaged climate that falls due in fifty years, and no future person has a vote.
items.o_zh: 選舉獎賞的是短期。一筆五十年後到期的債、一個五十年後才付代價的氣候，今天沒有任何一位選民受害；而未來的人沒有票。
items.r_en: This is a real weakness, and defenders of meritocratic rule in East Asia make much of it. Democracies answer it in part by removing some decisions from the daily contest, through independent courts, central banks, and constitutional limits. What they will not do is remove the power to dismiss the government. A ruler who cannot be dismissed may plan for fifty years, and there is no way of making him.
items.r_zh: 這是一個真實的弱點；東亞為賢能政治辯護的人很強調它。民主政體的部分回應，是把某些決定從每天的競爭裡拿出來：獨立的法院、中央銀行，以及憲法的限制。它們不肯拿走的，是解散政府的權力。一位不能被換掉的統治者，也許會為五十年做打算；而沒有任何辦法能逼他這樣做。

items.o_en: Popper sets the bar too low. A system that only lets us throw out bad rulers does nothing to bring in good ones.
items.o_zh: 波普把標準訂得太低了。一個只讓我們趕走壞統治者的制度，對於找來好的統治者毫無幫助。
items.r_en: Popper accepted this and thought it a strength. Hopes for the best ruler have a poor record, and the costs when they fail are very high. Confucians would reply that institutions are run by people, and that without some cultivation of character in those who hold office and those who choose them, no procedure will save a state. On that point Mencius and Mill, who wanted citizens educated by taking part, are closer to each other than either is to Han Fei.
items.r_zh: 波普接受這一點，而且認為這是優點。對「最好的統治者」的盼望，紀錄很差；而盼望落空時的代價非常高。儒家會回應：制度是由人來運作的；在位者與選擇他們的人，如果沒有某種品格上的修養，任何程序都救不了一個國家。在這一點上，孟子與彌爾（他希望公民藉由參與而受教育）彼此之間，比兩人各自與韓非都更接近。

said.claim: “Democracy is the worst form of government, except for all the others.” (Winston Churchill)
said.claim_zh: 「民主是最壞的政府形式；只除了其他所有的形式。」（邱吉爾）
said.verdict_en: He said it, and said he was quoting
said.verdict_zh: 他說過，而他說自己是在引用
said.en: Churchill spoke the line in the House of Commons on November 11, 1947, and the full sentence is longer: “Indeed it has been said that democracy is the worst form of Government except for all those other forms that have been tried from time to time.” The words “it has been said” show that he was repeating a remark he had heard, and no earlier source has been found. He was in opposition at the time. The voters had removed him from office two years before, at the moment of victory, and he was defending their right to do it.
said.zh: 邱吉爾 1947 年 11 月 11 日在下議院說了這句話；完整的句子比較長：「確實有人說過，民主是最壞的政府形式；只除了所有那些不時被嘗試過的其他形式。」「有人說過」這幾個字顯示，他是在複述一句他聽來的話；而至今沒有找到更早的出處。他當時是在野的。兩年前，選民在勝利的那一刻把他趕下了台；而他是在為他們這樣做的權利辯護。

terms.d_en: Plato’s ideal ruler, who governs because he knows what is good.
terms.d_zh: 柏拉圖理想中的統治者；他之所以統治，是因為他知道什麼是善。

terms.d_en: The quality that gives a government the right to rule and its subjects a reason to obey.
terms.d_zh: 使一個政府有權統治、使被統治者有理由服從的那種性質。

terms.d_en: The right to rule, held only as long as the ruler governs for the people’s good.
terms.d_zh: 統治的權利；只有在統治者為人民的好處而治理的時候才保有。

terms.d_en: Rule by one person in his own interest.
terms.d_zh: 一個人為了他自己的利益而統治。

terms.d_en: Rule by a few in their own interest, usually the rich.
terms.d_zh: 少數人（通常是富人）為了他們自己的利益而統治。

terms.d_en: Rule by those selected for ability and virtue. The word was coined in 1958 as a satire.
terms.d_zh: 由因為能力與德行而被選拔出來的人統治。這個詞是 1958 年為了諷刺而造的。

terms.d_en: Condorcet’s result that a majority of independent voters, each more likely right than wrong, is very likely right.
terms.d_zh: 孔多塞的結果：一群各自獨立、對的機率大於錯的投票者，其多數決非常可能是對的。

terms.o: Ch. 法 fǎ, 術 shù, 勢 shì
terms.d_en: Han Fei’s three instruments of rule: published law, the technique of managing officials, and the authority of the throne.
terms.d_zh: 韓非的三種統治工具：公布的法律、駕馭官員的技術，以及君位的權威。

vocab.eg: He watched a democracy put his teacher to death.
vocab.eg_zh: 他看著一個民主政體處死了他的老師。

vocab.eg: No one chooses a ship’s pilot by a show of hands.
vocab.eg_zh: 沒有人用舉手表決來選領航員。

vocab.eg: He drew the conclusion that made him notorious.
vocab.eg_zh: 他得出了那個使他聲名狼藉的結論。

vocab.eg: Monarchy decays into tyranny.
vocab.eg_zh: 君主制敗壞成僭主制。

vocab.eg: A government answerable only to the educated will serve the educated.
vocab.eg_zh: 一個只對受過教育的人負責的政府，就會為受過教育的人服務。

vocab.eg: The debt falls due in fifty years.
vocab.eg_zh: 那筆債五十年後到期。

vocab.eg: Defenders of meritocracy make much of this weakness.
vocab.eg_zh: 為賢能政治辯護的人，很強調這個弱點。

vocab.eg: Critics say that Popper sets the bar too low.
vocab.eg_zh: 批評者說，波普把標準訂得太低了。

vocab.eg: We have no reliable way to pick them out.
vocab.eg_zh: 我們沒有可靠的方法把他們挑出來。

vocab.eg: The theorem holds only if voters think for themselves.
vocab.eg_zh: 這個定理只有在投票者自己思考的時候才成立。

quiz.q: In Plato’s parable, whom does the deaf captain stand for?
options: The people.
The philosopher.
The politicians.
The gods.

quiz.q: By what two tests did Aristotle sort governments?
options: How many rule, and for whose benefit.
How rich the city is, and how large.
Whether they are old or new, and Greek or foreign.
Whether they have kings, and whether they have laws.

quiz.q: What does Mencius say about the killing of the tyrant Zhou?
options: That it was the execution of a mere fellow, since a tyrant is no longer a ruler.
That it was a crime against Heaven.
That it never happened.
That only another king may kill a king.

quiz.q: Why does Han Fei say we should not wait for a sage?
options: Sages appear once in a thousand generations, so a system must work under average rulers.
Sages are always dishonest.
The people do not want sages.
The age of the sages will return by itself.

quiz.q: What two conditions does Condorcet’s theorem need?
options: Each voter is more likely right than wrong, and voters judge independently.
Voters are wealthy and well born.
There are exactly twelve voters and one judge.
The voters agree with one another beforehand.

write.en: Think of a group you belong to: a school, a company, a temple, a family. Who rules it, and how could that person be removed? Write 150 words answering Popper’s question for that group.
write.zh: 想一個你所屬的團體：一所學校、一家公司、一座寺院、一個家庭。它由誰治理？那個人可以怎麼被換掉？寫 150 個字，為那個團體回答波普的問題。

write.en: Plato says ruling is a skill like medicine. Aristotle says the guest judges a feast better than the cook. Choose one public decision, such as where to build a hospital, and say which parts of it belong to experts and which to the public.
write.zh: 柏拉圖說，治理是像醫術一樣的技藝。亞里斯多德說，宴席好不好，客人判斷得比廚子好。選一個公共決策，例如醫院要蓋在哪裡；說說看，其中哪些部分屬於專家，哪些屬於公眾。

write.en: Han Fei designed a system for average rulers. So did the authors of modern constitutions. In 200 words, explain what the two designs share and the one thing that separates them.
write.zh: 韓非為平庸的君主設計了一個制度。現代憲法的作者也是。用 200 個字說明：這兩種設計有什麼共同點？又是哪一件事把它們分開？

paras.en: The Buddha was born in a small republic governed by an assembly of clan elders, and lived to see such states swallowed by kingdoms. The discourse on his last days opens with politics. King Ajātasattu wants to destroy the Vajji confederacy and sends a minister to learn what the Buddha thinks of his chances. The Buddha does not answer the minister directly. He turns to Ānanda and asks whether he has heard that the Vajjis “meet frequently and have many meetings,” and that they “meet in harmony, leave in harmony, and carry on their business in harmony.” He lists seven such practices, among them keeping to their established laws, listening to their elders, and not abducting women. “As long as these seven principles that prevent decline last among the Vajjis,” he says, “… they can expect growth, not decline.” The minister draws his own conclusion: the Vajjis cannot be beaten in war, and can be defeated only “by bribery or by sowing dissension.”
paras.zh: 佛陀出生在一個由氏族長老的集會來治理的小共和國；而他活著看到這樣的國家被王國吞併。記載他最後日子的那部經，是從政治開始的。阿闍世王想要消滅跋耆聯盟，派了一位大臣去探聽佛陀對他勝算的看法。佛陀並沒有直接回答那位大臣。他轉向阿難，問他是否聽說跋耆人「常常集會，集會很多」，而且「和合地集會，和合地散會，和合地處理事務」。他列出了七種這樣的做法，其中包括遵守既定的法律、聽從長老、不強擄婦女。他說：「只要這七種不衰退的法則在跋耆人當中持續下去，他們就可望增長，而不衰退。」那位大臣自己得出了結論：跋耆人在戰爭中是打不敗的；只能「用賄賂，或者用製造不和」才能擊敗他們。

paras.en: The Buddha then gave the same list to the monks, with the training rules in place of the laws. He governed his own community as the Vajjis governed theirs, by assembly, and at the end of the same discourse he declined to name a successor: “The teaching and training that I have taught and pointed out for you shall be your Teacher after my passing.” On the question of this lesson, his position is a third one. He does not say that the wise should rule, and he does not say that numbers decide. He says that a community lasts as long as it meets, speaks openly, keeps its rules, and stays united, and that it falls when it can be divided. His test of a government is the same as his test of a person, namely the conduct that can be observed (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18).
paras.zh: 接著，佛陀把同一張清單給了比丘們，只是把法律換成了學處。他治理自己的僧團，就像跋耆人治理他們的國家：用集會。而在同一部經的結尾，他拒絕指定繼承人：「我為你們所說、所指示的法與律，在我去世之後，就是你們的老師。」在這一課的問題上，他的立場是第三種。他沒有說應該由智者統治；他也沒有說由人數決定。他說的是：一個團體只要還在集會、公開地說話、遵守它的規則、保持團結，它就能持續；而當它可以被分化的時候，它就倒了。他檢驗一個政府的標準，跟他檢驗一個人的標準是同一個，也就是觀察得到的行為（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

further.t: Plato, Republic, Book VI (tr. Jowett)
further.n_en: The ship is near the beginning. Book VIII gives his account of how democracy turns into tyranny.
further.n_zh: 那艘船在接近開頭的地方。卷八是他對「民主如何轉成僭主制」的說明。

further.t: Aristotle, Politics, Book III (tr. Jowett)
further.n_en: Chapters 7 and 11: the six constitutions and the wisdom of the many.
further.n_zh: 第七章與第十一章：六種政體，以及眾人的智慧。

further.t: 《孟子・梁惠王下》《盡心下》
further.n_en: The fellow named Zhou, and the people as most important.
further.n_zh: 「聞誅一夫紂矣」與「民為貴」。

further.t: 《韓非子・難勢》《五蠹》
further.n_en: The middle sort of ruler, and the farmer who waited by the stump.
further.n_zh: 中等的君主，以及守株待兔的農夫。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Jury Theorems”
further.n_en: Condorcet’s result, its assumptions, and what happens when they fail.
further.n_zh: 孔多塞的結果、它的假設，以及假設不成立時會發生什麼。

further.t: Mahāparinibbāna Sutta, DN 16, section 1
further.n_en: The seven principles of the Vajjis.
further.n_zh: 跋耆人的七不衰法。

lessons.title: What Is Art?
lessons.blurb_en: In 1917 a urinal was sent to an art exhibition in New York. Four definitions of art, from Plato’s mirror to the artworld, each tested against ten objects that you sort yourself, with Xie He, Su Shi, and Dewey for company.
lessons.blurb_zh: 1917 年，有人把一個小便斗送到紐約的一場藝術展覽。四種藝術的定義，從柏拉圖的鏡子到「藝術界」；每一種都用十件由你自己分類的東西來檢驗。同行的還有謝赫、蘇軾與杜威。
lessons.big_en: People have made paintings, songs, and poems in every society we know of, and for most of history nobody needed to say what they had in common. The question became urgent when artists began to make things that looked like nothing art had been before. This lesson opens the unit on beauty and art by asking what the word covers.
lessons.big_zh: 在我們所知的每一個社會裡，人們都創作繪畫、歌曲與詩；而在歷史上大部分的時間裡，沒有人需要說出它們的共同點是什麼。當藝術家開始做出一些「跟從前的藝術完全不像」的東西時，這個問題才變得迫切。這一課是「美與藝術」單元的開頭；它問的是：這個詞到底涵蓋了什麼？

paras.en: In April 1917 the Society of Independent Artists held its first exhibition in New York. Its rule was simple: any artist who paid the fee could show a work, and there would be no jury. One entry was a porcelain urinal, laid on its back, signed “R. Mutt 1917,” and titled Fountain. The directors argued, and the object was kept out of sight behind a partition for the length of the show. Marcel Duchamp, a French artist who sat on the board, resigned in protest. A small magazine edited by his friends then printed a defense: “Whether Mr Mutt with his own hands made the fountain or not has no importance. He CHOSE it.” He took an ordinary article, the writer said, and “created a new thought for that object.”
paras.zh: 1917 年 4 月，獨立藝術家協會在紐約舉辦了它的第一次展覽。它的規則很簡單：任何付了費用的藝術家都可以展出一件作品，而且不設評審。有一件參展品是一個瓷製的小便斗：平放著，署名「R. Mutt 1917」，題為〈噴泉〉。理事們爭論了起來；整個展期，這件東西都被放在一道隔板後面，不讓人看見。法國藝術家馬塞爾・杜象是理事之一，他辭職以示抗議。接著，一份由他的朋友們編輯的小雜誌刊出了一篇辯護：「至於馬特先生是不是親手做了這個噴泉，並不重要。他『選擇』了它。」作者說，他拿了一件普通的物品，並且「為那件物品創造了一個新的想法」。

paras.en: The original was lost soon afterward. The examples now in museums are replicas made decades later. In 2004 five hundred British art professionals voted Fountain the most influential work of the twentieth century. Whatever one thinks of it, it did what a good philosophical example does. It was a case that every existing definition of art got wrong, or else got right for an embarrassing reason.
paras.zh: 原件不久之後就遺失了。現在博物館裡的那些，是幾十年後製作的複製品。2004 年，五百位英國的藝術界專業人士把〈噴泉〉票選為二十世紀最有影響力的作品。不管你怎麼看它，它做到了一個好的哲學例子該做的事。它是這樣一個案例：每一個既有的藝術定義，都把它判錯了；不然就是判對了，而理由很難堪。

essay.h_en: A mirror held up to the world
essay.h_zh: 對著世界舉起的一面鏡子

paras.en: The oldest definition says that art is imitation. Plato states it in order to attack it. There is the idea of a bed, he says, and there is the bed that a carpenter makes by looking to the idea, and then there is the bed in a painting, which copies only how the carpenter’s bed looks from one side. The imitator, he concludes, is “thrice removed from the king and from the truth.” Anyone can do what he does by “turning a mirror round and round.” Aristotle kept the definition and dropped the contempt: people learn by imitating and take pleasure in recognizing a likeness. For two thousand years most European theory began here. The trouble is that music imitates nothing in particular, and neither does a temple, a carpet, or a line of calligraphy.
paras.zh: 最古老的定義說：藝術是模仿。柏拉圖把它說出來，是為了攻擊它。他說：有床的理型；有木匠看著那個理型而做出來的床；然後有畫裡的床，它只摹仿了木匠的床從某一側看起來的樣子。他的結論是：模仿者「與王、與真理隔了三層」。他做的事情，任何人只要「拿一面鏡子轉來轉去」就做得到。亞里斯多德保留了這個定義，拿掉了輕蔑：人是藉著模仿來學習的，並且在認出相似之處時感到愉快。兩千年間，歐洲大部分的理論都從這裡出發。麻煩在於：音樂並不特別模仿什麼；一座神廟、一張地毯、一行書法也是。

essay.h_zh: 被傳遞出去的一份感受

paras.en: A second definition looks to the maker. In 1897 Leo Tolstoy, by then more preacher than novelist, wrote that “art is a human activity, consisting in this, that one man consciously, by means of certain external signs, hands on to others feelings he has lived through, and that other people are infected by these feelings, and also experience them.” A boy who meets a wolf and then tells the story so that his listeners feel his fear has made art. By this test Tolstoy rejected most of Shakespeare and Beethoven as insincere or unintelligible to plain people, and praised peasant songs.
paras.zh: 第二個定義看的是創作者。1897 年，那時候與其說是小說家、不如說是傳道者的列夫・托爾斯泰寫道：「藝術是人的一種活動，它在於：一個人有意識地藉著某些外在的符號，把自己體驗過的感受傳遞給別人；而別人被這些感受所感染，也體驗到它們。」一個男孩遇到了一隻狼，然後把這件事講出來，讓聽的人感受到他的恐懼；他就創作了藝術。用這個標準，托爾斯泰把莎士比亞與貝多芬的大部分作品都否定了，說它們不真誠，或者一般人聽不懂；而他稱讚農民的歌。

paras.en: China arrived at this view first and never held the other. The Book of Documents says that “poetry speaks what the heart is set on,” and the preface to the Book of Songs explains: “In the heart it is intent. Sent forth in words it is poetry.” Chinese critics took it for granted that a poem or a piece of calligraphy shows the person who made it. The weakness of the expression theory lies elsewhere. A cry of pain expresses a feeling and is not a poem, and much great art was made to order by people whose feelings we know nothing about.
paras.zh: 中國先得出了這個看法，而且從來沒有主張過另一個。《尚書》說：「詩言志。」〈毛詩序〉解釋：「在心為志，發言為詩。」中國的批評家理所當然地認為，一首詩或一件書法，顯露了創作它的那個人。表現論的弱點在別的地方。一聲痛苦的叫喊表現了一份感受，而它不是一首詩；而許多偉大的藝術，是由我們對其感受一無所知的人，受委託而製作的。

paras.en: A third definition looks at the work alone. In 1914 the English critic Clive Bell asked what a Persian bowl, a Chinese carpet, a Giotto fresco, and a Cézanne have in common, and answered: “lines and colours combined in a particular way, certain forms and relations of forms, stir our aesthetic emotions.” He called this significant form. What a picture shows is irrelevant, and Bell dismissed a famous painting of a crowded railway station, full of lifelike detail, as interesting and not art at all.
paras.zh: 第三個定義只看作品本身。1914 年，英國批評家克萊夫・貝爾問：一只波斯碗、一張中國地毯、一幅喬托的濕壁畫、一幅塞尚，有什麼共同之處？他回答：「以某種特定方式組合起來的線條與顏色、某些形式與形式之間的關係，激起了我們的審美情感。」他稱之為「有意味的形式」。一幅畫畫了什麼，是無關緊要的；有一幅畫著擁擠的火車站、充滿逼真細節的名畫，貝爾把它打發掉了：很有趣，但根本不是藝術。

paras.en: Chinese painters had long agreed that likeness is not the point. Around 500 CE Xie He listed six principles of painting and put first “spirit resonance, which means vitality.” Fidelity to the object came third. Su Shi wrote in the eleventh century: “To judge a painting by its likeness is to see as a child sees.” What these writers valued, though, was the life in the brushwork and the character of the painter that it revealed, which is nearer to expression than to Bell’s pure pattern. Bell’s definition has a further problem. When asked what makes a form significant, he could only say that it is the kind that moves us aesthetically, and the definition goes round in a circle.
paras.zh: 中國的畫家早就同意：形似不是重點。大約公元 500 年，謝赫列出了繪畫的六法，把「氣韻生動」放在第一。忠於物象的「應物象形」排在第三。蘇軾在十一世紀寫道：「論畫以形似，見與兒童鄰。」不過，這些作者所看重的，是筆墨裡的生命，以及它所顯露的畫家的品格；這更接近表現，而不是貝爾那種純粹的圖案。貝爾的定義還有一個問題。有人問：是什麼使一個形式「有意味」？他只能說：就是那種在審美上打動我們的形式；於是這個定義繞了一個圈。

paras.en: None of the three could explain Fountain. It imitates nothing, expresses no feeling that anyone can name, and has the same form as every other urinal from the same factory. In 1964 the philosopher Arthur Danto saw Andy Warhol’s Brillo Boxes, plywood copies of supermarket cartons, and concluded that what makes something art cannot be anything the eye can see. It is “an atmosphere of artistic theory, a knowledge of the history of art: an artworld.” George Dickie turned this into a definition: a work of art is an artifact that someone acting on behalf of the artworld has offered as a candidate for appreciation. On this account Fountain is art for the plain reason that it was put forward and taken up as art.
paras.zh: 這三個定義，沒有一個解釋得了〈噴泉〉。它不模仿任何東西；它不表現任何一種說得出名字的感受；它的形式，跟同一家工廠出產的每一個小便斗一模一樣。1964 年，哲學家亞瑟・丹托看到了安迪・沃荷的〈布瑞洛箱〉——超級市場紙箱的夾板複製品——並得出結論：使某樣東西成為藝術的，不可能是眼睛看得見的任何東西。它是「一種藝術理論的氛圍，一種對藝術史的知識：一個藝術界」。喬治・迪基把這變成了一個定義：藝術作品是一件人造物，由某個代表藝術界行事的人提出來，作為供人欣賞的候選者。照這個說法，〈噴泉〉是藝術，理由很平常：它被當作藝術提出來，也被當作藝術接受了。

paras.en: The institutional theory fits every case, and critics say that this is its fault. It tells us that something is art when the right people call it so, and is silent about why they should. Morris Weitz had argued in 1956 that the search was a mistake from the start. Art, like a game, has no single feature shared by all its instances. They are linked by overlapping resemblances, and each new movement extends the family. On this view the question “What is art?” has no final answer, and the changes in the answer from one age to the next are a record of what each age cared about.
paras.zh: 制度論符合每一個案例；而批評者說，這正是它的毛病。它告訴我們：當對的人把某樣東西稱為藝術的時候，它就是藝術；至於他們為什麼該這樣稱呼，它不說。莫里斯・韋茲在 1956 年就主張過：這場尋找從一開始就是個錯誤。藝術就像遊戲一樣，並沒有一個所有實例都共有的特徵。它們是由彼此交疊的相似之處連在一起的；而每一個新的流派，都把這個家族擴大了一點。照這個看法，「什麼是藝術？」這個問題沒有最終的答案；而答案在一個又一個時代之間的變化，記錄了每個時代在乎的是什麼。

paras.en: John Dewey thought all four definitions looked in the wrong place. They ask what kind of object a work of art is. In Art as Experience (1934) he argued that art is something that happens between a person and the world, and that the museum piece is only its most concentrated form. A mechanic absorbed in a job well done and a cook who cares about the meal have experiences of the same kind as the painter’s. A society that locks art in special buildings, he thought, has usually let it drain out of ordinary work.
paras.zh: 約翰・杜威認為，這四個定義都看錯了地方。它們問的是：藝術作品是哪一種「物品」？在《藝術即經驗》（1934）裡，他主張藝術是發生在一個人與世界之間的事，而博物館裡的作品只是它最濃縮的形式。一位全神貫注把工作做好的技工、一位在乎那頓飯的廚師，他們的經驗與畫家的經驗是同一類的。他認為，一個把藝術鎖在特別的建築物裡的社會，通常已經讓藝術從日常的工作裡流失了。

paras.en: The question has a new form today. A computer program can now produce an image that imitates well, has striking form, and wins a prize at an art fair, while no one involved has had any feeling to express. Whether it is art depends on which of these theories is right, and the answer will affect who is paid and who is credited.
paras.zh: 這個問題今天有了新的形式。現在，一個電腦程式就能產生一幅圖像：模仿得很好，形式醒目，還在藝術展覽上得了獎；而牽涉其中的人，沒有一個有任何感受要表現。它是不是藝術，取決於這些理論當中哪一個是對的；而答案會影響誰拿到報酬、誰得到名分。

lab.title_en: Try it: you are the curator
lab.title_zh: 親手做一次：你來策展
lab.lead_en: Ten things. For each, answer by your own lights: is it art? There are no right answers here. When you finish, you will see which of the four definitions agrees with you most, and which of your own answers it cannot explain.
lab.lead_zh: 十樣東西。每一樣，請照你自己的看法回答：它是藝術嗎？這裡沒有正確答案。做完之後，你會看到四個定義當中哪一個跟你最一致，以及你自己的哪幾個答案是它解釋不了的。

t.en: A factory-made urinal, signed with a false name and sent to an art exhibition.
t.zh: 一個工廠製造的小便斗，署了一個假名，被送到一場藝術展覽。

t.en: A painting of a bowl of fruit, so exact that it could be mistaken for a photograph. The painter made it only to show his skill.
t.zh: 一幅畫著一盆水果的畫，精確到會被誤認為照片。畫家畫它，只是為了展示技巧。

t.en: A sunset over the sea, more beautiful than any painting of one.
t.zh: 海上的一場日落，比任何一幅畫日落的畫都美。

t.en: A song a mother makes up for her sick child. It is never written down and no one else ever hears it.
t.zh: 一位母親為她生病的孩子編的一首歌。它從來沒有被寫下來，也沒有別人聽過。

t.en: A plain wooden chair of perfect proportions, made by a carpenter for his own kitchen.
t.zh: 一張比例完美的素面木椅；是一位木匠為自己的廚房做的。

t.en: A canvas covered with bold strokes of color by a chimpanzee, hung and sold in a gallery.
t.zh: 一張畫布，上面是一隻黑猩猩塗的大膽色塊；它被掛在一家畫廊裡賣掉了。

t.en: An image produced by a computer program from a one-line request. It shows a moving scene, and it wins first prize at an art fair.
t.zh: 一個電腦程式根據一行指令產生的圖像。它呈現了一個動人的場景，並且在一場藝術展覽上得了首獎。

t.en: A five-year-old’s crayon drawing of her family, taped to the refrigerator.
t.zh: 一個五歲孩子用蠟筆畫的全家福，貼在冰箱上。

t.en: A pianist walks on stage, sits at the piano for four and a half minutes without playing a note, and leaves. It is listed in the concert program.
t.zh: 一位鋼琴家走上舞台，在鋼琴前坐了四分半鐘，一個音也沒彈，然後離開。節目單上列著這個曲目。

t.en: A two-line note about a gift of oranges, brushed by a famous calligrapher seventeen centuries ago and treasured by collectors ever since.
t.zh: 一張兩行的便條，談的是送人的一批橘子；是一位著名的書法家在一千七百年前用毛筆寫的，從那以後一直被收藏家珍藏。

d.en: Art is the skilled representation of how things look or are.
d.zh: 藝術是以技巧再現事物的樣子或實況。

trouble.en: If this is your theory, the lullaby and the old note should worry you. Music and calligraphy represent nothing, and almost everyone counts them as art. The exact painting of fruit should worry you in the other direction: it is as good an imitation as can be made.
trouble.zh: 如果這是你的理論，那首搖籃曲與那張舊便條應該讓你擔心。音樂與書法並不再現任何東西，而幾乎每個人都把它們算作藝術。那幅精確的水果畫，則應該從另一個方向讓你擔心：模仿做到這樣，已經是最好的了。

d.en: Art is feeling that a person has lived through and conveys to others.
d.zh: 藝術是一個人體驗過、並且傳達給別人的感受。

trouble.en: If this is your theory, you have Tolstoy’s difficulty. The child’s drawing and the lullaby are art, and a great deal of what hangs in museums, made to order with great skill and no known feeling, is not. You must also say what the difference is between a poem and a cry.
trouble.zh: 如果這是你的理論，你就有托爾斯泰的那個困難。孩子的畫與搖籃曲是藝術；而掛在博物館裡的東西，有一大部分是以高超的技巧、在不為人知的心情下受委託製作的，卻不是。你還得說出：一首詩與一聲叫喊的差別是什麼。

d.en: Art is what moves us by its arrangement of line, color, shape, or sound alone.
d.zh: 藝術是單單以線條、顏色、形狀或聲音的安排來打動我們的東西。

trouble.en: If this is your theory, the chimpanzee and the computer are artists whenever their results are well composed, and the carpenter’s chair belongs in the museum. You may accept that. You will then need a reason why the sunset, which has form as fine as any, is left out.
trouble.zh: 如果這是你的理論，那麼只要成果的構圖好，黑猩猩與電腦就是藝術家；而木匠的椅子該進博物館。你也許可以接受。那麼你還需要一個理由：為什麼形式跟任何作品一樣好的日落，卻被排除在外？

d.en: Art is whatever is made and put forward to be appreciated as art, within the practices of the art world.
d.zh: 藝術是在藝術界的種種慣例之內，被製作出來、並且被提出來當作藝術欣賞的任何東西。

trouble.en: If this is your theory, your answers will match the gallery list exactly, and that is the objection. The mother’s song is not art until someone records it, and the urinal became art by being carried through a door. You can say what is called art, and you have given up saying why it deserves to be.
trouble.zh: 如果這是你的理論，你的答案會跟畫廊的清單一模一樣；而這就是別人的反駁。那位母親的歌，要等到有人把它錄下來才是藝術；而小便斗是因為被搬過了一道門才成為藝術的。你說得出什麼「被稱為」藝術；而你已經放棄了說它「憑什麼」是。

agree.zh: 跟你的 10 個答案當中的 {n} 個一致

best.en: Your answers fit this definition best: {name}.
best.zh: 你的答案最符合這個定義：{name}。

miss.en: It cannot explain your answer on: {list}.
miss.zh: 它解釋不了你在這幾項上的答案：{list}。

nomiss.en: It agrees with every one of your answers.
nomiss.zh: 它跟你的每一個答案都一致。

none.en: No definition agrees with more than six of your answers. That is Weitz’s position. He held that art has no essence and that the things we call art are held together by overlapping resemblances, as the members of a family are. You may be right. The cost is that you can no longer rule anything out on principle.
none.zh: 沒有一個定義跟你的答案一致超過六項。這就是韋茲的立場。他主張藝術沒有本質；我們稱為藝術的那些東西，是由彼此交疊的相似之處連在一起的，就像一個家族的成員。你也許是對的。代價是：你再也不能根據原則把任何東西排除在外了。

close.en: Dewey would point out that the ten descriptions say almost nothing about what happens to a person who looks or listens, and that this is where he would have begun.
close.zh: 杜威會指出：這十段描述，幾乎完全沒有提到一個觀看或聆聽的人身上發生了什麼；而他會從那裡開始。

argument.lead_en: Danto’s argument from indiscernible objects, the reasoning behind the institutional theory. Click a step to see what can be said against it.
argument.lead_zh: 丹托的「不可分辨之物」論證，也就是制度論背後的推理。點任何一步，看看別人可以怎麼反對它。

steps.en: Fountain is a work of art. An identical urinal in a plumber’s shop is not.
steps.zh: 〈噴泉〉是一件藝術作品。水電行裡一個一模一樣的小便斗不是。
steps.ob_en: Many people deny the first half. If Fountain is a joke or a protest and not a work of art, the argument never starts. Danto replies that a theory which rules out the most discussed works of a century has lost touch with its subject.
steps.ob_zh: 許多人否認前半句。如果〈噴泉〉是一個玩笑或一場抗議，而不是藝術作品，這個論證根本就起不了頭。丹托回應：一個把一整個世紀裡最常被討論的作品都排除在外的理論，已經跟它的主題脫節了。

steps.en: The two objects do not differ in anything that can be seen, heard, or touched.
steps.zh: 這兩件東西，在任何看得見、聽得到、摸得著的方面，都沒有差別。
steps.ob_en: They differ in position, signature, and title, and these can be seen. A formalist may say that the turned and titled object does look different once we attend to it as a shape. Duchamp said he chose it because it was visually indifferent.
steps.ob_zh: 它們在擺放的方式、署名與標題上不同；而這些是看得見的。形式主義者可以說：一旦我們把那件轉了方向、題了名的東西當作一個形狀來注意，它看起來確實不一樣。杜象說，他選它，是因為它在視覺上無關緊要。

steps.en: So what makes something art is not a property that the senses can detect.
steps.zh: 所以，使某樣東西成為藝術的，不是感官能察覺的性質。
steps.ob_en: This follows only for cases like Fountain. For most works the visible properties may still be what matters, and the odd case may be parasitic on the ordinary ones.
steps.ob_zh: 這只在像〈噴泉〉這樣的案例上才推得出來。對大多數的作品來說，看得見的性質可能仍然是要緊的；而那個古怪的案例，也許是寄生在尋常案例之上的。

steps.en: The difference lies in the object’s relation to a context of theory, history, and practice: the artworld.
steps.zh: 差別在於那件東西與一個由理論、歷史與慣例構成的脈絡的關係：藝術界。
steps.ob_en: The first art cannot have been art by relation to an existing artworld, since there was none. Something else must have made cave paintings art, and it may still be at work.
steps.ob_zh: 最初的藝術，不可能是因為與一個既有的藝術界有關係而成為藝術，因為那時候沒有藝術界。必定是別的東西使洞穴壁畫成為藝術；而那個東西也許至今還在起作用。

steps.en: So art is whatever the artworld presents as art.
steps.zh: 所以，藝術就是藝術界當作藝術來呈現的任何東西。
steps.ob_en: Danto himself did not accept this conclusion, which is Dickie’s. He held that a work must also be about something and embody its meaning. The bare institutional version explains status and leaves out value.
steps.ob_zh: 丹托自己並不接受這個結論；這是迪基的。他主張作品還必須「關於」某樣東西，並且體現它的意義。光禿禿的制度論版本，解釋了地位，漏掉了價值。

source.work: Plato, Republic, Book X, 596d–597e; Xie He, Classified Record of Ancient Painters, preface; Su Shi, “Written on a Painting of Flowering Branches by Secretary Wang of Yanling”
source.work_zh: 柏拉圖《理想國》卷十 596d–597e；謝赫《古畫品錄・序》；蘇軾〈書鄢陵王主簿所畫折枝二首〉其一
source.tr: Plato translated by Benjamin Jowett (public domain); Xie He and Su Shi translated for this series
source.lead_en: The founding statement of the imitation theory, and two Chinese texts that put likeness third and last.
source.lead_zh: 模仿論的奠基陳述；以及把「形似」排在第三、甚至排在最後的兩段中國文本。

passages.en: Well then, here are three beds: one existing in nature, which is made by God, as I think that we may say—for no one else can be the maker? No. There is another which is the work of the carpenter? Yes. And the work of the painter is a third? Yes. […] And the tragic poet is an imitator, and therefore, like all other imitators, he is thrice removed from the king and from the truth? That appears to be so.
passages.zh: 那麼，這裡有三張床：一張存在於自然之中，我想我們可以說是神造的；因為不可能有別的製造者吧？——不可能。另一張是木匠的作品？——是。而畫家的作品是第三張？——是。……那麼悲劇詩人是一個模仿者；所以他就像所有其他的模仿者一樣，與王、與真理隔了三層？——看來是這樣。
passages.note_en: Plato counts inclusively, so “thrice removed” means third in line: idea, object, picture. His target is Homer and the tragedians, whom Athenians treated as teachers. The argument is that a poet can describe a general or a doctor convincingly while knowing nothing of war or medicine.
passages.note_zh: 柏拉圖的數法是把頭尾都算進去的；所以「隔了三層」的意思是排在第三位：理型、實物、圖畫。他的靶子是荷馬與悲劇詩人；雅典人把他們當作老師。他的論證是：一位詩人可以把將軍或醫生描寫得令人信服，而對戰爭或醫術一無所知。

passages.ref: Xie He, c. 500 CE; Su Shi, 11th century
passages.en:
What are the six principles? The first is spirit resonance, which means vitality. The second is bone method, which means the use of the brush. The third is fidelity to the object in depicting forms. The fourth is conformity to kind in applying colors. The fifth is planning and placing. The sixth is transmission by copying.

To judge a painting by its likeness is to see as a child sees. To insist that a poem be on its stated subject is surely not to know poetry.
passages.zh:
六法者何？一，氣韻生動是也；二，骨法用筆是也；三，應物象形是也；四，隨類賦彩是也；五，經營位置是也；六，傳移模寫是也。

論畫以形似，見與兒童鄰。賦詩必此詩，定非知詩人。
passages.note_en: Xie He’s list was repeated by every later Chinese writer on painting. The punctuation of the six phrases is disputed, and the reading given here is the traditional one. Su Shi was praising a friend’s small picture of a sprig with one red flower, which he said conveyed a boundless spring.
passages.note_zh: 謝赫的這張清單，後來每一位談畫的中國作者都重複過。這六句的斷句有爭議；這裡給的是傳統的讀法。蘇軾是在稱讚一位朋友的小畫：一截折枝、一點紅花，他說它「解寄無邊春」。

items.o_en: This is a quarrel about a word. Call Fountain art or do not. Nothing changes.
items.o_zh: 這只是關於一個詞的爭吵。把〈噴泉〉叫做藝術也好，不叫也好。什麼都不會改變。
items.r_en: A good deal changes. The word decides what museums buy with public money, what schools teach, what copyright protects, and whose work is called craft and paid accordingly. For centuries embroidery and pottery were excluded and oil painting included, and the people on each side of that line were not a random selection.
items.r_zh: 會改變的可多了。這個詞決定了博物館用公家的錢買什麼、學校教什麼、著作權保護什麼，以及誰的作品被叫做「工藝」、並依此計酬。好幾個世紀裡，刺繡與陶器被排除在外，油畫被包括在內；而站在那條線兩邊的人，並不是隨機分配的。

items.o_en: If anything can be art, then the word means nothing, and skill, which is the one thing people can actually judge, has been thrown away.
items.o_zh: 如果任何東西都可以是藝術，那這個詞就沒有意義了；而技巧——人們唯一真正能評判的東西——就被丟掉了。
items.r_en: The institutional theory separates two questions that the objection runs together: whether something is art, and whether it is any good. A thing can be art and bad art. Skill remains a standard of quality. The reply has limits. If the classification carries no judgment at all, it is hard to see why anyone fought so hard to have Fountain admitted.
items.r_zh: 制度論把這個反駁混在一起的兩個問題分開了：某樣東西是不是藝術？它好不好？一樣東西可以是藝術，而且是壞的藝術。技巧仍然是品質的一個標準。這個回應有它的限度。如果這個分類完全不帶任何評價，那就很難看出，為什麼有人那麼拚命地要讓〈噴泉〉被接納。

items.o_en: “Art” as a single category is a modern European idea. Other cultures made beautiful and meaningful things without it.
items.o_zh: 把「藝術」當作一個單一的類別，是近代歐洲的觀念。其他的文化不用這個類別，也照樣製作出了美而有意義的東西。
items.r_en: This is true and important. The grouping of painting, sculpture, music, poetry, and architecture as the fine arts dates from eighteenth-century Europe. Classical China ranked calligraphy, poetry, and painting together as the pursuits of the educated and left sculpture and building to artisans. The modern Chinese word for art, 藝術, took its present sense from Japanese in the late nineteenth century. Recognizing this supports Weitz: the category has a history, and its edges have always been drawn by particular people for particular reasons.
items.r_zh: 這是真的，而且很重要。把繪畫、雕塑、音樂、詩與建築合稱為「美術」，始於十八世紀的歐洲。古典中國把書、詩、畫並列為讀書人的事業，而把雕塑與營造留給工匠。現代中文的「藝術」一詞，是在十九世紀末從日文取得現在這個意思的。認清這一點，支持了韋茲：這個類別有它的歷史；而它的邊界，從來都是由特定的人、為了特定的理由劃出來的。

said.claim: “Duchamp made Fountain.”
said.claim_zh: 「〈噴泉〉是杜象做的。」
said.verdict_en: Probably, and there is a letter that says otherwise
said.verdict_zh: 大概是；而有一封信說的不一樣
said.en: Duchamp said in later life that he bought the urinal, signed it, and sent it in, and nearly every museum label repeats this. But on April 11, 1917, within days of the object’s being refused, he wrote to his sister: “One of my female friends under a masculine pseudonym, Richard Mutt, sent in a porcelain urinal as a sculpture.” He never said who the friend was. Some researchers believe that she was the poet and artist Elsa von Freytag-Loringhoven and that the work was hers. Others think that the “friend” was a cover story or an early form of Duchamp’s own female alter ego. The original is lost and the question cannot be settled. The dispute is itself a lesson in the institutional theory: for a century the artworld attributed the work to the person who was in a position to speak for it.
said.zh: 杜象晚年說，是他買了那個小便斗、署了名、送去參展；幾乎每一張博物館的說明牌都重複這個說法。但是在 1917 年 4 月 11 日，也就是那件東西被拒絕之後沒幾天，他寫信給他的妹妹：「我的一位女性朋友，用一個男性的化名理查・馬特，送了一個瓷製的小便斗去當雕塑。」他從來沒有說那位朋友是誰。有些研究者認為，她就是詩人兼藝術家艾爾莎・馮・弗萊塔格—洛琳霍芬，而這件作品是她的。另一些人認為，那位「朋友」是一個掩護的說法，或者是杜象自己那個女性分身的早期形式。原件已經遺失，這個問題無法定案。這場爭議本身，就是制度論的一課：一百年來，藝術界把這件作品歸給了那個有地位為它發言的人。

terms.d_en: The branch of philosophy concerned with art, beauty, and taste.
terms.d_zh: 哲學的一個分支；關注藝術、美與品味。

terms.d_en: Imitation or representation, the oldest account of what art does.
terms.d_zh: 模仿或再現；對「藝術在做什麼」最古老的說明。

terms.d_en: Duchamp’s term for an ordinary manufactured object chosen and presented as a work of art.
terms.d_zh: 杜象的用語：一件普通的工業製品，被選出來、當作藝術作品來呈現。

terms.d_en: Bell’s term for the arrangement of lines and colors that produces aesthetic emotion.
terms.d_zh: 貝爾的用語：能產生審美情感的線條與顏色的安排。

terms.d_en: The network of artists, critics, museums, theories, and history within which things count as art.
terms.d_zh: 由藝術家、批評家、博物館、理論與歷史構成的網絡；東西是在它之內才算作藝術的。

terms.d_en: Wittgenstein’s term for a set of overlapping likenesses with no single feature common to all.
terms.d_zh: 維根斯坦的用語：一組彼此交疊的相似之處，其中沒有任何一個特徵是全體共有的。

terms.d_en: The life or vitality in a painting, the first of Xie He’s six principles.
terms.d_zh: 一幅畫裡的生命或生氣；謝赫六法的第一條。

terms.d_en: Resemblance to the outward shape of the thing depicted.
terms.d_zh: 與所畫之物外在形狀的相似。

vocab.zh: 不讓人看見、在視線之外
vocab.eg: The object was kept out of sight for the length of the show.
vocab.eg_zh: 整個展期，這件東西都被放在不讓人看見的地方。

vocab.eg: Duchamp resigned from the board in protest.
vocab.eg_zh: 杜象辭去理事以示抗議。

vocab.eg: The artist hands on to others feelings he has lived through.
vocab.eg_zh: 藝術家把自己體驗過的感受傳遞給別人。

vocab.eg: Much great art was made to order.
vocab.eg_zh: 許多偉大的藝術是受委託而製作的。

vocab.eg: Chinese critics took it for granted that a poem shows its maker.
vocab.eg_zh: 中國的批評家理所當然地認為，一首詩顯露了它的作者。

vocab.eg: For Su Shi, likeness is beside the point.
vocab.eg_zh: 對蘇軾來說，形似不是重點。

vocab.eg: Bell’s definition goes round in a circle.
vocab.eg_zh: 貝爾的定義繞了一個圈。

vocab.eg: It was put forward and taken up as art.
vocab.eg_zh: 它被當作藝術提出來，也被當作藝術接受了。

vocab.eg: You can no longer rule anything out on principle.
vocab.eg_zh: 你再也不能根據原則把任何東西排除在外。

vocab.eg: Answer each question by your own lights.
vocab.eg_zh: 每一題都照你自己的看法回答。

quiz.q: Why did Fountain matter to philosophers?
options: It was a case that the existing definitions of art could not handle.
It was the most beautiful object of its time.
It proved that plumbers are artists.
It was the first work shown without a jury.

quiz.q: Why does Plato call the imitator “thrice removed” from the truth?
options: The painting copies an object that is itself a copy of an idea.
The painter works three days on each picture.
Painters were the third class in his city.
The painter needs three colors.

quiz.q: What is Tolstoy’s definition of art?
options: The handing on of a feeling the artist has lived through, so that others share it.
The exact imitation of nature.
Whatever is shown in a museum.
The arrangement of lines and colors.

quiz.q: What did Xie He put first among the six principles of painting?
options: Spirit resonance, or vitality.
Fidelity to the object.
Copying old masters.
The application of color.

quiz.q: What is the main objection to the institutional theory?
options: It says what is called art without saying why it deserves to be.
It excludes Fountain.
It requires art to be beautiful.
It applies only to painting.

write.en: Choose something you have made, a meal, a lesson, a garden, a photograph, that you would call well made. Was it art? Answer with one of the four definitions, and then say what Dewey would add. About 150 words.
write.zh: 選一樣你自己做過、而且會說「做得好」的東西：一頓飯、一堂課、一座花園、一張照片。它是藝術嗎？用四個定義當中的一個來回答；然後說說杜威會補充什麼。約 150 個字。

write.en: A computer program produces a picture that moves everyone who sees it. No person intended anything by it. Is it art? Defend your answer against the definition that disagrees with you most.
write.zh: 一個電腦程式產生了一幅圖，看到的人都被打動了。沒有任何人藉著它想要表達什麼。它是藝術嗎？為你的答案辯護，回應跟你最不一致的那個定義。

write.en: Su Shi says that to judge a painting by its likeness is to see as a child sees. Explain what he thinks an adult should look for, and say whether the same holds for photographs.
write.zh: 蘇軾說：「論畫以形似，見與兒童鄰。」解釋他認為成年人應該看的是什麼；並且說說看，同樣的道理對照片成不成立。

paras.en: The early texts are wary of the arts as entertainment. Those who keep the eight precepts on observance days give up dancing, singing, music, and shows, and so do monks and nuns at all times. One discourse explains why. Tālapuṭa, the head of a company of performers, asks the Buddha whether it is true, as his teachers said, that a dancer who makes people laugh is reborn among the laughing gods. Twice the Buddha answers, “Enough, chief, let it be. Don’t ask me that.” Asked a third time, he says that people are already bound by greed, hate, and delusion, and that a performer who presents them with “even more arousing things” makes them more heedless. Tālapuṭa weeps, and says that he is not weeping at the answer. He weeps because he has been deceived for so long. The test applied is Tolstoy’s, with a different standard: art is judged by the states of mind it passes on.
paras.zh: 早期的經典對於「作為娛樂的藝術」是戒慎的。在齋日持守八關齋戒的人，要放下歌舞、音樂與觀看表演；比丘與比丘尼則是任何時候都如此。有一部經解釋了為什麼。一個表演團體的首領塔拉普塔問佛陀：他的老師們說，逗人發笑的舞者，死後會生到「歡笑天」，這是真的嗎？佛陀兩次回答：「夠了，首領，別管它。不要問我這個。」第三次被問的時候，他說：人們本來就被貪、瞋、癡所束縛；而一位表演者把「更加令人動情的東西」呈現給他們，使他們更加放逸。塔拉普塔哭了；他說，他不是為這個答案而哭。他哭，是因為自己被欺騙了這麼久。這裡用的檢驗，是托爾斯泰式的，只是標準不同：藝術是以它所傳遞的心的狀態來評判的。

paras.en: That standard cuts both ways, and the tradition drew the other conclusion as well. The Buddha taught in verse and in images that people remembered for a lifetime. Tālapuṭa became a monk, and a long poem under his name is preserved in the canon. Later Buddhists filled Asia with sculpture, painting, chant, and calligraphy, and gave an account of what these are for: they are a finger pointing at the moon, to be valued for what they direct the mind toward and not held on to for themselves. In Chan and Zen, brush painting and calligraphy became practices in their own right, in which the quality of the line was taken to show the state of the mind that made it, which is close to what Xie He meant by spirit resonance (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18).
paras.zh: 那個標準是兩面刃；而這個傳統也得出了另一個結論。佛陀用偈頌、用人們一輩子都記得的意象來教導。塔拉普塔後來出家了；經藏裡保存著一首歸在他名下的長詩。後來的佛教徒，讓整個亞洲充滿了雕塑、繪畫、梵唄與書法，並且說明了這些東西是做什麼用的：它們是指著月亮的手指；它們的價值在於把心引向哪裡，而不該為了它們本身而被執取。在禪宗，水墨與書法本身就成了修行；人們認為，線條的品質顯露了寫下它的那顆心的狀態。這與謝赫所說的「氣韻」很接近（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms: the finger pointing at the moon

further.t: Plato, Republic, Book X (tr. Jowett)
further.n_en: The three beds and the quarrel between philosophy and poetry.
further.n_zh: 三張床，以及哲學與詩之間的爭吵。

further.t: Leo Tolstoy, What Is Art? (tr. Aylmer Maude)
further.n_en: Chapter 5 gives the definition. The later chapters apply it without mercy.
further.n_zh: 第五章給出定義。後面的章節毫不留情地運用它。

further.t: Clive Bell, Art (1914)
further.n_en: The first chapter, “The Aesthetic Hypothesis,” is the whole theory.
further.n_zh: 第一章〈美學假說〉就是整個理論。

further.t: Tate, Marcel Duchamp, Fountain (1917, replica 1964)
further.n_en: A museum’s account of the object, its loss, and the replicas.
further.n_zh: 一家博物館對這件東西、它的遺失，以及那些複製品的說明。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “The Definition of Art”
further.n_en: Danto, Dickie, Weitz, and what came after.
further.n_zh: 丹托、迪基、韋茲，以及之後的發展。

further.t: 謝赫《古畫品錄》；蘇軾〈書鄢陵王主簿所畫折枝二首〉
further.n_en: The six principles in their original setting.
further.n_zh: 六法的原始出處。

dharma.title: No-Self and the West
dharma.blurb_en: Which Western philosopher comes closest to the Buddha’s teaching of not-self, where the likeness ends, and how to say it in English without being misunderstood.
dharma.blurb_zh: 西方哪一位哲學家最接近佛陀的無我教導？相似到哪裡為止？還有，怎麼用英文把它說出來而不被誤解？
dharma.verdict_en: Closest: Derek Parfit, with David Hume a near second. Both reach the Buddha’s conclusion about what a person is. Neither has his account of why it matters or his method for making the conclusion real.
dharma.verdict_zh: 最接近的是帕菲特，休謨緊跟在後。兩人都得出了佛陀關於「人是什麼」的結論。兩人都沒有他對「這為什麼重要」的說明，也沒有他那套讓這個結論成真的方法。

sections.eyebrow: 1 · What the Dharma says · 佛法怎麼說

h.en: The teaching in its own words
h.zh: 用它自己的話說

paras.en: The teaching was first given, according to the tradition, in the Buddha’s second discourse, to the five companions who had practiced austerities with him. He takes the five aggregates (khandha) into which a person can be analyzed, namely bodily form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, and says of each that it is anattā, not-self. He gives two reasons. The first is about control. “Form is not-self. For if form were self, it would not lead to affliction, and one could have it of form: ‘Let my form be thus, let my form not be thus.’” We cannot command the body not to age or a feeling not to arise. The second reason is put as a series of questions. Is form permanent or impermanent? Impermanent. Is what is impermanent satisfying or unsatisfying? Unsatisfying. “Is what is impermanent, unsatisfying, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?” The monks answer that it is not (Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.59).
paras.zh: 照傳統的說法，這個教導最早是在佛陀的第二次說法裡提出的，對象是曾經跟他一起修苦行的五位同伴。他舉出一個人可以被分析成的五蘊（khandha）——色、受、想、行、識——然後對每一蘊都說它是 anattā，非我。他給了兩個理由。第一個關於支配。「色非我。如果色是我，它就不會導致病苦，而人對於色也就可以如願：『願我的色如此，願我的色不如此。』」我們無法命令身體不老，也無法命令某個感受不生起。第二個理由是用一連串的提問來表達的。色是常還是無常？無常。無常的是樂還是苦？苦。「無常、苦、會變易的東西，適合被這樣看待嗎：『這是我的，這是我，這是我的自我』？」比丘們回答：不適合（《相應部》22.59）。

paras.en: Three things about the passage are easy to miss. The Buddha says of each aggregate that it is not self. He does not say here, in so many words, “there is no self.” On another occasion a wanderer named Vacchagotta asks him directly whether there is a self, and then whether there is no self, and both times the Buddha stays silent. He explains afterward that to say “there is a self” would side with the eternalists, and to say “there is no self” would side with the annihilationists and leave the questioner more confused than before (Saṃyutta Nikāya 44.10). Second, the target is a particular idea of self that was current in his day: something permanent, blissful, and in control. Third, the teaching is offered as something to be seen and not merely assented to. The discourse ends with the five listeners liberated by what they have understood.
paras.zh: 這段話裡有三件事很容易被忽略。佛陀對每一蘊說的是「它不是我」。他在這裡並沒有一字一句地說「沒有我」。另一個場合，一位名叫婆蹉種的遊方者直接問他：有我嗎？接著又問：沒有我嗎？兩次佛陀都保持沉默。事後他解釋：說「有我」，就站到了常見論者那一邊；說「沒有我」，就站到了斷見論者那一邊，而且會讓發問的人比先前更加迷惑（《相應部》44.10）。第二，被瞄準的是當時流行的一種特定的「我」的觀念：某個恆常、妙樂、能作主的東西。第三，這個教導是提出來讓人「看見」的，不只是讓人點頭同意。那部經的結尾，五位聽者因為他們所理解的而得到解脫。

paras.en: Later teachers made the positive account explicit. What we call a person is a designation applied to the aggregates when they occur together, as the word “chariot” is applied to assembled parts (Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.10). The aggregates arise and cease in dependence on conditions, and one moment conditions the next. That causal stream is enough for memory, for moral responsibility, and, in the traditional teaching, for rebirth. No owner travels along it.
paras.zh: 後來的論師把正面的說明講得更明白。我們稱為「人」的，是諸蘊同時出現時所施設的一個名稱，就像「車」這個字被用在組合起來的零件上（《相應部》5.10）。諸蘊依條件而生、依條件而滅，前一剎那作為後一剎那的條件。這道因果之流，足以說明記憶、說明道德責任，而在傳統的教導裡也足以說明再生。並沒有一個擁有者沿著它旅行。

sections.eyebrow: 2 · In standard form · 寫成標準形式

h.en: The argument, laid out
h.zh: 論證攤開來

steps.en: If anything were a self in the sense at issue, it would be permanent and under its own control.
steps.zh: 如果有任何東西是這裡所說的那種「我」，它就會是恆常的，並且能自己作主。
steps.ob_en: A Western critic may say that this sets the bar too high. Why must a self be permanent? Perhaps a self is just a living human being. The Buddhist reply is that this is the notion people actually cling to. What we fear losing at death is not an organism described in the third person.
steps.ob_zh: 西方的批評者可能會說，這個門檻設得太高了。為什麼「我」非得是恆常的？也許「我」就只是一個活著的人。佛教的回答是：這正是人們實際上執取的那個觀念。我們害怕在死亡時失去的，並不是一個用第三人稱描述的有機體。

steps.en: Each of the five aggregates is impermanent and is not under control.
steps.zh: 五蘊當中的每一個，都是無常的，而且不受支配。
steps.ob_en: Rarely disputed. Hume’s report of what he found on looking inward confirms it for the mental aggregates.
steps.ob_zh: 很少有爭議。休謨對自己往內看時所見的報告，為心理的諸蘊印證了這一點。

steps.en: There is nothing to a person over and above the five aggregates.
steps.zh: 在五蘊之外，人並沒有別的什麼。
