steps.ob_en: This is the step most often attacked, and the Buddha’s Brahmanical opponents attacked it at once. The self, they said, is the witness of the aggregates and so cannot be found among them, as the eye does not see itself. Descartes makes the same move: I am the one who is aware of all this. The Buddhist reply is that awareness is itself one of the aggregates, arising in dependence on its object, and that a witness which can never be observed is a hypothesis for which no evidence can be given.
steps.ob_zh: 這是最常被攻擊的一步，而佛陀的婆羅門教對手當下就攻擊了它。他們說：「我」是諸蘊的見證者，所以在諸蘊當中找不到它，就像眼睛看不見自己。笛卡兒走的是同一步：我就是那個覺知到這一切的。佛教的回答是：覺知本身就是五蘊之一，它依待它的對象而生起；而一個永遠無法被觀察到的見證者，是一個拿不出任何證據的假設。

steps.en: Therefore nothing in a person is a self of that kind.
steps.zh: 所以，人裡面沒有任何東西是那一種「我」。
steps.ob_en: Notice how limited the conclusion is. It denies a permanent, controlling owner. It does not deny that there are persons in the everyday sense, who make promises and are responsible for what they do.
steps.ob_zh: 留意這個結論多麼有限。它否定的是一個恆常的、能作主的擁有者。它並沒有否定有日常意義上的「人」；這些人許下承諾，並且為自己所做的事負責。

sections.eyebrow: 3 · The nearest Western views · 西方最接近的說法

h.en: Three philosophers who looked for the self
h.zh: 三位尋找自我的哲學家

text.en: Descartes doubted everything he could and found one thing left: “I am, I exist.” From this he concluded that he was a thinking substance, a single thing that persists and has thoughts as its states. The first step is one a Buddhist can accept, since no one denies that thinking is going on. The second step is the one that the not-self teaching refuses. Descartes moved from “there is thinking” to “there is a thing that thinks,” and that thing is the ātman under a French name.
text.zh: 笛卡兒懷疑了一切他能懷疑的，發現還剩下一樣東西：「我是，我存在。」他由此推斷，自己是一個思考的實體，一個持續存在、以種種思想為其狀態的單一事物。第一步是佛教徒可以接受的，因為沒有人否認有思考在進行。第二步正是無我的教導所拒絕的。笛卡兒從「有思考」跨到了「有一個在思考的東西」；而那個東西，就是換了法文名字的 ātman。

text.en: Hume repeated Descartes’ experiment and reported a different result. “When I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other, of heat or cold, light or shade, love or hatred, pain or pleasure. I never can catch myself at any time without a perception.” He concluded that a person is “nothing but a bundle or collection of different perceptions,” and that the identity we ascribe to the mind “is only a fictitious one.” This is the second premise of the Buddhist argument, reached independently and stated with great force. Hume’s account stops there. He has no theory of how the bundle is tied together, and in an appendix he admits it: “I find myself involved in such a labyrinth, that, I must confess, I neither know how to correct my former opinions, nor how to render them consistent.”
text.zh: 休謨重做了笛卡兒的實驗，報告的結果卻不同。「當我最貼近地進入我稱為『自己』的東西時，我總是碰到某個個別的知覺：冷或熱、明或暗、愛或恨、苦或樂。我任何時候都抓不到一個沒有知覺的『自己』。」他的結論是：一個人「不過是一束或一堆不同的知覺」，而我們歸給心靈的那種同一性「只是虛構的」。這就是佛教論證的第二個前提，被獨立地得出，而且說得極有力。休謨的說明到此為止。他沒有一套關於「這一束是怎麼繫在一起的」理論；在一篇附錄裡他承認了：「我發現自己陷入了這樣一座迷宮，我必須承認，我既不知道怎麼修正我先前的意見，也不知道怎麼使它們前後一致。」

role.en: The same conclusion, and its consequences
role.zh: 同樣的結論，以及它的後果

text.en: Parfit defends what he calls reductionism. A person’s existence consists in the existence of a brain and body and the occurrence of a series of connected physical and mental events. There is no further fact, no separately existing subject. He then draws consequences that Hume did not. What matters for survival is the continuation of the mental stream, whether or not we call the result “me.” The boundary between my future and other people’s is less deep than it seems, and so concern for others becomes more rational and the fear of death less so. He notes that the Buddha would have agreed, and he prints Buddhist texts in an appendix to make the point.
text.zh: 帕菲特為他所說的「化約論」辯護。一個人的存在，就在於一個腦與身體的存在，以及一連串相連的物理與心理事件的發生。此外沒有進一步的事實，沒有一個獨立存在的主體。接著他引出了休謨沒有引出的後果。對存活來說，重要的是心理之流的延續，不管我們稱不稱那個結果為「我」。我的未來與別人的未來之間的界線，沒有看起來那麼深；所以關心別人變得更合理，害怕死亡變得沒那麼合理。他指出佛陀會同意他，並且為了說明這一點，在附錄裡刊印了佛典。

sections.eyebrow: 4 · Verdict · 判定

h.en: Who is closest, and where the likeness ends
h.zh: 誰最接近，相似到哪裡為止

paras.en: Parfit is the closest. He holds all three parts of the Buddhist position: that there is no separate self, that a person is a causally connected series, and that seeing this changes how one should live. Hume holds the first with unsurpassed clarity, has no account of the second, and treats the third as a joke at his own expense, going off to play backgammon. Descartes holds none of them, and his cogito is the best Western statement of the view the Buddha was arguing against.
paras.zh: 帕菲特最接近。佛教立場的三個部分他都持有：沒有獨立的自我；人是一個因果相連的序列；看清這一點，會改變人應當怎麼活。休謨以無人能及的清晰持有第一點，對第二點沒有說明，對第三點則當成一個拿自己開的玩笑，跑去下雙陸棋了。笛卡兒三點都不持有；而他的 cogito，是西方對佛陀所反對的那個看法最好的陳述。

paras.en: The likeness to Parfit ends at four places. First, he reaches the view by argument about imaginary cases, and says frankly that he cannot always believe it: the conviction fades when he stops thinking about the arguments. Second, the continuity he describes is psychological, and it ends at death. The Buddhist stream includes the body, runs on causal conditions of which memory is only one, and is traditionally held to continue from life to life. Third, Parfit is content to say that persons reduce to physical and mental events and to stop there. The Madhyamaka philosophers pressed on and argued that those events have no independent nature either. Fourth, and most important, Parfit offers a conclusion and the Buddha offers a training.
paras.zh: 跟帕菲特的相似，在四個地方到了盡頭。第一，他是靠著對想像案例的論證得出這個看法的，並且坦白說他並不總是相信得了：一停止思考那些論證，那份確信就消退了。第二，他描述的連續性是心理的，而且到死亡為止。佛教的那道流包含身體，靠的是種種因果條件，記憶只是其中之一；而且傳統上認為它從一生延續到另一生。第三，帕菲特滿足於說「人可以化約為物理與心理的事件」，然後就停在那裡。中觀學派的哲學家繼續往下追，論證那些事件同樣沒有獨立的本性。第四，也是最重要的：帕菲特提供的是一個結論，佛陀提供的是一套訓練。

sections.eyebrow: Side by side · 並排比較

h.en: Four answers to five questions
h.zh: 五個問題，四種回答

rows.en: What is found on looking inward?
Five kinds of process, each arising and passing

rows.zh: 相連的心理與物理事件

rows.en: A designation applied to the aggregates
A brain, a body, and a series of events
An immaterial substance joined to a body
rows.zh: 與身體相連的非物質實體
什麼把各階段繫在一起？

rows.en: Dependent origination: each moment conditions the next
rows.zh: 緣起：前剎那為後剎那之緣

rows.en: Resemblance and causation; he admits he cannot say
rows.zh: 相似與因果；他承認說不清

rows.en: How did he take the result?
As a puzzle to be left in the study
rows.zh: 當作留在書房裡的難題

rows.en: As liberating, when he could believe it
rows.zh: 當作解脫——在他相信得了的時候

rows.en: A path of training that ends clinging
rows.zh: 一條止息執取的修習之道

rows.en: Less self-concern; ethics becomes more impersonal
rows.zh: 少一些自我關切；倫理更不偏私

sections.eyebrow: 5 · The step the Dharma takes further · 佛法多走的一步

h.en: From a view to a way of seeing
h.zh: 從一個見解，到一種看法

paras.en: The Buddhist tradition draws a distinction that neither Hume nor Parfit has. It separates the belief in a self from the sense of self. The belief, called identity view (sakkāya-diṭṭhi), is a matter of opinion and can be given up by understanding an argument. The sense, the conceit “I am” (asmimāna), is something else. In one discourse the monk Khemaka, who is ill, is questioned by his fellows. He says that he does not regard any of the five aggregates as “this I am,” and yet the feeling “I am” has not left him. He compares it to the scent that clings to a cloth after it has been washed clean (Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.89). This is exactly Parfit’s situation: convinced by the arguments, and still unable to feel what he believes.
paras.zh: 佛教傳統有一個休謨與帕菲特都沒有的區分。它把「相信有我」與「我的感覺」分開。前者稱為身見（sakkāya-diṭṭhi），是見解上的事，理解了一個論證就可以放下。後者，「我是」的慢（asmimāna，我慢），是另一回事。有一部經裡，生病的差摩比丘被同修們詢問。他說，五蘊當中的任何一蘊，他都不把它看作「這是我」；然而「我是」的感覺並沒有離開他。他把它比作一塊布洗乾淨之後，還殘留在上面的氣味（《相應部》22.89）。這恰恰就是帕菲特的處境：被論證說服了，卻仍然感受不到自己所相信的。

paras.en: The path is the answer to that gap. Ethical conduct loosens the habits that keep the sense of self inflamed. Concentration steadies attention enough to watch the aggregates arise and pass. Insight is the repeated, direct observation that each of them is impermanent and ownerless, until the perception is no longer an inference. The tradition says that the belief falls away early and the conceit only at the end. Western philosophy has the argument, and in Parfit it even has the report of what believing it is like. It has nothing corresponding to the method.
paras.zh: 道，就是對這個落差的回答。戒，鬆開那些讓「我的感覺」持續發炎的習慣。定，使注意力穩定到足以看著諸蘊生起、滅去。慧，是反覆而直接地觀察到它們每一個都是無常的、沒有主人的，直到這個認知不再是一個推論。傳統說：身見很早就會斷除，我慢要到最後才斷。西方哲學有那個論證；在帕菲特那裡，甚至有「相信它是什麼感覺」的報告。它沒有任何與那套方法相對應的東西。

sections.eyebrow: 6 · How to say it to a Western audience · 對西方人怎麼講

h.en: Words that work, and words that mislead
h.zh: 有用的說法，與誤導的說法

paras.en: Three habits of English cause most of the misunderstanding. The first is the phrase “no self,” which listeners hear as “you do not exist.” “Not-self” is closer to the Pāli and to the method: of each thing that you take to be you, see that it is not. The second is the word “soul.” Many in a Western audience will assume that what is being denied is the Christian soul, and will take the teaching as an attack on religion. It helps to say that the target is any fixed owner or controller of experience, religious or secular. The third is the fear of nihilism. It should be said early and plainly that the person who makes promises, feels pain, and deserves kindness is not being denied.
paras.zh: 英文的三個習慣，造成了大部分的誤解。第一個是 no self 這個說法，聽的人會聽成「你不存在」。not-self 比較貼近巴利原文，也貼近方法：對每一樣你當成「你」的東西，看出它不是。第二個是 soul 這個字。西方聽眾裡有許多人會以為，被否定的是基督教的靈魂，於是把這個教導當成對宗教的攻擊。講明「被瞄準的是任何固定的、擁有或支配經驗的東西，不論宗教的或世俗的」，會有幫助。第三個是對虛無主義的恐懼。應該及早而明白地說：那個許下承諾、感受痛苦、值得被善待的人，並沒有被否定。

lines.en: The Buddha did not say that you do not exist. He said that nothing you can point to is a fixed, lasting owner of your experience.
lines.zh: 佛陀沒有說你不存在。他說的是：你指得出來的任何東西，都不是你的經驗的一個固定而持久的擁有者。

lines.en: Think of a river. It is real and it has a name, and there is no water in it that stays.
lines.zh: 想想一條河。它是真實的，它有名字，而河裡沒有一滴水是留著不動的。

lines.en: David Hume looked inside for a self and found only thoughts and feelings passing by. The Buddha found the same, and then asked what follows if we stop treating them as “mine.”
lines.zh: 休謨往裡面找自我，只找到來來去去的念頭與感受。佛陀找到的是同樣的東西；然後他問：如果我們不再把它們當成「我的」，接下來會怎樣？

lines.en: This is something to observe more than something to believe. Watch a feeling arise and fade, and ask who owns it.
lines.zh: 這比較是要去觀察的事，而不是要去相信的事。看著一個感受生起又消退，然後問：是誰擁有它？

lines.en: The teaching is aimed at suffering. Most of our distress comes from defending a self that turns out, on inspection, to be a process.
lines.zh: 這個教導瞄準的是苦。我們大部分的苦惱，來自捍衛一個「自我」；而仔細一看，那原來是一個過程。

lines.en: Giving up the idea of a fixed self does not make you care less. People who see it clearly tend to care more, because the wall between “me” and “you” has become thinner.
lines.zh: 放下「固定的自我」這個觀念，不會讓你變得比較不在乎。把它看清楚的人往往更在乎，因為「我」與「你」之間的那道牆變薄了。

avoid.en: “You have no self.”
avoid.zh: 「你沒有自我。」

avoid.en: Heard as a denial that the listener exists. Say what is not found, and what is.
avoid.zh: 聽起來像在否認聽者的存在。要說「找不到什麼」，以及「找得到什麼」。

avoid.en: “The self is an illusion.”
avoid.zh: 「自我是幻覺。」

avoid.en: Suggests that nothing is there. The process is real. What is mistaken is taking it for a thing.
avoid.zh: 讓人以為那裡什麼都沒有。過程是真實的；錯的是把它當成一個東西。

avoid.en: “Buddhism denies the soul.”
avoid.zh: 「佛教否定靈魂。」

avoid.en: Turns the teaching into a quarrel with Christianity. The point is about clinging, whatever its object.
avoid.zh: 把這個教導變成跟基督教的爭論。重點在執取，不管執取的對象是什麼。

quiz.q: What two reasons does the Buddha give, in the second discourse, for calling each aggregate not-self?
options: It cannot be controlled at will, and it is impermanent.
It is evil, and it is invisible.
It was created by a god, and it is immortal.
It is made of atoms, and it is very small.

quiz.q: Why did the Buddha stay silent when Vacchagotta asked whether there is a self?
options: Either answer would have sided with a mistaken view and confused the questioner.
He did not know the answer.
He was forbidden to speak that day.
He held that the self is eternal.

quiz.q: Why is Parfit judged closer to the Buddhist position than Hume?
options: He adds an account of what connects the stages and of how the view should change one’s life.
He was a Buddhist monk.
He believed in rebirth.
He rejected all arguments.

quiz.q: What does the story of the monk Khemaka show?
options: The belief in a self can be given up while the sense “I am” remains.
Illness is caused by wrong views.
Monks should not be questioned.
The aggregates are permanent.

quiz.q: Why is “not-self” often a better translation than “no self”?
options: It describes each thing examined as not being a self, without asserting that the person does not exist.
It is shorter.
It is the older English phrase.
It avoids using a negative.

write.en: Explain the not-self teaching in five English sentences to a friend who has never heard of it, without using the words “illusion” or “soul.”
write.zh: 用五個英文句子，向一位從沒聽過無我教導的朋友解釋它，不要用 illusion 或 soul 這兩個字。

write.en: A listener objects: “If there is no self, who gets enlightened?” Write a reply of about 100 words.
write.zh: 一位聽眾提出反駁：「如果沒有自我，是誰開悟？」寫一段大約 100 個英文字的回應。

write.en: Where do you yourself stand between the belief and the feeling? Describe one situation in which the sense of “I” was especially strong.
write.zh: 在「見解」與「感覺」之間，你自己站在哪裡？描述一個「我」的感覺特別強的情境。

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.59, the Discourse on the Characteristic of Not-Self
further.n_en: The second discourse. Two pages.
further.n_zh: 第二次說法。兩頁。

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 44.10 (Vacchagotta) and 22.89 (Khemaka)
further.n_en: The silence, and the scent that remains.
further.n_zh: 沉默，以及殘留的氣味。

further.t: David Hume, A Treatise of Human Nature, Book I, Part IV, section 6, and the Appendix
Derek Parfit, Reasons and Persons (1984), chapters 10–13 and Appendix J
Mark Siderits, Buddhism as Philosophy (2007), chapters 3 and 6
further.n_en: The best single book for the comparison.
further.n_zh: 做這項比較最好的一本書。

dharma.title: The Five Aggregates and the West
dharma.blurb_en: The Buddha’s five-part map of experience, the Western pictures of the mind that resemble it, and how to explain each of the five in English without importing the wrong ideas.
dharma.blurb_zh: 佛陀那張把經驗分成五區的地圖；西方哪些對心靈的描繪與它相似；以及怎麼用英文解釋這五項，而不夾帶錯誤的觀念。
dharma.verdict_en: Closest: the picture in modern cognitive science of a mind made of many processes with no central controller, as in Marvin Minsky and Daniel Dennett. Hume is second. The aggregates differ from both in being a map for a practitioner to use on himself, and in giving feeling tone a place of its own.
dharma.verdict_zh: 最接近的是當代認知科學裡的那幅圖像：心靈由許多過程構成，沒有中央控制者，如明斯基與丹尼特所說。休謨其次。五蘊與兩者的不同在於：它是一張讓修行者用在自己身上的地圖；而且它給了「受」一個獨立的位置。

sections.eyebrow: 1 · What the Dharma says · 佛法怎麼說

h.en: Five heaps
h.zh: 五堆

paras.en: The Pali word khandha means a heap, a mass, or the trunk of a tree. The Buddha used it for five classes into which he sorted everything that makes up a living being’s experience: form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. He defines each in the plural and with the widest possible reach. “Any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: this is called the aggregate of form” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.48), and so for the other four. An aggregate is therefore a category of events. It is a mistake to picture five components fitted together like the parts of an engine.
paras.zh: 巴利文 khandha 的意思是一堆、一團，或樹幹。佛陀用這個字來稱呼五個類別；構成一個生命的經驗的一切，他都歸進這五類：色、受、想、行、識。他對每一蘊的界定都是複數的，而且涵蓋範圍盡可能地廣。「任何的色，不論過去、未來、現在，內或外，粗或細，劣或勝，遠或近，這稱為色蘊」（《相應部》22.48）；其餘四蘊也是這樣。所以，一蘊是一「類」事件。把它想成像引擎零件那樣組裝在一起的五個組件，是一種誤解。

paras.en: One discourse defines the five by what they do, with a play on each word (Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.79). Form is so called because it is “deformed” by cold and heat, hunger and thirst, and the touch of insects, wind, and sun. Feeling “feels pleasure, pain, and neutral.” Perception “perceives blue, yellow, red, and white,” which is to say that it recognizes and labels. Formations, which the translator here renders “choices,” are whatever shapes and constructs the others, the mind’s intentions and habits. Consciousness “cognizes sour, bitter, pungent, sweet”: it is the bare awareness of an object through one of the senses. Notice that every definition is a verb. The discourse describes five kinds of happening and names no one to whom they happen.
paras.zh: 有一部經用「它們做什麼」來界定這五者，每一個都帶著文字遊戲（《相應部》22.79）。色之所以稱為色，是因為它被冷熱、飢渴，以及蚊蟲、風、日的觸碰所「變壞」。受「感受樂、苦、不苦不樂」。想「認知青、黃、赤、白」，也就是辨認並且貼上標記。行（這位譯者譯作 choices）是塑造、建構其餘各蘊的東西，也就是心的意圖與習慣。識「了別酸、苦、辛、甜」：它是透過某一個感官，對一個對象的單純覺知。請留意：每一個定義都是動詞。這部經描述了五種「發生」，而沒有指出它們是發生在誰身上。

paras.en: The scheme was not offered as psychology for its own sake. The Buddha distinguishes the five aggregates from the five “grasping aggregates,” the same five when they are “accompanied by defilements” and “fuel grasping.” The reason for sorting experience in this way is given in another discourse: whatever anyone regards as a self, “all regard the five grasping aggregates, or one of them” (22.47). The list is meant to be exhaustive of the places where a self might be looked for. And a set of similes tells the practitioner what he will find when he looks closely: “Form is like a lump of foam; feeling is like a bubble; perception seems like a mirage; choices like a banana plant; and consciousness like an illusion” (22.95). A banana trunk can be peeled layer after layer, and there is no heartwood.
paras.zh: 這套架構並不是為了心理學本身而提出的。佛陀區分了「五蘊」與「五取蘊」；後者是同樣的五者，在它們「伴隨著煩惱」並且「助長執取」的時候。至於為什麼要這樣歸類經驗，另一部經給了理由：任何人把任何東西看作我，「都是把五取蘊、或其中之一看作我」（22.47）。這份清單的用意，是要窮盡一個「我」可能被找到的所有地方。還有一組比喻告訴修行者，當他細看的時候會發現什麼：「色如聚沫，受如水泡，想如陽燄，行如芭蕉，識如幻事」（22.95）。芭蕉的樹幹可以一層一層地剝開，而裡面沒有心材。

sections.eyebrow: 2 · In standard form · 寫成標準形式

h.en: The argument from exhaustion
h.zh: 窮舉論證

steps.en: Whatever a person takes to be himself, he takes to be his body, his feelings, his perceptions, his intentions and habits, his awareness, or some combination of these.
steps.zh: 一個人不管把什麼當成自己，他當成自己的，不外是他的身體、感受、認知、意圖與習慣、覺知，或這些的某種組合。
steps.ob_en: This is the claim that the list is complete, and it carries the whole argument. A Western reader will ask where memory is, or reason, or character. The tradition’s answer is that each is a pattern across several aggregates: a memory is a present perception and formation with a past object. The reader may test the claim by trying to name something he identifies with that falls outside all five.
steps.ob_zh: 這就是「這份清單是完整的」這個主張，而整個論證都靠它。西方的讀者會問：記憶在哪裡？理性呢？性格呢？這個傳統的回答是：它們每一個，都是橫跨幾蘊的一種樣式。一個記憶，是一個當下的想與行，對象是過去的。讀者可以這樣檢驗這個主張：試著說出一樣自己認同、卻落在五蘊之外的東西。

steps.en: Each of the five is a class of events that arise from conditions and cease when the conditions cease.
steps.zh: 這五者當中的每一個，都是一類事件；它們依條件而生起，條件息滅時也就息滅。
steps.ob_en: Established by observation. This is what the similes of foam, bubble, and mirage are for.
steps.ob_zh: 由觀察建立。聚沫、水泡、陽燄這些比喻，就是為此而設的。

steps.en: No further item is found that owns or directs the five.
steps.zh: 找不到另外一項東西，擁有或指揮這五者。
steps.ob_en: The Brahmanical schools replied that the owner is the witness, which is never among the things witnessed. Kant’s “I think” is a relative of that reply. The Buddhist answer is that witnessing is itself the fifth aggregate, and that it arises with its object and ceases with it.
steps.ob_zh: 婆羅門教各派回應：擁有者就是那個見證者，而它從來不在被見證的東西當中。康德的「我思」是這個回應的親戚。佛教的回答是：「見證」本身就是第五蘊；它隨著對象生起，也隨著對象息滅。

steps.en: So what is called a person is the five occurring together, each conditioning the others.
steps.zh: 所以，所謂的「人」，就是這五者一起發生，彼此互為條件。
steps.ob_en: The conclusion is the positive side of the not-self teaching. It says what there is, and the previous page in this series said what there is not.
steps.ob_zh: 這個結論是無我教導的正面。它說的是「有什麼」；這個系列的上一頁說的是「沒有什麼」。

sections.eyebrow: 3 · The nearest Western views · 西方最接近的說法

h.en: Three ways of taking the mind apart
h.zh: 把心靈拆開的三種方式

text.en: Aristotle’s On the Soul is the first Western analysis of a living being into capacities: nutrition, perception, desire, movement, and thought. The list looks like a cousin of the Buddha’s, and it is put to the opposite use. For Aristotle the capacities are powers of one substance. The soul is the form of a living body, the single principle that makes it this kind of thing and holds its activities together. To analyze the capacities is to understand the unity better. The aggregates are offered in order to show that there is no such unifying principle to be found.
text.zh: 亞里斯多德的《論靈魂》，是西方第一次把一個生命分析成各種能力：營養、感知、欲求、運動與思想。這份清單看起來像是佛陀那一份的表親，用途卻正好相反。對亞里斯多德來說，這些能力是「一個」實體的種種能力。靈魂是一個活的身體的形式，是使它成為這一種東西、並且把它的種種活動維繫在一起的那個單一原理。分析這些能力，是為了更了解那個統一。五蘊的提出，則是為了顯示：找不到這樣一個統合的原理。

role.en: The same result, without a map
role.zh: 同樣的結果，但沒有地圖

text.en: Hume agrees that the mind is a plurality with no owner: “a bundle or collection of different perceptions.” His own sorting is into two kinds, impressions and their fainter copies, ideas, with impressions divided into those of sensation and those of reflection, such as desire and aversion. That is a classification by vividness and origin, and it is thin beside the Buddhist one. It has no separate place for the body, none for the pleasant or painful tone of an experience as distinct from its content, and none for the forces that shape what arises next. Hume saw that there was a bundle and did not describe how it is put together.
text.zh: 休謨同意心靈是一個沒有擁有者的「多」：「一束或一堆不同的知覺。」他自己的歸類是分成兩種：印象，以及印象較淡的副本，也就是觀念；印象又分成感覺的印象與反省的印象，後者如欲望與厭惡。那是依鮮明程度與來源所作的分類；擺在佛教的分類旁邊，它是單薄的。它沒有給身體一個獨立的位置；沒有把一個經驗的樂或苦的調子，與它的內容分開；也沒有位置給那些塑造「接下來生起什麼」的力量。休謨看見了那裡有一束東西，卻沒有描述它是怎麼組成的。

text.en: Marvin Minsky, a founder of artificial intelligence, argued in The Society of Mind that what we call a mind is a great number of small processes, none of them intelligent, whose interaction produces everything we credit to a self. Daniel Dennett argued in Consciousness Explained that the brain contains no place where “it all comes together” before an inner audience. Many streams of processing run in parallel, and what we report as our experience is whichever content wins influence for the moment. Both deny the central controller and both explain the appearance of one. In The Embodied Mind, published in 1991, the neuroscientist Francisco Varela and two colleagues set this science beside the five aggregates and proposed that the Buddhist scheme supplies what the science lacks, a disciplined way of examining experience from within.
text.zh: 人工智慧的創始人之一明斯基，在《心智社會》裡論證：我們稱為心靈的，是為數眾多的小過程，其中沒有任何一個是有智能的；它們的互動，產生了我們歸功於一個「自我」的一切。丹尼特在《意識的解釋》裡論證：腦裡沒有一個地方，是「一切都匯集起來」呈現在一位內在觀眾面前的。許多處理的串流同時並行；我們回報為「自己的經驗」的，是當下贏得影響力的那個內容。兩人都否定中央控制者，兩人也都解釋了為什麼看起來好像有一個。在 1991 年出版的《具身心智》裡，神經科學家瓦瑞拉與兩位同事把這門科學跟五蘊並排擺在一起，並且提議：佛教的這套架構，補上了這門科學所缺的東西，也就是一種有紀律的、從內部檢視經驗的方法。

sections.eyebrow: 4 · Verdict · 判定

h.en: Who is closest, and where the likeness ends
h.zh: 誰最接近，相似到哪裡為止

paras.en: The society-of-mind picture is the closest. It shares the three structural claims of the aggregate analysis: experience is produced by many kinds of process, the processes condition one another, and no further item supervises them. Hume shares the first and third and has little to say about the second. Aristotle shares the method of analysis by function and rejects the conclusion.
paras.zh: 「心智社會」這幅圖像最接近。它跟五蘊的分析共有三個結構上的主張：經驗是由許多種過程產生的；這些過程彼此互為條件；沒有另外一項東西在監督它們。休謨共有第一與第三點，對第二點沒有多少話說。亞里斯多德共有「依功能來分析」的方法，卻拒絕那個結論。

paras.en: The likeness ends at four places. First, the standpoint differs. The cognitive scientist describes a mechanism from outside, in the third person, and the parts he names are not things anyone can observe in himself. The aggregates are categories of what shows up in experience, chosen so that a person can check them. Second, feeling tone has a category of its own. In the Buddhist analysis the bare pleasantness or unpleasantness of an experience is the point at which craving takes hold, and Western psychology gave valence that kind of weight only recently. Third, the body is inside the scheme. Form is the first aggregate, on a level with the other four, so the analysis never divides a person into a mind and a body and never has to rejoin them. Fourth, the purpose differs. Minsky wanted to build a mind and Dennett to explain one. The Buddha’s interest was in the grasping, and he analyzed the aggregates so that it could stop.
paras.zh: 相似在四個地方到了盡頭。第一，立足點不同。認知科學家是從外面、用第三人稱描述一個機制；他說出的那些部件，不是任何人能在自己身上觀察到的東西。五蘊則是「在經驗中出現的東西」的類別，選它們就是為了讓一個人可以自己檢查。第二，「受」有它自己的一個類別。在佛教的分析裡，一個經驗單純的樂或不樂，正是渴愛抓住人的那個點；而西方心理學直到晚近才給了「情緒效價」那樣的分量。第三，身體在這個架構之內。色是第一蘊，與其餘四蘊平列；所以這套分析從來不把人切成一個心與一個身，也就從來不必把它們重新接起來。第四，目的不同。明斯基想要造出一個心，丹尼特想要解釋一個心。佛陀關心的是那個「取」；他分析五蘊，是為了讓它可以停下來。

sections.eyebrow: Side by side · 並排比較

h.en: The five, one at a time
h.zh: 五蘊，一個一個來

rows.en: What is “deformed” by cold, heat, hunger, and contact: the body and what the senses meet
rows.zh: 被冷熱、飢渴與觸碰「變壞」的：身體，以及感官所遇到的

rows.en: Not “matter” as physics defines it. It is the bodily side of experience
rows.zh: 不是物理學界定的「物質」。它是經驗的身體面

rows.en: Not “emotion.” Anger and joy are complex states that belong mostly to the fourth aggregate
rows.zh: 不是「情緒」。憤怒與喜悅是複合的狀態，大部分屬於第四蘊

rows.en: It “perceives blue, yellow, red, and white”: recognizing and labeling
rows.zh: 「認知青、黃、赤、白」：辨認並貼上標記

rows.en: Recognition; categorization; Kant’s bringing of an intuition under a concept
rows.zh: 辨識；範疇化；康德所說把直觀歸到概念之下

rows.en: Narrower than English “perception,” which includes the sensing itself
rows.zh: 比英文的 perception 窄；後者包含感覺本身

rows.en: What “produces conditioned phenomena”: intention, and with it habit, attention, emotion
rows.zh: 「造作有為法」的：意圖，連同習慣、注意、情緒

rows.en: Volition; disposition; Hume’s passions and habits
rows.zh: 意志；傾向；休謨的情感與習慣

rows.en: No single Western term covers both a momentary choice and a lasting tendency
rows.zh: 沒有哪一個西方術語，能同時涵蓋一剎那的抉擇與持久的傾向

rows.en: It “cognizes sour, bitter, pungent, sweet”: awareness of an object at one of six sense doors
rows.zh: 「了別酸、苦、辛、甜」：在六個根門之一，對一個對象的覺知

rows.en: Not a mind or a subject. It is plural, momentary, and always of something
rows.zh: 不是一個心，也不是一個主體。它是複數的、剎那的，而且總是「對某物」的

sections.eyebrow: 5 · The step the Dharma takes further · 佛法多走的一步

h.en: A map that is meant to be used
h.zh: 一張要拿來用的地圖

paras.en: A theory of the mind is finished when it has been stated and tested. The aggregate scheme is unfinished until someone has applied it to his own experience, repeatedly, at the moment the experience occurs. Take a flash of irritation at a remark. Untrained, one experiences a single solid fact: he insulted me. With the map one can find a tightening in the chest, which is form, an unpleasant tone, which is feeling, the label “insult,” which is perception, an impulse to answer back and an old habit of resentment, which are formations, and the knowing of all this, which is consciousness. Nothing has been denied or suppressed. But five passing events are much harder to cling to than one fact about me, and the discourses claim that with practice the clinging stops.
paras.zh: 一個關於心靈的理論，在被陳述並且被檢驗之後，就算完成了。五蘊的架構，則要等到有人把它用在自己的經驗上，一再地、在經驗發生的當下去用，才算完成。就拿聽到一句話時閃過的一陣惱怒來說。未經訓練的人，經驗到的是一個單一而堅實的事實：他侮辱了我。有了這張地圖，可以找到胸口的一陣緊，那是色；一種不愉快的調子，那是受；「侮辱」這個標籤，那是想；一股回嘴的衝動，以及一個由來已久的怨恨的習慣，那是行；還有對這一切的知道，那是識。沒有任何東西被否認或壓抑。然而，五個來來去去的事件，比起「一個關於我的事實」，要難執取得多；而經典主張，經過修習，那個執取會停下來。

paras.en: The Mahāyāna takes one more step, and it is aimed at the map itself. The early schools sometimes spoke as though the aggregates, unlike the person, were finally real. The Heart Sūtra opens with the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, who “saw that the five aggregates are all empty”: 照見五蘊皆空. Form is no more a self-standing thing than the chariot was. The heaps are themselves designations for conditions, and analysis can be continued through them and never arrives at a floor. No Western account of the mind’s parts has turned on its own categories in this way (see D8, Emptiness).
paras.zh: 大乘又多走了一步，而這一步瞄準的是地圖本身。早期的部派有時說得好像：人不是最終真實的，五蘊卻是。《心經》一開頭就是觀自在菩薩「照見五蘊皆空」。色並不比那輛車更是一個自立的東西。這幾堆本身，也是對種種條件的假名；分析可以穿過它們繼續下去，而永遠到不了一層地板。西方對心靈各部分的說明，沒有哪一種像這樣回過頭來對付自己的範疇（見 D8〈空〉）。

sections.eyebrow: 6 · How to say it to a Western audience · 對西方人怎麼講

h.en: Five words that each need a sentence
h.zh: 五個各需要一句話的詞

paras.en: The difficulty in English begins with “aggregate,” a word nobody uses. “Heap” is literal and vivid, and “the five heaps” is worth saying once so that listeners stop imagining components. Of the five names, “feeling” causes the most trouble, because in English it means emotion. Say “feeling tone,” and give the three values: pleasant, unpleasant, neutral. “Perception” should be glossed as recognition. “Formations” means nothing to a newcomer, and each translator has tried something different: volitional formations, fabrications, choices. It helps to say “intentions and habits” first and introduce the technical word afterward. “Consciousness” invites the listener to think of a mind or a soul, so add at once that it means the simple knowing of a sight, a sound, or a thought, and that it comes and goes with its object.
paras.zh: 英文的困難，從 aggregate 這個沒有人在用的字就開始了。heap（堆）是直譯，也很生動；the five heaps 值得說一次，讓聽的人不再想像成「組件」。五個名稱當中，feeling 惹的麻煩最多，因為它在英文裡是「情緒」的意思。要說 feeling tone，並且給出三個值：樂、苦、不苦不樂。perception 應該解釋成「辨認」。formations 對新來的人毫無意義，而每一位譯者試的都不一樣：volitional formations、fabrications、choices。先說「意圖與習慣」，之後再引進術語，會有幫助。consciousness 會引誘聽者想到一個心或一個靈魂，所以要立刻補上：它指的是對一個景象、一個聲音或一個念頭單純的知道，而且它隨著對象來去。

lines.en: The Buddha sorted everything we experience into five heaps: the body, feeling tone, recognition, intentions and habits, and awareness.
lines.zh: 佛陀把我們經驗到的一切，歸成五堆：身體、感受的調子、辨認、意圖與習慣，以及覺知。

lines.en: Feeling here does not mean emotion. It means the pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral flavor that comes with every experience.
lines.zh: 這裡的「受」不是情緒的意思。它指的是伴隨每一個經驗的那種樂、苦或不苦不樂的味道。

lines.en: The list is a tool for looking. You take whatever you believe is “you” and ask which heap it belongs to.
lines.zh: 這份清單是用來「看」的工具。你拿任何你相信是「你」的東西，問它屬於哪一堆。

lines.en: None of the five is in charge of the others, and there is no sixth.
lines.zh: 這五者當中，沒有哪一個在管其他的；而且沒有第六個。

lines.en: When you are angry, try to find the five: the heat in the body, the unpleasantness, the label you put on the other person, the urge to strike back, and the knowing of it all.
lines.zh: 當你生氣的時候，試著找出這五者：身體裡的熱、那份不愉快、你貼在對方身上的標籤、想反擊的衝動，以及對這一切的知道。

lines.en: The Buddha compared them to foam, a bubble, a mirage, a banana tree, and a magic show. Each looks solid until you examine it.
lines.zh: 佛陀把它們比作聚沫、水泡、陽燄、芭蕉與幻術。每一樣在你細看之前，看起來都是實在的。

avoid.en: “A person is made of five parts.”
avoid.zh: 「人是由五個部分組成的。」

avoid.en: Suggests fixed components. They are five kinds of event, each arising and passing.
avoid.zh: 讓人想到固定的組件。它們是五類事件，各自生起又消逝。

avoid.en: “The second aggregate is emotion.”
avoid.zh: 「第二蘊是情緒。」

avoid.en: Emotions are compounds. The second aggregate is only the pleasant or unpleasant tone.
avoid.zh: 情緒是複合物。第二蘊只是那個樂或不樂的調子。

avoid.en: “Consciousness is what you really are.”
avoid.zh: 「識才是真正的你。」

avoid.en: This turns the fifth heap into a soul. The Buddha corrected a monk named Sāti for saying it.
avoid.zh: 這是把第五堆變成了靈魂。有一位名叫嗏帝的比丘這樣說，被佛陀糾正了。

quiz.q: What does the word khandha literally mean?
options: A heap or mass.
A soul.
A part of a machine.
A stage of life.

quiz.q: How does the second aggregate differ from “emotion”?
options: It is only the pleasant, unpleasant, or neutral tone of an experience.
It is a stronger kind of emotion.
It includes all thoughts.
It refers to the sense of touch alone.

quiz.q: What is the difference between the five aggregates and the five grasping aggregates?
options: The second are the same five when accompanied by defilements and clung to.
The second are five additional aggregates.
The first belong to humans and the second to animals.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: Why is Aristotle’s analysis of the soul called the opposing view?
options: He treats the capacities as powers of one unified substance.
He denied that living things have capacities.
He thought the soul was made of five heaps.
He did not write about perception.

quiz.q: What does the Heart Sūtra add to the early teaching on the aggregates?
options: That the aggregates themselves are empty of independent existence.
That there are six aggregates.
That consciousness is the true self.
That form is permanent.

write.en: Take a strong feeling you had today and sort it into the five heaps, one English sentence for each.
write.zh: 拿你今天有過的一個強烈感受，把它分進五堆，每一堆寫一個英文句子。

write.en: Explain “feeling tone” to someone who thinks vedanā means emotion. Use an example and about 80 words.
write.zh: 向一位以為 vedanā 就是情緒的人解釋 feeling tone。舉一個例子，寫大約 80 個英文字。

write.en: Name something you identify with, such as your memories or your character. Which aggregates does it fall under? Is anything left over?
write.zh: 說出一樣你認同的東西，例如你的記憶或你的性格。它歸在哪幾蘊之下？有沒有剩下什麼？

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.79, “Itchy” (Khajjanīya)
further.n_en: The five defined by what they do.
further.n_zh: 用「它們做什麼」界定五蘊。

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.95, “A Lump of Foam”
further.n_en: The five similes.
further.n_zh: 五個比喻。

further.t: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.48 and 22.47
further.n_en: Aggregates and grasping aggregates; what is regarded as self.
further.n_zh: 蘊與取蘊；什麼被看作我。

further.t: 《般若波羅蜜多心經》（玄奘譯，T251）
further.n_en: “Saw that the five aggregates are all empty.”
further.n_zh: 「照見五蘊皆空。」

further.t: Francisco Varela, Evan Thompson, and Eleanor Rosch, The Embodied Mind (1991), chapter 4
further.n_en: The aggregates set beside cognitive science.
further.n_zh: 把五蘊與認知科學並排。

further.t: Marvin Minsky, The Society of Mind (1986); Daniel Dennett, Consciousness Explained (1991)

dharma.title: What Kind of Ethics Is Buddhist Ethics?
dharma.title_zh: 佛教倫理是哪一種倫理學？
dharma.blurb_en: The Buddha judged actions by their results, gave rules, and taught the purification of character. Which Western theory does that make him closest to, and what words should an English-speaking teacher use and avoid?
dharma.blurb_zh: 佛陀依結果評判行為，也制定規則，也教導品格的淨化。這使他最接近西方的哪一種理論？用英文講的老師，又該用哪些詞、避開哪些詞？
dharma.verdict_en: Closest: Aristotle’s virtue ethics, for the early teaching. The Mahāyāna adds a concern for the welfare of all beings that reads like consequentialism. Kant is the furthest of the three. The likeness to Aristotle ends where the Buddha denies the self whose flourishing Aristotle’s ethics is about.
dharma.verdict_zh: 就早期的教導而言，最接近的是亞里斯多德的德行倫理學。大乘多了一份對一切眾生福祉的關懷，讀起來像後果論。三者當中康德最遠。跟亞里斯多德的相似，到佛陀否定「自我」的地方為止；亞里斯多德的倫理學談的，正是那個自我的興旺。

sections.eyebrow: 1 · What the Dharma says · 佛法怎麼說

h.en: Three strands and no theory
h.zh: 三股線，沒有一套理論

paras.en: The Buddha taught ethics constantly and never offered a theory of it. He did not ask what makes right acts right. He asked what leads to suffering and what leads to its end. Still, when the discourses give reasons for acting one way and not another, the reasons are of three kinds, and they are the three kinds this series met in the lesson on right action.
paras.zh: 佛陀不斷地教導倫理，卻從來沒有提出一套關於倫理的理論。他沒有問「是什麼使對的行為成為對的」。他問的是：什麼導向苦？什麼導向苦的止息？儘管如此，當經典為「這樣做而不那樣做」給出理由的時候，那些理由有三種；而這三種，就是這個系列在「對的行為」那一課遇到的那三種。

paras.en: The first is consequence. The Buddha tells his son Rāhula to reflect on every act of body, speech, and mind as one looks into a mirror: “Does this act with the body that I want to do lead to hurting myself, hurting others, or hurting both?” If it does, it is not to be done (Majjhima Nikāya 61). To the Kālāmas, who were confused by rival teachers, he gives a similar standard. They should not go by tradition, scripture, or logic alone. “But when you know for yourselves: ‘These things are unskillful, blameworthy, criticized by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to harm and suffering,’ then you should give them up” (Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.65).
paras.zh: 第一種是後果。佛陀告訴他的兒子羅睺羅：對身、語、意的每一個行為，都要像照鏡子那樣省察：「我想要做的這個身體的行為，會導致傷害自己、傷害別人，或兩者都傷害嗎？」如果會，就不該做（《中部》61）。對於被彼此競爭的老師們弄得困惑的迦羅摩人，他給了類似的標準。他們不應該只憑傳統、經典或邏輯。「但是，當你們自己知道：『這些事是不善的、該受責備的、被智者所批評的；去做它們，會導致傷害與苦』，那時你們就應該捨棄它們」（《增支部》3.65）。

paras.en: The second is rule. Lay followers undertake five precepts: to refrain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants. Monks and nuns keep several hundred. The third is character. The same discourse to the Kālāmas goes on to say why those things lead to harm. A person overcome by greed, hatred, or delusion kills, steals, and lies. These three are called the unwholesome roots, and an act is unwholesome because it grows from them (Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.69). The best-known summary of the teaching puts the third strand last, where it gathers up the other two: “Not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind: this is the instruction of the Buddhas” (Dhammapada 183).
paras.zh: 第二種是規則。在家弟子受持五戒：不殺生、不偷盜、不邪淫、不妄語、不飲酒。比丘與比丘尼持守好幾百條。第三種是品格。對迦羅摩人說的同一部經，接著說明了那些事為什麼導致傷害。一個被貪、瞋或癡所征服的人，會殺、會偷、會說謊。這三者稱為不善根；一個行為之所以不善，是因為它從這些根長出來（《增支部》3.69）。對這個教導最著名的總結，把第三股線放在最後，由它把另外兩股收攏起來：「諸惡莫作，眾善奉行，自淨其意，是諸佛教」（《法句經》183）。

sections.eyebrow: 2 · In standard form · 寫成標準形式

h.en: The case for reading it as virtue ethics
h.zh: 把它讀成德行倫理學的理由

steps.en: In the Buddha’s teaching the final good is awakening, and awakening consists in the complete absence of greed, hatred, and delusion.
steps.zh: 在佛陀的教導裡，最終的善是覺悟；而覺悟就在於貪、瞋、癡的徹底止息。
steps.ob_en: Accepted by all schools. Note that the goal is defined as a condition of the person and not as a state of the world.
steps.ob_zh: 各派都接受。請留意：這個目標被界定為「人」的一種狀態，而不是「世界」的一種狀態。

steps.en: An act is wholesome when it springs from and strengthens non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, and unwholesome when it springs from and strengthens their opposites.
steps.zh: 一個行為，當它出自並且增強無貪、無瞋、無癡的時候，是善的；當它出自並且增強它們的反面的時候，是不善的。
steps.ob_en: This is how the discourses define the terms. The consequentialist reader replies that the roots are called unwholesome because of the suffering they produce, so that outcomes are doing the real work.
steps.ob_zh: 經典就是這樣界定這些用語的。採後果論讀法的人回答：這些根之所以被稱為不善，是因為它們產生的苦；所以真正在起作用的是結果。

steps.en: Good conduct is therefore not a mere means to awakening. The cultivated traits are part of what awakening is.
steps.zh: 因此，善行並不只是通往覺悟的手段。被培養出來的那些特質，就是「覺悟是什麼」的一部分。
steps.ob_en: This step carries the argument. If virtue only produced the goal, as a ladder produces access to a roof, the theory would be consequentialist. The claim is that an awakened person is a perfectly virtuous person, as Aristotle’s flourishing person is. Critics point to the simile of the raft, in which the teaching is something to be left behind once the river is crossed.
steps.ob_zh: 整個論證靠的是這一步。如果德行只是「產生」那個目標，像梯子讓人上得了屋頂，那麼這個理論就是後果論的。這裡的主張是：一位覺悟者就是一位德行圓滿的人，就像亞里斯多德所說的那個活得興旺的人。批評者指向筏喻：在那個比喻裡，教法是過了河就該放下的東西。

steps.en: So Buddhist ethics has the structure of a virtue ethics: right action is what expresses and builds the character that constitutes the good.
steps.zh: 所以，佛教倫理具有德行倫理學的結構：對的行為，就是表現並且建立「構成善的那種品格」的行為。
steps.ob_en: This is the conclusion of Damien Keown’s The Nature of Buddhist Ethics (1992), which opened the modern debate. Charles Goodman replied in 2009 that the Mahāyāna, at least, is better read as consequentialist. A third group holds that the question forces a foreign grid onto the material.
steps.ob_zh: 這是基翁《佛教倫理學的本質》（1992）的結論；這本書開啟了現代的這場辯論。古德曼在 2009 年回應：至少大乘，讀成後果論比較恰當。第三派則主張：這個問題是把一張外來的格子硬套在材料上。

sections.eyebrow: 3 · The nearest Western views · 西方最接近的說法

h.en: Three theories, three fits
h.zh: 三種理論，三種合身的程度

text.en: Aristotle holds that the good for a human being is a life of excellent activity, that the excellences are settled traits acquired by practice, and that a person of practical wisdom sees what to do without consulting a rule. Each point has a Buddhist counterpart. The path is a training. The precepts are called training rules, and one “undertakes” them as one takes up an exercise. Feeling is to be educated and not merely overruled, so that the trained person no longer wants to harm. And the tradition has its own word for the trained perception of what a situation calls for: skill. Wholesome acts are kusala, skillful, the word used for a good craftsman.
text.zh: 亞里斯多德主張：對人而言的善，是一種卓越活動的人生；那些卓越是靠練習得來的穩定特質；有實踐智慧的人不查閱規則，就看得出該怎麼做。每一點在佛教都有對應。道是一種訓練。戒被稱為「學處」；人是「受持」它們，就像接下一項練習。情感要被教育，而不只是被壓過去，使受過訓練的人不再「想要」傷害。而這個傳統，對於「看出一個情境需要什麼」的那種受過訓練的知覺，有它自己的詞：善巧。善的行為是 kusala，「善巧的」；這個詞是用來形容一位好工匠的。

text.en: Utilitarianism shares the Buddha’s starting point, that suffering is bad wherever it occurs, and his scope, which is every being that can feel. The Mahāyāna comes closest. The bodhisattva vows to work for the liberation of all beings, and the eighth-century teacher Śāntideva argues, as a utilitarian would, that my suffering has no special claim because it is mine: suffering is to be removed simply because it is suffering. Stories in which a bodhisattva breaks a precept to prevent greater harm point the same way. What is missing is the sum. No Buddhist text adds the happiness of some to offset the misery of others, and the act that breaks a rule is judged by the purity of the compassion behind it.
text.zh: 效益主義跟佛陀有同樣的出發點：苦不管發生在哪裡，都是壞的；也有同樣的範圍：每一個能感受的眾生。大乘最接近它。菩薩發願為一切眾生的解脫而努力；八世紀的論師寂天，像效益主義者會做的那樣論證：我的苦，並不因為它是我的就有特別的地位；苦之所以應當被除去，僅僅因為它是苦。那些菩薩為了阻止更大的傷害而破戒的故事，指向同一個方向。缺少的是那筆總帳。沒有任何佛典把某些人的幸福加起來，去抵銷另一些人的悲慘；而那個破戒的行為，是依背後那份悲心的純淨程度來評判的。

text.en: The precepts look like Kantian duties, and both teachers hold that every person counts and that one must not make an exception of oneself. The resemblance does not go deep. Kant’s moral law is a command of reason, binding whatever one feels, and an act has moral worth only when done from duty. The Buddha issues no commands. A precept is a resolution that a person makes because he sees where its breach would lead, and its worth lies in the state of mind it expresses. Kant distrusts inclination. The Buddhist path aims to transform it. And Kant’s ethics rests on the autonomy of a rational self, the very thing the teaching of not-self takes apart.
text.zh: 戒看起來像康德式的義務；而兩位老師都主張每一個人都算數、都主張不可以把自己當成例外。這份相似並不深。康德的道德法則是理性的命令，不管一個人感受如何都有約束力；而一個行為只有在「出於義務」而做的時候才有道德價值。佛陀不下命令。一條戒，是一個人因為看出「違犯它會導向哪裡」而立下的決心；它的價值，在於它所表現的心的狀態。康德不信任愛好。佛教的道，目標是轉化它。還有，康德的倫理學建立在一個理性自我的自律之上；而那正是無我的教導所拆解的東西。

sections.eyebrow: 4 · Verdict · 判定

h.en: Who is closest, and where the likeness ends
h.zh: 誰最接近，相似到哪裡為止

paras.en: Aristotle is the closest. Buddhist ethics and his share a shape: a conception of the best condition of a person, an account of the traits that make it up, a method of acquiring them by practice, and a trust in trained judgment over formula. Utilitarianism shares the Buddha’s motive and his reach, and it captures something real in the Mahāyāna. Kant shares the least.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德最接近。佛教倫理與他的倫理學有同樣的形狀：一個關於「人的最佳狀態」的構想；對構成這種狀態的特質的說明；一套靠練習取得這些特質的方法；以及對受過訓練的判斷、而不是對公式的信任。效益主義共有佛陀的動機與範圍，並且抓住了大乘裡某些真實的東西。康德共有的最少。

paras.en: The likeness to Aristotle ends at four places. First, the self. Aristotle’s ethics is about my flourishing, and the virtues are good because they make my life go well. The Buddha teaches that the self whose life this is cannot be found, and the end of the path is described as the end of clinging to it. Second, scope. Aristotle’s virtues are those of a free male citizen of a Greek city. The Buddha’s concern extends to slaves, women, animals, and enemies. Third, the list. Aristotle counts proper pride and well-aimed anger as virtues, and the Buddha counts neither. He admits no right amount of hatred. Compassion and non-attachment, which are central for the Buddha, are not on Aristotle’s list at all. Fourth, the setting. For the Buddha acts have results that follow the agent beyond this life, by a law that no one administers. Aristotle’s ethics is complete within one lifetime.
paras.zh: 跟亞里斯多德的相似，在四個地方到了盡頭。第一，自我。亞里斯多德的倫理學談的是「我的」興旺；德行之所以好，是因為它們使我的人生過得好。佛陀教導：這個人生所屬的那個「我」是找不到的；而道的終點，被描述為對它的執取的止息。第二，範圍。亞里斯多德的德行，是一座希臘城邦裡自由男性公民的德行。佛陀的關懷延伸到奴隸、女性、動物與敵人。第三，清單。亞里斯多德把恰當的自豪與瞄得準的憤怒算作德行；佛陀兩者都不算。他不承認瞋有「恰當的分量」。而對佛陀來說居於核心的悲與無著，根本不在亞里斯多德的清單上。第四，背景。對佛陀來說，行為的果報會跟著行為者越過這一生，依循一條沒有任何人在執行的法則。亞里斯多德的倫理學，在一生之內就是完整的。

sections.eyebrow: Side by side · 並排比較

h.en: Four answers to five questions
h.zh: 五個問題，四種回答

rows.zh: 什麼使一個行為是善的？

rows.en: It springs from non-greed, non-hatred, non-delusion and leads away from suffering
rows.zh: 它出自無貪、無瞋、無癡，並且導離苦

rows.en: It is what a person of virtue and practical wisdom would do
rows.zh: 它是有德而具實踐智慧的人會做的事

rows.en: It produces the most happiness for all affected
rows.zh: 它為所有受影響者產生最多的幸福

rows.en: It is done from duty, on a maxim that can be a universal law
rows.zh: 它是出於義務而做的，所依的準則可以成為普遍法則

rows.en: Awakening: the end of the three roots and of suffering
Flourishing: a complete life of excellent activity
rows.zh: 興旺：卓越活動的完整一生

rows.en: A good will, and happiness in proportion to it
rows.zh: 善的意志，以及與之相稱的幸福
一切有感知者，一律平等
自願受持的訓練；一艘筏
粗略的指引；由判斷來決定

rows.en: Summaries of what usually works best
What is the place of feeling?
To be transformed: loving-kindness and compassion are cultivated
rows.zh: 要被轉化：慈與悲是修出來的

rows.en: To be educated to the right amount
rows.zh: 要被教育到恰當的分量

rows.en: What ultimately matters, as pleasure and pain
rows.zh: 作為苦樂，它是最終要緊的東西

rows.en: Not to be relied on. Worth lies in duty

sections.eyebrow: 5 · The step the Dharma takes further · 佛法多走的一步

h.en: Ethics as the first of three trainings
h.zh: 倫理作為三學的第一學

paras.en: In every Western theory ethics is a subject complete in itself. In the Buddha’s teaching it is the first third of a path. Ethical conduct comes first because a mind troubled by remorse cannot settle. Concentration is built on that calm, and wisdom on concentration. Then the order turns back on itself. The person who sees, as the previous pages in this series described, that there is no fixed owner of experience has lost the main reason anyone has for putting himself first. Kindness becomes easier because the wall it had to climb is lower. The tradition accordingly treats ethics both as the precondition of insight and as its natural expression, and it has practical methods for each stage: the precepts, the meditations on loving-kindness and compassion, and the analysis of the self.
paras.zh: 在每一種西方理論裡，倫理學都是一門本身就完整的學問。在佛陀的教導裡，它是一條道路的前三分之一。戒排在最前面，因為一顆被悔恨攪擾的心定不下來。定建立在那份平靜上，慧建立在定上。然後，這個次第又折回它自己。一個人如果像這個系列前幾頁所描述的那樣，看出經驗並沒有一個固定的擁有者，他就失去了任何人把自己擺在第一位的主要理由。仁慈變得比較容易，因為它本來要翻過的那道牆變矮了。因此，這個傳統既把倫理當作智慧的前提，也把它當作智慧的自然流露；而它對每一個階段都有實際的方法：戒、慈心與悲心的禪修，以及對自我的分析。

paras.en: This is why some scholars, Jay Garfield among them, say that the debate over labels misses the point. Buddhist ethics, on their reading, is chiefly concerned with changing how a person perceives: seeing others as fellow sufferers and oneself as one being among many. Right action follows from right seeing. Whether or not that is the whole story, it explains why the Buddha could teach ethics for forty-five years without once stating a criterion of right action.
paras.zh: 這就是為什麼有些學者（加菲爾德是其中之一）說，這場關於「標籤」的辯論沒有抓到重點。照他們的讀法，佛教倫理首要關切的，是改變一個人「怎麼看」：把別人看成同樣在受苦的眾生，把自己看成眾多生命當中的一個。對的行為，從對的看見而來。不管那是不是全部的真相，它解釋了為什麼佛陀可以教導倫理四十五年，卻一次也沒有陳述過「對的行為」的判準。

sections.eyebrow: 6 · How to say it to a Western audience · 對西方人怎麼講

h.en: Words that carry the wrong religion with them
h.zh: 夾帶著別的宗教的那些詞

paras.en: English moral vocabulary was shaped by Christianity, and several of its commonest words bring assumptions the Dharma does not make. “Commandment” implies someone who commands. The precepts are undertakings, and the formula for each is “I undertake the training rule to refrain from…” “Sin” implies an offense against God that calls for forgiveness. The Buddhist terms are “unwholesome” or “unskillful,” which describe an act by its roots and its results, as one would describe bad carpentry. “Good and evil” suggests two powers at war, and “skillful and unskillful” suggests competence, which is nearer the mark. “Karma” is heard as fate or as cosmic reward and punishment. It means action, and the teaching is that intentional acts shape the one who does them, with no judge involved. “Merit” can sound like a bank balance, and is better introduced as the strength that good habits build.
paras.zh: 英文的道德語彙是被基督教塑造的；其中幾個最常用的詞，帶來了佛法並不作的預設。commandment（誡命）蘊含了一位下命令者。戒是「受持」的；每一條的定式是「我受持不……的學處」。sin（罪）蘊含了對上帝的冒犯，需要赦免。佛教的用語是「不善」或「不善巧」；它們是依一個行為的根與果來描述它，就像描述一件差勁的木工。good and evil（善與惡）讓人想到兩股交戰的力量；skillful and unskillful（善巧與不善巧）讓人想到的是「能力」，比較接近靶心。karma 被聽成命運，或宇宙的賞罰。它的意思是「行為」；而教導說的是：有意圖的行為會塑造做它的人，其中並沒有法官。merit（功德）聽起來可能像銀行存款；比較好的介紹方式，是把它說成好習慣所累積的力量。

lines.en: The Buddha did not give commandments. He gave training rules, which a person takes up the way one takes up an exercise.
lines.zh: 佛陀沒有頒布誡命。他給的是學處；一個人受持它們，就像接下一項練習。

lines.en: An act is called unskillful when it comes from greed, hatred, or confusion, and it is recognized by the harm it leads to.
lines.zh: 一個行為被稱為不善巧，是因為它出自貪、瞋或癡；而它是從它所導致的傷害被認出來的。

lines.en: Before you act, the Buddha told his son, look at what you are about to do as you would look in a mirror, and ask whether it will hurt you or anyone else.
lines.zh: 佛陀告訴他的兒子：行動之前，像照鏡子那樣看看你即將要做的事，問它會不會傷害你或任何別人。

lines.en: Karma means action. What you do on purpose shapes what you become. Nobody is keeping score.
lines.zh: karma 的意思是行為。你有意去做的事，塑造你會成為什麼樣的人。沒有誰在記分。

lines.en: Ethics comes first on the path for a practical reason: a mind full of regret cannot become calm.
lines.zh: 倫理排在道的最前面，是出於一個實際的理由：一顆充滿悔恨的心靜不下來。

lines.en: In Buddhism kindness is a skill. You practice it, and you get better at it.
lines.zh: 在佛教裡，仁慈是一種技能。你練習它，然後越來越擅長。

avoid.en: “The five commandments of Buddhism.”
avoid.zh: 「佛教的五誡。」

avoid.en: No one commands them. Say “precepts” or “training rules,” and “undertake” in place of “obey.”
avoid.zh: 沒有誰在下命令。要說 precepts 或 training rules；用 undertake（受持），不用 obey（服從）。

avoid.en: “Bad karma is punishment for sin.”
avoid.zh: 「惡業是對罪的懲罰。」

avoid.en: There is no punisher and no sin. Say that harmful intentions leave their mark on the one who has them.
avoid.zh: 沒有懲罰者，也沒有 sin。要說：有害的意圖，會在懷著它的人身上留下痕跡。

avoid.en: “Buddhists must not kill.”
avoid.zh: 「佛教徒不准殺生。」

avoid.en: “Must not” is the language of law. Say that a Buddhist undertakes not to kill, and explain why.
avoid.zh: must not 是法律的語言。要說：佛教徒「受持」不殺，並且說明為什麼。

quiz.q: What test did the Buddha give his son Rāhula?
options: Before, during, and after an act, ask whether it leads to harm for oneself, others, or both.
Always obey one’s teacher.
Do whatever feels natural.
Follow the customs of one’s family.

quiz.q: Why is an act called unwholesome in the discourses?
options: It springs from greed, hatred, or delusion.
It breaks a divine commandment.
It is unpopular.
It is done by a layperson.

quiz.q: What is the main reason for classing Buddhist ethics as a virtue ethics?
options: The cultivated traits are part of what the final good is, and are acquired by practice.
It has many rules.
It counts the happiness of all beings.
It was influenced by Aristotle.

quiz.q: Where does the likeness to Aristotle end most sharply?
options: Aristotle’s ethics concerns the flourishing of a self that the Buddha says cannot be found.
Aristotle rejected practice.
The Buddha had no interest in character.
Aristotle believed in rebirth.

quiz.q: Why is “commandment” a misleading word for a precept?
options: A precept is a training rule a person undertakes, with no one commanding it.
There are more than ten precepts.
Precepts apply only to monks.
Commandments are easier to keep.

write.en: Explain the first precept to a Western friend in four sentences, without using “must,” “sin,” or “commandment.”
write.zh: 用四個句子向一位西方朋友解釋第一條戒，不要用 must、sin 或 commandment。

write.en: Someone says: “Karma means that people who suffer deserve it.” Write a reply of about 100 words.
write.zh: 有人說：「karma 的意思就是受苦的人活該。」寫一段大約 100 個英文字的回應。

write.en: Use the mirror test from the advice to Rāhula on one thing you said today. What did you find?
write.zh: 用給羅睺羅的那個「鏡子檢驗」，檢查你今天說過的一句話。你發現了什麼？

further.t: Majjhima Nikāya 61, Advice to Rāhula at Ambalaṭṭhika
further.n_en: The mirror.
further.n_zh: 鏡子。

further.t: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.65, to the Kālāmas; 3.69, the unwholesome roots
Dhammapada 183
further.n_en: The teaching in three lines.
further.n_zh: 三句話的教導。

further.t: Damien Keown, The Nature of Buddhist Ethics (1992)
further.n_en: The case for the Aristotelian reading.
further.n_zh: 主張亞里斯多德式讀法的論證。

further.t: Charles Goodman, Consequences of Compassion (2009)
further.n_en: The case for the consequentialist reading.
further.n_zh: 主張後果論讀法的論證。

further.t: Jay Garfield, Engaging Buddhism (2015), chapter 9
further.n_en: The case that it is neither.
further.n_zh: 主張兩者皆非的論證。

dharma.title: Buddha-Nature and Human Nature
dharma.blurb_en: The Buddha said that the mind is radiant and that an infant already carries the seeds of greed and hatred. What the teaching of Buddha-nature adds, which view of human nature it most resembles, and how to explain it without making it a soul.
dharma.blurb_zh: 佛陀說心是光淨的，也說嬰兒已經帶著貪與瞋的種子。佛性的教導多說了什麼？它最像哪一種人性觀？又該怎麼解釋它，而不把它講成靈魂？
dharma.verdict_en: Closest: Mencius, by a wide margin, with Rousseau second. Augustine’s original sin is the opposing view. The likeness to Mencius ends at what the endowment is: for him a set of moral feelings in human beings, for the Buddhist the capacity of any sentient mind to awaken, which the tradition insists is not a self.
dharma.verdict_zh: 最接近的是孟子，而且遙遙領先；盧梭其次。奧古斯丁的原罪是對立的看法。跟孟子的相似，到「那份稟賦是什麼」為止：對他來說，是人身上的一組道德情感；對佛教徒來說，是任何有情之心的覺悟能力，而這個傳統堅持它不是一個「我」。

sections.eyebrow: 1 · What the Dharma says · 佛法怎麼說

h.en: A radiant mind with visitors
h.zh: 一顆有訪客的光淨之心

paras.en: The early discourses contain a short text that later Buddhists returned to again and again. “This mind, mendicants, is radiant. But it’s corrupted by visiting corruptions. An unlearned ordinary person does not truly understand this.” And then: “This mind is radiant. And it is freed from visiting corruptions. A learned noble disciple truly understands this” (Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.51–52). Two things are said. The mind in itself is bright, and what darkens it has come from elsewhere and can go. The image is of guests in a house.
paras.zh: 早期經典裡有一段短短的文字，後來的佛教徒一再回到它。「比丘們，這個心是光淨的，卻被客塵煩惱所染污。無聞凡夫不如實了知這一點。」接著是：「這個心是光淨的，而且從客塵煩惱解脫了。多聞聖弟子如實了知這一點」（《增支部》1.51–52）。這裡說了兩件事。心本身是明亮的；使它變暗的東西是從別處來的，也可以離開。這個意象是屋子裡的客人。

paras.en: The same discourses refuse the conclusion that people are therefore born pure. A monk once reasoned that an infant, having no concepts, could have no fetters. The Buddha replied that a baby lying on its back has no notion of sensual pleasures, “yet the underlying tendency to sensual desire still lies within them,” and no notion of other beings, “yet the underlying tendency to ill will still lies within them” (Majjhima Nikāya 64). These tendencies are called anusaya, things that lie alongside. The early teaching holds the two claims together. Nothing in the mind’s nature is defiled, and no one arrives undefiled.
paras.zh: 同樣這些經典，拒絕了「所以人生下來是清淨的」這個結論。曾經有一位比丘推論：嬰兒沒有概念，所以不可能有結使。佛陀回答：一個仰臥的嬰兒沒有欲樂的概念，「然而欲貪的隨眠仍然潛伏在他裡面」；也沒有其他眾生的概念，「然而瞋恚的隨眠仍然潛伏在他裡面」（《中部》64）。這些傾向稱為 anusaya（隨眠），意思是「隨著躺在一旁的東西」。早期的教導把這兩個主張握在一起。心的本性裡沒有任何東西是染污的；而沒有任何人是不帶染污來的。

paras.en: The Mahāyāna gave the first claim a name and nine images. The Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra, composed around the third century, says: “All sentient beings, though they are in the various realms of rebirth, have within their bodies of affliction the womb of the Tathāgata, forever unstained and complete in its virtues, no different from me.” It is like honey in a tree, guarded by a swarm of bees. It is like gold dropped in filth, a treasure buried under a poor man’s house, and a future king in the womb of a destitute woman who does not know what she carries. In China the idea became central. The Nirvana Sūtra’s phrase “all sentient beings have Buddha-nature” was taken as the final teaching, and in the Platform Sūtra the Sixth Patriarch, on awakening, exclaims: “Who would have thought that our own nature is originally pure!”
paras.zh: 大乘給了第一個主張一個名字與九個意象。大約成於三世紀的《如來藏經》說：「一切眾生雖在諸趣，煩惱身中有如來藏，常無染污、德相備足，如我無異。」它像巖樹中的淳蜜，被群蜂圍繞守護。它像掉進不淨處的真金、像埋在窮人屋下的寶藏、像一位貧賤女子腹中未來的聖王，而她不知道自己懷著什麼。在中國，這個觀念成了核心。《涅槃經》的「一切眾生悉有佛性」被當成究竟的教導；而在《壇經》裡，六祖開悟時驚嘆：「何期自性，本自清淨！」

sections.eyebrow: 2 · In standard form · 寫成標準形式

h.en: The argument from the possibility of awakening
h.zh: 由「覺悟是可能的」出發的論證

steps.en: Awakening is possible: the defilements of greed, hatred, and delusion can be completely removed.
steps.zh: 覺悟是可能的：貪、瞋、癡這些煩惱可以被徹底去除。
steps.ob_en: This is the third noble truth and is accepted by every Buddhist school. A skeptic will ask for evidence. The tradition points to those who are said to have done it.
steps.ob_zh: 這就是第三聖諦，佛教各派都接受。懷疑者會要求證據。這個傳統指向那些據說已經做到的人。

steps.en: What belongs to a thing’s nature cannot be removed from it without destroying it.
steps.zh: 屬於一樣東西本性的，不可能從它身上去除而不毀掉它。
steps.ob_en: A principle shared with Mencius, who argues in the same way that the bareness of Ox Mountain is not its nature. Heat cannot be taken from fire.
steps.ob_zh: 這條原則是與孟子共有的；他用同樣的方式論證牛山的光禿不是它的本性。熱無法從火裡拿走。

steps.en: So the defilements are not the nature of the mind. They are adventitious.
steps.zh: 所以，煩惱不是心的本性。它們是外來的（客塵）。
steps.ob_en: Follows from the first two. Note that this is a negative claim. It says what the mind is not.
steps.ob_zh: 由前兩步推出。請留意這是一個否定的主張。它說的是心「不是」什麼。

steps.en: Therefore every sentient being has the nature of a Buddha, covered and not yet manifest.
steps.zh: 所以，每一個有情眾生都有佛的本性，被覆蓋著、尚未顯現。
steps.ob_en: The step from “the defilements are removable” to “a Buddha’s qualities are already present” is the one Buddhists themselves dispute. The Madhyamaka reading takes Buddha-nature to mean only that the mind is empty of fixed nature and can therefore change. The texts with the nine images say more, that something positive is there, and their critics, ancient and modern, have charged them with bringing back the self.
steps.ob_zh: 從「煩惱可以去除」跨到「佛的功德已經在那裡」的這一步，是佛教徒自己就在爭論的。中觀的讀法認為，佛性的意思只是：心空無固定的自性，所以能夠改變。有九喻的那些經典說得更多：那裡有某個正面的東西；而它們的批評者，從古到今，都指控它們把「我」帶了回來。

sections.eyebrow: 3 · The nearest views · 最接近的說法

h.en: Three accounts of what we start with
h.zh: 關於「我們從什麼開始」的三種說明

text.en: Mencius holds that every person has the beginnings of virtue, that bad conditions cover them without destroying them, and that cultivation is the growth of what was always there. Ox Mountain, stripped by axes and cattle, is not bare by nature. The match with the nine similes is close in form. Something precious is present in everyone, it is hidden, the person does not know it, and the teacher’s task is to point it out. Both draw the same practical conclusion: no one is to be despised, since the sage and the fool have the same endowment. Chinese Buddhists saw the kinship at once, and the vocabulary of “seeing one’s nature” is shared between the Chan schools and the later Confucians.
text.zh: 孟子主張：每個人都有德行的開端；惡劣的條件遮蓋它們，卻沒有毀掉它們；修養就是讓一直都在的東西生長。被斧頭與牛羊剝光的牛山，並不是本性光禿。它跟九喻在形式上對得很緊。每個人裡面都有某樣珍貴的東西；它被藏著；本人不知道；而老師的任務是把它指出來。兩者都引出同一個實際的結論：沒有任何人應該被輕視，因為聖人與愚人有同樣的稟賦。中國的佛教徒一眼就看出了這份親緣；「見性」的語彙，是禪宗與後來的儒者共用的。

text.en: Rousseau also holds that what we start with is sound and that corruption comes from outside. “God makes all things good; man meddles with them and they become evil.” The Buddhist term “visiting corruptions” could serve as a summary of his view. The difference lies in the source. For Rousseau the visitor is society, with its property, comparison, and vanity, and it arrived at a point in history. He therefore looks back to a lost condition. In Buddhism the defilements have no beginning, they are in the infant, and no institution put them there. Nothing has been lost. The radiant mind has never yet been uncovered.
text.zh: 盧梭也主張：我們起初所有的東西是健全的，腐化來自外面。「出自造物主之手的一切都是好的；一到了人的手裡，就全變壞了。」佛教的「客塵煩惱」一詞，可以拿來當他的看法的摘要。差別在於來源。對盧梭來說，那位訪客是社會，連同它的財產、比較與虛榮；而它是在歷史上的某個時點到來的。所以他回頭望向一個失去的狀態。在佛教裡，煩惱沒有開端；它們就在嬰兒身上，並不是任何制度放進去的。沒有什麼東西失去了。那顆光淨的心，只是從來還沒有被揭開過。

text.en: Augustine taught that human nature itself has been damaged since the first sin, that every infant is born with a will already turned the wrong way, and that it cannot right itself without help from outside. He watched babies closely and wrote in the Confessions of the jealousy of an infant who glares at another child at the breast. The Buddha’s remark on the infant’s latent tendencies makes the same observation. The interpretations are opposite. For Augustine the flaw is in the nature and only grace can mend it. For the Buddhist the flaw is a visitor and the mind can be cleared by its own cultivation. The Pure Land tradition, which holds that in this age one must rely on another’s power, is the nearest Buddhism comes to him.
text.zh: 奧古斯丁教導：人性本身自第一次犯罪以來就受了損；每一個嬰兒生下來，意志就已經轉向了錯誤的方向；而沒有來自外面的幫助，它無法自己扳正。他仔細觀察過嬰兒，並且在《懺悔錄》裡寫到一個嬰兒瞪著另一個正在吃奶的孩子時的嫉妒。佛陀談嬰兒潛伏傾向的那段話，作了同樣的觀察。詮釋卻相反。對奧古斯丁來說，缺陷在本性裡，只有恩典能修補它。對佛教徒來說，缺陷是訪客，心可以靠自己的修習被清理乾淨。主張「在這個時代必須仰賴他力」的淨土傳統，是佛教最靠近他的地方。

sections.eyebrow: 4 · Verdict · 判定

h.en: Who is closest, and where the likeness ends
h.zh: 誰最接近，相似到哪裡為止

paras.en: Mencius is the closest. He and the Buddha-nature texts share four claims: the endowment is universal, it is covered and not destroyed, the person is usually ignorant of it, and practice reveals what was present. Rousseau shares the judgment that corruption is external and little else. Xunzi and Hobbes resemble the Buddha’s remark about the infant and miss the other half. Augustine is the clearest contrast.
paras.zh: 孟子最接近。他與佛性的經典共有四個主張：這份稟賦是普遍的；它被遮蓋而沒有被毀掉；本人通常不知道它；修行所顯露的，是本來就在的東西。盧梭只共有「腐化是外來的」這個判斷，此外不多。荀子與霍布斯像的是佛陀談嬰兒的那段話，卻漏掉了另一半。奧古斯丁是最清楚的對照。

paras.en: The likeness to Mencius ends at four places. First, what the endowment is. His sprouts are feelings, compassion, shame, deference, and approval, and they grow into social virtues. Buddha-nature is the capacity to awaken, and in many texts it is identified with the empty and knowing character of the mind itself. It is prior to moral feeling. Second, who has it. Mencius is distinguishing human beings from animals. Buddha-nature belongs to every sentient being, and some East Asian schools extended it to grasses and trees. Third, the self. Mencius assumes a self that cultivates itself. Buddha-nature texts that speak of a “true self” were at once reinterpreted by other Buddhists, who warned that the phrase is a teaching device for those frightened by emptiness. Fourth, the account of the obstruction. Mencius blames bad conditions and neglect. Buddhism blames ignorance without beginning, and it adds the infant’s latent tendencies, on which Mencius is silent and Xunzi eloquent.
paras.zh: 跟孟子的相似，在四個地方到了盡頭。第一，那份稟賦是什麼。他的「端」是情感：惻隱、羞惡、辭讓、是非；它們長成社會性的德行。佛性是覺悟的能力；在許多經論裡，它被等同於心本身空而能知的特性。它先於道德情感。第二，誰擁有它。孟子是在把人與禽獸區分開來。佛性屬於每一個有情眾生；東亞的某些宗派還把它延伸到草木。第三，自我。孟子預設了一個修養自己的「我」。談到「真我」的那些佛性經典，當下就被其他佛教徒重新詮釋了；他們警告：這個說法，是給那些被「空」嚇到的人的方便教法。第四，對「障蔽」的說明。孟子歸咎於惡劣的條件與疏於照料。佛教歸咎於無始的無明，並且補上了嬰兒的隨眠；對於後者，孟子保持沉默，荀子則說得很多。

sections.eyebrow: Side by side · 並排比較

h.en: Five accounts of where we start
h.zh: 關於起點的五種說明

rows.en: A radiant mind, and latent tendencies to greed, hatred, delusion
rows.zh: 光淨的心，以及貪瞋癡的隨眠

rows.en: Four sprouts of virtue, and bodily appetites
Fondness for gain, envy, appetite, and intelligence
rows.zh: 好利、疾惡、耳目之欲，以及知性
順著天生的欲望而不加節制

rows.en: The first sin, inherited by all
Is the flaw part of our nature?
Training in conduct, concentration, and wisdom
Every person can become a Yao or Shun
The man in the street can become a Yu
Those to whom grace is given

sections.eyebrow: 5 · The step the Dharma takes further · 佛法多走的一步

h.en: Neither good nor bad, and workable
h.zh: 非善非惡，而可以修

paras.en: The Chinese debate asked whether human nature is good or bad, and the European one asked whether we are innocent or fallen. The Buddha’s analysis steps to one side of both. He describes a mind with no fixed nature at all. Greed, hatred, and delusion arise in it when their conditions are present and cease when the conditions are removed, and the same is true of generosity, kindness, and understanding. What is constant is that it can be trained. On this reading the statement that the mind is radiant is practical encouragement. It tells the practitioner that the work can succeed, as a goldsmith is told that the ore contains gold.
paras.zh: 中國的那場辯論問的是：人性是善還是惡？歐洲的那場問的是：我們是純真的，還是墮落的？佛陀的分析從兩者的旁邊走了過去。他描述的是一顆根本沒有固定本性的心。貪、瞋、癡在它們的條件具足時在其中生起，條件去除時就止息；布施、慈愛與了解也是一樣。恆常不變的只有一點：它是可以訓練的。照這個讀法，「心是光淨的」這句話是實際的鼓勵。它告訴修行者這項工作能夠成功，就像有人告訴金匠：這礦石裡有金子。

paras.en: This is also why the tradition could affirm Buddha-nature and deny the self. If Buddha-nature were a thing inside us, a pure soul wrapped in dirt, it would be the ātman the Buddha rejected. The Buddhist philosophers who defended the teaching said that it names the mind’s emptiness of any fixed nature together with its capacity to know, and that the images of gold and honey are skillful means. A modern Japanese movement called Critical Buddhism has argued that even so the doctrine is a mistake, and that it encouraged East Asian Buddhists to affirm things as they are, injustices included. The argument continues. It shows that the question raised by Mencius and Xunzi, whether to trust what we find in ourselves or to work against it, is alive within Buddhism too.
paras.zh: 這也就是為什麼這個傳統可以肯定佛性、同時否定自我。如果佛性是我們裡面的一樣「東西」，一個被污垢包著的純淨靈魂，它就會是佛陀所拒絕的 ātman。為這個教導辯護的佛教哲學家說：它所指稱的，是心「空無任何固定的自性」加上它「能知」的能力；而真金與蜂蜜的意象是方便善巧。現代日本一個名為「批判佛教」的運動論證：即使這樣，這個教義仍然是個錯誤；它鼓勵了東亞的佛教徒去肯定事物的現狀，連不公不義也包括在內。這場爭論還在繼續。它顯示：孟子與荀子提出的那個問題（是該信任我們在自己身上發現的東西，還是該逆著它下工夫），在佛教內部同樣是活的。

sections.eyebrow: 6 · How to say it to a Western audience · 對西方人怎麼講

h.en: A capacity, not a hidden soul
h.zh: 一種能力，不是藏著的靈魂

paras.en: Western listeners tend to hear “Buddha-nature” in one of two ways, and both mislead. Those from a Christian background hear a soul, a divine spark, and conclude that Buddhism has a self after all. Those drawn to self-help hear “you are already perfect,” and conclude that there is nothing to do. It helps to begin with the negative form: nothing that troubles the mind is built into it. Then give the positive form as a capacity: any mind can wake up. The comparison with original sin is useful if it is made carefully. The point of contrast is whether the flaw is in our nature. It is unwise to say that Buddhism teaches “original goodness,” since the tradition also teaches that we arrive with deep habits of greed and aversion.
paras.zh: 西方的聽眾聽到 Buddha-nature，往往有兩種聽法，而兩種都會誤導。有基督教背景的人，聽到的是一個靈魂、一點神聖的火花，於是推斷佛教終究還是有一個「我」。被自我成長吸引的人，聽到的是「你已經是完美的」，於是推斷沒有什麼事要做。從否定式開始會有幫助：擾亂心的東西，沒有一樣是內建在心裡的。然後把肯定式說成一種「能力」：任何一顆心都能醒過來。跟原罪作比較是有用的，只要作得小心。對比的要點是：缺陷在不在我們的本性裡？說佛教教的是 original goodness（原善）並不明智，因為這個傳統同樣教導：我們是帶著很深的貪與瞋的習氣來的。

lines.en: The Buddha said that the mind is naturally bright, and that what darkens it is like a visitor who can be asked to leave.
lines.zh: 佛陀說，心天然是明亮的；使它變暗的東西，就像一位可以請他離開的訪客。

lines.en: Buddha-nature does not mean a soul. It means that every mind is able to wake up.
lines.zh: 佛性的意思不是靈魂。它的意思是：每一顆心都有能力醒過來。

lines.en: We are not born pure. A baby already has the seeds of wanting and of anger. But the seeds are not what the mind is.
lines.zh: 我們不是生來清淨的。嬰兒已經帶著貪求與憤怒的種子。但那些種子，並不是心之所是。

lines.en: One old image is gold in ore. The gold does not have to be made. It has to be freed from what is mixed with it.
lines.zh: 一個古老的意象是礦石裡的金子。金子不必去製造。它需要的是從混雜物當中被提煉出來。

lines.en: Because everyone has this capacity, no one can be written off, including the person you find hardest to bear.
lines.zh: 因為每個人都有這份能力，所以沒有任何人可以被放棄，包括你覺得最難忍受的那個人。

lines.en: It is a reason for confidence, and it is no excuse for doing nothing. Gold that stays in the ore buys nothing.
lines.zh: 它是信心的理由，卻不是什麼都不做的藉口。留在礦石裡的金子，什麼也買不到。

avoid.en: “You are already a Buddha.”
avoid.zh: 「你已經是佛了。」

avoid.en: Heard as “there is nothing to practice.” Say that the capacity is complete and the work is not.
avoid.zh: 會被聽成「沒有什麼要修的」。要說：能力是具足的，工夫卻還沒做完。

avoid.en: “Buddha-nature is your true self.”
avoid.zh: 「佛性是你的真我。」

avoid.en: Brings back the soul that the Buddha denied. Say “the nature of the mind,” and explain that it is empty and knowing.
avoid.zh: 把佛陀否定的那個靈魂帶了回來。要說「心的本性」，並且說明它是空而能知的。

avoid.en: “Buddhism teaches that people are basically good.”
avoid.zh: 「佛教教導人基本上是善的。」

avoid.en: Half true. The tradition also teaches inborn tendencies to greed and hatred. Say “workable” in place of “good.”
avoid.zh: 只對了一半。這個傳統同樣教導天生的貪與瞋的傾向。用 workable（可以修）取代 good（善）。

terms: the womb (or embryo) of the Tathāgata
seeing one’s nature (Ch. jiànxìng, Jp. kenshō)

quiz.q: What does the early text say about the mind?
options: It is radiant, and it is corrupted by corruptions that visit it.
It is evil from birth.
It is a blank with no qualities.
It is identical with the body.

quiz.q: What did the Buddha say about an infant?
options: It has no concepts, yet the underlying tendencies to desire and ill will lie within it.
It is entirely pure.
It is already awakened.
It has no mind.

quiz.q: Why is Mencius judged the closest parallel?
options: He holds that a precious endowment is universal, covered by conditions, and revealed by cultivation.
He taught meditation.
He believed in rebirth.
He denied the self.

quiz.q: How does the Buddhist view differ from Rousseau’s?
options: The corruptions have no beginning and were not introduced by society.
Buddhism holds that society is always good.
Rousseau thought infants were wicked.
There is no difference.

quiz.q: Why is “Buddha-nature is your true self” a risky way to explain it?
options: It suggests a soul, which the teaching of not-self denies.
It is too difficult to pronounce.
It makes people practice too hard.
It is the Theravāda view.

write.en: Explain Buddha-nature in four English sentences to someone raised with the idea of original sin. Do not use the words “soul” or “perfect.”
write.zh: 用四個英文句子，向一位在「原罪」觀念裡長大的人解釋佛性。不要用 soul 或 perfect 這兩個字。

write.en: A student says: “If we all have Buddha-nature, why practice?” Write a reply of about 100 words using the image of gold in ore.
write.zh: 一位學生說：「如果我們都有佛性，為什麼還要修？」用「礦中之金」的意象，寫一段大約 100 個英文字的回應。

write.en: Think of a person you find difficult. What would it change, in practice, to hold that this person can also awaken?
write.zh: 想一個你覺得很難相處的人。主張「這個人同樣能夠覺悟」，在實際上會改變什麼？

further.t: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.49–52, the radiant mind
further.n_en: Four sentences.
further.n_zh: 四句話。

further.t: Majjhima Nikāya 64, the simile of the infant
《大方等如來藏經》（T666）
further.n_en: The nine similes. Short and vivid.
further.n_zh: 九喻。短而生動。

further.t: 《六祖大師法寶壇經》（T2008），行由品
further.n_en: “Who would have thought that our own nature is originally pure!”
further.n_zh: 「何期自性，本自清淨！」

further.t: Sallie B. King, Buddha Nature (1991)
further.n_en: The clearest philosophical account in English.
further.n_zh: 英文裡最清楚的哲學性說明。

further.t: Jamie Hubbard and Paul Swanson, eds., Pruning the Bodhi Tree: The Storm over Critical Buddhism (1997)
further.n_en: The modern controversy.
further.n_zh: 現代的那場爭議。

dharma.title: Compassion and the Bodhisattva Path
dharma.blurb_en: A boundless heart, a vow to free all beings, and the claim that compassion can be trained. Which Western philosopher comes nearest, where the likeness ends, and how to speak of it in English without saying “pity.”
dharma.blurb_zh: 無量的心、度盡眾生的誓願，以及「悲是可以訓練的」這個主張。西方哪一位哲學家最接近？相似到哪裡為止？又該怎麼用英文談它，而不說成 pity？
dharma.verdict_en: Closest: Schopenhauer, who made compassion the sole basis of morality and explained it by the unreality of the wall between self and other. Singer shares the scope and the demand. The likeness to Schopenhauer ends at his metaphysics of one Will, at his lack of any method, and at the pairing of compassion with wisdom that the bodhisattva path requires.
dharma.verdict_zh: 最接近的是叔本華；他把悲當作道德唯一的基礎，並且用「自他之間那道牆並不真實」來解釋它。辛格共有的是範圍與要求。跟叔本華的相似，到三個地方為止：他那套「唯一意志」的形上學、他沒有任何方法，以及菩薩道所要求的悲智雙運。

sections.eyebrow: 1 · What the Dharma says · 佛法怎麼說

h.en: A boundless heart
h.zh: 無量的心

paras.en: The early discourses describe four states of mind that they call divine abidings or immeasurables: loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity. Loving-kindness is the wish that beings be happy, and compassion the wish that they be free of suffering. The practitioner is to spread each in turn in every direction: “above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will” (Dīgha Nikāya 13). The Discourse on Love gives the measure: “Even as a mother would protect with her life her child, her only child, so too for all creatures unfold a boundless heart.” Three features stand out. The object is all beings, animals included. The state is to be cultivated, as a skill is. And it comes in a set of four, in which equanimity steadies the other three.
paras.zh: 早期經典描述了四種心境，稱之為「梵住」或「無量心」：慈、悲、喜、捨。慈是願眾生安樂；悲是願眾生離苦。修行者要把每一種依次向每一個方向遍布出去：「上、下、橫、遍一切處，以充滿慈的心遍滿整個世界，廣大、無量、無怨、無瞋」（《長部》13）。〈慈經〉給了它的尺度：「就像一位母親用生命保護她的孩子、她唯一的孩子，對一切眾生也要這樣展開無量的心。」有三個特徵很突出。對象是一切眾生，連動物在內。這種心境是要「修」出來的，像修一門技能。而且它是四個一組；其中「捨」穩住了其餘三個。

paras.en: The Mahāyāna made compassion the center of the whole path. Its ideal is the bodhisattva, who seeks awakening in order to free others and takes a vow that the Chinese tradition puts in four lines beginning: “Sentient beings are numberless; I vow to free them.” The Vimalakīrti Sūtra gives the ideal its most famous sentence. The layman Vimalakīrti is ill, and when asked the cause he replies: “Because all sentient beings are ill, I am ill. When the illness of all sentient beings is ended, my illness will be ended.” It is like parents with an only son, he says: when the son falls ill, the parents fall ill.
paras.zh: 大乘把悲放在了整條道路的中心。它的理想是菩薩：為了度脫他人而求覺悟，並且發一個誓願；中國的傳統把它寫成四句，第一句是：「眾生無邊誓願度。」《維摩詰經》給了這個理想最著名的一句話。居士維摩詰病了；被問到病因時，他回答：「以一切眾生病，是故我病；若一切眾生病滅，則我病滅。」他說，這就像只有一個兒子的父母：兒子病了，父母也跟著病。

paras.en: The same texts insist that compassion without wisdom is incomplete and can be harmful. A helper who believes that there is a solid “I” rescuing a solid “them” will be proud when he succeeds, crushed when he fails, and attached to those he helps. The bodhisattva is to act with full commitment while seeing that giver, gift, and receiver are all empty of fixed nature. Compassion and wisdom are compared to the two wings of a bird.
paras.zh: 同樣這些經典堅持：沒有智慧的悲是不完整的，而且可能有害。一位相信「有一個堅實的『我』在拯救堅實的『他們』」的助人者，成功時會驕傲，失敗時會被壓垮，並且會執著於自己所幫助的人。菩薩要全心投入地去做，同時看出施者、所施之物與受者，都空無固定的自性。悲與智，被比作鳥的雙翼。

sections.eyebrow: 2 · In standard form · 寫成標準形式

h.en: Śāntideva’s argument from the absence of a self
h.zh: 寂天由無我出發的論證

steps.en: Suffering is bad, and it is to be prevented because it is suffering.
steps.zh: 苦是壞的；而它之所以應當被阻止，是因為它是苦。
steps.ob_en: Shared with Singer and the utilitarians. An egoist will say that only his own suffering gives him a reason, and the next two steps are aimed at him.
steps.ob_zh: 這一點是與辛格及效益主義者共有的。利己主義者會說：只有他自己的苦才給他理由；而接下來的兩步就是對著他說的。

steps.en: I prevent my own future suffering although my future self does not yet exist and is not the same as I am now.
steps.zh: 我會阻止我自己未來的苦，儘管未來的我現在還不存在，也跟現在的我不是同一個。
steps.ob_en: This uses the teaching of not-self. The person who will feel tomorrow’s toothache is connected to me by a causal series and by nothing more. Parfit made the same observation and drew the same conclusion.
steps.ob_zh: 這一步用上了無我的教導。明天會感到牙痛的那個人，與我之間只有一條因果的相續，別無其他。帕菲特作了同樣的觀察，引出了同樣的結論。

steps.en: So what moves me to prevent suffering is not that it belongs to a self that is mine, since there is no such owner in either case.
steps.zh: 所以，推動我去阻止苦的，並不是「它屬於一個是我的自我」；因為在兩種情況下，都沒有這樣一個擁有者。
steps.ob_en: The step most open to challenge. A critic can grant that there is no metaphysical owner and still hold that my future states are related to me by memory and anticipation in a way that a stranger’s are not, and that this difference is a reason.
steps.ob_zh: 最容易受到挑戰的一步。批評者可以承認沒有形上學上的擁有者，卻仍然主張：我未來的狀態，是靠著記憶與預期，以一種陌生人的狀態所沒有的方式與我相關；而這個差別就是一個理由。

steps.en: Therefore the suffering of others is to be prevented as much as my own. The line between them has no basis.
steps.zh: 所以，他人的苦應當像我自己的苦一樣被阻止。兩者之間的那條界線沒有根據。
steps.ob_en: This is the argument of the eighth chapter of Śāntideva’s Guide to the Bodhisattva’s Way of Life, composed in India around 700 CE. He says that hand and foot are different and we protect both as parts of one body, and that the suffering of beings should be treated in the same way.
steps.ob_zh: 這是寂天《入菩薩行論》第八品的論證；這部論大約在西元 700 年成於印度。他說：手與腳各不相同，我們卻把兩者當作一個身體的部分來保護；眾生的苦，也應當這樣對待。

sections.eyebrow: 3 · The nearest Western views · 西方最接近的說法

h.en: Three philosophers on feeling for others
h.zh: 三位談「對他人的感受」的哲學家

text.en: Schopenhauer wrote a prize essay arguing that compassion is the only source of actions with moral worth. Self-interest explains most of what we do. Now and then a person acts purely to relieve another’s suffering, and in that moment, he says, the difference between myself and the other “is no longer an absolute one.” He calls this “the great mystery of Ethics.” His explanation is metaphysical. Individuals are separate only as appearances, and in reality all are one. The compassionate person has seen through the separation without knowing it. He found his view confirmed in the Indian texts then reaching Europe, kept a statue of the Buddha in his study, and was the first major Western philosopher to call himself a Buddhist in sympathy.
text.zh: 叔本華寫了一篇應徵論文，論證悲是具有道德價值的行為的唯一來源。自利解釋了我們所做的大部分事情。偶爾，一個人純粹為了解除別人的苦而行動；他說，在那一刻，我與對方之間的差別「不再是絕對的」。他把這稱為「倫理學的大奧祕」。他的解釋是形上學的。個體只是作為「表象」才彼此分離；在實在裡，一切是一。有悲心的人不自覺地看穿了這個分離。他發現，當時正傳到歐洲的印度文獻印證了他的看法；他在書房裡擺了一尊佛像，並且是第一位自稱同情佛教的重要西方哲學家。

text.en: Singer shares the bodhisattva’s scope. His principle extends to every being that can suffer, which has made him the leading philosophical advocate for animals, and it sets no limit of distance. He shares the demand as well: the argument of the pond, followed through, asks for a life given largely to the relief of others. What differs is the engine. Singer’s is argument. He does not ask anyone to feel more, and he is wary of feeling, since sympathy is partial and easily misled. He asks people to act on a principle they already accept. The Buddhist tradition agrees that the scope is everyone and holds that an argument alone will not carry a person there.
text.zh: 辛格共有菩薩的範圍。他的原則延伸到每一個會受苦的存在者（這使他成為在哲學上為動物發聲最主要的人），而且不設距離的限度。他也共有那份要求：池塘的論證，貫徹到底，要的是一個大半用來解除他人苦難的人生。不同的是引擎。辛格的引擎是論證。他並不要求任何人感受得更多；他對感受是有戒心的，因為同情是偏私的，而且容易被誤導。他要人們照著一條自己本來就接受的原則去做。佛教的傳統同意範圍是每一個；卻主張，單靠一個論證，載不動一個人走到那裡。

text.en: Nietzsche began as Schopenhauer’s disciple and became the sharpest critic of the morality of compassion. Pity, he argued, doubles the suffering in the world, since the one who pities now suffers too. It is often a hidden form of contempt, which enjoys the other’s weakness and its own superiority. And a culture that makes pity its highest value teaches people to regard suffering as the worst thing, when strength and greatness have always been formed by it. He named Buddhism, with respect, as the most consistent religion of the weary. A Buddhist reader will find that much of his attack lands on something the tradition also rejects. It distinguishes compassion from the grief that drags the helper down and from the pride of the rescuer, and calls these its near enemies.
text.zh: 尼采起初是叔本華的門徒，後來成了「悲憫的道德」最犀利的批評者。他論證：憐憫使世界上的苦加倍，因為憐憫的人現在也在受苦了。它往往是輕蔑的一種隱蔽形式，享受著對方的軟弱與自己的優越。而一個把憐憫當作最高價值的文化，教人把苦當成最壞的東西；然而力量與偉大，向來就是由苦塑造出來的。他帶著敬意，點名佛教是「疲憊者」最前後一致的宗教。佛教的讀者會發現，他的攻擊有很大一部分，打中的是這個傳統同樣拒絕的東西。這個傳統把悲，跟「把助人者拖下水的憂傷」以及「施救者的驕傲」區分開來，並且把後兩者稱為悲的「近敵」。

sections.eyebrow: 4 · Verdict · 判定

h.en: Who is closest, and where the likeness ends
h.zh: 誰最接近，相似到哪裡為止

paras.en: Schopenhauer is the closest. He alone among the major Western philosophers makes compassion the foundation of ethics, extends it to animals, and grounds it in the claim that the boundary between self and other is not finally real. Singer shares the range and the seriousness and replaces the feeling with a principle. Mozi and Mencius, met in the companion lesson, divide the Buddhist position between them: Mozi has its scope and Mencius its account of how care grows.
paras.zh: 叔本華最接近。在重要的西方哲學家當中，只有他把悲當作倫理學的地基，把它延伸到動物，並且把它奠基在「自他之間的界線終究不是真實的」這個主張上。辛格共有那個範圍與那份認真，卻用一條原則取代了那份感受。姊妹課裡遇到的墨子與孟子，把佛教的立場一人分走了一半：墨子有它的範圍，孟子有它對「關懷怎麼生長」的說明。

paras.en: The likeness to Schopenhauer ends at four places. First, the metaphysics. He says that all beings are one Will, which is the Upanishadic teaching of a single self.
