philosophers.name: David Hume
philosophers.tag_en: He followed empiricism to its conclusions about cause, self, and reason, and remained the most cheerful of philosophers.
philosophers.tag_zh: 他把經驗主義一路推到它對因果、自我與理性的結論，卻始終是最開朗的哲學家。
facts: University of Edinburgh, from about age eleven
A Treatise of Human Nature (1739–40); An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding (1748); Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion (1779)

life.h_en: A book written in his twenties

paras.en: Hume was born in Edinburgh in 1711 and grew up on his family’s small estate near the English border. His father died when he was two. He went to the University of Edinburgh at about eleven, which was early even for the time, and was expected to become a lawyer. He found that he could not bear the law and wanted only to read philosophy. At eighteen, he later said, there opened up to him “a new scene of thought,” and he worked at it so hard that his health broke down for several years.
paras.zh: 休謨 1711 年生於愛丁堡，在家族位於英格蘭邊界附近的小莊園長大。他兩歲時父親去世。大約十一歲他就進了愛丁堡大學，即使在當時也算早；家人期待他當律師。他發現自己受不了法律，只想讀哲學。他後來說，十八歲那年，「一片新的思想景象」在他面前展開；他用功到健康崩潰了好幾年。

paras.en: In 1734 he went to France to live cheaply and write, and settled at La Flèche, the town where Descartes had gone to school. There, between the ages of twenty-three and twenty-six, he wrote A Treatise of Human Nature. It is one of the great books of philosophy, and it failed. “It fell dead-born from the press,” he wrote, without even exciting a murmur among the zealots. He concluded that the fault lay in the manner and not the matter, and spent years recasting its arguments in shorter and more graceful works.
paras.zh: 1734 年他前往法國，為的是省錢過日子、專心寫作；他落腳在拉弗萊什，就是笛卡兒求學的那個小鎮。在那裡，從二十三歲到二十六歲，他寫了《人性論》。這是哲學史上的偉大著作之一，而它失敗了。他寫道：「它一出印刷廠就是個死胎」，連在狂熱分子當中激起一聲低語都沒有。他斷定毛病出在寫法、不在內容，於是花了多年，把書裡的論證改寫成比較短、比較優雅的作品。

paras.en: Hume never held a university post. He applied for the chair of moral philosophy at Edinburgh in 1745 and for a chair at Glasgow a few years later, and both times the clergy blocked him on the ground that he was an unbeliever. He earned his living as tutor to a mad nobleman, as secretary to a general, and then as keeper of the Advocates’ Library in Edinburgh, which gave him the books he needed to write a six-volume History of England. The History made him rich and, in his own time, far more famous than his philosophy did.
paras.zh: 休謨從來沒有擔任過大學教職。1745 年他申請愛丁堡大學的道德哲學教席，幾年後又申請格拉斯哥大學的一個教席；兩次都被神職人員擋下，理由是他不信神。他靠當一位瘋癲貴族的家庭教師、當一位將軍的秘書謀生，後來擔任愛丁堡律師公會圖書館的館長；這個職位給了他寫六卷本《英國史》所需要的書。《英國史》讓他致富，而且在他自己的時代，帶給他的名聲遠遠超過他的哲學。

paras.en: In 1763 he went to Paris as secretary to the British ambassador and found himself a celebrity. The French called him le bon David, and he was by every account a kind, sociable, and very fat man who loved good dinners. He tried to help the persecuted Jean-Jacques Rousseau by bringing him to England, and Rousseau, growing suspicious, accused him of plotting against him. The quarrel entertained Europe.
paras.zh: 1763 年他以英國大使秘書的身分前往巴黎，發現自己成了名人。法國人叫他「好人大衛」（le bon David）；從各方面的記載看，他是個和善、好交際、非常胖、喜歡美食的人。他試著幫助受迫害的盧梭，把他帶到英國；而盧梭疑心日重，反過來指控他密謀陷害自己。這場爭吵成了全歐洲的談資。

paras.en: He retired to Edinburgh, where he cooked for his friends and revised his works. In 1775 he learned that he had a fatal disorder of the bowels. He faced death without fear and without changing his views, to the dismay of James Boswell, who visited to see whether an unbeliever could really die calmly. He arranged for his Dialogues Concerning Natural Religion, which he had kept unpublished for twenty-five years, to appear after his death. His friend Adam Smith wrote that he had always considered him “as approaching as nearly to the idea of a perfectly wise and virtuous man, as perhaps the nature of human frailty will permit.”
paras.zh: 他退休回到愛丁堡，在那裡為朋友下廚，並且修訂自己的著作。1775 年他得知自己患了致命的腸疾。他面對死亡毫無恐懼，也沒有改變看法；這讓詹姆斯・包斯威爾很沮喪，包斯威爾特地去探望，想看看一個不信神的人是不是真的能平靜地死去。他安排好，讓那部他壓了二十五年沒有發表的《自然宗教對話錄》在他死後問世。他的朋友亞當・斯密寫道，自己向來認為他「接近一個完美的智者與有德者的理想，接近到人類脆弱的本性或許容許的極限」。

timeline: History of England begins to appear

idea.title_en: The central idea: Every idea is a copy of an impression
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：每個觀念都是印象的摹本

paras.en: Hume divides the contents of the mind into impressions, which are the vivid perceptions we have when we see, feel, love, or hate, and ideas, which are the faint copies of these that we use in thinking. His first principle is that every simple idea is copied from an earlier impression. This gives him a test. When a philosopher uses a word, ask from what impression the supposed idea is derived. If none can be found, the word has no meaning.
paras.zh: 休謨把心靈的內容分成「印象」與「觀念」：印象是我們在看、感受、愛、恨的時候所擁有的鮮明知覺；觀念是這些印象的微弱摹本，我們用它們來思考。他的第一原則是：每一個簡單觀念，都是從先前的某個印象摹寫來的。這給了他一個檢驗。當一位哲學家使用一個詞，就問：這個所謂的觀念，是從哪一個印象來的？如果一個都找不到，這個詞就沒有意義。

paras.en: He then applies the test to the most important ideas in philosophy, with destructive results. Necessary connection: we have an impression of one event following another and none of any tie between them. The self: “when I enter most intimately into what I call myself, I always stumble on some particular perception or other,” and so a person is “nothing but a bundle or collection of different perceptions.” Moral judgment: no observation of an act reveals its wrongness, which lies in the feeling of the observer, and no statement of what ought to be can be deduced from statements of what is. Even action is ruled by feeling: “Reason is, and ought only to be the slave of the passions.” Reason can tell us how to get what we want. It cannot tell us what to want.
paras.zh: 接著他把這個檢驗用在哲學裡最重要的幾個觀念上，結果是毀滅性的。必然連結：我們有「一個事件跟在另一個之後」的印象，卻沒有它們之間任何紐帶的印象。自我：「當我最貼近地進入我稱為『自己』的東西時，我總是碰到某個個別的知覺」，所以一個人「不過是一束或一堆不同的知覺」。道德判斷：對一個行為再怎麼觀察，也看不到它的「錯」；錯在觀察者的感受裡；而任何關於「應該如何」的陳述，都無法從關於「是如何」的陳述演繹出來。連行動也由感受統治：「理性是、而且只應該是激情的奴隸。」理性能告訴我們怎樣得到想要的東西；它不能告訴我們該想要什麼。

quote.en: Be a philosopher; but, amidst all your philosophy, be still a man.
quote.zh: 做一個哲學家吧；但是，在你一切的哲學當中，仍然要做一個人。
quote.ref: Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding, section I
quote.note_en: Nature’s advice to the thinker, as Hume imagines it, and a fair summary of how he lived.
quote.note_zh: 休謨想像中「自然」給思想者的忠告，也相當貼切地概括了他自己的活法。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: His own fork cuts him
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：他自己的叉子刺到了他

paras.en: The Enquiry ends with one of the most quoted paragraphs in philosophy. Take any book, Hume says, and ask whether it contains abstract reasoning about quantity or number, or experimental reasoning about matters of fact. If it contains neither, “Commit it then to the flames: for it can contain nothing but sophistry and illusion.” The obvious question is which of the two the Enquiry itself contains. The claim that all meaningful statements fall into these two classes is not a truth of mathematics. It does not look like a report of experiments either. By its own test the book seems to belong in the fire. The same difficulty returned in the twentieth century for the logical positivists, who revived Hume’s principle and were asked how it could itself be verified.
paras.zh: 《人類理解研究》的結尾，是哲學裡被引用最多的段落之一。休謨說，隨便拿起一本書，問它是否包含關於量或數的抽象推理，或者關於實際事情的實驗推理。如果兩者都沒有，「那就把它投進火裡：因為它包含的只能是詭辯與幻象。」顯而易見的問題是：《人類理解研究》本身包含的是這兩者中的哪一種？「一切有意義的陳述都落在這兩類之中」這個主張，並不是數學真理；看起來也不像實驗報告。照它自己的檢驗，這本書似乎該進火堆。同樣的困難在二十世紀又回到邏輯實證論者身上：他們重新啟用休謨的原則，然後被人問到，這個原則本身要怎麼檢證。

paras.en: Kant’s objection goes deeper. Hume assumed that the mind receives impressions passively and that order must be found among them. Kant replied that a stream of unconnected impressions would not be an experience of anything. To perceive a ball moving, one must already connect what is seen now with what was seen a moment ago, according to rules. The connections Hume could not find in his impressions are, on this view, what the mind contributes in order to have experience at all. Kant said it was Hume who “first interrupted my dogmatic slumber.”
paras.zh: 康德的反駁更深。休謨假定，心靈是被動地接受印象的，而秩序必須在印象當中去找。康德回答說，一連串互不相連的印象，根本算不上對任何東西的經驗。要知覺到一顆球在動，人必須已經按照規則，把此刻看見的跟片刻之前看見的連結起來。休謨在印象裡找不到的那些連結，照這個看法，正是心靈為了能有經驗而貢獻的東西。康德說，是休謨「首先打斷了我獨斷的沉睡」。

problem.title_en: A footnote that has not been forgiven
problem.title_zh: 一條沒有被原諒的註腳

paras.en: Hume’s reputation for good sense and good nature makes one passage harder to read. In a footnote added in 1753 to his essay “Of National Characters,” he wrote that he was inclined to suspect that Black people were naturally inferior to whites, and he dismissed a report of a learned Black man in Jamaica as probably exaggerated. The claim had no basis in evidence and was challenged in his own day by the philosopher James Beattie, among others. He revised the note late in life and did not withdraw it. In 2020 the University of Edinburgh removed his name from one of its buildings. The passage is sometimes excused as a prejudice of the age. It is fairer to say that the philosopher who told us to proportion belief to evidence failed, on this subject, to do so, and that the failure did harm.
paras.zh: 休謨以明理與好脾氣著稱，這讓有一段文字更難讀下去。1753 年，他在〈論民族性〉這篇文章加了一條註腳，寫道他傾向於懷疑黑人天生不如白人，並且把關於牙買加一位有學問的黑人的報導，當作多半言過其實而不予理會。這個主張沒有任何證據基礎，在他自己的時代就受到哲學家貝蒂等人的質疑。他晚年修改過這條註腳，但沒有撤回。2020 年，愛丁堡大學把他的名字從校內一棟建築上拿掉。這段文字有時被當成「時代的偏見」而獲得開脫。比較公允的說法是：這位教我們「使信念與證據成比例」的哲學家，在這個題目上沒有做到，而這個失誤造成了傷害。

said.claim: Hume was an atheist.
said.claim_zh: 休謨是無神論者。
said.en: His contemporaries called him “the great infidel,” and his arguments against miracles, the design argument, and the immortality of the soul are devastating. But he never described himself as an atheist, and his Dialogues end without a verdict. A story from Paris, told by Diderot, has him remark at dinner that he had never seen an atheist, and his host reply that he was sitting at table with seventeen. On his own principles, to assert that there is no God would go beyond the evidence as surely as asserting that there is one.
said.zh: 他同時代的人稱他為「大異教徒」；他反對神蹟、反對設計論證、反對靈魂不朽的論證，都是毀滅性的。但他從來沒有自稱無神論者，他的《對話錄》結尾也沒有下判決。有一個出自巴黎、由狄德羅轉述的故事：他在晚宴上說自己從沒見過無神論者，主人回答說，同桌就坐著十七位。照他自己的原則，斷言「沒有上帝」，跟斷言「有上帝」一樣，都確確實實超出了證據。

paras.en: No Western philosopher sounds more Buddhist than Hume on the self. He looked inward for the owner of his experiences and found only the experiences, “a bundle or collection of different perceptions, which succeed each other with an inconceivable rapidity, and are in a perpetual flux and movement.” A Theravāda monk analyzing the person into five aggregates would say almost the same. The psychologist Alison Gopnik has even argued that Hume could have heard of Buddhist ideas at La Flèche, where one of the Jesuits had lived in Siam and knew a fellow missionary’s report on Tibetan Buddhism. The evidence is circumstantial, and most scholars think Hume reached his view independently.
paras.zh: 在自我這個問題上，沒有哪一位西方哲學家聽起來比休謨更像佛教徒。他往內找自己種種經驗的主人，找到的只有經驗：「一束或一堆不同的知覺，以不可思議的速度彼此相續，處於永恆的流變與運動之中。」一位把人分析為五蘊的上座部比丘，說的幾乎是同樣的話。心理學家艾莉森・高普尼克甚至論證過，休謨有可能在拉弗萊什聽說過佛教的觀念：那裡有一位耶穌會士曾經住過暹羅，並且知道一位傳教士同伴關於藏傳佛教的報告。這些證據都是旁證，多數學者認為休謨是獨立得出這個看法的。

paras.en: The contrast lies in what each did next. Hume found his conclusions disturbing, and his remedy was to leave the study: “I dine, I play a game of backgammon, I converse, and am merry with my friends,” after which his speculations seemed cold and strained. For him the discovery that there is no self was a theoretical result with no practical use. For the Buddha it was the most practical discovery possible, because clinging to a self is the cause of suffering, and seeing through it, steadily and in experience, is release. Hume reached the insight by argument and then set it aside at dinner. The Buddhist path is a method for keeping it in view (Dharma and the West, D2).
paras.zh: 對比在於兩人接下來做了什麼。休謨覺得自己的結論令人不安，而他的解藥是離開書房：「我吃飯，我下一盤雙陸棋，我談天，跟朋友們同樂」；在那之後，他那些玄想就顯得冰冷而牽強。對他來說，「沒有自我」這個發現是一個理論上的結果，沒有實際用處。對佛陀來說，那是最實際不過的發現，因為執取一個自我正是苦的原因，而穩定地、在經驗中看穿它，就是解脫。休謨靠論證到達了這個洞見，然後在餐桌上把它擱下。佛教的道，是一套讓它一直留在視野裡的方法（佛法與西方哲學 D2）。

terms.d_en: Vivid original perceptions, and their fainter copies in thought.
terms.d_zh: 鮮明的原初知覺，以及它們在思想中較微弱的摹本。

terms.d_en: Every simple idea derives from a corresponding earlier impression.
terms.d_zh: 每一個簡單觀念，都來自一個對應的、先前的印象。

terms.d_en: The division of all knowable truths into relations of ideas and matters of fact.
terms.d_zh: 把一切可知的真理分成「觀念的關係」與「實際的事情」。

terms.d_en: The view that a person is a collection of perceptions with no underlying self.
terms.d_zh: 主張人是一堆知覺的集合，底下沒有自我。

terms.d_en: No conclusion about what ought to be follows from premises only about what is.
terms.d_zh: 從只談「是如何」的前提，推不出關於「應該如何」的結論。

terms.d_en: Hume’s own position: doubt about foundations, joined to modest reliance on experience in practice.
terms.d_zh: 休謨自己的立場：對基礎存疑，同時在實踐上適度地倚賴經驗。

quiz.q: What does Hume’s copy principle say?
options: Every simple idea is derived from an earlier impression.
Every book should be copied before it is burned.
The mind copies ideas from other minds.
Impressions are copies of ideas.

quiz.q: What did Hume find when he looked for the self?
options: Only particular perceptions, never a self apart from them.
A simple, unchanging substance.
His brain.
Nothing at all, not even perceptions.

quiz.q: Why does the last paragraph of the Enquiry seem to undermine the book?
options: The book’s own principle is neither mathematics nor experimental reasoning.
It contradicts the Treatise.
It was added by another author.
It praises metaphysics.

further.t: David Hume, An Enquiry Concerning Human Understanding
further.n_en: Start here; sections II to V and XII.
further.n_zh: 從這本開始；讀第二到五章與第十二章。

further.n_en: On personal identity, and the famous conclusion about backgammon.
further.n_zh: 論人格同一，以及關於雙陸棋的那段著名結語。

philosophers.name: Heraclitus
philosophers.tag_en: The first philosopher of process, who wrote in riddles and held that the world is a fire kept alive by its own changes.
philosophers.tag_zh: 第一位談「過程」的哲學家；他用謎語寫作，主張世界是一團靠自身的變化維持不滅的火。
facts: Ephesus, in Ionia, under Persian rule
Aristocratic; said to have given up a hereditary office to his brother
One book, now lost; about 130 fragments survive

life.h_en: A proud man in a great city

paras.en: Almost nothing is known of Heraclitus’s life, and most of what is told about it was invented later out of his own sayings. He belonged to Ephesus, one of the largest Greek cities of the eastern Aegean, which in his day was subject to the Persian king. He came from the old ruling family and is said to have handed its ceremonial office to his brother. He seems to have had no teacher and no pupils. “I have sought for myself,” he says in one fragment.
paras.zh: 赫拉克利特的生平幾乎無從得知；流傳下來的說法，大部分是後人從他自己的格言裡編出來的。他是以弗所人；以弗所是愛琴海東岸最大的希臘城邦之一，在他的時代臣屬於波斯國王。他出身古老的統治家族，據說把家族世襲的祭儀職位讓給了弟弟。他似乎沒有老師，也沒有學生。他在一條殘篇裡說：「我探求過我自己。」

paras.en: What the fragments do show is his temper. He had a low opinion of his fellow citizens and of nearly every famous name in Greece. When the Ephesians banished his friend Hermodorus, he wrote that they “would do well to hang themselves, every grown man of them, and leave the city to beardless lads.” Of the learned he said: “The learning of many things teacheth not understanding, else would it have taught Hesiod and Pythagoras.” He thought that most people go through life like sleepwalkers, each in a private world, while the order of things lies open in front of them.
paras.zh: 殘篇確實顯示出來的，是他的脾氣。他瞧不起自己的同胞，也瞧不起希臘幾乎每一個響亮的名字。以弗所人放逐他的朋友赫爾謨多羅斯時，他寫道，他們「最好全都去上吊，每一個成年人都去，把城邦留給還沒長鬍子的少年」。對於博學的人，他說：「博學並不能教人有見識，否則它早就教會了赫西俄德與畢達哥拉斯。」他認為大多數人像夢遊者一樣過完一生，各自活在私人的世界裡，而事物的秩序明明攤開在他們面前。

paras.en: He wrote a single book and, according to the tradition, deposited it in the great temple of Artemis at Ephesus. It was famous for its difficulty. Antiquity called him “the Obscure,” and a story has Socrates say that what he understood of the book was excellent, and so, he supposed, was what he did not understand, but that it would take a diver from Delos to get to the bottom of it. The style was deliberate. Heraclitus admired the oracle at Delphi, which “neither utters nor hides his meaning, but shows it by a sign,” and his own sentences work the same way. They are balanced, compressed, and often turn on a pun, and they make the reader do the work.
paras.zh: 他只寫了一本書；照傳統的說法，他把書存放在以弗所的阿提米斯大神廟裡。這本書以艱深聞名。古人稱他為「晦澀者」；有一個故事說，蘇格拉底表示，這本書他讀懂的部分好極了，所以他猜想沒讀懂的部分也一樣好，只是需要一位提洛島的潛水夫，才潛得到它的底。這種文風是刻意的。赫拉克利特欣賞德爾菲的神諭，它「既不說出、也不隱藏他的意思，而是用徵兆顯示它」；他自己的句子也是這樣運作的。它們對稱、濃縮，常常靠雙關語轉折，並且要讀者自己下工夫。

paras.en: The ancient biographer Diogenes Laertius reports that Heraclitus ended as a hermit in the hills, living on grass and herbs, fell ill with dropsy, and tried to cure himself by lying in the sun covered with cow dung, where he died. Scholars regard the story as a malicious fiction built from his own doctrines: the philosopher who said that it is death for souls to become water dies of too much water in his body. The later picture of him as “the weeping philosopher,” set beside the laughing Democritus, has no better basis. The real Heraclitus is the voice in the fragments, and there is nothing tearful about it.
paras.zh: 古代的傳記作者第歐根尼・拉爾修記載，赫拉克利特最後成了山裡的隱士，以草與野菜為食，得了水腫病，想用「全身塗滿牛糞躺在太陽下」的辦法治好自己，就這樣死了。學者認為這個故事是惡意的虛構，是用他自己的學說編出來的：這位說過「靈魂變成水就是死亡」的哲學家，死於體內的水太多。後世把他畫成「哭泣的哲學家」，跟大笑的德謨克利特擺在一起，這同樣沒有什麼根據。真正的赫拉克利特，是殘篇裡的那個聲音，而那個聲音一點也不帶淚。

timeline: Plato puts the river into the Cratylus
柏拉圖把那條河寫進《克拉底魯篇》
The Stoics adopt his fire and his logos
斯多噶學派採用他的火與 logos
Diels publishes the standard edition of the fragments
第爾斯出版殘篇的標準版本

idea.title_en: The central idea: A world held together by tension
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：靠張力維繫的世界

paras.en: The thinkers before Heraclitus had asked what the world is made of and had answered with a substance: water, air, the boundless. Heraclitus answers with a process. The world “was ever, is now, and ever shall be an ever-living Fire, with measures of it kindling, and measures going out.” A fire is not a thing in the way a stone is. It exists only while it is consuming fuel, and it keeps its shape because what it takes in balances what it gives off. He says the same of a river and of the cosmos.
paras.zh: 赫拉克利特之前的思想家問的是世界由什麼構成，回答的是一種實體：水、氣、無定者。赫拉克利特回答的是一個過程。世界「過去一直是、現在是、將來也永遠是一團永恆的活火，按一定的分寸燃燒，按一定的分寸熄滅」。火不是石頭那種意義上的「東西」。它只有在消耗燃料的時候才存在；而它之所以保持形狀，是因為吸收的與釋放的互相平衡。對於河、對於宇宙，他說的是同一件事。

paras.en: The balance depends on opposition. “Men do not know how what is at variance agrees with itself. It is an attunement of opposite tensions, like that of the bow and the lyre.” A bow is a piece of wood and a string pulling against each other. Remove the pull and nothing is left that could be called a bow. So conflict, for Heraclitus, is what holds the world together: “War is the father of all and the king of all.” Underneath the conflict is a single measure, the logos, which is the same for everyone and which hardly anyone notices. Wisdom is to understand it. “It is wise to hearken, not to me, but to my Word, and to confess that all things are one.”
paras.zh: 這個平衡靠的是對立。「人們不明白，相互乖離的東西如何與自身一致。那是一種相反張力的和諧，像弓與琴那樣。」一張弓，是一段木頭與一條弦彼此對拉。把那股拉力拿掉，就沒有什麼還能叫作弓的東西了。所以對赫拉克利特來說，衝突正是把世界維繫在一起的東西：「戰爭是萬物之父，萬物之王。」在衝突的底下有一個單一的分寸，logos；它對每個人都相同，卻幾乎沒有人留意。智慧就是理解它。「聽從的不是我，而是我的『道』（logos），並且承認萬物是一：這才是智慧。」

quote.en: The way up and the way down is one and the same.
quote.zh: 上坡的路與下坡的路，是同一條路。
quote.ref: Heraclitus, fragment 69 (Bywater), tr. John Burnet
quote.note_en: True of every road, and his shortest statement of the unity of opposites.
quote.note_zh: 對每一條路都是真的；也是他對「對立的統一」最短的陳述。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: If all flows, nothing can be said
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：如果一切皆流，就什麼都說不出來

paras.en: Plato took Heraclitus to mean that everything is changing in every respect all the time, and he argued that the view destroys itself. To say that a thing is white, there must be a white thing that stays white long enough for the word to apply. If the whiteness is itself flowing into another color while we speak, “white” was never true of it, and neither is any other description. Knowledge fares no better, since a known object would have changed before the knowing was complete. A doctrine of total flux cannot even be stated, because stating it requires words with stable meanings. This is why Cratylus fell silent.
paras.zh: 柏拉圖把赫拉克利特理解為：一切都在每一個方面、每時每刻地改變；然後他論證說，這個看法會毀掉它自己。要說一樣東西是白的，就得有一個白的東西，白得夠久，久到這個詞用得上。如果在我們說話的當下，那個白本身正在流變成另一種顏色，那麼「白」從來就不曾對它為真，別的任何描述也一樣。知識的處境也好不到哪裡去，因為被認識的對象，在認識完成之前就已經變了。徹底流變的學說甚至無法被陳述，因為陳述它需要意義穩定的詞。這就是克拉底魯沉默下來的原因。

paras.en: Aristotle added the charge of contradiction. If Heraclitus really means that the same thing both is and is not, he has denied the principle on which all reasoning rests, and there is no arguing with him. The defense in both cases is that the charges fit Cratylus better than Heraclitus. The fragments insist on measure, on a logos that does not change, and on opposites that are one in a definite respect. Whether the defense fully succeeds is hard to say when we have a hundred and thirty sentences from a lost book and no way of asking the author what he meant.
paras.zh: 亞里斯多德加上了「矛盾」這項指控。如果赫拉克利特真的是說「同一樣東西既是又不是」，那麼他就否定了一切推理所依據的原則，跟他也就無從爭辯了。對這兩項指控的辯護是：它們用在克拉底魯身上，比用在赫拉克利特身上更貼切。殘篇再三強調的是分寸、是一個不變的 logos、是在某個確定的方面合而為一的對立。這個辯護是否完全成立，很難說；我們手上只有一本失傳之書的一百三十個句子，也沒有辦法去問作者他是什麼意思。

problem.title_zh: 一位活在引號裡的哲學家

paras.en: Everything we have of Heraclitus was copied out by someone else for a purpose of his own. Plato and Aristotle quote him in order to disagree. The Stoics quote him as their ancestor and may have adjusted him to fit. Christian writers such as Clement of Alexandria and Hippolytus of Rome preserve many fragments, the first to show that the Greeks had glimpsed the truth and the second to show that a heresy was stolen from him. The quotations were first gathered and numbered in the nineteenth century, and the edition by Hermann Diels (1903) gave them the numbers still in use. We do not know the order of the sayings in the original book or how they were connected, and where two reports of one saying differ, as with the river, we cannot always tell which is closer to what he wrote.
paras.zh: 我們手上赫拉克利特的一切，都是別人為了自己的目的抄錄下來的。柏拉圖與亞里斯多德引用他，是為了反對他。斯多噶學派把他當作祖師來引用，而且可能為了合用而調整過他。亞歷山卓的克雷孟、羅馬的希波呂托斯這些基督教作者保存了許多殘篇：前者是為了證明希臘人曾經瞥見真理，後者是為了證明某個異端是從他那裡偷來的。這些引文到十九世紀才第一次被蒐集、編號；第爾斯的版本（1903）給了它們沿用至今的編號。我們不知道這些格言在原書裡的次序，也不知道它們是怎麼串連的；當同一句格言有兩種不同的記載時——就像那條河——我們不一定分得出哪一個更接近他寫下的原樣。

said.claim: “Panta rhei: everything flows.” (Heraclitus)
said.claim_zh: 「Panta rhei：萬物流轉。」（赫拉克利特）
said.en: The two Greek words that everyone associates with Heraclitus do not occur in any fragment. The phrase is a summary of his doctrine that goes back through Plato’s paraphrases and is found in this form only in a commentator of the sixth century CE, a thousand years after his death. The same is true of “the only constant is change,” which is modern. Both are fair as slogans, and neither is a quotation.
said.zh: 人人都跟赫拉克利特聯想在一起的這兩個希臘字，並沒有出現在任何一條殘篇裡。這個詞組是對他學說的概括，可以經由柏拉圖的轉述往上追溯；而以這個形式出現，只見於西元六世紀的一位註釋者，那已經是他死後一千年了。「唯一不變的就是變」也是如此，那是現代的說法。兩者當口號都算公允，但都不是引文。

paras.en: The two were contemporaries, and each made change the central fact about the world. Each used the river and the flame. Each said that people fail to see what is in front of them, and each compared them to sleepers. A reader who comes to Heraclitus from the Buddhist discourses will feel at home in sentence after sentence.
paras.zh: 這兩個人是同時代的人，而且各自都把「變化」當作關於世界的核心事實。兩人都用了河與火焰。兩人都說人看不見擺在眼前的東西，也都把這些人比作睡著的人。從佛經過來讀赫拉克利特的讀者，會在一句又一句話裡感到熟悉。

paras.en: Three differences should be kept in view. First, Heraclitus’s world has a permanent ground. The fire is ever-living and the logos is fixed, and the Stoics were not wrong to make a god of them. The Buddha points to no such ground. Second, Heraclitus praises strife. Conflict is the father of all things, and a world without it would fall apart. In the Buddhist analysis the corresponding fires are greed, hatred, and delusion, and the aim is their going out. Third, the unity of opposites is a doctrine about how contraries make one whole. The Buddhist middle way steps back from pairs of opposites, existence and non-existence, eternalism and annihilation, as two extremes that both miss how things arise. Heraclitus asks us to hear the harmony in the tension. The Buddha’s advice is to stop pulling on the string.
paras.zh: 有三個差別要放在視野裡。第一，赫拉克利特的世界有一個恆常的根基。那團火是永恆的活火，logos 是固定的；斯多噶學派把它們奉為神，並不算錯。佛陀沒有指向任何這樣的根基。第二，赫拉克利特讚美鬥爭。衝突是萬物之父，一個沒有衝突的世界會分崩離析。在佛教的分析裡，與之相應的火是貪、瞋、癡，而目標是讓它們熄滅。第三，「對立的統一」是一個關於「相反者如何構成一個整體」的學說。佛教的中道則是從成對的對立——有與無、常見與斷見——退後一步，把它們看成兩個極端，兩者都沒有看到事物是怎麼生起的。赫拉克利特要我們聽出張力裡的和諧。佛陀的建議是：別再拉那條弦了。

terms.d_en: The common, rational order according to which all things happen.
terms.d_zh: 萬事萬物據以發生的、共通的理性秩序。

terms.d_en: Continuous change.
terms.d_zh: 持續不斷的變化。

terms.d_en: The doctrine that contrary things form one whole and depend on each other.
terms.d_zh: 主張相反的事物構成一個整體，並且彼此依賴。

terms.d_en: A piece of a lost work, preserved as a quotation in a later author.
terms.d_zh: 失傳著作的片段，以被後世作者引用的形式保存下來。

terms.d_en: A Greek philosopher who worked before, or apart from, the influence of Socrates.
terms.d_zh: 在蘇格拉底之前、或不受其影響而從事思考的希臘哲學家。

terms.d_en: Heraclitus’s word for the attunement produced by opposed tensions.
terms.d_zh: 赫拉克利特用這個詞指相反張力所產生的調和。

quiz.q: Why does Heraclitus compare the world to a fire?
options: A fire exists only as a balanced process of taking in and giving off.
He believed that the world would soon burn up.
Fire was sacred to Artemis.
Fire is the hottest element.

quiz.q: What does the image of the bow illustrate?
options: A thing can be held together by opposed tensions.
War is always wrong.
Wood is stronger than string.
The Ephesians were archers.

quiz.q: Why is it hard to know what Heraclitus wrote?
options: His book is lost and survives only as quotations chosen by later authors.
He wrote in Persian.
He forbade anyone to read it.
Plato rewrote the whole book.

philosophers.name: Baruch Spinoza
philosophers.tag_en: Expelled from his community at twenty-three, he ground lenses for a living and wrote a geometry of God, the mind, and human freedom.
philosophers.tag_zh: 二十三歲被逐出自己的社群；他靠磨鏡片為生，寫下一部關於神、心靈與人類自由的幾何學。
facts: Portuguese-Jewish merchants who had fled the Inquisition

paras.en: Spinoza was born in Amsterdam in 1632, in the community of Portuguese Jews whose families had been forced to live as Christians in Iberia and had come to the Dutch Republic to practice their religion openly. His first name was Baruch, “blessed,” which he later Latinized as Benedictus. He was a gifted pupil in the community’s school and was expected to become a rabbi or to carry on his father’s business in dried fruit. The business failed, his father died, and by his early twenties he was studying Latin and the new philosophy of Descartes with a freethinking ex-Jesuit.
paras.zh: 史賓諾莎 1632 年生於阿姆斯特丹的葡萄牙猶太人社群；這些家族在伊比利半島曾被迫以基督徒的身分生活，後來遷到荷蘭共和國，才得以公開信奉自己的宗教。他的名字是巴魯赫，意思是「蒙福的」，後來他把它拉丁化為本尼迪克特。他是社群學校裡的優秀學生，大家期待他成為拉比，或者接手父親的乾果生意。生意垮了，父親過世了；二十出頭的時候，他正跟著一位思想自由的前耶穌會士，學拉丁文與笛卡兒的新哲學。

paras.en: On July 27, 1656, the congregation pronounced on him the harshest ban in its history. He was expelled and cursed “by day and by night,” and members were forbidden to speak with him, to do him any service, or to read anything he wrote. He was twenty-three and had published nothing. The document speaks of “abominable heresies” and “monstrous deeds” and does not say what they were. He seems to have accepted the sentence calmly, and he never sought to return.
paras.zh: 1656 年 7 月 27 日，會眾對他宣布了這個社群有史以來最嚴厲的逐出令。他被驅逐，並且「在白日、在黑夜」受到詛咒；成員被禁止與他交談、禁止為他提供任何幫助、禁止讀他寫的任何東西。當時他二十三歲，什麼都還沒發表過。文件裡提到「可憎的異端」與「駭人的行為」，卻沒有說那是什麼。他似乎平靜地接受了這個判決，而且從未尋求回去。

paras.en: He supported himself for the rest of his life by grinding lenses for microscopes and telescopes, work at which he was expert enough to be consulted by the scientist Christiaan Huygens. He lived in rented rooms, first in a village near Leiden and later in The Hague, owned very little, and turned down a pension from an admirer because he thought it too large. A circle of friends in Amsterdam read his writings in manuscript and discussed them by letter.
paras.zh: 此後的一生，他靠研磨顯微鏡與望遠鏡的鏡片維生；他在這門手藝上夠內行，連科學家惠更斯都來請教。他住在租來的房間裡，先是在萊頓附近的一個村子，後來在海牙；他擁有的東西很少，還拒絕了一位仰慕者提供的年金，因為他覺得數目太大。阿姆斯特丹有一圈朋友，讀他以手稿流傳的著作，並且用書信討論。

paras.en: In 1670 he published, anonymously and with a false place of printing, the Theological-Political Treatise. It argued that the Bible should be studied like any other ancient book, that its authority is moral and not scientific, and that a state is safest when its citizens are free to think and say what they like. The book was denounced across Europe. One critic called it “forged in hell,” and its author was soon known. In 1673 he was offered the chair of philosophy at Heidelberg, on condition that he not disturb the established religion. He declined, saying that he did not know within what limits his freedom to philosophize would have to be kept.
paras.zh: 1670 年，他匿名出版了《神學政治論》，還印上假的出版地。這本書論證：《聖經》應該像任何一本古書那樣被研究；它的權威是道德上的，不是科學上的；而一個國家最安全的時候，就是它的公民可以自由地想、自由地說的時候。這本書在全歐洲遭到譴責。有一位批評者說它是「在地獄裡鍛造的」，而作者是誰很快就人盡皆知。1673 年，海德堡大學請他擔任哲學教席，條件是不擾亂既有的宗教。他婉拒了，說他不知道自己做哲學的自由，得被限制在什麼範圍之內。

paras.en: His masterpiece, the Ethics, was finished by 1675. When he went to Amsterdam to see it through the press he found that a rumor was already abroad that he had written a book proving there is no God, and he put the manuscript away. He died of a lung disease, possibly made worse by years of breathing glass dust, on February 21, 1677, at the age of forty-four. His friends carried the desk containing his papers to Amsterdam and published them within the year, with only his initials on the title page. The volume was banned a few months later. For a century afterward “Spinozist” was a term of abuse, and then the German Romantics rediscovered him. The man once denounced as an atheist was described by the poet Novalis as intoxicated with God.
paras.zh: 他的代表作《倫理學》在 1675 年之前完成。他到阿姆斯特丹準備付印時，發現外面已經在謠傳他寫了一本證明沒有上帝的書，於是把手稿收了起來。1677 年 2 月 21 日，他死於肺病，可能因為多年吸入玻璃粉塵而加重；享年四十四歲。朋友們把裝著他文稿的書桌運到阿姆斯特丹，在一年之內出版了它們，書名頁上只印著他姓名的縮寫。幾個月後這本書就被查禁。此後一個世紀，「史賓諾莎主義者」是一句罵人的話；後來德國的浪漫主義者重新發現了他。這個曾經被斥為無神論者的人，被詩人諾瓦利斯形容為「醉心於神」。

idea.title_en: The central idea: God, or Nature
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：神，或自然

paras.en: The Ethics is laid out like Euclid, with definitions, axioms, and numbered propositions each proved from what came before. Its first conclusion is that there can be only one substance, one thing that exists in its own right, and that this substance is infinite. Spinoza calls it “God or Nature.” Everything else, every stone, tree, and person, is a mode of it, a way in which the one substance is for a time arranged, as a wave is a way the sea is arranged. God, on this account, did not make the world and does not stand outside it. God is the world, understood as a single self-sustaining system. And since everything follows from the nature of that system, “nothing in the universe is contingent.”
paras.zh: 《倫理學》的編排像歐幾里得：有定義、公理，以及編了號的命題，每一條都從前面的推證出來。它的第一個結論是：實體只可能有一個，也就是憑自身而存在的東西只有一個，而這個實體是無限的。史賓諾莎稱之為「神，或自然」。其餘的一切，每一塊石頭、每一棵樹、每一個人，都是它的「樣態」，是這唯一的實體暫時被安排成的一種樣子，就像波浪是海被安排成的一種樣子。照這個說法，神沒有創造世界，也不站在世界之外。神就是世界，被理解為一個單一的、自我維持的系統。而既然一切都從這個系統的本性推出，「宇宙中沒有任何東西是偶然的」。

paras.en: It might seem that such a system leaves no room for ethics. Spinoza’s answer is the point of the book. Each thing “endeavours to persist in its own being,” and our emotions are the forms this striving takes when it is helped or hindered. We are in bondage when we are pushed about by causes we do not understand. We become free, in the only sense available, as we come to understand them. “An emotion, which is a passion, ceases to be a passion, as soon as we form a clear and distinct idea thereof.” The more we see things as necessary, the less they have power to torment us, and the highest state is a calm joy in understanding that he calls the intellectual love of God. The last sentence of the book admits how hard this is: “all things excellent are as difficult as they are rare.”
paras.zh: 看起來，這樣的系統沒有給倫理學留下任何空間。史賓諾莎的回答，正是這本書的重點。每一樣東西都「努力保持自己的存在」；而我們的情感，就是這份努力受到幫助或阻礙時所呈現的形式。當我們被自己不理解的原因推來推去，我們就處於奴役之中。當我們逐漸理解它們，我們就變得自由，這也是唯一說得通的自由。「一個屬於被動的情感，只要我們對它形成清楚而分明的觀念，就不再是被動的情感。」我們愈是把事物看作必然的，它們折磨我們的力量就愈小；而最高的狀態，是在理解之中的一種平靜的喜悅，他稱之為「對神的理智之愛」。這本書的最後一句話承認了這有多難：「一切卓越的事物，既稀有，又艱難。」

quote.en: A free man thinks of death least of all things; and his wisdom is a meditation not of death but of life.
quote.zh: 自由的人最少想到死；他的智慧是對生的沉思，而不是對死的沉思。
quote.ref: Spinoza, Ethics, Part IV, proposition 67, tr. R. H. M. Elwes
quote.note_en: A deliberate reversal of Plato, who had called philosophy a preparation for death.
quote.note_zh: 刻意顛倒了柏拉圖；柏拉圖說哲學是為死亡做準備。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Why exhort a machine?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：何必勸告一部機器？

paras.en: If everything happens necessarily, then whether I come to understand my emotions is as fixed as everything else. Spinoza’s book urges the reader to take a path, and his system says that the reader will take it or not as causes dictate. The same difficulty touches his own praise and blame. He calls some lives better than others and some people slaves, which seems to assume that things could have gone differently.
paras.zh: 如果一切都必然地發生，那麼我會不會去理解自己的情感，就跟其他任何事一樣早已固定。史賓諾莎的書勸讀者走一條路，而他的體系說：讀者走不走，全看原因怎麼決定。同樣的困難也碰到他自己的褒貶。他說某些人生比另一些好，說某些人是奴隸；這似乎預設了事情本來可以有不同的發展。

paras.en: He has a reply, and it is the compatibilist’s. The book is itself a cause. Reading an argument can change a person, and a determined world in which the Ethics is read differs from one in which it is not. “Better” and “worse” describe how fully a thing realizes its own nature and need not imply that it could have done otherwise. Whether this is enough is disputed. A second objection, pressed by Leibniz and by many since, is that his one substance swallows individuals. If I am only a wave on the sea, it becomes hard to say what makes my joys and sufferings mine, or why they should matter.
paras.zh: 他有一個回答，而那是相容論者的回答。這本書本身就是一個原因。讀一個論證可以改變一個人；一個「《倫理學》被人讀了」的被決定的世界，跟一個「它沒被讀」的世界是不一樣的。「比較好」與「比較差」描述的是一樣東西把自己的本性實現到什麼程度，不必蘊涵它本來可以有別的做法。這樣夠不夠，還有爭議。第二個反駁是萊布尼茲提出、此後許多人跟進的：他那唯一的實體把個體吞沒了。如果我只是海上的一道波浪，就很難說是什麼使我的喜悅與痛苦成為「我的」，或者它們為什麼重要。

problem.title_zh: 無神論者，還是醉心於神？

paras.en: No philosopher has been read in more opposite ways. To his contemporaries the identification of God with Nature was atheism under a thin disguise: a God who has no purposes, hears no prayers, and could not have made things otherwise is no God at all. To the Romantics the same identification made everything divine. Both readings can cite the text. The geometrical form adds to the difficulty, since it hides the author’s voice behind proofs, and the proofs are often less convincing than the notes he attached to them. It is safest to begin with those notes, the scholia and appendices, where he drops the method and says what he means.
paras.zh: 沒有哪一位哲學家被人讀得這麼兩極。在他同時代的人看來，把神等同於自然，是披著薄薄偽裝的無神論：一個沒有目的、不聽禱告、也不可能把事物造成別的樣子的神，根本就不是神。在浪漫主義者看來，同一個等同，使萬物都成了神聖的。兩種讀法都舉得出文本根據。幾何學的形式又增加了困難，因為它把作者的聲音藏在證明後面；而那些證明，往往不如他附在後面的註記有說服力。最穩當的做法是從那些註記讀起，也就是附釋與附錄；在那裡他放下了方法，直接說出他的意思。

said.claim: Spinoza was excommunicated for atheism.
said.claim_zh: 史賓諾莎因為無神論而被逐出教門。
said.en: The text of the ban survives, and it names no doctrine. It mentions “abominable heresies which he practiced and taught” and “monstrous deeds,” and nothing more. He had written nothing at the time. Historians infer from later reports that he had been questioning the immortality of the soul, the divine origin of the Law, and the idea of a God who acts by choice. The word “excommunication” is also a loose fit: the Hebrew term is herem, a ban of separation, and it could in principle be lifted.
said.zh: 逐出令的文本保存了下來，而它沒有指名任何教義。它提到「他所實行與教導的可憎異端」與「駭人的行為」，僅此而已。當時他什麼都還沒寫。歷史學家根據後來的記載推斷，他那時在質疑靈魂不朽、律法出於神授，以及「神憑選擇而行動」這個想法。「逐出教門」（excommunication）這個詞也不太貼切：希伯來文的說法是 herem，一種隔離的禁令，而且原則上是可以解除的。

paras.en: Of the philosophers in this series so far, Spinoza is the one whose project most resembles the Buddha’s. Both begin from the fact that people suffer through their own emotions. Both trace the suffering to ignorance of causes. Both teach that the remedy is a clear seeing of how those emotions arise, and both report that such seeing is itself the change, with no further act of will required. Spinoza’s proposition that a passion ceases to be a passion once it is clearly understood could stand as a description of mindfulness. Both deny that there is a free-standing self that owns its states, and both end in a calm they decline to call a reward: “Blessedness is not the reward of virtue, but virtue itself.”
paras.zh: 在這個系列到目前為止談過的哲學家裡，史賓諾莎是計畫最像佛陀的一位。兩人都從這個事實出發：人因為自己的情感而受苦。兩人都把苦追溯到對原因的無知。兩人都教導，解方是清楚地看見這些情感怎麼生起；而且兩人都說，這樣的看見本身就是改變，不需要再加上一個意志的動作。史賓諾莎那條命題——被動的情感一旦被清楚理解，就不再是被動的情感——可以直接拿來描述正念。兩人都否認有一個獨立自存、擁有種種狀態的自我；兩人最後也都歸於一種平靜，而且都不肯把它叫作報酬：「至福不是德行的報酬，而是德行本身。」

paras.en: The difference is in the foundations. Spinoza’s world rests on one eternal, infinite substance, and liberation is seeing oneself as part of it, under what he calls the aspect of eternity. That is close to the Vedānta teaching that the self is one with Brahman, the view the Buddha’s followers argued against for a thousand years. Buddhism denies any such substance. For the Buddha things arise in dependence on one another, and there is no further thing in which they all inhere. Spinoza’s remedy is also purely intellectual. He offers arguments. The Buddhist path adds a training of attention and conduct, on the view that understanding which stays in the study, as Hume’s did, does not reach the passions (Dharma and the West, D17).
paras.zh: 差別在地基。史賓諾莎的世界建立在一個永恆、無限的實體上，而解脫就是把自己看成它的一部分，他稱之為「在永恆的相下」來看。這很接近吠檀多「我與梵合一」的教義，也就是佛陀的後學與之論辯了一千年的那種見解。佛教否認有任何這樣的實體。在佛陀看來，事物彼此依待而生起，並沒有另一個東西讓它們全都依附其中。史賓諾莎的藥方也是純粹理智上的：他提供的是論證。佛教的道路則多了對注意力與行為的訓練，因為它認為，像休謨那樣留在書房裡的理解，到不了情感那裡（佛法與西方哲學 D17）。

terms.d_en: In Spinoza, that which exists in itself and is conceived through itself. There is only one.
terms.d_zh: 在史賓諾莎，指存在於自身之內、並且透過自身而被理解的東西。只有一個。

terms.d_en: A particular thing, understood as a way in which substance exists.
terms.d_zh: 個別的事物，被理解為實體存在的一種方式。

terms.d_en: The view that God and the universe are identical. The word was coined after Spinoza’s death.
terms.d_zh: 主張神與宇宙是同一的。這個詞是史賓諾莎死後才造出來的。

terms.d_en: The striving by which each thing endeavors to persist in its own being.
terms.d_zh: 每一樣東西努力保持自己存在的那份力求。

terms.d_en: Seeing a thing as it follows necessarily from the nature of the whole.
terms.d_zh: 把一樣東西看作從整體的本性必然推出的。

terms.d_en: An explanatory note attached to a proof.
terms.d_zh: 附在證明之後的說明性註記。

quiz.q: What does Spinoza mean by “God or Nature”?
options: God is the one self-sustaining system of which all things are modes.
God created nature and then withdrew.
Nature is a poetic name for a personal God.
There are two gods.

quiz.q: How, according to the Ethics, does a person become free?
options: By understanding the causes of his own emotions.
By an uncaused act of will.
By obeying the law of the state.
By escaping from nature.

quiz.q: Why did Spinoza decline the chair at Heidelberg?
options: He could not tell what limits would be placed on his freedom to philosophize.
The salary was too small.
He did not know German.
He had been forbidden to teach.

further.t: Baruch Spinoza, Ethics, translated by R. H. M. Elwes
further.n_en: Begin with the Appendix to Part I, then the Preface to Part IV, then Part V.
further.n_zh: 先讀第一部分的附錄，再讀第四部分的序言，然後是第五部分。

further.t: Steven Nadler, Spinoza: A Life (1999)
further.n_en: The standard biography.
further.n_zh: 標準的傳記。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Baruch Spinoza”

philosophers.name: Augustine
philosophers.tag_en: A teacher of rhetoric who turned philosophy inward, and who wrote the first autobiography in order to understand his own will.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位修辭學教師；他把哲學轉向內在，並且為了理解自己的意志，寫下了第一部自傳。
facts: August 28, 430, Hippo Regius, during the Vandal siege
Patricius, a pagan town councilor; Monica, a Christian
Teacher of rhetoric; from 395, bishop of Hippo
Confessions (c. 397–400); On the Trinity; The City of God (413–426)
Latin, about five million words of which survive

life.h_en: A clever boy from a small town

paras.en: Augustine was born in 354 in Thagaste, a market town in the hills of what is now eastern Algeria, then a prosperous province of the Roman Empire. His father, Patricius, was a minor official who scraped together the money to educate a gifted son. His mother, Monica, was a devout Christian who wanted the son to be one too, and followed him across the Mediterranean to see it done. He was sent to study rhetoric at Carthage, the great city of Roman Africa, where, he says, “a cauldron of unholy loves” sang about his ears. He took a mistress, whose name he never tells us, lived with her faithfully for some fifteen years, and had a son by her.
paras.zh: 奧古斯丁 354 年生於塔加斯特，一個位於今天阿爾及利亞東部山區的市集小鎮，當時是羅馬帝國一個富庶的行省。父親帕特里修斯是個小官員，勉強湊出錢來栽培這個有天分的兒子。母親莫尼加是虔誠的基督徒，希望兒子也成為基督徒，並且跟著他渡過地中海，要親眼看到這件事成真。他被送到迦太基——羅馬非洲的大城——學修辭學；他說，在那裡「一口不潔之愛的大鍋」在他耳邊沸騰作響。他有了一位情婦，卻從沒告訴我們她的名字；他忠實地跟她同居了大約十五年，並且跟她生了一個兒子。

paras.en: At nineteen he read a dialogue of Cicero, now lost, that exhorted the reader to philosophy, and it changed his ambitions. For nine years he followed the Manichees, who taught that the world is a battleground between a good power and an evil one, a doctrine that explained why he did what he disapproved of. He became a teacher of rhetoric at Carthage, then at Rome, and in 384 won the public chair of rhetoric at Milan, the seat of the emperor’s court. He was thirty and had reached the top of his profession.
paras.zh: 十九歲那年，他讀了西塞羅的一篇對話錄（現已失傳），那篇對話錄勸人從事哲學，從此改變了他的志向。有九年之久，他追隨摩尼教徒；他們教導世界是善的力量與惡的力量之間的戰場，這套學說解釋了他為什麼會去做自己並不贊同的事。他先在迦太基、後來在羅馬當修辭學教師；384 年，他取得了米蘭的公立修辭學教席，那是皇帝宮廷的所在地。當時他三十歲，已經爬到了這一行的頂端。

paras.en: In Milan two things undid his certainties. He heard the bishop, Ambrose, interpret the scriptures in a way an educated man could respect, and he read the Platonist philosophers, who convinced him that reality is not all bodily and that evil is not a substance but a lack. He was persuaded, and he could not act. For months he wanted to change his life and found that he did not want it enough. “Give me chastity and continency,” he had once prayed, “only not yet.” The crisis came in a garden in the summer of 386. Weeping under a fig tree, he heard a child’s voice from a neighboring house chanting “Take up and read.” He opened a book of Paul’s letters at random, read a single verse, and the struggle was over.
paras.zh: 在米蘭，有兩件事瓦解了他原有的種種確信。他聽到主教安波羅修用一種受過教育的人也能尊重的方式詮釋經文；他也讀了柏拉圖學派哲學家的著作，他們讓他相信，實在並不全是物體性的，而惡不是一種實體，是一種缺乏。他被說服了，卻無法行動。一連好幾個月，他想改變自己的生活，卻發現自己想得不夠。他曾經這樣禱告過：「求你賜我貞潔與節制，只是先不要現在。」危機在 386 年夏天的一座花園裡到來。他在一棵無花果樹下哭泣，聽到鄰家傳來一個孩子的聲音，反覆唱著「拿起來讀」。他隨手翻開一本保羅書信，讀了一節，掙扎就結束了。

paras.en: He resigned his chair, was baptized by Ambrose at Easter 387, and set out for Africa. Monica died on the journey, at the port of Ostia, after a conversation with her son that he records as the happiest hour of his life. Back home he meant to live quietly with a few friends. In 391, visiting the port city of Hippo, he was seized by the congregation and ordained a priest against his will, and four years later he was its bishop.
paras.zh: 他辭去教席，387 年復活節由安波羅修為他施洗，然後啟程回非洲。莫尼加在途中、在奧斯提亞港去世；去世前她跟兒子有過一次談話，他把那次談話記為自己一生中最幸福的時刻。回到家鄉，他本來打算跟幾個朋友安靜度日。391 年，他造訪港口城市希波時，被當地會眾硬拉住，違背他的意願按立為神父；四年後，他成了那裡的主教。

paras.en: For thirty-five years he preached, judged disputes, answered letters from all over the Roman world, and wrote constantly. The Confessions dates from the first years of his episcopate. In 410 an army of Goths sacked Rome, and pagans blamed the disaster on the abandonment of the old gods. Augustine’s reply, The City of God, took thirteen years to write. It argues that no earthly state can be the object of a person’s final loyalty, and it shaped European political thought for a millennium. He died on August 28, 430, in his seventy-sixth year, while an army of Vandals was besieging Hippo. The city fell soon afterward. His library, by good fortune, survived.
paras.zh: 有三十五年之久，他講道、裁決糾紛、回覆來自羅馬世界各地的信件，並且不停地寫作。《懺悔錄》寫於他擔任主教的最初幾年。410 年，一支哥德人的軍隊洗劫了羅馬，異教徒把這場災難歸咎於拋棄了舊日的眾神。奧古斯丁的回應是《上帝之城》，花了十三年才寫成。它論證：沒有任何地上的國家，可以成為一個人最終效忠的對象；這本書塑造了此後一千年的歐洲政治思想。430 年 8 月 28 日，他在七十六歲那年去世，當時一支汪達爾人的軍隊正在圍攻希波。不久之後城就陷落了。幸運的是，他的藏書保存了下來。

idea.title_en: The central idea: The divided will
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：分裂的意志

paras.en: Greek philosophy had on the whole agreed with Socrates that to know the good is to do it, and that wrongdoing is a kind of ignorance. Augustine’s own experience told him otherwise. In the garden he knew perfectly well what he ought to do, and wanted to do it, and did not. He describes the puzzle with a rhetorician’s precision: “The mind commands the body, and it obeys instantly; the mind commands itself, and is resisted.” I tell my hand to move and it moves. I tell my will to will, and it only half obeys. His explanation is that the will is divided against itself, pulled one way by long habit and another by what it now sees to be better. Knowledge by itself does not move us. What moves us is what we love.
paras.zh: 希臘哲學大體上同意蘇格拉底：知道善就會行善，作惡是一種無知。奧古斯丁自己的經驗告訴他並非如此。在那座花園裡，他清清楚楚知道自己該做什麼，也想去做，卻沒有做。他用修辭學家的精確描述了這個難題：「心靈命令身體，身體立刻服從；心靈命令它自己，卻遭到抗拒。」我叫我的手動，它就動。我叫我的意志去意願，它只服從一半。他的解釋是：意志自己跟自己分裂了，一邊被長久的習慣拉著，另一邊被它現在看出來更好的東西拉著。知識本身並不推動我們。推動我們的，是我們所愛的東西。

paras.en: From this came a new way of doing philosophy. If the important facts are inside, in memory, desire, and will, then the philosopher’s method is to look inward and describe honestly what is found. The Confessions does this at length, examining an infant’s jealousy, a boy’s theft of pears he did not even want, a grown man’s grief. Its first paragraph states the theory that the rest illustrates: “Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.” Human desire, he holds, has no finite object that can satisfy it, and a life is made orderly or disorderly by the order of its loves. The same inward turn produced his analysis of time, and an argument against skepticism that Descartes would repeat twelve centuries later: if I am mistaken, I exist.
paras.zh: 由此產生了一種做哲學的新方式。如果重要的事實都在裡面——在記憶、欲望與意志裡——那麼哲學家的方法就是往內看，並且誠實地描述所見。《懺悔錄》詳盡地這樣做了：它檢視嬰兒的嫉妒、一個男孩偷他根本不想要的梨子、一個成年人的悲傷。它的第一段就陳述了全書其餘部分要說明的那個理論：「你為你自己造了我們，我們的心若不安息在你裡面，就不得安寧。」他主張，人的欲望沒有任何有限的對象可以滿足它；而一個人的生活有序或失序，取決於他所愛之物的次序。同一個向內的轉向，產生了他對時間的分析，也產生了一個反駁懷疑論的論證，笛卡兒在十二個世紀之後會再說一次：如果我弄錯了，我就存在。

quote.en: Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.
quote.zh: 你為你自己造了我們，我們的心若不安息在你裡面，就不得安寧。
quote.ref: Augustine, Confessions I.1, tr. E. B. Pusey
quote.note_en: The first paragraph of the book, and the thesis of the whole.
quote.note_zh: 全書的第一段，也是整本書的論旨。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Can we be blamed for what we cannot help?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：不由自主的事，可以怪我們嗎？

paras.en: As a young bishop Augustine wrote a book defending free will. Evil, he argued, comes from the misuse of a freedom that God rightly gave. As he grew older, his reflection on his own conversion led him to a darker view. The will, damaged since the first human sin, cannot turn itself toward the good. It must be turned by grace, which God gives to some and not to others, for reasons we cannot see. The British monk Pelagius was appalled. If people cannot avoid sin without a help that is not in their power to obtain, he asked, how can they justly be blamed, and what becomes of moral effort? A command that cannot be obeyed is not a just command.
paras.zh: 奧古斯丁年輕當主教的時候，寫過一本為自由意志辯護的書。他論證說，惡來自對自由的誤用，而那份自由是上帝正當地賜予的。隨著年歲增長，他對自己皈依經驗的反省，把他帶到一個更陰暗的看法。意志自從人類的第一次犯罪就受了損，無法自己轉向善。它必須被恩典轉過去；而恩典，上帝給了某些人、沒給另一些人，理由我們看不見。不列顛的修士伯拉糾對此大為震驚。他問：如果人沒有一種「不在自己能力範圍內取得」的幫助，就無法避免犯罪，那麼責備他們怎麼能算公正？道德上的努力又成了什麼？一條無法被遵守的命令，不是公正的命令。

paras.en: Augustine won the argument in the councils of the Church and never gave a reply that satisfied his critics. The difficulty is the one met in the lesson on free will, in a theological form: responsibility seems to require that we could have done otherwise, and his account of grace seems to deny it. A second charge concerns his conduct as bishop. Confronted by a rival church in Africa, he came to defend the use of imperial force to compel its members to conform, and his arguments were quoted by persecutors for centuries afterward.
paras.zh: 奧古斯丁在教會的會議上贏了這場爭論，卻始終沒有給出一個讓批評者滿意的回答。這個困難，就是在「自由意志」那一課遇到的那一個，只是換成了神學的形式：責任似乎要求我們「本來可以有別的做法」，而他對恩典的說明似乎否定了這一點。第二項指控針對的是他擔任主教時的作為。面對非洲的一個敵對教派，他後來為動用帝國的武力、強迫其成員歸順辯護；此後好幾個世紀，他的論證都被迫害者拿來引用。

problem.title_en: A book addressed to someone else

paras.en: The Confessions is not addressed to its reader. From the first line to the last it speaks to God, and we overhear. That shapes what it can tell us. The author selects the episodes that show a pattern of wandering and return, and he passes quickly over much that a biographer would want, including his years as a teacher and the name of the woman he lived with. He also wrote it a decade after the events, as a bishop with opponents to answer. None of this makes it unreliable in the ordinary sense. It makes it an argument in the form of a life. The word confessio in his Latin means praise and acknowledgment as much as admission of fault, and the last four of its thirteen books are philosophy and scriptural commentary, on memory, time, and creation.
paras.zh: 《懺悔錄》不是寫給讀者的。從第一行到最後一行，它都在對上帝說話，而我們是在旁邊聽到的。這決定了它能告訴我們什麼。作者挑選的是那些顯示出「迷途與歸返」這個樣式的片段；傳記作者會想知道的許多事，他都匆匆帶過，包括他當教師的那些年，以及與他同居的那位女子的名字。而且他是在事隔十年之後寫的，當時他是一位有對手要回應的主教。這一切並不使它在通常的意義上不可靠。這使它成為一個以「一生」為形式的論證。在他的拉丁文裡，confessio 這個詞的意思既是讚美與承認，也是認錯；而全書十三卷的最後四卷，是談記憶、時間與創造的哲學與經文註解。

said.claim: “The world is a book, and those who do not travel read only one page.” (Augustine)
said.claim_zh: 「世界是一本書，不旅行的人只讀了其中一頁。」（奧古斯丁）
said.en: This line appears on travel posters with Augustine’s name and in none of his five million surviving words. It seems to have been attached to him in the eighteenth century. He did compare the created world to a book in which God can be read, a different thought. A saying that sounds almost as modern is authentic: “Give me chastity and continency, only not yet” (Confessions VIII.7).
said.zh: 這句話掛著奧古斯丁的名字出現在旅遊海報上，卻不見於他流傳下來的五百萬字當中的任何一處。它似乎是在十八世紀才被安到他頭上的。他確實把受造的世界比作一本可以從中讀出上帝的書，但那是另一個想法。有一句聽來幾乎同樣現代的話，倒是真的：「求你賜我貞潔與節制，只是先不要現在」（《懺悔錄》卷八第七章）。

paras.en: The restless heart of the Confessions and the Buddha’s first two truths describe the same condition. Human beings want, obtain, and want again, and no finite thing ends the wanting. Augustine examined this with a closeness that no Western writer before him had attempted, and a Buddhist reader will recognize his account of how habit hardens into a chain. “The mind commands itself, and is resisted” is a fair description of what anyone finds on first trying to meditate.
paras.zh: 《懺悔錄》裡那顆不安的心，跟佛陀的前兩聖諦描述的是同一種狀態。人想要、得到、又再想要，而沒有任何有限的東西能終止這份「想要」。奧古斯丁對此檢視之細密，是他之前的西方作者不曾嘗試過的；佛教的讀者會認出他對「習慣如何硬化成鎖鍊」的描述。「心靈命令它自己，卻遭到抗拒」，相當貼切地描述了任何人第一次嘗試禪修時發現的事。

paras.en: The two then go in opposite directions. Augustine concludes that desire has been aimed at the wrong objects, and that it will rest when it is aimed at the one object that is infinite. On his view the remedy for craving is a greater love. The Buddha concludes that craving itself is the cause of the trouble, whatever its object, and that it can cease. Augustine also holds that the will cannot heal itself and must be healed from outside. Early Buddhism teaches the opposite: “you yourselves must make the effort; the Buddhas only point the way” (Dhammapada 276). Yet the Buddhist world contains a tradition that sounds remarkably like him. Pure Land teachers such as Shinran held that in a degenerate age no one can reach awakening by self-power, and that one must rely wholly on the other-power of Amitābha’s vow. The quarrel between Augustine and Pelagius was fought out again, on other ground, between the Pure Land schools and their critics (Dharma and the West, D23).
paras.zh: 接下來，兩人往相反的方向走。奧古斯丁的結論是：欲望一直瞄準了錯誤的對象；等它瞄準那唯一無限的對象，它就會安息。照他的看法，對治渴求的藥是一份更大的愛。佛陀的結論是：不管對象是什麼，渴愛本身就是問題的原因，而它是可以止息的。奧古斯丁還主張，意志無法醫治自己，必須從外面被醫治。早期佛教教的正好相反：「你們自己應當努力；如來只是指路的人」（《法句經》276）。然而佛教世界裡有一個傳統，聽起來跟他驚人地相像。親鸞這樣的淨土祖師主張，在末法時代沒有人能靠自力達到覺悟，必須完全仰賴阿彌陀佛本願的他力。奧古斯丁與伯拉糾之間的爭論，在另一片土地上，在淨土宗與批評它的人之間又打了一次（佛法與西方哲學 D23）。

terms.d_en: The power of choosing and loving, which Augustine made central to the account of human action.
terms.d_zh: 選擇與愛的能力；奧古斯丁把它放在說明人類行為的核心位置。

terms.d_en: Divine help that is not earned, without which, on Augustine’s later view, the will cannot turn to the good.
terms.d_zh: 不是掙來的神的幫助；依奧古斯丁晚期的看法，沒有它，意志就無法轉向善。

terms.d_en: His account of evil: it is the absence of a good that ought to be present, with no being of its own.
terms.d_zh: 他對惡的說明：惡是本該存在的善的缺席，它自己沒有存有。

terms.d_en: The turn toward the inner life as the place where truth is to be sought.
terms.d_zh: 轉向內在生活，把它當作尋求真理的所在。

terms.d_en: The doctrine that human nature has been damaged since the first sin and inclines toward wrong.
terms.d_zh: 主張人性自第一次犯罪以來就受了損，並且傾向於惡。

terms.d_en: A religion teaching that the world is the scene of a struggle between two equal powers, light and darkness.
terms.d_zh: 一種宗教，教導世界是光明與黑暗兩股對等力量爭鬥的場所。

quiz.q: What did Augustine’s experience in the garden lead him to deny?
options: That knowing the good is enough to do it.
That the world was created.
That memory is reliable.
That time is real.

quiz.q: What does he mean by the “restless heart”?
options: Human desire has no finite object that can satisfy it.
People sleep badly in hot climates.
The heart is the organ of thought.
Travel makes people unhappy.

quiz.q: What was Pelagius’s objection?
options: If people cannot avoid sin without grace they cannot obtain, they cannot justly be blamed.
Grace does not exist.
The Confessions was a forgery.
Free will is an illusion.

further.t: Augustine, Confessions, translated by E. B. Pusey
further.n_en: Books I–IX are the life; Book VIII is the garden; Books X and XI are memory and time.
further.n_zh: 卷一到九是生平；卷八是花園；卷十與十一談記憶與時間。

further.t: Peter Brown, Augustine of Hippo: A Biography (1967; revised 2000)
further.n_en: One of the great biographies of the twentieth century.
further.n_zh: 二十世紀最出色的傳記之一。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Augustine of Hippo”

philosophers.name: Zhuangzi
philosophers.place_en: Meng, in the state of Song
philosophers.tag_en: A minor official who turned down a kingdom’s highest office, and whose book of stories is the funniest and most unsettling work of ancient philosophy.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個回絕了一國相位的小吏；他那本由故事組成的書，是古代哲學裡最好笑、也最讓人不安的作品。
facts: c. 369 BCE, Meng (probably near modern Shangqiu, Henan)
Clerk at the Lacquer Garden 漆園吏
Zhuangzi, 33 chapters in the received text; the first seven are thought to be his own
Mencius, Hui Shi; Kings Hui of Liang and Xuan of Qi

life.h_en: The clerk at the Lacquer Garden

paras.en: Almost everything known about Zhuangzi’s life fits into a paragraph. Sima Qian, writing about two centuries later, records that he was a man of Meng, that his name was Zhou, and that he once held a post at a place called the Lacquer Garden. He lived at the time of King Hui of Liang and King Xuan of Qi, which puts him in the second half of the fourth century BCE, the most violent period of the Warring States. The historian adds that there was nothing his learning did not look into, that his writing ran to more than a hundred thousand characters, and that it was mostly made of parables. His words, says Sima Qian, were like a flood that spread wherever it pleased, and for that reason no king or minister could make use of him.
paras.zh: 關於莊子生平，我們所知的幾乎一段話就說得完。大約兩個世紀之後的司馬遷記載：他是蒙人，名周，曾經在一個叫漆園的地方當過小吏。他與梁惠王、齊宣王同時，這把他放在西元前四世紀的後半，戰國最暴烈的時期。這位史家還說，他的學問「無所不闚」，著書十餘萬言，「大抵率寓言也」。司馬遷說，他的話「洸洋自恣以適己」，像大水一樣隨意漫開，所以王公大人都沒辦法用他。

paras.en: One story is told in two versions. In Sima Qian’s, King Wei of Chu sent messengers with rich gifts and the offer of the post of chief minister. Zhuangzi laughed and asked whether they had seen the ox that is fattened for the great sacrifice. It is fed for years and dressed in embroidered cloth, and on the day it is led into the temple it would gladly change places with a lonely piglet. “Go away, and do not defile me.” In the version in the Zhuangzi itself he is fishing and does not turn his head. He has heard that Chu keeps a sacred tortoise, three thousand years dead, wrapped in cloth in the ancestral hall. Would that tortoise prefer to be dead with its bones honored, or alive and dragging its tail in the mud? Alive in the mud, the officials admit. “Then go. I will drag my tail in the mud.”
paras.zh: 有一個故事流傳著兩個版本。在司馬遷的版本裡，楚威王派使者帶著厚禮，許他當宰相。莊子笑了，問他們見過郊祭用的那頭犧牛沒有：養了好幾年，披上繡花的衣料；等到被牽進太廟的那一天，牠就算想當一隻孤單的小豬，也辦不到了。「你們快走，不要玷污我。」在《莊子》書裡的版本，他正在釣魚，連頭也不回。他聽說楚國有一隻神龜，死了三千年，用布包著供在廟堂之上。這隻龜是寧願死了、留下骨頭受人尊貴呢？還是寧願活著、拖著尾巴在泥巴裡爬？兩位大夫承認：寧願活著在泥裡。「那就請回吧。我要拖著尾巴在泥巴裡爬。」

paras.en: The other person who appears again and again in the book is Hui Shi, called Huizi, the leading logician of the age and for a time chief minister of Liang. The two disagreed about everything. When Zhuangzi came to visit, Huizi was told that he had come to take his post, and had the city searched for three days. Zhuangzi walked in and told him about a southern bird that rests only on the parasol tree and drinks only from sweet springs. An owl that had got hold of a rotten rat looked up as it flew over and screeched to protect its prize. “Are you screeching at me over your state of Liang?” The debate on the bridge over the Hao, about whether one can know that fish are happy, is the most famous of their exchanges.
paras.zh: 書裡一再出現的另一個人是惠施，人稱惠子；他是當時首屈一指的名家，有一段時間還當了梁國的宰相。兩個人什麼事都意見不合。莊子去看他，有人告訴惠子，莊子是來搶他的相位的；惠子就在國都裡搜了三天三夜。莊子自己走了進去，跟他講南方有一種鳥，非梧桐不棲，非甘泉不飲。一隻剛弄到腐鼠的貓頭鷹，看見牠飛過，仰頭「嚇！」了一聲護住自己的寶貝。「現在你是要拿你的梁國來『嚇』我嗎？」濠梁橋上那場關於「能不能知道魚快樂」的辯論，是兩人交鋒當中最有名的一次。

paras.en: Years later, passing Huizi’s grave, Zhuangzi told his companions a story. A plasterer of Ying used to let a speck of plaster as thin as a fly’s wing sit on the tip of his nose, and have his friend the carpenter slice it off with an axe. The axe whirled like the wind and the nose was never touched. A lord heard of it and asked the carpenter to do it for him. “I could once do it,” said the carpenter, “but my partner has long been dead.” Zhuangzi went on: “Since the Master died, I have had no one to use as my partner. I have no one to talk to.” It is the best thing ever said about what a thinker owes to an opponent.
paras.zh: 多年以後，莊子路過惠子的墳墓，對跟隨的人講了一個故事。郢地有個泥水匠，常讓一點薄如蠅翼的白灰沾在鼻尖上，再叫他的朋友、一位木匠，用斧頭把它削掉。斧頭揮得像一陣風，鼻子卻從來沒有碰到。有位國君聽說了，要木匠表演給他看。木匠說：「我從前是辦得到的；不過我的搭檔已經死了很久了。」莊子接著說：「自從先生死了以後，我沒有搭檔了，我沒有可以說話的人了。」關於一個思想者欠他的對手什麼，沒有比這更好的話了。

life.h_en: The drum and the open sky

paras.en: When Zhuangzi’s wife died, Huizi came to offer condolences and found him sitting with his legs sprawled, drumming on a pot and singing. This was too much. She had lived with him, raised his children, and grown old. Zhuangzi answered that when she first died he had grieved like anyone. Then he had looked back to her beginning, to the time before she had life, or form, or even the breath that takes form. Out of some dim confusion there came breath, then form, then life, and now another change had brought death. It was like the passage of the four seasons. “She is lying at rest in a great chamber. If I were to follow after her sobbing, I would show that I do not understand what is ordained. So I stopped.”
paras.zh: 莊子的妻子死了，惠子去弔喪，卻看見他伸開兩腿坐著，敲著瓦盆唱歌。這太過分了。她跟他一起生活，為他養大孩子，陪他到老。莊子回答：她剛死的時候，他也跟任何人一樣悲傷。後來他回頭去看她的開始，回到她還沒有生命、沒有形體、甚至連成形的那股氣都還沒有的時候。在某種恍惚渾沌之中，有了氣，然後有了形，然後有了生；現在又一次變化，帶來了死。這就像四季的運行。「她正安安穩穩地躺在一間大屋子裡。我要是跟在後面嗚嗚地哭，那就表示我不懂得命。所以我就停了。」

paras.en: When he himself was dying, his students planned a grand funeral. He told them that heaven and earth would be his inner and outer coffins, the sun and moon his jade discs, the stars his pearls, and the ten thousand things his funeral gifts. What could they add? They said they were afraid the crows and kites would eat him. “Above ground I will be eaten by crows and kites, and below ground by ants and crickets. To rob the one and give to the other: how partial that would be!”
paras.zh: 輪到他自己快死的時候，弟子們打算辦一場隆重的葬禮。他告訴他們：天地就是他的棺槨，日月是他的連璧，星辰是他的珠璣，萬物是他的陪葬。他們還能添什麼呢？弟子說，怕烏鴉和老鷹會吃了老師。「在地上給烏鴉老鷹吃，在地下給螻蛄螞蟻吃。從這一邊搶過來、送給那一邊，這是多麼偏心啊！」

timeline: Reign of King Wei of Chu, who is said to have offered him office
楚威王在位；相傳曾聘他為相
Guo Xiang edits the 33-chapter text we read today
郭象編定今本三十三篇

idea.title_en: The central idea: Every view is a view from somewhere
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：每一個看法，都是從某處看出去的

paras.en: The philosophers of Zhuangzi’s day, Confucians and Mohists above all, argued about which course of action is right and which is wrong. The second chapter of his book, “On Making Things Equal,” steps back from the quarrel. Each side, he observes, calls right what the other calls wrong, and each can see the other’s blindness without seeing its own. Words such as “this” and “that” depend on where the speaker stands, and he suggests that “right” and “wrong” work in the same way. “‘That’ comes out of ‘this,’ and ‘this’ depends on ‘that.’” A keeper told his monkeys they would get three nuts in the morning and four at night, and they were furious. He offered four in the morning and three at night, and they were delighted. Nothing had changed except their joy and anger. The sage, says Zhuangzi, does not take up a position among the positions. He stands at “the hinge of the Way,” the still point from which every view can be seen to be one view.
paras.zh: 莊子那個時代的哲學家，尤其是儒家與墨家，爭論的是哪一種作法是「是」、哪一種是「非」。他的書的第二篇〈齊物論〉從這場爭吵裡退了一步。他觀察到：每一方都把對方說的「非」稱為「是」；每一方都看得見對方的盲點，卻看不見自己的。「此」與「彼」這樣的詞，取決於說話的人站在哪裡；而他暗示「是」與「非」也是這樣運作的。「彼出於是，是亦因彼。」養猴子的人告訴猴子：早上給三顆、晚上給四顆，猴子都大怒。他改說早上四顆、晚上三顆，猴子都高興了。除了牠們的喜怒，什麼都沒變。莊子說，聖人不在各種立場當中選一個立場。他站在「道樞」，那個靜止的點；從那裡看得出來，每一個看法都只是一個看法。

paras.en: This could be a recipe for paralysis, and Zhuangzi means it as a release. His heroes are people who do something supremely well without deliberating: a wheelwright, a swimmer, a catcher of cicadas, and above all Cook Ding, who cuts up an ox for his lord with the grace of a dance. Asked about his skill, the cook says that what he cares for is the Way, which goes beyond skill. After nineteen years he no longer sees the ox with his eyes. His blade, which has no thickness, moves through the spaces that are already there in the joints, and it is as sharp as on the day it left the whetstone. The lord replies that he has learned from this how to care for life. To stop forcing one’s categories on things and to follow their grain is what the tradition calls wuwei, action without strain. The book’s first chapter is titled “Wandering Far and Free.”
paras.zh: 這本來可以是一帖讓人動彈不得的藥方；莊子卻把它當作一種解放。他筆下的英雄，是那些不經盤算就把某件事做到極致的人：做車輪的、游泳的、捕蟬的，尤其是庖丁，他為國君解牛，優雅得像一場舞蹈。被問到他的技術時，這位廚子說：他所愛好的是道，那已經超過技術了。十九年下來，他不再用眼睛看那頭牛。他的刀刃沒有厚度，在骨節之間本來就有的空隙裡遊走，還像剛從磨刀石上下來那天一樣鋒利。國君回答說，他從這裡學到了養生的道理。不再把自己的分類硬套在事物上，而是順著它們的紋理，這個傳統稱之為「無為」，不費強力的行動。這本書的第一篇，篇名就叫〈逍遙遊〉。

quote.en: What your servant cares for is the Way, which goes beyond skill. … Now I meet the ox with my spirit and do not look with my eyes.
quote.zh: 臣之所好者，道也，進乎技矣。……方今之時，臣以神遇而不以目視。
quote.ref: Zhuangzi, chapter 3, “The Secret of Caring for Life,” translated for this series
quote.note_en: Cook Ding to Lord Wenhui. The Chinese is the original text.
quote.note_zh: 庖丁對文惠君說的話。中文是原文。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Blinded by Heaven
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：蔽於天而不知人

paras.en: The first serious criticism came within a generation of his death. The Confucian philosopher Xunzi listed the partial views of his predecessors, each of whom had seen one corner of the truth and taken it for the whole, and gave Zhuangzi one line: he “was blinded by Heaven and did not know the human.” Zhuangzi saw so clearly how small human distinctions look from the standpoint of nature that he lost sight of what those distinctions are for. People must decide how to raise children, share food, and restrain the violent, and a state at war cannot be governed by a man who is dragging his tail in the mud. Refusing office is a clean choice for one person. It is no answer for a society.
paras.zh: 第一個認真的批評，在他死後一代之內就出現了。儒家的荀子列舉了前人的種種偏見（每一位都看見了真理的一角，卻把它當成全部），給莊子的只有一句：「莊子蔽於天而不知人。」莊子把「從自然的立場看，人的區分有多麼渺小」看得太清楚，以致看不見那些區分是做什麼用的。人必須決定怎麼養育孩子、怎麼分配食物、怎麼約束強暴的人；一個在打仗的國家，不能交給一個拖著尾巴在泥裡爬的人來治理。拒絕做官，對一個人來說是乾淨的選擇。對一個社會來說，它不是答案。

paras.en: The second objection is logical. If every judgment of right and wrong is only a view from somewhere, then so is that judgment, and Zhuangzi has no ground for preferring his outlook to the Confucian one. His defenders reply that he never says all views are equally good. The clumsy cook who hacks at the bone and changes his knife every month is plainly worse at living than Cook Ding. What Zhuangzi denies is that any fixed set of words can capture the difference in advance. He writes in stories and jokes because a doctrine would be one more position. His school understood this: the last chapter of the book describes his writing as “absurd talk and extravagant words.”
paras.zh: 第二個反駁是邏輯上的。如果每一個是非判斷都只是從某處看出去的一個看法，那麼這個判斷本身也是；莊子就沒有根據說他的眼光比儒家的更可取。為他辯護的人回答：他從來沒有說過所有看法一樣好。那個對著骨頭亂砍、每個月換一把刀的笨廚子，顯然比庖丁更不會過日子。莊子否認的是：有任何一套固定的言詞，可以預先把這個差別抓住。他用故事和笑話來寫，因為一套學說只會是又一個立場。他的學派懂得這一點：全書的最後一篇〈天下〉形容他的文字是「謬悠之說，荒唐之言」。

paras.en: The Zhuangzi that we read was put into its present shape around 300 CE by the commentator Guo Xiang, who cut a version in fifty-two chapters down to thirty-three and arranged them in three groups. Scholars generally accept the seven Inner Chapters as the work of Zhuang Zhou, or very close to him. The fifteen Outer Chapters and eleven Miscellaneous Chapters were written by followers and sympathizers over the next two centuries, and they vary in outlook and quality. This matters for the stories told here. The butterfly dream and Cook Ding are in the Inner Chapters. The fish on the Hao, the tortoise in the mud, the drumming on the pot, Huizi’s grave, and the deathbed are all in the later sections. They are what his school remembered or invented about him, and we cannot tell which. The figure they draw is so consistent, and so unlike anyone else in ancient literature, that readers have always felt they were meeting a real person. It is safer to say that they are meeting a character whom a real person made possible.
paras.zh: 我們今天讀的《莊子》，是西元 300 年前後由註家郭象編成現在這個樣子的；他把一個五十二篇的本子刪成三十三篇，並且分成三組。學者大體上接受內篇七篇是莊周本人、或非常接近他的人所作。外篇十五篇、雜篇十一篇，是此後兩個世紀裡的後學與同情者寫的，觀點與水準參差不齊。這對這裡講的故事是有影響的。夢蝶與庖丁在內篇。濠上的魚、泥裡的龜、鼓盆、惠子的墳墓、臨終的話，全都在後面的部分。它們是他的學派對他的記憶，或者是對他的創作，而我們分不出是哪一種。這些故事描繪出來的人物是那麼一致，又那麼不像古代文獻裡的任何別人，以致讀者總覺得自己遇見了一個真人。比較穩當的說法是：他們遇見的是一個角色，而這個角色是因為有一個真人才成為可能的。

said.claim: “相濡以沫” — to moisten each other with spit — as praise for a devoted couple. (Zhuangzi)
said.claim_zh: 用「相濡以沫」來稱讚患難與共的夫妻。（莊子）
said.verdict_en: His words, the opposite of his meaning
said.verdict_zh: 是他的話，意思卻正好相反
said.en: The four characters are his, from chapter 6, and in modern Chinese they are a standard compliment for two people who support each other through hardship. The sentence goes on: “When the springs dry up and the fish are stranded together on the ground, they breathe moisture on one another and wet one another with spit. It would be better to forget one another in the rivers and lakes.” Zhuangzi’s point is that such tenderness is a sign that something has gone badly wrong. Fish in deep water do not need to keep each other alive.
said.zh: 這四個字確實是他的，出自第六篇〈大宗師〉；在現代中文裡，它是對兩個在困境中互相扶持的人的標準讚美。原句後面還有：「泉涸，魚相與處於陸，相呴以濕，相濡以沫，不如相忘於江湖。」莊子的意思是：這樣的溫情，是事情已經大大不對勁的徵兆。深水裡的魚，用不著互相維持性命。

paras.en: When Buddhist texts reached China in the first centuries of the common era, the only native vocabulary subtle enough to translate them was that of Laozi and Zhuangzi. Emptiness was first rendered by the Daoist word for nothingness, and nirvana by wuwei. The practice was later called geyi, “matching concepts,” and it took Chinese monks some three hundred years to see how much it distorted. But the meeting left a permanent mark. Sengzhao, the first great Chinese exponent of the Middle Way, was formed by reading Zhuangzi before he ever saw a sutra, and Chan Buddhism owes to Zhuangzi much of its manner: the humor, the craftsmen and cooks as teachers, and the distrust of anything that can be put into words.
paras.zh: 佛典在西元最初幾個世紀傳到中國的時候，本土唯一夠精微、足以翻譯它們的語彙，是老子與莊子的語彙。「空」最初是用道家的「無」來譯的，「涅槃」是用「無為」來譯的。這種作法後來被稱為「格義」；中國的僧人花了大約三百年，才看出它造成了多大的扭曲。但這次相遇留下了永久的印記。中國第一位偉大的中觀闡釋者僧肇，在還沒見過任何一部經之前，就已經被《莊子》塑造了；而禪宗的風格有許多得自莊子：那份幽默、以工匠與廚子為師，以及對任何說得出口的東西的不信任。

paras.en: The resemblances are real. Zhuangzi’s “I lost myself” and his “sitting and forgetting,” in which one lets the limbs fall away and dismisses the intellect, would be recognized by any meditator, and his calm before death is what the Buddhist texts call equanimity. The two part company on what the trouble is. For Zhuangzi the endless transformation of things is to be welcomed: one rides the changes, and death is one more turn of the seasons. For the Buddha, being carried from birth to birth by causes one does not understand is the very thing from which liberation is sought. Zhuangzi offers no analysis of why we suffer and no graded path, and compassion for other beings is not among his themes: his fish do best when they can forget one another. The Buddha taught for forty-five years because he thought that the stranded fish should be helped back to the water (Dharma and the West, D24).
paras.zh: 相似之處是真的。莊子的「吾喪我」，還有他的「坐忘」（任肢體脫落、屏除聰明），任何禪修者都認得出來；而他在死亡面前的平靜，就是佛典所說的「捨」。兩者分道揚鑣的地方，在於「問題出在哪裡」。對莊子來說，萬物無窮的變化是該歡迎的：人乘著變化而行，死亡不過是四季又轉了一輪。對佛陀來說，被自己不明白的因緣帶著，一生又一生地流轉，正是要從中求解脫的東西。莊子沒有提供對「我們為什麼受苦」的分析，也沒有次第分明的道路；對其他眾生的悲憫，也不在他的主題之中：他的魚，在能夠彼此相忘的時候過得最好。佛陀說法四十五年，因為他認為，擱淺的魚應該有人幫牠們回到水裡（佛法與西方哲學 D24）。

terms.d_en: The course that things follow of themselves, which cannot be captured in any fixed form of words.
terms.d_zh: 萬物自己依循的路徑；任何固定的言詞都無法把它抓住。

terms.d_en: Action that follows the grain of a situation without forcing it. Often translated “non-action.”
terms.d_zh: 順著情勢的紋理而不強求的行動。常譯作 non-action。

terms.d_en: Seeing that the distinctions we draw, including right and wrong, depend on a standpoint.
terms.d_zh: 看出我們所作的種種區分（包括是與非）都取決於立足點。

terms.d_en: The passing of one form into another, as of Zhuang Zhou into a butterfly or of life into death.
terms.d_zh: 一種形態轉成另一種形態，如莊周之於蝴蝶、生之於死。

terms.d_en: The view that all judging is done from some standpoint. Distinguished from relativism, which adds that all standpoints are equally good.
terms.d_zh: 主張一切判斷都是從某個立足點作出的。與相對主義有別；後者還多主張所有立足點一樣好。

terms.d_en: Zhuangzi’s own term for his method: placing one’s words in the mouth of someone else.
terms.d_zh: 莊子自己對他的方法的稱呼：把話寄放在別人口中說出來。

quiz.q: Why did Zhuangzi refuse the offer from the king of Chu?
options: He preferred a free life in obscurity to honor that would cost him that freedom.
He was loyal to a rival king.
He was too ill to travel.
He wanted a higher post.

quiz.q: What does the story of the monkeys and the nuts illustrate?
options: That strong reactions of approval and anger can attach to differences that change nothing.
That monkeys cannot count.
That keepers should be generous.
That mornings are better than evenings.

quiz.q: What was Xunzi’s criticism?
options: Zhuangzi saw things from the standpoint of nature and lost sight of human needs.
Zhuangzi wrote too little.
Zhuangzi copied Confucius.
Zhuangzi was too fond of ritual.

philosophers.name: G. W. Leibniz
philosophers.tag_en: A court librarian who invented the calculus, built a calculating machine, read the Book of Changes as binary arithmetic, and argued that no machine could perceive.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位宮廷圖書館員：他發明了微積分，造了一台計算機，把《易經》讀成二進位算術，並且論證沒有任何機器能夠知覺。
facts: Counselor, librarian, and historian to the dukes of Hanover, from 1676
The calculus (independently of Newton); a machine that multiplies; binary arithmetic
Latin, French, and German; most of it left unpublished

life.h_en: The boy in his father’s library

paras.en: Leibniz was born in Leipzig in 1646, two years before the end of the Thirty Years’ War, which had killed perhaps a third of the population of the German lands. His father, a professor of moral philosophy, died when he was six and left a library. The boy was given the run of it at eight, taught himself Latin from an illustrated history, and by his teens had read the ancient authors and the medieval logicians. He took a doctorate in law at twenty and was offered a professorship, which he refused. He wanted, he said, a larger sphere of action, and he entered the service of a prince.
paras.zh: 萊布尼茲 1646 年生於萊比錫，兩年後三十年戰爭才結束；那場戰爭也許奪走了德意志地區三分之一的人口。他的父親是道德哲學教授，在他六歲時去世，留下了一間藏書室。這個男孩八歲時獲准在裡面自由出入，靠著一本有插圖的史書自學了拉丁文；到十幾歲，他已經讀過古代作家與中世紀的邏輯學家。他二十歲取得法學博士學位，並且得到一個教授職位，他回絕了。他說，他想要一個更大的活動範圍；於是他進入一位君主的幕下服務。

paras.en: A diplomatic errand took him to Paris in 1672, and the four years he spent there made him a mathematician. He arrived knowing little of the subject. Under the guidance of the Dutch physicist Christiaan Huygens he mastered it, and in the autumn of 1675 he worked out the differential and integral calculus, with the notation, dx and the long S of the integral sign, that is still used. Newton had reached the same results a decade earlier by another route and had published nothing. On a visit to London in 1673 Leibniz showed the Royal Society a wooden model of a machine that could multiply and divide by means of a stepped drum, and was elected a fellow.
paras.zh: 1672 年，一趟外交差事把他帶到了巴黎；他在那裡度過的四年，使他成為數學家。他到的時候對這門學問所知甚少。在荷蘭物理學家惠更斯的指引下，他掌握了它；1675 年秋天，他推演出了微分與積分，連同那套沿用至今的記號：dx，以及積分號那個拉長的 S。牛頓早十年就用另一條路得到了同樣的結果，卻什麼也沒發表。1673 年造訪倫敦時，萊布尼茲向皇家學會展示了一台機器的木製模型，它靠一個階梯狀的滾筒就能做乘法與除法；他因此當選為會員。

paras.en: No post could be found for him in Paris, and in 1676 he accepted one at the small court of Hanover, where he remained for the rest of his life. His duties were to keep the library and to write the history of the ruling family. Around them he pursued a range of projects that has never been matched. He designed windmills to drain the silver mines of the Harz mountains. He worked for the reunion of the Catholic and Protestant churches. He founded the academy of sciences in Berlin, and he studied fossils, Chinese philosophy, and the origins of languages. He corresponded with more than a thousand people. Very little of his philosophy was printed. It lay in letters and in drafts, and scholars are still editing them.
paras.zh: 巴黎找不到給他的職位；1676 年，他接受了漢諾威那個小宮廷的一個職位，此後終身留在那裡。他的職責是管理圖書館，以及為統治家族撰寫家史。圍繞著這些職責，他推動了範圍之廣至今無人能及的種種計畫。他設計風車，要為哈茨山的銀礦排水。他為天主教會與新教教會的重新合一而奔走。他創立了柏林的科學院；他研究化石、中國哲學與語言的起源。他跟一千多人通信。他的哲學付印的非常少。它躺在信件與草稿裡，學者至今還在整理。

paras.en: His curiosity about China was unusual for his time and was free of condescension. In 1697 he published a collection of reports from the Jesuit mission, in the preface of which he proposes that China should send missionaries to Europe to teach the practice of ethics. In 1701 the Jesuit Joachim Bouvet sent him from Beijing a diagram of the sixty-four hexagrams of the Book of Changes. Leibniz had recently devised a way of writing every number with only the signs 0 and 1, and he saw at once that if a broken line is read as 0 and an unbroken line as 1, the hexagrams in that arrangement count from 0 to 63. He concluded that the ancient Chinese had possessed his binary arithmetic and later forgotten it. He was wrong about the history. The notation is the one on which every computer now runs.
paras.zh: 他對中國的好奇，在他的時代是不尋常的，而且沒有居高臨下的態度。1697 年，他出版了一部耶穌會傳教團報告的彙編；在序言裡，他提議中國應該派傳教士到歐洲來，教導倫理的實踐。1701 年，耶穌會士白晉從北京寄給他一張《易經》六十四卦的圖。萊布尼茲不久前才設計出一種只用 0 與 1 兩個記號就能寫出每一個數的方法；他立刻看出，如果把陰爻讀作 0、陽爻讀作 1，那個排列裡的卦就是從 0 數到 63。他的結論是：古代的中國人曾經擁有他的二進位算術，後來忘了。就歷史而言他錯了。而那套記號，就是今天每一台電腦賴以運作的那一套。

life.h_en: The quarrel and the empty funeral

paras.en: His last years were poisoned by the dispute over the calculus. Newton’s followers accused him of having stolen the idea during his London visits, and in 1712 a committee of the Royal Society, whose report Newton himself secretly drafted, found against him. Historians now agree that the two discoveries were independent. In 1714 his employer became King George I of Great Britain and moved the court to London. Leibniz asked to follow and was told to stay in Hanover and finish the family history, which had reached the year 1005. He died there in November 1716. A friend recorded that he was buried more like a robber than like what he was, the ornament of his country. Of the whole court, only his secretary attended the funeral.
paras.zh: 他的晚年被微積分的爭端毒害了。牛頓的追隨者指控他在造訪倫敦期間偷了這個想法；1712 年，皇家學會的一個委員會作出了對他不利的裁定，而那份報告是牛頓本人暗中起草的。歷史學家現在一致認為，這兩項發現是各自獨立的。1714 年，他的雇主成了大不列顛國王喬治一世，把宮廷遷到了倫敦。萊布尼茲請求隨行，得到的答覆是留在漢諾威，把那部家史寫完；當時它才寫到西元 1005 年。1716 年 11 月，他在那裡去世。一位朋友記載：他下葬的樣子，比較像個盜賊，而不像他實際上的身分，也就是他的國家的光彩。整個宮廷，只有他的秘書出席了葬禮。
