idea.title_en: The central idea: Nothing is without a reason
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：沒有任何事是沒有理由的

paras.en: Leibniz said that all our reasoning rests on two principles. The first is that a contradiction cannot be true. The second, which he made his own, is the principle of sufficient reason: “there can be no fact real or existing, no statement true, unless there be a sufficient reason, why it should be so and not otherwise, although these reasons usually cannot be known by us.” Nothing simply happens to be the case. From this one demand he drew a whole account of the world. If there must be a reason why this universe exists and no other, the reason can only be that it is the best of those that were possible, and that a perfect being chose it for that reason. If two things were exactly alike in every respect, there could be no reason for one to be here and the other there, so no two things are exactly alike.
paras.zh: 萊布尼茲說，我們一切的推理都建立在兩條原理上。第一條是：矛盾不可能為真。第二條是他使之成為自己的招牌的，就是充足理由律：「若沒有一個充足的理由說明它為什麼是這樣而不是別樣，就不可能有任何事實是真實的或存在的，也不可能有任何陳述是真的，儘管這些理由通常不能為我們所知。」沒有任何事情只是「剛好如此」。從這一個要求，他引出了一整套對世界的說明。如果必須有一個理由說明為什麼存在的是這個宇宙、而不是別的宇宙，那個理由只能是：它是所有可能的宇宙當中最好的，而一位完美的存在者正是為此選擇了它。如果兩個東西在每一方面都完全相同，就不可能有理由說明為什麼一個在這裡、另一個在那裡；所以沒有兩個東西是完全相同的。

paras.en: The strangest consequence concerns what the world is made of. Anything extended in space can be divided, and what can be divided is a collection and depends on its parts. The ultimate constituents must therefore be simple, without parts, and so without extension. Leibniz called them monads. Since a thing without parts cannot be pushed or altered from outside, “the Monads have no windows, through which anything could come in or go out.” Each unfolds its own states from within, as a mind does, and what a monad has is perception, in degrees that run from the dim stirrings of what we call matter to the clear awareness of a rational soul. Each perceives the whole universe from its own position and is “a perpetual living mirror of the universe.” No monad acts on any other. They agree with one another because they were set in order together at the creation, like clocks made so well that they keep the same time forever. He called this the pre-established harmony.
paras.zh: 最奇特的後果，關乎世界是由什麼構成的。任何在空間中有廣延的東西都可以分割；而可以分割的東西是一個集合，依賴於它的部分。所以，最終的構成者必須是單純的，沒有部分，因而也沒有廣延。萊布尼茲稱它們為「單子」。由於沒有部分的東西無法從外面被推動或改變，「單子沒有窗戶，沒有任何東西可以經由窗戶進出」。每一個單子都從內部展開它自己的狀態，就像一個心那樣；單子所擁有的是知覺，程度不等，從我們稱為物質的那種昏暗的擾動，一直到理性靈魂清楚的覺察。每一個單子都從自己的位置知覺整個宇宙，是「宇宙的一面永恆的活鏡子」。沒有任何單子作用於別的單子。它們彼此一致，是因為它們在創世時就被一起安排妥當了，像是造得精良到永遠走得一樣準的鐘。他稱之為「預定和諧」。

quote.en: …there can be no fact real or existing, no statement true, unless there be a sufficient reason, why it should be so and not otherwise, although these reasons usually cannot be known by us.
quote.zh: ……若沒有一個充足的理由說明它為什麼是這樣而不是別樣，就不可能有任何事實是真實的或存在的，也不可能有任何陳述是真的，儘管這些理由通常不能為我們所知。
quote.ref: Leibniz, Monadology §32, tr. Robert Latta
quote.note_en: The principle of sufficient reason, in the form he gave it two years before his death.
quote.note_zh: 充足理由律；這是他去世前兩年給它的表述。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The best of all possible worlds
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：所有可能世界中最好的一個

paras.en: On November 1, 1755, an earthquake destroyed Lisbon while the churches were full for All Saints’ Day, and tens of thousands died. Four years later Voltaire published Candide, in which the tutor Pangloss, a disciple of Leibniz, passes through war, shipwreck, the earthquake, and the Inquisition explaining at each disaster that all is for the best. The satire is unfair in one respect. Leibniz did not say that everything in the world is good. He said that a world with free creatures and regular laws could not have had less evil in total without being worse in some other way, and that we, who see a fragment, are in no position to judge the whole. But the unfairness does not remove the difficulty. A claim that would be equally consistent with any amount of suffering explains none of it, and it is hard to say to the parents of a drowned child that the alternative worlds were worse.
paras.zh: 1755 年 11 月 1 日，一場地震摧毀了里斯本，當時各教堂正因為諸聖節而坐滿了人；數以萬計的人喪生。四年後，伏爾泰出版了《憨第德》：書裡的家庭教師潘格羅斯是萊布尼茲的信徒，他一路經歷戰爭、船難、那場地震與宗教裁判所，每逢一場災難就解釋說，一切都是為了最好的結果。這部諷刺作品在一點上是不公平的。萊布尼茲並沒有說世界上的每一件事都是好的。他說的是：一個有自由的受造者、有規律的法則的世界，如果總體上的惡要再少一些，就不可能不在別的某方面變得更糟；而我們只看到一個片段，沒有資格評判整體。然而，這份不公平並沒有消除困難。一個不論苦難有多少都同樣說得通的主張，並沒有解釋任何苦難；而且，很難對一個孩子溺死了的父母說：別的可能世界更糟。

paras.en: A second objection is aimed at the principle itself. If everything has a sufficient reason, then everything that happens could not have been otherwise, including each human choice and God’s choice of this world, and freedom disappears. Leibniz replied that reasons “incline without necessitating.” His contemporaries were not persuaded, and the charge that his system is Spinoza’s necessity in more pious language has followed it ever since.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁針對的是那條原理本身。如果每一件事都有充足的理由，那麼發生的每一件事都不可能是別的樣子，包括人的每一個選擇，以及上帝對這個世界的選擇；自由就消失了。萊布尼茲回答：理由「使人傾向，而不使人必然」。他同時代的人並沒有被說服；而「他的體系不過是用更虔誠的語言說出來的史賓諾莎式必然」這項指控，此後一直跟著它。

problem.title_en: A philosophy left in the drawer

paras.en: Leibniz published one philosophical book in his lifetime, the Theodicy, a long and courtly defense of the goodness of God. The works on which his reputation now rests were not written for print. The Discourse on Metaphysics of 1686 was a private summary. The Monadology was composed in 1714 for a few correspondents and appeared only after his death, and its title was supplied by an editor. His reply to Locke, the New Essays, he withheld because Locke had died, and it was printed in 1765. The rest is in some fifteen thousand letters and a mass of notes. As a result there were for two centuries several Leibnizes. The eighteenth century knew the optimist of the Theodicy. Bertrand Russell, reading the logical papers around 1900, argued that the public system was a façade and that the real philosophy was a logic kept in the desk. The complete edition of his writings, begun in 1923, is expected to take many more decades.
paras.zh: 萊布尼茲生前只出版過一本哲學書，《神義論》；那是一部冗長而帶著宮廷氣的著作，為上帝的善辯護。他今天的名聲所依靠的那些作品，都不是為了付印而寫的。1686 年的《形上學論》是一份私人的摘要。《單子論》是 1714 年為幾位通信者寫的，在他死後才面世，書名還是編者加的。他對洛克的回應《人類理解新論》，因為洛克已經去世而被他壓了下來，到 1765 年才印行。其餘的都在大約一萬五千封信與成堆的筆記裡。結果是，有兩個世紀之久，存在著好幾個萊布尼茲。十八世紀認識的是《神義論》裡的那位樂觀主義者。羅素在 1900 年前後讀了那些邏輯文稿，主張公開的體系只是門面，真正的哲學是鎖在書桌裡的一套邏輯。他的著作全集從 1923 年開始編纂，預計還要好幾十年才能完成。

said.claim: “This is the best of all possible worlds.” (Leibniz)
said.claim_zh: 「這是所有可能世界中最好的一個。」（萊布尼茲）
said.verdict_zh: 是他的學說，語氣卻是伏爾泰的
said.en: The thesis is his. The Monadology says that among the infinite number of possible universes God must have had a sufficient reason to choose one, and that the reason can only lie in “the degrees of perfection, that these worlds possess.” What most people hear in the sentence, a cheerful assurance that things are fine, comes from Candide, where the phrase is repeated as a refrain amid catastrophes. Leibniz meant a claim about the total and never denied that particular evils are real. The word “optimism” was coined in the 1730s to describe his view, from optimum, “the best.” It did not then mean a sunny temperament.
said.zh: 這個論點是他的。《單子論》說：在無限多個可能的宇宙當中，上帝必定有一個充足的理由選擇其中之一；而那個理由只能在於「這些世界所具有的完美程度」。多數人在這句話裡聽到的東西，也就是一種「事情都很好」的愉快保證，來自《憨第德》；在那本書裡，這句話在一場場災禍當中像副歌一樣反覆出現。萊布尼茲指的是一個關於「總體」的主張，而他從來沒有否認個別的惡是真實的。optimism（樂觀主義）這個詞是 1730 年代為了描述他的看法而造的，來自 optimum，「最好的」。它當時指的並不是開朗的性情。

paras.en: One image in Leibniz has a famous Buddhist twin. Each monad, he says, is a living mirror that reflects the entire universe from its own point of view. The Huayan school of Chinese Buddhism describes the net of the god Indra, which stretches without limit in every direction and has a jewel at every knot. Each jewel reflects all the others, and in each reflection all the others are reflected again. The Huayan masters used the net to teach that every phenomenon contains and is contained by every other. The two images arose with no contact between them, and they are put to opposite uses. Leibniz’s mirrors are substances: each monad is a self-contained thing that could exist if no other did, and it only represents the rest. A jewel in Indra’s net is nothing apart from the others. It exists by interdependence, and that is what the Buddhist means by calling it empty.
paras.zh: 萊布尼茲的一個意象，在佛教裡有一個著名的孿生兄弟。他說，每一個單子都是一面活的鏡子，從自己的觀點映照整個宇宙。中國佛教的華嚴宗描述了因陀羅網（帝釋天的網）：它往每一個方向無限延伸，每一個網結上都有一顆寶珠。每一顆寶珠都映照出所有其他的寶珠；而在每一個映像裡，所有其他的寶珠又再被映照出來。華嚴的祖師用這張網來教導：每一個現象都含攝其他一切現象，也被其他一切現象所含攝。這兩個意象是在彼此毫無接觸的情況下各自出現的，用途卻相反。萊布尼茲的鏡子是實體：每一個單子都是自足的東西，即使別的單子都不存在，它也能存在；它只是「表象」其餘的一切。因陀羅網上的一顆寶珠，離開了其他的寶珠就什麼也不是。它是靠相依而存在的；佛教徒說它是「空」的，指的就是這個。

paras.en: The principle of sufficient reason has a nearer relative in dependent origination: “when this exists, that comes to be.” Both deny that anything arises without conditions. They differ on where the series ends. Leibniz argues that the chain of reasons must terminate in a being that contains the reason for its own existence, and that this is God. The Buddha declined to posit a first cause and described a web of conditions with no beginning that can be found. The problem that occupied Leibniz for forty years, how a good creator could permit evil, therefore does not arise in Buddhism in that form. Suffering is explained by craving and ignorance, with no one having chosen the arrangement (Dharma and the West, D4).
paras.zh: 充足理由律在緣起裡有一個更近的親戚：「此有故彼有。」兩者都否認有任何東西是不依條件而生起的。它們的差別在於這個系列在哪裡結束。萊布尼茲論證：理由的鏈條必須終止於一個「自身就包含了自己存在的理由」的存在者，而那就是上帝。佛陀拒絕設定第一因；他描述的是一張因緣之網，找不到開端。因此，那個佔據了萊布尼茲四十年的問題（一位善的造物主怎麼會容許惡），在佛教裡並不以那種形式出現。苦是由渴愛與無明來說明的，並沒有誰選擇了這樣的安排（佛法與西方哲學 D4）。

terms: the mutual non-obstruction of all phenomena

terms.d_en: Nothing is the case without a reason why it is so and not otherwise.
terms.d_zh: 沒有任何事情是沒有「為什麼如此而不是別樣」的理由的。

terms.d_en: A simple substance without parts, whose only states are perceptions.
terms.d_zh: 沒有部分的單純實體；它唯一的狀態是知覺。

terms.d_en: The agreement of all substances with one another, arranged at the creation, without any acting on any other.
terms.d_zh: 一切實體彼此之間的一致；它是在創世時安排好的，沒有任何實體作用於另一個。

terms.d_en: If two things share every property, they are one thing.
terms.d_zh: 如果兩個東西的一切性質都相同，它們就是同一個東西。

terms.d_en: A complete way that things might have been. The actual world is one of them.
terms.d_zh: 事物「本來可以是」的一種完整的樣子。現實世界是其中之一。

terms.o: Gk. theos ‘god’ + dikē ‘justice’; coined by Leibniz
terms.d_en: A defense of the justice of God in the face of evil.
terms.d_zh: 面對惡的存在，為上帝的公義所作的辯護。

quiz.q: What does the principle of sufficient reason assert?
options: Nothing is the case without a reason why it is so and not otherwise.
Only what can be seen is real.
Human beings can know the reason for everything.
Reasons are habits of the mind.

quiz.q: Why do monads “have no windows”?
options: A thing without parts cannot be altered from outside, so nothing passes in or out.
They are too small to see.
They are made of glass.
God forbids them to communicate.

quiz.q: In what respect is Voltaire’s satire unfair to Leibniz?
options: Leibniz claimed that the world as a whole is the best possible, not that each event in it is good.
Leibniz never wrote about evil.
Leibniz believed the world was the worst possible.
Voltaire had not read any philosophy.

further.t: G. W. Leibniz, The Monadology, translated by Robert Latta (1898)
further.n_en: Ninety numbered paragraphs; the whole system in an hour.
further.n_zh: 九十個編號段落；一小時讀完整個體系。

philosophers.name: John Stuart Mill
philosophers.tag_en: A child raised as an experiment in education, who broke down at twenty, rebuilt himself with poetry, and wrote the classic defenses of utility, liberty, and the equality of women.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個被當成教育實驗養大的孩子；二十歲時崩潰，靠著詩把自己重建起來，然後寫下了為效益、自由與女性平等辯護的經典。
facts: At home, by his father James Mill; never attended school or university
East India Company, London, 1823–1858; Member of Parliament, 1865–1868
A System of Logic (1843); On Liberty (1859); Utilitarianism (1863); The Subjection of Women (1869)

paras.en: James Mill, a Scottish journalist and a disciple of the reformer Jeremy Bentham, believed that the mind at birth is a blank and that education can make of it whatever it chooses. He decided to prove it on his eldest son. “I have no remembrance of the time when I began to learn Greek,” John Stuart Mill wrote. “I have been told that it was when I was three years old.” Latin followed at eight, with geometry and algebra. By twelve he had read most of the Greek and Latin classics and was set to logic, and at thirteen he went through a complete course of political economy on daily walks with his father, writing up each lesson the next morning. He was kept from other children. He was not allowed holidays, lest the habit of work be broken. He reckoned afterward that the method had given him an advantage of a quarter of a century over his contemporaries.
paras.zh: 詹姆斯・彌爾是蘇格蘭出身的記者，也是改革家邊沁的信徒；他相信心靈在出生時是一片空白，而教育可以隨意把它造就成任何樣子。他決定在自己的長子身上證明這一點。約翰・史都華・彌爾寫道：「我不記得自己是什麼時候開始學希臘文的。有人告訴我，那是在我三歲的時候。」八歲接著學拉丁文，還有幾何與代數。到十二歲，他已經讀過大部分的希臘與拉丁經典，並且被安排去學邏輯；十三歲時，他在每天跟父親的散步當中上完了一整套政治經濟學，隔天早上再把每一課寫成筆記。他被隔離在別的孩子之外。他不准放假，免得工作的習慣被打斷。他後來估算，這套方法讓他比同時代的人領先了四分之一個世紀。

paras.en: At fifteen he read Bentham, and the principle of utility, he said, gave unity to everything he knew: he now had a creed, a philosophy, a religion. At seventeen he was briefly arrested for handing out pamphlets on birth control in the poor streets of London, and in the same year he followed his father into the London office of the East India Company, where he would work for thirty-five years, drafting dispatches to India in the mornings and writing philosophy in the time left over.
paras.zh: 十五歲時，他讀了邊沁；他說，效益原則為他所知的一切帶來了統一：他現在有了一個信條、一套哲學、一種宗教。十七歲時，他因為在倫敦的貧民街道散發節育傳單而短暫被捕；同一年，他跟著父親進了東印度公司的倫敦辦公室。他在那裡工作了三十五年，早上起草發往印度的公文，用剩下的時間寫哲學。

paras.en: In the autumn of 1826, when he was twenty, the machine stopped. “It occurred to me to put the question directly to myself: ‘Suppose that all your objects in life were realized; that all the changes in institutions and opinions which you are looking forward to, could be completely effected at this very instant: would this be a great joy and happiness to you?’ And an irrepressible self-consciousness distinctly answered, ‘No!’ At this my heart sank within me: the whole foundation on which my life was constructed fell down.” He had been trained to analyze and had never been taught to feel, and he now feared that the habit of analysis had worn his feelings away. For months he went through his work mechanically and told no one.
paras.zh: 1826 年秋天，他二十歲，那台機器停了。「我想到要直接問自己這個問題：『假設你人生的一切目標都實現了；你所期盼的制度與輿論上的一切改變，就在這一刻全部達成：這對你會是莫大的喜悅與幸福嗎？』而一種壓抑不住的自我意識清清楚楚地回答：『不會！』聽到這裡，我的心往下一沉：我的人生賴以建造的整個地基垮了。」他被訓練成會分析，卻從來沒有人教他感受；而他現在害怕，分析的習慣已經把他的感情磨光了。有好幾個月，他機械地做完工作，沒有告訴任何人。

paras.en: The first relief came by accident. He was reading the memoirs of the French writer Marmontel and came to the passage describing the death of the author’s father, and he found himself in tears. He was not, then, “a stock or a stone.” Two years later he read Wordsworth, whose poems gave him what he called a culture of the feelings. He drew two lessons that shaped everything he later wrote. Happiness cannot be had by aiming at it: “Ask yourself whether you are happy, and you cease to be so.” And a good life needs the cultivation of the inner person as well as the reform of outward circumstances. He never renounced Bentham’s principle. He spent the rest of his life enlarging what it meant.
paras.zh: 最初的紓解是意外來的。他正在讀法國作家馬蒙泰爾的回憶錄，讀到描寫作者父親去世的那一段，發現自己流下了眼淚。那麼，他並不是「一塊木頭或石頭」。兩年後，他讀了華茲華斯；那些詩給了他他所謂的「情感的陶冶」。他得出了兩個教訓，塑造了他後來寫的一切。幸福不能靠瞄準它而得到：「問問自己是否幸福，你就不再幸福了。」還有：美好的人生既需要改革外在的環境，也需要培養內在的人。他從來沒有背棄邊沁的原則。他用餘生去擴大它的意思。

paras.en: In 1830 he met Harriet Taylor, who was twenty-two, married, and the mother of two children. For twenty years they maintained an intense friendship that scandalized London and that her husband tolerated. Two years after his death they married, in 1851, and Mill signed a formal protest against the legal powers that marriage gave him over her. She died at Avignon in 1858. He bought a house within sight of the cemetery and spent half of every year there. On Liberty appeared the following year, dedicated to her as “the inspirer, and in part the author, of all that is best in my writings.”
paras.zh: 1830 年，他認識了海莉耶・泰勒；她二十二歲，已婚，是兩個孩子的母親。有二十年之久，他們維持著一段熱烈的友誼，使倫敦社會譁然，而她的丈夫容忍了。她丈夫去世兩年後，他們在 1851 年結婚；彌爾簽署了一份正式的抗議書，反對婚姻在法律上賦予他支配她的種種權力。1858 年，她在亞維儂去世。他買下了一棟看得見墓園的房子，每年有一半的時間住在那裡。《論自由》在隔年出版，題獻給她：「我著作中一切最好的東西的啟發者，而且有一部分是其作者。」

paras.en: In 1865 the voters of Westminster elected him to Parliament, though he had refused to campaign or to spend any money. In 1867 he moved that the word “man” in the Reform Bill be replaced by “person,” which would have given women the vote. The motion was lost, and seventy-three members voted for it, far more than anyone expected. The Subjection of Women followed in 1869. He died at Avignon in 1873 and was buried beside Harriet. He had agreed, the year before, to stand as godfather to the infant son of a friend. The child was Bertrand Russell.
paras.zh: 1865 年，西敏選區的選民把他選進了國會，儘管他拒絕競選、也拒絕花一分錢。1867 年，他提案把《改革法案》裡的 man（男人）一詞換成 person（人），這樣就會讓女性有投票權。提案沒有通過，卻有七十三位議員投了贊成票，遠多於任何人的預期。《女性的屈從地位》接著在 1869 年出版。1873 年，他在亞維儂去世，葬在海莉耶身旁。去世的前一年，他答應當一位朋友剛出生的兒子的教父。那個孩子是羅素。

idea.title_en: The central idea: Happiness, with a difference of kind
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：幸福，但有種類之別

paras.en: Bentham had held that pleasure is the only good, that pleasures differ only in amount, and that “pushpin is as good as poetry” if it pleases as much. Critics called this a philosophy fit for swine. Mill kept the foundation: “actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness, wrong as they tend to produce the reverse of happiness,” and the happiness that counts is that of everyone affected, extended “so far as the nature of things admits, to the whole sentient creation.” What he changed was the account of happiness. Pleasures differ in kind as well as in amount, he argued, and the test is the verdict of those who have known both. No one who has enjoyed the exercise of intelligence, feeling, and conscience would give them up for any quantity of an animal’s contentment. “It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied. And if the fool, or the pig, is of a different opinion, it is because they only know their own side of the question.”
paras.zh: 邊沁主張：快樂是唯一的善；各種快樂只有量的差別；只要帶來的快樂一樣多，「圖釘遊戲跟詩一樣好」。批評者說這是一套只配給豬的哲學。彌爾保留了地基：「行為之為對，與它們增進幸福的傾向成比例；行為之為錯，與它們產生幸福之反面的傾向成比例」；而算數的幸福，是每一個受影響者的幸福，並且「在事物的本性所容許的範圍內，推及一切有感知的受造物」。他改變的，是對幸福的說明。他論證：快樂不只有量的差別，也有種類的差別；而檢驗的標準，是那些兩種都體驗過的人的判決。凡是享受過運用智性、情感與良知的人，都不會為了任何數量的動物式的滿足而放棄它們。「做一個不滿足的人，勝過做一隻滿足的豬；做不滿足的蘇格拉底，勝過做一個滿足的傻瓜。如果那個傻瓜或那隻豬有不同的意見，那是因為他們只知道問題屬於自己的那一面。」

paras.en: On Liberty applies the same standard to society. A people is happiest in the long run, Mill argues, when its members are free to form their own opinions and try their own ways of living, because truth is found only by the collision of opinions and character is formed only by choice. He proposes one principle to mark the limit of what a society may force on a person: the only purpose for which power can rightfully be exercised over anyone against his will is “to prevent harm to others.” A person’s own good is not a sufficient warrant. And silencing an opinion is always a loss: “If all mankind minus one, were of one opinion, and only one person were of the contrary opinion, mankind would be no more justified in silencing that one person, than he, if he had the power, would be justified in silencing mankind.”
paras.zh: 《論自由》把同一個標準用在社會上。彌爾論證：一個民族，當它的成員可以自由形成自己的意見、嘗試自己的生活方式時，長遠來看是最幸福的；因為真理只有在意見的碰撞中才找得到，品格只有在抉擇中才能形成。他提出了一條原則，用來標出社會可以強加於個人的限度：違背一個人的意願而對他行使權力，唯一正當的目的是「防止對他人的傷害」。一個人自己的好處，並不是充分的理由。而讓一個意見噤聲，永遠是一種損失：「假如全人類除了一個人之外意見都相同，只有那一個人持相反的意見；那麼人類要使那個人噤聲，並不比那個人（假如他有那個權力）要使全人類噤聲，更有道理。」

quote.en: It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
quote.zh: 做一個不滿足的人，勝過做一隻滿足的豬；做不滿足的蘇格拉底，勝過做一個滿足的傻瓜。
quote.ref: J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism, chapter 2
quote.note_en: His answer to the charge that utilitarianism is a doctrine worthy only of swine.
quote.note_zh: 他對「效益主義是只配給豬的學說」這項指控的回答。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Can it protect the one from the many?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：它保護得了那一個人，不受多數人侵害嗎？

paras.en: If right action is whatever produces the most happiness on the whole, then it seems that an innocent person may be sacrificed whenever enough others would gain. A sheriff could hang a man he knows to be innocent in order to prevent a riot in which many would die. A surgeon could take one patient’s organs to save five. Mill’s own principle of liberty appears to be in danger from his principle of utility, since a majority might be made happier by silencing a hated minority. He saw the problem and gave the last and longest chapter of Utilitarianism to it. Justice, he argues, is the name for those rules that protect the most vital of human interests, security above all, and a society that kept them only when convenient would lose the security that makes every other good possible. Rights are to be respected almost without exception because that policy has the best results.
paras.zh: 如果對的行為就是在總體上產生最多幸福的行為，那麼，只要有夠多的別人會得利，一個無辜的人似乎就可以被犧牲。一位警長可以為了避免一場會死很多人的暴動，吊死一個他明知無辜的人。一位外科醫師可以取走一位病人的器官去救五個人。彌爾自己的自由原則，看來正受到他的效益原則的威脅，因為讓一群被憎恨的少數噤聲，也許會使多數人更幸福。他看到了這個問題，並且把《效益主義》最後也最長的一章用來處理它。他論證：「正義」是那些保護人類最攸關緊要的利益（尤其是安全）的規則的名稱；一個只在方便的時候才遵守這些規則的社會，會失去使其他一切善成為可能的那份安全。權利幾乎應該毫無例外地被尊重，因為這個方針有最好的結果。

paras.en: Critics have never been satisfied. If the rules matter only for their results, then in the rare case where breaking one would certainly do more good and never be discovered, the theory has no reason left to keep it, and those are the cases that test a theory. A second objection concerns the higher pleasures. If some pleasures are better in kind, apart from how pleasant they are, then something other than pleasure is making them better, and Mill has quietly given up the view that pleasure is the only good. A third fastens on his proof. “The sole evidence it is possible to produce that anything is desirable,” he wrote, “is that people do actually desire it.” But “visible” means can be seen, and “desirable” means ought to be desired, and from the fact that people want something it does not follow that they should.
paras.zh: 批評者始終沒有被滿足。如果規則之所以要緊，只是因為它們的結果，那麼在那個罕見的情況裡：違反一條規則確定會帶來更多的善，而且永遠不會被發現，這個理論就再也沒有理由遵守它了；而檢驗一個理論的，正是這種情況。第二個反駁針對較高級的快樂。如果有些快樂在「種類」上比較好，與它們有多令人愉快無關，那麼就有快樂之外的某個東西使它們比較好；而彌爾已經悄悄放棄了「快樂是唯一的善」這個看法。第三個反駁緊抓著他的證明。他寫道：「要證明任何東西是可欲的，所能提出的唯一證據，就是人們實際上欲求它。」然而，visible（可見的）的意思是「能夠被看見」，desirable（可欲的）的意思卻是「應該被欲求」；而從「人們想要某樣東西」這個事實，推不出他們應該想要它。

paras.en: Mill’s life is known chiefly from his Autobiography, written in the 1850s and revised until his death. It is a remarkable document and a partial one. It is organized as the history of an education. His mother is not mentioned in it, and his eight younger brothers and sisters, most of whom he taught, hardly appear. Of Harriet Taylor he writes in terms that readers have always found extravagant. He credits her with a mind greater than his own, and says of their later books that “the most valuable ideas and features in these joint productions… originated with her.” Scholars have disagreed ever since about how literally to take him. Little survives in her hand beyond an essay on the enfranchisement of women and her letters. Some hold that he exaggerated out of love and grief. Others point out that the works written during and just after their marriage, On Liberty above all, differ in spirit from what he wrote before, and that the assumption that a woman could not have contributed much is the very prejudice the two of them wrote against.
paras.zh: 彌爾的生平，主要是靠他的《自傳》為人所知；這本書寫於 1850 年代，一直修訂到他去世。它是一份非凡的文獻，也是一份片面的文獻。它被組織成「一場教育的歷史」。書裡沒有提到他的母親；他的八個弟妹（其中多數是他教的）也幾乎沒有出現。談到海莉耶・泰勒，他用的措辭，讀者向來覺得過度。他說她的心智比他自己的更偉大；談到他們後期的著作，他說：「這些共同作品裡最有價值的觀念與特色……是源自於她。」此後，學者們對於該多照字面相信他，一直意見分歧。她親筆留下的東西，除了一篇論女性參政權的文章與她的書信之外，所剩無幾。有些人認為，他是出於愛與悲傷而誇大了。另一些人指出：在他們婚姻期間與剛結束之後寫成的作品（尤其是《論自由》），在精神上與他先前寫的不同；而「一個女人不可能有多少貢獻」這個預設，正是他們兩人寫書所反對的那種偏見。

said.claim: “The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.” (Edmund Burke)
said.claim_zh: 「邪惡得勝唯一需要的，就是好人什麼也不做。」（艾德蒙・柏克）
said.verdict_en: Not Burke. Mill said something close
said.verdict_zh: 不是柏克。彌爾說過很接近的話
said.en: No one has found this sentence in Burke. The nearest thing in print comes from Mill, in the address he gave as rector of the University of St Andrews in 1867: “Bad men need nothing more to compass their ends, than that good men should look on and do nothing.” The thought suits him. It denies that a person can keep clean hands by standing still, which is the utilitarian’s answer to the bystander at the switch who says that the five deaths are not his doing.
said.zh: 沒有人在柏克的著作裡找到過這句話。見於印刷品而最接近的一句出自彌爾，是他 1867 年就任聖安德魯斯大學校長時的演說：「壞人要達到他們的目的，所需要的不過是好人袖手旁觀、什麼也不做。」這個想法很符合他。它否認一個人可以靠著站著不動而保持雙手乾淨；轉轍器旁那位旁觀者說「那五個人的死不是我造成的」，這就是效益主義者對他的回答。

paras.en: Mill’s morality and the Buddha’s have the same scope. Both take the suffering and happiness of every sentient being to count, both refuse to give one’s own a special weight, and Mill’s phrase “the whole sentient creation” could stand as a translation of the Buddhist wish that all beings be happy. Mill’s crisis also taught him something the Buddha had taught. Happiness sought directly recedes. Mill’s remedy was to aim at some other end and find happiness “by the way.” The Buddhist analysis goes a step further and says why: the seeking is itself the craving that makes contentment impossible.
paras.zh: 彌爾的道德與佛陀的道德，範圍是相同的。兩者都把每一個有情眾生的苦與樂算進去，兩者都拒絕給自己的苦樂特別的分量；而彌爾那句「一切有感知的受造物」，可以當作佛教「願一切眾生安樂」這個願望的翻譯。彌爾的危機也教了他一件佛陀教過的事：直接去追求的幸福會後退。彌爾的對治，是去瞄準某個別的目的，「順路」找到幸福。佛教的分析多走了一步，說出了為什麼：那個追求本身，就是使滿足成為不可能的渴愛。

paras.en: They differ on three points. Mill judges an act by its results and holds that “the motive has nothing to do with the morality of the action.” The Buddha judges it by the intention, and a harmful result that was not intended is not an unwholesome deed. Second, Mill adds happiness across persons, so that a loss to one can be outweighed by gains to many. Buddhist ethics has no such sum. It asks each agent not to harm, and the bodhisattva who gives his body to feed a tigress gives his own and no one else’s. Third, they mean different things by happiness. Mill’s higher pleasures are the satisfactions of a cultivated mind, and they remain satisfactions of desire. The Buddha ranks above all of these a happiness that comes from the ending of desire. Whether that is a still higher pleasure on Mill’s scale or something the scale cannot measure is a good question to put to both (Dharma and the West, D18).
paras.zh: 他們在三點上不同。彌爾依結果來評判一個行為，並且主張「動機與行為的道德性無關」。佛陀依意圖來評判；一個並非出於意圖的有害結果，不算是不善業。第二，彌爾把不同的人的幸福加總起來，所以一個人的損失可以被許多人的獲益抵過。佛教倫理沒有這樣一筆總帳。它要求每一個行動者不去傷害；而那位捨身飼虎的菩薩，捨的是自己的身體，不是別人的。第三，他們說的「幸福」不是同一個意思。彌爾的高級快樂，是一個有教養的心靈的滿足，而它們仍然是欲望的滿足。佛陀把一種「來自欲望止息」的樂，排在這一切之上。那是彌爾的量尺上一種更高的快樂，還是這把量尺量不了的東西？這是一個值得同時向兩人提出的好問題（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms.d_en: Actions are right in proportion as they tend to promote happiness.
terms.d_zh: 行為之為對，與它們增進幸福的傾向成比例。

terms.d_en: Pleasures of intellect, feeling, and conscience, which Mill held to be better in kind than bodily ones.
terms.d_zh: 智性、情感與良知的快樂；彌爾主張它們在種類上優於身體的快樂。

terms.d_en: Society may restrain a person only to prevent harm to others.
terms.d_zh: 社會只有為了防止對他人的傷害，才可以約束一個人。

terms.d_en: The oppression of individuals by prevailing opinion, which Mill feared more than oppression by governments.
terms.d_zh: 盛行的輿論對個人的壓迫；彌爾對它的恐懼，更甚於政府的壓迫。

terms.d_en: The view that we should follow the rules whose general observance has the best results. Often read into Mill.
terms.d_zh: 主張我們應該遵循那些「普遍被遵守時結果最好」的規則。常被認為是彌爾的意思。

terms.d_en: G. E. Moore’s name for inferring what is good from what is desired or natural.
terms.d_zh: 摩爾取的名字：從「被欲求的」或「自然的」推論出「善的」。

quiz.q: How did Mill change Bentham’s account of happiness?
options: He held that pleasures differ in kind as well as in amount.
He denied that happiness matters.
He limited it to the happiness of the agent.
He replaced it with duty.

quiz.q: What does the harm principle say?
options: Power may rightfully be used over a person against his will only to prevent harm to others.
No one may ever be harmed.
The state should make people happy.
Harmful opinions should be silenced.

quiz.q: What did Mill conclude from his mental crisis?
options: Happiness is found by aiming at something else, and the feelings need cultivation.
Philosophy is useless.
Bentham was entirely wrong.
Poetry should replace logic.

further.t: J. S. Mill, Utilitarianism
further.n_en: Five short chapters. Chapter 2 states the theory, chapter 5 defends it against the charge of injustice.
further.n_zh: 五個短章。第二章陳述理論，第五章回應「不正義」的指控。

further.t: J. S. Mill, On Liberty
J. S. Mill, Autobiography
further.n_en: Chapter 1 is the education. Chapter 5 is the crisis.
further.n_zh: 第一章是那場教育，第五章是危機。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “John Stuart Mill”

philosophers.name: Immanuel Kant
philosophers.tag_en: A harness-maker’s son who never left his province, and who drew the limits of human knowledge and the foundation of human dignity from a single principle: that reason gives the law to itself.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個馬具匠的兒子，一生沒有離開過他的省份；他從同一條原理——理性為自己立法——劃出了人類知識的界限，也立下了人類尊嚴的根基。
facts: Johann Georg Kant, harness-maker; Anna Regina Reuter. Devout Pietists
Professor of logic and metaphysics, University of Königsberg, from 1770
Critique of Pure Reason (1781); Groundwork (1785); Critique of Practical Reason (1788); Critique of Judgment (1790)

paras.en: Kant was born in 1724 in Königsberg, a Baltic port at the eastern edge of the German-speaking world, and he died there seventy-nine years later without ever having traveled more than a few days’ journey from it. His father made harnesses. The family belonged to the Pietists, a Lutheran movement that valued inward devotion, plain living, and strict self-examination, and Kant said in old age that no one could have had a better moral education than his parents gave him. The school the Pietists ran was another matter. He remembered its regime of prayer and drill with something like horror, and it left him with a lifelong dislike of religious enthusiasm.
paras.zh: 康德 1724 年生於柯尼斯堡，波羅的海邊的一個港口，位於德語世界的東緣；七十九年後，他在那裡去世，一生沒有到過離它幾天路程以外的地方。他的父親是做馬具的。這家人屬於敬虔派，那是路德宗內部一個看重內在虔誠、樸素生活與嚴格自我省察的運動；康德晚年說，沒有人能得到比他父母給他的更好的道德教育。敬虔派辦的學校則是另一回事。他回想起那裡的祈禱與操練，帶著近乎恐懼的心情；那所學校讓他一輩子不喜歡宗教狂熱。

paras.en: He entered the local university at sixteen and discovered Newton. When his father died he had to leave without a post, and for nine years he worked as a tutor in country houses. He returned in 1755 as an unsalaried lecturer, paid by the students who chose to attend, and he lectured for fifteen years on almost everything: logic, physics, mathematics, geography, anthropology, fortification. In those years he was known as an elegant and witty man, a good hand at billiards and cards and a sought-after dinner guest. He proposed, in a work on astronomy, that the solar system had condensed from a rotating cloud of gas, a hypothesis that is still accepted in outline.
paras.zh: 他十六歲進了當地的大學，發現了牛頓。父親去世時，他還沒有職位就不得不離開；有九年之久，他在鄉間的大宅裡當家庭教師。1755 年他回來，當一名沒有薪水的講師，收入來自選擇來聽課的學生；他講了十五年的課，幾乎什麼都講：邏輯、物理、數學、地理、人類學、築城學。那些年裡，人們知道他是一個優雅而風趣的人，撞球與牌都打得好，是受歡迎的晚宴賓客。他在一部天文學著作裡提出：太陽系是從一團旋轉的氣體雲凝聚而成的；這個假說的大綱至今仍被接受。

paras.en: In 1770, at forty-six, he was at last given the chair of logic and metaphysics. Then he published almost nothing for eleven years. He had read David Hume, and Hume’s argument that we have no rational ground for believing in causation had, he wrote, “first interrupted my dogmatic slumber.” If Hume was right, science had no foundation. If Hume was wrong, someone had to show how the mind can know in advance of experience that every event has a cause. Kant’s friends expected a book each year, and each year he wrote that it was nearly ready. The Critique of Pure Reason appeared in 1781, eight hundred pages put on paper, by his own account, in four or five months after twelve years of thought. The first reviewers found it unreadable.
paras.zh: 1770 年，四十六歲的他終於得到了邏輯與形上學的教席。然後，他有十一年幾乎什麼也沒發表。他讀了休謨；而休謨的論證（我們沒有理性的根據相信因果關係），他寫道，「最先打斷了我的獨斷論的迷夢」。如果休謨是對的，科學就沒有地基。如果休謨是錯的，就得有人說明：心靈怎麼能夠在經驗之前就知道每一個事件都有原因。康德的朋友們年年期待一本書，而他年年寫信說快好了。《純粹理性批判》在 1781 年問世；八百頁，照他自己的說法，是在十二年的思考之後，用四五個月寫到紙上的。最早的書評者覺得它根本讀不下去。

paras.en: He was fifty-seven, and the works that made him the central figure of modern philosophy were all still to come. They followed within a decade: the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals in 1785, a second edition of the first Critique in 1787, the Critique of Practical Reason in 1788, and the Critique of Judgment in 1790.
paras.zh: 那年他五十七歲；而使他成為近代哲學核心人物的那些著作，全都還沒寫出來。它們在十年之內接連問世：1785 年的《道德形上學基礎》、1787 年的第一批判第二版、1788 年的《實踐理性批判》，以及 1790 年的《判斷力批判》。

paras.en: By then his life had taken the fixed form for which he is remembered. He rose at five, drank tea, smoked one pipe, lectured from seven, wrote until one, and dined at length with guests chosen from outside the university, since he disliked talking philosophy at table. At half past three he walked, alone and breathing through his nose, and it is said that his neighbors set their clocks by him. The one recorded lapse came when he was reading Rousseau’s Emile and could not put it down. Rousseau’s portrait hung in his study, the only picture in the house. It was Rousseau, he wrote, who had cured him of despising the ignorant and taught him to honor human beings.
paras.zh: 到那時候，他的生活已經定型成後人記得的那個樣子。他五點起床，喝茶，抽一斗菸，七點開始講課，寫作到一點，然後跟賓客慢慢吃一頓午餐；賓客是從大學以外挑的，因為他不喜歡在餐桌上談哲學。三點半他去散步，一個人，用鼻子呼吸；據說他的鄰居靠他來對時。有紀錄的唯一一次失常，是他在讀盧梭的《愛彌兒》，放不下來。盧梭的肖像掛在他的書房裡，是屋子裡唯一的一幅畫。他寫道，是盧梭治好了他對無知者的輕視，教會了他尊重人。

paras.en: He welcomed the American and French revolutions and went on defending the principles of the second after the Terror had turned most of his countrymen against it. In 1794 his book on religion brought a rebuke from the Prussian king and an order to write no more on the subject, which he obeyed until the king died. His mind began to fail in his last years. He died on February 12, 1804. His last words, on being given a little wine and water, were “It is good.” The city turned out for the funeral.
paras.zh: 他歡迎美國與法國的革命；在恐怖統治使他大多數的同胞轉而反對後者之後，他仍然繼續為它的原則辯護。1794 年，他談宗教的那本書招來了普魯士國王的申斥，以及一道不准再寫這個題目的命令；他遵守到國王去世為止。在最後幾年，他的心智開始衰退。1804 年 2 月 12 日，他去世了。有人給了他一點摻水的酒，他最後的話是：「很好。」全城的人都出來送葬。

idea.title_en: The central idea: The mind gives the law
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：心靈立法

paras.en: Before Kant, philosophers assumed that knowledge is the mind’s conforming to objects, and they could not explain how we know anything about objects in advance, as we seem to in mathematics and in the principle that every event has a cause. Kant proposed to try the opposite assumption. Copernicus, unable to explain the motions of the heavens while supposing that they revolve around the spectator, tried “looking for the observed movements not in the heavenly bodies, but in the spectator.” Suppose, likewise, that objects conform to our way of knowing. Space, time, and causation are then the forms that the mind brings to experience. We can know in advance that everything we meet will be in space and time and subject to causal law, because nothing could be an experience for us otherwise. The price is that we know things only as they appear to beings like us. What they are in themselves we cannot know. Both halves are needed: “Thoughts without content are void; intuitions without conceptions, blind.”
paras.zh: 在康德之前，哲學家預設知識是心靈去符合對象；而他們無法解釋，我們怎麼能預先知道關於對象的任何事，就像我們在數學裡、以及在「每一個事件都有原因」這條原理上似乎做到的那樣。康德提議試試相反的預設。哥白尼假定天體繞著觀察者轉的時候，解釋不了天體的運動；於是他試著「不在天體那裡、而在觀察者這裡，去尋找所觀察到的運動」。同樣地，假設是對象來符合我們認識的方式。那麼，空間、時間與因果，就是心靈帶給經驗的形式。我們可以預先知道，我們遇到的一切都會在空間與時間之中，並且服從因果法則；因為若不如此，就沒有任何東西能成為我們的經驗。代價是：我們只認識事物對「像我們這樣的存在者」顯現的樣子。它們本身是什麼，我們無從得知。兩半都少不了：「思想無內容是空的，直觀無概念是盲的。」

paras.en: The same move governs his ethics. The moral law is not handed to us by God, nature, or society. A rational being gives it to itself, and Kant’s word for this is autonomy, self-legislation. To act morally is to act on a principle that one can will as a law for all rational beings, and to be capable of this is to have a worth that nothing can be traded for. Things have a price. Persons have dignity. Near the end of the second Critique he set the two halves of his philosophy side by side, in the sentence that was later cut on his tomb: “Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe, the oftener and the more steadily we reflect on them: the starry heavens above and the moral law within.”
paras.zh: 同樣的一步，支配著他的倫理學。道德法則不是上帝、自然或社會交給我們的。一個理性的存在者把它交給自己；康德用來稱呼這件事的詞是「自律」，自我立法。合乎道德地行動，就是依照一條自己能夠意願成為一切理性存在者之法則的原則去行動；而有能力這樣做，就擁有了一種什麼也換不走的價值。物有價格。人有尊嚴。在第二批判接近結尾的地方，他把自己哲學的兩半並排放在一起，那句話後來被刻在他的墓上：「有兩樣東西，我們越是經常、越是持續地反省它們，它們就越是以常新而且不斷增長的讚嘆與敬畏充滿心靈：我頭上的星空，與我心中的道德法則。」

quote.en: Two things fill the mind with ever new and increasing admiration and awe, the oftener and the more steadily we reflect on them: the starry heavens above and the moral law within.
quote.zh: 有兩樣東西，我們越是經常、越是持續地反省它們，它們就越是以常新而且不斷增長的讚嘆與敬畏充滿心靈：我頭上的星空，與我心中的道德法則。
quote.ref: Kant, Critique of Practical Reason, Conclusion, tr. T. K. Abbott
quote.note_en: The first shows us how small we are as animals. The second shows what we are worth as persons.
quote.note_zh: 前者讓我們看到，作為動物，我們多麼渺小。後者讓我們看到，作為人格，我們價值幾何。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Rigor without eyes
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：沒有眼睛的嚴格

paras.en: The charge made in his own lifetime was that the theory is too rigid to live by. When Benjamin Constant asked whether one must tell the truth to a murderer seeking one’s friend, Kant answered that one must, and the essay in which he said so has embarrassed his admirers for two hundred years. Hegel pressed a deeper version. The test of universal law, he argued, is empty. It can show that a maxim is consistent, and almost any maxim can be made consistent if it is described carefully. The real content of morality comes from the customs and institutions of an actual community, and Kant has mistaken the form of morality for its source. A third criticism comes from Aristotle’s side. A person who visits a sick friend because duty requires it has, most of us feel, missed something that the friend who comes out of affection has not.
paras.zh: 在他有生之年就有人提出的指控是：這個理論太僵硬，沒辦法照著過日子。貢斯當問：對一個正在找你朋友的兇手，是否也必須說實話？康德回答：必須；而他說這話的那篇文章，讓他的仰慕者難堪了兩百年。黑格爾提出了一個更深的版本。他論證：普遍法則的檢驗是空的。它能顯示一條準則是否前後一致；而幾乎任何準則，只要小心地描述，都可以弄得前後一致。道德真正的內容，來自一個實際共同體的習俗與制度；康德把道德的形式誤當成了它的來源。第三個批評來自亞里斯多德那一邊。一個因為義務要求而去探望生病朋友的人，我們多數人都覺得，他錯過了那位出於情誼而來的朋友沒有錯過的某個東西。

paras.en: A different objection has become prominent in recent decades. The philosopher of universal human dignity also lectured for years on anthropology and physical geography, and in those lectures and some essays he ranked the peoples of the world in a hierarchy of races with Europeans at the top. In his later political writings he condemned colonial conquest and slavery. Scholars disagree about whether he changed his mind or held both views at once. Either way, his case shows how a thinker can state a principle that condemns his own prejudice and fail for most of his life to apply it.
paras.zh: 近幾十年來，另一個反駁變得突出。這位講「普遍的人類尊嚴」的哲學家，也講了多年的人類學與自然地理學；在那些講課與某些文章裡，他把世界上的各個民族排成一個種族的等級，歐洲人在最上面。在後期的政治著作裡，他譴責了殖民征服與奴隸制。學者們對於他是改變了想法、還是同時抱持兩種看法，意見分歧。不管是哪一種，他的例子都顯示：一個思想者可以說出一條譴責他自己偏見的原則，卻在大半生當中沒有去運用它。

paras.en: The Kant of legend, a thinking machine who never altered his walk, comes mostly from three memoirs published by acquaintances in the year of his death, which describe the routines of a man over sixty, and from a brilliant page of the poet Heinrich Heine, written thirty years later, which says that he had neither life nor history. The record of his first forty-five years is thinner and shows someone else: a popular lecturer who was told by a friend that he spent too much time at dinners and card tables to write the books he was capable of. The regularity was adopted in middle age, on the advice of an English merchant friend, by a man with a weak chest who had decided that he had work to finish.
paras.zh: 傳說中的康德，是一台從不改變散步路線的思考機器；這個形象主要來自他去世那年三位熟人出版的回憶錄（它們描述的是一個六十多歲的人的作息），以及詩人海涅三十年後寫下的精彩的一頁，那一頁說他既沒有生活、也沒有歷史。關於他前四十五年的紀錄比較單薄，呈現的卻是另一個人：一位受歡迎的講師，有朋友告訴他，他花太多時間在晚宴與牌桌上，寫不出他有能力寫的書。那份規律是中年才採取的，出於一位英國商人朋友的建議；採取它的，是一個胸腔虛弱、並且認定自己有工作要完成的人。

paras.en: His books raise a different problem of access. He wrote in a technical vocabulary that he largely invented, and he revised his central work so heavily for its second edition that scholars cite the two by letter, A and B, and still argue about which represents his real view. He knew that he was hard to read and said that the fault lay in the subject.
paras.zh: 他的書帶來的，是另一種「怎麼進得去」的問題。他用一套大體上是自己發明的術語寫作；而他為了第二版，把自己的核心著作改得太多，以致學者用字母 A 與 B 分別引用兩個版本，並且至今仍在爭論哪一個代表他真正的看法。他知道自己難讀；他說，錯在題材。

said.claim: “Sapere aude! Have courage to use your own understanding!” (Kant)
said.claim_zh: 「Sapere aude！要有勇氣運用你自己的理智！」（康德）
said.verdict_zh: 他的座右銘，賀拉斯的話
said.en: The sentence opens Kant’s essay of 1784, “An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?” Enlightenment, he says, is a person’s emergence from an immaturity that is his own fault, the inability to use his understanding without direction from another, and Sapere aude is its motto. The two Latin words are borrowed. They come from the Roman poet Horace, who used them in a verse letter to a young friend around 20 BCE: he who has begun has half done; dare to be wise; begin. Kant turned a piece of private advice into the slogan of an age.
said.zh: 這句話是康德 1784 年那篇文章〈答「何謂啟蒙？」之問題〉的開頭。他說，啟蒙就是人從一種「咎由自取的未成年狀態」當中走出來；那種狀態，就是沒有別人的指導就無法運用自己的理智。Sapere aude 是啟蒙的座右銘。這兩個拉丁字是借來的。它們出自羅馬詩人賀拉斯；大約在西元前 20 年，他在寫給一位年輕朋友的詩體書信裡用了它們：開始了就是完成了一半；要敢於明智；動手吧。康德把一句私人的勸告，變成了一個時代的口號。

paras.en: The closest meeting is over the questions that cannot be answered. The Buddha was asked whether the world is eternal or not, finite or infinite, and whether the soul is the same as the body or different, and he set the questions aside as undetermined. Kant’s first Critique contains a section called the Antinomies, in which he takes the same questions, whether the world has a beginning in time and a limit in space, and proves both the yes and the no with equal rigor. His conclusion is that reason contradicts itself when it tries to speak of the world as a whole, because it has gone beyond any possible experience. The two give different reasons for the silence. The Buddha says that the questions do not lead to the end of suffering. Kant says that the human mind is not equipped to settle them. The Indian philosopher T. R. V. Murti argued in 1955 that the Madhyamaka school’s method, which shows that every view about ultimate reality leads to contradiction, is the nearest thing in world philosophy to Kant’s critique.
paras.zh: 兩人最接近的交會，是在那些無法回答的問題上。有人問佛陀：世界是永恆的還是不永恆的？有邊的還是無邊的？命（靈魂）與身體是同一個還是不同的？他把這些問題擱置為「無記」。康德的第一批判裡有一節叫作「二律背反」；他在那裡拿了同樣的問題（世界在時間上有沒有開端、在空間上有沒有界限），並且以同等的嚴格，把「有」與「沒有」都證明了出來。他的結論是：理性一旦試圖談論作為整體的世界，就會自相矛盾，因為它已經越出了任何可能的經驗。兩人對這份沉默給的理由不同。佛陀說，這些問題不導向苦的止息。康德說，人類的心靈沒有配備去解決它們。印度哲學家穆諦在 1955 年論證：中觀學派的方法（顯示關於究竟真實的每一種見解都會導致矛盾），是世界哲學當中最接近康德的「批判」的東西。

paras.en: Kant’s distinction between things as they appear and things in themselves has often been set beside the Buddhist two truths, and the comparison needs care. For Kant there is a reality behind appearances that we cannot reach. For Nāgārjuna there is nothing hidden behind the conventional world, and the ultimate truth is the emptiness of that very world. In ethics the two share a universal scope and part over the role of feeling. Kant distrusts inclination and locates moral worth in duty done against it. The Buddhist path is a training of inclination, so that kindness is finally what one wants to do. And Kant holds that morality needs a free and responsible self as its postulate, which is a place where the teaching of not-self would press him hard (Dharma and the West, D10 and D21).
paras.zh: 康德對「顯現的事物」與「物自身」的區分，常被拿來跟佛教的二諦並列；這個比較需要小心。對康德來說，在現象背後有一個我們到不了的實在。對龍樹來說，世俗的世界背後並沒有藏著什麼；勝義諦，就是這個世界本身的空。在倫理學上，兩者共有普遍的範圍，卻在情感的角色上分道揚鑣。康德不信任愛好，並且把道德價值放在違逆愛好而履行的義務上。佛教的道，則是對愛好的一種訓練，使仁慈最終成為一個人「想要」做的事。還有，康德主張道德需要一個自由而負責的自我作為它的設準；在這個地方，無我的教導會對他步步進逼（佛法與西方哲學 D10、D21）。

terms.d_en: Known independently of experience, as against a posteriori, known from it.
terms.d_zh: 獨立於經驗而被知道的；相對於 a posteriori（後天的），即由經驗而知的。

terms.o: Gk. phainomenon ‘what appears’; nooumenon ‘what is thought’
terms.d_en: A thing as it appears to us, and the thing as it is in itself.
terms.d_zh: 事物對我們顯現的樣子，以及事物本身的樣子。

terms.d_en: Concerned with the conditions that make experience possible.
terms.d_zh: 關乎使經驗成為可能的那些條件。

terms.d_en: Giving the moral law to oneself through reason. Its opposite is heteronomy, taking the law from outside.
terms.d_zh: 透過理性為自己立下道德法則。它的反面是他律，即從外面接受法則。

terms.d_en: A pair of contradictory claims each of which can apparently be proved.
terms.d_zh: 一對互相矛盾的主張，兩者看來都可以被證明。

terms.d_en: The worth of a person, which is beyond all price and admits no equivalent.
terms.d_zh: 人格的價值；它超乎一切價格，沒有等價物。

quiz.q: What is Kant’s “Copernican” move?
options: Supposing that objects conform to our way of knowing, instead of the reverse.
Proving that the earth goes around the sun.
Denying that anything can be known.
Deriving all knowledge from the senses.

quiz.q: What does autonomy mean in his ethics?
options: A rational being gives the moral law to itself.
Each person may do as he likes.
The state decides what is right.
Morality comes from feeling.

quiz.q: What was Hegel’s objection?
options: The universal law test is an empty form and cannot supply the content of morality.
Kant relied too much on feeling.
Kant denied free will.
Kant ignored logic.

further.n_en: The place to begin.
further.n_zh: 從這裡開始。

further.t: Kant, “An Answer to the Question: What Is Enlightenment?” (1784)
further.n_en: Six pages. His most readable piece.
further.n_zh: 六頁。他最好讀的一篇。

further.n_zh: 他自己為第一批判寫的簡短導讀。

further.n_en: The life that corrects the legend.
further.n_zh: 一部修正了傳說的傳記。

philosophers.name: Confucius
philosophers.tag_en: A failed official and wandering teacher who said he invented nothing, and whose conversations became the education of East Asia for two thousand years.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個失意的官員與周遊的老師；他說自己什麼也沒有創作，而他的談話成了東亞兩千年的教育。
facts: 551 BCE, Zou, in the state of Lu (near modern Qufu, Shandong)
479 BCE, Lu, aged seventy-three by Chinese reckoning
Family name Kong 孔, personal name Qiu 丘, courtesy name Zhongni 仲尼. “Confucius” is Latin for Kong Fuzi, Master Kong
Teacher; briefly an official in Lu
The Analects 論語, sayings recorded by his students and theirs
By tradition three thousand, seventy-two of them accomplished

life.h_en: A poor boy who loved the old ways

paras.en: Confucius was born in 551 BCE in Lu, a small state in what is now Shandong. The Zhou kings, who had ruled for five centuries, still reigned in name, and real power had passed to a dozen states that fought one another and were themselves torn by their great families. His father, an old soldier, died when he was a small child, and he grew up poor. He later summed up his life in six steps: “At fifteen I set my heart on learning. At thirty I stood firm. At forty I had no doubts. At fifty I knew the decree of Heaven. At sixty my ear was attuned. At seventy I could follow what my heart desired without overstepping the line.”
paras.zh: 孔子西元前 551 年生於魯國，一個位於今天山東的小國。已經統治了五個世紀的周王，名義上仍然在位；實權則已落入十幾個諸侯國手中，它們彼此攻伐，各自又被國內的大家族撕裂。他的父親是一位老武士，在他年幼時就去世了；他在貧寒中長大。他後來用六步總結了自己的一生：「吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。」

paras.en: What he set his heart on was the culture of the early Zhou: its rites, its music, its odes and records. He believed that the founders of the dynasty had known how human beings should live together, and that the violence of his own day came from forgetting it. He described himself as “a transmitter and not a maker, one who trusts and loves the ancients.” In his thirties he began to take students, and he seems to have been the first person in China to make a living by teaching. He took anyone who came. “From the man who brought a bundle of dried meat upward,” he said, “I have never refused instruction to anyone.”
paras.zh: 他立志去學的，是周初的文化：它的禮、它的樂、它的詩與典冊。他相信，這個王朝的開創者懂得人應該怎樣共同生活；而他自己那個時代的暴力，來自把這些忘掉了。他形容自己是「述而不作，信而好古」。三十多歲時，他開始收學生；他似乎是中國第一個以教書為生的人。來者不拒。他說：「自行束脩以上，吾未嘗無誨焉。」

paras.en: He wanted office, since he held that a good man’s place is in government. Around the age of fifty he was given a post in Lu and rose, tradition says, to be minister of justice. It did not last. Finding that the duke would not listen, he left the state in 497 with a band of students and spent fourteen years traveling from court to court in search of a ruler who would put his ideas into practice. None would. He was threatened, surrounded, and once nearly starved. At the gate of one city he became separated from his students, and a local man told them he had seen a stranger standing there who looked “like a dog from a house in mourning,” with no one to feed him. When this was repeated to Confucius he laughed and said, “That is it exactly.”
paras.zh: 他想做官，因為他主張好人的位置在政府裡。大約五十歲時，他在魯國得到一個職位；傳說他升到了大司寇。好景不長。他發現國君不肯聽，就在西元前 497 年帶著一群學生離開了魯國，花了十四年從一個朝廷走到另一個朝廷，尋找一位肯把他的主張付諸實行的君主。沒有一位肯。他被威脅過、被圍困過，有一次差點餓死。在一座城的城門口，他與學生走散了；有個當地人告訴他的學生，看見一個陌生人站在那裡，「纍纍若喪家之狗」。這話轉述給孔子聽，他欣然笑了，說：「然哉！然哉！」

paras.en: The hermits he met on the road thought him a fool. Two of them, plowing a field, told his student that the whole world was a flood and that it would be wiser to follow those who flee the age than one who merely flees one bad ruler after another. Confucius sighed when he heard it. “One cannot flock with birds and beasts. If I do not associate with these people, with whom should I associate? If the Way prevailed in the world, I would not be trying to change it.” A gatekeeper put the general opinion in one line: is that the man who knows it cannot be done and keeps on doing it?
paras.zh: 他在路上遇到的隱士，都認為他是個傻子。其中兩位正在耕田，他們告訴他的學生：天下滔滔，到處都是洪水；與其跟著一個只是躲開一個又一個壞君主的人，不如跟著躲開這整個時代的人。孔子聽了，悵然嘆息：「鳥獸不可與同群！吾非斯人之徒與而誰與？天下有道，丘不與易也。」一位守城門的人，用一句話說出了一般人的看法：「是知其不可而為之者與？」

paras.en: He came home to Lu in 484, aged sixty-seven, and gave his last years to teaching and to the old texts. Tradition credits him with editing the Odes and the Documents and with composing the chronicle of Lu, and says that he read the Book of Changes so often that the leather thongs binding its bamboo strips wore through three times. His son died before him, and so did Yan Hui, the student he loved best. He died in 479, believing that he had failed. Some of his students mourned at the grave for three years, and one stayed for six.
paras.zh: 西元前 484 年，他回到魯國，六十七歲；他把最後的歲月給了教學與古籍。傳統把刪定《詩》《書》、作《春秋》歸功於他，並且說他讀《易》讀到「韋編三絕」。他的兒子比他先死；他最鍾愛的學生顏回也是。西元前 479 年，他去世了，相信自己失敗了。有些學生在墓旁守喪三年，有一位守了六年。

paras.en: Four centuries later the historian Sima Qian visited the temple at Qufu, saw the carriage, the robes, and the ritual vessels, and watched the students practicing the rites. He wrote that he lingered and could not bring himself to leave. Kings and worthies beyond number were honored in their day and forgotten at their death. Confucius was a commoner, and after more than ten generations scholars still took him as their master.
paras.zh: 四個世紀之後，史家司馬遷造訪了曲阜的孔廟，看了那輛車、那些衣服與禮器，看著儒生們在那裡按時習禮。他寫道，自己「祗回留之不能去」。天下的君王與賢人多得數不清，「當時則榮，沒則已焉」。孔子是一介布衣，「傳十餘世，學者宗之」。

timeline: Han court makes the Confucian classics the basis of state learning

idea.title_en: The central idea: Becoming human through ritual
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：經由禮而成為人

paras.en: The word at the center of his teaching is rén, written with the signs for “person” and “two.” It has been translated as benevolence, humaneness, and goodness, and none fits exactly, because it names the whole quality of a person who is as a human being ought to be in relation to others. Asked what it is, he gives a different answer to each student. To one he says, “Love others.” To another he gives the rule he calls reciprocity: “What you do not want for yourself, do not do to others.” To his best student he gives the hardest answer: “To master oneself and return to ritual is rén.” Asked for the details, he adds: do not look at, listen to, say, or do what is contrary to ritual.
paras.zh: 他的教導的核心字是「仁」，由「人」與「二」組成。它被譯成 benevolence、humaneness、goodness，沒有一個完全貼切；因為它指稱的，是一個在與他人的關係裡「成為人所應當是的樣子」的人的整體品質。有人問它是什麼，他對每一個學生的回答都不同。對一位他說：「愛人。」對另一位，他給了他稱為「恕」的那條規則：「己所不欲，勿施於人。」對他最好的學生，他給了最難的答案：「克己復禮為仁。」學生請問細目，他補充：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」

paras.en: The pairing of inner goodness with outward ritual is his distinctive idea. By ritual, lǐ, he means the whole body of inherited forms through which people show respect: mourning, greeting, serving a meal, addressing a parent. A modern reader takes these for etiquette. Confucius saw in them the means by which raw feeling is shaped into something humane, as a language shapes thought. A child who is taught to bow to his elders is being taught to notice them. Done without feeling, the forms are empty, and he says so often. Done well, they make a community in which force is rarely needed. His political theory follows directly. Government is a matter of setting people right by example: “Let the ruler be a ruler, the minister a minister, the father a father, the son a son.” The person formed in this way he calls the jūnzǐ, the gentleman, a word that had meant a nobleman by birth and that he redefined as a nobleman by character.
paras.zh: 把內在的善與外在的禮配成一對，是他獨特的想法。他所說的「禮」，指的是人們藉以表達敬意的那一整套傳承下來的形式：守喪、問候、奉食、稱呼父母。現代的讀者把這些當成禮節。孔子在其中看到的，是把原始的情感塑造成合乎人道的東西的手段，就像語言塑造思想一樣。一個被教導要向長輩鞠躬的孩子，是在被教導去「注意到」他們。沒有情感而行，這些形式是空的；這一點他常說。行得好，它們造就一個很少需要動用強力的共同體。他的政治理論由此直接推出。為政就是以身作則地使人歸正：「君君，臣臣，父父，子子。」這樣養成的人，他稱為「君子」；這個詞原本指出身上的貴族，而他把它重新界定為品格上的貴族。

quote.en: At fifteen I set my heart on learning. At thirty I stood firm. At forty I had no doubts. At fifty I knew the decree of Heaven. At sixty my ear was attuned. At seventy I could follow what my heart desired without overstepping the line.
quote.zh: 吾十有五而志于學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十而知天命，六十而耳順，七十而從心所欲，不踰矩。
quote.ref: Analects 2.4, translated for this series
quote.note_en: The shortest autobiography in philosophy. The last step is the goal: a person whose desires and the right have become the same thing.
quote.note_zh: 哲學史上最短的自傳。最後一步就是目標：一個人的欲望與「對的事」已經成了同一回事。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Whose order?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：誰的秩序？

paras.en: His first critics were his contemporaries. Mozi, a generation later, attacked the Confucians on two counts. Their elaborate funerals and three years of mourning waste the wealth of the living, and their ethic of graded love, in which one cares most for one’s own family, is the very partiality that causes war. The Daoists said that he was treating the symptom. Preaching benevolence and ritual is what people do when natural harmony has already been lost. The Legalists, who actually built the first empire, said that he was naive. A state cannot be run on the hope that rulers will be sages. It needs clear laws and reliable punishments.
paras.zh: 他最早的批評者是他同時代的人。晚他一代的墨子，從兩方面攻擊儒者。他們繁複的葬禮與三年之喪，浪費了生者的財富；而他們那套「愛有差等」的倫理（最關心的是自己的家人），正是造成戰爭的那種偏私。道家說，他治的是標。宣講仁與禮，是人們在自然的和諧已經失去之後才做的事。真正建立了第一個帝國的法家說，他太天真。治國不能寄望於君主會是聖人。它需要明確的法與可靠的刑。

paras.en: The modern objection is different. For two thousand years his teaching was the official creed of the Chinese state, and the relations he named, ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, elder and younger, were used to demand obedience from the lower party in each. The students who marched in Beijing in 1919 blamed the weakness of China on “Confucius and Sons” and called for the shop to be torn down. His defenders answer that he taught duties in both directions and said that a ruler who is not a ruler has lost his claim. That is true of the Analects. It remains a fair question whether an ethic built on roles and deference can protect the person whom the roles oppress, and whether it has room for the kind of right that can be claimed against one’s own family.
paras.zh: 現代的反駁不同。有兩千年之久，他的教導是中國這個國家的官方信條；而他所舉出的那些關係（君臣、父子、夫婦、長幼），被用來要求每一對當中居下位的一方服從。1919 年在北京遊行的學生，把中國的積弱歸咎於「孔家店」，喊著要把它打倒。為他辯護的人回答：他教的是雙向的責任，並且說過，一位不像君主的君主，已經失去了他的資格。就《論語》而言，這是真的。然而這仍然是一個合理的問題：一套建立在角色與敬順之上的倫理，保護得了被那些角色壓迫的人嗎？它容得下那種可以向自己的家人主張的「權利」嗎？

problem.title_en: A book he did not write

paras.en: Confucius wrote nothing that we can be sure of. What we have is the Analects, some five hundred short passages in twenty books, most of them beginning “The Master said.” It was put together by his students and their students over a period that may have lasted two centuries, and scholars agree that the books differ in date. The earliest layers are thought to lie in books 3 to 9, and some of the later books show the concerns of schools that formed after his death. The passages have no context and are arranged in no clear order, so that every reader must decide what question a given saying was answering. The biography in Sima Qian’s Records was written about four hundred years after the events, from materials of very uneven value, and includes stories told by his enemies.
paras.zh: 我們能夠確定是孔子寫的東西，一樣也沒有。我們有的是《論語》：二十篇裡大約五百則簡短的文字，大多數以「子曰」開頭。它是由他的學生、以及學生的學生編成的，歷時也許長達兩個世紀；學者們一致認為各篇的年代不同。最早的層次被認為在第三到第九篇；較晚的幾篇，有些顯示的是他身後才形成的學派所關切的事。這些文字沒有脈絡，也沒有清楚的排列次序；所以每一位讀者都得自己判定，某一句話當初回答的是什麼問題。司馬遷《史記》裡的傳，寫於事發約四百年之後，所根據的材料價值極不均等，其中還包括他的敵人所講的故事。

paras.en: There is also the problem of the name. “Confucianism” has meant at different times the teaching of the Analects, the cosmology of the Han court, the metaphysics of the Song philosophers, and a state examination system. He would have recognized perhaps the first. Reading him well means setting aside what was later built in his name and listening to a man in conversation with his students, who is often tired, sometimes funny, and seldom sure that he has succeeded.
paras.zh: 還有名稱的問題。「儒家」在不同的時代，指的分別是《論語》的教導、漢代朝廷的宇宙論、宋代哲學家的形上學，以及一套國家考試制度。他大概只認得出第一個。要把他讀好，就得把後來以他的名義建造起來的東西擱在一邊，去聽一個正在跟學生談話的人說話；他常常疲倦，有時很風趣，而很少確定自己成功了。

said.claim: “Choose a job you love, and you will never have to work a day in your life.” (Confucius)
said.claim_zh: 「選一份你愛的工作，你這輩子就一天也不必工作。」（孔子）
said.verdict_zh: 任何儒家文獻裡都沒有
said.en: This is among the most widely shared “Confucius” quotations in English, and it has no Chinese original. It cannot be found in the Analects or in any other early text, and it began to be attached to his name in American publications in the late twentieth century. The thought is foreign to him. He did not think of work as something to be escaped, and the word he would have used for what one loves is learning. A genuine saying on the subject runs: “To know it is not as good as to love it, and to love it is not as good as to delight in it.”
said.zh: 這是英文世界裡流傳最廣的「孔子語錄」之一，而它並沒有中文原文。在《論語》或任何其他早期文獻裡都找不到它；它是在二十世紀後期的美國出版品裡，才開始被掛到他名下的。這個想法對他來說是陌生的。他並不把工作看成要逃離的東西；而他會用來稱呼「人所愛的事」的那個詞，是「學」。關於這個題目，一句真正出自他的話是：「知之者不如好之者，好之者不如樂之者。」

paras.en: The two were close contemporaries, three thousand kilometers apart, and neither knew of the other. They share a practical temper. When a student asked Confucius about serving the spirits and about death, he replied: “You cannot yet serve the living. How can you serve the spirits? You do not yet understand life. How can you understand death?” The Buddha set aside questions about the origin of the world on similar grounds. Both taught that a person is made by training, both distrusted speculation, and both said in almost the same words that one should not do to others what one would not want for oneself. “To master oneself” is an instruction either could have given.
paras.zh: 兩人是年代很接近的同時代人，相隔三千公里，誰也不知道對方。他們有同樣的務實性情。有學生問孔子怎麼事奉鬼神、問死是怎麼回事，他回答：「未能事人，焉能事鬼？……未知生，焉知死？」佛陀也基於類似的理由，把關於世界起源的問題擱在一邊。兩人都教導人是由訓練造就的，兩人都不信任玄想，兩人也都用幾乎相同的話說過：自己不想要的，不要加在別人身上。「克己」是兩人都可能下的指示。

paras.en: They part over the family. For Confucius the bonds of parent and child are the root of all virtue, and to cut them is to cut the root. The Buddha left his wife and infant son to seek awakening, and he founded an order of men and women who had done the same. When Buddhism entered China this was the first and deepest objection to it. A monk shaves his head, produces no heir, and does not bow to his parents or his king, and by Confucian standards each of these is a failure of filial duty. Chinese Buddhists replied for centuries that the monk repays his parents in a greater way by leading them toward liberation, and they gave new prominence to texts on gratitude to parents. The long negotiation produced the characteristically Chinese settlement in which the two teachings, with Daoism, were said to be three ways to one end. Each had its sphere. Confucius governed the family and the state, and the Buddha was consulted on suffering and death, about which the Master had declined to speak (Dharma and the West, D18).
paras.zh: 他們在「家」這件事上分道揚鑣。對孔子來說，親子之間的連結是一切德行的根；割斷它，就是割斷那條根。佛陀離開了妻子與襁褓中的兒子去尋求覺悟，並且創立了一個由做了同樣事情的男女組成的僧團。佛教傳入中國時，這是對它最先、也最深的反對。出家人剃髮、不留後嗣、不拜父母與君王；照儒家的標準，每一樣都是不孝。中國的佛教徒有好幾個世紀都這樣回答：出家人是以更大的方式報答父母，引導他們走向解脫；他們並且讓談報父母恩的經典有了新的顯著地位。這場漫長的協商，產生了中國特有的那個安排：這兩種教導，加上道教，被說成是通往同一個目的的三條路。各有各的領域。孔子管家與國；而關於苦與死（夫子不肯談的事），人們去請教佛陀（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms.d_en: Humaneness: the full goodness of a person in relation to others.
terms.d_zh: 一個人在與他人的關係中完滿的善。

terms.d_en: Ritual: the inherited forms of respectful conduct, from great ceremonies to everyday courtesy.
terms.d_zh: 傳承下來的、表達敬意的行為形式，從大典到日常的禮貌。

terms.d_en: The gentleman or exemplary person, noble by character and not by birth.
terms.d_zh: 品格上而非出身上高貴的人；典範人物。

terms.d_en: Reciprocity: measuring others by oneself. “What you do not want for yourself, do not do to others.”
terms.d_zh: 推己及人。「己所不欲，勿施於人。」

terms.d_en: Reverent care for one’s parents, which Confucians took to be the root of humaneness.
terms.d_zh: 對父母恭敬的奉養；儒家視之為仁的根本。

terms.d_en: Making realities answer to their titles, so that a ruler acts as a ruler should.
terms.d_zh: 使實際與名分相符，讓君主的作為像一位君主。

quiz.q: How did Confucius describe his own role?
options: As a transmitter and not a maker, one who trusts and loves the ancients.
As the founder of a new religion.
As a prophet sent by Heaven.
As a lawgiver.

quiz.q: Why did he give ritual such importance?
options: He saw it as the means by which feeling is shaped into humane conduct.
He thought the spirits demanded it.
It kept the common people obedient.
It was required by law.

quiz.q: What was Mozi’s objection to the Confucians?
options: Their costly rites waste wealth, and their graded love is a form of partiality.
They ignored the ancients.
They refused to teach the poor.
They relied too much on law and punishment.

further.t: The Analects, Chinese text with James Legge’s translation
further.n_en: Begin with books 4, 7, and 12.
further.n_zh: 從第四、七、十二篇讀起。

further.t: Sima Qian, Records of the Grand Historian, chapter 47, “The Hereditary House of Confucius”
Herbert Fingarette, Confucius: The Secular as Sacred (1972)
further.n_en: Eighty pages that changed how Western philosophers read him.
further.n_zh: 八十頁，改變了西方哲學家讀他的方式。

further.t: Annping Chin, The Authentic Confucius (2007)
further.n_en: A life built carefully from the early sources.
further.n_zh: 一部謹慎地由早期史料建構出來的傳記。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “Confucius”

philosophers.name: Mencius
philosophers.tag_en: The most eloquent of Confucius’s heirs, who told kings to their faces that the people matter more than the ruler, and who rested the whole of morality on a feeling anyone can find in himself.
philosophers.tag_zh: 孔子的繼承者當中最雄辯的一位；他當著國君的面說，人民比君主重要，並且把整個道德，建立在任何人都能在自己身上找到的一種感受上。
facts: Meng Ke 孟軻. “Mencius” is Latin for Mengzi, Master Meng
Studied under followers of Zisi, Confucius’s grandson
Mencius 孟子, seven books, each in two parts

paras.en: Mencius was born about a hundred years after Confucius died, in Zou, a day’s walk from the Master’s home. Sima Qian gives him one paragraph. He studied with the followers of Zisi, the grandson of Confucius, and when he had mastered the Way he went to serve King Xuan of Qi, who could not use him, and then King Hui of Liang, who thought his advice far-fetched and remote from actual affairs. The times explain why. Qin was growing strong under the Legalist reforms of Lord Shang. The other states were hiring generals. Everyone was busy with alliances and conquest, the historian says, and Meng Ke went about expounding the virtue of the ancient sage kings. Wherever he went he did not fit.
paras.zh: 孟子大約在孔子去世一百年後出生，生在鄒，離夫子的家鄉只有一天的路程。司馬遷只給了他一段。他受業於子思（孔子的孫子）的門人；「道既通」，去事奉齊宣王，宣王不能用他；又到了梁國，梁惠王認為他的建議「迂遠而闊於事情」。時代說明了為什麼。秦國靠著商鞅的法家改革日漸強大。其他各國都在延攬將領。這位史家說，天下正忙於合縱連橫、以攻伐為能事，而孟軻卻到處陳述唐、虞、三代之德，「是以所如者不合」。

paras.en: Later tradition filled the silence about his youth with stories of his mother. She is said to have moved house three times, away from a cemetery and then from a market, until she found a home beside a school, because the boy imitated whatever he saw. When he came home early from his lessons she cut through the cloth on her loom, to show him what it is to abandon work half done. The stories were written down some three centuries after his death and cannot be checked. They made her the model of a parent in East Asia, and they fit a philosopher who taught that character is a matter of what one is given to grow in.
paras.zh: 後來的傳統，用他母親的故事填補了關於他少年時代的空白。據說她搬了三次家：先是離開墓地旁，再離開市場旁，直到在學校旁邊找到一個家，因為這個男孩看到什麼就學什麼。他有一次提早從學堂回來，她就把織布機上的布割斷，讓他看看半途而廢是怎麼回事。這些故事是在他死後大約三個世紀才被寫下來的，無從查證。它們使她成為東亞父母的典範；而它們也很適合這樣一位哲學家：他教導，品格取決於一個人被放在什麼樣的環境裡生長。

paras.en: His book opens with an audience. King Hui of Liang greets him: “Venerable sir, you have not counted a thousand miles too far to come. You must have something that will profit my state?” Mencius replies: “Why must Your Majesty speak of profit? There is humaneness and rightness, and that is all.” If the king asks how to profit his state, his ministers will ask how to profit their houses and the people how to profit themselves, and the state will be torn apart. The exchange sets the tone for everything that follows. He lectured rulers as a tutor lectures a slow pupil. He told one that he did not love his people, another that he was leading beasts to devour men.
paras.zh: 他的書以一場晉見開頭。梁惠王迎接他：「叟！不遠千里而來，亦將有以利吾國乎？」孟子回答：「王！何必曰利？亦有仁義而已矣。」如果國君問怎麼利我的國，大夫就會問怎麼利我的家，百姓就會問怎麼利我自己，國家就會被撕裂。這段交談為後面的一切定了調。他訓誡國君，就像家庭教師訓誡一個遲鈍的學生。他告訴一位國君，他並不愛他的人民；告訴另一位，他是在率領野獸吃人。

paras.en: His political claims were the boldest of the age. “The people are the most important. The altars of soil and grain come next. The ruler is the least.” A king asked him whether it was true that the founder of the Zhou had killed his sovereign, the tyrant Zhou of Shang, and whether a subject may do such a thing. Mencius answered that one who outrages humaneness and rightness is a mere fellow. “I have heard of the punishment of the fellow Zhou. I have not heard of the killing of a ruler.” Eighteen centuries later the first Ming emperor, reading such passages, had Mencius’s tablet removed from the Confucian temple and ordered an edition with eighty-five sections cut out.
paras.zh: 他的政治主張是那個時代最大膽的。「民為貴，社稷次之，君為輕。」有位國君問他：周的開國者殺了自己的君主（商的暴君紂），這是真的嗎？臣子可以做這種事嗎？孟子回答：賊仁賊義的人，只是個「一夫」。「聞誅一夫紂矣，未聞弒君也。」十八個世紀之後，明朝的開國皇帝讀到這類段落，下令把孟子的牌位從孔廟撤掉，並且命人編了一個刪去八十五章的本子。

paras.en: He spent some twenty years at the courts, honored and unheeded, and resigned his post in Qi when the king ignored his advice about a war. A disciple told him that outsiders all called him fond of arguing. “How should I be fond of arguing?” he said. “I have no choice.” The teachings of Yang Zhu, who would not pluck out one hair to benefit the world, and of Mozi, who would love all equally, filled the land, and if no one refuted them the way of Confucius would not be seen. He went home to Zou, and with his student Wan Zhang and others set in order the Odes and Documents and composed the seven books that bear his name.
paras.zh: 他在各國的朝廷上度過了大約二十年，受尊敬而不被採納；齊王不理會他對一場戰爭的建議，他就辭去了在齊國的職位。有弟子告訴他，外面的人都說他好辯。他說：「予豈好辯哉？予不得已也。」楊朱（不肯拔一根毛來利天下）與墨翟（主張兼愛）的學說充斥天下；如果沒有人駁斥它們，孔子之道就無法彰顯。他回到了鄒，與學生萬章等人整理《詩》《書》，並且寫成了以他為名的七篇。

paras.en: For a thousand years the book was one Confucian text among many, and Xunzi was at least as much read. Its rise came in the Song dynasty, when Zhu Xi placed it among the Four Books that every candidate for office had to master. From then until 1905 it was memorized by every educated person in China, and Mencius was known as the Second Sage.
paras.zh: 有一千年之久，這本書只是眾多儒家文獻當中的一種；荀子被閱讀的程度至少不亞於他。它的地位上升是在宋代；朱熹把它列入《四書》，成為每一位求取功名的人必須精通的書。從那時起直到 1905 年，中國每一個受過教育的人都背過它，而孟子被稱為「亞聖」。

timeline: At the court of King Hui of Liang
Zhu Xi publishes the Four Books
The Ming founder orders an expurgated Mencius

idea.title_en: The central idea: The heart that cannot bear
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：不忍人之心

paras.en: Confucius had said what a good person does and left open why anyone should be able to do it. Mencius supplied the foundation. Every human being, he held, has a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others. His proof is the child at the well, and from it he draws a list of four beginnings: the feeling of compassion is the sprout of humaneness, the feeling of shame the sprout of rightness, the feeling of deference the sprout of propriety, and the sense of right and wrong the sprout of wisdom. People have these four as they have four limbs. Moral cultivation is the growth of what is already there, and it must be neither neglected nor forced. He tells of a farmer in Song who thought his grain was growing too slowly and went out and pulled up each stalk a little. He came home exhausted and pleased, and his son ran to the field and found the plants withered.
paras.zh: 孔子說了好人做什麼，卻沒有說明為什麼任何人都做得到。孟子補上了地基。他主張，每一個人都有「不忍人之心」。他的證明是井邊的那個孩子；由此他列出了四個開端：惻隱之心是仁之端，羞惡之心是義之端，辭讓之心是禮之端，是非之心是智之端。人有這四端，就像有四肢一樣。道德的修養，是讓本來就在那裡的東西生長；既不可以疏於照料，也不可以強求。他講過宋國一個農夫的故事：那人嫌自己的禾苗長得太慢，就到田裡去把每一株往上拔一點。他疲憊而得意地回到家；他的兒子跑到田裡一看，苗都枯了。

paras.en: From this psychology he derives a politics. A ruler has the same heart as anyone else, and good government is that heart extended: take what you feel for your own old people and children and extend it to the old people and children of others. A government that leaves the people without a steady livelihood and then punishes them for crime is setting a trap for them. And a state so governed would be irresistible, because people everywhere would wish to live in it. He also describes what the cultivated person gains. By long accumulation of right action one develops a “flood-like energy,” vast and unyielding, that fills the space between heaven and earth. Such a person cannot be corrupted by wealth, moved by poverty, or bent by force. And he will know what to choose when the choice is hard: “Fish is what I want, and bear’s paw is also what I want. If I cannot have both, I give up the fish and take the bear’s paw. Life is what I want, and rightness is also what I want. If I cannot have both, I give up life and take rightness.”
paras.zh: 從這套心理學，他引出了一套政治學。君主的心跟任何人的心一樣；而仁政就是把這顆心推出去：「老吾老，以及人之老；幼吾幼，以及人之幼。」一個讓人民沒有穩定生計、然後再因犯罪而懲罰他們的政府，是在給他們設陷阱。而一個這樣治理的國家會無敵於天下，因為各地的人都會想住到那裡去。他也描述了修養有成的人得到什麼。靠著長久積累合於義的行為，人會養成「浩然之氣」，至大至剛，充塞於天地之間。這樣的人，富貴不能使他墮落，貧賤不能使他動搖，威武不能使他屈服。而當抉擇很難的時候，他知道該選什麼：「魚，我所欲也；熊掌，亦我所欲也。二者不可得兼，舍魚而取熊掌者也。生，亦我所欲也；義，亦我所欲也。二者不可得兼，舍生而取義者也。」

quote.en: Life is what I want, and rightness is also what I want. If I cannot have both, I give up life and take rightness.
quote.zh: 生，亦我所欲也；義，亦我所欲也。二者不可得兼，舍生而取義者也。
quote.ref: Mencius 6A10, translated for this series
quote.note_en: The source of the phrase 舍生取義, which has been quoted by Chinese patriots and martyrs ever since.
quote.note_zh: 「舍生取義」一語的出處；此後一直被中國的志士與殉道者引用。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Xunzi’s reply
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：荀子的回答

paras.en: The sharpest critic was a fellow Confucian. Xunzi, who was born about the time Mencius died, wrote that Mencius did not understand the difference between nature and deliberate effort. What is inborn needs no learning: the eye sees and the ear hears without being taught. Courtesy and rightness have to be learned by everyone, with labor, from teachers. So they are not inborn. If people were good by nature, he adds, there would have been no need for sage kings or ritual, and the fact that every society has laws and punishments shows what its members would do without them. The passing pang at the well proves little. A feeling that leads nowhere unless it is trained is hardly the root of morality. The training is.
paras.zh: 最犀利的批評者是一位儒家同道。荀子大約在孟子去世前後出生；他寫道，孟子不懂「性」與「偽」的分別。天生的東西不必學：眼睛會看、耳朵會聽，都不用教。禮義卻是每個人都得費力向老師學的。所以它們不是天生的。他又說：如果人本性是善的，就不需要聖王與禮義了；而每一個社會都有法與刑，這個事實就顯示了，沒有它們的時候成員們會做什麼。井邊那一閃而過的不忍，證明不了多少。一個若不經訓練就哪裡也到不了的感受，很難算是道德的根。訓練才是。

paras.en: A second objection concerns his politics. He promised the kings that humane government would make them invincible, and the state that actually united China a few decades after his death was Qin, the harshest of them. His defenders say that the Qin empire lasted fifteen years and the dynasties built on Confucian principles lasted centuries. A third objection is about method. He argues by analogy, with water, sprouts, and mountains, and an analogy can always be met with another. Gaozi’s images were as good as his. He won the debates in his own book, which he wrote.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁針對他的政治學。他向國君們保證，仁政會使他們無敵；而在他死後幾十年真正統一中國的，是其中最嚴酷的秦。為他辯護的人說：秦帝國只維持了十五年；建立在儒家原則上的各個王朝，則延續了好幾個世紀。第三個反駁關乎方法。他靠類比來論證：水、嫩芽、山；而一個類比，永遠可以用另一個類比來回應。告子的意象並不比他的差。他在自己的書裡贏了那些辯論，而那本書是他寫的。

problem.title_zh: 一本只有一個聲音的書

paras.en: Unlike the Analects, the Mencius reads as the work of one mind. Its passages are long, its arguments are developed, and the same images recur. Sima Qian says that Mencius composed it himself with his students after retiring, and most scholars accept that it was at least put together under his eye or soon after his death. That makes it a better witness to its author’s thought than we have for almost any other early Chinese thinker. It also means that we hear his opponents only as he reports them. Gaozi, Yang Zhu, and the followers of Mozi are given a few sentences each and are then refuted, and of Gaozi nothing survives anywhere else. For his life there is little beyond the book: the paragraph in the Records and the stories of his mother, which first appear in the Han dynasty.
paras.zh: 跟《論語》不同，《孟子》讀起來像是出自一個人的心思。它的段落長，論證有所展開，同樣的意象一再出現。司馬遷說，孟子退隱之後與學生一起親自撰作了它；多數學者接受它至少是在他眼前、或他死後不久編成的。這使它比我們為幾乎任何其他早期中國思想家所擁有的文獻，都更能見證作者的思想。這也意味著：他的對手，我們只聽得到他轉述的版本。告子、楊朱與墨者，各自只得到幾句話，然後就被駁倒了；而關於告子，別處什麼也沒有留下。至於他的生平，除了這本書之外所知甚少：《史記》裡的那一段，以及他母親的故事，而後者最早見於漢代。

said.claim: “The great man is one who does not lose the heart of a newborn child.” (Mencius)
said.claim_zh: 「大人者，不失其赤子之心者也。」（孟子）
said.en: The sentence is Mencius 4B12, and it is quoted today in praise of people who stay playful and innocent. Mencius did not admire childishness. The “heart of a newborn” is the unspoiled moral responsiveness he believed everyone starts with, the heart that cannot bear to see suffering. The great man is the one who has kept that sprout alive through a lifetime of dealings with the world and has grown it into something a child could never have. The line just before it in his book says that the great man’s words need not be kept to the letter, since he goes where rightness is.
said.zh: 這句話是《孟子・離婁下》第十二章；今天它被引來稱讚那些保持童心與天真的人。孟子並不欣賞孩子氣。「赤子之心」是他相信每個人起初都有的、未受污損的道德感應力，也就是那顆不忍看見苦難的心。「大人」，是在一輩子與世界打交道的過程中讓那株嫩芽活了下來、並且把它養成了孩子絕不可能擁有的東西的那個人。在他的書裡，緊接在這句話前面的那一句說：「大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。」

paras.en: When the teaching that all beings have Buddha-nature reached China in the fifth century, Chinese readers had been prepared for it by Mencius for seven hundred years. They already believed that the capacity for sagehood is present in everyone, that it is covered over and not destroyed by bad conditions, and that cultivation uncovers what was there. The Chan saying that one should see one’s nature and become a Buddha is in a Mencian key, and so is the Sixth Patriarch’s exclamation that our own nature is “originally pure.” Some historians think that Buddha-nature thought flourished in China, and remained marginal in India, largely for this reason. The debt was repaid. The Neo-Confucians who made Mencius canonical in the Song had learned from Buddhists to speak of the mind’s original nature.
paras.zh: 「一切眾生皆有佛性」的教導在五世紀傳到中國的時候，中國的讀者已經被孟子預備了七百年。他們早已相信：成聖的能力人人都有；它是被惡劣的條件遮蓋，而不是被毀掉；修養所做的，是讓本來就在的東西顯露出來。禪宗「見性成佛」的說法，是孟子的調子；六祖驚嘆「何期自性，本自清淨」，也是。有些史家認為，佛性思想之所以在中國興盛、在印度卻始終處於邊緣，主要就是這個原因。這筆債後來還了回去。宋代把孟子奉為經典的理學家，是從佛教徒那裡學會談「心之本體」的。

paras.en: The two differ in what the inborn endowment is. For Mencius it is a set of moral feelings, and their natural growth is into the virtues of family and state. For the Buddhist it is the mind’s capacity to awaken, which is found in animals as well as people, and its fulfillment lies beyond every social role. Mencius’s extension of love moves outward by degrees, from one’s own parents to other people’s, and he attacked Mozi for loving all alike. The bodhisattva’s compassion makes no such distinction. And Mencius never doubts that there is a self to cultivate. He would have been puzzled to hear that the heart which cannot bear suffering has no owner (Dharma and the West, D25).
paras.zh: 兩者的差別，在於那份天生的稟賦是什麼。對孟子來說，它是一組道德情感；它們自然的生長方向，是家與國的種種德行。對佛教徒來說，它是心的覺悟能力，在動物身上跟在人身上一樣找得到；而它的圓成，在一切社會角色之外。孟子的「推恩」是一層一層往外推的，從自己的父母到別人的父母；他並且攻擊墨子的兼愛。菩薩的悲心不作這樣的分別。還有，孟子從來不懷疑有一個「我」可以修養。如果聽到有人說那顆不忍人之心並沒有主人，他會感到困惑（佛法與西方哲學 D25）。

terms.d_en: Compassion, shame, deference, and the sense of right and wrong, the inborn beginnings of the four virtues.

terms.d_zh: 把君主天然的不忍之心推及人民的統治，從他們的生計開始。

terms.d_en: The moral vigor built up by long practice of rightness.
terms.d_zh: 長久行義所積養出來的道德氣魄。

terms.d_en: Carrying a feeling one has for those near to those farther off.
terms.d_zh: 把對親近者的感受，推及較遠的人。

terms.d_en: What is fitting to do. Mencius pairs it with humaneness and contrasts both with profit.
terms.d_zh: 所當為的事。孟子把它與仁並舉，並且拿兩者與「利」對比。

terms.d_en: The right to rule, which Heaven confers and withdraws through the acceptance of the people.
terms.d_zh: 統治的資格；天透過人民的接受來授予與收回。
