philosophers.name: Epicurus
philosophers.tag_en: A schoolmaster’s son who taught in a garden that pleasure is the goal of life, lived on bread and water, and admitted women and slaves to philosophy.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個教書匠的兒子；他在一座花園裡教導「快樂是人生的目的」，自己靠麵包與水過活，並且讓女性與奴隸也來學哲學。
facts: 341 BCE, on the island of Samos, to Athenian parents
The Garden, founded in Athens about 306 BCE
Some three hundred scrolls, almost all lost
Three letters and forty Principal Doctrines, preserved by Diogenes Laertius; fragments from Herculaneum

paras.en: Epicurus was born in 341 BCE on Samos, an island off the coast of Asia Minor where his father, an Athenian settler, kept a school. The year he turned eighteen he went to Athens for his military service, and while he was there Alexander the Great died, the Athenian settlers were expelled from Samos, and his family became refugees on the mainland. He rejoined them and spent some fifteen years in the cities of the eastern Aegean, studying with followers of Plato and of the atomist Democritus, quarreling with most of his teachers, and gathering a circle of his own. He liked to say that he had taught himself.
paras.zh: 伊比鳩魯西元前 341 年生於薩摩斯，小亞細亞外海的一座島；他的父親是雅典來的殖民者，在那裡開了一所學校。十八歲那年，他到雅典服兵役；就在那期間，亞歷山大大帝去世，雅典的殖民者被逐出薩摩斯，他的家人成了大陸上的難民。他回去與他們會合，在愛琴海東岸的幾座城市裡度過了大約十五年：跟柏拉圖的追隨者與原子論者德謨克利特的追隨者學習，跟他大多數的老師吵架，並且聚集了自己的一個圈子。他喜歡說自己是自學的。

paras.en: The world he grew up in explains much of his teaching. The independent city, in which Plato and Aristotle had assumed a good life must be lived, was finished. Power lay with kings and their armies, and a private person could do little to affect it. Epicurus drew the conclusion that happiness must be made independent of public events. His advice was to “live unnoticed.”
paras.zh: 他成長的那個世界，說明了他的教導的許多地方。柏拉圖與亞里斯多德都預設美好人生必須在獨立的城邦裡過；而獨立的城邦已經結束了。權力在國王與他們的軍隊手上；一個私人，幾乎無法影響它。伊比鳩魯得出的結論是：幸福必須不依賴公共事件。他的建議是「隱居而活」。

paras.en: About 306 he came to Athens for good and bought a house with a garden outside the city wall, on the road to Plato’s Academy. The school that met there was unlike its rivals. It was a household. Its members lived together or near one another and held their goods as friends, and they included women and at least one slave, which scandalized the city. An inscription over the gate is said to have told the visitor that here pleasure was the highest good, and that the keeper would offer him barley cakes and fresh water. Epicurus wrote to a friend asking for a small pot of cheese, so that he might feast when he wished.
paras.zh: 大約在西元前 306 年，他定居雅典，在城牆外通往柏拉圖學園的路上，買下了一棟附花園的房子。在那裡聚會的學派，跟它的對手都不一樣。它是一個家。成員們住在一起，或住在彼此附近，以朋友的方式共享財物；其中有女性，也至少有一名奴隸，這讓全城譁然。據說大門上的銘文告訴來訪者：在這裡，快樂是最高的善；而看門的人會請他吃大麥餅、喝清水。伊比鳩魯寫信給一位朋友，要一小罐乳酪，好讓他想吃大餐的時候能吃上一頓。

paras.en: He taught there for thirty-five years and wrote more than any philosopher before him. The members memorized short summaries of the doctrine and were encouraged to act as though the Master were watching. Friendship was the center of the life. “Nothing enhances our security so much as friendship,” he wrote, and the school held a common meal on the twentieth of each month which his followers kept up for centuries after his death.
paras.zh: 他在那裡教了三十五年，寫的東西比他之前任何一位哲學家都多。成員們背誦教義的簡短摘要，並且被鼓勵要像老師正在看著那樣去行事。友誼是這種生活的中心。他寫道：「沒有任何東西比友誼更能增進我們的安全」；這個學派每個月二十日舉行一次共餐，他的追隨者在他死後還維持了好幾個世紀。

paras.en: He died in 270, at seventy-one, of a blockage of the bladder that had tormented him for two weeks. The letter he dictated on the last day survives. He calls it a blessed day, the last of his life. The pain in his bladder and bowels could not be worse, he says, and he sets against it the gladness of mind that comes from remembering his past conversations with his friend. He asks that the children of a dead disciple be looked after. Then, according to the story, he got into a warm bath, asked for a cup of unmixed wine, told his friends to remember his teachings, and died.
paras.zh: 西元前 270 年，他去世了，七十一歲；死因是膀胱阻塞，那折磨了他兩個星期。他在最後一天口授的那封信流傳了下來。他稱那一天是蒙福的一天，是他生命的最後一天。他說，膀胱與腸子的疼痛已經到了無以復加的地步；而他拿來與之對抗的，是回想起從前與朋友的種種談話時心裡的那份歡喜。他請人照顧一位已故弟子的孩子們。然後，照故事的說法，他泡進溫水澡盆，要了一杯沒有摻水的酒，囑咐朋友們記住他的教導，就去世了。

paras.en: His school lasted about six hundred years and spread across the Roman world. Its finest monument is a poem. Around 55 BCE the Roman Lucretius set the whole system into Latin verse in On the Nature of Things, and the single manuscript of it that survived the Middle Ages, found in a German monastery in 1417, helped to bring atomism back into European science.
paras.zh: 他的學派延續了大約六百年，傳遍了羅馬世界。它最精美的紀念碑是一首詩。大約在西元前 55 年，羅馬人盧克萊修把整個體系寫成了拉丁文的詩篇《物性論》；它熬過中世紀而倖存的唯一一份抄本，1417 年在德意志的一座修道院裡被發現，後來幫助了原子論重新回到歐洲的科學裡。

Lucretius, On the Nature of Things

盧克萊修的詩重新被發現

idea.title_en: The central idea: Enough
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：足夠

paras.en: Epicurus held that pleasure is the only thing good in itself and pain the only thing bad. From that starting point one expects a philosophy of indulgence, and he arrives at something close to the opposite. The reason lies in his analysis of pleasure. The greatest pleasure, he argues, is the state of having no pain in the body and no disturbance in the mind. Once hunger is satisfied, eating more adds variety and no increase. So the question for anyone who wants a pleasant life is how to be free of pain and fear at the least cost, and the answer is to want little. Natural and necessary desires, for food, shelter, safety, and friends, are easy to satisfy. Desires for luxury are natural and optional. Desires for wealth, fame, and power are empty. They come from false beliefs, they have no limit, and whoever acquires them has acquired a master.
paras.zh: 伊比鳩魯主張：快樂是唯一本身就是善的東西，痛苦是唯一本身就是惡的東西。從這個起點，人們預期的是一套縱欲的哲學；而他抵達的，卻是接近相反的東西。原因在於他對快樂的分析。他論證：最大的快樂，就是身體沒有痛苦、心靈沒有擾動的狀態。飢餓一旦解除，吃得更多只是增添了花樣，並沒有增加什麼。所以，對任何想要愉快生活的人來說，問題是：怎樣以最小的代價免於痛苦與恐懼？而答案是：少要一點。自然而必要的欲望（對食物、遮蔽、安全與朋友），是容易滿足的。對奢華的欲望，是自然而可有可無的。對財富、名聲與權力的欲望，是空的。它們來自錯誤的信念，沒有限度；而誰得到了它們，誰就得到了一位主人。

paras.en: Two fears, he thought, poison most lives: fear of the gods and fear of death. His physics was designed to remove both. The universe consists of atoms moving in empty space. The gods, if they exist, are perfectly happy beings who take no interest in us, so there is no one to placate. And the soul is a body made of fine atoms that scatter when we die. “Death, therefore, the most awful of evils, is nothing to us, seeing that, when we are, death is not come, and, when death is come, we are not.” There will be no one to suffer it. His followers compressed the teaching into four lines, called the fourfold remedy: God is not to be feared, death is not to be felt, what is good is easy to get, and what is terrible is easy to endure.
paras.zh: 他認為，有兩種恐懼毒害了大多數的人生：對神的恐懼，以及對死亡的恐懼。他的物理學，就是設計來去除這兩者的。宇宙是由在虛空中運動的原子構成的。諸神如果存在，是完全幸福的存在者，對我們毫無興趣；所以並沒有誰需要我們去討好。而靈魂是由精細的原子構成的一個物體，我們死的時候它們就散開了。「所以，死亡，這個最可怕的惡，對我們來說什麼也不是；因為我們在的時候，死亡還沒有來；死亡來了的時候，我們已經不在了。」那時候不會有任何人來承受它。他的追隨者把這個教導濃縮成四句，稱為「四重藥方」：神不足懼，死不足憂，善容易得，苦容易忍。

quote.en: By pleasure we mean the absence of pain in the body and of trouble in the soul.
quote.zh: 我們所說的快樂，是身體沒有痛苦、靈魂沒有擾動。
quote.ref: Epicurus, Letter to Menoeceus, tr. R. D. Hicks
quote.note_en: The sentence that separates Epicurus from everything his name has come to mean.
quote.note_zh: 這句話，把伊比鳩魯與他的名字後來所代表的一切區分開來。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Is the absence of pain a pleasure?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：沒有痛苦算是一種快樂嗎？

paras.en: The ancient critics, Cicero above all, attacked the definition. There is pleasure, there is pain, and there is a neutral state in between, they said. Epicurus has taken the neutral state and called it the highest pleasure. If that is what he means by the word, he is no hedonist, and his philosophy is a kind of asceticism under a misleading label. If he means pleasure in the ordinary sense, he has no right to tell us that bread and water give as much of it as a banquet. His defenders reply that the calm of a mind with nothing to fear is a positive condition and is felt as one, as anyone knows who has recovered from an illness. The experience machine sharpens the objection. If tranquility is all that matters, a tranquil life in a tank is as good as any, and Epicurus, who prized real friends, would not have accepted that.
paras.zh: 古代的批評者（尤其是西塞羅）攻擊的是那個定義。他們說：有快樂，有痛苦，中間還有一個中性的狀態。伊比鳩魯拿了那個中性的狀態，把它稱為最高的快樂。如果這就是他用這個詞的意思，他就不是享樂論者；他的哲學是貼著誤導性標籤的一種苦行。如果他指的是通常意義上的快樂，他就沒有資格告訴我們：麵包與水給的快樂，跟一場盛宴一樣多。為他辯護的人回答：一顆無所畏懼的心的平靜，是一種正面的狀態，而且感覺起來就是如此；任何從一場病裡康復過來的人都知道。體驗機把這個反駁磨得更利。如果寧靜就是唯一要緊的，那麼在水槽裡的寧靜人生就跟任何人生一樣好；而珍視真實朋友的伊比鳩魯，是不會接受這一點的。

paras.en: A second objection concerns what he leaves out. A person who lives unnoticed, avoids politics, and does not marry may be tranquil, and the Stoics asked what becomes of a city full of such people. Someone has to keep the walls. His account of justice as an agreement neither to harm nor be harmed gives a reason to be just only so long as one might be caught. And his argument about death, admired as it is, seems to prove too much. If death is nothing to the one who dies, it is hard to say why killing is the worst of crimes.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁，關乎他遺漏了什麼。一個隱居而活、避開政治、不結婚的人，也許是寧靜的；而斯多噶學派問：一座住滿了這種人的城邦，會變成什麼樣子？總得有人守城牆。他把正義說成「互不傷害的約定」；這只在一個人有可能被抓的時候，才給出了行正義的理由。至於他關於死亡的論證，儘管備受推崇，卻似乎證明得太多了。如果死亡對死去的人來說什麼也不是，就很難說明為什麼殺人是最重的罪。

paras.en: Almost nothing Epicurus wrote has come down to us directly. His major work, On Nature, ran to thirty-seven books. What we have complete are three letters summarizing his physics, astronomy, and ethics, and a list of forty sayings, all copied into the tenth book of Diogenes Laertius’s Lives of the Philosophers about five hundred years after his death. Everything else is quotation, much of it by enemies. The Stoics and later the Christians had reason to make him look like a glutton and an atheist, and the picture stuck: in Hebrew a word derived from his name came to mean a heretic, and Dante put him in the sixth circle of hell among those who say that the soul dies with the body.
paras.zh: 伊比鳩魯寫的東西，幾乎沒有一樣直接傳到我們手上。他的主要著作《論自然》有三十七卷之多。我們擁有的完整文本，是概述他的物理學、天文學與倫理學的三封信，以及一份四十條格言的清單；這些全都是在他死後大約五百年，被抄進第歐根尼・拉爾修《哲人言行錄》的第十卷的。其餘的全是別人的引述，其中許多出自敵人。斯多噶學派與後來的基督徒，都有理由把他描繪成饕客與無神論者；而這個形象就這樣固定下來：在希伯來文裡，一個從他的名字衍生出來的詞，意思變成了「異端」；但丁則把他放在地獄的第六圈，跟那些說靈魂隨身體而死的人在一起。

paras.en: New evidence has come from an unexpected place. A villa at Herculaneum, buried by Vesuvius in 79 CE, contained the library of an Epicurean philosopher. Its scrolls were carbonized into black lumps, and scholars have been unrolling and reading them since the eighteenth century, in recent years with X-ray imaging. They include parts of On Nature.
paras.zh: 新的證據來自一個意想不到的地方。赫庫蘭尼姆的一座別墅，在西元 79 年被維蘇威火山掩埋；裡面有一位伊比鳩魯學派哲學家的藏書。那些卷軸碳化成了黑色的硬塊；從十八世紀以來，學者們一直在把它們展開、解讀，近年來用上了 X 光造影。其中就有《論自然》的一部分。

said.claim: “Is God willing to prevent evil, but not able? Then he is not omnipotent. Is he able, but not willing? Then he is malevolent.” (Epicurus)
said.claim_zh: 「上帝願意阻止惡，卻做不到嗎？那他就不是全能的。他做得到，卻不願意嗎？那他就是懷著惡意的。」（伊比鳩魯）
said.verdict_en: Attributed to him six centuries later
said.verdict_zh: 六個世紀之後才歸到他名下
said.en: The argument is known as the Epicurean paradox and is not found in any surviving text by Epicurus. Our source is the Christian writer Lactantius, around 300 CE, who quotes it as an argument of Epicurus in order to answer it. The wording familiar today is David Hume’s, from his Dialogues of 1779. Epicurus may well have used some such argument, though not against the existence of gods. He believed in gods and denied only that they concern themselves with us, and the problem of evil would have served him as evidence for that.
said.zh: 這個論證被稱為「伊比鳩魯悖論」，卻不見於伊比鳩魯現存的任何文本。我們的出處是基督教作家拉克坦提烏斯；大約在西元 300 年，他為了反駁它，把它當作伊比鳩魯的論證引了出來。今天人們熟悉的措辭是休謨的，出自他 1779 年的《自然宗教對話錄》。伊比鳩魯很可能用過這一類的論證，只不過不是用來反對神的存在。他相信有神，否認的只是神會過問我們的事；而惡的問題，對他來說正好可以當作這一點的證據。

paras.en: No Greek philosopher sounds more like the Buddha. Both begin from suffering and treat philosophy as medicine. Both locate the trouble in desire and distinguish what we need from what we merely crave. Both founded communities outside the city where friends lived simply together, and both admitted people whom the society around them excluded. Both refused to make the gods the basis of the good life. Ataraxia, the unshaken calm that Epicurus sets as the goal, is the nearest Greek word to the peace of nibbāna, and his sorting of desires into those with a limit and those without would serve as a commentary on the second noble truth.
paras.zh: 沒有哪一位希臘哲學家，聽起來比他更像佛陀。兩人都從苦出發，都把哲學當作藥。兩人都把問題放在欲望上，並且區分了我們「需要」的與我們只是「渴求」的。兩人都在城外創立了團體，朋友們在那裡簡樸地共同生活；兩人也都接納了周圍的社會所排斥的人。兩人都拒絕以諸神作為美好人生的基礎。伊比鳩魯立為目標的 ataraxia（不被動搖的平靜），是最接近涅槃之寂靜的希臘字；而他把欲望分成有限度的與沒有限度的，可以當作第二聖諦的註解。

paras.en: They differ at the root. Epicurus holds that a person is a temporary arrangement of atoms and that death is the end, and he offers this as the cure for the fear of death. The Buddha lists that very view, annihilationism, among the errors, and teaches that the process continues until craving is ended. For Epicurus the goal is the most pleasant life available between birth and death. For the Buddha even the calmest pleasant feeling is impermanent and is not the goal. And the remedies differ in depth. Epicurus removes disturbing beliefs by argument and arranges a life in which few desires are aroused. The Buddha agrees that wrong views must go, and holds that craving has roots that argument does not reach, which is why his path includes a training of attention that has no counterpart in the Garden (Dharma and the West, D6 and D22).
paras.zh: 他們在根本處不同。伊比鳩魯主張：人是原子暫時的排列，死亡就是終點；而他把這一點當作治療死亡恐懼的藥。佛陀把這個看法本身（斷見）列在種種錯誤當中，並且教導：這個過程會繼續下去，直到渴愛止息。對伊比鳩魯來說，目標是出生與死亡之間所能擁有的最愉快的人生。對佛陀來說，即使最平靜的樂受也是無常的，並不是目標。而兩人的對治，深度也不同。伊比鳩魯用論證去除擾人的信念，並且安排一種很少激起欲望的生活。佛陀同意錯誤的見解必須去除，卻主張渴愛有論證搆不到的根；這就是為什麼他的道包含了一種對注意力的訓練，而那在花園裡是沒有對應物的（佛法與西方哲學 D6、D22）。

terms.d_en: Freedom from mental disturbance.
terms.d_zh: 心靈不受擾動。

terms.d_en: Freedom from bodily pain.
terms.d_zh: 身體沒有痛苦。

terms.d_en: The theory that everything consists of indivisible particles moving in empty space.
terms.d_zh: 主張一切都由在虛空中運動的不可分割的微粒構成。

terms.d_en: A tiny uncaused deviation in the motion of atoms, which Epicurus introduced to make room for free action.
terms.d_zh: 原子運動中微小而無原因的偏離；伊比鳩魯引進它，為自由的行動留出空間。

terms.d_en: God is not to be feared, death is not to be felt, the good is easy to get, the terrible is easy to endure.
terms.d_zh: 神不足懼，死不足憂，善容易得，苦容易忍。

terms.d_en: In philosophy, a follower of Epicurus. In ordinary English, a lover of fine food and drink, by a misunderstanding.
terms.d_zh: 在哲學上，指伊比鳩魯的追隨者。在日常英文裡，由於一個誤解，指講究美食美酒的人。

quiz.q: What did Epicurus mean by the highest pleasure?
options: The absence of bodily pain and mental disturbance.
The greatest possible quantity of sensual enjoyment.
Fame after death.
The approval of the gods.

quiz.q: Why did he teach physics?
options: To remove the fear of the gods and of death.
To build machines.
To prove that pleasure is bad.
To predict eclipses for the city.

quiz.q: What was Cicero’s objection?
options: The absence of pain is a neutral state, and calling it the highest pleasure is a trick with words.
Epicurus ate too much.
Atoms do not exist.
Friendship is unimportant.

philosophers.name: Epictetus
philosophers.place_zh: 希拉波利斯、羅馬與尼科波利斯
philosophers.tag_en: Born a slave and lame, he taught that no one can be enslaved who has understood what is his own, and counted an emperor among his readers.
philosophers.tag_zh: 生為奴隸，又是跛子；他教導：凡是明白了什麼才是自己的東西的人，誰也奴役不了他。他的讀者當中有一位皇帝。
facts: c. 50 CE, Hierapolis in Phrygia (now Pamukkale, Turkey), into slavery
Epiktētos means “acquired.” His birth name is unknown
He wrote nothing. Discourses (four of eight books survive) and the Handbook, both recorded by Arrian
Greek, in the plain speech of the street

life.h_zh: 尼祿的羅馬城裡的奴隸

paras.en: Epictetus was born around the year 50 in Hierapolis, a town in the highlands of what is now western Turkey. His mother was a slave, and so he was one. As a boy he was taken to Rome and became the property of Epaphroditus, who had himself been a slave and had risen to be secretary to the emperor Nero. It was a household at the center of power, and Epictetus watched at close range what men would do for the emperor’s favor and how quickly it could be lost. His later lectures are full of it: the senator who kisses the hands of a rich freedman, the man who cannot sleep for wondering whether he will be invited to dinner.
paras.zh: 愛比克泰德大約在西元 50 年生於希拉波利斯，位於今天土耳其西部高地的一座城鎮。他的母親是奴隸，所以他也是。他年少時被帶到羅馬，成了以巴弗提的財產；以巴弗提自己也曾經是奴隸，後來一路爬到了皇帝尼祿的祕書。那是一個位於權力中心的家；愛比克泰德在近距離看著人們為了皇帝的寵信肯做些什麼，也看著它可以多麼快就失去。他後來的講課裡滿是這些：親吻一個有錢的獲釋奴隸的手的元老；因為不知道自己會不會被邀去赴宴而睡不著的人。

paras.en: He was lame. One ancient account says that the leg was broken by his master, who was twisting it as a punishment. Epictetus is supposed to have said calmly, “You will break it,” and when it broke, “Did I not tell you so?” Another source says that he was lame from rheumatism, and the story may have been invented to fit the philosophy. While still a slave he was allowed to attend the lectures of Musonius Rufus, the leading Stoic of the day, who taught that women should study philosophy as men do and that a master has no right to do as he likes with a slave.
paras.zh: 他是跛的。有一則古代的記載說，他的腿是被主人弄斷的；主人為了懲罰他，正在扭他的腿。據說愛比克泰德平靜地說：「你會把它弄斷的。」腿斷了的時候，他說：「我不是告訴過你了嗎？」另一個來源說他是因為風濕而跛的；那個故事也許是為了配合這套哲學而編出來的。還是奴隸的時候，他就獲准去聽穆索尼烏斯・魯弗斯的課；那是當時首屈一指的斯多噶學者，他教導女性應該像男性一樣研習哲學，並且說主人沒有權利對奴隸為所欲為。

paras.en: At some point he was freed, and he began to teach in Rome. Around the year 93 the emperor Domitian, who distrusted philosophers as a source of opposition, expelled them all from Italy. Epictetus crossed the Adriatic and settled at Nicopolis, a port on the western coast of Greece where ships between Rome and the East put in. He opened a school and taught there for some forty years. Young men from the best Roman families came to hear him, and tradition says that the emperor Hadrian visited.
paras.zh: 他在某個時候獲得了自由，並且開始在羅馬教學。大約在西元 93 年，皇帝圖密善（他不信任哲學家，把他們看成反對勢力的來源）把他們全部逐出了義大利。愛比克泰德渡過亞得里亞海，在尼科波利斯定居下來；那是希臘西岸的一個港口，往來於羅馬與東方之間的船隻在那裡靠岸。他辦了一所學校，在那裡教了大約四十年。最好的羅馬家族的年輕人前來聽他講課；傳說皇帝哈德良也來拜訪過。

paras.en: He lived with great simplicity. His house is said to have contained a straw mat, a pallet, and an earthenware lamp, which he used after an iron one was stolen. He remarked that the thief had paid a high price for the lamp, since to get it he had become a thief. He did not marry. Late in life he took in a child whose parents were about to abandon it, and brought a woman into the house to help him raise it.
paras.zh: 他過著極為簡樸的生活。據說他家裡只有一張草蓆、一張鋪蓋，以及一盞陶燈；那是在一盞鐵燈被偷走之後才改用的。他說，那個小偷為那盞燈付了很高的代價，因為為了得到它，他把自己變成了一個賊。他沒有結婚。晚年他收養了一個父母正打算遺棄的孩子，並且請了一位婦人到家裡來幫他把孩子養大。

paras.en: Like Socrates, whom he took as his model, Epictetus wrote nothing. That we can read him is due to one student. Arrian of Nicomedia, who later governed a Roman province and wrote the best surviving history of Alexander, attended the school as a young man around 108 and took down what he heard, he says, word for word as far as he could, to preserve for himself a memorial of the teacher’s thought and frankness of speech. The notes were copied and circulated without his consent, and he then published them as the Discourses, in eight books of which four survive. From these he drew the short Handbook.
paras.zh: 跟他奉為典範的蘇格拉底一樣，愛比克泰德什麼也沒寫。我們今天讀得到他，要歸功於一位學生。尼科米底亞的阿里安（他後來治理過羅馬的一個行省，並且寫了現存最好的亞歷山大史），大約在西元 108 年，年輕的他到這所學校聽課，並且把聽到的記了下來；他說，他盡可能逐字記錄，為的是替自己保存一份對老師的思想與直言的紀念。這些筆記未經他同意就被傳抄、流通；於是他把它們出版為《語錄》，共八卷，現存四卷。他又從中摘編出那本簡短的《手冊》。

paras.en: The Handbook had a long afterlife. Marcus Aurelius thanks a teacher for lending him a copy of Epictetus. Christian monks adapted it as a rule of life, replacing the name of Socrates with that of Paul. It was translated into Chinese by the Jesuit Matteo Ricci in 1605, as The Book of Twenty-Five Sayings, to show Confucian scholars that Western ethics was respectable. And in 1965 a copy went into a prison camp in Hanoi in the memory of an American pilot.
paras.zh: 《手冊》身後的生命很長。馬可・奧理略感謝一位老師借給他一本愛比克泰德。基督教的修士把它改編成生活的規條，把蘇格拉底的名字換成了保羅。1605 年，耶穌會士利瑪竇把它譯成了中文，題為《二十五言》，要讓儒家的士人看到西方的倫理是體面的。而在 1965 年，有一本存在一位美國飛行員的記憶裡，進了河內的一座戰俘營。

timeline: In Rome, in the household of Nero’s secretary
在羅馬，尼祿祕書的家中
馬可・奧理略寫《沉思錄》
利瑪竇的中文譯本《二十五言》

idea.title_en: The central idea: The one thing that is yours
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：唯一屬於你的東西

paras.en: Epictetus asks his students to make an inventory. What do you have that cannot be taken from you? Your property can be confiscated and your body chained. Your reputation is made by other people’s talk. Your family can die. One thing is left, which he calls prohairesis, a word best translated as moral choice or the faculty of choice: the power to judge the impressions that come to you, to accept or refuse them, and to want or not want accordingly. Not even Zeus, he says, can overcome it. A tyrant can say, “I will put you in chains,” and the answer is, “You will chain my leg. My choice not even you can chain.”
paras.zh: 愛比克泰德要他的學生做一份清點。你擁有的東西裡，有什麼是無法從你身上被拿走的？你的財產可以被沒收，你的身體可以被鎖住。你的名聲是別人的談論造成的。你的家人會死。只剩下一樣東西，他稱之為 prohairesis；這個詞最好的譯法是「道德抉擇」或「抉擇的能力」：也就是判斷那些來到你面前的印象、接受或拒絕它們，並且據此想要或不想要的那個能力。他說，連宙斯也勝不過它。一個暴君可以說：「我要給你上鎖鏈。」而回答是：「你鎖得住的是我的腿。我的抉擇，連你也鎖不住。」

paras.en: From this follows his redefinition of freedom and slavery. A free man, as Rome understood the word, was one whom no one could command. Epictetus says that such a man does not exist, since everyone who wants anything outside his own choice has handed power to whoever can give or withhold it. The senator who needs the emperor’s smile is a slave with a purple border on his toga. The only free person is the one who wants nothing that another can control. The same analysis gives him his account of duty. Each of us has been given roles, as a child, a brother, a citizen, an old man, and the task is to play the role one has well. He does not ask whether the roles are fairly distributed. He asks what a good son would do now.
paras.zh: 由此推出了他對自由與奴役的重新界定。照羅馬對這個詞的理解，自由人是沒有任何人可以命令的人。愛比克泰德說，這樣的人並不存在；因為任何一個想要「自己的抉擇之外的東西」的人，都已經把權力交給了那個能給或不給的人。需要皇帝一笑的元老，是一個袍子上鑲著紫邊的奴隸。唯一自由的人，是不想要任何別人控制得了的東西的人。同樣的分析，給了他對「責任」的說明。我們每個人都被分派了角色：作為孩子、兄弟、公民、老人；而任務是把自己所擁有的角色演好。他不問這些角色分配得公不公平。他問的是：一個好兒子現在會怎麼做？

quote.en: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
quote.zh: 擾亂人的不是事物，而是人對事物所抱的看法。
quote.ref: Epictetus, Enchiridion 5, tr. T. W. Higginson
quote.note_en: The sentence that Albert Ellis said was the starting point of modern cognitive therapy.
quote.note_zh: 艾里斯說，現代的認知治療就是從這句話出發的。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The inner citadel
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：內在的堡壘

paras.en: The whole system depends on there being an inner region that the world cannot reach. Critics doubt it from two sides. The first doubt is psychological. Judgment and desire are produced by a brain and a history. A person who has been starved, drugged, or tortured long enough does not keep his power of choice intact, as Stockdale, who admired Epictetus, admitted from experience. If the citadel can be taken, the promise that nothing can harm a good person is false.
paras.zh: 整個體系有賴於這一點：有一個世界搆不到的內在區域。批評者從兩方面懷疑它。第一個懷疑是心理學上的。判斷與欲求，是由一個腦與一段歷史產生的。一個被餓得夠久、被下藥夠久、或被拷打夠久的人，並不能完整地保住他的抉擇能力；敬佩愛比克泰德的斯托克戴爾，就從親身經驗承認了這一點。如果那座堡壘是可以被攻下的，那麼「沒有任何東西傷害得了一個好人」這個保證就是假的。

paras.en: The second doubt is moral. The Stoic retreats to what he controls and declares the rest indifferent. But the rest includes other people’s suffering and the institutions that cause it. Epictetus had been a slave, taught that slaves and senators are equally children of God, and never suggested that slavery should end. The philosopher Isaiah Berlin called this the retreat to the inner citadel, and compared it to a man who cures a wounded leg by cutting it off: I cannot have what I want, so I will teach myself not to want it. Berlin granted that this is a kind of freedom. He denied that it is the kind a person should be content with while the door is still locked from outside.
paras.zh: 第二個懷疑是道德上的。斯多噶學者退守到他控制得了的東西，並且宣布其餘的都無關善惡。然而，「其餘的」包括別人的苦難，以及造成這些苦難的制度。愛比克泰德當過奴隸，教導奴隸與元老同樣是神的兒女，卻從來沒有提過奴隸制應該終結。哲學家以撒・柏林把這稱為「退入內在的堡壘」，並且把它比作一個人用鋸掉傷腿的方式來治腿傷：我得不到我想要的，所以我要教自己不去想要它。柏林承認這是一種自由。他否認的是：當門還從外面鎖著的時候，一個人應該滿足於這一種自由。

problem.title_en: A voice heard through one listener
problem.title_zh: 透過一位聽者傳來的聲音

paras.en: Everything we have of Epictetus comes through Arrian. The Discourses are lively and uneven. They record informal talks, often prompted by a visitor or by a student’s question, and they are written in the common Greek of the marketplace and not in the literary Greek that Arrian used for his own books, which is good evidence that he was reporting and not composing. Even so, we have a selection. The formal lectures of the school, on logic and on the texts of earlier Stoics, are not recorded. Half of the books are lost. And the Handbook, by which most readers have known him, is a compression made for a purpose, which keeps the commands and drops the humor, the stories, and most of the warmth. Readers who know only the Handbook often think him harsh. The Discourses show a teacher who teases his students, mocks himself, and loses patience with anyone who wants to discuss philosophy and not to change.
paras.zh: 我們所有的愛比克泰德，都是透過阿里安傳下來的。《語錄》生動而參差。它記錄的是非正式的談話，往往由一位訪客或學生的一個問題引起；而且是用市集上通行的希臘語寫的，不是阿里安寫自己的書時用的那種文言希臘語。這是很好的證據，顯示他是在「記錄」而不是在「創作」。即便如此，我們擁有的只是一份選錄。學校裡正式的課（講邏輯、講早期斯多噶學者的文本）並沒有被記下來。有一半的卷數失傳了。而多數讀者藉以認識他的《手冊》，是為了某個目的而作的濃縮；它保留了命令，卻拿掉了幽默、故事與大部分的溫度。只讀過《手冊》的讀者，往往覺得他嚴厲。《語錄》呈現的是一位會逗學生、會嘲笑自己，並且對任何「只想討論哲學、不想改變」的人失去耐心的老師。

said.claim: “God, grant me the serenity to accept the things I cannot change, courage to change the things I can, and wisdom to know the difference.” (Epictetus)
said.claim_zh: 「神啊，求你賜我寧靜，去接受我無法改變的事；賜我勇氣，去改變我能改變的事；並賜我智慧，去分辨兩者。」（愛比克泰德）
said.verdict_zh: 一位美國神學家，約 1932 年
said.en: The Serenity Prayer has been credited to Epictetus, to Francis of Assisi, and to Marcus Aurelius. It was written by the American Protestant theologian Reinhold Niebuhr in the early 1930s and became famous when Alcoholics Anonymous adopted it in the 1940s. The first clause is pure Epictetus. The second is not. He gives no instruction to change things in the world, only to act one’s part well, and the prayer’s balance of acceptance and reform is a modern correction of the Stoic view. The third clause names the problem that the exercise in the lesson above is about.
said.zh: 這篇〈寧靜禱文〉曾被歸給愛比克泰德、亞西西的方濟與馬可・奧理略。它是美國新教神學家尼布爾在 1930 年代初寫的；1940 年代被戒酒無名會採用之後，才變得家喻戶曉。第一句是純粹的愛比克泰德。第二句不是。他並沒有指示人去改變世界上的事，只要人把自己的角色演好；而這篇禱文在「接受」與「改革」之間的平衡，是現代人對斯多噶看法的一個修正。第三句點出的那個問題，正是上面那一課的練習所要處理的。

paras.en: The practical psychology is very close. Epictetus teaches his students to meet each impression with the words, “Wait for me a little, impression. Let me see what you are.” The Buddha teaches the guarding of the sense doors: on seeing a form with the eye, one does not grasp at its signs and features. Both locate freedom in a gap between what arrives and what we do with it, and both hold that the gap can be widened by training. The Stoic word for this watchfulness, prosochē, attention, describes a discipline that Buddhists would recognize as mindfulness, and the second arrow is the Buddha’s image for what Epictetus calls adding our view to the thing. Both taught in the open, to anyone, and both distrusted students who collected doctrines without practicing them.
paras.zh: 實用的心理學非常接近。愛比克泰德教他的學生用這樣的話來迎接每一個印象：「印象啊，等我一下。讓我看看你是什麼。」佛陀教的是守護根門：以眼見色時，不取其相、不取其隨形好。兩人都把自由放在「到來的東西」與「我們拿它怎麼辦」之間的一個間隙裡；兩人也都主張，這個間隙可以靠訓練加寬。斯多噶用來稱呼這份警覺的字是 prosochē（專注）；它所描述的那種紀律，佛教徒會認出那就是正念。而第二支箭，就是佛陀對「愛比克泰德所謂『把我們的看法加在事物上』」所用的意象。兩人都公開教學，來者不拒；兩人也都不信任那些只蒐集教義而不去實踐的學生。

paras.en: The difference lies in what is found in the gap. Epictetus finds a self. Prohairesis is who you really are, it is a portion of the divine reason that orders the world, and the aim of training is to make it sovereign. The Buddha looks in the same place and finds intention, attention, and judgment arising from conditions, with no sovereign among them. Stoic freedom is the independence of a ruler in his citadel. Buddhist freedom is the discovery that there is no citadel and nothing that needs to be defended. Their teachings on feeling for others differ in the same way. Epictetus allows one to groan with a grieving friend, taking care “not to groan inwardly, too.” The Buddhist ideal is a compassion that is fully felt and does not disturb (Dharma and the West, D20).
paras.zh: 差別在於：在那個間隙裡找到的是什麼。愛比克泰德找到的是一個自我。prohairesis 就是真正的你；它是那個安排世界的神聖理性的一份；而訓練的目標，是讓它成為主宰。佛陀看向同一個地方，找到的是依條件而生起的意圖、注意與判斷，其中並沒有主宰者。斯多噶的自由，是一位統治者在自己的堡壘裡的獨立。佛教的自由，是發現根本沒有堡壘，也沒有什麼需要防守。他們關於「對別人的感受」的教導，也以同樣的方式不同。愛比克泰德容許一個人陪著悲傷的朋友一起嘆息，卻要小心「不要在內心也嘆息」。佛教的理想，是一種充分感受到、卻不擾亂心的悲（佛法與西方哲學 D20）。

terms.d_en: The faculty of judging impressions and choosing, which Epictetus identifies with the true self.
terms.d_zh: 判斷印象並作抉擇的能力；愛比克泰德把它等同於真正的自我。

terms.d_en: Whatever presents itself to the mind, from a sight to a thought that one has been wronged.
terms.d_zh: 呈現在心面前的任何東西，從一個景象到「我被冤枉了」的一個念頭。

terms.d_en: The mind’s acceptance of an impression as true.
terms.d_zh: 心把一個印象接受為真。

terms.d_en: Continuous watchfulness over one’s judgments and impulses.
terms.d_zh: 對自己的判斷與衝動持續不斷的警覺。

terms.d_en: A station in life, such as son or citizen, that carries duties.
terms.d_zh: 人生中的一個位置，例如兒子或公民，帶著相應的責任。

terms.d_en: The Stoic image of the mind as a fortress that outside events cannot enter.
terms.d_zh: 斯多噶的意象：心是一座外在事件攻不進去的堡壘。

quiz.q: What does Epictetus say can never be taken from a person?
options: The faculty of choice: how one judges and what one wants.
The body.
Property.
Reputation.

quiz.q: Why does he call a powerful senator a slave?
options: Anyone who wants what another controls has given that person power over him.
Senators were legally slaves.
He disliked the Senate.
Senators could not own property.

quiz.q: What was Isaiah Berlin’s objection?
options: Curing frustration by ceasing to want is a retreat that leaves the outer obstacle in place.
Epictetus wrote too little.
Stoicism is too emotional.
Freedom does not exist.

further.t: Epictetus, The Enchiridion, translated by T. W. Higginson
Epictetus, Discourses, Book I
further.n_en: The teacher in his own voice. Chapters 1, 2, and 18 first.
further.n_zh: 老師自己的聲音。先讀第一、二、十八章。

further.t: A. A. Long, Epictetus: A Stoic and Socratic Guide to Life (2002)
further.n_en: The standard modern study.
further.n_zh: 標準的當代研究。

philosophers.name: Michel de Montaigne
philosophers.place_zh: 法國佩里戈爾與波爾多
philosophers.tag_en: A magistrate who retired to a tower at thirty-eight, took himself as his subject, and in trying to say honestly what he was like invented the essay.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位法官，三十八歲退隱到一座塔樓裡，拿自己當題目；他試著誠實地說出自己是什麼樣子，就這樣發明了「隨筆」。
facts: February 28, 1533, Château de Montaigne, near Bordeaux
Magistrate in Bordeaux, 1557–1570; mayor of Bordeaux, 1581–1585
Essais: Books I–II in 1580, Book III and many additions in 1588
French, with more than a thousand quotations from Latin

paras.en: Montaigne was born in 1533 on his family’s estate in the wine country east of Bordeaux. His great-grandfather had made a fortune in salt fish and bought the land and the title with it. His father had ideas about education. The infant was sent to nurse with a peasant family, so that he would feel close to the poor. He was then given a German tutor who spoke no French, and everyone in the household, including the servants, was required to address the child only in Latin. He was six before he heard French. Each morning he was woken by music. He said later that he had been brought up with such gentleness that he was unfit for effort, and it gave him a lifelong belief that learning should be a pleasure.
paras.zh: 蒙田 1533 年生於他家在波爾多以東產酒區的莊園。他的曾祖父靠鹹魚生意發了財，用那筆錢買下了土地與頭銜。他的父親對教育有一套想法。這個嬰兒被送到一戶農家去餵養，好讓他覺得自己跟窮人親近。接著，他有了一位不會說法語的德國家庭教師；而家裡的每一個人，連僕人在內，都被要求只能用拉丁文跟這個孩子說話。他六歲才第一次聽到法語。每天早上，他是被音樂喚醒的。他後來說，自己被養得太溫和，以致不適合吃苦；而這也讓他一輩子相信，學習應該是一件樂事。

paras.en: He studied law and at twenty-four became a magistrate in the high court at Bordeaux. There he met Étienne de La Boétie, a colleague three years older, a poet and the author of a bold essay against tyranny. The friendship lasted until La Boétie’s death in 1563. Montaigne sat by the bed through the last days and wrote a long account of them to his own father. He said that the rest of his life was smoke and a dark, tedious night. He married two years later, without much enthusiasm, and of his six daughters only one lived to grow up.
paras.zh: 他讀了法律，二十四歲成為波爾多高等法院的法官。他在那裡遇見了拉波埃西：一位比他大三歲的同事，是詩人，也是一篇大膽的反暴政文章的作者。這段友誼一直持續到 1563 年拉波埃西去世。最後那幾天，蒙田守在床邊，並且把經過寫成一封長信給自己的父親。他說，此後他的餘生不過是煙，是一個黑暗而乏味的夜。兩年後他結了婚，並不怎麼熱中；他的六個女兒當中，只有一個活到成年。

paras.en: In 1571, on his thirty-eighth birthday, he retired. He had a Latin inscription painted on the wall of his study, saying that Michel de Montaigne, long weary of the servitude of the court and of public employments, had withdrawn to the bosom of the learned Muses. The study was on the third floor of a round tower at the corner of the house, lined with a thousand books, and on its ceiling beams he had some fifty sayings painted, most of them from the ancient skeptics and from the Bible: I suspend judgment. What do I know? Man is clay. He meant to spend his remaining years in calm.
paras.zh: 1571 年，在三十八歲生日那天，他退隱了。他請人在書房的牆上漆了一段拉丁文銘文，說：米歇爾・德・蒙田，久已厭倦宮廷的奴役與公職，已經退到博學的繆思的懷抱裡。書房在宅邸一角一座圓塔的三樓，四壁排著一千本書；他請人在天花板的橫梁上漆了大約五十句格言，大多出自古代的懷疑論者與聖經：我擱置判斷。我知道什麼？人是泥土。他打算在平靜中度過餘年。

paras.en: The calm did not come. His mind, he found, behaved like a runaway horse and gave birth to so many chimeras and fantastic monsters that he began to write them down, hoping to make his mind ashamed of itself. That is how the Essays began. Outside the tower France was tearing itself apart. The wars between Catholics and Protestants broke out when he was twenty-nine and were still going on when he died, and the massacre of Saint Bartholomew’s Day took place the year after his retirement. His estate lay between the two parties. He left his gates unlocked through the whole of the wars and was robbed once.
paras.zh: 平靜並沒有來。他發現自己的心，表現得像一匹脫韁的馬，生出了那麼多的怪物與幻想，以致他開始把它們寫下來，指望讓自己的心感到羞愧。《隨筆集》就是這樣開始的。塔樓之外，法國正在把自己撕成碎片。天主教徒與新教徒之間的戰爭，在他二十九歲那年爆發，到他去世時還在打；而聖巴托羅繆日的大屠殺，就發生在他退隱的隔年。他的莊園位在兩派之間。整場戰爭期間，他的大門始終沒有上鎖；他被搶過一次。

paras.en: The first two books of the Essays were published in 1580. He then set off on horseback through Germany, Switzerland, and Italy, partly to see the world and partly to try the mineral springs, since he had begun to pass kidney stones, the disease that had killed his father. In Rome he learned that he had been elected mayor of Bordeaux. He served four years, carrying messages between the Catholic king and the Protestant Henry of Navarre, who twice stayed at his house. When plague broke out in the city at the end of his term, he declined to enter it to hand over his office, for which he has been blamed ever since.
paras.zh: 《隨筆集》的前兩卷在 1580 年出版。接著他騎馬出發，穿過德意志、瑞士與義大利；一部分是為了看看世界，一部分是為了試試礦泉，因為他開始排腎結石了，那是奪走他父親性命的病。在羅馬，他得知自己被選為波爾多市長。他做了四年，在天主教的國王與新教的納瓦拉的亨利之間傳遞訊息；亨利兩度住在他家。任期將滿時，城裡爆發了瘟疫；他婉拒進城去辦交接，為此被人責備至今。

paras.en: He spent his last years adding to the book. He never deleted. He wrote new passages in the margins of his own copy, so that an essay begun in his thirties may contain a remark from his fifties contradicting it. A third book appeared in 1588, franker and more personal than the first two. He died in 1592, during a mass said in his room, of an inflammation of the throat that had taken away his speech. He was fifty-nine.
paras.zh: 他把最後的歲月用來增補這本書。他從不刪。他在自己那一本的頁邊寫下新的段落；所以，一篇他三十幾歲開始寫的隨筆，裡面可能有一句他五十幾歲時的話，跟前文互相矛盾。第三卷在 1588 年問世，比前兩卷更坦率、也更個人。1592 年，他在自己房間裡舉行的一台彌撒當中去世；死因是喉嚨發炎，那已經使他說不出話。他五十九歲。

idea.title_en: The central idea: Trying oneself out
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：拿自己來試

paras.en: The French word essai means a trial or an attempt, and Montaigne chose it to describe what he was doing. He takes a subject, thumbs, cannibals, fear, the education of children, and tries his judgment on it, to see what he thinks. The subject of every essay is finally the one named in his note to the reader: “myself am the matter of my book.” Philosophers before him had asked what Man is. He asks what this man is, and reports what he finds with a candor nobody had attempted: his laziness and bad memory, his fondness for scratching his ears, his fear of pain, the way his opinions shift with his digestion. He justifies the project in a sentence. “Every man carries the entire form of human condition.” To describe one person truthfully is to describe something about all.
paras.zh: 法文的 essai 意思是「試驗」或「嘗試」；蒙田選這個字，來描述自己在做的事。他拿一個題目（大拇指、食人族、恐懼、兒童的教育），在它上面試一試自己的判斷，看看自己是怎麼想的。每一篇隨筆的題目，最終都是他在〈致讀者〉裡點名的那一個：「我自己就是我這本書的材料。」他之前的哲學家問的是「人」是什麼。他問的是「這個人」是什麼，並且以沒有人嘗試過的坦率，回報他的發現：他的懶惰與壞記性、他愛抓耳朵、他怕痛、他的意見怎樣隨著消化的好壞而變。他用一句話為這個計畫辯護：「每一個人身上，都帶著人類處境的完整形式。」把一個人如實地描述出來，就是描述了關於所有人的某件事。

paras.en: What he finds is movement. “I cannot fix my object; ’tis always tottering and reeling by a natural giddiness… I do not paint its being, I paint its passage,” from day to day and from minute to minute. He contradicts himself, he says, and does not contradict the truth. From this comes his skepticism. A creature so changeable, whose reason can be bent by a toothache, a custom, or a glass of wine, has small claim to certainty about God and nature, and none to burn other people for disagreeing. His longest essay turns the arguments of the ancient skeptics against human pride. The lesson he draws is tolerance and a certain cheerfulness. Since we cannot be angels, we had better learn to be human well. “There is nothing so fine and legitimate,” he writes at the end of the book, “as well and duly to play the man.”
paras.zh: 他發現的是「動」。「我沒辦法把我的對象固定住；它天生暈眩，總是搖搖晃晃……我不描繪它的存在，我描繪它的經過」，一天又一天，一分鐘又一分鐘。他說，他會自相矛盾，卻不會違背真實。他的懷疑論由此而來。一個這麼善變的生物，理性可以被一次牙痛、一種習俗或一杯酒扳彎；他對於上帝與自然，沒有多少資格宣稱確定；至於因為別人意見不同就把人燒死，更是毫無資格。他最長的那篇隨筆，把古代懷疑論者的論證轉過來對付人類的傲慢。他從中引出的教訓是寬容，以及某種開朗。既然我們當不了天使，就最好學著把人當好。他在全書的結尾寫道：「沒有什麼比把人這個角色演得好、演得恰如其分，更美、更正當的了。」

quote.en: I do not paint its being, I paint its passage.
quote.zh: 我不描繪它的存在，我描繪它的經過。
quote.ref: Montaigne, Essays III.2, “Of Repentance,” tr. Charles Cotton
quote.note_en: He is speaking of himself as the object of his own portrait.
quote.note_zh: 他說的是作為自己畫像對象的那個自己。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: The foolish project
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：那個愚蠢的計畫

paras.en: The deepest criticism came from his greatest reader. Blaise Pascal, two generations later, knew the Essays almost by heart, borrowed from them on every page, and condemned them. “The foolish project he has of painting himself!” Montaigne, he said, inspires indifference about salvation. He shows us how wretched and inconstant we are and then tells us to be at ease with it, and he thinks only of dying softly and without fuss. For Pascal the discovery that reason is weak and the self a muddle should drive a person to his knees. Montaigne makes a pillow of it.
paras.zh: 最深的批評，來自他最偉大的讀者。兩代之後的巴斯卡，幾乎把《隨筆集》背了下來，每一頁都從中借用，卻譴責了它。「他那個要描繪自己的愚蠢計畫！」他說，蒙田使人對得救漠不關心。他讓我們看到自己多麼可憐、多麼反覆無常，然後叫我們對此安之若素；而他只想著死得輕鬆、不費事。對巴斯卡來說，發現理性是軟弱的、自我是一團亂，應該把人逼得跪下來。蒙田卻拿它當了枕頭。

paras.en: A second objection is political. His skepticism leads him to conservatism. Since we cannot know that any new arrangement would be better, he argues, we should keep the laws and the religion we were born under, and he remained a Catholic and a royalist on those grounds. Critics reply that this is a comfortable conclusion for a landowner, and that the same argument would have told the Protestants of his day, and the slaves of the New World, to stay as they were. He saw part of the difficulty. His essay on the peoples of Brazil asks which is the more barbarous, to eat a man who is dead or to torture one who is alive, as his own countrymen were doing.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁是政治上的。他的懷疑論把他帶向保守。他論證：既然我們無法知道任何新的安排會更好，我們就應該保持自己生來所處的法律與宗教；而他就是基於這個理由，始終是一位天主教徒與保王派。批評者回答：對一位地主來說，這是一個舒服的結論；而同一個論證，也會叫他那個時代的新教徒與新大陸的奴隸維持原狀。這個困難，他看到了一部分。他那篇談巴西原住民的隨筆問道：吃一個死人，跟拷打一個活人（他自己的同胞正在這樣做），哪一個比較野蠻？

paras.en: With Montaigne the problem is the reverse of the usual one. We have too much of him. He published the Essays three times in his life and was preparing a fourth edition when he died, working in a printed copy whose margins he had filled with about a thousand additions in his own hand. That volume, the Bordeaux Copy, survives. Modern editions mark the three layers with the letters A, B, and C, so that a reader can see a sentence of 1580 interrupted by a second thought of 1588 and a third of 1592. Which Montaigne is the real one is a question he would have enjoyed. His literary executor, Marie de Gournay, a young admirer whom he called his adopted daughter, brought out an edition in 1595 from another annotated copy, now lost, and scholars still dispute which text is closer to his final wishes.
paras.zh: 蒙田的問題跟通常的正好相反。我們擁有的他太多了。他生前把《隨筆集》出版了三次，去世時正在準備第四版；他用的是一本印好的書，頁邊被他親手寫下的大約一千處增補填滿了。那一冊，「波爾多本」，留存至今。現代的版本用 A、B、C 三個字母標出這三個層次；所以讀者可以看到 1580 年的一個句子，被 1588 年的一個轉念打斷，接著又被 1592 年的第三個想法打斷。哪一個蒙田才是真的？這是一個他自己會樂在其中的問題。他的文學遺囑執行人瑪麗・德・古爾奈（一位他稱為義女的年輕仰慕者），在 1595 年根據另一本已經失傳的批註本出了一個版本；學者至今還在爭論，哪一個文本更接近他最後的意願。

paras.en: There is also the question of how far to trust the portrait. He promises to paint himself whole and naked, and he was a public man during a civil war, writing under the eye of the Church, which placed the book on its Index in 1676. He says a great deal about his kidney stones and very little about his wife or his mother.
paras.zh: 還有一個問題：這幅畫像能信到什麼程度？他承諾要把自己完整而赤裸地畫出來；而他是內戰期間的一位公眾人物，在教會的注視下寫作（教會在 1676 年把這本書列入了禁書目錄）。關於自己的腎結石，他說了很多；關於自己的妻子與母親，他說得很少。

said.claim: “My life has been full of terrible misfortunes, most of which never happened.” (Montaigne)
said.claim_zh: 「我這一生充滿了可怕的不幸，其中大部分從來沒有發生過。」（蒙田）
said.en: The line is quoted under Montaigne’s name in countless books on worry and has also been given to Mark Twain. It has not been located in the Essays. The thought is certainly his. In the essay on fear he writes that the thing he fears most is fear, and elsewhere that a man who is afraid of suffering already suffers from what he fears. The neat modern sentence seems to be a summary that acquired quotation marks. A reader who likes it will find the real passages longer, stranger, and better.
said.zh: 無數談「憂慮」的書都把這句話掛在蒙田名下引用；它也曾被歸給馬克・吐溫。在《隨筆集》裡，它並沒有被找到。這個想法倒確實是他的。在論恐懼的那篇隨筆裡，他寫道，他最怕的東西就是恐懼；在別處他又說，一個害怕受苦的人，已經在為他所害怕的東西受苦了。那句俐落的現代句子，看來是一個後來被加上了引號的摘要。喜歡它的讀者會發現，真正的段落更長、更怪，也更好。

paras.en: Montaigne did by temperament what the Buddha taught as a discipline. He watched his own mind, day after day, for twenty years, and wrote down what he saw without trying to make it consistent. What he saw was what the Buddha said one would see: no fixed thing, a passage. “I do not paint its being, I paint its passage” is as good a statement of impermanence applied to the self as European literature contains, and it was reached by observation with no doctrine to guide it. His essay arguing that to philosophize is to learn to die recommends keeping death always before the mind so that it loses its strangeness, which is the practice the Buddhist texts call mindfulness of death. And his refusal to assert, with “What do I know?” struck as a medal, recalls the Buddha’s warning against clinging to views.
paras.zh: 蒙田憑著性情，做了佛陀當作一門紀律來教的事。他日復一日地看著自己的心，看了二十年，並且把所見寫下來，不去設法讓它前後一致。他看到的，就是佛陀說人會看到的東西：沒有固定的東西，只有「經過」。「我不描繪它的存在，我描繪它的經過」，是歐洲文學裡把無常用在自我身上最好的陳述之一；而它是靠觀察得到的，沒有任何教義引導。他那篇論證「研究哲學就是學習死亡」的隨筆，建議把死亡時時放在心前，使它不再陌生；這就是佛典稱為「死隨念」的修習。而他的不肯斷言（連同鑄成紀念章的那句「我知道什麼？」），讓人想起佛陀對執取見解的警告。

paras.en: What he does with the discovery is his own. Having found the self to be a flux, he settles into it and enjoys the view. He has no wish to be liberated from himself. The Buddha treats the same finding as the start of a path, because he holds that clinging to this flux as “me” is the cause of suffering and can be ended. Montaigne also lacks a method. He observes whatever comes up, where the Buddhist practitioner observes in a set order and with a trained stillness of attention. Pascal accused him of resting where he should have gone on. A Buddhist would make the same criticism more kindly, and would add that he had seen more than most philosophers by simply looking (Dharma and the West, D5).
paras.zh: 他拿這個發現怎麼辦，則是他自己的事。發現自我是一道流之後，他在其中安頓下來，欣賞風景。他並不想從自己當中解脫出來。佛陀把同樣的發現當作一條道路的起點；因為他主張，把這道流執取為「我」，正是苦的原因，而它是可以止息的。蒙田也沒有方法。冒出什麼，他就觀察什麼；佛教的修行者則是依一定的次第、帶著訓練出來的專注的寂靜去觀察。巴斯卡指控他在應該繼續往前走的地方歇了下來。佛教徒會比較溫和地提出同樣的批評，並且會補上一句：單靠著「看」，他已經比大多數的哲學家看到得更多了（佛法與西方哲學 D5）。

terms.d_en: A short prose piece in which a writer tries out his thoughts on a subject. Montaigne’s invention.
terms.d_zh: 作者在一個題目上試驗自己想法的短篇散文。蒙田的發明。

terms.d_en: The withholding of assent where certainty is lacking.
terms.d_zh: 在缺乏確定性的地方，不輕易同意。

terms.d_en: The ancient school that suspended judgment on all questions and found peace in doing so.
terms.d_zh: 古代的一個學派：對一切問題擱置判斷，並且在其中得到平靜。

terms.d_en: For Montaigne, the main source of what each people takes to be natural and right.
terms.d_zh: 對蒙田來說，每一個民族視為「自然而正當」的東西的主要來源。

terms.d_en: What all human beings share by being human. The phrase is his.
terms.d_zh: 所有人因為是人而共有的東西。這個說法是他的。

terms.d_en: His image for the Essays: a likeness of one person, drawn over twenty years.
terms.d_zh: 他對《隨筆集》的比喻：一個人的肖像，畫了二十年。

philosophers.name: Mozi
philosophers.tag_en: A craftsman turned philosopher who taught that everyone’s welfare counts alike, walked ten days and nights to stop a war, and led a school that vanished for two thousand years.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位工匠出身的哲學家；他教導每個人的福祉同等算數，走了十天十夜去阻止一場戰爭，並且帶領了一個後來消失兩千年的學派。
facts: c. 470 BCE, probably in Lu or Song
Mo Di 墨翟. Mò means ink, and may have been a nickname for a branded convict or a dark-skinned laborer
Probably an artisan: a carpenter or military engineer
Mozi 墨子, 71 chapters originally, 53 surviving, written by his school
A disciplined organization under a Grand Master (巨子 jùzǐ)

paras.en: The great historian Sima Qian gave Confucius a chapter and Mencius a paragraph. To Mozi he gave twenty-four characters at the end of someone else’s biography: “Mo Di was a great officer of Song, skilled in defense and an advocate of frugal spending. Some say he lived at the time of Confucius, others that he came after.” Nothing more was known four centuries after his death. The rest has to be gathered from the book that bears his name. It suggests a man of the lower orders. His comparisons come from the workshop: the compass, the square, the plumb line, the wheelwright and the potter. His opponents called his teaching the way of menial laborers. He seems to have studied with Confucians as a young man and broken with them over their costly rites and their acceptance of fate.
paras.zh: 偉大的史家司馬遷給了孔子一整篇，給了孟子一段。給墨子的，是附在別人傳記末尾的二十四個字：「蓋墨翟，宋之大夫，善守禦，為節用。或曰並孔子時，或曰在其後。」在他死後四個世紀，人們知道的就只有這些了。其餘的，得從那本以他為名的書裡拼湊出來。那本書暗示他是一個出身下層的人。他的比喻來自作坊：規、矩、繩墨、輪匠與陶匠。他的對手把他的教導稱為「役夫之道」。他年輕時似乎跟儒者學過，後來因為他們昂貴的禮儀與他們對「命」的接受而決裂。

paras.en: He traveled from state to state as Confucius had, with one difference. Confucius sought office. Mozi sought to prevent particular wars, and he brought with him something rulers needed, a body of followers trained in the defense of walled cities.
paras.zh: 他像孔子那樣周遊列國，只有一點不同。孔子求的是官職。墨子求的是阻止某一場具體的戰爭；而他身邊帶著統治者需要的東西：一群受過守城訓練的門徒。

paras.en: The best-known story about him is in the book. The master craftsman Gongshu Ban had built scaling ladders for the king of Chu, who meant to use them against the small state of Song. Mozi heard of it in Qi and walked for ten days and ten nights to the Chu capital. He first argued with Gongshu Ban. You would refuse to kill one man for money, he said, and you are helping to kill multitudes. Gongshu Ban admitted the point and said that the matter was out of his hands. Before the king, Mozi took off his belt and laid it out as a city wall, and used small sticks for engines. Nine times Gongshu Ban set up a method of attack, and nine times Mozi repelled it. Gongshu Ban had used up his devices, and Mozi’s defenses were not exhausted.
paras.zh: 關於他最著名的故事就在那本書裡。巧匠公輸般為楚王造好了雲梯，楚王打算拿它去攻打小國宋。墨子在齊國聽說了，走了十天十夜，到了楚國的都城郢。他先跟公輸般論理。他說：你不肯為了錢去殺一個人，卻在幫忙殺許多人。公輸般承認他說得對，卻說這件事已經由不得自己了。在楚王面前，墨子解下腰帶，擺成一道城牆，用小木片當作器械。「公輸般九設攻城之機變，子墨子九距之。」公輸般的攻城器械用盡了，而墨子的守禦之法還有餘。

paras.en: Gongshu Ban then said, “I know how to defeat you, and I will not say it.” Mozi answered, “I know how you would defeat me, and I will not say it either.” The king asked what they meant. “He means to have me killed,” said Mozi. “But my disciple Qin Guli and three hundred others are already on the walls of Song with my devices, waiting for the army of Chu. You may kill me, and you will not have stopped them.” The king called off the attack. On his way home Mozi passed through Song in the rain and sought shelter in a gateway. The gatekeeper would not let him in.
paras.zh: 接著公輸般說：「吾知所以距子矣，吾不言。」墨子回答：「吾知子之所以距我，吾不言。」楚王問這是什麼意思。墨子說：他的意思是要殺了我。「然臣之弟子禽滑釐等三百人，已持臣守圉之器，在宋城上而待楚寇矣。雖殺臣，不能絕也。」楚王取消了進攻。回程中，墨子路過宋國，碰上下雨，想在一處閭門下躲一躲。守門的人不讓他進去。

paras.en: His followers formed something new in China, an organization. They lived under strict rules, wore coarse clothing, obeyed a Grand Master, and were sent out as officials and as defenders of threatened cities. A story tells of a Grand Master whose son committed murder in Qin. The king offered to pardon him, and the father refused, saying that the law of the Mohists was that he who kills shall die. Zhuangzi’s school, which thought their way too harsh for human nature, wrote of Mozi with respect: “He was truly one who loved the world. He sought it and could not get it, and though he withered away he would not give up. A man of real talent!”
paras.zh: 他的追隨者在中國形成了一種新的東西：一個組織。他們生活在嚴格的規矩之下，穿粗布衣，服從一位「巨子」，並且被派出去做官，或去防守受到威脅的城。有一個故事說，一位巨子的兒子在秦國殺了人。秦王願意赦免他，而這位父親拒絕了，說墨者的法是「殺人者死」。莊子的學派認為墨家的路對人性來說太苛刻，寫到墨子時卻帶著敬意：「墨子真天下之好也，將求之不得也，雖枯槁，不舍也，才士也夫！」

paras.en: In the fourth and third centuries BCE the Mohists were the main rivals of the Confucians, and Mencius complained that the words of Mozi filled the world. Their later members wrote the most rigorous work in logic, geometry, optics, and mechanics that survives from ancient China, including the first known description of an image inverted through a pinhole. Then, within a century of the unification of the empire in 221 BCE, the school was gone. A society at peace under one ruler had no need of specialists in defending small states, and Confucianism became the creed of the court. The book lay almost unread for two thousand years, its logical chapters garbled by copyists, until Qing scholars restored the text in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. Chinese reformers of the early twentieth century then discovered in Mozi a native tradition of science, logic, and equal concern for all.
paras.zh: 在西元前第四、第三世紀，墨者是儒者的主要對手；孟子抱怨過，墨翟之言盈天下。他們後期的成員，寫下了古代中國留存至今最嚴謹的邏輯學、幾何學、光學與力學著作，其中包括已知最早的針孔成倒像的描述。然後，在西元前 221 年帝國統一之後的一個世紀之內，這個學派就不見了。一個在一位君主之下太平無事的社會，不需要專門防守小國的人；而儒家成了朝廷的信條。那本書有兩千年之久幾乎沒有人讀，其中談邏輯的幾篇被抄寫者弄得錯亂不堪；直到十八、十九世紀，清代的學者才把文本校理出來。二十世紀初的中國改革者，接著在墨子身上發現了一個本土的科學、邏輯與「平等關懷一切人」的傳統。

timeline: Stops the Chu attack on Song
Later Mohists write the Canons on logic and optics
Qin unifies China; the school fades
Bi Yuan’s edition revives study of the text

idea.title_en: The central idea: Benefit to all as the test
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：以「利天下」為檢驗

paras.en: Mozi was the first Chinese thinker to argue for his positions, and the first anywhere to propose a single test for every policy and custom. A doctrine, he says, must be judged by three standards. It must have a basis in the deeds of the ancient sage kings. It must be verified by what the common people see and hear. And it must be applied, by putting it into practice in government and observing whether it benefits the state and the people. The third standard does most of the work. Whatever enriches the poor, increases the population, and brings order is right. Whatever does the opposite is wrong. He applies the test without fear of the result. Elaborate funerals and three years of mourning waste wealth and weaken the living, so they should go. Music at court consumes resources that could feed people, so it should go too.
paras.zh: 墨子是第一位為自己的立場提出論證的中國思想家；而在任何地方，他都是第一位為每一項政策與習俗提出單一檢驗的人。他說，一個主張必須用三個標準來判斷，「言必有三表」。它必須「本之」於古代聖王的事蹟。它必須「原察」百姓耳目所見所聞的實情。它還必須「用之」：把它實施在刑政上，觀察它是否符合國家與百姓人民的利益。第三個標準擔負了大部分的工作。凡是使窮人富足、使人口增加、帶來秩序的，就是對的。凡是造成相反結果的，就是錯的。他運用這個檢驗的時候，不怕結果。厚葬與三年之喪，浪費財富，削弱生者，所以該廢。朝廷上的音樂，耗掉了可以用來養活人的資源，所以也該廢。

paras.en: Two conclusions made him famous. The first is impartial care, that one should regard others’ families and states as one’s own, since partiality is the cause of all the great harms. The second is the condemnation of aggressive war. His argument is a model of consistency. If a man kills one person, we call it wrong and put him to death. If he kills ten, the wrong is ten times as great. Everyone knows this. “But when it comes to the great wrong of attacking a state, they do not know to condemn it. They praise it and call it right.” A person who called a little black black and a great deal of black white would be thought unable to tell the colors apart. He permitted defensive war, and made himself the best military engineer of his age in order to make attack unprofitable.
paras.zh: 有兩個結論使他聞名。第一個是兼愛：應該把別人的家與國看作自己的，因為「別」是一切大害的原因。第二個是對侵略戰爭的譴責（非攻）。他的論證是「前後一致」的典範。一個人殺了一個人，我們說這是不義，並且判他死罪。殺了十個人，不義就是十倍。這是人人都知道的。「今至大為不義攻國，則弗知而非，從而譽之，謂之義。」一個人看見一點點黑就說是黑，看見很多黑卻說是白，人們會認為他分不清顏色。他容許防衛性的戰爭；並且為了讓進攻變得無利可圖，把自己練成了那個時代最好的軍事工程師。

quote.en: To kill one man is called unrighteous, and must be punished with one death. … But when it comes to the great unrighteousness of attacking a state, they do not know to condemn it. They praise it and call it righteous.
quote.zh: 殺一人謂之不義，必有一死罪矣。……今至大為不義攻國，則弗知而非，從而譽之，謂之義。
quote.ref: Mozi, chapter 17, “Against Aggression,” translated for this series
quote.note_en: An argument from consistency, twenty-four centuries old and not yet answered.
quote.note_zh: 一個訴諸「前後一致」的論證；兩千四百年了，還沒有被回答。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: A life no one can live
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：一種誰也過不了的生活

paras.en: Mencius said that impartial care amounts to having no father, and the charge has two parts. The first is psychological. Human concern grows outward from the family, and a person trained to feel no more for his own parents than for strangers would end by feeling little for anyone. The second is that people will not do it. Mozi replied that rulers have got people to do harder things, such as starving themselves to please a king who liked slender waists, and that impartial care would be easy by comparison if rulers rewarded it. The reply reveals something about his view of motivation. He expects people to be moved by reward, punishment, and the will of Heaven, and he says little about how a person might come to want the good of strangers.
paras.zh: 孟子說兼愛等於「無父」；這項指控有兩個部分。第一個是心理學上的。人的關懷是從家往外長的；一個被訓練得對自己父母的感情不比對陌生人多的人，最後會對誰都沒有多少感情。第二個是：人們不會照做。墨子回答：統治者曾經讓人們做過更難的事，例如為了討好一位喜歡細腰的國君而把自己餓瘦；相較之下，只要統治者獎賞它，兼愛是容易的。這個回答透露了他對「動機」的看法。他預期人是被賞、罰與天志推動的；至於一個人怎樣才會變得「想要」陌生人過得好，他說得很少。

paras.en: Xunzi made a different criticism in one line: Mozi “was blinded by utility and did not understand culture.” A test that asks only whether a thing feeds, clothes, and orders the people will condemn music, ceremony, and ornament, and Mozi condemned them. Xunzi replied that human beings need form and beauty as they need food, and that rites and music are how feeling is shaped into something that can be shared. Zhuangzi’s school said the same more gently. Mozi would have people sing no songs in life and wear no mourning in death. “It makes people anxious and sorrowful. Its practice is hard to carry out. I fear it cannot be the way of the sage.”
paras.zh: 荀子用一句話提出了另一種批評：「墨子蔽於用而不知文。」一個只問「這樣東西能不能讓百姓吃飽、穿暖、有秩序」的檢驗，會把音樂、禮儀與文飾全部判為有罪；而墨子確實這樣判了。荀子回答：人需要形式與美，就像需要食物一樣；而禮與樂，就是把情感塑造成可以共享的東西的方式。莊子的學派把同樣的話說得比較溫和。墨子要人活著不唱歌，死了不服喪。「使人憂，使人悲，其行難為也，恐其不可以為聖人之道。」

paras.en: Mozi wrote nothing that we can identify. The book is the work of his school over two centuries. Its core is a set of essays on ten doctrines, among them impartial care, against aggression, frugality, and the will of Heaven, and each essay survives in up to three versions that say the same thing in different words. Scholars think that these come from three branches into which the school divided, each keeping its own record of the master’s teaching. The style is plain and repetitive, built for memorizing and for persuading an audience by hammering. Other parts are later: the Canons on logic and science, and twenty chapters on the defense of cities that are among the oldest military engineering texts in the world.
paras.zh: 我們辨認得出是墨子親筆的東西，一樣也沒有。那本書是他的學派歷時兩個世紀的作品。它的核心是談十項主張的一組論文，其中有兼愛、非攻、節用與天志；而每一篇論文都以多達三個版本流傳下來，用不同的話說同一件事。學者們認為，這些出自這個學派後來分成的三支，各自保存了自己那一份對老師教導的紀錄。文風樸素而反覆，是為了背誦、也為了用反覆敲打來說服聽眾而寫的。其他的部分是較晚的：談邏輯與科學的《墨經》，以及二十篇談守城的文字，那是世界上最古老的軍事工程文獻之一。

paras.en: Because the text was neglected for so long, a third of it is lost and parts of the rest are corrupt. What we read is a reconstruction by scholars of the last three centuries, and the man behind it is known only through followers who were more interested in his arguments than in him.
paras.zh: 由於這個文本被忽略了那麼久，它有三分之一失傳了，其餘的也有一部分訛誤。我們讀到的，是最近三個世紀的學者重建出來的；而文本背後的那個人，我們只能透過他的追隨者來認識，而那些人對他的論證，比對他本人更有興趣。

said.claim: 墨守成規 — “to hold to convention as Mozi held the wall,” said of a stubborn conservative. (After Mozi)
said.claim_zh: 「墨守成規」：用來形容頑固守舊的人。（典出墨子）
said.verdict_zh: 他的名字，被反過來用在他身上
said.en: The idiom is in daily use in Chinese for someone who clings to old rules and will not adapt. Its first two characters, Mò shǒu, “Mo’s defense,” go back to the story of the nine attacks repelled at the court of Chu, and for centuries they were pure praise: a defense so good that nothing could break it. The words “established rules” were added much later, and the sense turned from skill to rigidity. The irony is considerable. Mozi was the least conventional thinker of his age, and he judged every inherited custom, from funerals to music, by whether it did any good.
said.zh: 這個成語在中文裡天天有人用，指的是死抱著舊規矩、不肯變通的人。它的前兩個字「墨守」，可以追溯到在楚國朝廷上九次擋下進攻的那個故事；有好幾個世紀，這兩個字是純粹的讚美：一種好到攻不破的防守。「成規」兩個字是很久以後才加上去的；於是意思從「高明」轉成了「僵化」。這裡的反諷相當大。墨子是他那個時代最不守成規的思想家；從葬禮到音樂，每一項傳下來的習俗，他都拿「有沒有好處」來評判。

paras.en: The two were near contemporaries, and both taught a goodwill that makes no distinction of persons. Mozi’s “regard other people’s families as one’s own” and the Buddha’s wish for the happiness of all beings “with not a one left out” have the same reach. Both rejected the claims of birth: Mozi wanted office given to the worthy even if they were farmers or artisans, and the Buddha admitted all castes to his order. Both condemned the killing that their societies honored, and both founded communities of people who lived plainly under a rule.
paras.zh: 兩人是年代相近的同時代人，都教導一種不分對象的善意。墨子的「視人之家若視其家」，與佛陀願一切眾生安樂、「一個也不遺漏」，範圍是相同的。兩人都拒絕了出身的特權：墨子要把官職給賢能的人，即使他們是農夫或工匠（尚賢）；佛陀讓一切種姓都可以加入他的僧團。兩人都譴責他們的社會所推崇的殺戮；兩人也都創立了依規矩過簡樸生活的團體。

paras.en: They differ in what they think the trouble is and so in the cure. Mozi sees a problem of policy. People are partial because their rulers reward partiality, and they will be impartial when the incentives change and when they understand that Heaven wants it. He has no account of the mind. The Buddha sees a problem of craving and ignorance in each person, and he supplies what Mozi lacks, a method by which the feeling of goodwill can be made to grow. The meditation on loving-kindness begins with those who are dear and works outward to enemies. It thus accepts Mencius’s point about where care starts and arrives at Mozi’s conclusion. They differ, too, on war and on beauty. Mozi fortified cities. The Buddha taught that hatred is not ended by hatred. And where Mozi banned music as waste, the Buddhist tradition filled Asia with chant, painting, and sculpture, on the view that the mind is moved toward the good by what it loves (Dharma and the West, D19).
paras.zh: 他們的差別，在於認為問題出在哪裡，因而也在於對治的方法。墨子看到的是一個政策問題。人之所以偏私，是因為統治者獎賞偏私；等到誘因改變、等到他們明白這是天所要的，他們就會兼愛。他沒有對「心」的說明。佛陀看到的，是每一個人裡面渴愛與無明的問題；而他提供了墨子所缺的東西：一種可以使善意的感受生長起來的方法。慈心的禪修從親愛的人開始，往外修到怨敵。於是，它接受了孟子關於「關懷從哪裡起步」的論點，而抵達了墨子的結論。他們在戰爭與美這兩件事上也不同。墨子加固城防。佛陀教導：怨恨不能止息怨恨。墨子把音樂當作浪費而禁止；佛教的傳統卻讓唱誦、繪畫與雕塑遍布亞洲，理由是：心是被它所愛的東西帶向善的（佛法與西方哲學 D19）。

terms.d_en: Giving the interests of others the same weight as one’s own and one’s family’s.
terms.d_zh: 給別人的利益與自己、自己家人的利益同樣的分量。

terms.d_en: The condemnation of offensive war as murder on a great scale.
terms.d_zh: 把侵略戰爭譴責為大規模的殺人。

terms.d_en: Mozi’s tests for a doctrine: precedent, the evidence of the senses, and benefit in practice.
terms.d_zh: 墨子對一個主張的檢驗：先例、耳目之實，以及實行起來的利益。

terms.d_en: Spending only on what benefits the people.
terms.d_zh: 只把錢花在對百姓有利的事上。

terms.d_en: Appointing officials by ability and not by birth.
terms.d_zh: 依能力而不依出身來任用官員。

terms.d_en: Mozi’s belief that Heaven desires righteousness and rewards those who benefit others.
terms.d_zh: 墨子的信念：天欲義，並且賞那些利人的人。

quiz.q: What is Mozi’s test for whether a custom or policy is right?
options: Whether, in practice, it benefits the state and the people.
Whether it is ancient.
Whether it is beautiful.
Whether the ruler likes it.

quiz.q: What is his argument against aggressive war?
options: If killing one person is wrong, killing thousands is a far greater wrong, and it is inconsistent to praise it.
War is too expensive for small states only.
Soldiers are badly paid.
Heaven forbids all fighting, including defense.

quiz.q: What was Xunzi’s criticism of Mozi?
options: He was blinded by utility and did not understand culture.
He was too fond of music.
He ignored the common people.
He supported aggressive war.

philosophers.name: Xunzi
philosophers.tag_en: The most systematic of the early Confucians, who held that human nature is bad and civilization a hard-won artifact, and whose two most famous students helped to build the empire he would have hated.
philosophers.tag_zh: 早期儒者當中最有系統的一位；他主張人性是惡的，文明是一件得來不易的人造物。他最有名的兩個學生，幫忙建造了一個他會憎惡的帝國。
facts: c. 310 BCE, in the state of Zhao
Xun Kuang 荀況; also called Xun Qing 荀卿, “Minister Xun”
Three times libationer (head) of the Jixia Academy in Qi; magistrate of Lanling
Xunzi 荀子, 32 chapters, mostly by his own hand

paras.en: Xunzi was born about 310 BCE in Zhao, in the north, a generation after Mencius. Sima Qian says that he came to Qi to study at the age of fifty, though some scholars think the figure should be fifteen. Qi was then the intellectual center of China. Its kings maintained a kind of academy near the Ji gate of the capital, where scholars of every school were given houses and stipends and were expected only to debate. Daoists, Mohists, logicians, and experts on yin and yang all taught there. By the time the older generation had died, the historian says, Xunzi was “the most senior teacher,” and he was three times chosen as its libationer, the scholar who led the ceremonial offering and so the head of the gathering.
paras.zh: 荀子大約西元前 310 年生於北方的趙國，比孟子晚一代。司馬遷說他「年五十始來游學於齊」，不過有些學者認為那個數字應該是十五。齊國當時是中國的思想中心。齊王在都城的稷門附近，維持著一種學宮；各家各派的學者在那裡得到宅第與俸祿，唯一被期待的事就是辯論。道家、墨家、名家與陰陽家的專家，都在那裡講學。這位史家說，等到老一輩都去世了，荀子「最為老師」；他三度被選為祭酒，也就是主持祭奠之禮、因而是這個群體之首的那位學者。

paras.en: The setting shaped him. He knew every rival doctrine at first hand, and his book answers them one by one: Mozi was blinded by utility, Zhuangzi by Heaven, the logician Hui Shi by words. He believed that each had seen a corner of the truth and mistaken it for the whole, and that only the Confucian way, properly understood, was complete.
paras.zh: 這個環境塑造了他。每一種與之競爭的學說，他都有第一手的了解；而他的書逐一回應了它們：墨子蔽於用，莊子蔽於天，名家的惠施蔽於辭。他相信，每一家都看見了真理的一角，卻誤以為那是全部；只有恰當理解下的儒家之道，才是完整的。

paras.en: He traveled, as Confucius and Mencius had, and with no more success. The most revealing journey was to Qin, the western state that was then conquering its neighbors one by one. He was the only major Confucian to see it. The chief minister asked what he had observed. Xunzi replied with striking fairness. The people were simple and afraid of the officials. The officials were grave, frugal, and honest. Business at court was dispatched without delay. It was the height of good order. And yet, he said, measured against the standard of a true king it fell far short, and the reason was that it had almost no Confucians. Qin had law and lacked the moral education that makes people good from within. He called it a state that could be feared and could not be loved.
paras.zh: 他像孔子與孟子那樣周遊列國，成果也並不更多。最能看出他這個人的一趟旅程，是到秦國去；那個西方的國家，當時正在一個接一個地征服鄰國。重要的儒者當中，只有他親眼見過它。秦相問他看到了什麼。荀子的回答公允得驚人。百姓樸實，畏懼官吏。官吏肅然、儉約而清廉。朝廷上的事務處理起來毫不拖延。那是治理得極好的樣子。然而，他說，拿真正王者的標準來衡量，它還差得遠；原因是它幾乎沒有儒者。秦有法，卻缺少那種使人從內在變好的道德教化。他說那是一個讓人畏懼、卻無法讓人愛的國家。

paras.en: He was slandered in Qi and moved south to Chu, where the lord of Chunshen made him magistrate of Lanling. When his patron was assassinated in 238 he lost the post, and he stayed in Lanling teaching and writing until he died. He was buried there.
paras.zh: 他在齊國遭人讒毀，南下到了楚國；春申君任命他為蘭陵令。西元前 238 年，他的這位庇護者被刺殺，他失去了職位；他留在蘭陵教書、寫作，直到去世。他就葬在那裡。

paras.en: Among those who came to Lanling were a prince of Han named Han Fei and a clerk from Chu named Li Si. Han Fei became the greatest theorist of the Legalist school, which held that the state should be run by law, reward, and punishment, with no reliance on virtue. Li Si became chief minister of Qin, helped its king to conquer the other states and declare himself First Emperor in 221, and in 213 proposed the burning of the books of the philosophers. Before that he had brought about the death of his fellow student, Han Fei, in a Qin prison. Xunzi is said to have refused to eat on hearing that Li Si had taken office in Qin, foreseeing how it would end.
paras.zh: 到蘭陵來的人當中，有一位韓國的公子韓非，以及一位來自楚國的小吏李斯。韓非成了法家最偉大的理論家；法家主張，國家應該靠法、賞與罰來治理，完全不倚靠德。李斯成了秦的丞相，幫助秦王征服了其他各國，並在西元前 221 年自立為始皇帝；西元前 213 年，他提議焚燒諸子之書。在那之前，他已經在秦國的獄中，促成了同門韓非的死。據說荀子聽到李斯入秦為官的消息，就不肯進食，因為他預見了事情會怎麼收場。

paras.en: The connection damaged him permanently. For the first thousand years of the empire he was read and respected as much as Mencius. When the Song philosophers chose Mencius as the true heir of Confucius, they condemned Xunzi for his doctrine of human nature and for his students, and his book dropped out of the curriculum. His tablet was removed from the Confucian temple in 1530. Modern scholars have restored him, as the early Confucian who argued most carefully and who saw most clearly what institutions do.
paras.zh: 這層關係永久地損害了他。在帝國的頭一千年裡，他被閱讀、被尊重的程度不亞於孟子。等到宋代的哲學家選定孟子為孔子真正的繼承者，他們就因為荀子的人性論與他的學生而譴責他；他的書也從課程裡消失了。1530 年，他的牌位被移出了孔廟。現代的學者使他恢復了地位：他是早期儒者當中論證最謹慎、也最看清楚「制度做了什麼」的一位。

timeline: At the Jixia Academy in Qi
Loses his post; stays to teach
His student Li Si helps unify China
他的學生李斯協助統一中國

idea.title_en: The central idea: Goodness is made
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：善是做出來的

paras.en: Xunzi’s best-known sentence is “Human nature is bad. Its goodness is the product of deliberate effort.” He means that what we are born with, appetite, envy, and the love of gain, leads to conflict if it is simply followed, and that everything admirable in human life has been achieved against that pull. His book opens with the consequence: “Learning must never stop. Blue dye comes from the indigo plant and is bluer than the plant. Ice is made from water and is colder than water.” A person is raw material, and education can make of him something better than the material. The method is accumulation. “If you do not pile up small steps, you cannot go a thousand li. If you carve and give up, you cannot cut through rotten wood. If you carve and do not give up, you can engrave metal and stone.”
paras.zh: 荀子最廣為人知的一句話是：「人之性惡，其善者偽也。」他的意思是：我們生來就有的東西（欲望、嫉妒與好利），如果只是順著它走，會導向衝突；而人類生活裡一切值得敬佩的東西，都是逆著那股拉力成就的。他的書一開頭就說出了由此而來的結論：「學不可以已。青，取之於藍，而青於藍；冰，水為之，而寒於水。」人是原料；而教育可以把他造就成比原料更好的東西。方法是積累。「不積跬步，無以至千里……鍥而舍之，朽木不折；鍥而不舍，金石可鏤。」

paras.en: What we accumulate is ritual, the forms of conduct worked out by the sages. Xunzi gives the fullest defense of ritual in Chinese thought. It assigns each person a place and a share and so ends contention. It also shapes feeling. Mourning rites, he says, are set up “in proportion to the emotion,” so that grief has a form and a limit. He is as original about nature. “Heaven’s course is constant. It does not exist for the sake of Yao or perish because of Jie.” The sky sends no messages. Asked why it rains after the rain sacrifice, he answers, “For no reason. It is the same as when it rains without the sacrifice.” People perform such rites to give form to their concern. “The gentleman regards them as culture, and the common people regard them as supernatural.” Order and disorder come from human beings, and it is our business to manage what Heaven provides.
paras.zh: 我們所積累的是禮，也就是聖人制定出來的行為形式。在中國思想裡，荀子為禮作了最完整的辯護。禮給每個人分派一個位置、一份所得，因而止息了爭奪。它也塑造情感。他說，喪禮是「稱情而立文」，使悲傷有一個形式、一個限度。他談「天」也同樣有原創性。「天行有常，不為堯存，不為桀亡。」天並不傳遞訊息。有人問，舉行求雨的祭祀之後下了雨，是為什麼？他回答：「無何也，猶不雩而雨也。」人們舉行這類儀式，是為了給自己的關切一個形式。「君子以為文，而百姓以為神。」治與亂來自人；而經營天所提供的東西，是我們自己的事。

quote.en: Heaven’s course is constant. It does not exist for the sake of Yao or perish because of Jie. Respond to it with order and there is good fortune. Respond to it with disorder and there is misfortune.
quote.zh: 天行有常，不為堯存，不為桀亡。應之以治則吉，應之以亂則凶。
quote.ref: Xunzi, chapter 17, “Discourse on Heaven,” translated for this series
quote.note_en: Yao was the best of the ancient kings and Jie the worst. Nature treats them alike.
quote.note_zh: 堯是古代最好的君王，桀是最壞的。自然對兩人一視同仁。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Where did the sages come from?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：聖人是從哪裡來的？

paras.en: If human nature is bad, the first sages had the same nature as everyone else, and it is hard to see how they could have invented goodness. Xunzi raises the objection himself and answers that the sages differed from others in accumulated thought and effort and were born with the same nature. A potter is no different in substance from the clay he shapes. Critics have not been satisfied. To want to bring order out of chaos, and to care enough to devise rites that nourish everyone, already looks like a good impulse, and if the sages had it by nature, then nature is not wholly bad. Mencius would say that Xunzi has smuggled the four sprouts back in under the name of intelligence.
paras.zh: 如果人性是惡的，那麼最初的聖人跟每個人有同樣的性；就很難看出他們怎麼能發明出善來。荀子自己提出了這個反駁，並且回答：聖人與別人不同的地方，在於積累的思慮與努力；他們生來的性是相同的。陶匠在本質上，跟他所塑造的陶土並無不同。批評者並沒有被滿足。想要從混亂中建立秩序、並且在乎到去制定「養」每一個人的禮，這看起來已經是一種善的衝動了；而如果聖人生來就有它，那麼性就不完全是惡的。孟子會說：荀子是用「知」的名義，把四端偷運了回來。

paras.en: The second objection is the one his students made by their careers. If people are moved by desire and goodness comes only from outside, the quickest way to good behavior is to arrange rewards and punishments, and moral education is a slow and uncertain detour. Han Fei drew that conclusion. Xunzi rejected it. He held that ritual transforms a person so that he comes to love what is right, and that a state run on fear, like Qin, has order without loyalty and will not last. On the facts he was proved correct within a generation. The question remains whether his premises entitled him to the hope.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁，是他的學生用他們的事業提出來的。如果人是被欲望推動的，而善只從外面來，那麼通往良好行為最快的路，就是安排賞與罰；而道德教化，是一條緩慢而沒有把握的彎路。韓非得出了那個結論。荀子拒絕了它。他主張，禮會轉化一個人，使他變得愛好「對的事」；而一個靠恐懼運作的國家，像秦那樣，有秩序而沒有忠誠，是不會長久的。就事實而言，不出一代，他就被證明是對的。留下來的問題是：他的那些前提，是否使他有資格抱這個希望？

problem.title_en: A book that was nearly lost to neglect
problem.title_zh: 一本差點因為被冷落而失傳的書

paras.en: Unlike the Analects and the Mencius, the Xunzi consists mostly of sustained essays on set topics, with titles such as “An Exhortation to Learning,” “Discourse on Heaven,” and “Dispelling Blindness,” and most scholars accept that the bulk of it is his own writing. That makes it the first book of philosophical prose in Chinese by a single author arguing a case from start to finish. The text was put in order by the Han librarian Liu Xiang, who reduced several hundred bundles of bamboo strips, many of them duplicates, to thirty-two chapters. A few of the later chapters are collections of sayings and stories that may come from his school.
paras.zh: 跟《論語》與《孟子》不同，《荀子》大部分是針對既定題目的長篇論文，題目像是〈勸學〉〈天論〉〈解蔽〉；多數學者接受，其中的主體是他自己寫的。這使它成為中文裡第一部由單一作者、從頭到尾論證一個主張的哲學散文著作。這個文本是漢代主管圖書的劉向整理的；他把好幾百捆竹簡（其中許多是重複的）刪定為三十二篇。較晚的幾篇是語錄與故事的彙編，可能出自他的學派。

paras.en: Because he fell out of favor, the book was little copied and received its first commentary only in 818 CE, more than a thousand years after it was written. Much of it was unread for long stretches, which has left the text in better condition than its reputation: few people cared enough to alter it.
paras.zh: 因為他失了寵，這本書很少被傳抄，直到西元 818 年才有了第一部註解；那已經是成書一千多年之後了。有很長的時間，它的大部分沒有人讀；這使文本的狀況比它的名聲更好：沒有多少人在乎到要去改動它。

said.claim: 「青出於藍而勝於藍」（荀子）
said.claim_zh: 「青出於藍而勝於藍」（荀子）
said.verdict_en: His image, later wording and a shifted meaning
said.verdict_zh: 是他的意象；措辭是後來的，意思也移動了
said.en: The proverb is used in Chinese of a student who surpasses his teacher. Xunzi’s sentence, the second in his book, runs: “Blue dye is taken from the indigo plant and is bluer than the plant.” The familiar wording with “surpasses” came later. More interesting is the change of meaning. Xunzi is not speaking of students and teachers. The indigo is a person’s raw nature, and the blue is what learning makes of it. His claim is that education can produce something better than what we are born with, which is the thesis of his whole philosophy.
said.zh: 這句成語在中文裡用來形容學生勝過了老師。荀子的原句（他書裡的第二句）是：「青，取之於藍，而青於藍。」帶著「勝」字的那個熟悉的措辭是後來才有的。更有意思的是意思的改變。荀子談的並不是學生與老師。「藍」是一個人未經加工的本性；「青」是學習把它造就成的東西。他的主張是：教育可以產出比我們生來所有的更好的東西；而那正是他整套哲學的論旨。

paras.en: Xunzi is the early Chinese philosopher closest to the Buddha in his picture of the untrained mind and in his trust in training. Both begin from desire as the source of conflict. Both hold that what we are at birth is unreliable and that a person is made by sustained practice, step upon step. Both strip the sky of moral agency: Xunzi’s Heaven that does not answer the rain sacrifice has a counterpart in the Buddha’s teaching that no rite, bath, or offering purifies a person and that only conduct does. And Xunzi’s account of how the mind comes to know the Way reads like a manual of meditation. The mind, he says, must be “empty, unified, and still.” Empty means that what one has already stored does not get in the way of what one is about to receive. Unified means that one thing is not allowed to disturb another. Still means that dreams and fancies do not disorder knowing.
paras.zh: 在早期的中國哲學家當中，荀子對「未經訓練的心」的描繪、以及他對訓練的信任，最接近佛陀。兩人都從「欲望是衝突的來源」出發。兩人都主張，我們生來的樣子靠不住；人是由持續的、一步一步的修習造就的。兩人都把道德上的作為從「天」那裡拿走：荀子那個不回應求雨祭祀的天，在佛陀那裡有對應：沒有任何儀式、沐浴或供品能淨化一個人，只有行為可以。而荀子說明「心如何認識道」的那一段，讀起來像一本禪修手冊。他說，心必須「虛壹而靜」。虛，是不讓已經收藏的東西妨礙將要接受的東西。壹，是不讓這一樣擾亂那一樣。靜，是不讓夢想與雜念攪亂了知。

paras.en: They part over what is to be done with desire. Xunzi’s rites exist to nourish desires, to give them objects in due measure so that wants and goods “sustain each other and grow.” He thought it foolish to try to reduce or remove desire, and criticized thinkers who proposed it. The Buddha holds that craving itself, however well regulated, is the root of suffering and can be brought to an end. Xunzi’s goal is a well-ordered society of people whose desires have been civilized. The Buddha’s is the release of a mind in which craving has ceased. The two could agree about the first precepts and the value of a rule of life, and would disagree about how far the training should go (Dharma and the West, D18 and D25).
paras.zh: 他們在「該拿欲望怎麼辦」上分道揚鑣。荀子的禮，存在的目的是「養」欲：給欲望有分寸的對象，使欲與物「相持而長」。他認為試圖減少或去除欲望是愚蠢的，並且批評過提出這種主張的思想家。佛陀主張：渴愛本身，不管調節得多好，都是苦的根，而且可以止息。荀子的目標，是一個由「欲望已經被教化」的人組成的井然有序的社會。佛陀的目標，是一顆渴愛已經止息的心的解脫。兩人可以在最初的幾條戒與「生活要有規矩」的價值上意見一致；而對於這個訓練該走多遠，則會意見分歧（佛法與西方哲學 D18、D25）。

terms.d_en: What is achieved by conscious human activity, as opposed to what is inborn.
terms.d_zh: 由有意識的人為活動所成就的東西，相對於天生的東西。

terms.d_en: For Xunzi, the system of forms and divisions devised by the sages to end contention and shape feeling.
terms.d_zh: 對荀子來說，是聖人為了止爭與塑造情感而制定的那一套形式與分別。

terms.d_en: The allotment of roles and shares that makes group life possible.
terms.d_zh: 使群體生活成為可能的角色與份額的分派。

terms.d_en: The piling up of small efforts by which character is formed.
terms.d_zh: 一點一點努力的堆積；品格由此養成。

terms.d_en: In Xunzi, the regular course of nature, which has no purposes and takes no sides.
terms.d_zh: 在荀子，指自然有常的運行；它沒有目的，也不偏袒誰。

terms.d_en: Freeing the mind from fixation on one part of the truth.
terms.d_zh: 使心不再執著於真理的某一部分。

quiz.q: What does Xunzi mean by saying that goodness is the product of deliberate effort?
options: It is achieved by learning and practice, against the pull of inborn desire.
It is a pretense.
It comes from Heaven.
It cannot be achieved.

quiz.q: What is his view of Heaven?
options: Nature runs a constant course and does not reward or punish.
Heaven rewards good kings with rain.
Heaven speaks through omens.
Heaven is the source of ritual.

quiz.q: Why did his reputation fall after the Song dynasty?
options: Because of his doctrine of human nature and the careers of his students Han Fei and Li Si.
Because his book was lost.
Because he opposed Confucius.
Because he supported the Mohists.

further.n_en: Begin with chapters 1, 17, 19, and 23.
further.n_zh: 從〈勸學〉〈天論〉〈禮論〉〈性惡〉讀起。

further.n_en: The standard English translation.
further.n_zh: 標準的英譯本。

further.n_zh: 他的傳與孟子同在一篇。
