philosophers.name: John Rawls
philosophers.place_zh: 巴爾的摩、普林斯頓與哈佛
philosophers.tag_en: A shy man with a stutter who spent twenty years on one book, and with it brought political philosophy back to the question of what a just society would be.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一個害羞、口吃的人，花了二十年寫一本書；而他用這本書，把政治哲學帶回到了「一個正義的社會會是什麼樣子」這個問題上。
facts: February 21, 1921, Baltimore, Maryland, the second of five sons
Princeton (BA 1943, PhD 1950); a year at Oxford
A Theory of Justice (1971), Political Liberalism (1993), The Law of Peoples (1999)

paras.en: John Rawls was born in Baltimore in 1921. His father was a prominent lawyer and his mother campaigned for women’s right to vote. In 1928, when he was seven, he caught diphtheria. His brother Bobby, twenty months younger, came into his room to keep him company, caught the disease, and died. The following winter Rawls had pneumonia. Another younger brother, Tommy, caught it from him and also died. Rawls recovered both times. He developed a stutter that stayed with him for life, and he himself connected it with these deaths.
paras.zh: 約翰・羅爾斯 1921 年生於巴爾的摩。他的父親是一位知名的律師；他的母親為婦女的投票權奔走。1928 年他七歲的時候，染上了白喉。比他小二十個月的弟弟巴比，進他的房間陪他，染上了這個病，死了。隔年冬天，羅爾斯得了肺炎。另一個弟弟湯米被他傳染，也死了。羅爾斯兩次都康復了。他從此有了口吃，跟了他一輩子；而他自己把它跟這兩次死亡連在一起。

paras.en: His biographer Thomas Pogge calls the loss of the brothers the most important events of his childhood. It is hard not to connect them with the idea that runs through his work: that who lives and who dies, who is gifted and who is not, who is born into which house, are matters of luck for which no one can take credit or blame. Rawls rarely spoke of it.
paras.zh: 他的傳記作者湯瑪斯・博格說，失去這兩個弟弟，是他童年最重要的事件。很難不把它們跟貫穿他著作的那個觀念連在一起：誰活、誰死，誰有天賦、誰沒有，誰生在哪一戶人家，都是運氣的事；沒有人能為此居功或受責。羅爾斯很少談起這件事。

paras.en: At Princeton he wrote an intensely religious senior thesis and thought of becoming an Episcopal priest. He graduated in 1943 and enlisted in the army. He served as an infantryman in New Guinea, where he was awarded the Bronze Star, and in the Philippines, where he saw heavy fighting. It was there that he lost his Christian faith. After Japan surrendered he was part of the occupying army and saw what was left of Hiroshima. He was promoted to sergeant. Then he refused an order to discipline a fellow soldier, because he believed that no punishment was justified, and he was demoted to private. He left the army in January 1946.
paras.zh: 在普林斯頓，他寫了一篇宗教情感濃烈的畢業論文，並且考慮過成為聖公會的牧師。他 1943 年畢業，隨即入伍。他在新幾內亞當步兵，在那裡獲頒銅星勳章；又到菲律賓，在那裡見到了激烈的戰鬥。他就是在那裡失去了基督信仰。日本投降之後，他隨佔領軍進駐，見到了廣島剩下來的樣子。他被升為中士。後來他拒絕執行一項懲處同袍的命令，因為他認為沒有任何懲罰是正當的；他被降回二等兵。1946 年 1 月，他離開了軍隊。

paras.en: He went back to Princeton for a doctorate in moral philosophy, and married Margaret Fox in 1949. They had four children. A year at Oxford in 1952 brought him into contact with Isaiah Berlin and the legal philosopher H. L. A. Hart. Fifty years after the bombing, in one of the few pieces he wrote for a general audience, he argued that the destruction of Hiroshima had been a grave wrong.
paras.zh: 他回到普林斯頓攻讀道德哲學的博士學位，並在 1949 年與瑪格麗特・福克斯結婚。他們有四個孩子。1952 年在牛津的一年，使他接觸到以撒・柏林與法哲學家哈特。原爆五十年後，在他為一般讀者寫的少數幾篇文章之一裡，他主張摧毀廣島是一個嚴重的錯誤。

paras.en: He taught at Cornell and at MIT, and in 1962 moved to Harvard, where he remained until he retired. In 1958 he had published a paper called “Justice as Fairness.” He spent the next thirteen years turning it into a book, circulating drafts among students and colleagues and rewriting in response. A Theory of Justice appeared in 1971. Its preface begins, “This is a long book, not only in pages.” At the time many philosophers believed that their subject could say nothing substantive about how society should be arranged. The book changed that. Nozick, who disagreed with nearly all of it, wrote that political philosophers must now either work within Rawls’s theory or explain why not.
paras.zh: 他在康乃爾與麻省理工任教；1962 年轉到哈佛，在那裡一直待到退休。1958 年，他發表了一篇論文，題為〈作為公平的正義〉。接下來的十三年，他把它變成一本書：把草稿傳給學生與同事看，再根據回應重寫。《正義論》在 1971 年問世。它的序言開頭是：「這是一本很長的書，不只是頁數上。」當時許多哲學家相信，他們這門學問對於「社會應該怎麼安排」說不出任何實質的東西。這本書改變了這一點。幾乎完全不同意它的諾齊克寫道：政治哲學家現在要嘛在羅爾斯的理論之內工作，要嘛解釋為什麼不。

paras.en: Fame did not change his habits. He gave almost no interviews and described himself as having a horror of the limelight. Students remember a teacher who took careful notes on what they said and presented the philosophers he lectured on in their strongest form. In 1989 student protesters in Tiananmen Square held up copies of his book. In 1999 he received the National Humanities Medal. A series of strokes from 1995 slowed his work, and he died at home in Lexington, Massachusetts, in 2002, aged eighty-one.
paras.zh: 名聲並沒有改變他的習慣。他幾乎不接受訪問，並且形容自己對鎂光燈有一種恐懼。學生記得的是這樣一位老師：他仔細記下他們說的話；講到哪一位哲學家，就以那位哲學家最強的形式來呈現。1989 年，天安門廣場上抗議的學生舉起了他的書。1999 年，他獲頒美國國家人文獎章。從 1995 年開始的一連串中風，拖慢了他的工作；2002 年，他在麻薩諸塞州萊辛頓的家中去世，享年八十一歲。

timeline: Two younger brothers die of illnesses caught from him
兩個弟弟被他傳染而病逝
With the occupying army in Japan, sees Hiroshima
隨佔領軍到日本，見到廣島
在普林斯頓取得哲學博士

idea.title_en: The central idea: Justice as fairness
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：作為公平的正義

paras.en: Rawls begins from a conviction: “Each person possesses an inviolability founded on justice that even the welfare of society as a whole cannot override.” Utilitarianism, the leading theory of his day, could not explain this. If only the total of happiness matters, the suffering of a few may be outweighed by the gains of many. Rawls wanted a theory in which each person counts separately. He found it in the old idea of the social contract, which he made more abstract. Principles are just if free and equal people would agree to them in a fair situation. He described that situation as an original position in which the parties stand behind a veil of ignorance: “no one knows his place in society, his class position or social status; nor does he know his fortune in the distribution of natural assets and abilities.”
paras.zh: 羅爾斯從一個信念出發：「每一個人都擁有一種基於正義的不可侵犯性，即使是整個社會的福利也不能凌駕其上。」他那個時代的主流理論是功利主義；而它解釋不了這一點。如果只有幸福的總量要緊，那麼少數人的痛苦就可以被多數人的得益蓋過去。羅爾斯要的是一個「每個人各別算數」的理論。他在社會契約這個古老的觀念裡找到了它，並且把它變得更抽象。如果自由而平等的人會在一個公平的情境裡同意某些原則，這些原則就是正義的。他把那個情境描述為一個「原初立場」，其中的各方都站在一道無知之幕的後面：「沒有人知道自己在社會裡的位置、階級地位或社會身分；他也不知道自己在天生資質與能力的分配上運氣如何。」

paras.en: From that position, he argued, two principles would be chosen, and in a fixed order. First, equal basic liberties for all, which may not be traded for economic gain. Second, fair equality of opportunity, and inequalities only where they benefit the least advantaged. He did not claim to have deduced these from nothing. His method, which he called reflective equilibrium, is to move back and forth between principles and our firmest particular judgments, such as that slavery is unjust, adjusting each to the other until they fit. Behind the principles is a view of society as a fair system of cooperation over generations, in which the lucky and the unlucky share one another’s fate.
paras.zh: 他主張，從那個位置會選出兩條原則，而且有固定的先後順序。第一，人人享有平等的基本自由；它們不可以拿來交換經濟上的好處。第二，公平的機會平等；以及只有在對最不利者有好處的地方，才容許不平等。他並沒有宣稱這些是他憑空演繹出來的。他的方法，他稱之為「反思的均衡」：在原則與我們最堅定的個別判斷（例如「奴隸制是不正義的」）之間來回移動，互相調整，直到兩者相符。在這些原則的背後，是把社會看成一個跨越世代的公平合作體系；在其中，幸運的人與不幸的人分擔彼此的命運。

quote.en: Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought.
quote.zh: 正義是社會制度的首要德性，正如真理是思想體系的首要德性。
quote.ref: A Theory of Justice (1971), section 1
quote.note_en: The first sentence of the argument. He goes on: a theory however elegant must be rejected if it is untrue, and laws however efficient must be reformed if they are unjust.
quote.note_zh: 整個論證的第一句。他接著說：一個理論不管多麼優雅，如果不真，就必須拒絕；法律不管多麼有效率，如果不正義，就必須改革。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Whose veil?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：誰的幕？

paras.en: The objection that troubled Rawls most came from critics such as Michael Sandel, who are often called communitarians. The parties behind the veil know nothing of their religion, their family, or their idea of a good life. Sandel argued that such a chooser is no one in particular, and that the choice is rigged from the start in favor of a liberal view on which people are, at bottom, independent choosers and their attachments are optional. For most people, their faith or their duty to their parents is part of who they are. Asking them to set it aside when they reason about justice, he said, is taking a side.
paras.zh: 最讓羅爾斯困擾的反駁，來自桑德爾這樣的批評者；他們常被稱為社群主義者。幕後的各方對自己的宗教、家庭，或自己對美好人生的想法一無所知。桑德爾主張：這樣的一個選擇者，誰也不是；而這個選擇從一開始就被動了手腳，偏向一種自由主義的看法：人在根本上是獨立的選擇者，他們的種種牽繫都是可有可無的。對大多數人來說，他們的信仰、或他們對父母的責任，是「他們是誰」的一部分。他說，要求他們在推理正義的時候把它擱在一邊，本身就是選了邊。

paras.en: Rawls took the point seriously enough to write a second book. In Political Liberalism he no longer presented justice as fairness as the truth about morality. He presented it as a basis on which citizens who disagree deeply about religion and the good can still live together on terms each can accept from within his own tradition. He called this an overlapping consensus. Critics on the other side, such as G. A. Cohen, thought he had conceded too much, and that a theory of justice should say what is right whether or not everyone can be brought to accept it.
paras.zh: 羅爾斯很認真地看待這一點，認真到寫了第二本書。在《政治自由主義》裡，他不再把「作為公平的正義」當作關於道德的真理來提出。他把它提出來，當作一個基礎：在宗教與善的問題上有深刻分歧的公民，仍然可以在這個基礎上共同生活，而其條件是每個人從自己的傳統內部都能接受的。他稱之為「交疊共識」。另一邊的批評者，例如柯亨，認為他讓步太多了；他們認為，一個正義理論應該說出什麼是對的，不管是不是每個人都能被帶到接受它。

problem.title_zh: 只給一個國家用的理論？

paras.en: The veil hides a person’s class and talents. Many readers expected that it would also hide his nationality. Being born in a poor country is as much a matter of luck as being born into a poor family, and it affects a life far more. Philosophers who had learned from Rawls, among them Thomas Pogge and Charles Beitz, drew what seemed the obvious conclusion: the difference principle should apply to the whole world.
paras.zh: 那道幕遮住了一個人的階級與才能。許多讀者預期，它也會遮住他的國籍。生在一個窮國，跟生在一個窮人家一樣是運氣的事；而它對一生的影響大得多。向羅爾斯學過的哲學家，其中有博格與貝茲，得出了那個看起來很明顯的結論：差異原則應該用在全世界。

paras.en: Rawls refused. In The Law of Peoples he argued that justice as fairness is a theory for a single society whose members share institutions and take part in governing them. Between peoples he proposed a shorter list of duties: to respect human rights, to refrain from aggressive war, and to assist societies burdened by unfavorable conditions until they can manage their own affairs. He set no continuing duty to reduce inequality between nations. Whether this was sound realism about what distant peoples can owe one another, or a failure to follow his own argument, is still disputed (Big Questions A24).
paras.zh: 羅爾斯拒絕了。在《萬民法》裡，他主張「作為公平的正義」是給單一社會用的理論；這個社會的成員共享著制度，並且參與治理它們。在各個民族之間，他提出的是一張比較短的義務清單：尊重人權、不發動侵略戰爭；以及協助那些被不利條件拖累的社會，直到它們能管理自己的事務為止。他沒有設下一個持續縮小國與國之間不平等的義務。這究竟是對「遙遠的民族之間能彼此欠什麼」的穩健現實感，還是沒有把自己的論證貫徹到底，至今仍有爭議（大哉問 A24）。

said.claim: “Rawls invented the veil of ignorance.”
said.claim_zh: 「無知之幕是羅爾斯發明的。」
said.verdict_en: His name for it; the device is older
said.verdict_zh: 名字是他取的；這個設計比較早
said.en: The phrase is Rawls’s, and so is the use of the device to derive principles of justice from a contract. The idea of judging a society by asking which one you would choose without knowing your place in it had been used by economists before him. William Vickrey sketched it in 1945, and John Harsanyi developed it in papers of 1953 and 1955, reaching a utilitarian conclusion. Rawls knew this work and discusses it. Older relatives include Adam Smith’s impartial spectator and Kant’s test of asking whether one’s rule could hold for everyone. Rawls added the thick veil, which hides even the odds, and the claim that behind it one would refuse to gamble.
said.zh: 這個詞是羅爾斯的；用這個設計從契約推導出正義原則，也是他的。至於「問你在不知道自己位置的情況下會選哪一個社會，用這個方法來評判社會」的想法，在他之前已經有經濟學家用過。威廉・維克里在 1945 年勾勒過它；約翰・海薩尼在 1953 與 1955 年的論文裡發展了它，並得出功利主義的結論。羅爾斯知道這些研究，也討論了它們。更早的親戚，包括亞當・斯密的「公正的旁觀者」，以及康德的檢驗：問自己的準則能不能對每個人都成立。羅爾斯加上的，是那道厚的幕，連機率都遮住；以及這個主張：在它的後面，人會拒絕賭博。

paras.en: The veil of ignorance is an exercise in thinking without “I” and “mine.” For the length of one argument a person sets aside his name, his family, his advantages, and his interests, and asks what would be good from no position in particular. Buddhist training aims at something similar as a lasting change. The meditations on loving-kindness extend to all beings the wish one naturally has for oneself, and the teaching of non-self holds that the line we draw around “my” welfare has no ultimate basis. Śāntideva’s argument that suffering should be removed simply because it is suffering, whoever’s it is, would be at home behind the veil (Dharma and Western Philosophy D19).
paras.zh: 無知之幕，是一個不帶著「我」與「我的」來思考的練習。在一個論證的時間裡，一個人把自己的名字、家庭、優勢與利益擱在一邊，問：不從任何特定的位置來看，什麼是好的？佛教的修習要達成的，是類似的東西，而且是持久的改變。慈心的修習，把一個人自然為自己懷有的願望，擴及一切眾生；而無我的教導主張：我們繞著「我的」福祉劃出的那條線，沒有究竟的根據。寂天的論證是：苦應當被除去，只因為它是苦，不管是誰的；這個論證放在那道幕的後面，再合適不過（佛法與西方哲學 D19）。

paras.en: They differ on luck. For Rawls, where and to whom a person is born is arbitrary, and justice is largely the work of correcting for it. In the Buddhist account birth is connected with past action, and so it is not arbitrary. The two views come apart less in practice than one might expect. The Buddha denied that birth fixes a person’s worth: “You’re not a lowlife by birth, nor by birth are you a brahmin. You’re a lowlife by your deeds, by deeds you’re a brahmin.” He admitted people of every class to his community on equal terms. And the tradition does not treat a person’s past as a reason for others to withhold help. They differ more deeply in aim. Rawls asks what institutions free and equal citizens could accept. The Buddha asks how a person comes to stop grasping at a share at all.
paras.zh: 他們在運氣上不同。對羅爾斯來說，一個人生在哪裡、生給誰，是任意的；而正義大體上就是矯正它的工作。照佛教的說法，出生與過去的行為有關，所以不是任意的。這兩種看法在實踐上的分歧，比人們預期的小。佛陀否認出身決定一個人的價值：「不因出身而成為賤民，不因出身而成為婆羅門；因行為而成為賤民，因行為而成為婆羅門。」他以平等的條件，接納每一個階級的人進入他的僧團。而且這個傳統並不把一個人的過去，當成別人可以不伸出援手的理由。他們更深的不同在目標上。羅爾斯問的是：自由而平等的公民能接受什麼樣的制度？佛陀問的是：一個人怎麼樣才不再抓取自己的那一份？

terms.d_en: Rawls’s name for his theory: just principles are those that would be agreed to in a fair situation.
terms.d_zh: 羅爾斯為自己的理論取的名字：正義的原則，就是會在一個公平的情境裡被同意的那些原則。

terms.d_en: The imagined situation of choice behind the veil of ignorance.
terms.d_zh: 在無知之幕後面的那個設想中的選擇情境。

terms.d_en: Things every person is presumed to want whatever else he wants: liberties, opportunities, income, and the bases of self-respect.
terms.d_zh: 不管一個人還要什麼，都被推定為想要的東西：自由、機會、收入，以及自尊的基礎。

terms.d_en: The state reached when one’s principles and one’s considered judgments have been adjusted to fit each other.
terms.d_zh: 一個人的原則與他深思過的判斷，經過互相調整而相符時所達到的狀態。

terms.d_en: Agreement on political principles among people who hold different religious and moral views, each for his own reasons.
terms.d_zh: 抱持不同宗教與道德觀的人，各自基於自己的理由，對政治原則達成的共識。

terms.d_en: The main institutions of a society taken together: its constitution, economy, property law, and family.
terms.d_zh: 一個社會的主要制度合在一起：它的憲法、經濟、財產法與家庭。

quiz.q: What does the veil of ignorance hide from the parties?
options: Their own class, talents, and idea of the good life.
The general facts of economics and psychology.
The fact that they live in a society.
The meaning of the word justice.

quiz.q: Why did Rawls reject utilitarianism?
options: It allows the suffering of a few to be outweighed by the gains of many.
It pays too little attention to happiness.
It was unpopular in his day.
It depends on a social contract.

quiz.q: How did Rawls change his theory in Political Liberalism?
options: He presented it as a basis for agreement among citizens with different deep beliefs, and no longer as the whole truth about morality.
He gave up the two principles.
He extended the difference principle to the whole world.
He adopted Nozick’s entitlement theory.

further.n_en: Read sections 1–4, 11–13, and 24 first.

further.t: John Rawls, Justice as Fairness: A Restatement (2001)
further.n_en: His own short version, written late, with replies to critics.
further.n_zh: 他晚年自己寫的短版本，附有對批評者的回應。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “John Rawls”
further.n_en: The best free overview of all three books.
further.n_zh: 涵蓋三本書的最佳免費概述。

further.t: Thomas Pogge, John Rawls: His Life and Theory of Justice (2007)
further.n_en: A short life by a former student, followed by a clear account of the theory.
further.n_zh: 一位昔日學生寫的簡短傳記，後面接著對這個理論的清楚說明。

philosophers.name: Laozi
philosophers.greek: 李耳 Li Er, 老聃 Lao Dan
philosophers.tag_en: An archivist who may never have existed, credited with five thousand characters on the Way that have been translated more often than any other Chinese book.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位也許從來不曾存在的史官；人們把談「道」的五千個字歸在他名下，而這五千字被翻譯的次數，超過任何一本中文書。
facts: By tradition the 6th century BCE, in Ku county in the state of Chu
Unknown. Sima Qian: “no one knows where he ended”
Li Er 李耳, courtesy name Dan 聃. Laozi means “the Old Master”
Keeper of the archives at the Zhou court
Daodejing 道德經, about 5,000 characters in 81 chapters
Guodian bamboo slips (c. 300 BCE); Mawangdui silk manuscripts (before 168 BCE)

paras.en: Almost everything said about Laozi’s life comes from one page written by the historian Sima Qian about 100 BCE, and Sima Qian was not sure of it himself. According to that page, Laozi was a man of Chu named Li Er who served as keeper of the archives at the court of Zhou. Confucius traveled to Zhou to ask him about ritual. The old man was not encouraging. The people you talk about, he said, have rotted along with their bones, and only their words remain. “Get rid of your proud airs and your many desires, your fine manner and your excessive ambitions. None of them is of any use to you. That is all I have to tell you.”
paras.zh: 關於老子生平的說法，幾乎全部來自史家司馬遷在大約公元前 100 年寫下的一頁；而司馬遷自己對它也沒有把握。照那一頁的說法，老子是楚國人，名叫李耳，在周的朝廷擔任守藏室之史。孔子到周去向他問禮。老人並沒有鼓勵他。他說：「子所言者，其人與骨皆已朽矣，獨其言在耳。……去子之驕氣與多欲，態色與淫志，是皆無益於子之身。吾所以告子，若是而已。」

paras.en: Confucius went back and told his disciples: “Birds, I know, can fly. Fish can swim. Animals can run. For what runs there are nets, for what swims there are lines, for what flies there are arrows. But the dragon I cannot understand. It rides the wind and the clouds and rises into the sky. Today I have seen Laozi, and he is like a dragon.” The story is almost certainly a later invention, and it was told with relish by Daoists because it shows the founder of the rival school at a loss.
paras.zh: 孔子回去之後，對弟子們說：「鳥，吾知其能飛；魚，吾知其能游；獸，吾知其能走。走者可以為罔，游者可以為綸，飛者可以為矰。至於龍，吾不能知其乘風雲而上天。吾今日見老子，其猶龍邪！」這個故事幾乎可以確定是後來編的；道家講得津津有味，因為它讓對手學派的創始人不知所措。

paras.en: Sima Qian goes on. Laozi cultivated the Way and its power, and “his teaching aimed at self-concealment and namelessness.” After living long in Zhou he saw that the dynasty was in decline and left. At the western pass the keeper, Yin Xi, stopped him and said: “You are about to withdraw from the world. Force yourself to write a book for me.” So Laozi wrote a book in two parts, setting out the meaning of the Way and its power in something over five thousand characters, and departed. “No one knows where he ended.”
paras.zh: 司馬遷接著說：老子修道德，「其學以自隱無名為務」。他在周住了很久，見到周的衰落，就離開了。到了西邊的關口，關令尹喜攔住他說：「子將隱矣，彊為我著書。」於是老子寫了上下兩篇的書，「言道德之意五千餘言而去，莫知其所終」。

paras.en: The scene has been painted for two thousand years: an old man on an ox, leaving civilization behind and handing a manuscript to a border guard. It suits the book so well that it is hard to believe. A man who taught that those who know do not speak is made to write by a customs officer, and then vanishes before anyone can ask him what he meant.
paras.zh: 這個場景被畫了兩千年：一個老人騎在牛背上，把文明留在身後，把一份手稿交給一位守邊的官吏。它跟那本書配得太好，好到令人難以相信。一個教人「知者不言」的人，被一位關吏逼著寫作；然後在任何人來得及問他是什麼意思之前，就消失了。

paras.en: Sima Qian then does something unusual for a biographer. He admits that he does not know who his subject was. Some say, he reports, that Laozi was a certain Lao Laizi, also of Chu. Some say he was Dan, a Zhou historian who visited the court of Qin one hundred and twenty-nine years after Confucius died. Some say he lived to be more than a hundred and sixty. “No one in the world knows whether this is so or not. Laozi was a gentleman in hiding.”
paras.zh: 接著，司馬遷做了一件對傳記作者來說很不尋常的事。他承認自己不知道傳主是誰。他記載：有人說，老子就是某位也是楚人的老萊子。有人說，他就是周太史儋，在孔子死後一百二十九年見過秦獻公。有人說，他活了一百六十多歲。「世莫知其然否。老子，隱君子也。」

paras.en: Modern scholars mostly think that the book grew over time from a body of sayings and took something like its present form in the fourth or third century BCE. Two finds changed the discussion. In 1973 two silk copies were recovered from a tomb at Mawangdui sealed in 168 BCE. They place the second half of the book, on de, before the first, on dao. In 1993 bamboo slips from a tomb at Guodian, closed about 300 BCE, were found to contain about a third of the text in a different order, which shows that much of it was already circulating by then. In later centuries Laozi became a god. The Tang emperors, who shared his surname Li, claimed him as their ancestor.
paras.zh: 現代學者大多認為：這本書是從一批格言隨著時間長成的，在公元前四世紀或三世紀有了大致接近今天的樣子。有兩次出土改變了這個討論。1973 年，從公元前 168 年封閉的馬王堆墓裡，取出了兩份帛書抄本。它們把書的後半（談「德」）放在前半（談「道」）之前。1993 年，在大約公元前 300 年封閉的郭店墓裡發現的竹簡，含有大約三分之一的文本，順序也不同；這顯示其中許多內容當時已經在流傳了。在後來的世紀裡，老子成了神。唐代的皇帝與他同姓李，尊他為祖先。

idea.title_en: The central idea: The way of water
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：水的道

paras.en: The book begins by warning the reader about books: “The way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way.” The Dao is the source and pattern of everything. It cannot be defined, since any definition marks off one thing from another, and the Dao is prior to all such divisions. What can be done is to observe how it works. It works without effort and without claiming credit: it “gives birth and does not possess, acts and does not presume.” Its movement is reversal. Whatever is pushed to an extreme turns into its opposite, so that “misfortune is what fortune leans on, and fortune is where misfortune hides.”
paras.zh: 這本書一開頭就警告讀者提防書本：「道可道，非常道。」道是一切事物的源頭與模式。它無法被定義；因為任何定義都是把一樣東西從另一樣東西劃分出來，而道先於所有這樣的劃分。能做的，是觀察它怎麼運作。它運作起來不費力，也不居功：「生而不有，為而不恃」。它的運動是「反」。任何被推到極端的東西，都會轉成它的反面；所以「禍兮福之所倚，福兮禍之所伏」。

paras.en: From this Laozi draws a way of acting that he calls wuwei, non-action. It does not mean doing nothing. It means not forcing: “The pursuit of learning adds something every day. The pursuit of the Way takes something away every day. Take away and take away again, until you reach non-action. Do nothing, and nothing is left undone.” His favorite image is water, which is soft, seeks the low places everyone else avoids, and wears down rock. His second image is emptiness. Thirty spokes meet at a hub, and the cart is useful because the hub has a hole in it. A pot is useful because it is hollow. The same holds for a ruler. The best ruler is one whose people barely know that he exists, and when his work is done, they say, “We did it ourselves.”
paras.zh: 由此，老子引出了一種行動的方式，他稱之為「無為」。它的意思不是什麼都不做。它的意思是不強求：「為學日益，為道日損。損之又損，以至於無為。無為而無不為。」他最愛的意象是水：柔弱，往人人都避開的低處去，卻能磨穿石頭。他的第二個意象是空。三十根輻條共用一個轂；車之所以有用，是因為轂的中間是空的。陶器之所以有用，是因為它是中空的。統治者也一樣。最好的統治者，人民幾乎不知道有他；等到事情辦成了，百姓都說：「我自然。」

quote.en: The highest good is like water. Water benefits the ten thousand things and does not contend. It stays in the places that people dislike, and so it is close to the Way.
quote.zh: 上善若水。水善利萬物而不爭，處眾人之所惡，故幾於道。
quote.ref: Daodejing, chapter 8, translated for this series
quote.note_en: Chapter 78 completes the thought: nothing in the world is softer or weaker than water, and nothing is better at attacking what is hard and strong.
quote.note_zh: 第七十八章把這個想法說完：「天下莫柔弱於水，而攻堅強者，莫之能勝。」

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Yielding as a weapon
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：把退讓當武器

paras.en: The book can be read as a manual of manipulation. “If you want to shrink something, you must first stretch it. If you want to weaken something, you must first strengthen it. If you want to take, you must first give.” The Legalist Han Fei, who wrote the earliest surviving commentary on it, took such lines as advice to a ruler on how to conceal his intentions and let his rivals overreach. On this reading softness is a tactic and the sage a patient schemer. The chapters on government give the reading some support. The ruler is to keep the people’s minds empty and their bellies full, and the ancients who “did not enlighten the people but kept them simple” are praised.
paras.zh: 這本書可以被讀成一本操縱術的手冊。「將欲歙之，必固張之；將欲弱之，必固強之……將欲奪之，必固與之。」法家的韓非寫了現存最早的一部解說；他把這樣的句子，當作給統治者的建議：如何隱藏自己的意圖，讓對手自己做過頭。照這種讀法，柔弱是一種戰術，而聖人是一個有耐心的謀略家。談治國的幾章，給了這種讀法一些支持。統治者要讓人民「虛其心，實其腹」；而「非以明民，將以愚之」的古人，受到了稱讚。

paras.en: Xunzi made a different complaint: “Laozi saw the value of bending and did not see the value of stretching out.” A doctrine that always advises retreat has nothing to say to someone who must build a dam or resist an invader. Defenders reply that the book is a correction addressed to rulers who were doing far too much, and was never meant as a complete ethics, and that the simplicity it praises is freedom from artificial desires, which it does not confuse with stupidity. The text is brief enough and dark enough that both sides can quote it.
paras.zh: 荀子的抱怨不一樣：「老子有見於詘，無見於信。」（他看到了「屈」的價值，沒有看到「伸」的價值。）一個總是勸人後退的學說，對一個必須築壩或抵抗侵略的人，無話可說。辯護者回答：這本書是對「做得太多太多」的統治者的矯正，從來就不打算是一套完整的倫理學；而它所稱讚的「樸」，是擺脫人為造作的欲望，它並沒有把這個跟愚笨混為一談。這個文本夠短，也夠隱晦，雙方都能引用它。

paras.en: Classical Chinese marks neither tense nor number and often leaves out the subject, and the Daodejing uses these freedoms more than any other early text. Its first line has six characters, three of which are the same word used as noun and verb. A translator has to supply what the original leaves open, and each one supplies something different. There are several hundred versions in English alone. Some of the best known were made by writers who could not read Chinese and worked from earlier translations. A reader with no Chinese should compare at least two versions by scholars and should distrust any that reads too smoothly.
paras.zh: 文言文既不標示時態，也不標示單複數，還常常省略主詞；而《道德經》比任何其他的早期文本，都更充分地利用了這些自由。它的第一句有六個字，其中三個是同一個字，分別當名詞與動詞用。譯者必須補上原文留白的東西；而每一位補的都不一樣。光是英文就有好幾百個版本。其中最出名的幾個，出自不能讀中文、只是根據更早的譯本來改寫的作家之手。不懂中文的讀者，至少應該比較兩個出自學者之手的版本；而且應該對任何讀起來太順的版本保持懷疑。

paras.en: The manuscripts add a further difficulty. The received text, fixed by the commentator Wang Bi in the third century CE, differs in many places from the Mawangdui and Guodian copies. In chapter 17 Wang Bi’s text says of the best ruler that those below “know that he exists.” Other versions read “do not know that he exists.” One character separates a ruler who is discreet from one who is invisible. There is no original to appeal to. The Daodejing, like its author, exists as a family of versions.
paras.zh: 抄本又添了一層困難。通行本是由注釋者王弼在公元三世紀確定的；它在許多地方與馬王堆、郭店的抄本不同。在第十七章，王弼本說到最好的統治者時是「下知有之」。別的版本作「不知有之」。一字之差，分開了一位低調的統治者，與一位看不見的統治者。沒有一個「原本」可以訴諸。《道德經》就像它的作者一樣，是以一整個家族的版本存在的。

said.claim: “Give a man a fish and you feed him for a day. Teach a man to fish and you feed him for a lifetime.” (Laozi)
said.claim_zh: 「給他一條魚，你餵他一天；教他釣魚，你餵他一輩子。」（老子）
said.en: The saying is attributed to Laozi all over the internet, and sometimes to Confucius or Maimonides. Nothing like it appears in the Daodejing, which shows little interest in teaching people skills and says that the more skills men acquire, the more strange things appear. The English proverb has been traced to the nineteenth century. An early form is in a novel of 1885 by Anne Thackeray Ritchie. The Chinese version 授人以魚不如授人以漁 is modern in that wording. A real line of Laozi’s that became a proverb is in chapter 64: “A journey of a thousand li begins beneath the feet.” English usually renders it as “a single step.”
said.zh: 這句話在網路上到處被歸給老子，有時候被歸給孔子或邁蒙尼德。《道德經》裡沒有任何類似的話；這本書對教人技能沒什麼興趣，還說「人多伎巧，奇物滋起」。這句英文諺語可以追溯到十九世紀。它較早的一個形式，出現在安妮・薩克萊・里奇 1885 年的一部小說裡。中文的「授人以魚不如授人以漁」，就這個措辭而言是現代的。一句真正出自老子、後來成了諺語的話，在第六十四章：「千里之行，始於足下。」英文通常譯成「一步」（a single step）。

paras.en: When Buddhism reached China in the first centuries CE, its translators borrowed Laozi’s vocabulary because they had no other. Dharma and bodhi were rendered as dao. Nirvana was rendered as wuwei. The practice of explaining Buddhist ideas through Daoist ones was called “matching meanings,” and later translators worked hard to undo it. A legend even grew up that Laozi, after leaving through the pass, had traveled to India and become the Buddha. The borrowing was not arbitrary. Both teachers distrust words, since the Way that can be spoken of is not the constant Way and nirvana is said to be beyond description. Both locate the trouble in desire. And both recommend letting go where the world recommends holding on: “the sage does not grasp, and so does not lose.”
paras.zh: 佛教在公元最初的幾個世紀傳到中國時，譯者借用了老子的詞彙，因為他們沒有別的可用。Dharma 與 bodhi 被譯成「道」。Nirvāṇa 被譯成「無為」。用道家的觀念來解釋佛教觀念的做法，叫做「格義」；後來的譯者花了很大的力氣才把它解開。甚至還長出了一個傳說：老子出關之後，到了印度，成了佛陀。這種借用並不是任意的。兩位老師都不信任語言：可以說出來的道不是常道；而涅槃被說成是言語道斷的。兩人都把毛病定位在欲望。而在世人勸人抓緊的地方，兩人都勸人放手：「聖人……無執故無失。」

paras.en: The differences were just as real, and Chinese Buddhists came to insist on them. Laozi’s Dao is a source from which the ten thousand things are born and to which they return. The Buddha taught dependent arising, in which there is no first source at all. Laozi advises having few desires and returning to simplicity, and his goal is a long, unharmed life in accord with nature. The Buddha’s goal is the complete ending of craving and release from the round of birth, which he did not regard as a home to return to. And Laozi has no path: no precepts, no stages of meditation, no account of how the mind is trained. Chan Buddhism is often described as what happened when the two met, with its distrust of scripture taken from one side and its discipline from the other (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18, D25).
paras.zh: 差異也同樣真實；而中國的佛教徒後來堅持這些差異。老子的道是一個源頭：萬物由它而生，又回到它那裡。佛陀教的是緣起；其中根本沒有第一個源頭。老子勸人「少私寡欲」、「見素抱樸」；他的目標是順應自然、長久而不受傷害的一生。佛陀的目標是渴愛的完全止息，以及從生死輪迴裡解脫；他並不把那個輪迴看成一個該回去的家。此外，老子沒有道次第：沒有戒，沒有禪定的階段，也沒有說明心是怎麼訓練的。禪宗常被描述為這兩者相遇之後發生的事：對經典的不信任取自一邊，修行的紀律取自另一邊（佛法與西方哲學 D18、D25）。

terms.d_en: The source and pattern of all things, which cannot be named.
terms.d_zh: 萬物的源頭與模式；無法命名。

terms.d_en: The Way as it is present and effective in a particular thing or person.
terms.d_zh: 道在某一個具體的事物或人身上的呈現與作用。

terms.d_en: Acting without forcing or contending.
terms.d_zh: 不強求、不爭的行動方式。

terms.d_en: What is so of itself, without being made so from outside.
terms.d_zh: 自己如此，不是由外面使它如此。

terms.d_en: Simplicity, the state of a thing before it has been cut into shape.
terms.d_zh: 素樸；一樣東西還沒有被削成形狀之前的狀態。

terms.d_en: The tendency of anything pushed to an extreme to turn into its opposite.
terms.d_zh: 任何被推到極端的東西轉成其反面的傾向。

quiz.q: What does wuwei mean in the Daodejing?
options: Acting without forcing.
Refusing to act at all.
Obeying the ruler.
Seeking long life through medicine.

quiz.q: Why does Laozi praise water?
options: It is soft, seeks the low places, and overcomes what is hard.
It is the most expensive of things.
It always flows upward.
It was sacred to the Zhou kings.

quiz.q: What did the Mawangdui and Guodian finds show?
options: That the text circulated early, in more than one form and order.
That Laozi wrote the book in a single night.
That the book was first written in Sanskrit.
That Confucius was its real author.

further.n_en: The received Chinese text with an older English translation alongside.
further.n_zh: 通行本中文原文，旁附一個較早的英譯。

further.n_en: Sima Qian’s page on Laozi, doubts included.
further.n_zh: 司馬遷寫老子的那一頁，連同他的疑問。

further.t: D. C. Lau, Tao Te Ching (Penguin Classics, 1963)
further.n_en: A sober scholarly translation with a good introduction.
further.n_zh: 一個持重的學術譯本，導論很好。

further.n_zh: 談年代、抄本，以及主要的幾條詮釋路線。

philosophers.name: Han Feizi
philosophers.tag_en: A prince with a stutter who wrote the clearest account of power in Chinese, was admired by the king who would become the First Emperor, and died in that king’s prison.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位口吃的公子；他寫下了中文裡對權力最清晰的說明，受到後來成為始皇帝的那位秦王的讚賞，而死在那位秦王的監獄裡。
facts: c. 280 BCE, a prince of the ruling house of Han
233 BCE, in prison in Qin, by poison
Xunzi. His fellow student was Li Si
Legalism 法家, which he brought to its final form
A stutter that kept him from speaking at court, and the best prose of his age

life.h_en: The prince who could not speak

paras.en: Han Fei was born about 280 BCE into the royal family of Han, the smallest and most exposed of the seven warring states, with the rising power of Qin on its western border. Sima Qian records two facts about the man himself. He “stuttered and could not present his views in speech, but was good at writing books.” And he studied under Xunzi together with Li Si, who “considered himself not the equal of Fei.” From Xunzi he took the view that people are moved by self-interest. He did not take the conclusion that they can be remade by ritual and learning.
paras.zh: 韓非大約在公元前 280 年生於韓國的王室。韓是戰國七雄當中最小、處境最危險的一個；西邊就是崛起中的秦。關於這個人本身，司馬遷記了兩件事。他「為人口吃，不能道說，而善著書」。他與李斯一同在荀子門下求學，而李斯「自以為不如非」。他從荀子那裡接受了「人是被自利推動的」這個看法。他沒有接受那個結論：人可以經由禮與學被重新塑造。

paras.en: He watched his state grow weaker and several times wrote to its king with advice. The king did not use it. Han Fei was angry, the historian says, that the ruler did not clarify the laws, use his position to control his ministers, and enrich the state and strengthen the army, and that he instead honored “vermin” who lived on reputation and fine words. Since he could not speak at court and was not heeded when he wrote to it, he wrote for readers he would never meet: essays called “Solitary Indignation,” “The Five Vermin,” and “The Difficulties of Persuasion,” more than a hundred thousand characters in all.
paras.zh: 他看著自己的國家日漸削弱，好幾次上書向韓王進言。韓王沒有採用。史家說，韓非憤恨的是：國君不致力於修明法制、不憑藉權勢來駕馭臣下、不富國強兵，反而尊崇那些靠名聲與漂亮話過活的「蠹蟲」。既然他在朝廷上說不出話，寫給朝廷的又不被理會，他就為他永遠見不到的讀者而寫：〈孤憤〉〈五蠹〉〈說難〉等篇，總共十餘萬言。

paras.en: Someone carried the essays to Qin. The young king, the future First Emperor, read “Solitary Indignation” and “The Five Vermin” and said: “Ah, if I could meet this man and keep his company, I would die without regret.” Li Si, by then a minister in Qin, told him who the author was. Qin attacked Han, and the king of Han, who had ignored his cousin for years, sent him to Qin as an envoy.
paras.zh: 有人把這些文章帶到了秦國。年輕的秦王，也就是未來的始皇帝，讀了〈孤憤〉與〈五蠹〉，說：「嗟乎，寡人得見此人與之游，死不恨矣！」這時已經在秦國為臣的李斯告訴他作者是誰。秦國於是急攻韓國；而多年來不理會這位公子的韓王，派他出使秦國。

paras.en: The king of Qin was pleased with him and did not yet trust him. Li Si and another minister saw their chance. Han Fei, they said, is a prince of Han. Now that Your Majesty means to annex the other states, he will in the end work for Han and not for Qin, for such is human nature. To keep him here and then send him home is to make trouble for yourself. It would be better to find a legal charge and execute him. The king agreed and had him jailed. Li Si sent poison to the prison. Han Fei asked to plead his case before the king and was not allowed to. The king later regretted the order and sent a pardon, but Han Fei was already dead. The year was 233 BCE.
paras.zh: 秦王喜歡他，但還沒有信任他。李斯與另一位大臣看到了機會。他們說：「韓非，韓之諸公子也。今王欲并諸侯，非終為韓不為秦，此人之情也。今王不用，久留而歸之，此自遺患也，不如以過法誅之。」秦王認為有理，把他下獄。李斯派人送毒藥到獄中。韓非要求向秦王當面陳述，不被允許。秦王後來後悔了，派人去赦免他；但韓非已經死了。那一年是公元前 233 年。

paras.en: The argument Li Si used against him came from his own books: no one is to be trusted whose interests point elsewhere, and a ruler should act on interests and ignore professions of loyalty. Sima Qian noticed the irony and wrote the most personal line in the biography: “I grieve only that Master Han wrote ‘The Difficulties of Persuasion’ and could not escape them himself.” The essay explains with great subtlety how an adviser can be destroyed by saying the right thing at the wrong moment or to the wrong man.
paras.zh: 李斯用來對付他的那個論證，出自他自己的書：任何一個利益指向別處的人都不可信任；君主應該依據利益行事，不理會表白忠誠的話。司馬遷注意到了這個諷刺，寫下了這篇傳記裡最有個人感情的一句：「余獨悲韓子為說難而不能自脫耳。」那篇文章極其細膩地說明了：一位進言者，怎麼會因為在錯的時刻、或對錯的人說了對的話而被毀掉。

paras.en: Twelve years after his death the king of Qin completed the conquest of the six states, governing by methods that Han Fei had described. Li Si became chancellor of the empire and was himself executed in 208 BCE. The dynasty fell the following year. Later ages drew the lesson that Legalism wins wars and loses the peace, and for two thousand years no Chinese government admitted to following it, though all of them kept its laws, its bureaucracy, and its examinations of performance.
paras.zh: 他死後十二年，秦王完成了對六國的征服；用來治理的，正是韓非描述過的方法。李斯成了帝國的丞相，而他自己在公元前 208 年被處決。隔年，這個王朝覆亡。後世得出的教訓是：法家贏得了戰爭，卻輸掉了和平。此後兩千年，沒有一個中國的政府承認自己奉行法家；雖然它們全都保留了它的法律、它的官僚體系，以及它對政績的考核。

timeline: Studies with Xunzi alongside Li Si
Writes his essays after his advice is ignored
Qin attacks Han. He is sent to Qin as envoy
Qin destroys Han, the first of the six states to fall
秦滅韓，六國中第一個滅亡
The king of Qin becomes First Emperor

idea.title_en: The central idea: Law, method, and position
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：法、術、勢

paras.en: Han Fei starts from an observation about what moves people. Parents love their children, and a spoiled son does not reform for their love, for the scolding of neighbors, or for the wisdom of teachers. When the district officer arrives with soldiers and the law, he is frightened and changes his ways. “The people are by nature spoiled by love and obedient to authority.” Confucius, the sage of the whole world, won seventy followers by his goodness. Duke Ai of Lu, a mediocre ruler, was obeyed by everyone within his borders, Confucius included. Government should therefore be built on what works for nearly everyone. Hoping for virtue is no basis, since few respond to it.
paras.zh: 韓非從一個關於「什麼能推動人」的觀察出發。父母愛孩子；而一個被寵壞的兒子，不為父母的愛、鄉人的責備、師長的智慧而改過。等到州部的官吏帶著官兵、拿著公法來了，他才害怕，才改變行為。「民固驕於愛、聽於威矣。」孔子是天下的聖人，以他的仁義贏得了七十個追隨者。魯哀公是個平庸的君主，國境之內卻沒有人敢不臣服，孔子也在其中。所以，治國應該建立在幾乎對每個人都有效的東西上。寄望於德行不能當作基礎，因為會回應德行的人很少。

paras.en: He joined three ideas that earlier Legalists had held separately. Law, fa, is written, published, and applied to all: “The law does not favor the noble, as the plumb line does not bend for what is crooked. Punishment for faults does not spare great ministers, and reward for good does not pass over commoners.” Method, shu, is the ruler’s private technique for managing officials: assign duties, compare what a man promised with what he delivered, and hold in his own hands the “two handles” of punishment and reward. Position, shi, is the authority that belongs to the throne whoever sits on it. To these he added a view of history. Times change, and remedies must change with them, so that “the sage does not aim at practicing antiquity.”
paras.zh: 他把更早的法家各自分開主張的三個觀念結合起來。法，是成文的、公布的、對所有人一體適用的：「法不阿貴，繩不撓曲……刑過不避大臣，賞善不遺匹夫。」術，是君主用來駕馭官員的私下的技術：「因任而授官，循名而責實」，並且把刑與德這「二柄」握在自己手裡。勢，是屬於君位的權威，不管坐在上面的是誰。他還加上了一個歷史觀。「世異則事異」，對策必須跟著改變；所以「聖人不期修古」。

quote.en: The law does not favor the noble, as the plumb line does not bend for what is crooked. What the law applies to, the clever cannot talk their way out of and the brave dare not contest.
quote.zh: 法不阿貴，繩不撓曲。法之所加，智者弗能辭，勇者弗敢爭。
quote.ref: Han Feizi, chapter 6, “Having Standards,” translated for this series
quote.note_en: The most quoted sentence of Chinese Legalism, and the one that reformers of every later age could admire.
quote.note_zh: 中國法家最常被引用的一句；也是後來每一個時代的改革者都能欣賞的一句。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: Nothing binds the ruler
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：沒有東西約束君主

paras.en: Han Fei’s law applies to ministers and commoners alike, and he means it. But it comes from the ruler and serves the ruler, and nothing in the system tells the ruler what the law should contain or restrains him when he breaks it. The whole design assumes that the man at the top is at least of the “middle sort.” Han Fei admits that a Jie or a Zhou will bring disorder, and accepts this as the price of one bad age in a thousand. His own state was destroyed and he himself was killed by rulers who were using his methods, which suggests that the price is higher. A system that makes everyone below the throne predictable makes the throne itself the single point of failure.
paras.zh: 韓非的法對大臣與平民一體適用；他是認真的。但它出自君主，為君主服務；而這個制度裡，沒有任何東西告訴君主法律應該包含什麼，或者在他違法的時候約束他。整個設計假定了最上面的那個人至少是個「中者」。韓非承認，來了一個桀或紂就會亂；而他接受這是「一千世裡有一世壞」的代價。他自己的國家，是被使用他的方法的統治者滅掉的，他自己也是被這樣的統治者殺掉的；這表示代價比他說的高。一個讓君位以下每個人都可以預測的制度，使君位本身成了唯一的失效點。

paras.en: The second objection is Sima Qian’s: his doctrine was “extreme in its harshness and short on kindness.” A state that runs on fear and reward alone teaches its people that only fear and reward matter, and such people will serve the next master as readily as this one. In one of Han Fei’s own stories, a ruler falls asleep drunk and the keeper of the royal hat covers him with a robe. On waking, the ruler punishes the keeper of the robe for neglecting his duty and the keeper of the hat for exceeding his. Han Fei tells this with approval. A reader may conclude that in such a court no one will ever again do more than he is told, and that when the ruler is in real danger everyone will keep to his post.
paras.zh: 第二個反駁是司馬遷的：他的學說「其極慘礉少恩」。一個只靠恐懼與賞賜來運轉的國家，教給人民的是「只有恐懼與賞賜才要緊」；而這樣的人民，為下一個主人效力，會跟為這一個效力一樣爽快。在韓非自己講的一個故事裡，韓昭侯醉了睡著，管帽子的官（典冠）替他蓋上了衣服。昭侯醒來之後，處罰了管衣服的官，因為他失職；也處罰了管帽子的官，因為他越職。韓非講這個故事是帶著贊許的。讀者也許會得出結論：在這樣的朝廷裡，再也不會有人做得比被吩咐的多；而當君主真的有危險的時候，人人都會守在自己的崗位上。

problem.title_en: A Legalist who commented on Laozi

paras.en: Two chapters of the Han Feizi are the oldest surviving commentary on the Daodejing. Sima Qian put Han Fei in the same biography as Laozi and said that his thought, though it dealt in law and administration, “had its root in Huang-Lao.” This has puzzled readers, since the gentle book of the Way and the harsh book of the state seem to have nothing in common. The link is the ruler who does nothing. Han Fei’s ideal sovereign is still, empty, and hidden. He shows no preferences, so that no minister can flatter them. He takes no action himself, and the machinery of law and reward does the work. Laozi’s non-action thus became a technique of control, which is a reading the Daodejing permits and which many think a betrayal of it.
paras.zh: 《韓非子》裡有兩篇，是現存最古老的《道德經》解說。司馬遷把韓非跟老子放在同一篇傳裡，並且說他的思想雖然談的是刑名法術，卻「歸本於黃老」。這讓讀者困惑：那本談道的溫和的書，與那本談國家的嚴酷的書，看起來毫無共同之處。兩者的連結，是那位「什麼也不做」的君主。韓非理想中的君主是靜的、虛的、隱藏的。他不顯露好惡，這樣就沒有臣子能投其所好。他自己不行動，而由法與賞的機器來做事。老子的無為，就這樣成了一種控制的技術；這是《道德經》容許的一種讀法，而許多人認為這是對它的背叛。

paras.en: There is also a question about the man. He was a prince of Han who wrote the manual by which Han’s enemy conquered the world. One chapter of his book urges Qin to spare Han, and its authenticity is disputed. Whether he hoped to save his state by making himself useful to Qin, or simply followed his argument where it led, the texts do not settle.
paras.zh: 關於這個人，還有一個問題。他是韓國的公子，卻寫下了韓國的敵人用來征服天下的那本手冊。他的書裡有一篇勸秦國保全韓國；它的真偽有爭議。他究竟是希望藉著讓自己對秦有用來保住自己的國家，還是只是順著自己的論證走到哪裡算哪裡，這些文本並沒有給出定論。

said.claim: 「自相矛盾」與「守株待兔」出自韓非
said.claim_zh: 「自相矛盾」與「守株待兔」出自韓非
said.verdict_en: Both are his, and both were arguments
said.verdict_zh: 都是他的；而且兩個都是論證
said.en: The Chinese word for contradiction, 矛盾, means “spear and shield,” and it comes from Han Fei. A man selling both praised his shield as so strong that nothing could pierce it, and his spear as so sharp that it could pierce anything. Someone asked what would happen if his spear were used on his shield, and he could not answer. Han Fei did not tell the story as a joke. He used it against those who wanted both rule by worthy men, who cannot be restrained, and rule by position, which restrains everyone. The farmer who waited by the tree stump for a second rabbit is likewise his picture of the Confucians, who wanted to govern the present with the policies of the ancient kings. Both stories have survived as proverbs. The philosophy they were written to support has largely been forgotten.
said.zh: 中文裡表示「互相牴觸」的詞「矛盾」，出自韓非。有個人同時賣矛與盾：他誇他的盾堅固到沒有東西刺得穿，又誇他的矛銳利到沒有東西刺不穿。有人問：「以子之矛，陷子之楯，何如？」他答不出來。韓非講這個故事並不是當笑話講。他用它來反駁那些既要「賢治」又要「勢治」的人：賢人是不可禁的，而勢是無所不禁的。守在樹樁旁邊等第二隻兔子的農夫，同樣是他為儒者畫的像：他們想用先王的政策來治理當世。兩個故事都作為成語流傳了下來。它們原本要支持的那套哲學，大半已經被人遺忘了。

paras.en: Han Fei and the Buddha agree on one fact and draw opposite conclusions from it. The fact is that fear and desire move nearly everyone. A verse of the Dhammapada begins exactly as Han Fei might: “All tremble at the rod, all fear death.” Han Fei concludes that a ruler should take hold of these two handles and steer the people with them. The verse continues: “Treating others like oneself, neither kill nor incite to kill.” The Buddha takes the universal fear of punishment as a reason for compassion. In Buddhist terms the Legalist state governs by cultivating greed and fear in its subjects, which are two of the three roots of suffering, and so it makes people easier to rule by making them worse.
paras.zh: 韓非與佛陀在一個事實上意見一致，而從中得出了相反的結論。那個事實是：恐懼與欲望推動著幾乎每一個人。《法句經》有一首偈的開頭，簡直就是韓非會說的話：「一切都害怕刀杖，一切都畏懼死亡。」韓非的結論是：君主應該握住這兩個把柄，用它們來駕馭人民。那首偈接下去說：「以自己推想他人，不要殺，也不要教人殺。」佛陀把「人人都怕刑罰」當作慈悲的理由。用佛教的話來說，法家的國家，是靠著在臣民心裡培養貪與懼來治理的；而這是苦的三個根當中的兩個。所以它讓人民更容易統治的辦法，是把他們變得更壞。

paras.en: The comparison should be fair to Han Fei. The Buddha’s own community had rules, procedures, and graded penalties, and he did not rely on the goodness of monks any more than Han Fei relied on the goodness of ministers. The differences are in the purpose and the limit. The monastic rules exist to train the person who keeps them, and the heaviest penalty is to be sent away. There is no throne above the rules, since the Buddha left the teaching and the discipline as the only teacher. Han Fei saw clearly that institutions must not depend on saints. He did not see that an institution also shapes the people who live under it (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18).
paras.zh: 這個比較應該對韓非公平。佛陀自己的僧團有規則、有程序、有分等級的處分；他並不倚賴比丘的善良，就像韓非不倚賴大臣的善良。不同在於目的與界限。戒律的存在，是為了訓練持守它的那個人；而最重的處分是擯出。規則之上沒有君位，因為佛陀留下法與律作為唯一的老師。韓非看得很清楚：制度不能依賴聖人。他沒有看到的是：一個制度也塑造著活在它底下的人（佛法與西方哲學 D18）。

terms.d_en: Written, published standards applied equally to all below the ruler.
terms.d_zh: 成文的、公布的標準；對君主以下的所有人一體適用。

terms.d_en: The ruler’s technique for appointing, testing, and controlling officials.
terms.d_zh: 君主任用、考核與控制官員的技術。

terms.d_en: The power that belongs to an office apart from the qualities of its holder.
terms.d_zh: 屬於一個職位的權力；與在位者個人的品質無關。

terms.d_en: Punishment and reward, which the ruler must never let out of his own hands.
terms.d_zh: 刑與賞；君主絕不可以讓它們離開自己的手。

terms.d_en: Holding an official to exactly what his title and his own proposal promised.
terms.d_zh: 要求一位官員做到的，恰好就是他的職稱與他自己的提案所承諾的。

terms.d_en: The school that held that a state is ordered by law and power, not by the virtue of rulers.
terms.d_zh: 一個學派；主張國家是靠法律與權力而得到秩序的，不是靠統治者的德行。

quiz.q: What does Han Fei think moves most people?
options: Fear of punishment and hope of reward.
Love of virtue.
Respect for the ancient kings.
The wish for a quiet life.

quiz.q: What are law, method, and position?
options: Published rules for all, the ruler’s technique for managing officials, and the authority of the throne.
Three kinds of punishment.
The three books Han Fei wrote.
Three ranks of minister.

quiz.q: What did Sima Qian grieve over?
options: That Han Fei explained the dangers of persuading rulers and could not escape them himself.
That Han Fei’s books were burned.
That Han Fei refused to serve Qin.
That Han Fei had no students.

philosophers.name: John Dewey
philosophers.tag_en: The philosopher who ran a school to test his ideas, lectured across China for two years, and held that thinking, democracy, and art are all things we learn by doing.
philosophers.tag_zh: 一位為了檢驗自己的想法而辦了一所學校的哲學家；他在中國各地講學兩年，並且主張思考、民主與藝術，都是我們「從做中學」的東西。
facts: University of Vermont; PhD, Johns Hopkins
Pragmatism, with Peirce and William James
Democracy and Education (1916), Experience and Nature (1925), Art as Experience (1934)

paras.en: John Dewey was born in Burlington, Vermont, in 1859, the son of a shopkeeper. He was named for a brother who had died in an accident nine months before. After college he taught high school for a few years, found that he was better at thinking about teaching than at keeping order, and went to Johns Hopkins for a doctorate in philosophy. He taught at Michigan and in 1894 moved to the new University of Chicago as head of a department that combined philosophy, psychology, and education.
paras.zh: 約翰・杜威 1859 年生於佛蒙特州的伯靈頓，是一位店主的兒子。他的名字，取自九個月前在一場意外中死去的哥哥。大學畢業後，他教了幾年中學，發現自己思考教學比維持秩序在行；於是到約翰・霍普金斯大學攻讀哲學博士。他先在密西根大學任教；1894 年，他轉到新成立的芝加哥大學，主持一個把哲學、心理學與教育合在一起的系。

paras.en: In Chicago he did something few philosophers have done. In 1896 he and his wife Alice opened an elementary school in order to test a theory. The children cooked, built, sewed, and gardened, and arithmetic, chemistry, and history were taught as the problems arose from the work. Dewey called it the Laboratory School. He was also a trustee of Hull House, Jane Addams’s settlement among the city’s immigrants, and learned there what democracy looked like from below. In 1904, after a dispute with the university over the running of the school, he resigned and went to Columbia in New York, where he stayed for the rest of his career.
paras.zh: 在芝加哥，他做了一件很少有哲學家做過的事。1896 年，他和妻子愛麗絲開辦了一所小學，為的是檢驗一個理論。孩子們煮飯、蓋東西、縫紉、種菜；而算術、化學與歷史，是在工作裡出現問題的時候才教的。杜威稱它為「實驗學校」。他也是赫爾館的董事；那是珍・亞當斯在這個城市的移民當中設立的睦鄰之家。他在那裡學到了，從底層看上去的民主是什麼樣子。1904 年，因為學校的經營問題與大學起了爭執，他辭了職，轉到紐約的哥倫比亞大學，在那裡度過了其餘的學術生涯。

paras.en: In 1919 Dewey took a sabbatical in Japan. Former students of his, among them Hu Shih, invited him to cross to China for a short visit. He and Alice landed in Shanghai on April 30. Four days later students in Peking took to the streets against the terms of the Versailles treaty, and the May Fourth Movement began. Dewey was fascinated. He stayed for more than two years, leaving in July 1921, and lectured in many provinces with Hu Shih and others interpreting. His lectures on education, democracy, and scientific method were printed in newspapers and sold as books.
paras.zh: 1919 年，杜威趁休假到日本。他從前的學生（其中有胡適）邀請他渡海到中國短暫訪問。他與愛麗絲在 4 月 30 日抵達上海。四天之後，北京的學生走上街頭，抗議凡爾賽和約的條款；五四運動開始了。杜威深深著迷。他留了兩年多，到 1921 年 7 月才離開；由胡適等人口譯，在許多省分演講。他關於教育、民主與科學方法的演講，被刊在報紙上，並且印成書出售。

paras.en: No Western philosopher had been heard so widely in China before, and few have been since. His students carried his ideas into Chinese schools, and one of them, Tao Xingzhi, turned two of his slogans around. Dewey had said that education is life and the school a small society. Tao, working among the rural poor, said that life is education and society is the school. After 1949 Dewey’s name was attacked on the mainland together with Hu Shih’s. His influence on education in Taiwan continued through Hu Shih and his colleagues.
paras.zh: 在這之前，沒有一位西方哲學家在中國被這麼多人聽過；之後也很少。他的學生把他的想法帶進了中國的學校；其中一位，陶行知，把他的兩句口號倒了過來。杜威說過：教育即生活，學校即社會。在農村窮人當中工作的陶行知說：生活即教育，社會即學校。1949 年之後，杜威的名字在大陸與胡適的名字一起受到批判。他對台灣教育的影響，經由胡適與他的同事們延續了下來。

paras.en: Back in New York, Dewey wrote steadily for the next thirty years, in books for scholars and in magazine articles for everyone else. He helped to found associations for university teachers and for civil liberties. In 1937, at the age of seventy-eight, he traveled to Mexico to chair a commission of inquiry into Stalin’s charges against Leon Trotsky. He disagreed with Trotsky’s politics, and the commission found the charges false. He published Art as Experience at seventy-five and a major work on logic at seventy-nine.
paras.zh: 回到紐約之後，杜威在接下來的三十年裡持續寫作：為學者寫書，為其他所有人在雜誌上寫文章。他協助創立了大學教師的組織與維護公民自由的組織。1937 年，他七十八歲，遠赴墨西哥，主持一個調查委員會，調查史達林對托洛斯基的指控。他並不同意托洛斯基的政治主張；而委員會的結論是：那些指控是假的。他七十五歲出版《藝術即經驗》，七十九歲出版一部關於邏輯的重要著作。

paras.en: Alice died in 1927. In 1946, at eighty-seven, he married again, and he and his wife adopted two children. He died of pneumonia in New York in 1952, aged ninety-two. A Canadian historian who deplored his influence on schools wrote that he had been to his age what Aristotle was to the later Middle Ages: “not a philosopher, but the philosopher.” His prose is plain and often heavy, and he has been praised more often than read.
paras.zh: 愛麗絲在 1927 年去世。1946 年，他八十七歲時再婚；他與妻子領養了兩個孩子。1952 年，他因肺炎在紐約去世，享年九十二歲。一位對他在學校裡的影響深感痛惜的加拿大歷史學者寫道：他之於他的時代，就像亞里斯多德之於中世紀後期：「不是一位哲學家，而是『那位』哲學家。」他的文筆樸素，常常還很沉重；人們稱讚他的次數，比讀他的次數多。

timeline: PhD at Johns Hopkins; begins teaching at Michigan
獲約翰・霍普金斯大學博士；開始在密西根大學任教
Opens the Laboratory School in Chicago
在芝加哥開辦實驗學校
Chairs the Trotsky inquiry in Mexico
在墨西哥主持托洛斯基調查委員會

idea.title_en: The central idea: Experience and inquiry
idea.title_zh: 核心觀念：經驗與探究

paras.en: Older philosophies pictured the mind as a spectator that looks at the world from outside and tries to form a correct copy of it. Dewey, who had read Darwin, started from a living creature in an environment. Such a creature is always doing something. When its habits work, it does not think. When they fail and it does not know how to go on, it has a problem, and thinking is what it does to solve it: it forms a guess, acts on the guess, and sees what happens. Dewey called this inquiry, and held that science, morals, and politics are all forms of it. An idea is a plan of action, and it is tested by what follows when we act on it.
paras.zh: 較早的哲學，把心靈描繪成一個旁觀者：從外面看著世界，設法形成一份正確的摹本。讀過達爾文的杜威，是從一個「在環境裡的活生生的生物」出發的。這樣的生物，總是在做著什麼。它的習慣行得通的時候，它並不思考。當習慣失靈、它不知道怎麼繼續的時候，它就有了一個問題；而思考，就是它為了解決問題所做的事：形成一個猜測，依照這個猜測行動，看看會發生什麼。杜威稱之為「探究」，並且主張科學、道德與政治，都是探究的不同形式。一個觀念是一個行動的計畫；檢驗它的，是我們依它行動之後發生的事。

paras.en: Education follows directly. If thinking begins with a real difficulty, a school that hands children answers to questions they have not asked will teach them to memorize and to obey. Children learn when they have something to do that matters to them and that cannot be done without thought. Dewey defined education as “that reconstruction or reorganization of experience which adds to the meaning of experience, and which increases ability to direct the course of subsequent experience.” Democracy is the same process on a larger scale: “A democracy is more than a form of government; it is primarily a mode of associated living, of conjoint communicated experience.” Art, finally, is experience at its most complete, when doing and undergoing are so joined that nothing is wasted.
paras.zh: 教育直接由此而來。如果思考始於一個真實的困難，那麼一所把「孩子沒有問過的問題」的答案交給他們的學校，教會他們的是背誦與服從。孩子是在「有一件對他們要緊、而且不思考就做不成的事要做」的時候學習的。杜威把教育定義為：「經驗的改造或重組；它增加了經驗的意義，也增進了指引後續經驗方向的能力。」民主是同一個過程，只是規模更大：「民主不只是一種政府的形式；它首先是一種共同生活的方式，一種共同交流的經驗。」最後，藝術是最完整的經驗：做與受緊密相連，沒有一點浪費。

quote.en: I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living.
quote.zh: 所以我相信：教育是生活的過程，而不是為未來的生活做準備。
quote.ref: My Pedagogic Creed (1897), Article II
quote.note_en: Written in the year after he opened his school. Each paragraph of the Creed begins “I believe.”
quote.note_zh: 寫於他開辦學校的隔年。〈信條〉的每一段都以「我相信」開頭。

objection.title_en: The strongest objection: What is left to teach?
objection.title_zh: 最強的反駁：那還剩什麼可教？

paras.en: The complaint against Dewey’s schools is as old as the schools. If lessons must grow out of what interests the child, the child may never be interested in the multiplication table, grammar, or the dates of anything. Projects take a great deal of time and cover little. Children from homes full of books will pick up the missing knowledge elsewhere, and children from poor homes will not, so that a method meant to be democratic widens the gap. Critics such as E. D. Hirsch have argued that shared knowledge has to be taught directly and in order, and that progressive methods gave American schools a generation of confident students who knew very little.
paras.zh: 對杜威式學校的抱怨，跟這些學校一樣老。如果課程必須從孩子感興趣的事情裡長出來，那麼孩子也許永遠不會對九九乘法表、文法或任何年代感興趣。專題花掉大量的時間，涵蓋的卻很少。來自滿屋子是書的家庭的孩子，會在別的地方補上缺少的知識；來自貧窮家庭的孩子不會。於是一個原本要追求民主的方法，反而把差距拉大了。赫希這樣的批評者主張：共同的知識必須直接地、按順序地教；而進步主義的方法，給了美國學校一整代很有自信、卻所知甚少的學生。

paras.en: Dewey made much of this criticism himself. In Experience and Education (1938) he rebuked his own followers. He had never said, he wrote, that any activity a child enjoys is educational, or that teachers should stand back. The teacher’s task is harder in the new school, since she must know the subject thoroughly and also see how to lead a child’s present interest toward it. Experience that goes nowhere is not education. The reply is fair to Dewey and leaves the practical problem standing. His method asks more of teachers than most systems are able to train or pay for.
paras.zh: 這個批評，杜威自己就說過不少。在《經驗與教育》（1938）裡，他斥責了自己的追隨者。他寫道：他從來沒有說過，孩子喜歡的任何活動都有教育意義；也沒有說過老師應該退到一旁。在新式學校裡，老師的任務更難：她必須透徹地懂得學科，還要看得出怎樣把孩子眼前的興趣引向它。哪裡也去不了的經驗，不是教育。這個回應對杜威是公平的，而實務上的問題依然還在。他的方法對老師的要求，超過了大多數制度所能培養、或付得起薪水的程度。

paras.en: Pragmatism is often summed up as the view that a belief is true if it is useful to believe it. Bertrand Russell attacked it in that form: it would be useful to a tyrant that his subjects believe him wise, and that does not make it true. William James sometimes wrote in a way that invited the charge. Dewey took care to avoid it. He preferred to drop the word truth and speak of “warranted assertibility”: a claim is warranted when careful inquiry has tested it against the facts and it has held up. Usefulness to our wishes has nothing to do with it. What works, in his sense, is what solves the problem that started the inquiry, and the facts decide that.
paras.zh: 實用主義常被概括成這個看法：一個信念如果相信起來有用，它就是真的。羅素攻擊的就是這種形式：臣民相信暴君是英明的，對暴君很有用；但這並不使它為真。威廉・詹姆斯有時候的寫法，確實招來了這個指控。杜威很小心地避開了它。他寧可不用「真理」這個詞，而說「有保證的可斷言性」：當仔細的探究用事實檢驗過一個主張，而它站得住的時候，這個主張就是有保證的。「對我們的願望有用」與此毫不相干。在他的意義上，「行得通」的，是解決了引發探究的那個問題的東西；而這由事實來決定。

paras.en: Critics have not been wholly satisfied. If every warranted belief may be revised by later inquiry, it seems we never arrive at anything simply true, and we are owed some account of what inquiry is getting closer to. Dewey was content to say that it gets us out of the difficulty we were in, and into the next one.
paras.zh: 批評者並沒有完全滿意。如果每一個有保證的信念，都可能被後來的探究修正，那我們似乎永遠到不了任何「就是真的」的東西；而總該有人說明：探究是在接近什麼？杜威滿足於這樣說：它讓我們脫離了原本所在的困難，然後進入下一個。

said.claim: “Education is not preparation for life; education is life itself.” (John Dewey)
said.claim_zh: 「教育不是為生活做準備；教育就是生活本身。」（杜威）
said.verdict_en: A fair paraphrase; the wording is not his
said.verdict_zh: 意思沒錯；措辭不是他的
said.en: The sentence appears on school walls everywhere with Dewey’s name under it, and no one has found it in his writings in that form. What he wrote, in My Pedagogic Creed in 1897, is: “I believe that education, therefore, is a process of living and not a preparation for future living.” The popular version is a tidied form of this. Another favorite, “We do not learn from experience, we learn from reflecting on experience,” is also not found in his works, though it agrees with what he says about thinking. The slogan “learning by doing” is fair to him only with his own warning attached: doing teaches nothing unless the learner connects what he did with what happened as a result.
said.zh: 這句話掛在到處的學校牆上，底下署著杜威的名字；而沒有人在他的著作裡找到這個形式的句子。他在 1897 年的〈我的教育信條〉裡寫的是：「所以我相信：教育是生活的過程，而不是為未來的生活做準備。」流行的版本，是這句話整理過的樣子。另一句受歡迎的話：「我們不是從經驗中學習，而是從對經驗的反思中學習」，同樣不見於他的著作，雖然它符合他對思考的說法。「從做中學」這個口號，只有在附上他自己的那句警告時，對他才算公平：除非學習者把「他做了什麼」與「結果發生了什麼」連起來，否則「做」什麼也教不了。

paras.en: Dewey never studied Buddhism closely, and yet a Buddhist reader finds much that is familiar. Both he and the Buddha distrust teaching that is accepted on authority and never tried. The Buddha told the Kālāmas to accept a teaching “when you know for yourselves” what it leads to, and he described his path as a training, something done. Both think of a person as a bundle of habits in motion with no fixed inner core. For Dewey character is “the interpenetration of habits,” formed by what we repeatedly do and open to being formed again. And both hold that the ordinary moment, fully attended to, is where the real work is. What Dewey calls “an experience,” complete and unified, is not far from what a meditator means by being present.
paras.zh: 杜威從來沒有仔細研究過佛教；然而一位佛教徒讀他，會發現許多熟悉的東西。他與佛陀都不信任那種「憑權威接受、從不去試」的教導。佛陀告訴卡拉瑪人：「當你們自己知道」一個教導會導向什麼的時候，才接受它；而他把自己的道路描述為一種「學」，也就是要去做的事。兩人都把一個人想成一束運動中的習慣，沒有固定的內在核心。對杜威來說，品格是「種種習慣的相互滲透」：由我們反覆做的事所形成，也可以被重新形成。而兩人都主張，尋常的當下，只要充分地留意它，就是真正下工夫的地方。杜威所謂的「一個經驗」，完整而統一；這與禪修者所說的「活在當下」相去不遠。

paras.en: The difference is in where the process leads. Dewey refused to name a final goal. Growth, he said, has no end beyond more growth, and a school or a society is to be judged by whether it makes further growth possible. The Buddha did name a goal, the ending of craving and of suffering, and he measured every practice by whether it leads there. A Buddhist would say that Dewey describes very well how habits are remade and gives no reason to remake them in one direction and not another. Dewey would reply that fixed ends are the mark of the philosophies he was trying to leave behind. For a teacher the two can be used together. Dewey gives a method for how people learn, and the Dharma gives an account of what is worth learning (Dharma and Western Philosophy D18, D25).
paras.zh: 差別在於這個過程通往哪裡。杜威拒絕說出一個最終的目標。他說，成長除了更多的成長之外沒有別的目的；評判一所學校或一個社會，要看它是否使進一步的成長成為可能。佛陀確實說出了一個目標：渴愛與苦的止息；而他用「是否導向那裡」來衡量每一種修行。一位佛教徒會說：杜威把習慣如何被重塑描述得很好，卻沒有給出理由，說明為什麼要朝這個方向而不是那個方向去重塑。杜威會回應：固定的目的，正是他想要拋在後面的那些哲學的標記。對一位老師來說，兩者可以一起用。杜威給的是「人怎麼學」的方法；佛法給的是「什麼值得學」的說明（佛法與西方哲學 D18、D25）。

terms.d_en: The view that the meaning and worth of an idea lie in what follows from acting on it.
terms.d_zh: 一種看法：一個觀念的意義與價值，在於依它行動之後所發生的事。

terms.d_en: Dewey’s term for thinking as the controlled solving of a real problem.
terms.d_zh: 杜威的用語：把思考看成對一個真實問題有控制的解決過程。

terms.d_en: For Dewey, the whole transaction between a living being and its world, including what it does and what it undergoes.
terms.d_zh: 對杜威來說，是一個生命與它的世界之間的整個往來；包括它所做的與它所承受的。

terms.d_en: An acquired way of acting that makes up character and can be re-formed.
terms.d_zh: 一種習得的行動方式；它構成了品格，也可以被重新塑造。

terms.d_en: Schooling organized around the learner’s activity and interests. Dewey was its chief source and one of its critics.
terms.d_zh: 以學習者的活動與興趣為中心來組織的學校教育。杜威是它主要的源頭，也是它的批評者之一。

terms.d_en: Dewey’s replacement for “truth”: the standing a claim has when inquiry has tested and supported it.
terms.d_zh: 杜威用來取代「真理」的說法：一個主張經過探究的檢驗並得到支持時所具有的地位。

quiz.q: According to Dewey, when does thinking begin?
options: When a habit fails and a real problem arises.
When a teacher asks a question.
At the age of seven.
When the mind turns away from the world.

quiz.q: What did Dewey say in 1938 to followers who let children do whatever they liked?
options: That not every enjoyable activity is educational, and the teacher’s task is harder, not lighter.
That they had understood him perfectly.
That schools should be closed.
That only science should be taught.

quiz.q: How does Dewey describe democracy?
options: As a mode of associated living, more than a form of government.
As rule by the educated.
As a system for counting votes.
As an unreachable ideal.

further.t: John Dewey, Democracy and Education (1916)
further.n_en: Begin with chapters 1–4, 7, and 11.
further.n_zh: 從第一到四章、第七章與第十一章讀起。

further.t: John Dewey, Experience and Education (1938)
further.n_en: Ninety pages. His own correction of what was being done in his name.
further.n_zh: 九十頁。他親自糾正別人以他的名義所做的事。

further.t: John Dewey, Art as Experience (1934), chapters 1–3
further.n_en: The link is to an overview. The book’s third chapter, “Having an Experience,” is the place to start.
further.n_zh: 連結是一篇概述。書的第三章〈擁有一個經驗〉是起點。

further.t: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, “John Dewey”
further.n_en: A map of a very large body of work.
further.n_zh: 一份很龐大的著作的地圖。
